   - Objective: Validate operator escalation flow, oncall handoff, and customer communication cadence.
   - Steps:
     1. Fire synthetic alert: p99 latency > 1.5x SLO for 5 minutes.
     2. Confirm PagerDuty page fires, escalation proceeds to the correct rotation.
     3. Incident Commander opens incident ticket, CSM crafts initial customer notification using template.
   - Success criteria: Page acknowledged within 5 minutes, incident communications sent within 15 minutes, runbook tasks initiated.

Execution Playbook (step-by-step):
1. Kickoff (CSM): Share agenda, objectives, and success criteria. Confirm observation points and who will own each scenario.
2. Baseline capture (SRE): Collect baseline dashboards (latency, error-rate, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth) and snapshot logs.
3. Execute scenario (Incident Commander assigns tasks): Use validated scripts from /contrib/game-day-scripts. Capture timestamps for key events.
4. Immediate mitigation (Support / SRE): Apply documented mitigations; if not available, escalate to Engineering and note time-to-escalate.
5. Document (Support Engineer): Open post-game ticket with timestamps, logs, and screenshots.
6. Debrief (All): 15–30 minute structured debrief in which each role provides findings, blockers, and proposed fixes.
7. Post-game artifacts (CSM owner): Post a short report to customer record and update the knowledge base article referenced in the ticket.

Post-Game Report Template (must be completed within 48 hours):
- Executive summary (1 paragraph).
- Timeline of events (table with timestamps, actor, action).
- Metrics observed vs. expected (latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, instance counts).
- Root cause hypotheses and confirmed root cause (if any).
- Action items (owner, priority, ETA).
- Knowledge base updates (links).

Sample Timeline Table (ASCII):
| Time (UTC) | Actor | Event | Notes |
|------------|-------|-------|-------|
| 15:02 | Support | Customer switched to go-live key | SE verified config |
| 15:08 | SRE | Autoscaler triggered +3 nodes | scale latency 75s |
| 15:22 | SRE | Model failover initiated | fallback to variant v1-stable |

Metrics and SLOs to validate during game day:
- API success rate (2xx): target >= 99.0% during simulation window.
- p95 latency: target <= 350ms for short-form text models; p99 <= 800ms.
- Autoscaler reaction time: scale-up start < 120s after threshold breach.
- PagerDuty page-to-ack: < 5 minutes.
- Mean time to mitigation for mitigatable incidents: < 30 minutes.

Common failure modes and recommended mitigations:
- Failure mode: KV cache invalidation after model variant swap.
  - Mitigation: Warm caches using replay of peak traffic; pre-warm sequence cache for pinned variants.
- Failure mode: KMS timeouts in high-latency regions.
  - Mitigation: Enable regional KMS proxy and client-side retry/backoff.
- Failure mode: Misconfigured rate limits cause 429 storm.
  - Mitigation: Gradual ramp plan with automated throttling and synthetic traffic gating.

Artifacts and Repositories:
- Game-day traffic scripts: git@redwood:infra/game-day-scripts.git (branch: enterprise-onboarding).
- Templates: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/health-and-qbr/qbr-template-and-operational-checklist-2026.
- Runbooks referenced: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/incident-process and /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/rollouts.

Communication Templates (short):
- Initial customer notification (15min):
  Hi <Customer Team>,
  We are conducting a scheduled verification exercise for your go‑live. You may see elevated traffic and controlled rollbacks during the window. We will keep you updated every 15 minutes.

- Incident status update (30min):
  Current status: Investigating elevated p99 latency. Impact: API errors for 2% of requests. Next update in 30 minutes. Owner: <SRE Lead>.

Debrief & Continuous Improvement:
- All post-game action items must be tracked in the customer onboarding Jira board and closed within 30 days (CSM owner).
- Quarterly re-run recommended for customers on Dedicated/Private who cross 10% month-over-month usage growth.
- Add new scenarios to the playbook when we encounter gaps; maintain change log in the page history.

Appendix A — Example CLI snippets:
- Run load script (local):
  ./scripts/ramp_load.sh --api-key $TEST_KEY --rps 200 --duration 600

- Capture baseline traces (SRE):
  curl -sS "https://api.redwood.dev/metrics?env=staging&customer=<id>" | jq . > baseline.json

Appendix B — Known limitations:
- This playbook cannot safely simulate hardware failures (NVLink/GPU hang) in customer Dedicated pools without explicit engineering signoff.
- Some quality-monitoring thresholds are model-specific; coordinate with Applied ML to define correct pass/fail gates.

Document ownership and review cadence:
- Owner: Customer Success (CSM Guild).
- Recommended review cadence: every 6 months or after any enterprise incident.
- Required reviewers: SRE Lead, Support Manager, Solutions Engineering Lead.

Contact & escalation list (short):
- CSM: priya.desai@redwood.ai
- Support Manager: support-manager@redwood.ai
- SRE Rotation (pager): +PD:eng-sre-oncall
- SE lead: se-lead@redwood.ai

End of playbook.

title: Enterprise Stabilization: Technical Sweep & SLA Readiness Checklist
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes a coordinated technical sweep and SLA readiness checklist for enterprise go-lives during the first 14 days after cutover. It is designed for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Platform SRE, Product Ops, and the customer's technical leads to validate production readiness, confirm SLO alignment, and establish a backstop for fast mitigation of any regression in availability, latency, or cost.

Intended audience:
- Customer Success (primary)
- Eng SRE and Platform teams
- Onboarding Solutions Engineers
- Customer technical contacts and architecture owners

Goals:
- Verify telemetry, alerting, and dashboards are accurately reflecting tenant traffic within 48 hours of cutover.
- Confirm SLA eligibility and billing flags are correct prior to first billing cycle.
- Execute lightweight smoke and regression checks for core flows (generation, embeddings, streaming) at production scale for the customer traffic profile.
- Establish a documented mitigation and rollback path if SLOs are breached.

When to run this playbook:
1) Immediately after tenant cutover in staging -> production (day 0) for an initial smoke sweep.
2) Full technical sweep during day 1–3 to validate telemetry, throttles, and model fallbacks.
3) SLA readiness confirmation and billing gating on day 7 and day 14.

Ownership and contacts:
- CSE Onboarding Lead: Asha Patel (owner)
- Platform SRE Incident Lead: Marcus Nguyen
- Product Ops (billing gate): Lena Ortiz
- Escalation path: eng-sre-oncall -> platform-incident -> customer-success-manager

High-level coordination checklist (roles):
- CSE: coordinate customer runbook, run smoke tests, validate sample prompts, confirm token accounting.
- SRE: confirm alert routing, synthetic checks, latency percentiles, and circuit-breakers.
- Product Ops: verify usage metering, free-credit accounting, and SLA flags.
- Customer: provide production traffic pattern, hold a 30-minute daily sync for first 72 hours.

Pre-sweep prerequisites (verify these before starting):
- Deployment flag for tenant set to PRODUCTION and correct model pins applied.
- Ingress certificates valid and client certs authenticated (if mutual TLS used).
- Observability forwarding configured for tenant (metrics, traces, logs).
- Billing tenant_id set and test charge accepted in sandbox.
- SLO definitions imported into the tenant record (latency P50/P95, availability).

Technical sweep procedure (Step-by-step):
1) Smoke tests (immediate, ~30–60 minutes):
   a) Validate health endpoints: curl -sS https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health | jq .
   b) Run 10 production-like generation requests using customer's sample prompts. Capture latency and tokens used.
   c) Confirm streaming connection setup (websocket/wss) and EOF behavior with 5 streaming requests.

2) Telemetry and sampling validation (within 4 hours):
   a) Confirm traces appear in X-Ray/Jaeger for these requests with span names: request.receive, runtime.batch, kv.cache.hit, runtime.render.
   b) Check metrics in Grafana: tenant.<tenant_id>.requests_total, token_count, latency_ms.p50, latency_ms.p95, error_rate. Expected baselines should be within +/-20% of staging profile.

3) Rate limit and quota exercise (within 8 hours):
   a) Simulate burst at 1.5x expected peak to validate adaptive rate-limiter behavior.
   b) Validate 429 handling and graceful backoff behavior in client.

4) Model fallback and compatibility (24 hours):
   a) Trigger a model variant cutoff (simulate an out-of-capacity fallback) and confirm auto-fallback to pinned-compatible-model returns correct format and acceptable quality.

5) Cost and meter sanity (day 1–3):
   a) Inspect token accounting for test requests vs. expected cost models.
   b) Verify the usage connector has forwarded billing rows to Billing pipeline with tenant tag.

6) SLO and alert confirmation (day 1):
   a) Confirm alerting rules fire on synthetics when latency or error budget thresholds are crossed.
   b) Validate escalation flow triggers pager when a high-severity alert threshold is breached.

SLA readiness gating table (to be signed by Product Ops and CSE):
| Gate | Criterion | Pass Signal | Owner | Deadline |
|-----|----------|------------|-------|---------|
| Telemetry | Metrics and traces visible for tenant | Grafana and Jaeger traces with tenant tag | SRE | Day 1 EOD |
| Functionality | Core API requests succeed at expected success rate (>99%) | Synthetic pass rate >= 99% for 1hr | CSE | Day 1 |
| Latency | P95 latency within SLO target (configurable by customer) | P95 < configured threshold for 30m window | SRE | Day 3 |
| Billing | Usage rows present and mapped to tenant with expected token accounting | Billing pipeline shows non-zero rows for test traffic | Product Ops | Day 7 |
| SLA Flag | Tenant eligible flag set for SLA and billing protections | Manual approval in Billing console | Product Ops | Day 14 |

NOTE: If any gate fails, follow the Mitigation and Rollback section below before approving SLA flag.

Common validation commands and snippets:
- Check recent metrics: kubectl exec -it grafana-query -- curl -s "http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=rate(tenant_requests_total[5m])" | jq .
- Sample generation request (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-v1","input":"Summarize customer invoice records for April.","max_tokens":200}' | jq .
- Streaming test (node example):
  const ws = new WebSocket('wss://stream.redwood.example.com/v1/stream?tenant=$TENANT');
  ws.on('open', () => ws.send(JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-xl-v1',input:'Hello'})));

Telemetry assertions (quick checklist):
- Tenant tag present on request metrics and billing metrics.
- KV cache hit ratio reported in telemetry (should be between 10%–60% depending on workload).
- CPU/GPU utilization per node under 85% for sustained 5-minute window.
- Error rate per route < 1% (excluding expected 429s during rate-limit tests).

Mitigation and rollback options (ordered by preference):
1) Feature-level rollback: disable new feature flags (CSE/Product) and continue traffic on previous path.
2) Model variant switch: pin customer to previous model version with known stable profile.
3) Traffic diversion: redirect subset of tenant traffic to a safe capacity pool (dedicated to burst/fallback).
4) Tenant freeze: throttle requests to a safe limit while extended investigation completes.
5) Emergency rollback: revert cutover and return to the old endpoint (requires coordinated release and database state verification).

Escalation playbook (if SLO breached):
1) Declare SEV-1 if availability < 99% for > 15 minutes or latency > 2x SLO for > 30 minutes.
2) Notify oncall SRE, CSE owner, Product Ops, and customer primary via designated Slack channel and incident bridge.
3) Run triage checklist: gather logs, top 10 error stacks, recent deploys, quota and KVM cache metrics.
4) If mitigation above cannot restore service within 30 minutes, initiate traffic diversion.

Communication plan with customer:
- Day 0: immediate post-cutover email with links to dashboards, daily sync times, and escalation contacts.
- Day 1–3: 30-minute daily sync (standup) to review telemetry and runbook actions.
- Day 7: SLA readiness summary and ask for sign-off on billing gate.
- Day 14: Final stabilization review and transition to standard support cadence.

Acceptance signoff template (copy into meeting notes):
- CSE confirms telemetry and functionality gates: YES/NO
- SRE confirms alerting and latency gates: YES/NO
- Product Ops confirms billing and SLA flag: YES/NO
- Customer confirms acceptance and operational readiness: YES/NO

Appendices:
A) Quick reference: typical SLO defaults
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for enterprise Dedicated tenants (changeable by contract)
- Latency: P50 50ms, P95 300ms (depends on model and region)
- Error budget: 0.1% monthly

B) Example synthetic test payloads
- Short generation: {"model":"redwood-small","input":"Give three bullet points about product packaging."}
- Embedding batch sample (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"embed-compact-v1","inputs":["invoice text 1","invoice text 2"]}' | jq .

C) Ops contacts and escalation channels
- Slack: #oncall-sre, #cse-enterprise, #platform-ops
- Pager: +1-555-0100 (primary oncall)
- Incident bridge: https://meet.example.com/incident-bridge

Revision history:
- 2027-01-05: Created by Asha Patel (initial draft).
- 2027-02-10: Expanded model fallback tests, added SLA gate table, updated owners.

Related templates and further reading:
- Tenant acceptance testing template: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/tenant-onboarding-acceptance-testing-and-telemetry-assertions-2027

title: Enterprise Deployment Compliance Evidence Playbook and E2E Signoff
content:
Overview:

This playbook documents the end-to-end (E2E) evidence collection, verification, and signoff process required for enterprise deployments and compliance-driven cutovers. It is intended for Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Platform Operations, and the customer's compliance or security stakeholders. Use this playbook to produce a reproducible audit trail for regulatory review, internal compliance checks, and third-party audits.

Scope:
- Applies to Dedicated and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments where documented evidence is required prior to go-live.
- Covers technical evidence (telemetry, access logs, configuration snapshots), organizational signoffs, and the post-cutover audit window.
- Does NOT replace security penetration tests or SOC/ISO certification artifacts; it aggregates the project-specific evidence package for release.

Owner and roles:
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (Riley Chen)
- Primary technical owner: Platform Operations (on-call platform lead)
- Security reviewer: Security & Compliance (security reviewer assigned per-customer)
- Customer liaison: Solutions Engineering / Customer Technical Lead
- Audit contact: Legal / Compliance (named per account)

Service & SLO baseline to validate before signoff:
- Availability: >= 99.95% measured over 24h pre-cutover window
- Request success rate: >= 99.9% for production-like traffic pattern
- Token latency (p99): <= 300ms for hosted model variants; for Dedicated p99 should match contract (documented per-customer)
- Telemetry ingress latency: <= 30s for events from gateway to observability stack

Key systems referenced (examples):
- ingress-gateway (TLS termination, mTLS to backend)
- tenant-isolator (network and quota enforcement)
- model-router (routing to model variants and fallbacks)
- kvcache-service (prefix cache and KV eviction metrics)
- telemetry-gatekeeper (contract validation & forwarding)
- obs-collector (metrics/traces/logs forwarder)

Pre-cutover checklist (technical):
1. Configuration snapshot: export and store JSON/YAML of: ingress-gateway, tenant-isolator, model-router, and quota rules.
2. Access control review: confirm RBAC roles and service accounts; audit log enabled for key services.
3. Telemetry contract verification: run telemetry-contract-check.sh (see snippet) and confirm schema compliance.
4. Synthetic traffic run: execute 6h synthetic run matching 75–100% expected QPS and validate SLOs.
5. KVCache warmup: run cache-warmup micro-batch with representative prefixes.
6. Model variant smoke: exercise primary and fallback variants, verify identical response schema and function calling behavior.
7. Backup & rollback snapshot: store infra state, TLS certs (references), and database snapshot where applicable.

Evidence artifacts required (store in customer-audit-bucket):
| Artifact ID | Description | Required format | Owner |
|------------|-------------|----------------|-------|
| CFG-001 | Configuration snapshot (pre-cutover) | JSON/YAML | Platform Ops |
| ACC-002 | RBAC & service-account export | CSV/JSON | Security |
| TEL-003 | Telemetry contract validation report | JSON + log tail | Platform Ops |
| SYN-004 | Synthetic run report (6h) | HTML/PDF + metrics snapshot | Customer Success |
| KV-005 | KV cache hit-rate and eviction snapshot | CSV/JSON | Platform Ops |
| LOG-006 | Access & audit logs (rolling 7d) | gzipped logs | Customer Success / Security |
| SMK-007 | Model smoke test results and example payloads | JSON | Solutions Eng |
| ROLLBACK-001 | Rollback plan & snapshot pointers | Markdown | Platform Ops |

Step-by-step E2E signoff workflow:
1. Prepare artifacts: Platform Ops and Customer Success ensure all artifacts from the table above are uploaded to the customer-audit-bucket with consistent naming: <customer>-<artifact-id>-<timestamp> (e.g., acme-CFG-001-20260601T0300Z).
2. Automated verification: Trigger the evidence-verifier pipeline (CI job: ci/evidence-verifier) which runs schema validations and smoke-test replays. Pipeline must return green with zero critical failures.
3. Security review: Security reviewer performs RBAC and audit-log spot checks within 24 hours. Reviewer documents findings in SECURITY-REVIEW.md and attaches to the artifact set.
4. Customer acceptance: Customer Technical Lead validates the synthetic run and model smoke tests. A signed acceptance email or JIRA approval is required.
5. Legal & Compliance: Legal confirms contractual obligations are represented; Compliance approves retention and evidence redaction plan.
6. Executive signoff: Customer Success Lead and Platform Lead confirm readiness and set the go-live window.
7. Cutover execution: Follow cutover runbook (link below). During cutover, collect pre-defined live telemetry and produce the live-run evidence package.
8. Post-cutover validation: Run 24h high-fidelity validation and compare to pre-cutover SLOs. If any critical SLO fails, follow rollback criteria below.
9. Archive & retention: After 30 days of stable operation, move evidence package to long-term archive and produce an Audit Manifest.

Rollback criteria (abort or roll back immediately if any of the following occur during the 24h post-cutover window):
- Availability drops below 99.0% for a sustained 15 minute window.
- Request success rate drops below 98.5% for 10m with customer-visible errors.
- Model correctness regressions exceed the evaluated threshold (as determined by solutions eng eval harness).
- Unauthorized access or privilege escalation detected.

Cutover smoke tests (run as part of the live window):
- Functional: 50 representative user flows against the production tenant (sample payloads stored in SMK-007).
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 token latencies captured and compared to baseline.
- Cost-safety: per-minute token emission rate validated against burst limits and quota controllers.

Telemetry verification snippet (example):
# Telemetry contract check (bash)
# Usage: ./telemetry-contract-check.sh acme-staging
cat <<'JSON' > sample-event.json
{
  "tenant_id": "acme",
  "event_type": "inference.request",
  "timestamp": "2026-06-01T03:00:00Z",
  "payload_size": 832
}
JSON

curl -s -X POST https://telemetry.example.internal/contract-validate \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  --data @sample-event.json | jq .

Expected output: {
  "status": "ok",
  "schema_version": "v2.1",
  "errors": []
}

Traceability matrix (how artifacts map to compliance controls):
- CFG-001 -> Control INF-CONFIG-1 (configuration immutability)
- ACC-002 -> Control ACC-AUDIT-3 (role separation & access logging)
- TEL-003 -> Control MON-INGEST-2 (telemetry contract compliance)

Communication templates (abbreviated):
- Customer announcement: brief summary of go-live window, expected impact, rollback policy, and contacts.
- Internal incident slack template: pre-filled with artifact pointers and runbook links.
- Audit submission email: to auditor@example.com with artifact manifest and retention policy.

Post-go-live audit & retrospective (30 days):
- Compile Audit Manifest: list of artifacts, retention dates, hashes, and redaction notes.
- 30-day stability report: metrics, incidents, cost delta, and customer feedback.
- Lessons learned: 1-page runbook changes and owners for follow-up.

Appendix A — Sample evidence manifest (JSON snippet):
{
  "customer": "acme",
  "cutover_time": "2026-06-01T03:00:00Z",
  "artifacts": [
    "acme-CFG-001-20260601T0300Z.json",
    "acme-TEL-003-20260601T0320Z.json"
  ]
}

Appendix B — Links & runbooks:
- Cutover runbook (live): /confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/dedicated-tenant-cutover-safety-net-playbook-2026
- Evidence verifier CI: ci/evidence-verifier (internal)
- Incident escalation matrix: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/stakeholder-incident-briefing-and-commitment-playbook-2026

Contact & escalation list:
- Primary Platform Ops: platform-oncall@example.internal
- Customer Success (Lead): riley.chen@example.internal
- Security reviewer (on-call): security-reviewer@example.internal
- Legal / Audit intake: compliance-intake@example.internal

Notes & best practices:
- Use consistent artifact naming and include checksums for all stored files.
- Prefer machine-readable evidence (JSON) accompanied by human-readable summary PDF for auditors.
- Automate as many verification steps as possible; manual checks should be limited to items explicitly requiring human judgment (e.g., legal redaction approvals).

Revision history:
- 2026-01-15: Created by Riley Chen
- 2026-03-02: Added telemetry contract check and rollback thresholds (reviewers: Asha Patel)
- 2026-06-10: Finalized communication templates and evidence manifest format (reviewers: Samir Gupta, Elena Novak)

title: Tenant Onboarding: Acceptance Testing & Telemetry Assertions
content:
summary:
A structured acceptance-testing playbook to validate tenant readiness after provisioning and before hand-back. Defines telemetry assertions, synthetic scenarios, and safe rollback/fallback steps tailored to Dedicated and Private tenants.

body:
Purpose

This playbook provides a repeatable acceptance-testing and telemetry-assertion checklist for enterprise tenant cutovers (Dedicated and Private modes). Its goal is to ensure customers meet their SLOs and observability expectations before the CX hand-off.

Scope and audience

- Audience: Customer Success Engineers (CSE), Solutions Engineers, Oncall SREs, and Platform Engineers executing go-live validation.
- Scope: Post-provisioning validation window (first 72 hours), focused on latency, error rates, throughput, billing signals, and data-plane connectivity. Not intended for long-term performance tuning.

Prerequisites

1. Tenant is provisioned and accessible; operator has admin token and tenant ID.
2. Telemetry forwarding (metrics/traces/logs) enabled to central telemetry workspace or customer-managed forwarder.
3. Canary API key created and injected into test harness.

Quick checklist (high level)

- [ ] DNS / network reachability verified (ping, curl).
- [ ] TLS certificate chain validated for private endpoints.
- [ ] Basic API call succeeds and returns expected schema.
- [ ] Ingress egress firewall rules allow control-plane callbacks (if Private).
- [ ] Telemetry streams ingest baseline synthetic traffic.

Acceptance criteria (signal-level)

Provide these pass/fail assertions to the customer and engineering stakeholders. If any assertion fails, execute the rollback/fallback procedure below.

| Signal | Metric | Assertion (pass) |
|---|---:|---|
| Availability | 5m rolling availability | >= 99.5% during acceptance window |
| Latency (generate) | p95 gen latency | <= 600ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) |
| Error rate | 1m error rate (5xx + 429) | < 0.5% |
| Throughput | steady-state rps | Sustains expected commit profile ±10% |
| Cost signal | estimated projected daily token cost | Within agreed finance cap ±15% |
| Telemetry lag | metric ingestion lag | < 60s for critical alerts |

Telemetry assertions (concrete checks)

- Metrics to assert in the first 72 hours:
  - request.count by route and model variant
  - request.latency.p50/p95/p99 by route
  - request.errors.5xx and request.errors.ratelimit
  - kvcache.hit_ratio and kvcache.miss_ratio (if KV cache enabled)
  - pod.resource.cpu_util and pod.resource.gpu_util per node pool
  - billing.estimate.daily_tokens and billing.estimate.24h_projection

- Alert thresholds to temporarily enable for acceptance:
  - latency.p95 > 800ms for 2 consecutive 1m windows -> Sev2
  - errors.5xx >= 1% for 3 consecutive 1m windows -> Sev2
  - telemetry.lag > 120s -> Sev3

Synthetic test scenarios (run in order)

1) Smoke: Basic generation and embeddings
   - Command: curl -X POST https://{tenant-host}/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer {canary_key}" -d '{"prompt": "Hello world","max_tokens": 20}'
   - Expected: 200 OK, model output length <= 40 tokens, schema contains request_id and latency_ms

2) Latency profile: Burst of short prompts
   - Run: 100 short prompt requests over 60s (ramp 0->100rps) using our load harness
   - Expected: p95 latency within asserted bound; no tail errors or rate-limit biasing normal routes

3) Throughput profile: Sustained throughput at committed RPS
   - Run: sustained RPS for 15 minutes equal to tenant commit (or 50% of commit if in dry-run)
   - Expected: no autoscaler thrash; no OOMs on pods; stable CPU/GPU util curves

4) KV cache warm/cold cycle (if enabled)
   - Run a prefix-heavy scenario, measure kvcache.hit_ratio rising above 40% within 5 minutes for typical workloads

5) Failure injection: Simulate model fallback
   - Trigger: mark primary variant unhealthy via platform toggle; confirm automatic routing to fallback variant within policy window and acceptable quality degradation metrics tracked

Operational commands and tooling

- Test harness quickstart (example):
  - docker run --rm -e TENANT_HOST={tenant-host} -e API_KEY={canary_key} redwood/load-harness:latest --script short-burst.json

- Curl example for telemetry assertion (prometheus query):
  - curl -s "https://telemetry.redwood.internal/api/v1/query?query=request_latency_p95{tenant=\"{tenant_id}\"}" | jq .data.result

Rollback and fallback (safe steps)

If acceptance fails for any critical assertion, follow the safe rollback below in order. Document each step in the ticket.

1. Pause customer traffic (edge ACL or routing flag). Record timestamp.
2. If degraded due to model variant, revert routing to the last verified variant (platform toggle):
   - UI: Console -> Tenants -> {tenant} -> Traffic routing -> Revert to stable
   - API: POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenant}/routing?action=revert&to=stable
3. If resource saturation (OOMs/GC spikes): scale up GPU pool by +1 node or apply temporary burst capacity policy.
4. If networking (Private) issues: re-run firewall handshake and verify peering configurations; escalate to network infra.
5. If cost projection exceeded: engage FinOps and set soft quota throttle at 90% of projected cap.

Ownership and escalation matrix

| Role | Primary | Secondary | Pager | Escalation criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CSE | Aisha Kaur | Ruth Chen | N/A | Any acceptance failure requiring customer comms |
| Platform SRE | Owen Patel | Diego Martinez | oncall-sre@redwood.com | Resource OOMs, autoscaler thrash
| Network | Priya Sharma | Lukas Berg | network-oncall@redwood.com | Private peering / firewall failures
| FinOps | Maya Singh | Jonah Park | finops@redwood.com | Projected spend > cap + 10%

Post-acceptance handback checklist

- Confirm all temporary high-sensitivity alerts are returned to normal thresholds.
- Remove canary API key and rotate if requested.
- Share a short acceptance report with: customer, AE, CSE, and Platform owner. Report should include: acceptance window metrics snapshot, synthetic script outputs, and any remediation performed.
- Schedule QBR readiness meeting within 30 days to review long-term SLOs and cost profile.

Telemetry dashboard templates (recommended panels)

- Tenant Overview: availability, p95/p99 latency, error rate, synthetic test pass/fail
- Model Variants: per-variant request count, fallbacks, average latency
- Resource Utilization: per-node GPU/CPU, pod restarts, OOM counts
- Cost: 24h token estimate, projected 7d and 30d spend

Appendix: Example acceptance report snippet

- Acceptance window: 2026-02-10 02:00 -> 2026-02-10 08:00 UTC
- p95 latency (generate, short prompts): 412ms
- Availability: 99.92%
- kvcache.hit_ratio: 46% after warm-up
- Actions performed: Increased burst capacity by 1 node at 02:45 UTC; reverted routing at 03:10 UTC after model health check.

Related pages and artifacts

- Customer onboarding playbook (handback checklist): /confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/onboarding-handback-and-first-90-days-ops-guide-2026
- Canary harness repo: git@github.com:redwood/load-harness.git
- Telemetry queries library: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/tenant-telemetry-queries-2025

Contact and communication templates

- Short acceptance success email template included in internal snippets: "Subject: Tenant {tenant} — Acceptance Complete. Summary: [key metrics]. Next: schedule QBR"

Notes and version history

- v1.0 (2025-11-12) initial creation by Aisha Kaur
- v1.1 (2025-12-08) added KV-cache warm/cold assertions (reviewer: Diego Martinez)
- v1.2 (2026-02-15) tightened latency assertions for p95 and clarified rollback step 2 (reviewer: Ruth Chen)

End of document

title: Dependency Failure Resilience Playbook (Enterprise Onboarding)
content:
Purpose

This playbook documents a standardized approach for identifying, preventing, and remediating failures caused by third-party or internal dependency outages during enterprise onboarding and early go-live. It focuses on the technical mitigations, telemetry assertions, and communication patterns Customer Success (CS), SRE, and Platform teams should follow when dependencies degrade or fail.

Scope

- Applies to enterprise onboarding windows, canary rollouts, and first-72-hour post-go-live stability runs.
- Covers external partners (cloud provider APIs, SCM, identity providers, SaaS connectors) and internal services we rely on (ingress-gateway, fanout-proxy, telemetry-gatekeeper, embedding-indexer, kvcache, model-router).
- Does NOT cover purely customer-side outages (e.g., customer DB down) except where we coordinate cutover.

Owners and RACI

- Primary owner: Customer Success (Onboarding) — Ava Chen
- Technical owner (SRE escalation): Eng SRE — Diego Morales
- Platform mitigations and config changes: Eng Platform — Priya Natarajan
- Observability contract owner: Eng DevEx — Samir Gupta

RACI summary:
1) Detection: Eng SRE (R), Eng DevEx (C), CS (I)
2) Triage/Customer comms: CS (R), Eng SRE (A)
3) Mitigation (routing/fallback): Eng Platform (R/A)
4) Postmortem & action items: Eng SRE (R), CS (C)

Pre-Go-Live Dependency Map Checklist (must be completed before go-live gate)

1. Dependency inventory: maintain a single table with service name, owner, SLA (external), API endpoints, auth method, and last verified test run.
2. Telemetry assertions: add at least three assertion checks for each dependency (latency, error rate, presence of expected metrics).
3. Fallback compatibility: confirm an alternate path exists for each critical dependency (e.g., cached read, degraded feature, queued processing).
4. Runbook verification: ensure a runbook paragraph exists for each item with detection signal and mitigation steps.
5. Communication template: verify customer comms and internal incident templates are available and signed-off.

Dependency Resilience Matrix (example table)

| Dependency | Criticality | SLO tie | Failure modes | Primary detection signal | Immediate mitigation | Owner |
|-----------|-------------|---------|---------------|--------------------------|----------------------|-------|
| ingress-gateway | P0 | 99.9% availability | TLS handshake failures, 502 spikes | 5xx rate > 0.5% over 5m, TLS errors spike | Reroute to standby gateway, enable traffic-shaping to slow new sessions | Eng Platform (Priya) |
| telemetry-gatekeeper | P0 | Inference telemetry 1h TTL | Missing spans, dropped metrics | Missing ingestion heartbeat for 2m, sample rate drop | Fallback to passive buffering sidecar; enable synchronous flush | Eng DevEx (Samir) |
| fanout-proxy | P1 | 99% throughput | Queue growth, per-tenant blocking | Queue depth > 80% capacity for 3m | Enable per-tenant throttles, route low-priority tenants to degraded path | Eng Platform |
| external-idp (SCIM) | P2 | External SLA 99.5% | 429/403 from idp | auth failures or 429s > 1% | Switch to cached user mapping; pause provisioning jobs | Customer Success |
| embedding-indexer (internal) | P1 | Indexing SLA 95% | Index lag, OOM | indexing-lag > 10m | Apply incremental backfill window, drop non-critical batches | Eng Serving Runtime |
| model-router | P0 | Serving SLA 99.95% | Model load failures, KV cache misses | model load errors, cache miss rate > 15% | Switch to compatible quantized variant, enable cache warmup | Eng Serving Runtime |

Operational Runbook (detection -> mitigation -> validate)

1. Detection (first 5 minutes)
   - Watchers: SRE alerting channels receive automated signals (PagerDuty, Slack #sre-ops).
   - Initial checks: run ./tools/check-dependency-health --service <name> to confirm alarm.

2. Triage (5–20 minutes)
   - Assign a triage lead (SRE) and a customer liaison (CS).
   - Confirm blast radius: run tenant impact query (example):

     curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $MONITOR_API" "https://telemetry-api.prod/tenant-impact?service=fanout-proxy&window=10m" | jq .

   - If impact > threshold (defined below) escalate to on-call Eng Platform.

3. Immediate mitigations (20–60 minutes)
   - If ingress-gateway is degraded: flip to standby gateway with the CLI:

     rwdctl gateway failover --from ingress-gw-us-west-2 --to ingress-gw-us-east-1 --reason "onboarding surge"

   - If telemetry-gatekeeper ingestion is missing: enable buffering and start a fast-backfill:

     kubectl -n telemetry apply -f buffering-sidecar-override.yaml
     ./tools/backfill-telemetry --start $(date -u -d '15 minutes ago' +%s) --end $(date -u +%s)

   - If model-router fails to load a quantized variant: re-route traffic to fallback model:

     rwdctl model route --from model:prod:v2 --to model:prod:quantized-v1 --percent 100 --force

4. Validate (after 60 minutes)
   - Confirm telemetry asserts: all dependency assertions pass for 10 consecutive minutes.
   - Confirm SLO posture re-evaluated for impacted tenants and document customer-facing impact.

Escalation thresholds (examples)

- Severity P0: Any customer-facing error rate causing >1% 5xx across the tenant fleet or single large tenant with >0.5% 5xx for 10m. PagerDuty P0, incident bridge, executive notify.
- Severity P1: Throughput drops causing queue growth beyond 50% for >15m. PagerDuty P1; CS alerts impacted customers.
- Severity P2: Auxiliary systems (SCIM, billing connector) errors causing background job failures. Email + Slack notify; CS to log and monitor.

Customer Communication templates

- Initial acknowledgement (under 15 minutes):
  "We’ve detected a degradation affecting [feature/service]. Our engineering team is triaging. We will provide an update within 30 minutes and a root-cause timeline within 4 hours.

  Impact: [brief impact].
  Mitigation: [what we’re doing].
  Contact: your CS rep, [name], + link to status page."

- Mitigation update (30–90 minutes):
  "Summary: We identified [dependency] as the primary cause. We’ve applied [mitigation] which restored service for X% of requests. Engineers continue to monitor and will follow up with next steps by [time]."

Telemetry Assertions (examples to add to onboarding checks)

1. Ingestion heartbeat: telemetry-gatekeeper.heartbeat == true in last 1m
2. Model load success rate: model-router.load_success_rate >= 99.9% over 5m
3. KV cache hit ratio: kvcache.hit_ratio >= 85% over 10m

Add these to the onboarding synthetic suite; example JSON snippet for assertion: 

{
  "assertion_name": "kvcache_hit_ratio_onboarding",
  "expr": "avg(kvcache_hit_ratio{env=\"prod\",stage=\"onboarding\"}) > 0.85",
  "window": "10m",
  "owner": "eng-serving-runtime"
}

Canary Failure Simulation (run prior to go-live)

1. Simulate partial dependency failure: throttle upstream responses to 50% for 10 minutes using traffic-shaper job.
2. Verify that fallback paths engage within target time (<= 30s) and degraded responses are metric-tagged.
3. Run customer communication dry-run: ask CS to publish the initial acknowledgement and verify internal observers see it.

Post-Incident Walkthrough and Action Items (within 72h)

- Convene triage + CS + platform; capture timeline and mitigation chronology.
- Generate action items: code fix, observability gaps, config changes, customer compensation if SLA breach. Assign owners and target dates.
- Update dependency map and onboarding checklist with any missed validations.

Common Failure Mode Playbooks (short form)

- Telemetry ingestion drop
  1) Buffer sidecar enablement
  2) Backfill telemetry for the gap window
  3) Postmortem: add assertion and test to synthetic suite

- External SCIM throttling
  1) Pause provisioning
  2) Switch to cached identity mapping for auth flows
  3) Retry queue with exponential backoff and jitter

- KV cache cold start leading to latency spike
  1) Warm cache using sample keyset: ./tools/warm-kvcache --tenant <tenant-id> --keys-file warm-keys.json
  2) If warmfail, route to model variant with smaller memory footprint

Appendix: Useful commands and references

- rwdctl status dependencies --tenant <id> --since 15m\- shows dependency health summary\- 
- ./tools/check-dependency-health --service telemetry-gatekeeper --verbose\- detailed probe for the service\-
- Example buffering-sidecar-override.yaml (snippet):

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: telemetry-buffer-override
data:
  buffer.max_bytes: "50000000"
  flush.interval_s: "10"

Appendix: Postmortem checklist template (to attach to incident)

- Incident title and severity
- Detection time, mitigation applied, time to recovery
- Impacted tenants (list) and customer-facing communication timeline
- Root cause and contributing factors
- Concrete action items (owner, due date, verification test)

FAQ (short)

Q: When should CS ask for credits or SLA remedies?
A: Follow the existing SLA reconciliation playbook — if the incident breaches the contracted uptime or per-tenant SLO defined in the contract, CS should initiate the billing remediation flow after the postmortem is complete.

Q: Can we always failover to another region?
A: Not always. Region-based failover is a last-resort for data residency or private deployment customers. Follow the regional failover checklist and confirm customer consent where required.

Related pages and references

- Onboarding failure mode scenarios (linked internally)
- Canary simulation playbook (Eng SRE)
- SLA remediation and billing process

This playbook is intended to be a living document. Update the dependency matrix and telemetry assertions after every simulation and postmortem.

title: Enterprise bulk data ingest, backfill, and live cutover playbook
content:
Summary:
This playbook provides a prescriptive, low-risk process for performing large-scale data ingest and backfill work for enterprise customers, followed by the live cutover to Redwood inference pipelines (hosted, dedicated, or private). It codifies roles, pre-cutover validation, dry-run and backfill strategies, SRE guardrails, escalation paths, rollback criteria, and post-cutover checks.

Scope:
- Target audience: Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Customer SRE, Redwood Platform Ops, and customer engineering teams.
- Applies to: bulk ingestion of telemetry, prompt sets, embedding indices, or any dataset used by inference features where size or throughput requires coordinated cutover.
- Out of scope: routine small-scale batch imports (<100k records) — use standard integration guide.

Goals and success criteria:
- Cutover completes with <1% data loss and no more than 5 minutes of degraded inference latency compared to baseline.
- Backfill throughput sustained to complete within agreed SLA (example: 48 hours for 100M rows).
- No customer-visible errors beyond planned degradation windows; all incidents resolved or rolled back per runbook.

Roles & ownership:
- Customer Success (CS): overall cutover coordination, stakeholder comms, runbook lead.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): integration plan, test harnesses, schema mappings.
- Customer SRE: responsible for customer's production environment, networking, and ACLs.
- Redwood Platform Ops: capacity reservation, dedicated pool config, rollback hooks.
- Redwood SRE/Oncall: live monitoring, alerts, and incident triage.

Contact matrix (primary -> fallback):
- CS lead: alyssa.chen@redwood.ai -> jordan.patel@redwood.ai
- SE lead: ravi.narayanan@redwood.ai -> sofia.martinez@redwood.ai
- Platform Ops pager: #platform-ops -> escalation to oncall@redwood.ai

Pre-cutover checklist (required before any dry run):
1) Contract & SOW confirmation: confirm ingestion SLA, cost model, and storage retention with customer procurement.
2) Capacity and quota reservation: Platform Ops must reserve GPU/CPU pools and token quota for estimated peak load + 30% buffer.
3) Network & permissions validated: firewall rules, VPC peering, service accounts, and KMS/HSM access verified.
4) Schema & mapping validation: SE confirms schema compatibility with runtime and embedding pipelines.
5) Observability hooks enabled: request/response tracing, token-level cost tagging, custom metrics for ingest rate and validation failures.
6) Rollback criteria agreed and documented with sign-off by CS and Customer SRE.

Configuration matrix (example):
| Item | Recommended value | Owner |
|------|-------------------|-------|
| Dedicated pool size | 8x A100 equivalent | Platform Ops |
| Backfill batch size | 5k - 50k records (tune) | SE/Customer |
| Max concurrent streams | 200 | Platform Ops |
| Retention during backfill | 30 days (temp) | Customer |

Pre-run validation tests (execute in staging or shadow environment):
- Synthetic ingest at 1.5x expected rate for 30 minutes to validate autoscaling and queueing.
- Schema edge-case validation (nulls, UTF-8, truncation).
- End-to-end inference correctness checks on representative subset.

Dry-run procedure (recommended and must be green before full backfill):
1) Schedule a 2–4 hour maintenance window with stakeholders and publish comms.
2) Run a limited backfill on a 1–5% subset of data that mirrors distribution.
3) Metrics to observe: ingest success rate >= 99.5%, average token latency within SLO ±10%, error budget < 1%.
4) Run data reconciliation: sample hash checks between source and target for 1000 randomly selected rows.
5) Post-dry-run sign-off meeting: SE, CS, Customer SRE, Platform Ops. If any gate fails, remediate and rerun.

Backfill execution strategy options (choose one):
A) Continuous streaming backfill: best for near-live pipelines, low-latency requirements.
B) Batch windowing with checkpointing: recommended for very large datasets (>=50M rows) to limit peak load.
C) Hybrid (fast-forward then streaming): seed the index with a bulk snapshot, then stream real-time deltas.

Example backfill batch configuration (YAML):
---
batch_size: 20000
parallel_workers: 12
checkpoint_interval: 100000
retry_policy:
  max_retries: 5
  backoff_seconds: 60
validation_checks:
  - checksum
  - schema_match
  - sample_inference_compare
---

Operational monitoring and SLOs during backfill:
- Ingest success rate: target 99.9% (alert if <99.5% for 10m).
- Average per-request latency (inference path): SLO depends on customer tier; e.g., Dedicated <= 150ms p50, <= 500ms p95. Alert if p95 increases >2x baseline for 5 minutes.
- Token cost inflation: track cost-per-thousand-tokens; alert if >30% above forecasted.
- Queue depth and backpressure: alert if queue length > 5x normal for 10 minutes.

Incident detection and immediate mitigation steps (triage flow):
1) Detect: Alert fires (one of the SLO alerts above).
2) Triage: Platform Ops and Redwood SRE examine logs, traces, and queue metrics within 10 minutes.
3) Contain: Throttle backfill by reducing parallel_workers or switching to smaller batch_size.
4) Mitigate: Route high-priority customer traffic to fallback model variant or alternative region (see routing policy).
5) Escalate: If containment fails within 20 minutes, page engineering lead and open an incident in PagerDuty.

Escalation matrix (severity mapping):
- Sev3 (performance degradation): CS lead notified, Platform Ops mitigates, 1-hour P1 work window if unresolved.
- Sev2 (partial loss / repeated failures): Page Redwood SRE and SE, require immediate rollback gating.
- Sev1 (customer outage / data loss): Full incident protocol, immediate rollback, legal and exec comms.

Rollback criteria and procedure (pre-agreed):
- Rollback triggers:
  - Data loss detected in reconciliation > 0.5% of sampled rows.
  - Sustained latency >3x SLO for 15+ minutes with no mitigation.
  - Unrecoverable consumer queue corruption.
- Rollback steps:
  1) Stop all ingestion jobs and place system in read-only mode.
  2) Revert model routing to previous stable variant.
  3) Restore snapshot from pre-backfill checkpoint (store snapshots in S3 or customer-provided bucket).
  4) Run reconciliation checks and issue post-mortem.

Post-cutover validation checklist (24–72 hours):
- Full reconciliation completed for initial import window and sampled full dataset.
- Latency and error metrics stable within thresholds.
- Cost report generated and reviewed with CS and customer.
- Retention policy and cold-storage lifecycle rules applied.
- Runbook: close action items and create any follow-ups for engineering or infra.

Telemetry and observability (required tags and dashboards):
- Required metric tags: customer_id, ingest_job_id, batch_id, dataset_name, environment.
- Dashboards to create prior to run: Backfill Overview, Per-job Errors, Cost vs Forecast, Model Latency Heatmap.

Sample CLI commands and checks:
- Kick off a dry-run (example):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ingest/run \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n    -d '{"dataset":"customer_xyz_sample","mode":"dry_run","workers":4}'

- Check backfill job status (example response):
  {
    "job_id": "bf-20260301-01",
    "status": "running",
    "processed": 1200000,
    "failed": 12,
    "eta_minutes": 360
  }

- Reconciliation hash check (pseudo-command):
  redwood-reconcile --source s3://cust-bucket/2026-02-01/ --target redwood://ingest/datasets/customer_xyz --sample 1000 --output reconciliation-report.csv

Cost & billing notes:
- Enable per-job cost tagging before backfill so cost is attributed to customer SOW line items.
- Notify Finance if estimated credit consumption during backfill exceeds committed usage by >20%.

Run completion & sign-off:
- Required sign-offs: SE (schema/mapping), Customer SRE (network/permissions), CS (stakeholder comms), Platform Ops (capacity and final state).
- Closing artifacts to attach to this page: job logs, reconciliation report, cost worksheet, post-mortem if any.

Post-mortem template (if incident during cutover):
1) Summary of incident and impact.
2) Timeline of events (timestamped).
3) Root cause analysis.
4) Corrective actions with owners and due dates.
5) Lessons learned and changes to the runbook.

References and links:
- Integration guide: Event-driven batch ingest connector (internal)
- Network checklist: private-network-firewall-peering-checklist (internal)
- Cost attribution guide: enterprise-telemetry-cost-attribution-connector-playbook

Appendix: common troubleshooting commands and quick checks:
- Verify token usage: redwood-metrics query "sum(tokens) by job_id" --env prod --since 1h
- Inspect queue depth: kubectl -n ingest get hpa,deployments --selector=app=ingest -o wide
- Snapshot restore (example): aws s3 cp s3://backups/customer_xyz/2026-02-09/snapshot.tar.gz /tmp && redwood-restore --file /tmp/snapshot.tar.gz --target dataset/customer_xyz

Document history:
- 2026-02-10: created by Alyssa Chen
- 2026-03-05: edits — added rollback criteria and expansion of monitoring SLOs

If you are the runbook lead and need assistance: page #cs-backfill in Slack or email alyssa.chen@redwood.ai for an immediate consult.

title: Model Migration & Cutover Governance: telemetry contracts, safety gates, and SLA carveouts
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the governance, telemetry contracts, safety gates, and SLA carveouts for enterprise model migrations and cutovers. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), SRE, Product, and Security stakeholders who jointly own customer-facing model upgrades or tenant re-allocations (hosted, dedicated, or private).

Why this exists:
- Model migrations change output fidelity, token cost, and performance characteristics. Customers expect minimal disruption and an auditable trail for decisions that affect SLA eligibility and service credits.
- This document standardizes pre-cutover readiness checks, telemetry contracts, launch gates, and a clear escalation matrix to reduce surprise rollbacks and disputes.

Scope:
- Applies to: enterprise tenant cutovers, major model version rollouts (e.g., gen-1 -> gen-2), quantization or architecture changes that affect response semantics, and high-risk routing changes (regional failover).
- Excludes: routine minor model config tweaks that are covered by auto-canary thresholds (see auto-canary spec).

Owners and roles:
- CS Owner: Aisha Patel — customer comms and consent
- Cutover Lead (SRE): Miguel Fernandez — orchestration, telemetry gating
- Product Lead: Emily Chen — model selection, rollback criteria
- Security/Compliance: Rajesh Kumar — data residency and KMS checks
- Billing/FinOps reviewer: Priya Menon — cost impact and SLA carveouts

Pre-cutover checklist (gates that must be green before customer-facing switch):
1) Telemetry contract signed (CS/SRE/Product) and baselines captured (see telemetry snippet).
2) Synthetic regression suite pass: latency, p99, token-per-request, and quality checks (at least 95% of prompt set within expected metric bands).
3) Observability enabled: tenant-level traces, sample output capture, and per-request model-id tagging.
4) Backout plan documented: automated switchback playbook, expected RTO (<= 5 mins) and RPO (<= 0 requests).
5) SLA carveout agreement noted for migration window (timeboxed with explicit credit formula).
6) Security & compliance signoff for any new network egress or KMS usage.

Telemetry contract (example JSON snippet to be checked in with cutover):
{
  "contract_version": "1.0",
  "signals": [
    {"name": "latency_p95_ms", "sampling": "100% request-level", "owner": "sre"},
    {"name": "token_rate_per_min", "sampling": "aggregate per-minute", "owner": "billing"},
    {"name": "semantic_regression_pct", "sampling": "per-prompt-suite daily", "owner": "product"},
    {"name": "kv_cache_hit_rate", "sampling": "1s sliding window", "owner": "runtime"}
  ],
  "retention": "90 days",
  "access": ["cs-team", "sre-oncall", "product"]
}

Minimum signal thresholds and actions (table):
| Signal | Threshold (migration baseline) | Immediate action if breached | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| latency_p95_ms | <= 1200 ms | Abort migration, switchback within 5m | SRE |
| latency_p99_ms | <= 3000 ms | Trigger L2 paging and investigate | SRE/Product |
| semantic_regression_pct | <= 7% deviation vs baseline | Hold rollout, run extended evals | Product/CS |
| token_rate_per_min | < 3x expected | Auto-scale or throttle; notify FinOps | Runtime/FinOps |
| kv_cache_hit_rate | >= 60% | Proceed; if <40% abort and investigate cache warming | Runtime |

Cutover day runbook (high-level steps):
1. T-minus 4 hours: Finalize customer comms (scheduled window, expected impacts, on-call roster). CS sends templated notice (see Slack template below).
2. T-minus 2 hours: Run a full synthetic pass and upload results artifact to cutover ticket.
3. T-minus 30 minutes: Confirm telemetry contract live, sampling turned on, and retention set to 90 days.
4. T-minus 5 minutes: Set circuit-breaker thresholds to conservative values.
5. T0: Execute canary at 1% of traffic for 15 minutes. Monitor signals every minute.
6. T0 + 15m: If canary green, ramp to 10% for 20 minutes (automated step).
7. Progressive ramps: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with hold windows and explicit approvals from Cutover Lead.
8. Post-switch: Run end-to-end customer acceptance prompts and log outputs to the customer audit stream.

Rollback criteria (explicit, must be documented before T-minus 2h):
- Any threshold in "Immediate action" column breached.
- >10% of customer-critical prompt-suite failures in a 10-minute window.
- p99 latency > 2x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Unexpected increase in token billing estimate > 25% over projection for the hour.
If rollback is triggered: execute automated switchback, open an incident in the Incident Tracker, and initiate a post-mortem owner assignment within 24 hours.

Escalation matrix (who to page in order):
1) Cutover Lead (SRE) -> Miguel Fernandez (primary), paging channel: #sre-cutover-paging
2) Product (model quality) -> Emily Chen (primary)
3) CS escalation -> Aisha Patel (customer updates & acceptance)
4) Security -> Rajesh Kumar (if data-residency/KMS issues suspected)
5) FinOps -> Priya Menon (billing anomalies)
6) Exec on-call -> Engineering Director (if customer outage > 60 mins or material SLA dispute)

Slack templates (use before/after cutover):
- Pre-cutover notice (CS -> customer):
  Hi <customer-team>,
  We will start a scheduled model upgrade at <start-time UTC>. Expected user-visible changes: 
  - latency: +/- small variance
  - improved semantic accuracy for X prompts
  We expect a <duration> window; if you observe regressions after <T+30m> please open a support ticket and we will prioritize.

- Internal rapid update (SRE -> stakeholders):
  Cutover update: stage=<canary|ramp|complete|rollback>, traffic=<percent>, key_signals={latency_p95: 420ms, semantic_regression: 1.2%}. Next decision in 10m.

Post-cutover validation checklist (within 24h):
- Confirm autoscaling behaved as expected and no abnormal token spikes.
- Confirm synthetic regression suite still within expectations.
- Execute run of customer-critical prompts and collect adjudicated pass/fail.
- Prepare a short runbook for customer-facing operational quirks observed.
- Schedule QBR slot to review migration metrics and SLA carveouts if any.

SLA carveout template (example language):
- Time window: <start> to <end> (migration window)
- Carveout scope: latency and availability credit eligibility paused for customer-impact incidents directly caused by model semantic regressions discovered during the window (requires documented trial and rollback attempts).
- Credit formula: prorated daily uptime * 0.5 for migration window if rollback executed; otherwise standard credit rules apply. Decisions require signoff from CS + FinOps.

Dispute resolution steps (if customer rejects migration outcome):
1. CS collects adjudicated evidence: sampled outputs, synthetic suite results, and telemetry.
2. Convene 3-way review (CS/Product/SRE) within 48 hours to attempt remediation or offer rollback.
3. If unresolved, escalate to Legal & Finance for SLA credit arbitration.

Postmortem and QBR integration:
- Any migration with rollback or with a carveout invoked must produce a 1-page incident summary and a 45-minute QBR deep-dive within the next quarterly QBR cycle.
- Include the following QBR artifacts: baseline vs actual telemetry charts, adjudicated prompt examples, cost delta analysis, and customer sentiment summary.

Appendix A: Example queries to validate telemetry (CLI):
# p95 latency for tenant-123 in last 15m
redwood metrics query --tenant tenant-123 --metric latency_p95_ms --range 15m

# sample output capture for 10 requests containing prompt-set id 987
redwood audit fetch --tenant tenant-123 --prompt-set 987 --limit 10 --output sample.json

Appendix B: Sample automated canary policy (YAML):
policy:
  name: model-migration-canary
  steps:
    - percent: 1
      duration: 15m
      pass_criteria:
        latency_p95_ms: <1200
        semantic_regression_pct: <7
    - percent: 10
      duration: 20m
      approval: cutover_lead
    - percent: 50
      duration: 10m
      approval: cs_owner

Appendix C: Contacts and paging channels:
- SRE Cutover: miguel.fernandez@redwood.ai, slack: @miguel_f (channel #sre-cutover-paging)
- Product: emily.chen@redwood.ai, slack: @emily_c
- CS: aisha.patel@redwood.ai, slack: @aisha_p
- Security: rajesh.kumar@redwood.ai, slack: @rajesh_k
- FinOps: priya.menon@redwood.ai, slack: @priya_m

Notes and caveats:
- This playbook does not replace the dedicated security acceptance checklist for Private deployments; for Private, ensure on-prem KMS rotation and IP whitelists are validated at T-minus 24h.
- For very high-sensitivity customers (PHI/PCI), migrations require a dry-run in a mirrored staging environment with customer observers and explicit legal signoff.

Revision history:
- 2026-11-15: Created by Aisha Patel (initial draft)
- 2026-12-10: Added telemetry contract template and rollback thresholds (review: Miguel Fernandez)
- 2027-01-10: Finalized SLA carveout wording and dispute workflow (review: Emily Chen, Rajesh Kumar)

End of document.

title: Enterprise Onboarding — Post-Provisioning Stability & Fallback Checklist
content:
Overview
This playbook defines the post-provisioning stability and fallback verification steps we run for enterprise customers after Dedicated or Private (VPC / on-prem) environments are provisioned and before handing back to Product/Engineering for live traffic. The goal is to validate functional correctness, confirm SLOs and capacity assumptions, exercise fallback and routing policies, and confirm monitoring/alerting is wired end-to-end. This document is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Solutions Engineers, and the Redwood SRE/Platform teams.

Key objectives
- Verify baseline latency and throughput for representative workloads.
- Confirm automatic fallback paths and model variant switchover behave as expected.
- Validate KV/prefix cache priming and persistence (where applicable).
- Ensure observability: dashboards, tracing, and alerting triggerable and readable by customer ops.
- Document owners, rollback criteria, and escalation steps.

When to run
- Immediately after dedicated/private environment provisioning completes and the control plane shows "provisioned" state.
- After canary deploys or model version upgrades prior to 100% traffic.
- After network configuration changes, routing policy updates, or capacity reservations change.

Prerequisites
- Customer tenant ID and API credentials with a staging/test API key.
- Access to the customer's VPC peering / VPN details (for Private deployments).
- A canonical set of prompts (prompt-set) representative of expected traffic; include edge cases.
- Access to Redwood Console for the tenant and to internal SRE dashboards.
- Test VM or container with curl / python / k6 installed for load testing.

Stability checklist (high-level)
1) Connectivity and auth checks
   - Confirm control-plane API responds: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <STAGING_KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account/status
   - Verify TLS certificates are valid and CN/SANs match the customer's domain where relevant.
   - For Private: validate VPC routes and firewall rules allow traffic to inference nodes on ports 443 and internal gRPC ports (if used).
2) Basic functional smoke tests (AND golden outputs)
   - Run 10 deterministic prompts from the provided prompt-set, assert no 5xx errors.
   - Capture token counts and ensure shape matches expected model behavior. Example curl: 
     curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n       -d '{"model":"redwood-rt-1","input":"Translate to French: The server is healthy."}' \n       https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | jq '.'
3) Latency and tail latency verification
   - Run 50 sequential single-request latency samples. Compute P50/P90/P99. Acceptable pass thresholds: P50 < 120ms, P90 < 250ms, P99 < 800ms for short-context workloads (<=256 tokens).
   - Document results in the Handback Report (see "Handback template" section).
4) Throughput and concurrency test
   - Use k6 or a simple Python worker to simulate concurrent clients. Start with concurrency=8, ramp to concurrency=64 over 5 minutes. Goal: No 5xx errors and <5% request error budget.
   - Observe autoscaler behavior (Dedicated only): confirm new worker pods/instances spawn and throughput increases.
5) KV / prefix cache priming and persistence
   - For workloads that benefit from KV cache (chat rerendering or repeated prefix expansions), run a session workload that primes the cache. Note cache hit rate in runtime metrics (target > 60% after priming for representative sessions).
   - Restart one serving process (or node) to verify cache recovery and TTL settings.
6) Model variant fallback and routing exercise
   - Intentionally create a synthetic capacity constraint: apply a routing policy that returns the model to a "degraded" variant (e.g., quantized lower-cost variant). Validate end-to-end: requests succeed, outputs remain within quality guardrails, and customer-visible headers indicate fallback.
   - Confirm automated rollback triggers fire if quality/regression monitors cross threshold (see "Quality thresholds").
7) Observability and alerting verification
   - Confirm dashboards show: request rate, latency percentiles, error rate, KV cache hit rate, token cost per request.
   - Trigger a synthetic alert by causing a controlled 5xx surge and confirm SRE-oncall receives notifications and that pager routing matches the runbook.
8) Cost and billing sanity check
   - Run a short burst of typical workload and compare estimated cost vs. forecasted unit economics. Flag >20% deviation to finance/CS ops.

Quality thresholds (automated regression gates)
| Metric | Acceptable | Warning | Failure |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| P50 latency (short context) | <120ms | 120-250ms | >250ms |
| P99 latency | <800ms | 800-1500ms | >1500ms |
| 5xx error rate | <0.5% | 0.5%-2% | >2% |
| Prompt-level BLEU/ROUGE change (sample eval) | <1% delta | 1%-3% | >3% |
| KV cache hit rate (primed) | >60% | 40%-60% | <40% |

Handback template (required for sign-off)
- Customer: <tenant-name>
- Environment: Dedicated / Private (VPC)
- Provisioned at: <timestamp>
- Test key used: staging-xxxxx
- Test prompt-set summary: (attach file or link)
- Latency P50/P90/P99: <values>
- Peak throughput achieved (rps): <value>
- Errors: 5xx count and %
- Cache hit rates: <values>
- Fallback exercised: yes/no and notes
- Open action items: list owners and due dates
- Acceptance: CSE signoff and customer technical contact signoff (names & signatures)

Runbook — rapid remediation steps (triage first 15 minutes)
1) If >2% 5xx errors or P99 > 1.5x expected: immediately switch traffic to fallback model variant or lower-load region according to routing policy. Owner: SRE (pager).
2) If autoscaler fails to add capacity under load: scale to reserved capacity (Dedicated) or request capacity burst via capacity API. Owner: Platform Ops.
3) If KV cache hit rate drops >30% after restart: check cache mount points, persistence config, and system logs (service: redwood-kv). Owner: Runtime team.
4) If customer cannot authenticate: verify API key rotation and KMS/HSM integration for Private. Owner: Customer Success & Security.

Escalation matrix
- Customer-facing CSE: first responder for customer communication.
- Platform SRE (pager): handles capacity, autoscaling, and high-traffic incidents.
- Runtime engineering on-call: kernel/runtime regressions, KVCACHE corruption.
- Security on-call: suspected credential compromise or data exfiltration.
- Escalation channels: Slack channel #cs-enterprise-ops, PagerDuty service "redwood-dedicated-prod", and email enterprise-ops@redwood.ai.

Example troubleshooting commands and snippets
- Check API health: curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
- Query runtime metrics (internal) via Prometheus API: 
  curl -s "https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query?query=redwood_request_duration_seconds_p99{tenant=\"<tenant>\"}" | jq .
- Priming a chat session (Python): 
  import requests
  resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat', headers={'Authorization':f'Bearer {KEY}'}, json={'model':'redwood-rt-1','messages':[{'role':'user','content':'Hello world'}]})
  print(resp.json())

Healthchecks config example (YAML)
apiHealthcheck:
  path: /v1/health
  expected_status: 200
  timeout_ms: 1500
latencySloProbe:
  percentile: p99
  threshold_ms: 800
  sample_interval_s: 30

Acceptance and sign-off process
1) CSE runs checklist and fills Handback template.
2) Share results with customer technical contact and SRE for review.
3) Hold a 30-minute go/no-go call: review anomalies and mitigation plans.
4) Once customer and CSE sign off, mark the environment as "Customer Ready" in the provisioning system and schedule a production cutover window.

Post-handback operational recommendations (first 30 days)
- Weekly: compare observed unit costs vs. forecast.
- Twice weekly: run the smoke prompt-set and store results in the evaluation harness.
- Daily for first 72 hours of live traffic: monitor P99 and 5xx errors on Redwood Console and keep an open incident channel.

Ownership and contact info
- CSE lead: Aisha Martin (aisha.martin@redwood.ai)
- SRE rotation owner: see internal rota at /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-rotations
- Platform ops: platform-ops@redwood.ai

Attachments and references
- Prompt-set (attach)
- Handback spreadsheet template (attach)
- Related runbooks: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/migration-cutover-stability-playbook-2026

title: Cross-Regional Cutover, Telemetry Gates, and Cost-Gating Playbook for Enterprise Onboarding
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines steps, telemetry gate criteria, and cost-gating policies for cross-regional enterprise tenant cutovers. It is intended for Customer Success engineers, Solutions Engineers, SRE on-call, and the customer’s cloud/networking contact. The goal is a safe, observable cross-region activation with automatic failback triggers and cost mitigation if unexpected billing or token-rate anomalies occur.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to enterprise customers migrating from single-region hosted or Dedicated deployments to multi-region (active-primary + passive-secondary) configurations during go-live windows.
- Covers pre-cutover verification, telemetry gate definitions, automated gate enforcement, manual and automatic failback, cost gating thresholds, and post-cutover QBR metrics.
- Does NOT replace tenant-specific security acceptance tests (see security gates playbook).

Roles and ownership:
- Customer Success (CS): runbook owner, coordinates stakeholders and business signoffs.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): pre-cutover config and ingress verification.
- Eng-SRE: on-call for capacity and traffic shaping; owns automated failback tooling.
- Customer (networking/security): provide firewall, routing, and cert rotations.
- Escalation: follow standard escalation matrix; primary CS owns customer comms.

Pre-cutover checklist (must be completed no earlier than 72 hours before scheduled cutover):
1) Capacity & model pinning
   - Verify dedicated pools or reserved capacity are provisioned in target region(s) with 20% buffer over expected steady-state TPS.
   - Confirm model versions and quantization profiles are pinned in tenant config (model_id + version).
2) Network & certs
   - Confirm peering or Transit Gateway is established; test 3-way TCP handshake to each inference proxy IP.
   - Ensure client certs and ingress certs rotate with no downtime (test cert chain).
3) Telemetry gating assertions deployed in gatekeeper service
   - Install telemetry assertions bundle (JSON spec) to customer-facing gatekeeper namespace.
4) Cost guard setup
   - Define billing thresholds and emergency cost caps in Tenant FinOps panel; add CS and finance contacts.
5) Synthetic workload
   - Create tenant-specific synthetic journeys that emulate common request shapes (chat, streaming, embeddings).

Telemetry Gate Criteria (these must be green to proceed):
- Latency SLOs (per-route and per-model): 99th percentile latency for short-chat (<=128 tokens) must be <= 350ms.
- Token success rate: >= 99.5% for tokenized responses (no stream resets, 4xx/5xx).
- Error budget burn rate: must be < 2x baseline for the 30-minute rolling window.
- Cost per 1k tokens deviation: <= +25% vs expected unit cost baseline for the first 60 minutes.
- Synthetic fidelity: synthetic journeys must achieve >= 95% success (passes semantic assertions).

Telemetry Gate Table (quick reference - assertions enforced by Gatekeeper):
- "latency_p99_short_chat": threshold 350ms, evaluation_window 30m, action "hold"
- "token_success_rate": threshold 99.5%, evaluation_window 15m, action "alert"
- "error_budget_burn": threshold 2x, evaluation_window 30m, action "failback"
- "cost_delta_1k": threshold +25%, evaluation_window 60m, action "cost-cap"
- "synthetic_journey_pass_rate": threshold 95%, evaluation_window 15m, action "hold"

Cutover procedure (step-by-step):
Pre-cutover (T-minus 2 hours):
1. Notify stakeholders via Cutover channel and update status page.
2. Run a full synthetic run (3 iterations) from multiple regions; validate gate assertions locally.
3. Ensure autoscaling groups are warm and KV caches are primed with representative prefixes.

At cutover (execution window):
1. Gradual DNS / routing change: shift 10% of production traffic to target region for 10 minutes. Observe telemetry gates in real time.
2. Increase to 30% for 15 minutes if gates remain green; run synthetic journeys.
3. Proceed to 60% for 20 minutes; monitor cost delta closely.
4. Final 100% switchover only allowed if all gate assertions remained green across the incremental windows.

Automated failback and remediation rules:
- Immediate automatic failback to previous region (or queued fallback model pool) if any gate with action "failback" trips (e.g., error_budget_burn).
- Throttled rollback (graceful): if "hold" gates trip, cut traffic back by 25% and run diagnostics.
- Cost-cap trigger: when cost_delta_1k > threshold, automatically enable token-rate limiters for non-critical routes and notify CS/FinOps.

Failback runbook (SRE execution):
1) On alert, acknowledge and open incident in PagerDuty with tag "cross-regional-cutover".
2) Execute automated rollback script: /opt/redwood/bin/region-failback --tenant $TENANT --target-region $PRIMARY --reason $ALERT_TAG
3) If rollback script fails, perform manual routing rollback via the routing console (steps included in appendix).
4) Post-rollback: collect the following artifacts within first 30 minutes: trace slices (x-trace ids), pod logs, gatekeeper assertion logs, synthetic journey results. Attach to incident.

Cost-gating and emergency billing protection:
- Emergency cost cap: default = 200% of daily expected spend (tenant-configurable). When reached: (a) pause low-priority embedding jobs and batch ingestion, (b) enable per-API token caps, (c) notify FinOps and customer billing contact.
- Tiered actions by severity:
  - Severity 1 (blocker): immediate pause of all non-essential routes and rollback to previous topology.
  - Severity 2 (high): apply 50% token rate reduction to best-effort routes, keep primary customer transactions.
  - Severity 3 (medium): raise alert to CS and schedule QBR follow-up to review FinOps anomalies.

Communication templates (use in Cutover channel and customer emails):
- Short update (while cutover in progress): "Cutover to region eu-west-1 at 10:10 UTC: currently 30% traffic, gates nominal. Will update in 15m or on exception."
- Failback notice: "Automated failback executed for tenant <TENANT>. Reason: <GATE_NAME> tripped. CS lead <NAME> coordinating next steps. Incident: <PD_LINK>"

Post-cutover QBR & SLA evaluation (first 72 hours):
- Metrics to collect and include in QBR: 99/95/50 latency percentiles by route, token success rate, per-model cost per 1k tokens, synthetic journey pass rate, error budget burn curves, and customer-facing error traces.
- Evaluation framework: compare each metric to pre-cutover baseline and flag regressions >10% for prioritized RCA.
- Suggested agenda items (30–45 minute review): cutover timeline, telemetry gate events, cost delta analysis, customer impact summary, action items and owners.

Appendix A — Example Gatekeeper assertion JSON (deploy via gatekeeper-api):
{
  "assertions": [
    {"name": "latency_p99_short_chat", "type": "p99_latency", "threshold_ms": 350, "window_minutes": 30, "action": "hold"},
    {"name": "cost_delta_1k", "type": "unit_cost_delta", "threshold_pct": 25, "window_minutes": 60, "action": "cost-cap"}
  ]
}

Appendix B — Routing console quick commands:
- Check active weights: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://routing-console.prod/api/tenants/$TENANT/weights
- Set weight: POST to /api/tenants/$TENANT/weights {"region":"eu-west-1","weight":30}

Appendix C — Escalation contacts (order):
1. CS on-call: cs-oncall@redwood.ai (Primary: Aisha Gupta)
2. Eng-SRE on-call: sre-oncall@redwood.ai (Primary: Ethan Park)
3. Solutions Engineering: se-lead@redwood.ai (Primary: Marta Lopez)
4. Finance alerts: finops@redwood.ai

Related artifacts and references:
- Telemetry Gatekeeper onboarding guide: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/integration-guides/telemetry-gatekeeper-onboarding-and-qbr-integration-guide-2026
- Dedicated tenant cutover safety net (reference): /confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/dedicated-tenant-cutover-safety-net-playbook-2026

Change log:
- 2026-01-12: Draft created by Aisha Gupta.
- 2026-03-03: Added cost-cap automation and synthetic journey guidance (review: Samir Khan).
- 2026-06-02: Updated failback automation command and adjusted latency SLO to 350ms (review: Ethan Park).

End of document

title: Private Network: Firewall & Peering Checklist for Enterprise Onboarding
content:
Purpose

This document is a practical, sequence-driven checklist to validate network, firewall, and peering configurations during enterprise private deployment onboarding (VPC and on-prem). It consolidates recommended rules, verification steps, and escalation paths to minimize go-live delays caused by connectivity issues between customer networks and Redwood Inference Private control and data planes.

Audience

- Customer network and security teams
- Redwood Solutions Engineering (SE) and Customer Success (CS) onboarding leads
- Redwood Private deployment engineers

Scope and intent

This checklist covers:
- Outbound and inbound firewall rules for control plane and data plane services
- VPC peering and route validation patterns
- Basic NAT and proxy considerations
- Diagnostic commands and test vectors to validate traffic flows
- Acceptance criteria and how to escalate unresolved issues

Summary of assumptions

1. Customer environment: VPC (AWS/Azure/GCP) or equivalent private network with ability to add routes/security-group/firewall rules.
2. Customer will provide a network contact, CIDR ranges, and preferred peering method (VPC peering, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, VPN, or dedicated circuit).
3. Private deployment uses two logical planes: control-plane endpoints (API/management) and data-plane endpoints (inference endpoints, egress to telemetry).

Network ownership and run roles

- Customer network owner: single point-of-contact for rule changes and routing (required).
- Redwood SE onboarding lead: coordinates validation steps and performs Redwood-side checks.
- Redwood Private ops: accepts packet captures / logs and performs further investigation when escalated.

Checklist: Pre-provision (customer to confirm before scheduling provisioning)

1) Provide required values (email these to SE):
   - Primary VPC CIDR(s) and subnets (e.g., 10.100.0.0/16)
   - NAT / egress architecture details (NAT Gateway or egress proxies)
   - Peering preference: VPC Peering / Transit Gateway / PrivateLink / VPN / Direct Connect
   - Egress to 3rd-party KMS or identity provider endpoints (if used)
   - Internal DNS resolution strategy (will customer resolve Redwood hostnames internally?)

2) Schedule a 60m network validation call with network owners and Redwood SE.

Firewall and routing rules (required)

Apply these rules to customer perimeter firewalls / security groups / network appliances. Replace example CIDRs and hostnames with the values provided by Redwood in the deployment manifest.

| Purpose | Protocol | Direction | Destination / Port | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Control plane API (management) | TCP | Outbound | redwood-control.example.com:443 | TLS 1.2+; allow SNI "redwood-control.example.com" |
| Data plane inference endpoints | TCP | Outbound / Peered | 10.200.0.0/22:443 | Customer should allow peered subnet range for inference requests |
| KV cache and internal telemetry | TCP | Outbound | 10.201.0.0/24:443 | Encryption required; avoid deep packet inspection |
| Healthcheck probes (from Redwood) | TCP | Inbound (when enabled) | <customer-health-probe-ip>:443 | Optional; customer may whitelist Redwood probe IPs |
| NTP (time sync) | UDP | Outbound | 0.pool.ntp.org:123 or NTP server IPs | Time skew > 2s can break TLS session validation |
| DNS resolution | UDP/TCP | Outbound | <customer-dns-ips>:53 | If private DNS resolvers used, confirm recursive replies for redwood hostnames |

Note: If the deployment uses PrivateLink/Private Endpoint, data-plane traffic does not require NATed egress but still requires Security Group/ACL rules permitting the private endpoint.

Peering and route validation

- VPC Peering: Ensure both sides have explicit route table entries for each other's CIDRs pointing to the peering attachment. No overlapping CIDRs allowed.
- Transit Gateway: Confirm route propagation and attachment associations include the subnets in scope.
- VPN / Direct Connect: Verify BGP prefixes and BGP session state are UP (use show ip bgp summary / cloud console BGP diagnostics).
