Communication templates (use in alerts/email to customer):
- Short alert subject: [Onboarding] Tenant t123: success_rate dropped to 96% (automated mitigation applied)
- Body: Include: what happened, immediate mitigation, expected customer impact (e.g., 10% reduced throughput), next steps, and POC contacts.

Acceptance signoff checklist (CSM to obtain):
- Telemetry assertions green for 30 minutes after mitigations reversed.
- Customer confirms in-product sampling/observability surface is visible and usable.
- FinOps confirms cost-projections within expected band and quota-protector hooks are registered.
- Legal/Compliance signoff (if restricted data flows required).

QBR and handoff artifacts to generate after go-live:
- Canary telemetry packet: include time-series of assertions, synthetic run output, failure-and-mitigation timeline.
- Action items: items requiring changes before ramp (instrumentation gaps, model test coverage, policy changes).
- Post-go-live stability window: 72 hours active monitoring with daily summaries to customer.

Operational notes & tips:
- Prefer model fallback to global rollback when the issue is domain-specific (model-behavior drift).
- Watch for tokenization edge-cases that cause apparent latency spikes; token-level traces are critical.
- Use the telemetry enrichment helper (redwoodctl telemetry enrich --tenant t123 --since 15m) to attach request metadata to alerts.

Appendix: Useful commands and JSON snippets
1) Route weight change (example API payload):
{
  "route_id": "onboarding/t123",
  "action": "set_weight",
  "weight": 0.1,
  "duration_minutes": 30
}
2) Model fallback toggle (example):
{
  "tenant_id": "t123",
  "from_model": "gptx-20b-v2",
  "to_model": "gptx-20b-baseline-v1",
  "apply_immediately": true
}
3) Telemetry completeness query (example):
redwoodctl metrics query --tenant t123 --metric telemetry_completeness --window 15m --group-by route

Related pages and references:
- Telemetry Gatekeeper Onboarding (integration guide)
- Onboarding post-provisioning stability checklist (enterprise)
- Escalation-playbook (for high-severity or prolonged incidents)

Revision history:
- 2026-02-15: Initial draft (Lena Ortiz)
- 2026-05-02: Added automated mitigation rules and synthetic test guidance (Arjun Mehta)
- 2026-09-08: Tuned thresholds and clarified fail-forward timeline (Sofia Alvarez)

End of document.

title: Tenant Observability Contract Lifecycle and Versioning Playbook
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the lifecycle, versioning rules, testing gates, and rollout procedures for tenant-specific observability contracts used during enterprise onboarding and post-go-live operations. It standardizes how telemetry schemas, labels, and SLO-related metrics are introduced, evolved, and deprecated for dedicated and private tenants. The aim is to reduce integration friction, preserve downstream SLO integrity, and provide clear rollback and remediation steps for customers and internal teams.

Goals
-----
- Provide a predictable, auditable change process for tenant telemetry schemas ("contract").
- Minimize customer-side parsing and dashboard breakage during schema changes.
- Ensure SLO and billing signals remain consistent across contract versions.
- Define operational runbooks for validation, rollout, and rollback.

Scope
-----
Includes: ingress metrics, request/response metadata, model-identifiers, latency/billing tokens, event tracing IDs, and tenant-specific labels emitted by ingress-proxy, model-router, and telemetry-gatekeeper.
Excludes: internal-only debug traces and ephemeral dev-only flags.

Principles
----------
1) Backward compatibility first: additive fields only for patch/minor updates whenever possible.
2) Explicit version header: every telemetry payload must include `telemetry_contract_version` and `schema_version`.
3) Consumer-driven validation: create a consumer schema test harness prior to rollout.
4) SLO continuity: any change that impacts token counting or latency buckets requires SLO owner sign-off.

Contract Versioning Rules
-------------------------
- Versioning scheme: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (SemVer-like, but focused on consumer compatibility):
  - MAJOR: incompatible changes (removal/rename of required fields, semantic changes to metric meaning). Requires coordinated migration and 90-day deprecation notice.
  - MINOR: additive fields and new optional labels. Safe for rolling updates.
  - PATCH: bug fixes in serialization, typos, or clarifications that do not change semantics.
- Filesystem path / registry: contracts are stored in the telemetry registry (internal git repo: infra/telemetry/contracts/). Each version has a manifest and migration notes.

Telemetry Contract Example (minimal JSON payload example)
--------------------------------------------------------
Note: this example is intentionally concise — real payloads will include additional tracing and debug metadata.

{
  "telemetry_contract_version": "1.2.0",
  "tenant_id": "enterprise-42",
  "request_id": "r-8ab3cd",
  "model_id": "redwood-compat-13b-q4",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "tokens_input": 128,
  "tokens_output": 42,
  "latency_ms": 78.2,
  "cost_units": 0.0038,
  "timestamp": "2026-01-29T15:22:03Z",
  "labels": {"region":"eu-west-1", "deployment_tier":"dedicated", "privacy_level":"high"}
}

Migration and Rollout Procedure
-------------------------------
1) Design phase (owner: CS integration engineer)
   - Author the new contract in the registry and add migration notes.
   - Identify all internal consumers (billing, SLO dashboards, QBR reports, cost attribution jobs, alerting rules).
   - Create a migration ticket and assign reviewers (SRE, Billing, Observability, Product).

2) Validation harness (owner: Observability team)
   - Add the new schema to the consumer test harness.
   - Run the following checks:
     a) Parsing test (clickhouse/bq ingestion): ingest 1000 synthetic payloads and confirm no schema rejections.
     b) SLO equivalence: simulate token counts and latency buckets to ensure SLOs do not change >1%.
     c) Dashboard smoke: run dashboard snapshots of top-10 queries for differences.

3) Canary (owner: CS + SRE)
   - Canary window (default 48 hours): enable new contract for 2% of tenant traffic per region.
   - Monitor: error rate, ingestion rejects, billing delta, and SLO drift. Alerts: any of the following triggers immediate rollback:
     - ingestion_reject_rate > 0.1% sustained over 30m
     - billing_signal_delta > 5% compared to baseline
     - SLO metric drift > 2%

4) Gradual rollout
   - 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over successive windows (24–72 hours each), adjust based on risk and test results.

5) Complete and document
   - Mark registry entry as active and update related onboarding docs and QBR templates.
   - Notify customer success contacts and tenant POCs.

Rollback and Emergency Remediation
----------------------------------
- Hot rollback: flip ingestion to last-stable schema at the telemetry-gatekeeper layer. This is expected to be near-instant but requires a follow-up migration postmortem.
- If hot rollback is not possible (e.g., semantic change in token counting), escalate immediately to SRE and Billing and open a severity-1 incident with the standard incident comms template.
- Triage checklist for rollback incident:
  1) Capture affected tenant list and time window.
  2) Freeze billing-related aggregations and mark as provisional.
  3) Notify customer POCs with a templated message (see Appendix A).

Validation Tests and Gating
--------------------------
Mandatory gating checks before any minor or major update: 
- Schema lint (jsonschema) passes.
- Consumer test harness run with zero parsing failures.
- SLO smoke equivalence within guardrails (default: SLO drift < 1% for latency; token count variance < 0.5%).
- Billing delta within tolerance (default: < 2% over the canary window).

Sample Prometheus Alert Rule (conceptual)
----------------------------------------
# name: Telemetry_Ingestion_Rejects
expr: rate(telemetry_ingestion_rejects_total[5m]) / rate(telemetry_ingest_total[5m]) > 0.001
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "High telemetry ingestion reject rate (>0.1%)"
  runbook: "/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/telemetry-ingest-failure"

SLO Mapping and QBR Implications
--------------------------------
- Each telemetry contract version must include a metadata file that maps emitted fields to product SLOs and QBR KPIs. Example mapping: `tokens_output` -> billing.units, `latency_ms` -> platform.latency.slo.
- During QBR prep, the CS team must verify that the contract version used in the QBR timeframe matches the contract recorded in the migration registry. Discrepancies must be annotated in the QBR appendix.

Ownership and Notifications
---------------------------
- Contract author: CS integration engineering (primary).
- Observability: owns consumer test harness and alerting.
- Billing: approves any change that affects token counting or cost_units.
- SRE: approves rollout windows and manages canary routing.

Communication and Customer-Facing Steps
--------------------------------------
1) Pre-schedule notification: send a 14-day heads-up for major changes, 7 days for minor changes.
2) Pre-cutover checklist: share a migration plan and sample payloads with tenant POC and solutions engineer.
3) Post-cutover confirmation: within 24 hours confirm telemetry ingestion is stable and provide a simple validation script tenant can run.

Appendix A — Templated Customer Notification (short)
---------------------------------------------------
Subject: Upcoming Telemetry Schema Update (telemetry_contract_version 1.2.0)

Hello <Tenant POC>,

We are planning a telemetry schema update that will be enabled for your tenant on <date>. The change is additive (new optional labels and an additional `cost_units` field) and should not require action. During the canary window, you may see a small variance in billing aggregates; we will monitor closely and share results. If you prefer a scheduled cutover or need a private testing window, reply to this thread and we will coordinate.

Regards,
Redwood Customer Success

Appendix B — Example Validation CLI (tenant-facing)
----------------------------------------------------
# curl example payload to the telemetry gatekeeper (test endpoint)
curl -X POST "https://telemetry-test.redwood.com/ingest" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"telemetry_contract_version":"1.2.0","tenant_id":"<your-tenant>","request_id":"r-test","model_id":"m-test","tokens_input":10,"tokens_output":5,"latency_ms":40.0,"timestamp":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}'

# quick parse check (jq required)
cat sample-payload.json | jq '.telemetry_contract_version == "1.2.0" and .tokens_output > 0'

Appendix C — Quick Checklist (for rollout ticket)
-------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Registry entry created and reviewed
- [ ] Consumer harness run and green
- [ ] Billing sign-off obtained (if required)
- [ ] Canary window scheduled (2% start)
- [ ] Pager/alert rules adjusted and runbook linked
- [ ] Customer POC notified per pre-schedule
- [ ] Post-cutover validation completed

Related pages and artifacts
--------------------------
- telemetry contracts repo: infra/telemetry/contracts/ (internal git)
- Observability test harness: /confluence/eng-platform/telemetry-test-harness
- Incident runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/telemetry-ingest-failures

Questions or feedback
--------------------
If you are the owner of an internal consumer (dashboards, billing jobs, or QBR reports), please review the contract registry entry during the design phase and add yourself as a reviewer. For urgent issues during a rollout, page #observability on Slack and follow the incident escalation procedure.

title: First 72 Hours Post-Go-Live: Stability, Observability, and Cost-Control Playbook
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes the operational runbook for the first 72 hours after an enterprise customer goes live on Redwood (hosted, dedicated, or private). The goal is to stabilize traffic, validate cost controls, confirm quality metrics, and provide clear escalation paths if production behavior diverges from expectations. Use this document as the canonical checklist for Customer Success (CS), Oncall, and Platform Engineers during the initial post-cutover period.

Scope and objectives
--------------------
- Scope: Applies to enterprise cutovers where a customer begins production traffic to Redwood inference endpoints for the first time or after major migration. Includes hosted API, Dedicated tenants, and Private deployments.
- Objectives (first 72h):
  - Ensure customer-facing SLOs are met (latency, availability).
  - Validate cost/usage profile against the agreed ramp plan and trigger throttles or quota protections if anomalies occur.
  - Confirm model fidelity (no major quality regressions vs. eval baselines).
  - Maintain clear communications to customer stakeholders and internal execs.

Owner and primary contacts
--------------------------
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (Maya Chen)
- Oncall escalation: Platform Oncall (rotation lead) — contact via #oncall-pager Slack and PagerDuty escalation: ENG-PLATFORM-PG
- Customer-facing lead: assigned CSM and Solutions Engineer (listed in cutover runbook)
- Exec escalation: Head of Customer Success (Priya Singh)

Pre-cutover checklist (completed during go/no-go window)
-------------------------------------------------------
1) Configuration validation (CS / Solutions Eng)
   - Confirm API key provisioning and tenant mapping.
   - Validate routing and VPC peering / private network rules.
   - Confirm dedicated capacity reservation and autoscale limits for Dedicated customers.
2) Telemetry and observability
   - Ensure synthetic probes are configured for: latency P50/P95, error rate, token-per-request distribution, and model-quality sentinel prompts.
   - Verify metrics forwarding and access for customer telemetry (Prometheus, OTLP, or partner CTX).
3) Cost guardrails
   - Set conservative quota/ratelimits for first 24h: initial quota = 30% of expected ramp unless customer requests otherwise.
   - Configure quota-protector webhook with emergency override and alerting to CS.
4) Communication plan
   - Publish cutover schedule and primary contacts to customer and internal stakeholders.
   - Pre-stage status page entries and templated customer messages.

Immediate post-cutover (0–4 hours) — stabilization window
-------------------------------------------------------
Action items (who / what / timeframe):
- 0–15 minutes: confirm API key acceptance and successful token exchange with 3 probe requests across customer regions. (Solutions Eng)
- 15–60 minutes: verify streaming and synchronous endpoints respond under expected concurrency. Check P50/P95 latency against target. (Platform Oncall)
- 30–90 minutes: ensure KV cache hit-rate (if configured) is within expected range; validate cold-start behavior and warmup logs. (Runtime team)
- 60–120 minutes: validate billing meter increments and initial usage appears in cost dashboards. (Finance Ops + CS)
- 120–240 minutes: review model-quality sentinel runs and manual spot-check 10-20 samples for hallucination/regression. (CS + Applied ML)

First 24 hours — defensive posture and telemetry escalation
--------------------------------------------------------
- Maintain conservative quotas and allow scheduled step-ups only after stability is proven for 4 consecutive 15-minute windows.
- Key dashboards to watch (links or names):
  - Tenant health overview: availability, total requests, token throughput
  - Runtime performance: GPU utilization, batching latency, KV cache metrics
  - Cost telemetry: tokens/sec, cost-per-token estimate, billing-meter lag
  - Model-quality sentinel: BLEU/ROUGE proxy metrics and classification/regression diffs
- Automated alerts to treat as P0 during first 24h:
  - Availability < 99% in a 5-minute window
  - Error rate > 2% sustained for 10 minutes
  - Token cost spike > 40% over expected baseline (10m moving avg)
  - Sudden drop in model-quality sentinel score > 15% from baseline
- Communications cadence: hourly status updates to customer by CSM for first 8 hours, then every 4 hours until 24h if stable.

24–72 hours — measured ramp and post-cutover validation
-----------------------------------------------------
- If the first 24 hours are stable, gradually increase quotas to planned ramp over the next 48 hours in pre-agreed increments (example: 30% -> 60% -> 100%). Only increase when the following are green for 30 minutes: latency P95, error rate, cost delta.
- Run a structured quality regression check at 48 hours using the agreed eval prompt set (report outputs to both CS and Applied ML).
- Conduct a billing reconciliation snapshot at 48 hours (Finance Ops) and confirm customers are seeing expected metering.

Rollback and emergency mitigations
---------------------------------
- Immediate rollback (trigger conditions): severe latency regression (P95 > 2x SLO for 30m), catastrophic error rate (>10%), or critical data-exposure alert.
- Rollback steps (Platform Oncall):
  1) Switch routing to the previous stable model/variant via traffic-split control (documented in deployment runbook).
  2) If tenant-level, trigger tenant quiesce and move to safe-fallback pool.
  3) Notify CSM and CS leadership; open incident in status tool and declare severity.
  4) If routing cannot be switched, throttle at the API gateway and enable degraded-mode responses with client-friendly error messages.
- Post-rollback postmortem: Rapid RCA within 24h (comprised of Platform, Runtime, Applied ML, CS). Follow with full P1 postmortem within 72h.

Escalation matrix and contact templates
--------------------------------------
- P0: Platform Oncall -> Platform Eng Lead -> Head of Platform -> CTO (pager escalation).
- P1: CS Lead -> Solutions Eng -> Platform Oncall.
- For each escalation, use templated messages: initial incident summary, impact to customer, mitigation steps in progress, ETA for next update.
- Example customer update (30m after detection):
  "Hello <CustomerContacts>, we detected elevated error rates affecting your inference traffic. Our oncall team has scoped the issue and is performing a controlled rollback to the previous model variant. We will follow up within 30 minutes with progress and impact details. We apologize for the disruption and are prioritizing restoration of service."

Operational controls and automation recipes
-----------------------------------------
- Auto-throttle policy: enable adaptive rate limiter for first 24h with action types: 429 throttle -> 503 degrade -> webhook to CS for manual override.
- Canary synthetic schedule: 1 probe every minute from three global vantage points, escalate after 3 consecutive failures.
- Quota protector: require two-step approval for quota increases >25% during first 72h. Approvals logged to audit trail.

Monitoring thresholds (recommended defaults)
-----------------------------------------
| Metric | Warning threshold | Critical threshold | Owner |
|--------|-------------------|--------------------|-------|
| Availability (tenant) | < 99.5% (5m) | < 99% (5m) | Platform Oncall |
| Error rate | > 1% (10m) | > 2% (10m) | Platform Oncall |
| P95 latency | > 1.5x SLO | > 2x SLO | Runtime Team |
| Token cost delta | > 20% | > 40% | Finance Ops |
| Model-quality sentinel | drop > 10% | drop > 15% | Applied ML |

Note: thresholds above should be calibrated to the customer's SLOs and contract.

Customer communications and status templates
------------------------------------------
- Pre-approved short-form status updates, incident acknowledgement, and recovery confirmation templates are stored in the shared CS templates library. Use the following minimum fields in every update: timestamp, impact (users/requests affected), mitigation steps, ETA, contact person, and link to incident page.

Post-72h wrap-up and QBR inputs
-------------------------------
- 72-hour deliverables:
  - Stability sign-off from Platform Oncall and CS (signed checklist).
  - Cost variance report vs. expected ramp with explanations for deltas.
  - Model-quality regression report and any corrective actions taken.
  - Customer debrief meeting scheduled within 5 business days; include QBR artifacts if onboarding impacted contractual metrics.
- Suggested QBR artifacts: time-series of tokens, cost per token, P50/P95 latency, error rate, sentinel evaluation scores, and a list of action items and owners.

Appendix A — Useful commands and snippets
----------------------------------------
- Check tenant routing: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/tenants/<TENANT_ID>/routing/status
- Force a traffic-split rollback (CLI example): redwoodctl route update --tenant <TENANT_ID> --from <NEW_VARIANT> --to <OLD_VARIANT> --force --reason "post-go-live rollback"
- Quota protector webhook payload (example):
  {
    "tenant_id": "<TENANT_ID>",
    "requested_increase_pct": 50,
    "requested_by": "csm@example.com"
  }

Appendix B — Related runbooks and docs
-------------------------------------
- Deployment rollback runbook (Platform)
- Canary simulation and auto-alert playbook (eng-platform)
- Billing reconciliation checklist (finance-and-legal)
- Customer onboarding handback and first-90-days ops guide (customer-success-and-support)

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-11-02: Created by Maya Chen.
- 2026-12-14: Added cost-control guardrails and webhook approval flow (reviewers: Ethan Morales).
- 2027-01-10: Revisions to monitoring thresholds and escalation templates (reviewers: Priya Singh, Samir Rao).

title: Tenant Stability Predictive Signals Runbook
content:
Purpose and scope
-----------------
This runbook defines the predictive signals, automated enrichment, and operational play for preventing tenant instability during the first 90 days after provisioning and at scale. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), SREs, Platform Engineers, and on-call Support. The playbook covers detection thresholds, triage steps, automated mitigations, customer communications, and post-incident follow-up templates.

Why this exists
-----------------
- Many early-stage incidents for enterprise tenants are preceded by measurable leading indicators (cache miss spikes, request token variance, route fan-out changes, model mismatch regressions).
- Acting on signals reduces severity, shortens time to mitigation, and reduces churn risk.
- Provides clear ownership and automation recipes to reduce manual toil.

Key definitions and roles
------------------------
- Tenant: A single enterprise customer tenant (dedicated or hosted).
- Predictive signal: A metric or composite metric that historically correlates with a stability degradation within 1–72 hours.
- Owner roles:
  - CSE (Customer Success Engineer): Primary customer-facing technical owner during onboarding and early life.
  - SRE: Operational owner responsible for infra/slo remediation and incident escalation.
  - Platform Eng: Owner for deployment/rollback actions and model routing policies.
  - Escalation Lead: Designated cross-functional lead for Sev2+ events.

SLOs referenced
---------------
- Tenant 99p tail latency (in-region): 500 ms target, 750 ms warning, 1200 ms Sev2 threshold
- 95p success rate (per-tenant, per-hour): 99.5% target, 99.0% warning, 97.0% Sev2 threshold
- KV cache hit rate (per-tenant, rolling 10m): 85% target, 70% warning, 50% Sev2 threshold

Priority predictive signals (ranked)
----------------------------------
1) KV cache miss rate sudden increase (delta > 20 pp within 10 minutes)
   - Why: Causes token re-computation and tail latency spikes.
   - Detection: rolling10m_kv_cache_miss_rate{tenant_id="$TENANT"} - alert if > 0.20 AND increase > 0.20 vs prev10m
   - PromQL example: (increase(kv_cache_misses_total{tenant="$TENANT"}[10m]) / increase(kv_cache_requests_total{tenant="$TENANT"}[10m])) > 0.2
2) Token-per-request (TPR) variance spike (p99 TPR > baseline * 1.6)
   - Why: Unexpected prompt/agent behavior or malformed client input causes cost and latency escalation.
   - Detection: compare p99(TPR, 30m) vs tenant baseline over 7d.
3) Model-variant mismatch errors (client requested variant not available + auto-fallback rate > 5%)
   - Why: Rollouts or capacity limits can trigger silent fallbacks and degrade quality.
4) Request fan-out increase (downstream retries causing multiple backend requests)
   - Why: Retries/backpressure loops amplify load; common during intermittent network issues.
5) 99p latency climb above warning threshold while success rate holds steady
   - Why: Often first sign of degraded hardware or contention (GPU saturation, NVMe throttling).

Alerting taxonomy and severity mapping
------------------------------------
- Predictive Warning: Single-signal threshold crossed (pager suppressed, Slack #cs-early-warning posted, ticket created).
- Predictive Sev3: Two related signals active for > 15m; page CSE and SRE (Slack @oncall and create incident record).
- Predictive Sev2: Any Sev2 SLO breached OR composite signal score > 0.8 for 30m. Pager escalation: SRE, Platform Eng, Escalation Lead.

Automated enrichment and alert payload content
--------------------------------------------
Every predictive alert must include:
- tenant_id, tenant_name, customer_tier (dedicated/hosted/private), region, active_model, model_variant, recent_deployments (IDs), recent_rollout_percentages, last_2h_kv_cache_rates, last_2h_tpr_p95_p99, last_5m_error_types, related_traces (URLs), recent_autoscale_events, current_capacity_pool_id
- Attach: 1) top 10 slow traces (sampled), 2) snapshot of the last successful and failed request payloads (redact PII), 3) CSV of per-route qps last 60m.

Initial automated remediation recipes (safe by default)
----------------------------------------------------
These automation recipes are executed by the Platform Eng runbook bot (redwood-ops). All actions are reversible.
1) Read-only route throttle (rate-limit non-critical routes)
   - Command: redwood-ops route throttle --tenant $TENANT --route-pattern "/api/v1/agents/*" --qps 10 --reason "auto-kvcache-miss-mitigation"
2) Increase KV cache warming priority for tenant (pin prefixes to warm pool)
   - Command: redwood-ops cache prioritize --tenant $TENANT --prefix-list-file recent-prefixes.csv
3) Temporary model routing to stable variant (no config changes to customer code)
   - Command: redwood-ops reroute --tenant $TENANT --from-variant v2 --to-variant v1 --duration 30m --annot "predictive-signal-failback"
4) Allocate burst capacity from dedicated reserve (if tenant is on Dedicated plan)
   - Command: redwood-ops capacity allocate --pool reserve-dedicated --tenant $TENANT --minutes 60

Triage play (ordered steps)
---------------------------
1) Receive alert and review automated enrichment (within 5m).
   - Who: CSE + oncall SRE (piggyback on Slack alert).
2) Validate signal: check KV cache hit/miss graphs, top traces, and recent deploy IDs.
   - Who: SRE.
3) If KV cache miss delta is confirmed, trigger cache prioritize recipe (automated or manual).
   - Who: Platform Eng or redwood-ops bot.
4) If TPR spike present, open Customer Insights ticket and ask CSM to validate recent prompt changes or agents.
   - Who: CSE + CSM.
5) If model-variant fallback is >5% or quality regression signalled, initiate controlled rollback to last known-good model variant and notify customer (see Customer Communication templates).
   - Who: Platform Eng + CSE.
6) If latency continues to degrade or success rate drops below 97%, escalate to Sev2 and follow incident process (page Execs per escalation matrix).

Customer communications (templates)
--------------------------------
Use these templates to reduce confusion and set expectations. Customize cadence depending on severity.
- Early-warning (Predictive Warning, not service impacting):
  Subject: Redwood – Early Notice: Observed increased request variance for your tenant
  Body: Hello <Customer Contact>, our monitoring has detected an increase in request complexity for tenant <tenant_name> that may cause degraded latency. We are applying targeted, reversible mitigations (cache warming and route throttles) and will update in 30 minutes. No action is required from your side unless you observed recent agent/prompt changes.
- Action required (Sev3):
  Subject: Redwood – Attention: Elevated errors affecting some requests
  Body: Hello <Customer Contact>, we are investigating elevated errors and have initiated mitigations. Please confirm whether you have recently modified prompts, added agents, or changed request fan-out. We will provide a status update within 20 minutes.
- Outage/Sev2:
  Subject: Redwood – Incident: Impacting availability for <tenant_name>
  Body: Hello <Customer Contact>, we are actively responding to an incident impacting request success for your tenant. Our teams (SRE, Platform, CSE) are engaged. We will provide ETA for restoration and next steps within 15 minutes. We will also give a post-incident summary after remediation.

Escalation matrix and contact list
----------------------------------
- Sev3: CSE -> SRE on-call -> Platform Eng (pager)
- Sev2: CSE -> SRE on-call -> Platform Eng -> Escalation Lead -> Head of Customer Success (page all)
- Pager channels: Ops PagerDuty, #cs-early-warning, #prod-incidents
- Contact list (on-call rota referenced from roster page):
  - CSE: oncall-cse@redwood.ai
  - SRE oncall: ops-oncall@redwood.ai
  - Platform Eng: platform-oncall@redwood.ai

Post-incident follow-up checklist
--------------------------------
- Short-term (within 24h):
  1) Confirm root cause hypothesis and mitigation timeline.
  2) Share initial incident summary with customer and internal stakeholders.
  3) Create postmortem ticket and assign owners.
- Long-term (within 14 days):
  1) Implement durable fixes (hotfix or config change).
  2) Add predictive signal tuning (threshold/weight) to the sentinel rules if noisy or missed.
  3) Schedule QBR discussion if customer impact > 2 days or repeat issues occurred within 90 days.

Runbook maintenance and signal governance
----------------------------------------
- Quarterly signal review: CS + SRE + Platform will review predictive signal performance (precision, recall, false positives).
- Owners must adjust thresholds and enrichment payload fields if root cause patterns change.
- New signals should be documented with: name, owner, detection query, historical precision/recall, and a test harness for simulation.

Telemetry and dashboards (reference)
-----------------------------------
- Dashboards: Tenant Stability Overview (per-tenant filter), KV Cache Heatmap, Model Variant Rollout Monitor, Route Fanout Explorer.
- Key Grafana panels and queries required for triage are linked from the alert (always include dashboard URL in the alert).
- Required metrics: kv_cache_misses_total, kv_cache_requests_total, request_tokens_per_request, request_latency_p50_p95_p99, request_success_count, model_variant_fallback_count, autoscale_events_total

Playbook automation safety and governance
----------------------------------------
- Auto-mitigations are enabled for enterprise tenants after a 7-day probation window and only if the customer has opted into "proactive mitigations" during onboarding.
- All automated actions are logged and must include: actor, reason, diff of the config change, and rollback command.
- For restricted tenants (high-security), auto actions are dry-run only and require manual approval by the customer contact.

Appendix A — PromQL examples and helper queries
------------------------------------------------
- KV cache miss rate (10m):
  increase(kv_cache_misses_total{tenant="$TENANT"}[10m]) / increase(kv_cache_requests_total{tenant="$TENANT"}[10m])
- p99 tokens per request (30m):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(tokens_per_request_bucket{tenant="$TENANT"}[30m])) by (le))
- Composite predictive score (example heuristic):
  0.5 * normalized_kv_miss_delta + 0.3 * normalized_tpr_p99_delta + 0.2 * model_fallback_rate

Appendix B — Example incident Slack message (copy template)
---------------------------------------------------------
- Channel: #cs-early-warning
- Message: @oncall SRE, predictive-warning for tenant *$TENANT* (KV miss + TPR spike). Enrichment: <link to alert>. Action: running cache-prioritize; if latency 99p > 900ms in 15m escalate to Sev2.

Appendix C — Post-incident report template (fill-in)
---------------------------------------------------
- Incident ID:
- Tenant:
- Timeline: detection -> mitigation -> resolved (timestamps)
- Root cause:
- Mitigation steps taken: automated and manual
- Customer impact: number of failed requests, duration, affected routes
- Action items (owner + due date)

Contacts and escalation URLs
--------------------------
- Redwoods Ops Console (internal): https://internal.redwood.ai/ops
- Incident ticketing (internal): https://issues.redwood.ai/browse/OPS
- On-call roster: https://people.redwood.ai/oncall-roster

Notes and versioning
--------------------
- Owner: Customer Success Engineering (Aisha Patel)
- Document version: 1.2
- Next review date: 2026-04-01

End of document

title: First 14-Day Entitlement and Remediation Runbook for Enterprise Go-Live
content:
Summary:

This runbook defines the operational checklist, entitlement validation, telemetry assertions, and remediation steps for the first 14 calendar days after an enterprise tenant goes live with Redwood. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), and oncall SRE/Platform engineers supporting dedicated and private deployments.

Purpose and scope:
- Ensure contractual entitlements and configuration match production behavior (rate limits, reserved capacity, feature flags).
- Verify baseline performance, cost signals, and functional correctness across the tenant surface (ingress, model routing, responses).
- Provide clear, actionable remediation steps for common failure modes observed during early adoption.
- Standardize communication templates for customer updates and internal escalation.

Quick reference SLOs to validate (tenant-visible):
- Token generation latency: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 400ms (hosted); for Dedicated SLA values negotiated per contract.
- Request success rate: >= 99.5% (5xx + client-error excluding rate-limit).
- Input-to-output throughput: within +/-25% of capacity reservation in first 14 days.
- Cost anomaly guardrail: daily spend drift <= 30% vs baseline estimate.

Prerequisites (pre-go-live verification):
1) Entitlement manifest uploaded to tenant account and validated (rate limits, model access, quota tiers).
2) Telemetry gatekeeper integration completed and test events flowing to telemetry index (tenant-metrics-collector).
3) Ingress and egress firewalls or peering verified (for Private deployments).
4) Canary traffic and synthetic journeys executed with pass criteria met (see Acceptance criteria).

Roles & ownership:
- Customer Success Lead: primary contact for customer communication and business escalation.
- Solutions Engineer: owns configuration validation, post-provision tuning, and acceptance tests.
- SRE oncall: owns production remediation activities, service-level alerts, and rollbacks.
- Model Ops: validates model correctness, quality drift, and rollout adjustments.

Entitlement and configuration validation checklist (first 48 hours):
1) Confirm rate-limiting policy applied to tenant: run endpoint check against /v1/usage/limits and compare to contract.
2) Validate model catalog access: attempt to instantiate the tenant-default model with SDK key and ensure model-router returns expected model hash.
3) Verify reserved capacity is reachable: confirm at least one GPU pool connection is established (service: gpu-allocator).
4) Confirm data plane encryption and KMS key access (for Private): kms: TestEncrypt API returns 200.
5) Check billing tags and cost attribution metadata are attached to tenant requests.

Telemetry assertions (queries and thresholds to run daily):
- Request success rate (PromQL):
  sum(rate(redwood_api_requests_total{tenant="TENANT_ID",code!~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_api_requests_total{tenant="TENANT_ID"}[5m])) > 0.995

- Request latency (p95):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="TENANT_ID"}[5m])) by (le)) < 0.4

- Token cost per 1k tokens (derived): daily_token_cost = sum(token_cost_daily{tenant="TENANT_ID"}) / (sum(tokens_generated_daily{tenant="TENANT_ID"})/1000)
  Alert if daily_token_cost > expected_unit_cost * 1.5

- Synthetic journey success (example curl):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TENANT_KEY}" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-7b", "input":"The capital of France is"}'
  Expected: 200, contains "Paris" or equivalent.

Acceptance criteria for steady state (end of day 14):
- All telemetry assertions pass for at least 72% of 12-hour windows during day 8–14.
- No more than two major incidents attributable to platform plumbing (networking, quota enforcement, ingress) during first 14 days.
- Customer-specified quality regression tests (prompt-set) maintain >= 90% pass rate versus baseline.

Runbook: top-level remediation flows (ordered by likelihood)

1) High error rate (5xx spikes)
- Observable signals: 5xx spike in redwood_api_requests_total, sudden p95 latency surge, GPU pool utilization near 100%.
- Immediate steps (SRE oncall):
  a) Silence non-actionable alerts and annotate incident channel (#cs-tenant-TENANTID) with initial findings.
  b) Check gpu-allocator and model-router health: kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=gpu-allocator; kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-router\  c) If GPU pool OOMs or ejects pods, remove tenant from routing (via control plane: POST /admin/route/remove-tenant) and failover to a compatible fallback model (see control-plane runbook snippet).
  d) If ingress NLB shows connection errors, run tcpdump on ingress gateway and escalate to network team.
- Customer comms template: "We've detected elevated error rates affecting your tenant. We've removed traffic from the impacted pool while we investigate; your traffic is being routed to a fallback model to preserve availability. Expected ETA: 30–90 minutes."

2) Latency regressions with normal error rate
- Signals: p95 latency increased > 2x baseline while success rate remains > 99%.
- Remediation (SE + SRE):
  a) Check continuous batching and KV cache hit rate stats: query tenant_kvcache_hit_ratio{tenant="TENANT_ID"}[10m]
  b) If cache miss spike: warm cache by replaying synthetic prefix requests (see synthetic warmup script below).
  c) If batching latency high: adjust max_batch_size for tenant via tenant config API and schedule a controlled scaling of worker replicas.

Synthetic warmup script (example):
```
for i in {1..100}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TENANT_KEY}" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"tenant-default","input":"Warmup prompt '$i'"}' >/dev/null &
done
wait
```

3) Unexpected quality regressions (model output accuracy or hallucinations)
- Signals: customer report, failing prompt-set evals, sudden divergence in evaluation scores in eval-harness.
- Remediation (Model Ops + SE):
  a) Re-run prompt-set locally against model hash reported in runtime logs.
  b) If regression confirmed, initiate model rollback to prior model hash using the rollout API and notify customer.
  c) Open a model-regression ticket with Research with full prompt-set + failure examples.

4) Cost surge (unexpected spend)
- Signals: daily_token_cost spike, unexpected embedding indexing runs, long-running batch jobs attributed to tenant.
- Remediation (CS + FinOps + SE):
  a) Temporarily restrict tenant concurrency or reduce max_tokens and max_concurrent requests via entitlement config.
  b) If chargeback rules apply, create a cost hold and notify billing.
  c) Analyze request traces to identify runaway loops or bots. Provide sample request IDs to customer.

Escalation matrix (when to escalate to engineering and execs):
- Level 1 (CS + SE): service-impacting but contained, ETA < 4 hours.
- Level 2 (SRE + Model Ops): multi-region impact or stuck routing, ETA < 8 hours.
- Level 3 (VP-eng + Legal + Customer Exec): prolonged outage > 8 hours, data exposure, contract breach risk.

Internal communication templates (use in incident channel and customer emails):
- Initial: "We have observed an operational issue affecting your service. We are investigating and have put temporary mitigations in place. We will provide an update within 30 minutes."
- Update: "Root cause update: [summary]. Current impact: [number of affected requests / %]. Next action: [action]. ETA: [time window]."
- Resolution: "The issue is resolved. Root cause: [summary]. Remediation steps taken: [list]. Postmortem ETA: [date/time]."

Checklist: daily run cadence (days 0–14):
- Day 0–2: entitlement checks, basic telemetry smoke tests, synthetic journeys every 2 hours, billing tag verification.
- Day 3–7: add expanded prompt-set runs, monitor for anomalies in quality and cost, weekly SE tuning session.
- Day 8–14: stability acceptance tests, QBR prep package assembled for customer (see QBR signals below).

QBR signals to prepare for week 2 review (deliverable list):
- Telemetry summary: request volume, latency curves (p50/p95), error rate, token cost per 1k tokens.
- Prompt-set evaluation results (pass/fail counts and examples).
- Entitlement verification report (actual vs contracted limits).
- Incidents and remediation log (timeline, impact, and customer-facing notes).
- Recommended changes: capacity, batching, or model variant suggestions.

Related runbooks & links:
- tenant-observability-contract-lifecycle (link internal)
- canary-simulation-and-auto-alert-playbook (link internal)
- model-switchover-fallback-triage-runbook (link internal)

Appendix: common commands and API snippets
- Validate entitlement API:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_KEY}" https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/tenants/TENANT_ID/entitlements

- Remove tenant from pool (control-plane):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_KEY}" -d '{"tenant":"TENANT_ID","action":"remove_from_pool"}' https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/admin/route

- Rollback model (example):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_KEY}" -d '{"tenant":"TENANT_ID","route":"default","model_hash":"<previous_hash>"}' https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/admin/rollout

Concluding notes:
This runbook is iterative. During onboarding of new enterprise tenants, please capture any new failure modes in the ticket stub below and propose additions to this document. Maintain a record of all customer-facing messages in the tenant's go-live folder for audit and QBR preparation.

Audit ticket stub (copy into JIRA/Ticket):
- Tenant: TENANT_ID
- Onboarded by: <CS lead>
- Start date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Key incidents (summary, timestamps, owner)
- Actions taken and follow-ups
- Postmortem link (if applicable)

title: Model Switchover & Fallback: Triage Runbook for Enterprise Support
content:
Summary
-------
This runbook describes the operational triage, model switchover, and fallback procedures to use during degraded model behavior, spike latency, or model availability loss for enterprise customers (Dedicated or Private). It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), SRE on-call, and Solutions Engineers performing operational support during a customer-facing incident.

When to use this runbook
-----------------------
Use this document when a customer reports one or more of the following:
- Significant increase in token latency (P95 or P99) for generation/chat endpoints beyond SLA thresholds.
- Consistent quality regressions or hallucinations after a model rollout.
- Errors related to model runtime (kernel OOMs, model load failures, KV cache corruption).
- Automatic fallback triggered by the routing layer and impacting request success rate.

Preconditions and prerequisites
-------------------------------
Before initiating switchover/fallback:
1. Confirm access: ensure you have redwood-console access and active SSH to the customer's Dedicated/private control plane (if applicable).
2. Identify customer configuration: model pinned version, route policy, cache keys, and any custom prehooks. See the customer’s route config in the Console: Routes > {customer} > {route-id}.
3. Check current SLOs and active incidents on status.redwood-internal: SLOs for this customer are typically:
   - Latency SLO: P95 < 800ms (hosted) / P95 < 1200ms (dedicated)
   - Error rate SLO: < 1% for 5m window
4. Notify stakeholders: CSE, SRE on-call, Account Manager (AM), and Product (if model regression suspected).

Ownership matrix
----------------
- CSE: customer communication, coordination, and runbook ops.
- SRE: runtime health checks, performing switchover commands, monitoring rollback safety.
- Solutions Eng: investigate prompt/regression and advise model/quantization changes.
- Product/Model Ops: invoked for suspected model quality regressions (A/B test data required).

Immediate triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
--------------------------------------------
1. Capture symptoms: collect sample requests/responses, timestamps, route-id, model name/version, and offtake rate.
2. Verify health: run quick health checks. Run from support workstation:
   - curl -sS -X GET "https://console.redwood/api/internal/health/{route-id}" | jq
   - Check runtime status: runbook-utils report-runtime {route-id} 
3. Confirm scope: is the issue per-customer, per-region, or global? Check metric dashboards:
   - Customer route dashboard: /console/dash/{route-id} > Last 60m
   - Global model healthboard: /console/dash/models/{model}"

(CONTINUED)
Detailed step-by-step switchover procedure
------------------------------------------
Use these steps to switch an affected route to a fallback model variant. Do not start without notifying AM & SRE.

1) Prepare fallback model variant
   - Identify approved fallback: look up the customer’s allowed model set in Console > Routes > {route-id} > "allowed_models". Typical fallback names: "gpt-like-3.5-v2-quant", "redwood-llm-slim-1.1".
   - Validate model binary: ensure the candidate is loaded on the target cluster by running: 
     rctl --cluster {cluster-name} list-models | grep {fallback-model}
2) Quiesce cache-sensitive requests (if applicable)
   - If prefix caching is active, enable read-only fallback for the route to avoid cache corruption: 
     rctl routes update {route-id} --cache-mode read-only --reason "fallback triggger"
3) Execute model switchover (can be automated via Console or CLI)
   - Console quick path: Routes > {route-id} > Edit > Model > Select {fallback-model} > Save & Canary 5% for 5 minutes.
   - CLI safe command (recommended for full automation):
     rctl routes rollout --route {route-id} --to {fallback-model} --strategy canary --canary-size 0.05 --canary-duration 300
4) Observe canary metrics (5–10 minutes)
   - Monitor: request latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, success rate, model output quality sample set.
   - Success criteria to promote: latency back within SLO AND error rate drop below 1% for 10m.
5) Promote or rollback
   - Promote: rctl routes rollout --route {route-id} --promote
   - Rollback: rctl routes rollback --route {route-id} --to {previous-model} --force --reason "canary-fail"

Safety & rollback considerations
--------------------------------
- Never promote if model outputs fail basic safety filters (see safety filter logs).
- If fallback increases hallucinations or changes customer SLA-significant output: escalate to Product immediately and revert to pinned model with controlled throttling.
- If KV cache integrity is suspect, perform cache flush for the route: 
  rctl cache flush --route {route-id} --confirm

Quick troubleshooting checklist (error classes)
------------------------------------------------
- High latency + increased tail tokens: check batching policies and kernel saturation.
  - Commands: ssh to runtime node and run: top/gpu-top; /usr/local/bin/runtime-inspect --tail-queue
- OOMs during model load: check model quantization variant and node free memory. If OOM, switch to smaller quantized variant.
- Route-level 5xx errors: check router-service logs for 502/504 patterns: 
  - kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/router-service --since=10m | grep "{route-id}" | head

Thresholds & quick reference table
----------------------------------
(Displayed as pipe table for quick reference)
| Metric | Alert threshold | Immediate action | Owner |
| Latency P95 | > 2x SLO for 5m | Initiate canary to fallback | SRE/CSE |
| Error rate | >= 2% for 5m | Immediate route canary to fallback | SRE |
| Model load failures | any model-load-failure | Disable autoscale, perform manual load | SRE + Model Ops |
| Safety filter blocks | > 0.5% of responses | Hold promotion, escalate to Product | Product/CSE |

Customer communication templates (short)
---------------------------------------
Use these statements in the first customer message while you triage:
- Acknowledgement: "We’ve received your report and are triaging with our SRE and Model Ops teams. We will update within 15 minutes with mitigation steps."
- During switchover: "We are routing a small portion of traffic to an alternate model variant to stabilize latency while we investigate. You may see minor differences in responses for a short period."
- Post-incident: Provide a short summary with root cause (if known), actions taken, and next steps (postmortem ETA).

Escalation matrix
------------------
1. SRE on-call (primary) — page: SRE-oncall@pagerduty — 0–15m
2. Model Ops (secondary) — page: model-ops@pagerduty — 15–60m
3. Product (for quality regressions) — @product-lead — 15–24h
4. Exec/Legal (if customer SLA breach & contractual exposure) — contact via AM — within 24h

Post-incident actions and RCA requirements
-----------------------------------------
- Required deliverables:
  1. Initial incident summary (within 4h) with timeline and mitigation.
  2. Full RCA (within 72h) including logs, canary graphs, samples of affected requests/responses, and suggested preventative measures.
  3. Action items with owners and deadlines (e.g., model rollback automation, expanded canary window).
- Add incident to customer QBR: include impact, duration, customer-reported severity, and improvements planned.

Monitoring playbook (what to watch)
-----------------------------------
- Dashboards to open:
  - Console > Dashboards > Route Overview ({route-id})
  - Console > Dashboards > Model Healthboard ({model})
  - Grafana: redwood/request-latency, redwood/error-rate, redwood/model-loads
- Logs: router-service, runtime-agent, model-loader, safety-filter
- Alerting channels: #incidents, SRE-pagerduty, CSE-team slack channel

Related artifacts & links
-------------------------
- Route config schema: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/route-config-schema
- Canary rollout CLI reference: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/rollout-cli-usage
- Model approval list (customer-specific): Console > Customers > {customer-id} > Approved Models

Appendix: sample CLI snippets
----------------------------
1) Start a 5% canary to fallback model: 
   rctl routes rollout --route r-abc123 --to redwood-llm-slim-1.1 --strategy canary --canary-size 0.05 --canary-duration 300 --reason "support-triage-2026-01-12"
2) Promote canary after success:
   rctl routes rollout --route r-abc123 --promote
3) Rollback to previous model immediately:
   rctl routes rollback --route r-abc123 --to redwood-llm-recent-3.0 --force --reason "rollback-on-failed-canary"

Contact list (internal)
-----------------------
- CSE on-call: cse-oncall@redwood.com
- SRE on-call: sre-oncall@redwood.com
- Model Ops: model-ops@redwood.com

Document change log
--------------------
- 2025-11-02: Created by Elena Martinez (initial draft).
- 2025-12-08: Reviewed by Rajesh Iyer; added cache-flush safety guidance.
- 2026-01-12: Published with updated thresholds and CLI examples (Maya Chen).

title: Tenant Decommission & Data Erasure Certification Playbook
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the operational process, verification steps, and evidence collection required to safely decommission a tenant and produce a Data Erasure Certification for enterprise customers. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), Account Security leads, and the Privacy Compliance team.

Scope:
- Applies to all Dedicated and Private tenants (reserved capacity or VPC/on-prem) where a customer requests a full tenant decommission and verified data purge.
- Excludes transient test tenants created under internal dev projects.
- Covers: configuration metadata, KV caches, embedding indices, logs and telemetry tied to tenant IDs, backups/snapshots, and any customer-managed on-prem artifacts we control.

Goals:
- Ensure data belonging to a tenant is irrecoverably deleted from all Redwood-managed storage within agreed SLA windows.
- Produce a signed Data Erasure Certification (PDF) including verification artifacts suitable for customer audit.
- Provide a clear rollback and exception path if deletion interferes with legal holds, active billing disputes, or regulatory constraints.

Prerequisites and gating checks (Pre-decommission):
1) Confirm formal request: must come from the customer’s authorized admin contact or a signed CSM request form. Attach request to ticket.
2) Confirm account state: Tenant must be quiesced for at least 48 hours unless an accelerated erase is explicitly authorized by Legal.
3) Verify no active legal holds or retention policies: Check Legal/Evidence mailbox and related JIRA signals.
4) Snapshot list: Enumerate all active snapshots, backups, and object storage buckets that contain tenant data.
5) Billing & contracts: Finance must sign off that invoicing and reconciliations are complete, or place a hold if a dispute exists.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Customer Success Engineer (CSE): owner of the decommission process, customer comms, and final handoff of the certification.
- SRE / Infra Owner: executes deletion commands, validates low-level storage and KV cache removal, updates runbook evidence.
- Privacy & Compliance: reviews evidence, prepares certification language, and signs final PDF.
- Account Security Lead: verifies no remaining credentials, SSH keys, certificates, or cross-tenant links.
- Finance: confirms final billing state.

High-level decommission checklist (stepwise):
1) Prepare: Create a decommission incident ticket (PREFIX: DECOM-{tenant_id}) and add all owners and reviewers. Attach customer request and any hold flags.
2) Quiesce: Disable API keys, revoke incoming webhooks, and switch routing policy to reject new traffic. Record timestamps.
3) Export minimal retention artefacts (if requested): generate requested audit logs and export them to a customer-managed bucket; document the export SHA256.
4) Snapshot verification: Ensure latest snapshot is stored in immutable archive (if contractually required). Note location and checksum.
5) Delete operational artifacts (order matters):
   a) Revoke and purge tenant IAM roles and tokens.
   b) Remove routing and DNS entries.
   c) Stop and delete serving instances (record instance IDs).
   d) Wipe KV caches and in-memory stores with secure-delete commands.
   e) Delete embedding indices and associated vector DB partitions.
   f) Remove object storage buckets and blobs.
   g) Delete logs and telemetry for tenant IDs (respecting retention law exceptions).
6) Cease backups: ensure backup jobs no longer include tenant and delete retained backup files.
7) Final storage sweep: run storage-level compliance scan to find orphaned objects or references.
8) Evidence collection: collect command outputs, checksums, S3 / object delete receipts, and storage listings that show 404/NotFound.
9) Generate Draft Certification: Privacy prepares draft certification with attached evidence links.
10) Sign-off: Legal/Privacy and Finance must approve. Once approved, deliver signed PDF to customer via secure channel and close the decommission ticket.

Commands and verification examples (examples - replace with tenant values):
- Revoke API keys (CLI): redwood-cli tenants revoke-keys --tenant-id tenant-123 --force
- KV cache wipe (runbook snippet): curl -X POST https://kv.internal.redwood/delete-namespace -d '{"tenant":"tenant-123","mode":"secure"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>'
- Object store delete + verification (bash):
  aws s3 rm s3://redwood-tenants/tenant-123 --recursive && aws s3 ls s3://redwood-tenants/tenant-123 || echo "Bucket not found"
- Snapshot checksum (example): sha256sum tenant-123-snapshot-20260101.tar.gz > snapshot.sha256

Evidence packaging requirements:
- Include: ticket export, customer request, command stdout logs (with timestamps), storage deletion receipts, backup job logs, checksum files, and the pre-decommission inventory.
- Redact: Do not include PII of Redwood employees in delivered artifacts. Replace internal ticket IDs with redacted tokens when necessary.
- Evidence TTL: Internal evidence must be retained in the audited evidence bucket for 2 years (Compliance mandate).

Verification checklist (to be ticked in ticket):
- [ ] Customer request attached and validated against admin contact.
- [ ] Quiesce actions completed and timestamped.
- [ ] All API keys and webhooks revoked.
- [ ] Embedding indices removed and index count = 0.
- [ ] Object storage bucket returns NotFound.
- [ ] Backups and snapshots removed or archived as per contract.
- [ ] KV cache namespace removed and confirmed.
- [ ] Logs trimmed or removed respecting legal holds.
- [ ] Privacy & Legal sign-off obtained.
- [ ] Signed Data Erasure Certification produced and delivered.

Rollback and exceptions:
- Legal Hold: If a legal hold is identified mid-process, immediately pause deletion steps and notify Legal and the customer. Rehydrate any removed snapshots from immutable archive if possible.
- Accidental deletion: If accidental deletion is detected within the retention window, follow the Incident Recovery Runbook (link in related_pages) and escalate to SRE Lead and CTO on-call.
- Customer Revocation: Customer may revoke the decommission within the quiesce window if approved; in that case, restore routing and reactivate keys following the Tenant Reactivation checklist.

Communication templates (summary snippets to use in ticket and email):
- Initial acknowledgement to customer: "We have received your decommission request. The tenant has been scheduled for quiesce on {date}. Expected completion: {date + X business days}. We will provide a Data Erasure Certification when the process completes."
- Final delivery message: "Attached is your Data Erasure Certification for tenant {tenant_id}. This confirms Redwood-managed artifacts have been erased per the contract. Contact your CSM with any audit questions."

Audit and certification content (what we include in the PDF):
- Statement of scope (tenant id, dates, artifacts included/excluded).
- Listing of deleted artifact types and counts (buckets deleted, indices removed, instances terminated).
- Verification artifacts (checksums, deletion receipts, ticket references).
- Signatures: Privacy & Compliance lead + CSE.
- Optional: a notarized stamp if requested and pre-approved by Legal (adds 3-7 business days).

Operational metrics and SLAs for decommission requests:
- Standard FIFO SLA: 10 business days from validated request to certified completion.
- Accelerated SLA: 48–96 hours (requires signed acceleration waiver from customer and Legal approval).
- Verification SLA: Privacy has 5 business days to review and sign evidence once uploaded.

Automation and tools:
- Decommission Orchestrator (internal service): Use the decommission orchestration UI for walk-through steps and to collect structured evidence. If the orchestrator is unavailable, follow the manual runbook steps above.
- Evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/decom/tenant-{tenant_id}/{ticket_id}/
- Template generator: internal tool that assembles evidence links into the draft certification.

Post-decommission monitoring (30 days):
- Watch for retroactive billing anomalies or customer follow-ups. Set a 30-day ticket cooling period where CSE monitors any reappearance of tenant artifacts.
- Run a weekly orphan-object scan for the tenant id for 4 weeks post-deletion and archive results into the ticket.

Appendices:
A) Example minimal Data Erasure Certification language (copy into PDF generator):
"Redwood Inference certifies that, as of {date}, Redwood-managed storage and runtime artifacts associated with tenant {tenant_id} were deleted and validated in accordance with the contract and Redwood internal data retention policies. Evidence artifacts are appended/linked in this certification. Signed: {PrivacyLead}, {CSEName}."

B) Quick checklist for small tenants (one-liner):
1) Verify request -> 2) Revoke keys -> 3) Delete bucket -> 4) Remove indices -> 5) Deliver certification.

C) Emergency contacts:
- Customer Success Incident Pager: +1-555-0123 (internal)
- Privacy & Compliance Slack: #privacy-compliance (tag @privacy-lead)
- SRE On-call: see internal roster or PagerDuty schedule

Change log:
- 2026-01-12: Playbook created by Aisha Raman.
- 2026-01-25: Added accelerated SLA flow and notarization note (review by Legal).
- 2026-02-10: Clarified evidence TTL and added orphan-object weekly-scan requirement (reviewers: Diego Morales, Priya Nair).

Related references and links:
- Tenant quiesce runbook: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/scheduled-tenant-quiesce-and-safe-failback-playbook-2026
- Data residency & retention policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/policy-2025
- Incident recovery runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/incident-recovery-2025

Owner and contact:
- Playbook owner: Aisha Raman (CSE Lead) - aisha.r@redwood.ai
- Privacy reviewer: Priya Nair - priya.n@redwood.ai
- SRE liaison: Diego Morales - diego.m@redwood.ai

title: Traffic smoothing, quiet-hours and tenant notification playbook
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines operator and customer-facing procedures for smoothing traffic during predictable and ad-hoc tenant burst events. It covers automatic quiet-hours smoothing, tenant-level throttling/fan-out controls, notification templates, escalation ladders, telemetry queries, and rollback guidance. The goal is to preserve platform SLOs (latency/availability) while protecting customer experience and cost boundaries.

When to use this playbook:

- Planned quiet-hours or maintenance windows where we will intentionally reduce tenant throughput to conserve capacity or schedule upgrades.
- Rapid tenant traffic bursts (spikes in requests or tokens) that threaten SLOs for other tenants.
- Customer-requested temporary throttle during migration/backfill events.
- As a standard operating response prior to capacity augmentation or emergency capacity scaling.

Key objectives:

1) Maintain 99th percentile p95 token latency SLOs and >99.9% availability for host-level API endpoints.
2) Minimize customer-facing error rate and provide clear, timely communication.
3) Apply smoothing/throttles with least possible disruption using automated, observable controls.

Ownership and roles:

- Primary owner: Customer Success Operations (Customer Success) — coordinates customer comms, approves manual throttles.
- Secondary owner: Platform SRE (Engineering) — implements rate-limiter changes, monitors platform metrics, executes emergency capacity procedures.
- Response lead (oncall): person listed on the current oncall rota for Eng SRE.

Preconditions / prerequisites:

- Tenant must have telemetry forwarding enabled (tenant.metrics and tenant.traces).
- Tenant-specific quota and throttle policies must exist in the RateLimit Service (service: rate-limit-svc).
- Customer Success must have an agreed contact from the tenant (email + pager for enterprise).

SLOs and thresholds (operational):

| Metric | Threshold (trigger) | Severity | Initial action | Escalation timer |
|-------|---------------------:|----------|----------------|------------------|
| p95 token latency (global) | > 1.8x baseline for 3 consecutive minutes | Sev-2 | Auto-smooth tenants contributing >30% load | 10 min -> SRE oncall |
| error rate (5xx >= host) | >0.5% absolute increase over baseline (5 min) | Sev-1 | Immediate rollback of recent config + alert | 5 min -> Incident page |
| requests-per-min per-tenant | > 10x baseline sustained 2 min | Sev-3 | Apply per-tenant burst windowing + backpressure | 15 min -> CS PD notification |

Automated controls and tuning knobs:

- Quiet-hours smoothing: schedule-based traffic shaping that lowers max active concurrent requests by x% (default 30%) during predefined windows. Config stored as YAML in config-store:

  examples: &config-example
  - tenant_selector: "label:batching=true"
    window: "23:00-05:00 UTC"
    concurrency_limit_pct: 70
    burst_window_seconds: 60

- Tenant burst windowing: dynamic token-bucket policy applied per-API key that allows short bursts but enforces an average over a sliding 60s window.

- Graceful response headers: when rate-limited, return 429 with headers: Retry-After, X-Redwood-Limit, X-Redwood-Remaining, X-Redwood-Quota-Reset. Include optional human-readable JSON in body with guidance on next steps.

Telemetry & queries (examples):

- Grafana / Prometheus:
  - redwood.requests_total{tenant_id=~"<TENANT>"}
  - redwood.tokens_per_minute{tenant_id=~"<TENANT>"}
  - redwood.p95_token_latency{region="us-west-2"}
  - redwood.5xx_rate{host="api.redwood.com"}

- Example PromQL:
  avg_over_time(redwood.tokens_per_minute{tenant_id=~"T123"}[2m]) > 10 * avg_over_time(redwood.tokens_per_minute{tenant_id=~"T123"}[1h])

Operational runbook (step-by-step):

1) Detect: automated alert or CS report. Confirm tenant_id(s), time window, and affected routes.
2) Quick triage (5 min): verify telemetry, check deploys in last 30 min (ci-cd activity), confirm whether traffic is legitimate (backfill / scheduled job).
3) Apply automated smoothing if hit threshold: enable "quiet-hours smoothing" for tenant selector or apply per-tenant rate-limit override. Use CLI:

  # apply per-tenant override (example)
  rwctl rate-limit set --tenant T123 --max-rps 250 --burst 500 --window 60s --reason "auto-smoothing-trigger-2027-02-15"

4) Notify customer: send templated email and optional in-console banner (see templates below). Mark the change in incident tracker with runbook link.
5) Monitor 0-30 minutes: watch p95 latency, 5xx rate, and tenant error rates. If metrics improve, prepare staged rollback: reduce throttle by 20% every 10 minutes until normal.

Escalation matrix and timers:

- If p95 latency not improved after 15 minutes -> escalate to Eng SRE oncall (page) and SRE escalation Slack channel (#sre-incident).
- If 5xx error rate increases after smoothing -> immediate rollback and incident page start.
- If customer reports data loss or persistent functional errors -> raise Sev-1 and schedule cross-team warroom.

Customer communications (templates):

- In-console banner (short):
  "We are applying temporary traffic smoothing to maintain platform performance during a high-volume event. Your requests may be delayed or throttled. We will update you within 30 minutes. Contact support@redwood.ai for urgent concerns."

- Email template (first notification):
  Subject: Temporary traffic smoothing active for your Redwood tenant

  Hello <Customer Name>,

  We detected a high-volume traffic event affecting your Redwood tenant (ID: <TID>). To maintain platform stability, we've temporarily limited peak throughput for your tenant. This is a protective measure — your data is not at risk. Expected impact: brief 429s for short bursts and up-to-30s increased latency for long requests.

  What we are doing: applying per-tenant smoothing, monitoring performance, and escalating if needed.

  ETA for update: 30 minutes. Contact: <CS rep + pager>.

  Regards,
  Redwood Support

- Follow-up template (when resolved):
  Subject: Traffic smoothing removed — event resolved

  Hello <Customer Name>,

  The temporary smoothing has been removed and your normal throughput limits restored. Incident runbook: <link>. If you observed any functional problems, please reply and we will investigate further.

Configuration table (required fields for a scheduled quiet-hours rule):

| Field | Type | Description | Example | Required |
|-------|------|-------------|---------|----------:|
| rule_id | string | Unique rule identifier | quiet-window-batch | yes |
| tenant_selector | string | Selector expression (labels or tenant_id) | label:batching=true | yes |
| window | string | Time window in UTC | 23:00-05:00 | yes |
| concurrency_limit_pct | integer | Percent of normal concurrency to allow | 70 | yes |
| burst_window_seconds | integer | Sliding window for burst smoothing | 60 | no |
| owner | string | Team/owner to notify | customer-success | yes |

Rollback guidance:

- If smoothing causes unacceptable customer errors, immediately remove rule and clear rate-limit overrides using rwctl:

  rwctl rate-limit delete --tenant T123 --reason "rollback-due-to-5xx-2027-02-15"

- If rollback triggers platform instability, revert to platform-wide safe-mode throttle (config: global.safe_mode_pct = 50) and open incident page.

Post-incident actions and reporting:

1) Run a 72-hour retrospective: who acted, what thresholds fired, and whether automation behaved as expected.
2) Produce a short incident digest for the Customer (one-pager) within 48 hours.
3) Update the tenant onboarding checklist with any gap identified (telemetry, contact, agreed quiet-hours).

Observability checklist (what to capture):

- Alert triggers and timestamps.
- rwctl commands executed (audit log).
- Grafana snapshot links and PromQL used.
- Customer comms artifacts (email, banner text).

Related runbooks and docs:

- Capacity surge and degraded throughput playbook (eng/sre)
- Tenant onboarding acceptance testing (CS)
- Rate limit service configuration guide (infra)

Appendix A — Example rate-limit YAML snippet:

  - rule_id: "quiet-window-batch-2027"
    tenant_selector: "label:batching=true"
    window: "23:00-05:00"
    concurrency_limit_pct: 70
    burst_window_seconds: 60
    owner: "customer-success"

Appendix B — Short checklist for CS before applying manual throttle:

1) Confirm authorized contact and approval in CRM.
2) Validate telemetry and rule selector matches intended workload.
3) Log expected duration and rollback criteria to incident tracker.
4) Send pre-action notice to customer.

Document history and change log:

- 2026-11-10: Created by Maya Chen (initial draft).
- 2027-01-11: Added automated CLI examples and telemetry PromQL — reviewer: Ravi Patel.
- 2027-02-15: Finalized templates and escalation timers — reviewer: Elena Gómez.

title: Automated Tenant Incident Orchestration and Remediation Playbook
content:
Overview

This playbook documents the end-to-end automated orchestration and manual handoff procedures used by Redwood Customer Success and Support to detect, remediate, and verify tenant-level incidents with minimal customer impact. It is intended for use during production incidents that affect a single tenant or a small cohort of tenants (not full platform outages). The goal is to resolve service-impacting problems within the tenant SLO window or apply safe fallbacks that preserve availability while engineering diagnoses root causes.

When to use this playbook

- Tenant-facing degradation detected by telemetry (latency, errors, KV-cache regressions, model-quality signals).
- Sudden unit-cost spikes or quota exhaustion that threaten availability.
- Failed automated model upgrade rollouts that affect a tenant.
- Routing and network flakiness isolated to a customer’s region or private deployment link.

Scope and ownership

- Primary owner: Customer Success (tenant stability squad).
- Secondary owner: Eng-Platform (runtime orchestration).
- On-call escalation: Dedicated SRE for the affected region.
- This playbook covers: detection signals, enrichment, automated remediation actions, verification tests, escalation thresholds, and post-incident RCA inputs.

Key SLOs and thresholds (tenant-level)

- Availability: 99.9% (per-tenant request success, 5xx < 0.1%).
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for short text generation (<= 256 tokens); alert if p95 increases by >20% over baseline for 5 minutes.
- Cost: unit-token cost deviation > 40% triggers investigation.
- KV-cache hit-rate: fall below 70% sustained for 3 minutes -> alert.

Automated detection signals (examples)

- Telemetry rule: p95_latency_tenant > baseline * 1.2 for 5m.
- Error spike: 5xx_rate_tenant > 0.5% sustained for 3m.
- Token-cost spike: token_cost_rate per-minute increases > 40%.
- Model-quality regressions: eval-alerts flagged by tenant’s eval set (similarity loss or hallucination metric).
- Networking: TLS handshake failure rate or connection resets > 1% absolute.

Enrichment pipeline (what automation performs before action)

1. Correlate tenant signals with model, route, and infra pool (tags: model_id, route_id, pool_id).
2. Attach last 2 minutes of request traces (sampled).
3. Run quick synthetic check against tenant route (see Verification tests).
4. Generate incident stub in incident system with priority recommendation and suggested remediation.

Automated remediation actions (ordered by safety)

- Action A: Tenant read-only traffic shaping for non-critical routes
  - Purpose: reduce cost and limit degradation scope while preserving critical API calls.
  - Command example: curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood.example/v1/tenants/T-123/traffic-shape -d '{"mode":"critical-only","expiry":"15m"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'

- Action B: Switch tenant routing policy to fallback model variant
  - Purpose: move traffic to a compatible smaller/quantized model to restore latency and availability.
  - Safe variants must be pre-approved in tenant config.
  - CLI example: rwdctl tenants route-set --tenant T-123 --route fallback --model redwood/small-2b-q4f

- Action C: Promote tenant to reserved capacity (burst)
  - Purpose: temporary capacity allocation from dedicated pools. Requires entitlement check.
  - API example: POST /ops/tenants/T-123/reserve-capacity {"pool":"dedicated-gnx-1","duration":"30m"}

- Action D: KV cache warm-up/restore script
  - Purpose: rehydrate prefix cache to reduce cold-start token costs and latency.
  - Script snippet:
    #!/bin/bash
    REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
    python tools/rehydrate_cache.py --tenant T-123 --sample-size 500

- Action E: Quiesce long-running background jobs (embedding indexes, reindexes)
  - Purpose: stop noisy background workloads temporarily to reduce contention.
  - Note: notify customer success and log action.

Automated decision logic (simplified)

- If p95_latency > 20% and 5xx_rate < 0.5% -> run cache-warmup + synthetic test.
- If 5xx_rate >= 0.5% -> immediate route switch to fallback model and notify SRE.
- If token_cost_spike && cost deviation > 40% -> apply traffic-shape (critical-only) and schedule FinOps review.

Runbook: Incident lifecycle (detailed steps)

1) Detection and enrichment (automated)
   - Telemetry rule fires -> enrichment workflow runs and creates incident stub.
   - System posts summary in #cs-ops and creates a PagerDuty alert if priority >= P2.

2) Immediate automated remediation (0-5 minutes)
   - Orchestration engine evaluates tenant policy and executes the highest-safety remediation allowed.
   - Record every action with an audit log and create reversible change unit.

3) Verification (5-15 minutes)
   - Automated synthetic verification executes the tenant’s smoke tests and records p50/p95, error-rate, and a small token-cost sample.
   - If verification passes, incident moves to ‘stabilizing’. If not, escalate to on-call SRE.

4) Manual escalation and deeper mitigation (15-60 minutes)
   - On-call SRE inspects traces and profile data, may perform pool-scale out, failover to another region, or trigger a model rollback.
   - Customer Success prepares proactive customer communication templates (see Communications section).

5) Post-stabilization (60m+)
   - Open an RCA task and schedule triage meeting if impact > 1 hour or > 5% request loss.
   - Re-run tenant evals on the pre/post request samples.

Verification tests (automated)

- Smoke script (example):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_KEY' \\n    -d '{"model":"current","input":"SYNTHETIC_SMOKE_PROMPT","max_tokens":64}' | jq '{status: .status, latency_ms: .latency_ms}'

- Synthetic assertions:
  | Assertion | Threshold | Action if fail |
  |---|---:|---|
  | p95 latency | <= baseline * 1.2 | escalate to SRE |
  | 5xx rate | < 0.5% | route fallback |
  | KV cache hit | >= 70% | initiate rehydrate script |

- Canary traffic replay: reply last-30s of tenant requests against fallback route in an isolated sandbox. Verify token usage and output quality against tenant eval set.

Communication templates (quick copy)

- Customer alert (short):
  Subject: Temporary mitigation applied to your Redwood tenant (T-123)
  Body: 
  Hi <CustomerName>,

  We detected degraded performance on your tenant and applied a temporary mitigation (fallback routing / rate shaping) to protect availability. Our engineers are investigating — we will share updates every 15 minutes. If you need escalation, reply with URGENT.

- Internal update: 
  Incident T-123 - automated mitigation applied: fallback routing -> redwood/small-2b-q4f; verification passed at 09:42 UTC. Owner: Leah Kim.

Operational requirements and permissions (table)

| Permission | Minimum Role | Required by automation |
|---|---|---|
| tenants.route-set | ops-runbooks | Yes |
| tenants.reserve-capacity | ops-admin | Conditional |
| telemetry.read | monitoring | Yes |
| incidents.create | cs-ops | Yes |

Rollout, testing and guardrails

- Feature toggles: automated remediation must be behind a feature flag per-region and per-tenant. Default: off for first 7 days after tenant creation.
- Staging tests: weekly synthetic stress tests that exercise fallback routing and cache rehydration.
- Safety limits: automation may not change encryption/keying configs or customer-provided model artifacts.

Audit and observability

- Every automated change writes a change-event to the audit log with: actor=automation, reason=trigger-rule-id, actions=[...], revert-token.
- Metrics to monitor: automation_success_rate, automation_false_positive_rate, manual_override_count. Target: automation_success_rate >= 90% and false_positive_rate < 5%.

Escalation matrix (summary)

- P3: automated mitigation succeeded, customer notified by CS -> owner: CS on-call.
- P2: automation applied but verification failed -> owner: regional SRE on-call. PagerDuty P2.
- P1: platform-wide cross-tenant impact or data-loss suspected -> company-wide incident; follow incident-response runbook in eng-sre.

Post-incident activities

1. Immediate actions (within 24h):
   - Confirm revert of temporary changes if not needed.
   - Export request and trace samples and attach to incident.

2. 72-hour follow-up:
   - Run tenant-level replays against production and canary models to validate regression fixes.
   - Create RCA draft and assign owners for remedial engineering work.

3. QBR inputs:
   - Capture impact window, affected customers, mitigation timeline, and cost delta. Include synthetic verification artifacts and automation logs.
