Contact and escalation:
- Primary: CSE assigned to tenant (see ticket owner)
- Security on-call: security-oncall@redwood.ai
- Escalation: Support L3 pager (see internal oncall list)

Change log:
- 2026-01-20: v1.0 initial published by Maya Chen
- 2026-03-01: v1.1 updated sampling defaults and added redaction audit step (reviewers: Arjun Patel, Sofia Martinez)

End of document.

title: Autonomous Triage Playbook for LLM Quality Anomalies
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines an autonomous-first triage process for LLM quality anomalies that impact customer-facing traffic. It is intended for SREs, Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), and first-line support to reduce mean-time-to-detect (MTTD) and mean-time-to-resolve (MTTR) using automated detection, quick remediations, and a controlled escalation path. The goal is to keep customer-impacting sessions within our SLOs while minimizing manual intervention.

When to use this playbook:
- Model output quality regressions (semantic drift, hallucination spikes, or abrupt response truncation) detected by telemetry or reported by customers.
- Automated synthetic checks trip quality gates (see "Synthetic checks" section).
- Multiple customers show correlated reductions in evaluation scores, or high false-positive rates in reranking endpoints.

Ownership and roles:
- Primary owner: Customer Success (CSEs) — initial customer communication and impact validation.
- Secondary owner: Eng SRE — metrics triage, routing, and capacity-related checks.
- Escalation owner: Runtime/Serving Engineering — model rollout and kernel-level investigation.
- Communications lead: Customer Success Manager (CSM) — external comms and timeline updates.

SLOs and thresholds (product-impact):
| Metric | SLO | Alert threshold (auto) | Severity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Quality eval delta (customer prompt-set) | < 1.0 point drop | >= 1.5 point drop | Sev-2 |
| Synthetic pass rate (paraphrase tests) | >= 98% | <= 95% | Sev-2 |
| Customer-reported critical failures / hour | 0 | > 3 | Sev-1 |
| End-to-end median latency (critical path) | < 250 ms | > 400 ms | Sev-3 |

Preconditions and safeguards:
- This playbook assumes telemetry pipelines are healthy and ingestion latency < 2 minutes. If telemetry is lagging, follow the "Telemetry degraded" checklist in the related SRE runbook before proceeding.
- All automated actions have a 2-step safety check: 1) internal detection + 2) synthetic confirmation or customer report. Exceptions require on-call approval.

Synthetic checks (automated):
- Nightly and rolling synthetic suites run against every active model variant:
  1) Intent preservation (20 queries per domain)
  2) Hallucination probes (10 factual checks)
  3) Paraphrase consistency (50 paraphrase pairs)
  4) Tokenization integrity (edge-case input set)
- Synthetic checks use tenant-focused prompt-sets when available. Any tiered tenant with > 100k tokens/day has a private prompt-set.
- Synthetic alerting thresholds configured in the orchestration layer: two consecutive windows of failing checks (5 minutes apart) triggers an automated triage.

Autonomous triage flow (high-level):
1) Detection: anomaly is flagged by either synthetic suite or customer telemetry (first-line).
2) Rapid classification: an automation job runs a prioritized checklist (see "automated diagnostics").
3) Quick mitigation: if automation classifies the issue as a reversible configuration or routing problem, it runs a guarded remediation (auto-rollback window: 10 minutes).
4) Human review: CSE or SRE reviews automation outputs; if unresolved, escalate per matrix.
5) Post-incident: produce short RCA and update customer and internal artifacts.

Automated diagnostics (scripts run in parallel):
- Verify model variant and pinned version for affected tenant(s).
- Re-simulate customer prompt-set against last-known-good model snapshot (runtimes: local replay).
- Check KV-cache hit rates and delta from baseline (significant drops indicate cache eviction regressions).
- Validate routing policy: confirm requests are not being routed to fallback variant with different tokenization/quantization profile.
- Confirm recent rollout timeline: check deploy logs for canary failures or rollback events in the previous 60 minutes.
- Execute a small golden test of 5 deterministic prompts to validate tokenization and truncation behavior.

Guarded automatic remediations (only when checks pass safety gate):
- Re-route 5% -> 50% of affected traffic to last-known-good model variant (gradual in 5% increments with 2-minute observation).
- Clear tenant prefix cache for affected tenant (single-key clear followed by throttled rebuild).
- Temporarily disable experimental tokenization fallback for the tenant.
- Auto-rollback of the most recent model rollout if success rate < 80% in 10-minute window.

Automated remediation CLI examples:
- Re-route command (internal):
  redwood ctl routing set --tenant TENANT_ID --from VARIANT_B --to VARIANT_A --percent 20 --observe 120

- Rollback model rollout (internal):
  redwood ctl model rollback --model-id model-llama-13b-q4_1 --to-version v2028-01-22 --force --dry-run=false

Escalation matrix and timings:
- Sev-1 (customer-visible critical failure; >3 critical failures/hour or >5% eviction of customers): immediate page to on-call SRE and CSE; 15-minute bridge. Notify Eng Runtime within 30 minutes.
- Sev-2 (quality regression, synthetic fail): page CSE on-call; 60-minute bridge target. Invoke guarded remediation first.
- Sev-3 (degraded latency or single-tenant non-critical): ticket to SRE queue; 4-hour review.

Escalation contacts (examples):
- On-call SRE: PagerDuty schedule (primary/secondary)
- Runtime lead: runtime-oncall@redwood.internal
- Model Ops: modelops@redwood.internal

Customer communication templates (short):
- Initial acknowledgement (automated):
  "We have detected an issue affecting model responses for your tenant. Our systems have started an automated triage and we will follow up within 30 minutes with next steps. — Redwood Support"

- Follow-up (if mitigation in progress):
  "We've temporarily routed a portion of traffic to a stable model variant and are monitoring results. You may see transient differences in output format while we complete verification. We expect to confirm resolution within 60 minutes. — CSE"

Investigation checklist (human-driven):
1) Confirm customer context and recent actions (model pinning, prompt-set changes, schema changes).
2) Re-run synthetic prompt-set targeted to the tenant; compare token-level diffs.
3) Review recent deployments and canary logs. Note any kernel or CUDA errors.
4) Inspect backend logs for partial responses, aborted streams, or gRPC resets.
5) Validate KV-cache metrics and persistence store latency.
6) If applicable, request a sample conversation from the customer and replay it against known-good snapshot.

Telemetry assertions to collect during incident:
- eval.score.{tenant_id} (time-series)
- synthetic.passrate.{model_variant} (rolling 5m)
- kvcache.hit_rate.{tenant_id} and kvcache.evictions.{tenant_id}
- routing.swap_events.{tenant_id}
- model.deploy.duration.{model_id}

Post-incident actions and RCA template (deliverables):
- Short RCA (one-page): timeline, impact (tenants affected, duration), root cause, contributing factors, immediate remediation, and permanent fix owner + ETA.
- Customer summary (plain language) and compensation recommendation if needed per SLA.
- Update synthetic prompt-sets if gaps discovered; add new probes.
- Add automated checks or tighten thresholds where automation missed signal.

Permanent fixes matrix (examples):
| Problem class | Permanent fix | Owner | ETA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cache eviction surge | Increase per-tenant cache cap + eviction backpressure | Eng Runtime | 3 weeks |
| Tokenization mismatch after quantized rollout | Add tokenization regression tests in CI | Model Ops | 2 weeks |
| Undetected partial stream truncation | Add end-of-stream guard metric and alert | Eng SRE | 1 week |

Runbook review cadence and training:
- Quarterly playbook review with Eng Runtime, SRE, and CSEs.
- Annual game-day where automation is disabled for 2 full hours to validate human procedures.
- New CSE on-boarding: 90-minute hands-on lab using the synthetic harness and the simulated incident runner.

Appendix: quick check commands and sample queries
- Check recent deploy events:
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://deploys.redwood.internal/api/v1/events?model=model-llama-13b | jq '. | .[0:5]'

- Query synthetic pass rate (example PromQL):
  avg_over_time(synthetic_passrate{model_variant="prod-llama-13b"}[10m])

- Sample deterministic prompt to validate hallucination regression:
  "Q: Who is the current Secretary-General of the United Nations? A:"

Notes and provenance:
- This playbook consolidates lessons from customer incidents in 2026–2027 and the runtime kernel regressions in 2027. It favors an autonomous-first posture with human gates for customer-visible rollbacks.
- Related runbooks: eng-sre/runbooks/telemetry-degraded-checklist and eng-serving-runtime/release-notes/rollback-guidelines.

Contact for feedback: Ravi Shah (ravi.shah@redwood.ai)

title: Go-Live Protocols: Cross-Org Communications & Escalation
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines the cross-organizational go-live protocol used by Redwood Inference for enterprise tenant cutovers. It focuses on communications, stakeholder coordination, and an escalation ladder tailored for high-risk or high-visibility customers. Use this runbook as the canonical checklist for the 72 hours before, during, and 72 hours after a cutover where multiple teams (Customer Success, SRE, Solutions Engineering, Product, and Sales) must be coordinated.

Scope
-----
- Applies to: Dedicated and Private deployment go-lives and tenant migrations with SLA commitments (any customer with an enterprise contract or > $50k monthly spend).
- Out of scope: self-serve trial accounts, routine model-only updates without routing changes.

Goals and SLOs to Protect
-------------------------
- Availability SLA target to protect during cutover: 99.9% (monthly) for production routes.
- Immediate remediation thresholds (trigger escalation):
  - Error rate spike: sustained >5% errors for 5 minutes across tenant endpoints.
  - Latency spike: P95 latency >2000ms for 10 minutes.
  - Token cost anomaly: >200% of projected token spend in 30 minutes.
  - KV cache miss-rate >30% sustained for 15 minutes (for cache-sensitive workloads).

Pre-Cutover (T-72 to T-1 hours)
-------------------------------
1. Confirm stakeholders and channels
   - Primary CSM (Customer Success Manager): name + mobile number.
   - Tech lead (Customer): contact + escalation path.
   - Solution Engineer (SE): responsible for ingress, API contract verification.
   - Oncall SRE/Platform owner: PagerDuty schedule and runbook owner.
   - Slack channels: #cs-<customer>-go-live (private channel), #oncall-redwood, #se-ops.
2. Telemetry sanity checks — must pass before proceeding:
   - Synthetic journey (happy path) passes end-to-end: <customer> -> Redwood API -> response < 1s.
   - PromQL checks: error_rate/instance < 0.005 for 10m; p95_latency_query < 1500ms.
3. Canary plan and acceptance criteria
   - Canary traffic: route 1% of production for 30 minutes with zero critical errors.
   - Acceptance: no P0/P1 incidents during canary and no regression in model quality metrics (if applicable).
4. Whitelist and firewall confirmations
   - Verify ingress IP ranges, customer egress rules, and TLS client certs.

During Cutover (T0 to +4 hours) — Immediate Checklist
----------------------------------------------------
- Primary communications protocol:
  - All updates posted to #cs-<customer>-go-live every 10 minutes during the first hour, then every 30 minutes until stable.
  - The CSM posts customer-facing status updates; technical details posted to private channel only.
- Live monitoring dashboard (owner: Oncall SRE):
  - Tenant-specific dashboard showing throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, KV cache hits, token consumption.
- Escalation triggers (first responder must escalate within 5 minutes if triggered):
  1) P0: service unavailable for customer routes — immediate page to P1 oncall and notify Engineering Director.
  2) P1: sustained SLO breach (see thresholds above) — page SE and PM, start RCA and mitigation steps.
  3) P2: model quality regression detected — notify Applied ML and SE; consider traffic switch to verified model snapshot.

Escalation Ladder (contact order and responsibilities)
----------------------------------------------------
| Level | Trigger example | Primary contact | Secondary contact | Action required |
|-------|-----------------|-----------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| L1 (CSM) | Customer questions, minor errors | CSM | SE | Acknowledge to customer within 15m, open internal thread |
| L2 (SRE) | Error rate >5% | Oncall SRE | SRE Lead | Execute diagnostics, apply mitigations (rate-limit, route switch) |
| L3 (SE/PM) | Persistent degradation >30m | Solutions Engineer | Product Manager | Coordinate config changes, model fallback, communicate to customer executives |
| L4 (Exec) | SLA breach or major incident | Head of Customer Success | Head of Engineering | Declare incident, engage legal/finance if SLA credits likely |

Note: The table above is intended as a quick reference. The full escalation paging list with phone numbers and PagerDuty IDs is stored in /confluence/people-ops/rosters and in the private channel pinned messages.

Common Mitigations (ordered by lowest customer impact first)
----------------------------------------------------------
- Increase routing to a higher-capacity pool (if Dedicated: burst pool)
- Apply tenant-level throttles to protect shared resources (quota reduce to 30% of projected steady-state)
- Enable model fallback: route to last-known-stable model snapshot
- Temporarily switch customer to hosted API endpoint (if allowed by contract)
- Quiesce long-running batch jobs from the customer side

Rollback and Safe-fail Strategies
--------------------------------
1. Safe rollback to previous routing config (SE executes):
   - Command: curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal.redwood/v1/route/revert -d '{"tenant":"<tenant-id>","to_config":"<previous-config-id>"}' 
   - Confirm routing table via: kubectl get svc ingress-<tenant> -o yaml (requires ops role)
2. Tenant quiesce API (customer-facing graceful shutdown):
   - POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/tenants/<tenant>/quiesce?actor=ops
   - Expected behavior: existing requests drain, new requests return 429 with Retry-After header.
3. Emergency switchback to hosted region: update DNS TTL and apply traffic policy TTL=30s for faster re-routing.

Communication Templates
-----------------------
- Customer-facing 1-line (acknowledge): "We are investigating increased latency for your production routes and will provide an update within 15 minutes. No action required from your side unless we ask."
- Customer-facing status update (10m cadence): include short bullet list: observed metric, action taken, owner, ETA for next update.
- Internal P0 page message sample:
  - "P0: <customer> production routes returning 503s since 08:12 UTC. Oncall SRE investigating. Initial hypothesis: ingress proxy thread exhaustion. Paging SRE Lead and SE. Next update in 5 minutes"

Telemetry checks / Queries (examples)
----------------------------------
- PromQL (errors): sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant="<tenant>",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant="<tenant>"}[5m])) > 0.05
- Token consumption anomaly (example):
  - Query: increase(token_count_total{tenant="<tenant>"}[30m]) / expected_token_rate > 2.0
- Synthetic validation command (curl):
  - curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input":"synthetic health check"}' | jq '.latency_ms'

Post-Cutover (T+4 to T+72 hours)
--------------------------------
- Stability window monitoring: SRE to keep watch for 72 hours; escalate on any SLO breach.
- Cost and quota reconciliation: Finance Ops and CSM to review token consumption, forecast delta, and apply quota protections if needed.
- Customer QBR prep: collect first-week metrics and any incident notes for the 30-day QBR.

Runbook Ownership and RACI
-------------------------
- CSM: customer comms and executive escalation.
- SE: onboarding technical lead, API contract signoff, whitelist verification.
- Oncall SRE: monitoring, mitigation, and platform config changes in emergencies.
- Product/Applied ML: model quality regressions and rollbacks.
- Finance Ops: post-cutover cost anomalies and quota adjustments.

Appendix A — Playbook Checklist (copyable)
-----------------------------------------
- [ ] Confirm private channel and all stakeholder contacts pinned
- [ ] Telemetry smoke test passed (synthetic happy path)
- [ ] Canary plan scheduled and accepted by SE and SRE
- [ ] Firewall/whitelist config validated by Network team
- [ ] PagerDuty rotations confirmed and escalation contacts available
- [ ] Customer-facing status template approved by CSM
- [ ] Post-cutover QBR slot scheduled with customer (within 30 days)

Appendix B — Links and References
--------------------------------
- Tenant cutover checklist (internal): /confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/onboarding-handback-and-first-90-days-ops-guide-2026
- Incident comms templates: /confluence/eng-sre/incident-communication-templates
- PagerDuty runbook: https://pagerduty.com/orgs/redwood-incidents (private)

Appendix C — Escalation Contact Quickview
----------------------------------------
- Oncall SRE: pagerduty (PD ID: PD12345), Slack: @oncall-sre, mobile: +1-555-0102
- SE on duty: Slack: @se-ops, mobile: +1-555-0148
- CSM (Primary): Priya Patel, Slack: @priya.cs, mobile: +1-555-0190

Revision History
----------------
- 2027-02-10: Created by Priya Patel.
- 2027-03-02: Reviewed and clarified rollback steps; added expense reconciliation task (Marisol Gomez).

Notes and governance
--------------------
Keep this page updated after every enterprise go-live. If the customer contract contains additional communication obligations (e.g., weekly executive summaries), add them to the post-cutover tasks and pin them in the customer channel.

title: Customer-facing debugging flow for LLM output variance
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes a reproducible, customer-facing debugging and escalation flow for investigating reports of inconsistent or degraded LLM outputs (quality variance, hallucinations, or surprising style/length changes). It is written for Customer Success (CS) engineers and first-line support, and includes data collection templates, quick mitigations, metric thresholds, synthetic test guidance, and an escalation matrix for SRE/Model teams.

When to use:
- Customer reports that previously-stable prompts now return lower-quality or inconsistent answers.
- Widespread deviations observed after a deploy, model switch, or config change.
- Intermittent variance tied to time-of-day, tenant load, or routing changes.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm customer-visible failure with a single canonical example. Ask customer to provide: a reproducible prompt, desired behavior, timestamp (UTC), and the request-ID if available.
2) Check service health dashboard (Redwood Console) for model rollout events, latency spikes, or capacity fallback during the incident window.
3) Lock sampling settings: ask customer to run with explicit parameters (model, model_version, temperature, top_p, max_tokens) and collect both request and response payloads.
4) If output is inappropriate, offer immediate mitigation: set temperature=0.0-0.2, pin to last-known-good model_version, and enable deterministic sampling if supported.

Mandatory data collection (customer + CS):
- Canonical prompt(s) (1–5) that reproduce the issue.
- Full request payload including headers and query params.
- Full response payload(s) (including streaming chunks).
- Exact model name and model_version / build id.
- Sampling parameters: temperature, top_k/top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, max_tokens, stop sequences.
- Date/time (UTC) and request-id(s).
- Customer SDK/SDK-version or API client and region.
- Any recent application changes (prompt templating, pre/post processing, tokenization or sanitization).

Triage flow (detailed steps):
1) Reproduce locally (CS):
   - Run the canonical prompt against the same model_version and sampling params. Use the customer’s SDK or our recommended curl to mirror environment.
   - Example curl (replace placeholders):
     curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
       -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>'
       -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
       -d '{"model":"<MODEL>","model_version":"<VERSION>","input":"<PROMPT>","temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":256}'
2) If not reproducible:
   - Query logs for the customer request-id and window.
   - Check for routing/fanout proxies, A/B rollout headers, tenant isolation, or fallback to quantized model variants.
   - Ask customer to run with explicit model_version pinned.
3) If reproducible and deterministic changes observed:
   - Compare outputs across three axes: exact token sequences (string diff), n-gram overlap, and semantic similarity (embedding cosine).
   - Compute a quick similarity score: run an embedding on both outputs and compare cosine similarity. Threshold guidance is below.
4) Investigate probable root causes by triage category:
   - Model rollout / version change: check deployment events, rollout percentage, and canary logs.
   - Sampling/config drift: verify client-sent params vs server defaults (auto-top-p overrides, max_tokens truncation).
   - Prompt pre/post-processing: templating errors, accidental whitespace/newline changes, or escaping errors.
   - KV cache or context clipping: long histories may evict critical context; verify total tokens and effective context window.
   - Quantization or runtime variant mismatch: customer's tenant routed to a quantized runtime variant may produce stylistic differences.
   - Non-deterministic ops under load: continuous batching and token-level latency management can alter timing-sensitive sampling; check concurrency and burst events.

Similarity thresholds (guidance table):
- Metric | Action threshold | Notes
- Embedding cosine similarity | < 0.82 => likely semantic regression -> escalate to Model team
- BLEU / ROUGE quick overlap | drop > 30% from baseline => quality regression on structured tasks
- Exact token match rate | < 60% on deterministic tasks => sampling/config mismatch

Synthetic validation (set up a short suite):
- Purpose: reproduce, quantify regression, and create a stable artifact for ML/evals.
- Minimal suite design: 10–50 golden prompts that exercise critical behavior (edge cases, api-specific formatting, regulated phrasing).
- Example run command (ci-friendly):
  - curl the test harness endpoint which runs the prompt set and returns JSON with metrics.
  - Sample harness response fields to capture: prompt_id, baseline_embedding, current_embedding, cosine_similarity, tokens_used, model_version.

Immediate mitigations to offer customers (ordered by risk):
1) Pin model_version to last-known-good. Notes: This is the fastest control but may require org permission for dedicated tenants.
2) Reduce temperature and randomness settings (temperature <= 0.2, top_p <= 0.6).
3) Shorten the effective context window (trim history) to avoid context clipping.
4) Route to an alternate runtime pool (non-quantized) if stylistic differences are suspected to come from quantization.
5) Temporarily enable a content filter or safety layer to block hallucinations while investigation proceeds.

Escalation matrix and SLAs:
- Level 1 (CS): initial triage, data collection, and mitigation offer. Target response time: 30 minutes SLA for P1 customer-impacting degradation. Owner: customer-success.
- Level 2 (SRE/runtime): investigate routing, runtime variant, capacity/fallback, and rollout telemetry. Target: 2 hours SLA for initial findings. Owner: eng-sre/eng-serving-runtime.
- Level 3 (Model/Applied ML): analyze model regressions, run eval harness, and propose model rollback or fine-tune. Target: 24–72 hours depending on severity. Owner: research/applied-ml.

Escalation template (to open an internal incident ticket):
- Title: [CS-INC] Output variance observed — tenant <TENANT_ID> — model <MODEL>@<VERSION>
- Required attachments: canonical prompts, customer request-ids, curl reproduction, synthetic harness results (if available), console timeline screenshot.
- Priority guidance: P1 if customer go-live affected or high-volume production impact.

Post-incident steps and ownership:
1) CS: confirm customer mitigation acceptance and document customer impact in ticket.
2) SRE: annotate deployment and routing events in incident ticket; capture logs and traces.
3) Model team: run regression evaluation, publish a short technical RCA and proposed actions (rollback, parameter change, or retrain).
4) Product/CS: schedule a customer-facing summary and QBR note if impact was material.
5) Create a regression test (golden prompts) and add to the continuous evaluation harness with a regression alert threshold.

Appendix A — Required CLI/API snippets:
- Fetch request details (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" "https://console.redwood.ai/v1/requests?request_id=<REQ_ID>"
- Run basic embed compare (pseudo):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-small","input":["OUTPUT_A","OUTPUT_B"]}'

Contacts and ownership:
- Customer Success escalation lead: Maya Thompson (maya@redwood.ai)
- Runtime/SRE on-call: eng-sre pager and Slack #sre-runbooks
- Model team triage: Applied ML triage queue (applied-ml@redwood.ai)

Related references:
- Runtime rollout playbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/release-notes/
- Eval harness onboarding: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/

Document maintenance:
- Keeper: Maya Thompson (customer-success). Review cadence: quarterly or after any major model or runtime change.

End of playbook.

title: Adaptive Auth Connector Failure: Triage and Automated Recovery Playbook
content:
Summary
=======
This playbook describes detection, triage, and automated recovery steps for failures of customer-managed authentication connectors used during enterprise Private and Dedicated onboarding. The procedures target failures that prevent client sessions from establishing streaming (SSE/WebSocket) or authenticated REST requests to Redwood ingress endpoints.

Scope
-----
- Affects enterprise Private (VPC) and Dedicated tenants that integrate a custom OIDC/SAML/JWT verifier or sidecar auth-proxy.
- Applies to production and staging environments where ingress authentication is enforced.
- Does NOT cover: internal Redwood IAM issues, customer-managed identity provider outages (except for diagnostic suggestions).

Goals
-----
1) Reduce mean time to recovery (MTTR) by providing a deterministic triage path.
2) Provide automated remediation that is safe to run without customer changes where possible.
3) Clarify when to escalate to SRE, Security, or Customer Engineering.

Indicators: What to watch for
--------------------------------
High-confidence signals (automated alert should fire):
- Authentication error rate > 5% for an enterprise tenant over a 5m window AND absolute 5xxs on the ingress proxy > 1%
- Streaming session establishment failures (SSE open failures / WebSocket handshake failures) > 3% for 5m
- Sudden increase in latency for token verification path (token-verify RT 95th percentile increases by >200ms)

Low-confidence signals (use with other signals):
- 401 spike on a single client IP range
- Repeated JWT signature failures with same kid

Severity levels
---------------
- Sev2: >30% auth failures or streaming unavailable for >10% of traffic for >10m. Requires SRE and CS on-call.
- Sev3: 5-30% auth failures or degraded streaming for <30% of traffic for 5-30m. CS primary triage.
- Sev4: <5% auth failures or short blips <5m. Monitor and document.

Quick kill-switch (when to run before full triage)
-----------------------------------------------
If customer-facing production is impacted broadly (Sev2) and immediate remediation is required:
1) Move tenant to fallback auth mode (if enabled) via control-plane toggle. Command:

# curl (internal)
curl -X POST https://control-plane.redwood-inference.internal/api/tenants/{tenant_id}/auth/fallback \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"mode":"allow-read-only"}'

2) If fallback is not available, route traffic to a verified backup verifier (see Backup Verifier section).
Note: These actions are disruptive  notify customer, open incident, and run full triage in parallel.

Triage checklist (ordered, try each step until resolved)
--------------------------------------------------------
1) Confirm alerts and scope
   - Identify impacted tenant(s) and start an incident channel.
   - Query traffic & auth errors: Prometheus/Insights example:

# PromQL: auth error rate for tenant
sum(rate(ingress_auth_errors_total{tenant_id=\"TENANT123\"}[5m])) by (code)

2) Correlate with deployment events
   - Check recent canary/rollout timestamps for ingress-sidecar or control-plane changes in last 60 minutes.
   - Command (internal): gitops status --tenant TENANT123 --since 60m

3) Verify token issuance path
   - If customer uses external IdP: validate IdP token issuance latency and errors. Suggested IdP checks:
     - Okta: /api/v1/logs for token errors in last 5m
     - AzureAD: sign-in logs, conditional access failures

4) Inspect verifier logs
   - Container logs (kubectl or cloud logs): search for signature verification, kid mismatch, and clock skew errors. Example grep:

kubectl logs -n tenant-TENANT123 deployment/auth-verifier --since=15m | egrep 'kid mismatch|signature|clock skew|token expired'

5) Check clock skew and TLS certs
   - Confirm NTP drift < 2s on verifier hosts.
   - Confirm TLS chain validity for verifier to IdP and ingress TLS certs.

6) Streaming-specific checks
   - Inspect connection accept counts on ingress proxies and check for 4xx during handshake.
   - If SSE handshake is failing but REST auth passes, inspect SSE proxy and connection limits.

Automated remediation recipes (safe-by-default)
------------------------------------------------
A) Restart verifier process with rolling backoff (safe):
- Use when logs show transient errors (memory spikes, temporary failures).

kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-verifier -n tenant-TENANT123
# Wait with exponential backoff and validate auth-success-metric returns to baseline

B) Refresh JWKS cache and confirm key rotation handling (idempotent):
- Triggered when 'kid mismatch' or JWKS fetch error is detected.

# internal-control API
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/tenants/TENANT123/auth/jwks/refresh -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN'

C) Automated fallback to short-lived allowlist mode (temporary):
- Only use under approved incident runbooks and with customer consent. This operates by allowing read-only traffic that does not require full verifier validation. Rollback is immediate.

D) Circuit-broken IdP requests caching:
- If IdP is rate-limited/out, enable a limited TTL cache of previously validated tokens for principal UIDs for 60s. This requires a control-plane toggle:

curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/tenants/TENANT123/feature-flags \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN' -d '{"auth_token_cache_ttl":60}'

Decision matrix: alert -> automated action
---------------------------------------
- auth_error_rate > 5% AND jwks_fetch_failures > 0 -> trigger JWKS refresh (B) then restart verifier (A).
- streaming_handshake_failures > 3% AND handshake_4xx_count > 1% -> increase SSE connection limit and restart ingress proxy; if still failing -> fallback mode.
- idp_rate_limit_detected -> enable token cache (D) and notify customer.

Ownership & escalation
----------------------
- CS On-call: first responder for Sev3/Sev4. Responsibilities: customer comms, initial triage, run automated recipes (A/B).
- SRE On-call: engage for Sev2 or if rolling restart does not restore auth within 10m. Responsibilities: ingress proxy restarts, scaling, and network debugging.
- Security/Identity Engineering: engage when signature mismatches, unusual key rotations, or suspected credential compromise.

Telemetry queries and dashboards (examples)
-----------------------------------------
- Auth error rate (per-tenant):
  sum(rate(ingress_auth_errors_total{tenant_id=\"TENANT123\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(ingress_requests_total{tenant_id=\"TENANT123\"}[5m]))
- JWKS fetch latency: histograms under jwks_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant_id=\"TENANT123\"}
- SSE handshake failures: sum(rate(sse_handshake_failures_total{tenant_id=\"TENANT123\"}[5m]))

Configuration checklist (table)
------------------------------
- Required items to validate during onboarding:
  - OIDC metadata URL reachable from verifier hosts
  - JWKS TTL configured >= 60s and <= 24h
  - Control-plane fallback mode enabled (boolean)
  - Token cache feature flag available for tenant
  - Ingress proxy connection limit documented per tenant

Suggested commands and scripts
------------------------------
- Run a single-step verifier restart and validate with synthetic:

#!/bin/bash
TENANT=TENANT123
set -e
kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-verifier -n tenant-$TENANT
sleep 20
curl -s -I -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN\" https://ingress.$TENANT.api.redwood-inference.com/health | head -n 1

Communication templates
-----------------------
- Short customer update (on Sev3):
  \"We've detected intermittent authentication failures for your tenant between 14:12-14:27 UTC. Our team is performing controlled restarts of the auth verifier and monitoring traffic. No action required on your side. We will update in 30 minutes or on resolution.\"

- Escalation to SRE (on Sev2):
  \"Sev2: Tenant TENANT123 experiencing >30% auth failures since 14:10 UTC. CS has toggled fallback mode. Request SRE to investigate ingress proxy logs, restart proxy if needed, and confirm NTP/TLS state. Incident channel: #inc-TENANT123-auth\"

Unsafe actions (do NOT run without Security)
-------------------------------------------
- Disabling signature checks globally.
- Rolling back customer-managed verifier config to a prior secret without owner consent.

Post-incident checklist
-----------------------
1) Collect verifier logs, JWKS fetch traces, and control-plane toggles.
2) Run root-cause analysis template and attach to incident.
3) Review whether automated remediation should be adjusted (thresholds, timers).
4) Schedule customer-facing RCA if customer impacted beyond SLA.

Appendix: Example incident timeline template
-------------------------------------------
- 14:05: Alert fired (auth_error_rate 7%)
- 14:07: CS created incident channel #inc-TENANT123-auth
- 14:09: JWKS refresh (automated) triggered
- 14:12: Rolling restart auth-verifier initiated
- 14:18: Error rate dropped to 1.2%
- 14:25: Fallback toggles reverted; monitoring for 30m

Related artifacts & links
------------------------
- Private deployment ingress runbook: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/ingress-runbook
- Control-plane feature toggle API docs: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/control-plane-api

Document history
----------------
- 2026-03-15: Created by Sana Rodriguez
- 2026-04-02: Added automated token-cache recipe (review: Evan Park)
- 2026-06-01: Clarified PromQL examples and SSE handshake thresholds (review: Maya Singh)

title: Support Ops: Reconciling token accounting discrepancy reports (intake + triage)
content:
## Purpose
This page documents how Support should handle and count reports of a **token accounting discrepancy** across intake channels. These cases frequently arrive via Slack, email, or Jira, and can be double-counted unless we normalize to a single canonical support record.

## Definition (use this phrase)
We classify a case as a *token accounting discrepancy* when a customer claims that billed token totals (Console Usage and/or invoice export) do not match their own calculation from application logs or local tokenization.

## Approved intake channels
We track where the report first arrived, because it affects response time and deduplication.
- Jira (customer-support): SUP-* ticket created directly by Support
- Slack: #support threads (often started from Intercom/Zendesk summaries)
- Gmail: finance/billing or CSM forwards to leadership/finance

## How to avoid double counting
1. If a report arrives in Slack or Gmail, file a SUP ticket and link it.
2. Mark the SUP ticket label `token-accounting` and add the origin channel in the description (Slack/Gmail).
3. In weekly reporting, count the case by *origin* (Slack vs Gmail vs Jira), not by total artifacts.

## Common root causes to check
- Streaming retries/reconnect (tokens can be emitted twice)
- Client counts only final chunk tokens
- Different tokenizer / unicode normalization
- Whitespace/newlines included in input strings
- Tool-call serialization adds tokens
- Prefix-cache billing bug (rare; see SUP-3009)

## Known examples (for reference)
- SUP-2841: streaming retry/reconnect behavior leading to perceived token accounting discrepancy
- SUP-2917: embeddings tokenizer mismatch leading to perceived token accounting discrepancy
- SUP-3009: cache-hit + tool calling bug leading to real token accounting discrepancy

## Reporting note
When answering: "Which intake channel has the most reports of token accounting discrepancy?" be sure to include Slack and Gmail-origin cases even if a SUP ticket was created later.

title: Silent Degradation Detection and Automated Remediation Playbook
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines how Redwood detects 'silent degradations' (performance or quality regressions that do not immediately trigger customer-facing errors) and how we automatically remediate or escalate them. It centralizes detection signals, automated mitigation actions, ownership, and customer communication templates.

Scope: Applies to hosted API, Dedicated, and Private tenants for production inference pipelines. Focus areas: inference quality drift (semantic regressions), behind-the-scenes latency/cost regressions, and resource contention that degrades tail latency without complete failures.

Principles

- Detect early using behavioral signals instead of waiting for incident thresholds.
- Prefer automated safe remediation (circuit breakers, model fallback, synthetic rollbacks) when available.
- Keep customers informed for any automated action that modifies their request routing, model variant, or cost profile.

Key Definitions

- Silent Degradation: Degradation in availability, latency tail, unit cost, or model output fidelity that does not meet an immediate SLA but will materially affect customer experience over time (e.g., 15% increase in 95th percentile latency sustained for 30 minutes while error rate remains <1%).
- Mitigation Ladder: Ordered set of remediation steps ranked by low customer-impact and safety-first (observability -> soft mitigation -> hard mitigation -> human escalation).
- Synthetic Journey: End-to-end customer request simulation that verifies correctness, latency, and token cost against a baseline.

Signals and Detection Rules

1) Telemetry signals (primary):
   - p95 latency increase: >20% over rolling 60-min baseline for a customer segment.
   - Median tokens-per-generation increase: >30% vs. expected prompt distribution.
   - Inference unit cost variance: >25% sustained for 30 minutes.
   - Model-quality drift: decrease in internal eval accuracy/QA score by >5% on control prompt-set.
   - Synthetic journey failure rate: >3% failed assertions in last 10 runs.

2) Composite alerts (trigger when 2+ signals occur within a 30-minute window):
   - Example: p95 latency + tokens increase -> composite degradation alert.

3) Noise control and suppression:
   - Require minimum sample size (50 requests) in 30-minute window to avoid noisy triggers.
   - Apply anomaly detection smoothing: use robust median-of-means to ignore one-off spikes.

Mitigation Ladder (Automated-first flow)

Stage 0 — Observability escalation (automatic, no customer impact):
- Enrich alert with correlating dimensions: region, model_variant, tenant_id, pod_id, request_path.
- Run synthetic journey (fast) against the same variant and region.
- Snapshot KV cache hit ratio and batch size distribution.
- Notify oncall via Slack channel #ops-customer-alerts with prefilled context.

Stage 1 — Soft mitigations (safe, reversible):
1. Adaptive single-tenant batching loosen: reduce max batch wait time from config (default 25 ms -> 10 ms) to reduce tail latency for latency-sensitive customers.
   - Command: curl -X POST $ADMIN_API/tenants/{tenant}/config -d '{"batch_wait_ms":10}'
2. Prefix-KV cache warmup disable/enable toggle: temporarily disable prefix cache prefetch for affected tenant to prevent thrash.
3. Reduce quantization aggressiveness for the specific model_variant (if supported) to restore tail latency at expense of small cost increase.
- Automation: playbook automation runs these incrementally with health checks after each change (10-minute stabilization window).

Stage 2 — Hard mitigations (automated but higher-impact):
1. Model-fallback to higher-latency but more stable variant (e.g., redwood-model-v2.small -> redwood-model-v2.base).
   - Route policy change: set "fallback=true" for affected tenant and route for 15 minutes.
2. Cross-region failover for regional capacity anomalies (only for customers with cross-region enabled).
3. Temporary request-throttling or per-tenant fairshare enforcement to protect shared capacity.
- Automation: require 3 confirmation checks (composite signal persists across 3 consecutive 10-minute windows) before applying.

Stage 3 — Human-in-the-loop and customer-impacting actions:
- Paging to SRE and Customer Success for coordinated action.
- Consider scheduled model rollback (if recent model rollout is correlated).
- Initiate coordinated customer communication and QBR action items.

Escalation matrix and Ownership

- Primary owner: SRE (eng-sre) — responsible for automated runbook maintenance and operations targeting.
- Secondary owner: Customer Success — responsible for customer notification and follow-up.
- Tertiary owner: Runtime/Serving team — responsible for fixing systemic regressions (kernel changes, batching logic).

Severity mapping (example):
- Sev-3 (Degradation): p95 latency up 20%, small customer impact. Action: Stages 0-1 automated. Notify CS.
- Sev-2 (Significant Degradation): p95 up 50% or synthetic failures >10%. Action: Stages 0-2 automated plus SRE paging.
- Sev-1 (Critical): sustained degradation causing customer SLA breach or data loss. Action: Full incident runbook; immediate human response and customer-wide comms.

Customer Communication Templates

- Auto-notify (low impact): "We detected increased latency affecting your tenant in region X. We've applied temporary mitigations and are monitoring. No action required on your side. Status: investigating."
- Escalated notification (when model-fallback or throttling applied): "To prevent downstream impact we temporarily routed requests to a stable model variant. Expected impact: small quality delta for 15–60 minutes. We will notify when normal routing is restored."

Implementation details and examples

1) Synthetic Journey definition (YAML example):
| name: conversational-check
| frequency_minutes: 5
| tenant_scope: control
| steps:
|   - send_prompt: "Summarize: The market yesterday..."
|   - assert_latency_lt_ms: 350
|   - assert_tokens_lt: 300
|   - compute_quality_score: baseline_eval.json

2) Example alert rule (pseudo):
- name: silent-degradation-composite
  condition: (p95_latency > 1.2 * rolling_p95) AND (median_tokens > 1.3 * rolling_median_tokens)
  min_samples: 50
  window: 30m
  action: trigger_auto_mitigation_workflow

3) Sample automation flow (CLI snippets):
- Run synthetic journey: 
  curl -X POST $SYNTH_API/run -d '{"journey":"conversational-check","region":"us-west-2"}'
- Apply batching config tweak: 
  curl -X POST $ADMIN_API/tenants/tenant-123/config -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"batch_wait_ms":10}'
- Apply model-fallback (atomic): 
  curl -X POST $ADMIN_API/routing -d '{"tenant":"tenant-123","route_override":{"model":"redwood-model-v2.base","duration_min":15}}'

Safety checks and guardrails

- Automatic changes must be bounded: no single automated change should increase tenant costs >20% without human approval.
- Any automated model-fallback that alters output fidelity requires CS notification and an opt-out flag for customers who have strict fidelity SLAs.
- All automated actions must be logged with request-level correlation IDs and rollback timers.

Testing and validation

- Nightly synthetic runs against Canary tenants to validate auto-remediation code paths.
- Game-day quarterly validation: simulate silent degrations (increase latency, reduce KV cache hits) and verify automation triggers and rollbacks.
- Regression validation in PRs that modify batching/kv/quantization code paths: include synthetic journey baseline runs in CI.

Runbook: Step-by-step response (when automation triggers)

1. T=0: Composite alert triggers -> run automated diagnostic snapshot (observability enrichment).
2. T=0–10m: Orchestrator runs synthetic journey and posts results to incident channel.
3. T=10–25m: Automation applies Stage 1 mitigations sequentially with 10-minute stabilize checks.
4. T=25–60m: If composite persists, automation promotes to Stage 2 mitigations; SRE is paged.
5. T>60m: If unresolved, escalate to incident playbook (oncall rotation, CS outreach, exec notification if >2 customers impacted).

Operational metrics to track

- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for silent degradations.
- % of degradations mitigated fully by automation (no human involvement).
- False positive rate of composite alerts.
- Average cost delta introduced by automated actions.
- Customer satisfaction delta post-remediation (tracked in QBR).

QBR inputs and Recommended Reporting

For Quarterly Business Reviews (CS + Customer): provide:
- Incidents summary that used this playbook (count, mitigation type, customer impact).
- MTTD/MTTR and how many were fully automated.
- Any recurring root causes and action items (e.g., batching kernel bug, KV cache cold-start).
- Cost vs. quality tradeoffs observed and recommended model/quantization profile changes.

Appendices

A. Sample JSON payload for alert enrichment:
{
  "alert_id":"sd-20260702-001",
  "tenant":"tenant-123",
  "signals":["p95_latency","tokens_increase"],
  "region":"us-west-2",
  "snapshot_time":"2026-07-02T14:35:00Z"
}

B. Quick checklist for Customer Success when notified:
1. Confirm automated action applied and duration.
2. Validate customer critical flows (support request or synthetic) if requested.
3. Proactively schedule a short postmortem if customer observes visible impact.
4. Log follow-up items in customer QBR agenda.

C. Related runbooks and pages:
- Tenant synthetic suite onboarding guide (link in related_pages).
- SLO taxonomy and burn-rate thresholds (eng-sre).

Document maintenance

- Owner: SRE (primary) — review every 3 months or after any major automation incident.
- Reviewer cadence: CS/Runtime/Observability teams to review changes prior to publication.
- Change log: Record brief entries below with date and author.

Change log:
- 2026-03-15 — Asha Kapoor — first published (initial detection rules and mitigation ladder).
- 2026-07-02 — Liam Chen — added composite alert logic and cost-guardrails.

End of playbook.

title: Escalation classification + tagging (Support)
content:
# Purpose
This page defines what counts as a Support escalation at Redwood Inference and the required tags/fields for reporting.

# Definition: Support escalation
A Support issue is considered an **escalation** when **any** of the following are true:
- Priority is **P0 or P1**, OR
- Severity is **Sev0 or Sev1**, OR
- The ticket is handed off to an on-call engineer or triggers an incident workflow.

Escalations must be labeled with **label: escalated**.

# Required fields for escalation reporting
For escalations, Support must ensure the Jira issue includes all of the following (either as fields or as explicit labels):

## 1) Deployment offering
Exactly one of:
- Hosted API
- Dedicated
- Private

Support tagging:
- Label one of: **offering-hosted**, **offering-dedicated**, **offering-private**

## 2) Primary symptom
Exactly one primary symptom should be chosen even if multiple symptoms are observed. Examples:
- Request timeouts
- Elevated latency
- 5xx errors
- Streaming disconnects
- 429s / throttling
- Auth failures

Support tagging:
- Label one of the symptom labels. For timeouts: **symptom-timeout**

## 3) Customer impact summary
In the description, include:
- A short impact statement (what users see)
- Affected regions
- If known: approximate error rate and timeframe

# Notes on ‘request timeouts’
Use the ‘request timeouts’ primary symptom when the customer reports any of:
- 504 gateway timeouts
- client-side ‘context deadline exceeded’
- load balancer / proxy timeouts
- long-hanging requests that end with timeout rather than completing

# Reporting
Monthly offering-level escalation reporting is computed by counting all Jira issues in that month with:
- label: escalated
- label: symptom-timeout
- exactly one offering label (offering-hosted/dedicated/private)

Support Ops will reconcile any escalation threads in #support that did not result in a Jira ticket within 24 hours.

title: Customer Telemetry Synthesis and Action Runbook
content:
Overview

Purpose: This runbook describes the standardized process Customer Success and Support use to synthesize customer telemetry into actionable signals during enterprise onboarding, early go‑live, and post‑cutover QBRs. It is designed to reduce time‑to‑remediation, align SLO interpretations across teams, and automate low‑risk actions where safe.

Scope: Applies to Dedicated and Private tenants and hosted customers that have integrated Redwood telemetry (metrics, traces, logs, synthetic tests) via the Telemetry Gatekeeper or native SDK integration. Does NOT replace incident runbooks for platform SRE; it supports customer‑facing stability and cost alerts.

Audience: Customer Success Managers, Support Engineers (L1/L2), Solutions Engineers, Onboarding Engineers, and Customer Reliability Engineers.

Summary of key flows

- Telemetry ingestion mapping and synthesis: map raw metrics -> SLIs -> composite customer stability score.
- Alert triage flow: auto‑enrich alerts with context (tenant profile, recent model rollouts, recent config changes) before paging L2.
- Automated remediation actions: controlled actions that Support can trigger (cache flush, model fallback, transient quota bump).
- QBR inputs: aggregated signals and synthetic results to inform health reviews and contractual SLO discussions.

Definitions and SLO mapping

Important definitions (abbreviations used in this runbook):
- SLI: Service Level Indicator (e.g., p50/p95/latency, token cost per request).
- SLO: Service Level Objective (target on an SLI, e.g., p95 < 600ms).
- Stability Score: 0–100 composite derived from weighted SLIs for a tenant.

Example SLI -> SLO mapping (table):
| SLI name | Collection source | Aggregation | Baseline SLO | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| inference_p95_latency_ms | ingress-gateway.metrics/latency_ms | 5m window p95 | < 600 | Apply per‑route, per‑model when available |
| error_rate_pct | service.errors/total_requests | 1h window rate | < 0.5 | Include 4xx/5xx split |
| kvcache_hit_rate_pct | runtime.kvcache/hits_total | 30m avg | > 75 | Most effective for prompt-heavy workloads |
| token_cost_per_1k | billing.tokens/units | rolling 24h avg | < $0.08 | Important for FinOps/QBR |

SLO thresholds in alerts: the thresholds above are defaults; for enterprise customers we expect to map contract SLAs to these fields and override thresholds in tenant config.

Telemetry synthesis: algorithm (high level)

1. Normalize raw metrics to common time windows (5m/30m/1h/24h).
2. Compute scaled z‑scores relative to tenant historic baseline (30 days).
3. Apply weightings: latency 40%, error_rate 30%, kvcache_hit_rate 20%, cost 10%.
4. Output Stability Score = 100 - weighted_penalty, with discrete buckets: Healthy >= 90, Watch 70-89, Degraded 50-69, Critical < 50.

Actionable alerts and enrichment

When an alert fires, the gatekeeper enrichment pipeline must attach:
- Tenant metadata: tier (self-serve/enterprise), region, dedicated/private, service owner contact.
- Recent deployments: last model version deploy time, quantization profile version, recent rollout policy.
- Recent telemetry anomalies: 30m jump in token_cost_per_1k, 5m p95 spike, kvcache drop.

Example alert rule (Prometheus/Alertmanager style, translated):
- alert: TenantHighLatency
  expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(ingress_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant_id=~"$TENANT"}[5m])) by (le)) * 1000) > 0.6
  for: 5m
  labels: { severity: warn, category: latency }
  annotations: { runbook_url: "https://confluence/redwood/customer-telemetry-synthesis-and-action-runbook" }

Auto‑enrichment example (pseudocode):
1. Receive alert payload -> extract tenant_id.
2. Query tenant profile API: GET /internal/api/tenant/{tenant_id}/profile -> return tier, owner, models_in_use.
3. Query rollout history: GET /internal/api/deployments?tenant={tenant_id}&since=1h.
4. Attach top 3 correlated anomalies (promql results) to alert.

Triage playbook (step‑by‑step)

1) L1 intake (first 10 minutes)
- Confirm alert details and enrichment metadata.
- Run quick checks: synthetic latency test (see commands below), kvcache delta check, model version consistency.
- If Stability Score >= 90 and alert severity warn, file a ticket and set PENDING_AUTOMATION; if automation exists, trigger (see AutomatedRemediations section).

2) L2 triage (10–45 minutes)
- Validate root cause hypothesis: traffic surge, model rollback, upstream DNS/peering, customer config change.
- Check recent deployments and customer change log (tracked in tenant audit index).
- If infrastructure issue (network/cloud provider), hand off to Platform SRE via #sre-customer-handoff and include enriched evidence.

3) Escalation to Customer Success & Solutions (45–120 minutes)
- If customer-visible impact and partial mitigation not found, notify CSM and schedule a 15‑minute bridge.
- Notify legal/compliance for regulated tenants if data exfil or KMS errors are indicated.

AutomatedRemediations (approved actions L1 can run)

- flush_kvcache (low risk): clears Redis/KV cache for tenant; idempotent.
- fallback_to_small_model: switch tenant routing to a compatible smaller model variant for 1 hour.
- transient_quota_bump: raise rate limit by 20% for 10 minutes for bursty onboarding flows (requires audit logging).

To execute via support CLI (example):
$ rw-support run-action --tenant t-12345 --action flush_kvcache --reason "p95 spike during onboarding"
Response: { "status": "accepted", "action_id":"act-20270310-0001" }

Safety checks before automation: verify that tenant is not on restricted list and that action is allowed in tenant profile (tenant_profile.automation_allowed==true). All automated actions create an audit event and a support ticket.

Diagnostic commands and queries

- Synthetic latency probe (curl):
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_API_KEY" -X POST https://ingress.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-7b", "prompt":"ping"}' -D /tmp/latency_hdrs -o /tmp/latency_body
- KV cache delta (PromQL):
avg_over_time((increase(runtime_kvcache_hits_total{tenant_id="$TENANT"}[30m]) / increase(runtime_kvcache_requests_total{tenant_id="$TENANT"}[30m])) * 100)[30m:5m]
- Recent model deployment (curl):
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_API_KEY" https://internal-api.redwood.ai/deployments?tenant=$TENANT&limit=5

Sample webhook payload to create an action ticket in the Support system (JSON):
{
  "tenant_id": "t-12345",
  "alert_id": "alert-9876",
  "stability_score": 62,
  "playbook_step": "L2 triage",
  "recommended_actions": ["flush_kvcache","fallback_to_small_model"],
  "evidence": ["p95 1200ms (5m)", "kvcache hit rate 41% (30m)"]
}

Customer onboarding checklist (telemetry specific)

- Telemetry Gatekeeper configured and validated (ingress metrics, traces, logs forwarded).
- SDK installed for detailed request tagging when Gatekeeper not available.
- Baseline period collected: 72 hours of production‑like traffic for baseline modeling.
- Synthetic test suite created: 10 synthetic journeys covering critical routes (generation, embeddings, streaming).
- Cost guardrails configured: per‑tenant token cost alerting and Quota Protector webhook configured.

QBR and health report inputs

For quarterly business reviews (QBR) produce the following tenant deliverables:
- 1‑page health snapshot: Stability Score trend, p95 latency trend, error rate, top 3 regressions and actions.
- Cost delta analysis: token_cost_per_1k and top heavy prompts/calls.
- Synthetic report: pass/fail for the canonical 10 journeys and median latency for each.
- Action log: all automated remediations and manual interventions since last QBR.

Maintenance and ownership

- Telemetry synthesis service (team: Observability Platform) owns the pipeline and model weights for stability score.
- Support Playbook owner: Customer Success Operations (Maya Chen).
- Scheduled runbook review: once per quarter or after major infra changes; owners must sign off on tuning parameters.

Onboarding ramp guidelines (recommended cadence)

Week 0: Gatekeeper/Synthetic setup and baseline data collection.
Week 1: Monitor Stability Score hourly; run daily health sweep with L1.
Week 2: Tune kvcache config and batching settings with Solutions Eng.
Week 3–4: Move to automated guardrails for cost and token spikes; transition monitoring to standard QBR cadence.

Appendix: common root causes and fast checks

- Root cause: Model rollback/upgrade -> Check deployment history, model perf delta, and revert if regression confirmed.
- Root cause: Ingress gateway misrouting -> Verify route table, certificates, and ingress error logs.
- Root cause: Customer traffic pattern shift (batching/parallelization) -> Review request histogram and kvcache utilization.

Useful links and references

- Telemetry Gatekeeper onboarding guide: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/integration-guides/telemetry-gatekeeper-onboarding-and-qbr-integration-guide-2026
- Support CLI reference: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/support-cli-reference
- Platform SRE handoff template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/sre-handoff-template

Change log

- 2027-02-15: Initial published version (Maya Chen).
- 2027-03-10: Added automated remediation safeguards and CLI examples (reviewers: Jose Alvarez, Priya Narang).

title: Automated Degradation Classifier and Customer Failover Runbook
content:
Overview

This runbook describes the automated degradation classifier (ADC) used by Customer Success and SRE to detect service-quality regressions for enterprise tenants, validate safe failover eligibility, and orchestrate tiered customer notifications and remediation. It documents classification thresholds, telemetry mappings, alert routing, escalation windows, and step-by-step procedures for automated and manual remediation.

Goals

- Detect real customer-impacting degradation (latency, error-rate, model-quality drift) with <80% false-positive rate in steady-state traffic.
- Automate non-destructive mitigations (routing to fallback model variants, traffic shaping) within 5 minutes of classification.
- Provide clear, auditable customer communications and playbook for escalation to engineering/ops.

Scope

- Applies to Dedicated and Private tenants and high-volume Hosted API customers with SLOs.
- Covers: inference latency P95, error rate, model-generation-quality regression (eval score deltas), KV cache hit-rate, and telemetry signal health (ingest gaps).
- Out of scope: customer billing disputes, hardware-only incidents covered by cloud-provider runbooks.

Telemetry and Signals

Key signals the ADC consumes (priority order):
- p95_inference_latency_ms (per-tenant, 1m/5m windows)
- request_error_rate_pct (HTTP 5xx + model-serve-specific rejects)
- model_eval_delta_pct (per-customer prompt-set baseline vs rolling 24h)
- kvcache_hit_rate_pct (prefix/KV reuse)
- telemetry_ingest_lag_sec (agent/sidecar -> collector)
- synthetic_user_synthetic_score (synthetic journeys score: 0-1)

Signal mapping and derived metrics (table):
| Metric | Window | Threshold (class = degraded) | Notes |
| p95_inference_latency_ms | 5m | >= 1200 ms and delta >= 2x baseline | Baselines stored per-tenant in telemetry-store |
| request_error_rate_pct | 5m | >= 1.5% absolute or 3x baseline | Exclude client-side timeouts |
| model_eval_delta_pct | 24h | >= 7% absolute drop on evaluation suite | Use tenant-specific eval prompt-set |
| kvcache_hit_rate_pct | 10m | drop >= 30% from baseline | Indicates cache invalidation/regression |
| telemetry_ingest_lag_sec | 2m | > 60s | May indicate sidecar/drop or pipeline issue |

Classification logic (simplified):
1) Ingest real-time signals into ADC engine (stream).
2) Compute z-score of each metric vs baseline; apply weights: latency 0.35, error-rate 0.3, model-eval 0.25, kvcache 0.05, ingest-lag 0.05.
3) If weighted score >= 0.7 AND at least two signals exceed thresholds, label tenant_state = "degraded".
4) Run fast deterministic checks (synthetic journey drop, region outage markers).

False-positive protection and cooldowns

- Require sustained classification for 2 consecutive 1-minute intervals before any automated customer-impacting action.
- If classification flips back to healthy within 10 minutes, cancel automated mitigation and create an advisory event only.
- Max automated mitigation frequency per tenant: 3/hr.

Automated Mitigation Options (ordered by least-intrusive first)

1) Lightweight routing fallback: switch small percentage (10-25%) of traffic to a lower-capacity but stable model variant for 3–10 minutes.
2) Dynamic batching adjustment: temporarily increase batching window for background, non-low-latency routes.
3) KV cache warmup prefetch for affected model shards (if kvcache hit-rate drop detected).
4) Regional failover: redirect traffic to secondary region if regional capacity or infra flags are present.
5) Tenant soft-throttle: shed best-effort/lowest-priority routes (e.g., embeddings bulk jobs) while preserving interactive tokens.

Each mitigation must be reversible via the ADC control plane and is subject to TTL and canary rollback.

Escalation Matrix and Ownership

- ADC Alert level 1 (detect only): Customer Success on-call paged by PagerDuty; SRE watch notified (Slack #sre-observe) — 15 minute SLAs for initial triage.
- ADC Alert level 2 (automated mitigation triggered): SRE & Serving Runtime on-call paged; CS notified for customer comms — 10 minute SLA for mitigation validation.
- ADC Alert level 3 (automated mitigation failed or model-quality regression persisted >30m): Incident Commander activated, full incident playbook (see related_pages for incident process).

Routing to escalation teams (table):
| Condition | Primary Team | Secondary Team | Escalation Channel | PagerDuty Policy |
| latency-only | eng-serving-runtime | eng-infra | #serving-runtime | PD-policy-serving |
| error-rate | eng-sre | eng-serving-runtime | #sre-oncall | PD-policy-sre |
| model-eval-delta | applied-ml-and-evals | eng-serving-runtime | #applied-ml | PD-policy-ml |
| telemetry-ingest | eng-infra | customer-success | #telemetry | PD-policy-infra |

Customer Communications (templates)

- Advisory (detect only): "We are monitoring an elevated latency signal affecting X% of your requests and are investigating. No action has been taken. We will follow up within 15 minutes."
- Mitigation notice (automated action): "We detected a service degradation and routed a small percentage of traffic to a stable model variant to preserve availability. We will continue to monitor and notify you of material changes."
- Escalation/update: "Mitigation attempted succeeded/rolled back. Next step: engineering investigation underway; ETA 60 minutes for next update."

All outbound customer messages are logged to the customer-notification-audit stream with template_id and PD-incident id.

Operational Runbook: Step-by-step

1) Detection (automatic)
  a) ADC marks tenant_state = degraded.
  b) ADC posts event to incident-bridge and creates internal ticket (prefix ADC-<tenant>-<ts>).
  c) PagerDuty route triggers based on classification.
2) Initial human triage (CS or SRE) — within 15 minutes
  a) Validate telemetry (run provided queries below).
  b) Check for known issues: maintenance, provider alerts, model rollout windows.
  c) If false positive (e.g., client-side spike), tag ticket and resolve; annotate ADC baseline if needed.
3) If mitigation allowed (policy check) and classification sustained -> ADC triggers mitigation.
4) Post-mitigation verification (5–10 minutes)
  a) Verify p95 latency and error-rate returned to within 90% of baseline.
  b) If improved, send Mitigation notice to customer; schedule 1-hour monitoring window.
  c) If not improved, escalate to Level 3.
5) Full incident (if escalated)
  a) Run full incident template (see oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process).
  b) Capture RCA inputs: model binary, kernel config, KV cache eviction logs, batch window changes.

Observability Queries and Debug Helpers

- Example Prometheus-like queries:
  p95_inference_latency_ms{tenant="TENANT_ID"}[5m]
  sum(rate(request_errors_total{tenant="TENANT_ID"}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{tenant="TENANT_ID"}[5m])) * 100
  kvcache_hit_rate_pct{tenant="TENANT_ID"}
- Synthetic journey probe: synthetic_probe_status{tenant="TENANT_ID",journey="interactive-check"}
- Model-eval delta: fetch latest eval-run and compare to tenant-baseline stored in eval-store: eval_store.query(tenant_id=..., window=24h)

Diagnostic artifacts to collect for RCA

- ADC classification payload (raw signals and weights)
- Serving runtime shard logs for affected model version (last 60 minutes)
- Kernel scheduling trace (if latency spike)
- KV cache eviction and rewarm traces
- Customer request-id traces (correlated via request-correlation-id header)

Policy and Access Controls

- Only SRE and CS on-call roles can approve automated mitigations for regulated tenants.
- ADC control plane actions are auditable and logged to the CIAM audit stream for 13 months.
- Make/Model variant list that ADC may route to is controlled by Applied ML (whitelist per-tenant).

Testing and Validation

- Quarterly game-days: induce synthetic degradations for 10 tenants across Dedicated and Private modes to validate ADC detection and mitigation runbook.
- Canary tests: ADC changes must pass a canary window of 48h in staging with monitored false-positive rate < 8%.

Appendix: Example alert payload (JSON)

{
  "tenant_id": "tenant_acme_inc",
  "timestamp": "2026-07-15T10:12:34Z",

title: LLM Output Audit and Customer Ops Handbook
content:
Overview
-------
This playbook defines the program and operational runbook for periodic LLM output audits performed during enterprise onboarding, and for recurring quality audits that feed QBRs and escalation flow. The document is intended for Customer Success Engineers, Support Engineers, Solutions Architects, and SREs who participate in customer-facing quality investigations and acceptance checks.

Goals
-----
- Provide a repeatable, low-friction audit process that verifies model fidelity, prompt safety, latency/cost trade-offs, and business-relevant correctness for enterprise customers.
- Map telemetry assertions to customer SLAs and QBR artifacts so audits directly inform action items and supplier-level escalations.
- Establish clear roles, ownership, and timelines for audit, remediation, and customer communication.

Scope
-----
This handbook covers:
- Acceptance audits performed during the first 30 days after tenant provisioning.
- Monthly stability and fidelity audits for Dedicated and Private tenants.
- Ad-hoc investigation audits triggered by customer reports or anomaly alerts.
It does NOT cover: low-level kernel performance tuning (eng-serving-runtime), legal data-exposure forensics (security-and-compliance), or billing disputes (finance-and-legal).

Key Definitions
---------------
- Audit Run: a discrete execution of the audit harness over a defined prompt set and telemetry window.
- Golden Prompt Set: a customer-specific set of 50–250 canonical prompts provided by product/CS and derived from customer workflows.
- Fidelity Score: weighted metric combining semantic-match (embedding cosine), hallucination rate, and instruction-following pass/fail.
- Telemetry Assertions: measurable signals (latency p95, token cost per request, model mismatch rate) that must meet thresholds.

Ownership and Roles
-------------------
- Customer Success Engineer (CSE): primary owner of the audit schedule, customer comms, and acceptance criteria.
- Support Engineer (Tier 2): executes the audit, collects artifacts, and runs the evaluation harness.
- Platform SRE: verifies infrastructure signals (GPU preemption, KV cache hit-rates, batching behaviour).
- Applied ML / Model Onboarding: interprets fidelity regressions and recommends model or quantization adjustments.
- Escalation Liaison (CS lead): coordinates cross-team escalation and external SLAs.

Audit Types and Cadence
-----------------------
1) Day-0 Acceptance Audit (CSE + Support Engineer)
   - When: within 72 hours of tenant provisioning or cutover.
   - Scope: golden prompt set x baseline model + production routing config.
   - Outputs: acceptance report PDF, pass/fail gate, action list.
   - Decision: if critical failures (>10% catastrophic hallucinations or SLA breaches), pause cutover and invoke go-live safety net.

2) 30-Day Stability Audit (CSE + Platform SRE + Applied ML)
   - When: 30 days after provision and monthly thereafter for Dedicated/Private customers.
   - Scope: extended prompt set, synthetic traffic replay at 10th/50th/90th percentile concurrency.
   - Outputs: fidelity and economics dashboard snapshot, model-version drift check.

3) Ad-hoc Investigation Audit (Support Engineer)
   - When: triggered by customer-reported issue, automated fidelity alert, or QBR signal.
   - Scope: focused prompt subset plus relevant request traces and telemetry window.
   - Outputs: RCA outline, mitigation steps, recommended rollback or model-variant switch.

Audit Preconditions and Prerequisites
------------------------------------
- Golden Prompt Set approved and stored in the customer workspace (S3 path or internal asset id).
- Synthetic traffic harness referencing the tenant’s routing and model pinning configuration.
- Access to tenant metrics: request traces, model selection logs, KV cache metrics, latency histograms, and cost-by-token metrics.
- List of acceptance thresholds agreed in the contract or QBR baseline.

Audit Procedure (step-by-step)
------------------------------
1. Prepare environment (Support Engineer)
   - Pull latest golden prompt set: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-customer-assets/<tenant-id>/golden-prompts.json ./prompts.json
   - Confirm model pins: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/tenants/<tenant>/config | jq .model_pin
   - Validate telemetry window: ensure 72h of request logs and metric retention is available.

2. Run fidelity harness
   - Run: python3 tools/audit_runner.py --prompts ./prompts.json --tenant <tenant> --samples 3 --output ./audit-artifacts/<date>/
   - Collect: generated outputs, per-sample embeddings, similarity scores, hallucination annotations.

3. Score and thresholding (Support Engineer + Applied ML)
   - Compute: semantic-match (cosine >= 0.78), hallucination-rate <= 5%, exact-instruction-following >= 90% (values gated per-customer).
   - Generate: PDF audit-summary including top-10 failures, example traces, and per-route latency/cost tables.

4. Telemetry correlation (Platform SRE)
   - Confirm: p50/p95 latency meets SLOs (p95 < 450ms for interactive tier; verify if dedicated private SLO differs).
   - Check: KV cache hit-rate, batch sizes distribution, and preemption logs around audit windows.

5. Draft customer-facing report (CSE)
   - Include: executive summary, pass/fail status, actionable remediation items, and expected timeline.
   - Template snippets: see "Customer Communication Templates" below.

Evaluation Metrics and Thresholds (example table)
---------------------------------------------------
- Fidelity Score: pass if > 0.85 (weighted).
- Semantic Match (embedding cosine): median >= 0.78.
- Hallucination Rate: <= 5% of prompts flagged as hallucinated.
- Instruction-Following: >= 90% pass on binary checks.
- Token Cost Delta vs baseline: <= +15% acceptable for first-30-day period.
- p95 Completion Latency: Dedicated <= 400ms, Hosted Interactive <= 450ms.

Customer Communication Templates
--------------------------------
- Initial Audit Notification (CSE)
  Subject: Audit scheduled: LLM output acceptance for <tenant-name>
  Body snippet: "We will run the agreed acceptance tests on <date>. Expected duration 2–4 hours. We will share an executive summary and remediation items within 24 hours."

- Failure Triage Notification (CSE)
  Subject: Action required: fidelity issues detected in acceptance audit for <tenant-name>
  Body snippet: "We observed elevated hallucination rates on prompts related to <feature>. We recommend activating fallback model-variant B and scheduling a joint trial with Applied ML. See attached artifacts and proposed timeline."

Escalation Matrix and SLA Intervals
-----------------------------------
- Severity P1 (customer-critical production degradation): contact sequence within 30 minutes; full incident bridge within 60 minutes. Owner: Customer Success lead + Platform SRE.
- Severity P2 (functional regressions impacting >10% of workflows): initial contact within 2 hours; remediation plan within 24 hours. Owner: Support Engineering.
- Severity P3 (cosmetic or minor discrepancies): reply within 48 hours; plan when convenient. Owner: CSE.

Automations and Tooling
-----------------------
- Audit harness: tools/audit_runner.py – supports parallel sampling, synthetic replay, and per-sample annotation export.
- Eval dashboard: internal Grafana panel "Customer Audit - <tenant>" with prebuilt panels for fidelity, latency, cost, and model-variant distribution.
- Alerting: fidelity-regression alert triggers a JIRA with labels audit-regression/<tenant>.

Acceptance Gates and Decisioning
--------------------------------
- Gate PASS: CSE marks tenant as "accepted-for-prod" in provisioning tracker and proceeds with final cutover.
- Gate FAIL (critical): pause further traffic increases; open cross-team incident and enforce rollback to previously pinned model-variant.
- Gate FAIL (non-critical): schedule remediation backlog item with delivery SLA aligned to customer's support tier (e.g., 7 days for standard, 3 days for enterprise).

Post-Audit Remediation Playbook
-------------------------------
1. Identify root cause category: prompt drift, model regression, quantization artifact, infra contention, or routing mismatch.
2. Short-term mitigations: swap to a verified model-variant, apply prompt transformations, increase KV cache segment retention, or throttle concurrency.
3. Medium-term fixes: coordinate with Applied ML on model re-finetune, with eng-serving-runtime on quantization reprofile, or with Platform SRE for capacity adjustments.
4. Confirm fix via focused re-run of the failed prompt subset and update the audit artifacts.

QBR Integration and Artifacts
-----------------------------
- Include audit-pass/fail trend (last 6 months), top recurring failure classes, and cost-per-1000-requests delta.
- Provide a prioritized remediation roadmap with owners and expected impact estimate (latency, fidelity, cost).
- Recommended QBR slide deck sections: Executive Summary, Fidelity Trend, Synthetic Suite Results, Proposed Actions.

Example CLI snippets and queries
-------------------------------
- Retrieve top failed prompts by fidelity score:
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://internal-api.redwood.ai/audit/failures?tenant=<tenant>&days=30 | jq .results | head -n 20

- Run local audit harness sample command:
  python3 tools/audit_runner.py --prompts ./prompts.json --tenant acme-corp --samples 5 --parallel 8 --output ./audit-artifacts/2026-11-02/

Documented Known Failure Modes and Workarounds
----------------------------------------------
- Symptom: Intermittent semantic drop concentrated on long-context prompts.
  Root cause: KV cache eviction policy misaligned with production sequence lengths.
  Workaround: Increase KV cache retention window for the tenant (Platform SRE).

- Symptom: Elevated token cost after quantized model upgrade.
  Root cause: quantization configuration caused longer decode paths in certain layers.
  Workaround: Revert to prior quantization profile or apply selective dequantization for last layers.

Audit Schedule Template (example table)
--------------------------------------
- Day 0: Acceptance Audit (CSE + Support) – 72 hours post provisioning
- Day 30: Stability Audit (CSE + Platform SRE + Applied ML)
- Monthly: Synthetic pass/fail slice for Dedicated/Private tenants
- On trigger: Ad-hoc audit within SLA per escalation matrix

Attachments and Artifacts to Include with Every Audit
----------------------------------------------------
- Prompts used (golden set)
- Generated outputs (JSONL) with trace ids
- Embeddings and similarity matrix CSV
- Telemetry window export (request logs, model-selection logs)
- Audit summary PDF and action items list

Metrics for Continuous Improvement
----------------------------------
- Mean time from audit failure to mitigation deployed (target < 72 hours for P1/P2).
- Fraction of audits that require model-variant rollback (target < 5%).
- Customer satisfaction score on audit process (CSAT target > 4.3/5).

Appendix: Escalation Contact Template
-------------------------------------
- Incident bridge: #customer-incident-<tenant> on Slack (create at start)
- Pager: Platform SRE on-call (follow sequence in oncall-and-incident-response)
- Escalation email alias: cs-escalations@redwood.ai

References
----------
- Internal audit harness README: /docs/internal/tools/audit_runner.md
- QBR telemetry storyboard: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/health-and-qbr/qbr-telemetry-storyboard-and-action-plan-2026
- Onboarding telemetry gatekeeper guide: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/integration-guides/telemetry-gatekeeper-onboarding-and-qbr-integration-guide-2026

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-02-11: Created by Aisha Patel (initial draft)
- 2026-05-03: Added telemetry assertion table and automated JIRA mapping (reviewer: Marco Rivera)
- 2026-11-02: Finalized communication templates and example CLI snippets (published)

title: SOP: intake and coordination for customer-managed audit log export requests
content:
# Purpose
This SOP describes how Customer Success (CS) and Support intake, scope, and coordinate **customer-managed audit log export** requests across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

# When to use
- A customer asks to export Redwood audit logs to their cloud storage or SIEM pipeline.
