- Objective: exercise cache eviction and fallbacks.
- Method: run high-variance prefix traffic (burst of 1000 unique prefixes over 5 minutes).
- Expected: p99_kvcache_hit_rate decreases but should not cause token_error_rate to rise > 0.5%.

Alerting and Thresholds (table)

| Alert name | Query / Signal | Threshold | Urgency | Owner |
|------------|----------------|-----------|---------|-------|
| Canary: latency spike | query: request_latency_ms{tenant=\"canary-123\"} | p99 > 600ms for 2m | high | SRE-oncall |
| Canary: error rate | query: token_error_rate{tenant=\"canary-123\"} | error_rate > 1% for 1m | high | SRE-oncall |
| Canary: quality drop | script: quality_check(golden_set) | absolute drop >= 3% | high | CS / Applied ML |
| Canary: cost spike | query: tokens_per_request_avg{tenant=\"canary-123\"} | > 30% above baseline for 5m | medium | FinOps / CS |
| Canary: kvcache miss cascade | query: p99_kvcache_hit_rate{tenant=\"canary-123\"} | < 20% for 3m | medium | Platform |

Example Prometheus alert rule (YAML)

groups:
- name: canary.rules
  rules:
  - alert: CanaryHighP99Latency
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{tenant=\"canary-123\"}[1m])) by (le)) > 0.6
    for: 2m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: \"p99 latency for canary-123 > 600ms\"
      runbook: \"/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/canary-deployment-validation\"

Automated Playbook (step-by-step)

1. Start canary window (Customer Success)
   - Notify internal channel #cs-canary-run and the customer via scheduled email.
2. Kick off baseline synthetic workload (SRE)
   - Command: curl -X POST https://ci-sim.redwood.local/simulate -d '{"tenant":"canary-123","profile":"baseline","duration":600}'
3. Monitor the dashboard and watch the top three alerts (latency, error, quality) for the first 10 minutes (SRE / CS).
4. If quality alert triggers, pause canary and run a focused evaluation:
   - Run: python3 tools/quality_eval.py --tenant canary-123 --golden golden_v1.json --output /tmp/canary_eval.json
   - If model_confidence_degradation >= 3% absolute, proceed to Escalation Ladder.
5. If latency or error alerts trigger, triage live traces:
   - Run: otel-cli query --service redwood-inference-api --tenant canary-123 --trace-scan 10m
   - Check KV cache hit rate across nodes via: curl http://telemetry-collector/api/cache/summary?tenant=canary-123
6. Decide: continue, throttle, or rollback. Use the decision matrix below.

Decision Matrix (short)

- Continue: transient alert < 2m, no quality degradation, infra GPU util < 85%
- Throttle: sustained cost spike or p99 latency between 400–600ms with no errors (Platform + CS).
- Rollback: any of the following: token_error_rate > 1% for >1m; quality drop >=3% absolute; p99 latency > 800ms for >2m.

Escalation Ladder

1. SRE-oncall page (immediate)
2. Platform engineer (30 min)
3. Applied ML engineer for quality anomalies (15 min)
4. Customer Success lead + Customer technical contact for customer-impacting degradations (immediate)

Escalation contact table

| Role | PagerDuty | Slack channel | Backup |
|------|----------|---------------|--------|
| SRE-oncall | PD: SRE-CANARY | #sre-oncall | Platform-oncall |
| Platform | PD: PLATFORM | #platform | Eng-infra-manager |
| Applied ML | PD: ML-APPLIED | #applied-ml | ML-lead |

Rollback and Failback Procedure (if rollback chosen)

1. Set routing-policy to legacy (Platform):
   - curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/routing -d '{"action":"route","filter":"tenant=canary-123","target":"legacy-pool"}'
2. Disable any automated scaling or batch warmers for the canary (SRE).
3. Notify customer and schedule a follow-up remediation meeting within 48 hours (CS).
4. Capture artifacts: export traces, the canary_eval.json file, dashboard snapshots, and a short incident summary (SRE + CS).

Post-Mortem and QBR Integration

- Required artifact checklist after any canary with a high-severity alert:
  - Incident timeline (UTC)
  - Trace links and top 5 offending traces
  - Quality evaluation report vs golden set
  - Cost delta report (tokens and estimated spend)
  - Action items and owners
- Feed the summary into the next customer QBR under: \"Cutover Learnings\" with recommended SLO adjustments or config changes.

Runbook snippets and queries (copyable)

1) PromQL - p99 latency by route\   histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{tenant=\"canary-123\"}[5m])) by (le, route))

2) SQL - tokens per request (timeseries)\   SELECT bin, avg(tokens_per_request) FROM telemetry.tokens WHERE tenant = 'canary-123' AND ts >= now() - interval '15 minutes' GROUP BY bin ORDER BY bin DESC;

3) Quality check script invocation\   python3 tools/quality_eval.py --tenant canary-123 --profile regression --golden s3://redwood-golden/canary/golden_v1.json --out /tmp/canary_eval.json

Ownership and run cadence

- Canary simulations should be run for all enterprise cutovers and recorded in the Cutover Registry (Customer Success).
- Standard window: 2 hours; extend by mutual agreement with customer and SRE.
- Retrospective: 48–72 hours after any significant alert (CS + SRE + Platform).

Frequently asked questions

Q: What if the customer traffic shape cannot be replicated?
A: Use a hybrid simulation: replay recorded production traces anonymized with adaptive rates. Document difference in the runbook artifacts.

Q: Who owns quality metrics if model outputs degrade?
A: Applied ML triages model-level regressions; CS handles customer communications and rollback decisions.

Related pages and artifacts

- Cutover registry entry (create link in customer ticket)
- /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/canary-deployment-validation
- /confluence/customer-success-and-support/health-and-qbr/governed-inference-qbr-metrics-and-eval-framework-2026

Appendix: Example checklist (copyable)

- [ ] Canary tenant created and pinned to model_version
- [ ] Dashboards populated and filtered for tenant
- [ ] Synthetic baseline simulation executed
- [ ] Golden set evaluation run and recorded
- [ ] PagerDuty escalation policy verified
- [ ] Post-run artifacts uploaded to the customer ticket

Contact and feedback

For improvements to this playbook, open a PR on the internal docs repo or ping #cs-playbooks.

title: Tenant synthetic workload design and validation playbook
content:
Overview

This playbook describes the recommended approach for designing, running, and validating tenant-level synthetic workloads during enterprise onboarding, cutover canaries, and QBR-driven stability assessments. It targets customer-success engineers, SREs, and solutions engineers who are responsible for validating that a tenant's production traffic profile will meet latency, cost, and fidelity targets on Redwood Inference.

Goals and success criteria

- Validate tenant SLA / SLO alignment before production cutover. Typical thresholds: P99 latency < 450ms (generation-only paths), error rate < 0.5% for 5m window, and no more than 15% token-cost uplift vs. forecast.
- Detect functional regressions introduced by model or infra changes (output fidelity checks).
- Identify capacity hotspots (KV cache miss ratios, batching inefficiencies, burst throttling).
- Produce artifact for QBR: run report, signal deltas, and remediation recommendations.

When to run

1. Pre-cutover validation: after tenant config and telemetry hooks are provisioned, before final DNS cutover.
2. Canary validation: during incremental traffic ramp (1% → 25% → 100%).
3. Quarterly stability review (QBR): scheduled synthetic runs that mimic seasonal peak patterns.

Synthetic workload taxonomy

- Deterministic replay (traffic replayer): replay of sanitized historical requests (best-fidelity for output regression checks).
- Probabilistic generator (template-based): parameterized prompt templates covering length, instruction complexity, and tool-calling patterns (best for stress and variety).
- Spike/burst test: short windows of extremely high RPS to exercise autoscaling and fairshare.
- Long-tail test: low-QPS wide-distribution of rare prompts to exercise model cache cold-starts and fallback routing.

Design principles

1. Safety-first: sanitize PII before replay; enforce privacy and retention rules.
2. Observability-driven: every synthetic request must carry tracing headers and a unique synthetic tag (tenant.synthetic_run_id).
3. Signal parity: ensure synthetic requests traverse the same ingress, auth, and routing layers as real traffic (no bypasses).
4. Incremental scope: start with smoke → functional → load → spike. Halt on safety or SLO failures.

Required telemetry & assertions

- Core telemetry (required): request_id, tenant_id, model_name, route, trace_id, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate_usd, kv_cache_hit (boolean), batch_size, response_status.
- SLO/Assertion matrix (examples):
  | Assertion | Threshold | Action on fail |
  |---|---:|---|
  | P95 end-to-end latency (route: /v1/generate) | < 220ms | Pause ramp, triage |
  | P99 token-latency generation | < 450ms | Escalate to runtime oncall |
  | KV cache hit ratio (common-prefixes) | >= 70% | Investigate cache keying / prefixing |
  | Token cost uplift | <= 15% vs forecast | Flag for finops review |
  | Model fidelity regression (BLEU/ROUGE or eval set drift) | delta <= 2% | Trigger model rollback plan |

Workload construction checklist

- Obtain tenant traffic profile: average RPS, peak RPS, typical prompt length, usage mix (single-shot, chat, embeddings).
- Prepare sanitized sample corpus (size: 1k–10k requests depending on test). Mask PII using redaction script.
- Create templates to increase/decrease prompt complexity. Examples: short-instruction (5–20 tokens), medium-context (50–250 tokens), long-context (250–4k tokens).
- Define time distribution: steady-state, daily-peak window(s), burst windows.
- Map templates to routing rules (hosted/dedicated/private / fallback variants).

Validation run procedure (step-by-step)

1. Pre-flight (owner: customer-success):
   - Confirm telemetry forwarding is active and dashboards ingest synthetic tags.
   - Ensure dedicated canaries are provisioned for isolation (if required).
   - Prepare stakeholder channel and incident paging list.
2. Smoke test (5m):
   - Run 50–100 requests across each route/model. Verify reachability, auth, and baseline latency.
   - Command example (template-based):
     curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
       -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TENANT_API_KEY}" \\
       -H "X-Synthetic-Run: tenant.synthetic_run_id=run-20260210-01" \\
       -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
       -d '{"model":"rwd-small-compat","input":"Summarize: The quarter...","max_tokens":64}'

3. Functional regression checks (30–60m):
   - Replay deterministic corpus against pinned model versions. Collect evaluation metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity) against golden outputs.
   - Run automated diff job to compute percent of responses flagged by heuristic safety checks.

4. Load ramp (1–3 hours):
   - Ramp per agreed plan: 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%. At each step, hold for 10–30 minutes and evaluate assertions.
   - Observe batching behavior: watch average batch_size and token-latency.

5. Spike test (15–30 minutes):
   - Generate multiple short bursts (10x baseline RPS) for 2–5 minutes each to validate autoscaling and fairshare.

6. Long-tail sweep (60–120 minutes):
   - Execute a wide variety of low-frequency prompts to assess cache cold-starts and fallback.

7. Post-run analysis and artifact generation:
   - Produce run report with graphs: latency percentiles, kv_cache_hit ratio over time, batch_size distribution, error traces, token cost per minute.
   - Attach diff-summary for functional regression and fidelity metrics.

Failure modes, common root causes, and mitigations

- High P99 token-latency:
  - Root causes: insufficient batching due to low aggregation window, oversized model variant, KV cache misses.
  - Mitigations: increase batching window for non-latency-critical routes, enable smaller quantized variant, tune cache keying.
- Elevated error rate during ramp:
  - Root causes: rate limits, quota enforcement, auth issues, misconfigured ingress ACL.
  - Mitigations: throttle client, raise quota with cust-success approval, verify tenant API key and IP allowlist.
- Token cost far above forecast:
  - Root causes: model switchover to larger size, repeated retries causing duplicate tokens, unexpected long-context prompts.
  - Mitigations: pin model version, add client-side deduplication and debounce, apply prompt-length caps at ingress.

Runbook snippets and tools

- Redactor (Python): simple sanitize example

  # sanitize.py
  import re
  def sanitize(text):
      text = re.sub(r"\\b\\d{12,16}\\b", "[REDACTED]", text)
      text = re.sub(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}", "[REDACTED]", text)
      return text

- Sample synthetic run job (JSON payload for synthetic agent):
  {
    "tenant_id": "tenant-1234",
    "run_id": "run-2026-02-10-01",
    "pattern": "ramp",
    "templates": ["short-instruction","chat-context"],
    "duration_minutes": 180
  }

- Quick queries to validate telemetry (promql-like pseudo):
  - error_rate = sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant_id=\"tenant-1234\",synthetic=\"true\",status!~\"2..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant_id=\"tenant-1234\",synthetic=\"true\"}[5m]))
  - kv_hit = sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{tenant_id=\"tenant-1234\",synthetic=\"true\"}[10m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{tenant_id=\"tenant-1234\",synthetic=\"true\"}[10m]))

Roles and ownership

- Customer Success (owner): coordinates the run, confirms corpus, communicates with customer stakeholders, compiles QBR artifact.
- SRE / Runtime (support): monitors infra during ramp, performs fast rollback, escalates to oncall if P99 or error thresholds breached.
- Solutions Engineering (support): validates fidelity thresholds and performs golden-output regression comparison.

Post-run artifacts and QBR inputs

1. Run report (required): PDF/HTML containing the timeline, key metric graphs, assertion outcomes, and remediation items.
2. Fidelity diff report: tabular list of requests with deviation scores and sample pairs (golden vs run).
3. Remediation backlog: prioritized list with owners and ETA.
4. Cost delta summary: projected monthly cost impact if current pattern persisted.

Appendix: sample acceptance gate checklist

- Gate A (Smoke): All routes reachable, auth validated, P95 latency < 250ms.
- Gate B (Functional): Regression delta < 2% on gold-set, safety flags < 0.2%.
- Gate C (Load): P99 latency < 450ms, error rate < 0.5%, kv_cache_hit >= 70%.
- Gate D (Cutover readiness): All previous gates passed for 2 consecutive runs, and run report approved by SRE and customer-success.

Related resources

- See onboarding telemetry contract: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/integration-guides/telemetry-gatekeeper-onboarding-and-qbr-integration-guide-2026
- Runtime performance standards and SLOs: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/runtime-slo-policy

Revision history

- 2026-02-10: Created by Priya Nambiar.
- 2026-03-01: Expanded spike and long-tail test sections; added run artifact templates.

title: Customer Model Economics Deep Dive Template
content:
Summary:

This template is a standardized, customer-facing deep-dive used during QBRs and technical review sessions to explain the economics of a customer's inference footprint on Redwood. It focuses on translating telemetry and billing signals into actionable recommendations: model mix, batching and cache strategy, quantization/variant choices, and reserved capacity sizing.

Audience:
- Customer Success Manager (CSM)
- Solutions Engineer (SE)
- Customer SRE / Platform lead
- Finance contact for the customer (optional)

When to use:
- Quarterly business reviews (QBR) where cost/perf is a top objective
- Post-cutover stabilization if spend or latency deviates from expectations
- Prior to pricing or dedicated capacity negotiations

Prerequisites and data sources:
1) Time window: last 28 / 90 / 365 days (choose based on volatility).
2) Telemetry sources:
   - Redwood inference telemetry (per-tenant token/embedding counts, model name/version, route tags)
   - Observability: latency P50/P95/P99, error rates (per-route), batch size distribution
   - Cost signals: per-token billing extracts, reserved capacity charges, GPU hours by tenant (for Dedicated)
   - Cache stats: prefix/KV cache hit rate and hit latency
   - Infrastructure: GPU utilization, queue depth, autoscaling events
3) Representative prompts/promotions sets and any recent model upgrades or prompt engineering changes.

Key metrics to present (suggested table):

KPI | Description | Aggregation | Example target 
----|-------------|-------------|----------------
Effective unit cost (USD per 1k tokens) | All-in cost combining per-token billing + allocated infra | 28-day median | $0.85 (customer target)
Model mix by spend (%) | Percent of spend per model family (e.g., redwood-v1-small, llama-2-70B) | 28-day | 4 models, top 2 = 78% spend
Latency P95 (ms) | Tail latency for customer routes | 28-day P95 | <= 350ms
Cache hit rate (prefix + KV) | Percent of requests served at cache layer | 28-day | >= 45%
Batching effectiveness | Median tokens/request per batch | 7-day rolling | >= 12 tokens/batch
Reserved capacity utilization | Average shard utilization (Dedicated) | 24h avg | 60–85%
Cold start frequency | Requests that miss warm KV cache/state | 28-day rate | < 0.5%
Model-induced error rate | Failure/invalid response rate per 1k requests | 28-day | < 0.3%

Core sections of the deep-dive (structure to follow during the QBR):

1) Executive summary (1 slide / 1 paragraph)
- One-sentence summary of the customer's cost vs. target, plus one recommended high-level action (e.g., "Move 30% of traffic from redwood-v2-large to quantized redwood-v2-medium to reduce unit cost by ~37% with minimal latency change").

2) Observed telemetry and spend breakdown (2–3 slides)
- Model-by-model spend table and charts (last 28/90d)
- Route-level latency and cost per 1k tokens
- Time-of-day and georegional variance (if applicable)

3) Root-cause analysis for deviations (2 slides)
- Example triggers: sudden model upgrade, increased prompt length, agricultural traffic spike, disabled caching, batch size regression, or dedicated pool oversubscription.
- For each issue: evidence (query/metric), likely cause, confidence, and immediate mitigation.

4) Actionable recommendations (3–4 items)
- Low friction (customer-facing): adjust default model on non-critical routes, enable prefix caching for high-cardinality prompts, shorten default max tokens on ephemeral endpoints.
- Medium friction (needs engineering): rollout of quantized variant + canary, small model distillation trial, adjust batch-windowing to favour throughput on non-latency-critical routes.
- High friction (contract/ops): purchase X reserved GPUs for peak savings, migrate heavy routes to Dedicated with fair-share slots.
- Each recommendation should include estimated cost delta (USD/mo), expected latency impact, implementation owner, and risk.

5) Simulation and sensitivity scenarios
- Show 2–3 what-if scenarios with simple math: e.g., "If 40% traffic shifts to quantized model -> unit cost -36%; if batching improves by 25% -> token cost -18%." Include assumptions used (model throughput, batching gain, cache hit uplift).

6) Short-term runbook (30/60/90-day plan)
- 0–30 days: enable prefix caching on top 3 routes, shorten max_tokens on ingest pipeline, adjust rate-limit burst window.
- 30–60 days: deploy quantized model canary for 10% traffic, measure latency/QA regressions, instrument golden prompts.
- 60–90 days: review reserved capacity sizing, finalize new per-route model defaults, schedule cost-sharing / pricing discussion.

7) Ownership and OLA (who does what)
- CSM: schedule QBR, prioritize customer sign-off for low-friction actions.
- SE: prepare canary build + telemetry dashboards, run A/B test.
- Customer SRE: validate cache keys and integrate sampling of golden prompts.
- Finance: review forecasting model and margin sensitivities.

8) Escalation triggers (for post-QBR monitoring)
- Daily unit cost > 30% above baseline for 3 consecutive days -> SE + CSM alert.
- P95 latency increase > 50% vs baseline for 2 windows -> schedule incident review.
- Model error rate spike (>=1% absolute increase) -> immediate rollback canary.

9) Appendix: suggested queries & dashboard panels (examples)
- Example PromQL: "sum by (tenant, model) (rate(tokens_consumed_total[1d]))"
- Billing extract SQL (BigQuery) example:
  SELECT tenant_id, model_name, SUM(tokens) as tokens, SUM(cost) as cost
  FROM `billing.tokens_by_request`
  WHERE event_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 28 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE()
  GROUP BY tenant_id, model_name
  ORDER BY cost DESC;
- Suggested dashboard panels: cost-by-model, token-rate heatmap, batch-size histogram, cache-hit-rate timeseries, reserved-utilization gauge.

Presentation tips and anti-patterns:
- Use representative "golden prompts" to demonstrate quality trade-offs for any model/quantization suggestion.
- Don't surface raw billing numbers without normalizing for prompt length and model mix.
- Avoid recommending under-provisioning reserved capacity to hit a short-term cost target; instead present tiered scenarios with safety margins.

Deliverables to attach to the QBR packet:
- Exported dashboards (PNG/PDF) for last 28 / 90 days
- CSV with model-by-model spend and top 20 routes by tokens
- Runbook checklist for short-term actions and owners
- A one-page executive summary with suggested next steps and estimated savings

Template checklist (pre-QBR):
- [ ] Confirm time window and obtain billing extract
- [ ] Validate telemetry mapping (tenant tags, route naming)
- [ ] Identify golden prompts and QA test suite
- [ ] Run baseline cost simulation and prepare 2 alternative scenarios
- [ ] Draft CSM talking points and action owners

Common pitfalls and mitigations (real examples):
- Pitfall: Large ephemeral prompts from a background job inflate avg tokens. Mitigation: Add a separate route, cap tokens, and apply batch-friendly settings.
- Pitfall: Cache keys contain transient IDs so cache hit rate is low. Mitigation: Normalize prompt templates and add pre-processing to strip unique IDs.
- Pitfall: Quantized variant introduces subtle hallucination rate increase. Mitigation: Canary on 5% of traffic and expand golden prompt set for automatic regression detection.

Contact and ownership logging:
- Document author: Marina Lopez (CSM)
- Standard reviewers: Ethan Park (SE), Riya Shah (Finance), Liam O'Connor (SRE)
- Next review cadence: every 90 days or after any model migration affecting >10% of customer traffic.

Related templates and playbooks:
- QBR inference economics overview (link in related_pages)
- Tenant synthetic health suite onboarding playbook (for automated monitoring after changes)

Change log:
- 2026-03-15: Created initial template.
- 2026-11-10: Added sensitivity scenario examples and reserved capacity guidance.

title: Enterprise Fidelity & Stability Playbook
content:
Purpose:
Provide a repeatable, cross-team playbook for measuring, maintaining, and communicating model service fidelity and stability for enterprise customers. This document explains the metrics, instrumentation, SLO decomposition, detection rules, escalation ladder, and pre-QBR preparation steps used by Customer Success, SRE, and Product to ensure customer-facing SLAs and quality expectations are met.

Scope:
- Applies to production inference paths used by enterprise customers (hosted API + Dedicated).
- Covers telemetry for generation, embeddings, and reranking endpoints.
- Excludes internal research workloads and non-production staging clusters.

Definitions (quick):
- Fidelity: semantic correctness and stability of responses relative to a customer’s expected behavior / golden prompt set.
- Availability: percentage of requests returning successful (2xx) responses within latency SLO.
- Degradation window: contiguous period where fidelity or availability falls below thresholds for the same tenant.
- Guardrail failure: an automated safety check (e.g., toxic content filter or format validator) that rejected >= 0.5% of a tenant’s requests in a 1h window.

Key owners and contacts:
- Customer Success lead: Priya Natarajan (owner for customer comms and QBR agenda)
- Oncall SRE: eng-sre oncall (primary for infrastructure/latency incidents)
- Model Quality Lead: Diego Alvarez (owner for fidelity regressions and evals)
- Dedicated Deployment SME: Lina Patel (private/dedicated cutover and rollback)
- Slack channels: #cust-success-ops (customer comms), #sre-inference (infra), #model-quality

Fidelity and Stability Metrics (measured per-tenant and rolled up):
- Golden-prompt pass rate (GPR): percent of golden-prompts that produce expected label/format. Target: >= 97% weekly for enterprise tiers.
- Semantic drift score (SDS): normalized similarity delta vs. baseline embeddings on prompt-set. Target: SDS <= 0.06 (lower is better).
- Successful-response rate (SRR): 2xx responses within latency SLO. Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly.
- Median P95 latency (request-to-first-token): baseline depends on tier: hosted < 180ms median; dedicated < 120ms median.
- Guardrail reject rate (GRR): percent of responses failing guardrails. Threshold: < 0.3% over 1 hour.
- Cost-per-1000-tokens (CPT): used in QBRs to explain economics.

SLO decomposition (example mapping):
- Customer-facing SLA (contract): 99.9% availability and fidelity >= 95% across golden prompts.
- Internal SLOs: SRR >= 99.95% service-wide; GPR >= 97% per-tenant weekly; GRR <= 0.3% hourly.
- Error budget policy: for enterprise customers, a monthly error budget consumption > 20% triggers proactive review and proposed remediation plan; > 50% triggers formal escalation and potential credits.

Instrumentation & telemetry (how we measure):
1) Golden prompt harness: each enterprise onboarding includes a 100–300 prompt set run nightly. Results are stored in the fidelity index and surfaced to the QBR dashboard. CLI example to run locally if needed:

$ redwood-eval-run --tenant-id T-12345 --prompt-set /prompts/enterprise/handbook-core.json --output s3://redwood-evals/T-12345/

2) Production sampling: 0.1% of production requests are shadowed to the fidelity evaluation pipeline to compute SDS and GPR without adding latency.
3) Distributed tracing: spans created with tags: service=inference, model_version, tenant_id, route. Example Prometheus metrics exported: inference_requests_total, inference_latency_seconds_bucket{quantile,tenant}, guardrail_rejects_total.
4) Cost telemetry: token_count and computed CPT stored per-request in the billing stream and aggregated daily. Example SQL snippet to produce CPT by tenant:

SELECT tenant_id, SUM(tokens) as tokens, SUM(cost) as cost, (SUM(cost)/SUM(tokens))*1000 as cost_per_1000_tokens FROM billing.events WHERE date >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY tenant_id;

Detection rules & alerting (who gets paged):
- Alert: fidelity-regression-tenant (severity P2): triggered when tenant GPR < 90% for 30m AND SDS > 0.12. Pager to: model-quality oncall -> then customer-success for high-value tenants.
- Alert: availability-degradation (severity P1): SRR < 99.5% for 10m -> paged to eng-sre primary and infra-rotation.
- Alert: guardrail-spike (severity P2): GRR > 1.0% in 15m -> paged to model-quality and #cust-success-ops channel (no immediate page unless customer impact).
- Cost anomaly: CPT increases > 40% week-over-week -> routed to FinOps and Customer Success (email).

Runbook: first 30 minutes (triage cadence)
1) Responsible: first responder (SRE or Model Quality depending on alert).
2) Immediately collect:
   - Request traces for the window (tracing service link),
   - Golden-prompt nightly run report (S3 path),
   - Deployment history (k8s rollout events / model_version),
   - Recent config changes (routing rules, quantization profile changes).
3) Quick triage checklist (do this in parallel):
   - Is the issue isolated to a single tenant or global? (check tenant_id cardinality in alerts)
   - Has a model version rolled out in the last 2 hours? (kubectl rollout history / model-registry)
   - Are infra metrics (GPU memory pressure, OOMs, pod restarts) elevated?
   - Any network anomalies / cloud provider advisories? (status pages)
4) If fidelity regression and root cause not obvious in 30m -> escalate to Model Quality lead and prepare an immediate rollback to last known-good model variant (see rollback steps).

Escalation ladder (roles and SLAs):
- 0–15m: oncall SRE / first responder performs initial mitigation and informs #incident-ops.
- 15–45m: Model Quality joins if fidelity-related. Customer Success lead notified for enterprise tenants; initiate customer-safe message draft.
- 45–120m: Cross-functional war room (SRE, Model Quality, Dedicated SME, Customer Success) if issue persists or customer-impacting.
- >120m: Exec briefing and legal/compliance loop if the issue affects contractual SLA or PII exposure.

Rollback and safety actions (when to rollback):
- Rollback to previous model variant when GPR drops > 7 percentage points and manual checks confirm output regressions for golden prompts.
- For dedicated/private tenants, coordinate with Dedicated SME to schedule in-window rollback (can require tenant approval for private infra).
- Quick rollback steps (engineer-run):
  1. Identify last-known-good model_version: CURR_VER -> grep model_registry | tail -n 10
  2. Trigger rollout: redwood-deploy --model-version CURR_VER --target pool-<tenant-pool> --strategy immediate
  3. Verify: run 20 golden prompts against the tenant endpoint and confirm GPR >= 95%.

Customer Communication play (templates & timing):
- Initial acknowledgement: within 30 minutes for P1/P2 impacting an enterprise account. Include summary, impacted services, and expected next update window.
- Status cadence: every 60 minutes until remediation or formal rollback.
- Post-incident report: within 48 hours include timeline, root cause analysis, and mitigation plan. Use the Postmortem template and attach telemetry graphs.
- Template snippet (copy-pasteable):

Subject: Incident update — inference instability for <tenant_name>

Hi <Customer_POC>,

We are actively investigating an issue affecting model response quality for requests to <endpoint>. Our engineers have identified a regression in fidelity for a subset of requests and are performing a rollback to a previous model variant as an immediate mitigation. Next update: in 60 minutes.

Regards,
<Redwood CS lead>

Pre-QBR preparation checklist (quarterly operationalization):
1) 14 days before QBR: confirm nightly golden-prompt runs have completed and upload the pass/fail CSV to the QBR folder.
2) 7 days: generate cost delta report (CPT), P95 latency trends, guardrail spikes, and top-5 fidelity regression examples with annotated prompts.
3) 3 days: dry-run the QBR deck with the CS lead and Model Quality to ensure explanations are actionable.
4) QBR deck contents (minimum): executive summary, availability & fidelity SLO performance, cost per 1k tokens trends, open risk items and remediation plan, proposed model/config changes with expected economic impact.

Dashboard and queries to include in QBRs:
- Tenant fidelity timeline: GPR daily moving average + golden-prompt failure examples (link to table).
- Availability heatmap: SRR by region and model_version.
- Cost bridge: CPT delta and contributor breakdown (batching, quantization, model_size).
- Example PromQL for SRR drop detection:

sum(rate(inference_requests_total{tenant_id=\"T-12345\",status=~\"2..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total{tenant_id=\"T-12345\"}[5m])) < 0.995

Post-incident follow-ups and continuous improvement:
- All incidents that consume > 20% of an enterprise customer’s monthly error budget require a triage meeting including Customer Success, Model Quality, and SRE within 7 business days.
- Maintain a shared regression test set: add newly discovered problematic prompts to the tenant's golden set and tag with failure mode.
- Quarterly model audit: Model Quality to run a model-variant stress test (1000+ edge prompts) and produce a mitigation plan for any regressions.

Appendices:
A) Example golden-prompt CSV columns:
- prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_label, match_threshold, last_valid_model_version, last_run_timestamp

B) Escalation contact matrix (internal):
- model-quality-oncall: paged via PagerDuty (PD alias: pd-model-quality)
- eng-sre-oncall: pd-sre-primary
- customer-success-lead: email and slack @Priya Natarajan

C) Quick checklist for Dedicated tenants (network & infra specific):
1) Validate tenant peering: confirm all firewall rules and peering entries are present and no recent ACL changes.
2) If private deployment: check KMS logs for key rotation events in the last 24h.
3) For on-prem: confirm GPU driver versions and CUDA patch level are as expected (recommended: CUDA 12.2, driver >= 535.xx).

Document maintenance and versioning:
- Owner: Customer Success (Priya Natarajan). Review cadence: quarterly or after any P1 incident.
- Change log: note significant changes below (include PR and reviewer IDs).

Change log:
- 2025-10-02: created (Maya Chen)
- 2025-12-15: added SDS metric and guardrail thresholds (Diego Alvarez)
- 2026-02-11: updated alert thresholds and QBR checklist (Maya Chen)

End of document.

title: Postmortem-to-QBR Translation and Customer Readout Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a repeatable process for turning internal incident postmortem findings into a concise, customer-facing QBR (Quarterly Business Review) narrative and readout. The goal is to:
- Surface root causes and mitigations in a way that maps to customer SLAs/SLOs and business impact.
- Provide a clear, action-oriented plan customers can review and sign off on.
- Standardize the rhythm and artifacts for CS-led incident readouts so engineering, SRE, and account teams stay aligned.

When to use this playbook:
1) Any incident that triggered a postmortem with customer-visible impact (latency SLO breach, model-quality regression, outage affecting >1% of tenant traffic, billing anomalies tied to runaway token usage).
2) Major configuration or migration failures that change expected behaviour for a customer.
3) Recurring or high-severity issues flagged by the Customer Success or Enterprise Support teams.

Scope and audience:
- Primary audience: Customer Success Manager (CSM), Account Executive (AE), Engineering Lead on the incident, and the affected customer’s technical stakeholders.
- Secondary audience: SRE, Product PM, and Support.

High-level process overview:
1) Postmortem author finalizes root-cause analysis and mitigation items.
2) CS partner maps technical findings to customer-facing metrics and prepares readout slide deck.
3) Joint internal rehearsal with engineering and CS to agree on messaging and acceptance criteria.
4) Customer readout meeting and follow-up commit list.
5) Tracking through to closure; reflect changes in the next QBR.

Roles and responsibilities (quick reference):
- Postmortem Author (Engineering): Produce final postmortem doc, timeline of events, RCA, impact window, and proposed technical mitigations.
- SRE/Oncall Lead: Confirm artifact accuracy (metrics, graphs, SLO timelines) and sign off on planned mitigations and rollbacks.
- CSM (Owner of Readout): Draft customer narrative, schedule readout, lead the meeting, and maintain follow-up tracker.
- AE: Coordinate customer commercial expectations and any contractual communications.
- Product PM: Provide roadmap context for long-term fixes and prioritization.

Minimum artifact checklist (required before scheduling a customer readout):
- Final internal postmortem (link) with clear RCA and timeline.
- Impact table (customers, tenant IDs, affected routes/endpoints, time windows).
- SLO/SLA graph(s) showing deviation and recovery (PNG/SVG).
- Action items table with owners, due dates, and verification steps.
- Customer-facing 6-slide deck (template below).

6-slide customer readout deck template (concise):
1) Title slide: incident name, customer, date, presenters.
2) Executive summary: one-sentence outcome, one-sentence customer impact, and current status.
3) What happened: brief timeline and root cause (non-technical summary first, technical appendix as follow-up).
4) Impact on your service: mapped to the customer’s SLOs/usage and any financial impact or credits.
5) Actions we took and next steps: short-term mitigations and planned long-term fixes with target dates.
6) Ask of the customer and close: verification plan, acceptance criteria, and scheduled follow-up checkpoint.

Translating technical findings into QBR metrics (mapping guide):
- Latency spike -> translate to: percentage of requests > 2x SLO, P95 and P99 delta vs baseline, affected endpoints, and customer business flows impacted (e.g., search, generation).
- Model-quality regression -> translate to: evaluation testset delta (accuracy/score), customer-facing examples (before/after), percentage of calls classified as ‘regression’ by monitoring rules, and remediation confidence level.
- Partial availability / degraded throughput -> translate to: minutes of reduced capacity, number of failed/queued requests, and effective availability percentage for the customer during the window.
- Cost anomaly -> translate to: additional token spend, specific prompt patterns, tenant configuration that caused increase, and recommended guardrails.

Customer readout runbook (step-by-step):
1) Internal sign-off (T-72h): postmortem author and SRE sign the artifacts. CSM schedules the readout with customer and internal stakeholders.
2) Draft deck (T-48h): CSM drafts slides using the 6-slide template; include appendices with graphs and raw query samples.
3) Rehearsal (T-24h): 30–45 minute dry run with engineering and AE to align on answers to likely questions (root cause, regression probability, rollback options, ETA for fix).
4) Readout meeting: 30–45 minutes max. Suggested agenda: 5m exec summary, 10m technical but non-dense timeline, 10m actions and verification plan, 10m Q&A + next steps. Keep the readout focused on outcomes and customer verification.
5) Post-readout (within 48h): CSM publishes the slide deck and the public-friendly incident summary to the customer. Create/update a follow-up tracker in the customer’s onboarding board.
6) Checkpoint (T+14 days): Verify short-term mitigations; engineering provides status update and evidence (metrics, synthetic runs).
7) QBR inclusion (next scheduled QBR): One slide summarizing the incident, impact, mitigations completed, and remaining open items with owners.

Acceptance criteria for customer sign-off (examples):
- Short-term mitigation validated by both engineering (SRE) and customer via agreed synthetic test (pass criteria: <X% error over 24h; configurable per customer).
- Long-term fix scheduled into product/infra backlog with a committed target quarter and owner assigned.
- Any commercial remediation (credits, SLA adjustments) agreed and captured in the renewal/billing system.

Templates and language guidance (do/don’t):
- Do: Use plain language first, then technical appendix. Lead with the impact to the customer and what we have done about it.
- Do: Provide concrete verification (metrics, test names, runbook checks).
- Don’t: Overuse internal jargon in the customer-facing slides. Avoid speculative language (e.g., 'probably', 'might').
- Don’t: Dump raw logs into the readout — include curated examples in the appendix instead.

Example translation (short):
Internal postmortem finding: "KV cache eviction race under heavy prefix fanout caused N+1 model loads between 11:12–11:41 UTC, increasing P99 latency from 420ms to 1.8s for /v1/stream."
Customer QBR translation: "Between 11:12–11:41 UTC we observed a cache coordination issue that temporarily increased tail latency for streaming responses used by your search feature. Approximately 3.2% of requests served hit the degraded window, resulting in elevated P99 (1.8s vs normal 0.42s). We deployed config changes (KV cache backoff and faster rehydration) and are monitoring; a long-term fix (improved cache coordination and bakeoff) is scheduled for the next release. A synthetic test is in place and will be shared for customer verification."

Communication templates (short):
- Readout invite subject: "Readout: [Incident name] — impact summary and next steps"
- Readout invite body: "Hi <Customer>, we’d like to schedule a 30-minute readout to review the incident on <date>. We will cover impact, immediate mitigations, and proposed next steps. Please invite any technical stakeholders who should sign off on the verification plan."
- Post-readout email subject: "Follow-up: [Incident name] — artifacts and verification plan"

Tracking and verification fields (example table - store in customer board):
- item_id | short_description | owner | due_date | verification_method | status
- PM-101 | KV cache fix scheduled | Eng-Cache | 2026-12-15 | E2E synthetic v2 pass | open
- CS-202 | Customer synthetic verification | CSM-Jane | 2026-11-30 | Shared test run and screenshot | in_progress

Escalation and sensitivity notes:
- If the incident has regulatory or data-exposure implications, escalate to Security and Legal immediately and adjust customer messaging to ‘restricted’ confidentiality.
- For incidents with contractual SLA impacts, involve Finance and Sales leaders before the readout to pre-clear commercial remediation options.

Metrics and artifacts to attach to the readout (required):
- Tenant-level availability and latency time series (P50/P95/P99).
- Synthetic test results before/after mitigation.
- Short curated log snippets and query samples (appendix).
- Postmortem link and the public-friendly incident summary.

Follow-up governance and closure criteria:
- All action items must have owners and dates and be tracked in the customer’s board.
- CSM verifies short-term mitigations within 14 days and marks the checklist items green when verified.
- Long-term fixes are tracked quarterly; any slip requires notification in the next scheduled QBR.

Related playbooks and templates:
- QBR slide templates (internal asset link)
- Incident postmortem template (eng-sre)
- Customer synthetic validation guide (integration-guides)

Appendix: Example Q&A prep (anticipated questions and suggested answers):
Q: "How likely is recurrence?"
A: "We have applied a short-term mitigation that reduces the known attack surface and put a synthetic monitor in place. Probability is low in the short term; the long-term fix will remove the root cause and is scheduled for Q1. We will provide a confidence update after the T+14 validation."

Q: "Will my usage bill be affected?"
A: "We have evaluated the token spend impact for the incident window and will surface any credit recommendation if the customer experienced material additional cost. Commercial remediation requires AE and Finance approval and will be captured in the follow-up tracker."

Document ownership and updates:
Owner: Customer Success (CSM guild).
Update cadence: Review after every readout that includes technical incidents; refresh template quarterly or when guidance changes.

End of playbook.

title: Activation Milestones and Customer Health Playbook
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the activation milestones, customer health scoring model, routine health-check procedures, and handoff steps for Enterprise customers during the first 180 days (Day 0 -> Day 180). It is intended for CSMs, Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and Onboarding Eng teams.

Scope: Applies to Dedicated and Private deployment customers and to any Hosted customers with enterprise contracts where the CSM is assigned.

Why this matters
- Early detection of friction reduces time-to-value and lowers incident risk.
- Consistent activation milestones improve predictability for Renewals and Expansion.
- A single, measurable health model aligns cross-functional teams on priorities.

Owner & Contacts
- Playbook owner: Samira Patel (Customer Success Director)
- Onboarding lead (SE): Ethan Park
- Support escalation liaison: Priya Raman
- Engineering on-call for initial rollout: eng-platform-oncall@redwood.ai

Activation milestones (Day 0 -> Day 90)
1. Pre-kickoff (Day -14 -> 0)
   - Contract & infrastructure checklist completed by CSM. Required items: PO on file, network allowlist, KMS/HSM details (if private), estimated throughput and peak RPS, compliance requirements (DPA/BAA where applicable).
   - Deliverables: Welcome packet, onboarding calendar (weekly cadence), invite to shared Slack channel.

2. Kickoff (Day 0) — 60–90 minute meeting
   - Attendees: CSM, customer engineering lead, SE, Security/Network SME, Support liaison.
   - Objectives: Confirm success criteria, SLO expectations, data flows, initial test plan, and rollback/fallback strategy.
   - Outputs: Kickoff minutes uploaded to customer page and action items assigned in Jira (label: onboarding/<customer-shortname>).

3. Test deployment & baseline validation (Day 1 -> 14)
   - SE to run baseline inference tests (throughput, p95 latency, memory) with customer workloads or representative samples.
   - Required baseline metrics: p50, p95 latency < agreed SLO (default 150ms p95 for dedicated small tier), token cost estimate, error rate < 0.5%.
   - Deliverable: Baseline report (template below) and recommended config: batching policy, kv-cache TTL, model quantization profile.

4. Integration & usage ramp (Day 14 -> 60)
   - Customer integrates SDK/REST endpoints, implements retry/backoff per support guidance, and enables streaming where relevant.
   - SE recommends production routing policy (primary model + fallback variant) and autoscaling thresholds.
   - Weekly checkpoints: CSM + SE sync. Escalate to eng-platform if test failures persist >48h.

5. Operational validation & go-live readiness (Day 60 -> 90)
   - Run canary traffic at 5–10% for 48–72 hours. Monitor health signals (see Health Metrics).
   - Confirm SLO readiness and cost estimates; complete runbook handoff to customer ops + Redwood SRE.

6. Post-go-live optimization (Day 90 -> 180)
   - Redwood Optimize recommendations applied (batching, cache, quantization) and tracked.
   - Prepare QBR (see QBR cadence section). Capture expansion signals.

Health metrics and scoring model
Overview: Health is a weighted score (0-100). Thresholds: Healthy >= 80, Watch 60–79, At-Risk < 60. Use this score to trigger Playbook actions (playbooks for Watch and At-Risk included below).

Health score components (weights):
- Usage adoption (30%) — MAU or weekly active sessions vs. expected plan (normalized 0–100).
- Reliability (25%) — SLO compliance (p95 latency and error rate) over the last 14 days.
- Cost predictability (15%) — Deviation of actual token spend vs. forecasted monthly run-rate.
- Feature coverage (10%) — % of agreed integration surface completed (webhooks, streaming, tool calling).
- Support health (10%) — open P1/P2 tickets, MTTR.
- Customer sentiment (10%) — CSAT from onboarding touchpoints and anecdotal signals.

Calculation example (pseudocode):
- health = round(usage*0.3 + reliability*0.25 + cost*0.15 + features*0.1 + support*0.1 + sentiment*0.1)

Health metrics table (for CSM dashboard)
Metric | Source | Collection Window | Healthy Threshold
--- | --- | ---: | ---
p95 latency (in ms) | Runtime metrics / tracing | 14 days | <= 150ms
Error rate (%) | Runtime metrics / error-logs | 14 days | <= 0.5%
Active weekly clients | Usage analytics | 7 days | >= 80% of expected ramp
Avg token spend variance | Billing analytics | 30 days | +/- 20%
Open P1/P2 count | Support ticketing | 7 days | 0 P1; <=1 P2
Onboarding CSAT | Survey (post-kickoff / post-go-live) | 30 days | >= 8/10

Automated health queries (examples)
- Runtime p95 latency (Prometheus):
  curl -G 'https://prom.redwood.internal/api/v1/query' --data-urlencode 'query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[14d])) by (le, service))'

- Ticket backlog (Zendesk API):
  curl -s -u user:token 'https://redwood.zendesk.com/api/v2/search.json?query=type:ticket tags:customer-<shortname> status<solved'

Health-based playbook actions
1. Watch (score 60–79) — Trigger: weekly score in Watch for 2 consecutive weeks
   - CSM action: schedule technical health sync within 3 business days; prioritize top 3 impediments.
   - SE action: run targeted perf profile and provide tuning recommendations within 5 business days.
   - If no improvement in 14 days, create cross-functional incident review and escalate to Customer Success Manager Lead.

2. At-Risk (score < 60) — Trigger: score below 60 or a P1 incident
   - Immediate: CSM to notify customer and schedule a priority remediation call within 24 hours.
   - Support: open a P1 ticket and assign on-call engineer; aim MTTR <= 8 hours for infra-related issues.
   - Engineering: owner from eng-platform assigned within 4 hours.
   - Execute rollback/fallback policy if degradation impacts business-critical flows.

Communication templates
- Initial health alert email (CSM -> customer & internal):
  Subject: "Redwood: Health alert for <customer> — action requested"
  Body: "Summary of triggered condition, current score, immediate mitigation steps, scheduled remediation call (time), owner list."

- Internal escalation Slack template (channel: #cs-escalations):
  /create-escalation customer=<shortname> severity=watch score=72 owner=@samira

QBR and cadence
- 30/60/90 checkpoints (structured):
  - 30 day: Technical validation complete, baseline report accepted, initial health score recorded.
  - 60 day: Integration complete, canary pass, go/no-go decision.
  - 90 day: Go-live, baseline of production SLOs, initial Optimize recommendations applied.

- Quarterly Business Review (QBR) cadence:
  - Pre-QBR (2 weeks before): collect usage trends, cost delta, top incidents, CSAT. SE provides performance retrospective and Optimize outcomes.
  - QBR agenda: Exec summary, Adoption metrics, Reliability review, Cost & optimization plan, Roadmap for next quarter, Ask & support items.
  - Artifacts: QBR deck, one-pager action plan with owners and due dates (stored on customer Confluence page).

Runbooks & playbooks (links and attachments)
- Canary deployment checklist (attachment): steps to execute 5% canary, metrics to watch, rollback criteria.
- P1 incident runbook (support-process): escalation path, paging list, incident comms templates.
- Cost spike investigation playbook: telemetry queries, billing drill-down steps, temporary throttling guidance.

Ownership & SLAs
- CSM: overall customer relationship, adoption milestones, QBR owner. SLA: respond to health alerts within 1 business day.
- SE (Onboarding): technical integration, validation, baseline testing. SLA: action on technical escalations within 2 business days (urgent incidents within 4 hours).
- Support: ticket triage & resolution; P1 MTTR target 8 hours, P2 target 48 hours.
- Engineering (eng-platform): take ownership of platform incidents routed by Support; respond to escalations within 4 hours.

Templates and artifacts (copyable content)
1) Baseline report template (CSV/Markdown)
- Customer, deployment type, model(s), test date, p50/p95 latency, throughput, error rate, recommended batching/cache/quantization profile, notes/action items.

2) Onboarding calendar (sample week-by-week)
- Week 0: Kickoff, environment setup
- Week 1: Baseline tests, SDK integration
- Week 2–3: Integration & retries, build test harness
- Week 4: Canary & tuning
- Week 6–8: Scale to production traffic
- Week 12: Optimization & QBR prep

Operational notes & known workarounds
- Private VPCs: If customer reports intermittent egress connection resets when KV cache is enabled, recommend toggling kv-cache.ttl from 30s -> 10s and enable connection keepalives on client side as an interim workaround. Escalate to eng-platform for root cause analysis.
- Quantization-induced hallucinations: For customers using 4-bit quantized variants, if quality regressions appear on specific prompt families, pin to a higher-fidelity model variant for those routes and file a model-quality ticket with Applied ML team (label: model-quality/<customer>).

Measurement and reporting
- Dashboard: CSM Health dashboard (Grafana) updated daily by automated ETL. Manual health review monthly during CSM 1:1.
- QBR deliverables: deck, action items sheet, consolidated health score history (CSV).

Appendices
- Appendix A: Access checklist (required credentials, network ranges, KMS config, support contacts)
- Appendix B: Sample Jira labels and workflows for onboarding (use label onboarding/<customer-shortname> and component=onboarding)
- Appendix C: SLA summary table (P1/P2 MTTR, alert response windows)

How to use this doc
- CSMs: follow activation milestones sequentially and update the customer Confluence page at each milestone.
- SE: attach baseline reports and performance notes to the customer page.
- Support: triage tickets in the context of current health state; notify CSM on any P1/P2 creation.

Revision history
- 2025-01-15: Created by Samira Patel (initial draft).
- 2025-03-12: Updated health weights and Watch/At-Risk thresholds after pilot with three enterprise customers (reviewers: Ethan Park, Maya Lin).
- 2025-06-02: Published with added automation queries and runbook links.

title: Customer Migration Readiness Scorecard and Action Playbook
content:
Overview
========

Purpose: This document defines a repeatable readiness scorecard and associated action playbooks to evaluate enterprise customers prior to major migrations (model upgrades, Dedicated tenant cutovers, Private deployment go-lives). It turns qualitative readiness discussions into a quantified pass/fail state and prescribes concrete remediation steps for each risk tier.

Scope: Applies to any enterprise migration where the customer will experience user-visible behavior changes or infrastructure cutovers. Not intended for trivial config flips.

When to use this playbook
------------------------
- Pre-cutover health review (recommended 14 days before migration).
- Canary-to-production transition decision (after canary window).
- Escalation input for QBRs when planning major changes.

Success criteria
----------------
- Readiness score >= 85% => Green: proceed with standard cutover.
- Readiness score 65%–84% => Amber: require mitigation plan and extended monitoring window before cutover.
- Readiness score < 65% => Red: block cutover until corrective actions completed and re-evaluated.

Scorecard structure (summary table)
----------------------------------
Each category is scored 0–10. We compute a weighted score. Weighted categories and target thresholds are in the table below.

| Category                         | Weight | Acceptable threshold (Green)        | Evidence required (examples) |
|----------------------------------|--------|-------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| Telemetry & Observability        | 0.25   | Full coverage, P50/P95 dashboards   | Dashboards, queries, synthetic tests |
| Stability & Synthetic Validation | 0.20   | No silent degradations in 72h       | Synthetic job history, alert history |
| Security & Compliance            | 0.15   | All gates passed (SSO, KMS, audit) | Audit logs, SAML test, KMS access test |
| Performance & Latency            | 0.15   | P95 latency within SLA              | Perf benchmark results, profiled traces |
| Cost & Quota                     | 0.10   | Cost guardrails, quota presets in place | Billing preview, quota config screenshots |
| Operational Runbooks & Staffing  | 0.10   | On-call documented and trained      | Runbook links, oncall roster, tabletop notes |
| Stakeholder Alignment & Signoff  | 0.05   | Executive and technical signoff     | Signed email / ticket approvals |

Scoring rubric
--------------
1. For each category assign 0–10 points using the guidance in the Evidence required column.
2. Multiply by the weight and sum to produce a final percent score (0–100).
3. Document the subjective risk notes for each category.

Example scoring calculation (short):
- Telemetry: 8/10 * 0.25 = 2.0
- Stability: 6/10 * 0.20 = 1.2
- Security: 9/10 * 0.15 = 1.35
- Performance: 8/10 * 0.15 = 1.2
- Cost: 7/10 * 0.10 = 0.7
- Runbooks: 6/10 * 0.10 = 0.6
- Stakeholders: 10/10 * 0.05 = 0.5
Total = 7.55 -> 75.5% => Amber.

Detailed category checks and remediation playbooks
------------------------------------------------
Telemetry & Observability (owner: CS-observability-engineer)
- Required checks:
  - P50/P95 latency dashboard exists for affected routes and models.
  - Error-rate, 4xx/5xx, and tokenized-error events tracked.
  - Synthetic journeys (happy path + two edge cases) running every 5 minutes with alerting.
  - Correlation between request_id and customer_request_id in traces.
- Telemetry assertions (examples you can copy):
  - avg(request_latency_ms{tenant=\"ACME\"}[15m]) < 200
  - increase(rate(error_count_total{tenant=\"ACME\"}[10m])) < 3x baseline
  - synthetic_success_rate{scenario=\"invoice_parse\"} > 0.99 over 24h
- Remediation steps (Amber):
  1. Instrument missing metrics using the ingestion helper: curl -X POST $OBS_INGEST_URL -d '{"metric": "synthetic_success", "tenant": "ACME"}'
  2. Add quick dashboards via template: /dashboards/templates/latency-tenant-template -> copy + update tenant filter.
  3. Re-run synthetic suite and wait 24 hours before re-score.

Stability & Synthetic Validation (owner: CS-reliability-lead)
- Required checks:
  - No silent degradation in last 72 hours (trend-based detection).
  - Canary tests exercised with production-like payloads for min 48 hours.
  - No surge-induced queueing or token-throttles in logs.
- Canary validation checklist (executable):
  1. Seed canary traffic at 1% of production for 24h, then 5% for 24h.
  2. Compare model output quality on guarded prompts (sample set of 250 prompts); flag regression > 2% by eval harness.
  3. Verify KV-cache hit-rate remains within 10% of baseline.
- Remediation (Amber):
  - Reduce canary traffic and extend observation window; introduce gradual route weight increase script.
  - If output-quality regression observed: revert candidate model to previous model for canary and open model-quality ticket.

Security & Compliance (owner: Security-Integrations)
- Required checks:
  - SSO/SAML authentication end-to-end test signed off.
  - KMS/HSM integration tested for key unwrap on sample workloads.
  - Audit logging enabled for all tenant-sensitive endpoints.
- Evidence examples:
  - SAML assertion capture screenshot.
  - KMS access logs showing UnwrapKey actions for tenant.
- Remediation (Red/Amber):
  1. Block cutover if KMS tests fail or if audit logging is incomplete.
  2. Run security dry-run with Security-Integrations team and re-check.

Performance & Latency (owner: Platform-performance)
- Required checks:
  - P50 and P95 latencies measured under production-shaped synthetic load.
  - Memory and GPU utilization profiles during load test captured.
  - SLOs: P95 < 600ms for interactive routes; batch routes P95 < 1200ms (customize per customer SLA).
- Load test commands (example):
  - ./loadgen --target-endpoint https://api.redwood.example/tenant/ACME/generate --concurrency 50 --duration 30m --payload-file samples.json
- Remediation (Amber):
  - Tune batching and concurrency knobs; update autoscaler target from 70%->60% if resource pressure observed.
  - Consider temporary capacity bump (Dedicated burst) for cutover window.

Cost & Quota (owner: CS-finops)
- Required checks:
  - Billing-preview run for projected model consumption for 14 days post-cutover.
  - Quota & rate-limit presets aligned with customer's SLAs and cost-guardrails.
- Evidence examples:
  - Billing preview CSV attached to migration ticket.
  - Quota config screenshot from tenant admin.
- Remediation (Amber):
  - Apply conservative rate limits or token caps for first 72 hours.
  - Enable automated quota alerts to oncall and CS-finops.

Operational Runbooks & Staffing (owner: CS-ops)
- Required checks:
  - Runbooks linked in migration ticket for rollback, failback, and incident triage.
  - On-call rotation and primary/secondary names listed with pager numbers.
  - Tabletop tabletop noted (one simulated cutover rehearsal within 7 days).
- Runbook checklist snippet:
  1. Rollback command set: tenant_switch --tenant ACME --model old-model-id --force
  2. Diagnostic bundle collection: /scripts/collect-tenant-bundle.sh ACME -> artifact uploaded to ticket.
  3. Customer communication templates present and approved.

Stakeholder Alignment & Signoff
------------------------------
- Required signoffs: Technical lead (customer), Technical lead (Redwood CS/Platform), Security approver (if private/delegated), Commercial approver for any temporary pricing changes.
- Signoff template (copy into ticket):
  - Technical lead (customer): [name] - APPROVED / NEEDS_WORK
  - Redwood platform lead: [name] - APPROVED / NEEDS_WORK
  - Security: [name] - APPROVED / NEEDS_WORK
  - Finance (if applicable): [name] - APPROVED / NEEDS_WORK

Automated gating and CI enforcement
----------------------------------
- We integrate the scorecard into the migration ticket workflow via a checklist macro. If score < 65% the ticket status auto-blocks through the CI rule: migration_gate :fail. If Amber (65–84%) the migration_gate returns soft-block with required mitigation checklist attached.
- Implementation note for engineers: the migration checker reads a YAML artifact stored in the ticket as follows: 
  - readiness_score: 75
  - blockers: ["canary_quality_regression"]
  - owner: "CS-reliability-lead"

Cutover runbook (high level)
---------------------------
1. Pre-cutover (T-48h): final smoke synthetic run, verify dashboards, confirm on-call.
2. Pre-cutover (T-2h): freeze config changes, create final snapshot of model config and KV cache metadata.
3. Cutover (T0): route weight shift in 3 steps: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with validation windows (10m, 20m, 30m).
4. Observe (T0 + 0–24h): telemetry assertions monitored; pager escalation on any P95 regression > 20% or error_rate spike > 0.5%.
5. Post-cutover (T+24–72h): cost preview re-run and customer QBR notification for final signoff.

Rollback criteria (must be explicit)
-----------------------------------
Trigger an automatic rollback if any of the following happen within the first 24 hours after reaching 100%:
- P95 latency increases > 2x baseline and absolute P95 > SLA threshold.
- Error rate (5xx) increases > 0.5% absolute and sustained for 10m.
- Synthetic success rate drops below 97% for the primary scenario over 30m.
- Customer visible quality regression flagged by their technical lead and reproduced by CS QA.

Escalation matrix (contact order)
--------------------------------
1. On-call Engineer (Platform) — 15 minutes to acknowledge.
2. CS Reliability Lead — 30 minutes to engage with customer.
3. Product/Model Owner — 60 minutes to provide root cause guidance.
4. Security — immediate if any PII/data-access concerns.
5. Executive on-call — for degraded SLA incidents longer than 4 hours.

Post-mortem and QBR integration
-------------------------------
- For any cutover that required rollback or produced an incident with customer impact, create a 72-hour incident summary and a 30-day technical retro. Feed outcomes into the next customer QBR: include readiness score history, mitigations performed, and updated risk posture.

Appendix: Example queries, commands, and artifacts
--------------------------------------------------
- Synthetic run command (example):
  - curl -X POST https://ci.redwood.example/synthetics/run -d '{"tenant":"ACME","suite":"invoice_parse","duration_minutes":60}'
- Example PromQL snippets:
  - p95_latency_ms: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{tenant=\"ACME\"}[5m])) by (le))
  - error_rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant=\"ACME\", status=~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant=\"ACME\"}[5m]))
- Templates and artifacts to attach to a migration ticket:
  - billing-preview.csv
  - synthetic-summary-<date>.json
  - runbook-links.txt
  - signed-approvals.pdf

Contacts and ownership quick reference
-------------------------------------
- CS Migration Lead: Nina Kaur (nina@redwood.example)
- CS Reliability Lead: Liam Chen (liam@redwood.example)
- Platform Performance: Maria Ortiz (maria@redwood.example)
- Security Integrations: Elena Morales (elena@redwood.example)
- CS FinOps: Aaron Patel (aaron@redwood.example)

Change history
--------------
- 2026-03-15: Initial draft (Nina Kaur).
- 2026-06-20: Added automated gating section and PromQL examples (Liam Chen).
- 2026-11-02: Tuned weights and rollback thresholds; added contact roster (Elena Morales).

Related runbooks and dashboards
------------------------------
- /eng-platform/runbooks/migration-rollback
- /eng-platform/dashboards/tenant-latency-overview
- /customer-success-and-support/support-process/first-72-hours-post-go-live-stability-cost-controls-playbook-2027

End of document
