title: Governed Inference QBR: Metrics & Evaluation Framework
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document describes a repeatable, governed framework for quarter‑by‑quarter customer QBRs focused on inference health, LLM evaluation, and operational signals. The goal is to give Customer Success (CS), Engineering, and Product a shared set of metrics, evaluation artifacts, dashboards, and playbooks so QBR conversations are evidence‑driven and actionable.

Audience
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs) and Customer Reliability Engineers (CREs)
- Product owners responsible for model and feature roadmaps
- Engineering owners for serving runtime and telemetry pipelines

Scope
- Hosted and Dedicated customers; guidance includes private deployment considerations where telemetry may be delayed or sampled.
- Metrics span cost, latency, availability, quality (evaluations), and request patterns that drive economics.

Key Outcomes for a QBR using this framework
1) Shared indicator set with one golden dashboard per customer.
2) Actionable health classifications (Green/Amber/Red) with recommended runbook steps.
3) A reproducible evaluation snapshot (prompt set, baseline model, scoring summary).

Governed Metric Set (minimum required)
| Metric | Purpose | Owner | Frequency | Threshold (Amber) | Threshold (Red) | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| P50 P95 token latency (inference) | Customer perceived responsiveness | infra-serving | daily | P95 > 350ms | P95 > 700ms | Break out by route/model variant |
| Request success rate (2xx/total) | Availability signal | sre | 10m | < 99.5% | < 98.0% | Include 5xx and 429 rates separately |
| Tokens per USD (cost efficiency) | Cost economics | finance/cs | weekly | 10% degradation vs baseline | 25% degradation | Compute per-route and model family |
| Eval pass rate (gold prompt suite) | Quality regression detector | cs/product | per-release | delta < 2% | delta > 5% | See Eval snapshot section below |
| Embedding similarity drift | Semantic regressions in retrieval | product | daily | cosine drop > 0.02 | cosine drop > 0.05 | Compare to rolling 30d baseline |
| Prefix cache hit rate | Cost/latency optimization | infra | hourly | < 60% | < 40% | Indicative of prompt variability |

Data sources and instrumentation
- Golden dashboards must be composed from: API access logs, model runtime metrics (GPU tail latencies, queue lengths), cost attribution (token-level billing), and evaluation harness outputs.
- For Private deployments: collect the same artifacts via the customer telemetry agent; if sampling is required, include sampling multiplier metadata in the dashboard.

Evaluation snapshot (what to store for each QBR)
- Baseline model name and exact version (e.g., redwood/gptx-rlhf@2026-01-20)
- Prompt set: canonical list of N=150 prompts representing high-impact flows (attach as CSV).
- Scoring rubric: automated metrics (exact match/F1, BLEU for structured data, embedding cosine for semantic retrieval) and human annotations for top 10 failure cases.
- Eval summary: pass rate, false negative rate, top 5 failure prompts with short transcripts.

Example evaluation artifact (CSV header)
prompt_id,prompt_text,expected_label,model_version,automated_score,human_flag,notes

Dashboard templates and sections (minimum panes)
1) Executive summary: SLO status, cost delta, top 3 risks.
2) Latency & availability: heatmaps by region/model, P50/P95/P99.
3) Cost breakdown: tokens, embeddings, per-route unit economics.
4) Quality & evals: pass rate trend, per-prompt failure list.
5) Usage patterns: spikes, client SDK versions, burst sources.
6) Action items & owners.

Suggested SQL/BigQuery examples
- 7‑day P95 token latency per model\
```
SELECT model_name, APPROX_QUANTILES(token_latency_ms, 100)[OFFSET(95)] AS p95_latency_ms
FROM `redwood_prod.api_logs`
WHERE event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
GROUP BY model_name;
```

- Eval pass rate per release tag\
```
SELECT release_tag, COUNTIF(pass) / COUNT(1) AS pass_rate
FROM `redwood_prod.evals.results`
WHERE eval_suite = 'qbr-golden-150' AND event_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 90 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY release_tag
ORDER BY event_date DESC;
```

Health classification and recommended QBR actions
- Green: All core SLOs met. Action: continue trend monitoring; highlight positive optimizations.
- Amber: One or more SLOs breached at Amber. Action: open a short remediation ticket and schedule a 72‑hour stabilization plan (see Remediation Runbook).
- Red: Critical SLO or quality regression. Action: immediate incident coordination with CS, SRE, and Product; consider temporary model rollback or rate limiting.

Remediation Runbook (72‑hour stabilization)
1) Triage (within 1 hour): Confirm metric source; capture log window and sampling. Owner: CRE.
2) Containment (within 4 hours): If quality regression, pin production traffic to previous model version or enable fallback routing. If latency/capacity, enable burst capacity or autoscale policy. Owner: infra-serving oncall.
3) Mitigation (24 hours): Apply prompt-level mitigations (truncate inputs, enforce early-cache keys), adjust batching policy, or temporarily increase compute commit. Owner: engineering and CS.
4) Recovery verification (48–72 hours): Re-run golden evals, monitor pass rate and latency trend, and validate cost impact. Owner: CS + infra.
5) Post‑mortem and QBR action item creation.

Ownership and cadence
- CSM (primary): prepares customer narrative, highlights business impact, and tracks action items.
- CRE (telemetry & triage): provides data pulls, golden dashboard, and supports oncall during the quarter.
- Product (quality owner): curates the prompt suite and reviews eval rubric.
- SRE/Infra: provides availability/latency context and executes runtime mitigations.

QBR Preparation checklist (2 weeks before meeting)
1) Verify data completeness for the quarter (CSM + CRE). 2) Run the golden eval suite and attach results to QBR deck. 3) Confirm proposed action items and owners. 4) Smoke test the dashboard links and include reproducible queries. 5) Share pre-read with customer 3 business days before QBR.

Example action triggers (automated)
- Auto-create ticket when eval pass rate drops by >3% vs rolling 14d baseline.
- Create cost alert when tokens per USD drop by >15% month-over-month on a customer route.
- Auto-assign CRE when prefix cache hit rate < 40% for >6 hours.

Appendix: Template subject lines and pre-reads
- Email subject: "[QBR] Inference Health & Action Items — Q1 2026 — <Customer Name>"
- Pre-read attachment list: golden_eval_summary.csv, dashboard_links.md, cost_snapshot.pdf, proposed_actions.xlsx

Related standards and links
- See: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/instrumentation-standards
- See: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/release-notes/model-versioning-policy

Contact and escalation
- Primary CS contact: <assigned CSM>
- CRE oncall rota: /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-rotations
- Emergency escalation: follow enterprise escalation playbook (link in related_pages).

Revision history
- 2025-11-03: Initial draft (Aisha Khan)
- 2026-01-12: Added automated triggers and SQL examples (Liam O'Connor)
- 2026-02-08: Finalized remediation runbook and private deployment notes (Priya Nair)

title: LatticeBridge Support — QBR Account Brief (2026 Q1)
content:
executive_summary:
LatticeBridge Support is evaluating Redwood Dedicated to replace their in-house retrieval + Lambda-based reranker in order to increase top-5 answer precision and reduce per-query infrastructure cost for ticket deflection and agent assist. In Q1, the team completed a Dedicated POC on a 1M-document subset and validated latency targets for their NA interactive path, with measurable top-5 precision lift over their current Elastic + bespoke reranker baseline. Primary open items are finalizing VPC peering architecture approval, confirming data residency language, and aligning on a commercial model for burst traffic (light deflection checks) vs sustained full rerank traffic.

what_changed_since_last_brief:
POC moved from planning to completed benchmark phase (Dedicated POC executed on 1M-doc subset).
Close date slipped from 2026-04 to 2026-05 due to security review queueing and VPC peering design iterations.
Cold-start KV cache SLA concern narrowed: now focused on predictable warmup time after deploy/scale events rather than per-request cache misses.
Cost modeling updated to separate 'light deflection checks' from 'full rerank + generation' paths; customer accepted blended cost framing for QBR.

customer_goals_and_success_metrics:
Increase top-5 accuracy/precision enough to materially improve ticket deflection and reduce agent handling time.
Meet NA interactive latency: p95 retrieval + rerank under 200ms; soft p99 under 350ms.
Provide a transparent unit-cost model with a target blended average below $0.025 per full rerank query at scale, and a low-cost path for high-QPS deflection checks.
Satisfy security requirements: SSO (SAML), audit logs to their SIEM, KMS integration, SOC 2, and clear data residency commitments.

current_stack_and_context:
Customer currently runs Elastic for hybrid search with an internal retrieval layer and a Lambda-based reranker. The engineering team is experienced with Elastic and FAISS-like pipelines and is sensitive to vendor lock-in and portability. Their knowledge corpus includes tickets, KB articles, and community posts; average document size is ~3KB with steady growth.

scale_and_traffic_profile:
Knowledge index is ~12M documents today with expected growth of ~2M/year. Peak ingest can reach ~50k docs/day during major releases. Query traffic is split into two main paths: (1) lightweight ticket-deflection checks at high burst (historically discussed as up to ~5k QPS), and (2) full rerank + generation at lower sustained volumes (historically discussed as ~600 QPS). Updated Q1 discussions emphasized that burst deflection checks and sustained full rerank workloads will be priced and capacity-planned separately.

performance_targets:
Latency SLOs (NA interactive): p50 < 40ms, p95 < 200ms, soft p99 < 350ms for retrieval + rerank.
Throughput planning: support bursty light-check traffic and sustained full rerank workloads without tail-latency regression.
Cost targets: blended average target remains <$0.025 for full rerank queries; light deflection checks should remain materially lower cost than full rerank.

reranking_requirements:
Top-5 candidate quality is the primary KPI; customer previously cited a desired 12–15% improvement as a material operational win.
Reranker must allow configurable feature inputs (e.g., BM25 score, vector distance, recency, ticket metadata).
Prefer a CPU-friendly fast path with an optional heavier path for complex queries; must support A/B testing and automated rollback.

q1_poc_scope:
2-week Dedicated POC executed on a 1M-document subset. Benchmarked retrieval + rerank latency under representative NA load profiles and tested reranker configurations (CPU-first with GPU fallback for heavier rerank). Evaluated quality uplift against their baseline using a labeled query set provided during onsite benchmark preparation.

q1_poc_results_summary:
Latency: met NA p95 target for retrieval + rerank on the tested 1M subset under the agreed harness; tail behavior improved after cache warmup tuning.
Quality: achieved target top-5 precision lift versus baseline on the provided evaluation set (validated with customer scoring methodology).
Ops: customer requested additional documentation on KV cache warmup/eviction behavior and explicit rollback procedures tied to SLO degradation.

q1_poc_metrics_detail:
Customer-reported success criteria alignment: p95 retrieval+rerank under 200ms on the POC harness; top-5 precision lift at or above the agreed threshold; cost estimate within acceptable variance of the commercial quote.
Notes on methodology: customer emphasized production-like traffic mix and requested that we separate metrics for 'light deflection check' vs 'full rerank' paths in future tests.

open_blockers_and_risks:
Security sign-off on VPC peering architecture (network flow diagram and ingress/egress controls requested).
Data residency language confirmation for NA-hosted workloads and any operational telemetry retention.
Commercial: finalize burst traffic policy and any overage model for deflection-check spikes.
Perception risk: engineering skepticism around portability; needs a crisp story for export/migration strategy and operational transparency.

security_and_compliance_status:
Security kickoff completed in Q1. SOC 2 package and security FAQ provided. Customer requests remaining: finalized network flow diagram for Dedicated in their VPC peering model, confirmation of audit log forwarding format and integration guidance, and data residency guarantees. SSO (SAML) remains required for Console access. KMS integration is expected for encryption key control and rotation alignment with their internal policy.

next_steps_q2_plan:
Deliver final VPC peering architecture diagram and complete security review responses (target: early April).
Provide KV cache warmup/eviction documentation and an explicit rollback runbook tied to p95/p99 regression thresholds.
Run a short follow-up validation test focused on burst deflection checks (tail latency + cost) using the customer’s latest traffic assumptions.
Commercial: finalize order form with Dedicated capacity plan and an agreed burst policy; align procurement timeline to a May close.

customer_quotes:
Head of Product: "If we can get top-5 accuracy up 12–15% and keep p95 under 200ms, this is a material win for ops."
Security team: "We need the network flows and data residency language to match what we present internally—then we can clear the architecture."

timeline_q1_2026:
2026-01-18 — Technical deep-dive with SE (Diego): vector store costs, KV cache behavior, and reranker architecture.
2026-02-18 — Exec demo (Avery + Diego): reviewed latency SLOs and fallback policy; customer requested a Dedicated POC.
2026-02-25 — Security kickoff (Renee): shared SOC2 materials; customer requested VPC architecture diagram and residency details.
2026-03-01 — Onsite benchmarks requested: customer submitted sample traces and test corpus.
2026-03-14 — POC benchmark readout: reviewed latency/quality outcomes and identified follow-up documentation items.

internal_owner_notes:
Keep the narrative anchored on measurable outcomes: quality lift + latency compliance + predictable cost model.
Be proactive on portability concerns: provide export strategy and clear boundaries of managed components.
Treat KV cache predictability as an SLO-adjacent requirement; document warmup expectations after deploys/scale events.

title: Enterprise Adoption Accelerator - First 180 Days Ops Guide
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines a cross-functional, prescriptive operations guide to accelerate enterprise customer adoption during the first 180 days after provision. It is designed for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Platform Engineering, and SRE to coordinate a predictable path from provisioning -> stability -> value realization -> QBR.

Scope:
- Applies to Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) enterprise customers where Redwood provides onboarding support.
- Covers technical readiness, SLO/SLA alignment, telemetry gating, cost controls, training, and QBR preparation.
- Not a substitute for customer-specific legal or compliance requirements; use security gates documented in the enterprise compliance checklist.

Quick summary of phases:
1) Pre-provisioning (Days -14 to 0)
2) Provision & Cutover (Days 0–7)
3) Stabilize & Harden (Days 8–45)
4) Optimize & Expand (Days 46–120)
5) QBR Prep & Handoff (Days 121–180)

Owners & contacts:
- CS Lead: Maya Patel (owner)
- SE: Jordan Lee
- Platform Oncall: Carlos Mendoza
- Customer Dev Lead: <customer-contact>
- Security Gatekeeper: Priya Nair

Phase 0 — Pre-provisioning checklist (Days -14 to 0)
- Verify contract/tenant ID and region mapping with Finance (billing code).
- Confirm required networking (VPC peering, firewall rules), collect CIDR ranges, and exchange IP allowlists.
- Validate KMS/HSM integration requirements and key policies.
- Review model catalog and pin initial model families (e.g., rdx-7b-q4f) with customer for predictability.
- Create a shared runbook document in the customer repo and populate the following variables: tenant_id, contact_emails, escalation_phone, expected_peak_rps.

Pre-provisioning gating criteria (must pass before cutover):
- Networking test OK (ingress + egress)
- Auth provisioning validated (SAML/SCIM or API-key test)
- Telemetry contract agreed (metrics and traces endpoints)

Phase 1 — Provision & Cutover (Days 0–7)
Primary goals: successful traffic cutover with safety nets and initial verification of SLIs.
Key steps (ordered):
1. Provision tenant with reserved capacity or private control-plane configuration.
2. Run automated ingress smoke tests (see snippet below).
3. Enable monitoring hooks (per-route tracing, token-level billing stream) and confirm metrics flow.
4. Perform two staged traffic shifts: 5% -> 30% -> 100% (wait 30–60m between stages).
5. Execute customer acceptance tests (happy-path prompts and latency checks).

Example smoke-test curl command:

curl -X POST https://ingress.customer.example/api/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rdx-7b-q4f","input":"Hello, smoke test"}'

Acceptance criteria for cutover:
- 95th percentile latency within agreed SLO (example: p95 < 250ms for short prompts)
- Error rate < 0.5% for 30m after 100% traffic shift
- Token billing counters reported and reconciled with billing view

Phase 2 — Stabilize & Harden (Days 8–45)
Objectives: resolve early regressions, tune batching/kv cache, and enforce cost guardrails.
Stability checklist:
- Deploy per-tenant retry/backoff configuration (adaptive retry policy)
- Confirm KV cache warmup for conversational workloads (cache hit rate target >= 60% within 24h)
- Validate autoscaling behavior under a 2x synthetic spike (runload simulator ID: loadgen-1801)
- Apply rate limits and quota thresholds with notification hooks to CS and customer dev team
- Schedule a mid-30-day technical health review with SRE + CS + SE

Known categories of early failures and mitigation (examples):
- Symptom: Sudden p50/p95 spike after model change
  - Immediate action: rollback to pinned model in control plane (owner: SE).
- Symptom: High token usage unexpectedly
  - Immediate action: enable soft throttle and trigger cost alert to customer and CS.
- Symptom: KV cache miss storm after restart
  - Immediate action: gradual ramp and pre-warm cache, adjust caching TTLs.

Phase 3 — Optimize & Expand (Days 46–120)
Focus: tuning for unit economics and broader feature adoption.
Tactics:
- Run prompt suite evals against production traffic sample to identify hallucination regressions.
- Suggest quantization/variant recommendations for cost-sensitive routes and validate quality impact on eval sets.
- Implement batching and request coalescing for high-throughput endpoints (target average tokens/req).
- Introduce model fanout for non-latency-critical workflows (lower-cost variants).

Optional experiments (A/B):
- Canary a q4f quantized variant on 10% traffic for 14 days, collect quality metrics via eval harness.
- Test prefix caching on highest-volume customer route and measure token savings.

Phase 4 — QBR Prep & Handoff (Days 121–180)
Deliverables:
- Compile QBR packet including: availability, latency, model performance (evals), cost breakdown (token usage by route), adoption milestones, and roadmap asks.
- Actionable items: 1–3 prioritized ops or product changes with owners and due dates.
- Handoff checklist: transfer technical ownership to customer success long-term owner and document runbook escalation links.

QBR metrics mapping (recommended):
| Customer outcome | Internal metric | Threshold / target |
|---|---|---|
| Responsiveness | p95 latency / route | < agreed SLO (e.g., 250ms) |
| Reliability | Error rate / day | < 0.5% |
| Cost efficiency | tokens per useful response | reduce by >= 10% vs baseline |
| Consistency | eval regression rate | 0 critical regressions |

Telemetry & gating rules
- Minimum telemetry to validate adoption: per-request latency histogram, token counts, model-version tags, and trace ID.
- Telemetry retention for the onboarding period: 90 days by default (longer for enterprise upon request).
- Gating rule examples:
  - If p95 latency increases > 40% over baseline for 1h -> auto-scale and notify SRE/CS.
  - If token cost delta > 25% week-over-week -> trigger cost governance review.

Escalation matrix (technical)
- Tier 1 (CS/SE triage, 15-minute response): CS Lead + Assigned SE
- Tier 2 (Platform SRE, 30-minute response): Platform Oncall (Carlos Mendoza)
- Tier 3 (Engineering & Exec notification, 60-minute response): Eng Platform Lead + CS Director

Communication templates (examples)
- Customer ops update subject line: "[Redwood] Week 2 – Cutover Health & Next Steps"
- Short status template (use in Slack/email):
  - Summary: 2-sentence overview of current state
  - Key metrics: p95 latency, error rate, token burn delta
  - Actions this week: 3 bullets with owners

Security & compliance checklist (minimum for go-live)
1. Confirm SAML user provisioning and least-privilege roles implemented.
2. Verify TLS termination location and certificate rotation policies.
3. Confirm KMS integration and key access audit events are flowing to the customer audit collector.
4. Run a scoped data residency verification test (if customer requires).

Cost-control guardrails
- Configure soft quotas per-route and per-tenant with automated notifications to CS and the customer budget owner.
- Enable token burn anomaly detection; default threshold 2.5x baseline within 24h -> auto-throttle to 20% and open investigation ticket.
- Recommend monthly cost review cadence during first 3 months.

Training & enablement plan
- Week 1: Developer ramp-up workshop (1 hour) — example prompts, rate limit behaviors, telemetry dashboards.
- Week 4: Runbook walkthrough and incident simulation (game-day).
- Week 8: Product feature enablement session (integrations, caching knobs, model tuning).

Runbook snippets & automation examples
- Safe rollback CLI example:
  redwoodctl tenant rollback --tenant-id <TENANT> --model rdx-7b-q4f --to-version 2026-02-01

- Telemetry query example (PromQL-like pseudo-query):
  sum(rate(redwood_request_errors_total[5m])) by (tenant) / sum(rate(redwood_requests_total[5m])) by (tenant)

Escalation play examples
1. If error rate > 1% sustained for 20m: notify CS, pause non-critical batched jobs, and open high-priority incident.
2. If p95 latency > SLO * 1.5 for 30m: enable emergency autoscale, rollback recent model change, and notify eng oncall.

Postmortem & continuous improvement
- At the end of the 180-day engagement, produce a joint retrospective with the customer including: incident log, cost delta analysis, feature adoption report, and 3 prioritized improvements.
- Keep a living action register (shared doc) and track closure within QBRs.

Appendix: Templates and checklists
- Provision readiness table (sample):
| Item | Owner | Status |
| Networking (VPC peering) | Customer NetOps | DONE |
| KMS access | Security Gatekeeper | PENDING |
| Initial model pin | SE | DONE |

- Customer acceptance test (short list):
  1) Submit 100 short inference requests and verify p95 < SLO
  2) Submit a 1000-token document generation and verify stability under load
  3) Verify billing events appear in token stream ingestion

Related references
- See: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/incident-oncall-quickstart (incidents)
- See: /confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/tenant-autoscaling-guidelines (autoscale)

Revision history
- 2026-01-18: Draft created by Maya Patel
- 2026-02-24: Reviewed and published after feedback from SE and SRE leads

title: Renewals and Scale Readiness Playbook — Enterprise Accounts
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines a structured program for (1) assessing enterprise accounts for scale readiness post-launch, (2) detecting renewal risk early, and (3) coordinating cross-functional remediation plans that reduce churn and operational surprises when customer usage grows. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support L2/L3, and Product/Platform stakeholders.

Goals:
- Ensure customers approaching renewal are operating within predictable cost and reliability envelopes.
- Provide a reproducible, score-driven renewal risk assessment that drives action items and engineering prioritization.
- Align scale-readiness remediation to measurable SLO improvements and cost optimizations.

Scope:
- Applies to enterprise customers with Dedicated or Private deployments and mid-market accounts with predictable Hosted usage > $10k/month.
- Excludes one-off POCs under $1k/month; those follow the standard onboarding checklist.

Quick definitions:
- Scale Readiness: Customer’s ability to increase traffic 2–5x without service degradation or >25% token-cost inflation.
- Renewal Risk Score (RRS): Composite score (0–100) combining health, cost, and reliability signals used to categorize accounts: Green (>=75), Yellow (50–74), Red (<50).

Owner and escalation path:
- Playbook owner: Customer Success Operations (CS Ops).
- Day-to-day: Assigned CSM owns customer comms and remediation tracker.
- Technical remediation: Platform SE owns backlog items for runtime/model changes.
- Escalation: For RRS Red, file a Severity-3 cross-functional ticket in JIRA and notify on #cs-urgent with tag @oncall-platform.

Signals and telemetry (inputs to RRS):
1) Service health (40% weight) — SLO adherence for last 30 days:
   - Availability SLO: 99.9% (target), measured per deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
   - Error budget burn: >10% monthly triggers caution.
   - Latency: P95 < 600ms for short-chat routes (<= 256 tokens), P95 < 900ms for long generation routes (>256 tokens).
   Example PromQL checks:
   - availability_30d = (sum_over_time(up{service="redwood-api"}[30d]) / 30) * 100
   - p95_latency = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/complete"}[30d])) by (le))

2) Cost & efficiency (30% weight) — Monthly token spend trends and per-token cost variance:
   - Warning: month-over-month token spend growth > 40% without matching traffic increase.
   - Cost anomaly query (example):
     SELECT customer_id, sum(token_count * unit_price) AS cost FROM billing.events WHERE month = current_month GROUP BY customer_id

3) Quality / Behavioral signals (20% weight):
   - Eval regressions from baseline prompt-sets (failure rate > 10% on key prompts).
   - Increased rate of human-in-loop corrections or re-roll requests logged with support.

4) Operational readiness (10% weight):
   - Customer has runbook and on-call contacts on file.
   - Backup routing/policy configured (fallback to smaller model family during outages).

Renewal Risk Scoring (calculation):
- Composite RRS = 0.4*H + 0.3*C + 0.2*Q + 0.1*O where H=health_score (0–100), C=cost_score (0–100), Q=quality_score (0–100), O=ops_score (0–100).
- Each sub-score is bucketed: Green (85–100), Amber (60–84), Red (<60).
- Example: A customer with H=78, C=62, Q=90, O=80 => RRS = 0.4*78 + 0.3*62 + 0.2*90 + 0.1*80 = 31.2 + 18.6 + 18 + 8 = 75.8 (Green).

Operational cadence (30/60/90 and renewal cycle):
- Week 0 (Go-Live): Handback call between SE and CSM. Handoff runbook completed and uploaded to customer page in Console.
- 30 days: Initial health check (CSM + SE) using the Scale Readiness Checklist below. Produce an action tracker with owners and ETA.
- 60 days: Progress review; re-score RRS and adjust priority backlog. If RRS drops to Red, trigger an emergency remediation sprint (see Escalation section).
- 90 days: Post-launch optimization (cost/perf) and QBR prep. Recommend scheduling executive QBR 30–60 days prior to renewal.

Scale Readiness Checklist (30-day exam):
1) Traffic profile baseline captured (per-route token distribution).
2) KV cache hit-rate >= 60% for chat workloads that benefit from prefix caching.
3) Autoscaling thresholds validated for 2x expected peak traffic.
4) Quantization profile in use for large model families that support it (int8 or int4 where validated).
5) Fallback routing policy defined for cross-region and model-variant failover.
6) Cost guardrails (per-route budgets) assigned in Console.

Common remediation play types and sample runbooks:
A. Latency spikes under load
   - Quick triage (CSM+SE within 24 hours): check P95/P99, queue lengths, GPU utilization.
   - Runbook steps:
     1) Pull last 2 hours of runtime metrics: `kubectl logs` + `prometheus` queries.
     2) If GPU saturation > 80% on Dedicated, switch to larger instance class or enable burst capacity.
     3) Enable short-term autoscaling policy: min_replicas += 2 for peak windows.
     4) Longer term: introduce batching and KV cache tuning. SE to file RFC for model kernel optimization.

B. Unexpected cost growth
   - Triage (48 hours): identify routes with increased tokens per request, regression in caching, or model family cost differences after model pin updates.
   - Immediate actions:
     1) Apply per-route rate-limits or quota ceilings in Console.
     2) Suggest model quantization and a lower-cost fallback model for non-critical paths.
     3) Recommend prompt engineering changes to cap max_tokens.

C. Quality regressions detected by evals
   - Triage path (7 days): run regression harness from applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks.
   - Steps:
     1) Reproduce failure locally with the same model+params.
     2) If caused by model upgrade, request controlled rollback or canary.
     3) Align with Research to produce micro-adjustment (prompt/template) and ship via rollback/canary.

Escalation matrix and SLAs:
- Yellow RRS: CSM to open action tracker; respond to customer within 48 hours; SE triage within 5 business days.
- Red RRS: Create JIRA P3 (technical) + P0 customer communication ticket; notify platform oncall; target remediation window 72 hours.
- Severity criteria for invoking executive attention: >3 customer-facing incidents in a 30-day window, or projected >20% MRR risk at next renewal.

Action tracker template (one-line per item):
- ID, Owner, Priority (High/Med/Low), Action, Acceptance Criteria, Target Date, Status, Linked JIRA.

Sample API snippet: (used by SEs to produce a usage export for customer)
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/usage/export -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY' -d '{"customer_id":"cust_123","range":"30d","granularity":"daily"}'

QBR content checklist (recommended slide deck sections):
1) Executive summary: SOW, ARR, renewal date, RRS and trend.
2) Operational health: availability, latency, error budget burn, incidents since last QBR.
3) Cost & efficiency: token spend, cost-per-1k-tokens, top routes contributing to spend.
4) Product roadmap: planned infra changes that affect customer performance or cost.
5) Action tracker with owners and progress.
6) Ask: renewal options, reserved capacity proposal, or commitment incentives.

Example renewal conversation triggers and offers:
- For customers with steady usage and RRS Green: propose 12-month reserved capacity discount of 10% with a 3-month early renewal credit.
- For Yellow accounts: offer a 6–9 month commitment with a performance SLA addendum contingent on remediation.
- For Red accounts: avoid renewal offers until remediation succeeds; focus on operational restoration and microscopically defined SLO milestones.

Templates (paste into Salesforce/CRM when logging findings):
- Subject: Post-launch 30-day Readout and Action Items — <Customer>
- Body: Hello <Name>, attached is the 30-day scale readiness report for <Customer>. Key items: RRS=<score>, actions: <list>. Next checkpoint: <date>. Owner: <CSM>.

Appendix A — Example queries and thresholds:
- PromQL: `sum(rate(requests_total{customer_id="cust_123"}[5m])) by (route)` — use to detect sudden traffic shifts.
- SQL: `SELECT route, avg(tokens_per_request) FROM usage WHERE customer_id='cust_123' GROUP BY route` — use to find cost drivers.

Appendix B — Ownership table:
- CSM: primary customer contact, owns action tracker and QBR scheduling.
- Platform SE: runtime tuning, quantization recommendations, and JIRA backlog owner.
- Applied ML: evals and regressions owner.
- Billing: pricing/commitment proposals and reserved capacity contracts.

Appendix C — Example acceptance criteria for successful scale-readiness remediation:
- P95 latency reduced to <700ms across top 3 routes for 7 consecutive days.
- Monthly token spend growth capped at <15% MoM while traffic grows expectedly.
- KV cache hit-rate > 65% for chat workloads where prefix caching applies.

If you have questions or need a template workbook (spreadsheet) for calculating RRS, contact CS Ops (cs-ops@redwood.ai) or open a ticket with the tag `scale-readiness`.

title: QBR action plan template for model quality regression
content:
Overview

This document is a repeatable QBR action-plan template to triage, contain, and communicate model quality regressions observed for enterprise customers. It is intended for Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and the Model Ops/Applied ML teams to prepare a concise, technical-to-executive handoff that can be reviewed during a QBR or an ad-hoc postmortem review.

When to use this template

- Any sustained customer-facing degradation in automated evaluation metrics (examples: eval score drop >= 5% relative, BLEU/ROUGE delta, semantic-similarity regression, or embedding downstream accuracy drop).
- Significant rise in customer complaints tied to model outputs (false positives/negatives, hallucinations, policy violations).
- Persistent customer-side error-rate or latency increase that correlates with model changes.

Quick summary structure (one-slide / one-paragraph target)

1. Summary: what changed, when observed, customers impacted (count & priority).
2. Impact: short list of user-facing symptoms and metric deltas.
3. Immediate containment actions taken (if any).
4. Next steps & owners (72-hour action plan).

Stakeholders and ownership

- Customer Success (owner): primary customer liaison, collects customer evidence and priority, coordinates QBR agenda.
- Applied ML / Model Ops (owner): investigative lead on model changes, checkpoints, and rollback.
- Platform / Runtime (owner): verifies infra/serving factors (cache, routing, quantization variants, autoscaler).
- Solutions Engineering: provides reproduction harnesses or prompt sets.
- Legal / Security (as required): if regression leads to data exposure or policy violation.

Detection and verification checklist (first 60 minutes)

1. Confirm alert provenance: determine whether detection came from automated eval, telemetry, customer report, or test harness.
2. Reproduce with canonical prompt set: run the canonical prompt set used for eval and customer seeds. Capture diffs.
3. Verify rollout history: query model rollout timeline, pinned versions, and canary status.
   - Example: runbook query: SELECT version, rolled_at, rollout_type FROM model_rollouts WHERE model = 'text-sim-1' ORDER BY rolled_at DESC LIMIT 5;
4. Check serving variant parity: compare outputs across host, dedicated, and private variants (if customer on Dedicated/Private).
5. Confirm telemetry signals: inspect the following (examples):
   - Automated eval pipeline: mean_eval_score by day (last 14 days).
   - Production request sampling: failure_rate, latency_p50/p95, token_error_rate.
   - Output quality heuristics: hallucination_score, policy_violation_rate.
   - PromQL example: increase(error_count_total{job=\"inference\",customer_id=\"CUST-123\"}[30m]) / increase(requests_total{job=\"inference\",customer_id=\"CUST-123\"}[30m])

Immediate containment (hours 0–6)

- If regression confirmed and customer impact high: pin customer to previous model version or route to a verified fallback variant. Owner: Model Ops.
- Increase sampling: enable high-fidelity request capture for affected tenants for 72 hours (obfuscate PII per privacy policy). Owner: Platform + Customer Success.
- Rate-limit risky traffic patterns if outputs cause safety violations. Owner: Platform / Security.
- Notify affected customers (template below). Owner: Customer Success.

Sample customer notification (first touch)

Subject: Service update — investigation into observed output changes

Hi <Customer-Contact>,

We are investigating a change in model outputs that may affect your service. Our initial analysis shows a regression in automated quality metrics affecting approximately <X>% of recent requests. We have pinned your tenant to a known-good model version while our team investigates. We will share a detailed timeline and remediation plan within 24 hours.

If you have specific examples please reply to this thread or upload them to the shared bucket: s3://redwood-customer-evidence/<customer-id>

Regards,
Aisha Patel, Customer Success

Triage and root-cause analysis (6–48 hours)

1. Re-run controlled A/B: run affected model version vs previous pinned version on representative seed set. Capture token-level diffs and confidence/entropy metrics.
2. Check model artifacts: commit hashes, tokenizer versions, quantization steps, and any export-time flags.
3. Evaluate config drift: request batching size, KV cache warm-starts, truncation lengths, and tokenization truncation.
4. Review infra signals: kernel fallback events, out-of-memory metadata, preemption logs, and autoscale spikes.
5. Confirm no data/regression introduced via prompt templates or input sanitizers in the client stack.

Root cause classification matrix (use one)

| Root cause category | Typical indicators | Remediation pattern | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model artifact regression | New model commit, metric drop in eval harness | Rollback to previous model; patch and re-run eval | Applied ML |
| Tokenizer/Preprocessing drift | Tokenization mismatch, different seq lengths | Re-align tokenizer, rebuild cache, re-evaluate | Model Ops |
| Serving variance (quantization/kernel) | Degraded samples only on quantized path | Serve from higher-precision variant; rebuild quant profile | Serving Runtime |
| Data-/training-distribution shift | Recent training data added, eval shift | Retrain with corrected dataset or mitigate via fine-tune | Research/Applied ML |
| Upstream prompt/contract change | New prompt templates causing output format change | Revert/normalize prompt, add validation at ingress | Solutions Eng/CS |

72-hour action plan template (deliverables and owners)

- Day 0–1: Containment (pin, sampling, customer comms) — Owner: Customer Success / Platform / Model Ops.
- Day 1–2: Diagnostic A/B, artifact review, infra check — Owner: Model Ops / Serving Runtime.
- Day 2–3: Fix candidate & test: either rollback or small patch + canary — Owner: Applied ML / Model Ops.
- Day 3: Customer validation & staged rollout plan — Owner: Customer Success / Solutions Eng.

QBR presentation structure (recommended slides)

1. Title slide: Incident/regression short summary.
2. Impact snapshot: customer(s) affected, user-visible symptoms, revenue/risk tier.
3. Telemetry timeline: eval-score, request volume, failure/latency, and sample outputs (before/after).
4. Root cause hypothesis & evidence.
5. Actions taken (containment & fixes) + status.
6. Risk & follow-up items (longer-term mitigations).
7. Acceptance criteria and rollback criteria for full rollout.

Metrics and thresholds to include in QBR

- Eval delta: relative drop in the chosen automated metric (e.g., mean_eval_score) — flag if >= 5% relative drop.
- Customer error reports: count and severity (P1/P2).
- Production mismatch rate: percentage of sampled requests where output differs meaningfully from canary baseline — flag if >= 4%.
- Latency and token error surge: p95 latency delta > 30% or token_error_rate > 0.5%.

Acceptance criteria for rollout back to production

- Automated eval shows improvement to within 1% of baseline across the canonical prompt set.
- Customer samples validated by Solutions Eng & CS (>= 50 representative samples).
- No recurring infra anomalies during 24-hour canary (no OOMs, kernel fallbacks).
- Observability enabled: alerts and synthetic checks for the next 14 days.

Follow-up prevention controls (long-term)

- Expand canary test harness to include customer-specific prompt sets for top-10 customers.
- Add preflight eval gating for quantized variants and tokenizer changes.
- Implement a ‘regression budget’ alert where cumulative delta across evals triggers a staged rollback.
- Strengthen QBR artifact template so every major model rollout includes an expected behavior doc and degradation scenarios.

Appendices

A. Example telemetry queries
- Eval trend (SQL): SELECT date_trunc('day', run_ts) AS day, avg(score) AS mean_eval_score FROM eval_runs WHERE model = 'prod-text-v2' AND seed_set = 'canonical' AND run_ts > now() - INTERVAL '14 days' GROUP BY day ORDER BY day;
- Sample diff (python snippet):
  ```python
  for seed in seeds:
      b = run_model(seed, version='prod-text-v2')
      a = run_model(seed, version='prod-text-v1')
      print(seed, compute_semantic_similarity(a, b))
  ```

B. Customer comms templates
- See the Sample customer notification above and the escalation email template in /confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/urgent-escalation-handoff-and-sla-triage-2026 for escalation variants.

C. Ownership contact matrix
| Role | Primary contact | Backup |
|---|---|---|
| Customer Success | Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai) | Riley Thompson (riley@redwood.ai) |
| Model Ops | Marcus Chen (marcus@redwood.ai) | Priya Kapoor (priya@redwood.ai) |
| Serving Runtime | Omar Reyes (omar@redwood.ai) | Linh Nguyen (linh@redwood.ai) |

D. Post-QBR follow-up cadence
- Within 1 week: publish short RCA with evidence bundles and action owners.
- Within 2–4 weeks: implement software hotfix or rollback and validate with customer.
- 30–90 days: incorporate preventative controls into release gating and QBR playbooks.

Document maintenance
- Owner: Customer Success (Aisha Patel).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after each major regression incident.
- Related pages: governed inference QBR metrics framework, model rollout guidelines, and incident postmortem templates.

title: Enterprise cost anomaly detection and action playbook
content:
Overview

This playbook defines detection, triage, and remediation steps for enterprise billing and inference-cost anomalies observed against Redwood-hosted or Dedicated/Private deployments. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Support Engineers (L2/L3), and the Cost Ops oncall. Use this document when automated alerts or customer reports indicate unexpected token spend, embedding usage spikes, or model-switch-related cost regressions.

Goals
- Detect large-cost deviations early (target: detect >20% day-over-day spend delta within 60 minutes).
- Reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) for cost anomalies to < 4 hours for Class A incidents.
- Preserve customer trust with clear comms and remediation options (credits, rate-limits, rollbacks).

Scope
- Applies to Hosted API calls, Dedicated capacity customers, and Redwood Private control plane billing events.
- Does NOT cover non-inference billing (e.g., storage-only charges) — see Finance billing runbook.

When to use this playbook
- Alert conditions met from the Cost Anomaly detector (see "Detection sources" below).
- Customer reports a cost spike or unexpected raft of usage in support ticket or QBR review.
- Rollout of a new model/quantization profile resulting in large unit-cost changes.

Detection sources (inputs)
1) Cost Anomaly Detector (CAD) — primary signal
   - Triggers when a 1-hour spend exceeds 3x the 7-day moving average OR a 24h spend delta > 50% vs prior 7-day average.
   - Enrichment: customer_id, project_id, model_variant, region, pipeline_id, request_bucket (chat/generation/embeddings).
2) Token-level telemetry from Ingest Pipeline
   - High tokens-per-request rate or sudden increase in long-context tokens (>5k tokens) causes per-token unit cost blowups.
3) SDK / Integration Alerts
   - Client-side exponential retries or misconfigured batching can flood endpoints; detected via >200 TPS sustained for 5 minutes above normal.
4) Manual customer report or finance billing anomaly

Alert thresholds and classification
- Class A (Critical): Customer spend projection >$10k over expected next 24h OR sustained x10 spike in per-minute spend.
- Class B (Major): 200%–1000% hourly spike OR unexplained 3–10x token-rate increase.
- Class C (Minor): <200% hour spike or localized to a single non-critical project.

Immediate actions (first 60 minutes)
1) Acknowledge and owner assignment
   - CS owner creates/update ticket, tags #cost-ops, assigns L2 engineer.
   - Communicate ETA to customer: initial update in 30 minutes, hourly thereafter.
2) Triage checklist (parallel):
   - Verify CAD alert details and enrichment fields.
   - Pull billing projection run for affected customer_id (Finance dashboard: /dash/billing/customer/{customer_id}).
   - Query request telemetry for last 2 hours: model_variant, route, client_ip, sdk_version, request_size distribution.

Runbook: triage and remediation steps (detailed)
1) Validate scope and confirm impact
   - Execute sample query (SQL-like) in Telemetry Explorer:

      SELECT timestamp, model_variant, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate
      FROM inference_requests
      WHERE customer_id = 'CUST_12345'
      AND timestamp >= now() - interval '2 hours'
      ORDER BY timestamp DESC

   - Identify top 5 request signatures by cost_estimate.
2) Identify root cause vectors (check each):
   - Model change: recent rollout, canary -> check rollout timeline and revisions in Rollouts console.
   - Prompt explosion: repeated retries or user prompts that append context in loop.
   - Integration bug: SDK infinite loop or retry storm. Check client sdk_version and recent deploys.
   - Config mismatch: batch_size or max_tokens configured incorrectly for embedding pipelines.
   - Billing/config mismatch for Dedicated/Private: check reserved capacity vs burst mapping.
3) Immediate mitigations (choose minimal customer-impact step first):
   - Apply per-route temporary rate limit (example CLI):

      redwoodctl routes set-rate-limit --customer CUST_12345 --route "/v1/generate" --rps 10 --duration 2h

   - Enable auto-throttle on offending model (console toggle) to cap tokens per request at 2,048.
   - For Critical incidents, perform on-path fallback to a lower-cost variant (same quality tier):

      redwoodctl rollout promote --customer CUST_12345 --from modelX-v3 --to modelX-v2 --immediate

   - If a dedicated customer is misrouting to hosted endpoints, update routing policy and notify infra.
4) Cost protection and credits
   - For confirmed platform side issues, CS to propose a temporary credit (finance approval required for >$5k). Use credit template: /templates/credits/cost-protection.

Escalation matrix and ownership
- L2 Support: initial triage, run Telemetry Explorer queries, implement temporary rate-limits (Primary owner).
- CS Manager: customer comms and approval for service-level mitigations.
- Cost Ops (oncall): model-switch suggestions, immediate rollback authority for Hosted.
- SRE / Infra: network or Dedicated routing and capacity issues.
- Finance: approve credits >$5k or contractual adjustments.

Escalation steps by severity
- Class A: escalate to Cost Ops and SRE within 30 minutes. Daily executive summary to be prepared for customers with >$50k impact.
- Class B: escalate to Cost Ops within 2 hours. CS manager to own customer comms.
- Class C: L2 to resolve; document findings in ticket.

Communication templates
- Initial ack (30 min):
  "Thanks for flagging this — we've opened ticket #TKT-XXXXX and an engineer is investigating. We'll follow up within 60 minutes with initial findings and next steps."
- Follow-up (after triage): include root-cause summary, mitigations applied, expected impact, and next milestone.
- Post-incident summary: structured RCA, cost impact table, and recommended prevention actions for QBR.

Prevention controls and long-term fixes
- Alert tuning: reduce CAD false positives by refining model-variant baselines and segmenting quotas by route type.
- SDK safe-guards: ship SDK 2.1.0+ with client-side batching guardrails and exponential-backoff caps.
- Template rate-limits: recommend conservative default per-route rate-limits for new customers (10 rps per route per project).
- Automated rollback policies: enable canary auto-rollback when unit-cost increases >200% after rollout.

QBR and reporting guidance
- Metrics to include in QBR slides:
  - 7-day and 30-day cost trend, normalized by monthly active routes.
  - Number of cost anomalies, MTTR, and total cost delta recovered.
  - Top 3 root causes observed and prevention status.
- Recommended cadence: include a Cost Risk slide in monthly QBR for all customers with >$10k monthly spend.

Operational dashboards and canned queries (Appendix)
- Dashboard names/locations:
  - Cost Anomaly Center: /dash/ops/cost-anomalies (primary)
  - Customer Billing Snapshot: /dash/billing/customer/{customer_id}
  - Token Distribution Explorer: /dash/telemetry/token-dist

- Example time-series alert (PromQL-like pseudo):
  - cost_rate_by_customer[1h] > 3 * avg_over_time(cost_rate_by_customer[7d])

Post-incident actions (within 72 hours)
1) Root Cause Analysis (RCA) doc: owner = L2 engineer. Include timeline, query outputs, config diffs, and mitigation rationale.
2) Permanent remediation: schedule engineering ticket for SDK fix, rate-limit defaults, or rollout policy change.
3) Customer-facing summary and credit reconciliation (if applicable).
4) Update detection rules and dashboards to reduce recurrence.

Appendix: example SLAs and thresholds
| Metric | Warning threshold | Critical threshold | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Hourly spend vs 7-day MA | > 50% | > 300% | Cost Anomaly detector / Cost Ops |
| Sustained TPS (5m) vs baseline | > 2x | > 10x | Telemetry / SRE |
| Token size per request | > 2,048 tokens | > 10,000 tokens | Runtime / Serving team |

Appendix: quick-reference CLI snippets
- Temporarily limit route:
  redwoodctl routes set-rate-limit --customer CUST_12345 --route "/v1/embed" --rps 20 --duration 4h
- Promote rollback:
  redwoodctl rollout rollback --customer CUST_12345 --model modelY --to-revision modelY-v12

Related resources
- Cost Anomaly detector design doc: /confluence/eng-platform/roadmap/cost-anomaly-detector-2025
- Billing and credits policy: /confluence/finance-and-legal/billing/credits-policy-2024
- SDK batching guidance: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides/safe-batching-v2

Ownership and contacts
- CS owner (playbook custodian): Maya Alvarez (maya@redwood.example.com)
- Cost Ops oncall: see /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-schedule
- Finance approver: Angela Boyd (angela@redwood.example.com)

Change log
- 2026-01-10: Created (M. Alvarez)
- 2026-02-15: Added CLI snippets and clarified credit thresholds (E. Cole)

End of document

title: Customer Onboarding: SLO–Contract Mapping and QBR Calibration
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a repeatable process for translating enterprise contract commitments (SLA / SLO clauses) into operational SLOs, telemetry contracts, alert thresholds, and the Quarterly Business Review (QBR) calibration agenda. It is intended for Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and EngOps stakeholders responsible for onboarding enterprise customers with Dedicated or Private deployments.

Goals:
- Ensure every contractual SLA/SLO has an unambiguous operational mapping to metrics and alerts.
- Produce a calibrated QBR agenda that highlights contractual compliance, trends, and actionable remediation steps.
- Reduce post-go-live churn caused by misaligned expectations between contract language and telemetry.

Scope and Audience:
- Scope: Redwood-hosted Dedicated and Private deployments; multi-tenant customers with contractual SLOs; QBRs for customers > $100k ARR.
- Audience: CSMs, SEs, EngOps, SRE liaison, customer technical leads.

Prerequisites (Before using this playbook):
1) Signed Service Agreement with SLO/SLA clauses and penalties.
2) Customer onboarded to telemetry forwarding (metrics + traces + logs) or Redwood-managed telemetry ingestion setup.
3) Assigned Redwood owners: CSM, SE, EngOps engineer, and Onsite/Customer success contact.

Definitions (short):
- SLA: Legal commitment in contract (uptime, response time guarantees).
- SLO: Operational objective measured by telemetry (e.g., p99 inference latency <= X ms).
- Error budget: Allowable window for SLO misses over evaluation period.
- Telemetry contract: The list of metrics, tags/labels, traces, and logs the customer and Redwood agree to exchange and retain.

1) One-page mapping template (mandatory)
Populate the following table and attach to the customer onboarding packet. Use concrete metric names and queries.

| Contract clause (verbatim) | Operational SLO (human) | Metric name | Aggregation/window | Alert threshold | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| "API availability 99.95% monthly" | API availability >= 99.95% per calendar month | system.uptime.redwood-api | availability/month | < 99.95% -> P2 oncall + notify CSM | EngOps (api-team) |
| "Median latency under 120ms" | request.latency.p50 <= 120ms (rolling 7d) | request.latency.p50.redwood-api | p50/7d rolling | > 120ms for 30m -> P2 | Runtime Observability |
| "99th percentile inference latency < 2s" | inference.p99 < 2000ms (1h) | model.inference.latency.p99 | p99/1h | > 2000ms for 15m -> P1 | Serving Runtime |

Notes on the template: enter exact MQL/PromQL/SQL snippets in the Metric name field if available and store them in the customer telemetry folder.

2) Telemetry contract checklist (must be executed during provisioning)
- Metrics: availability, request.latencies (p50/p90/p95/p99), error rates, kvcache.hit_ratio, batch.size distribution, concurrency per tenant, token_count_per_request.
- Traces: end-to-end request traces spanning API gateway -> routing -> model runtime, with a correlation id (trace.customer_request_id).
- Logs: structured error logs with error.code, error.stage. Include sampling policy for debug-level logs for high-volume customers.
- Retention: default 90 days for metrics, 365 days for aggregations (QBR-ready), 30 days for full raw traces. Any deviation must be explicitly approved and added to the contract appendix.

3) QBR calibration agenda (recommended 60–75 minutes)
1. Executive summary (5m): usage, ARR impact, top 3 wins/risks.
2. SLO compliance snapshot (10m): last 90 days, error budget burn, recent misses. Attach the one-page SLO mapping.
3. Inference economics (10m): tokens/day, avg cost per 1k tokens, trends vs previous QBR, recommendation for batching/quantization if cost drift > 12%.
4. Reliability and incidents (10m): top incidents, actions completed, remaining mitigations.
5. Capacity and scaling plan (10m): autoscale behavior, reserved capacity headroom, burst strategy.
6. Roadmap alignment (10m): product features that affect customer (e.g., new caching, kernel upgrades), expected impact and rollback plan.
7. Action items and owner sign-off (10m): explicit owners and due dates.

Deliverables for the QBR: updated SLO table (signed off by customer and EngOps), runbook excerpts for any outstanding mitigations, and a 3-point action plan with owners and ETA.

4) Alert and incident escalation mapping (short matrix)
Use this matrix to set alert severity and who is paged. Insert these rows into the customer-specific alerting policy in PagerDuty/Opsgenie.

| Symptom | Metric/Query example | Severity | Page | Escalation path | Customer notification tier |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| High 99th inference latency | model.inference.latency.p99 > 2000ms (15m) | P1 | Serving-runtime oncall | 15m -> SRE lead -> Eng RTE | Notify CSM (1h) if sustained 30m |
| API availability drop | availability < 99.95% (1h) | P2 | EngOps oncall | 30m -> infra lead | Notify CSM (1h) and AE |
| Elevated error rate | request.errors.rate > 0.5% (rolling 10m) | P2 | Runtime Observability | 30m -> SE triage | Initial email to customer technical contact |

5) Example telemetry queries and alert rules (copy-paste)
- PromQL: 
  - request.latency.p99: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, job))
  - availability: 100 * sum(up{service=\"redwood-api\"}) / count(up{service=\"redwood-api\"})
- Example alert (pseudo-YAML):
  - alert: HighInferenceP99
    expr: model_inference_latency_p99{tenant_id=\"{{tenant}}\"} > 2.0
    for: 15m
    labels:
      severity: P1
    annotations:
      summary: \"{{tenant}}: inference p99 > 2s\"

6) Contractual reporting appendix (what to include in monthly/quarterly compliance reports)
- Monthly uptime statement (ISO-8601 month window) with calculation method.
- SLO evaluation windows and raw data snapshots (CSV of time buckets for the quarter).
- Incident summaries mapped to SLO impacts (time lost, segments affected).
- Any compensations/credits calculation with detailed math and applied time windows.

7) Calibration and dispute process (step-by-step)
1. Detection: Customer or Redwood flags an SLO miss in QBR or via support channel.
2. Evidence collection (3 business days): EngOps exports raw telemetry, traces, and logs for the evaluation window. Owner: EngOps.
3. Analysis (5 business days): Runtime and SE analyze root cause and propose whether the miss is operational (Redwood responsibility) or customer-caused (network, tenant misuse).
4. Reconciliation (2 business days): Finance and Legal calculate credits if applicable.
5. Remediation and closure (ongoing): Implement runbook fixes, monitoring changes, and calendar follow-up in next QBR.

8) Runbook excerpts (examples to add to customer runbook)
- Safe degrade: automatically route to lower-capacity model variant when p99 > 2s for 10m (fallback policy ID: fallback-model-2025).
- Emergency quiesce: reduce non-essential batch jobs and dev-tier traffic during major capacity incidents.
- KV cache warmup: after model rollout, run cache-warmup script for top N prefixes (script path: /opt/ops/cache-warmup.sh).

9) Ownership and sign-off checklist (onboarding gate)
- CSM: Confirm SLO mapping table reviewed with customer.
- SE: Validate telemetry queries and access.
- EngOps: Configure alerts and retention settings.
- SRE liaison: Approve escalation matrix and on-call routing.
- Customer: Sign-off on one-page SLO mapping and QBR cadence.

10) Templates and attachments (references)
- One-page SLO mapping template (CSV).
- QBR slide template (PPTX).
- Example PromQL/SQL snippets (TEXT).
- Sample incident-to-SLO impact worksheet (XLSX).

Related pages:
