- Feature switch disable: temporarily turn off expensive features (tool-calls, multimodal pre-processing).
- Cache-only mode: serve responses exclusively from prefix/KV cache when hit rate is high.

Operator templates (one-command w/ revert)

1) Isolate non-critical tenants (weighting)
- Intent: free GPU cycles for high-value customers by reducing weight of low-priority slices.
- Command: trafficctl set-weight --slice hosted-free --region us-west --weight 0.05 --reason "latency-surge-2026-02"
- Revert: trafficctl set-weight --slice hosted-free --region us-west --weight 0.5 --reason "revert-latency-surge"
- Success criteria (10m): p95 latency in region decreases by >= 25% OR 5xx rate drops below alert threshold.

2) Model downgrade for a problematic variant
- Intent: switch traffic from model X-large-v2 to X-large-v1 (same token semantics).
- Command (rolling): redwoodctl rollout --service inference-router --from-model x-large-v2 --to-model x-large-v1 --percent 30 --wait 120s
- Revert: redwoodctl rollback --service inference-router --to-model x-large-v2 --wait 60s
- Notes: ensure KV cache compatibility; if caches are incompatible, prefer gradual route (10% increments) with cache warmup enabled.

3) Enforce conservative token caps for non-enterprise slices
- Intent: reduce runaway costs and tail token generation during degraded periods.
- Config snippet (example YAML):

slice_overrides:
  hosted-free:
    max_tokens: 256
    top_p: 0.95
    model_variant_preference: ["x-medium-q", "x-small-q"]

- Apply: redwoodctl apply-slice-config --file /tmp/slice-override.yaml --region eu-central --reason "token-cap-emergency"
- Revert: remove override by applying an empty override file or reapplying baseline config.

Runbook: step-by-step actions

1) Triage and scope (0-5 minutes)
- Confirm alert source and scope: check Grafana incident panel and query the last 15 minutes.
- Key queries:
  - High-level: sum(rate(requests_total{job="inference"}[1m])) by (region, slice)
  - Error rate: sum(rate(errors_total{job="inference",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{job="inference"}[5m]))
- Attach initial note to incident channel #ops/inference (automated template below).

2) Quick mitigation (5-20 minutes)
- If 5xx% > 3% for > 5m in a region: reduce weight of publicly uncommitted slices (see template 1).
- If p99 latency > SLAT (see SLOs below) and 5xx low: enable model downgrade for a small percent of traffic (template 2).
- Record action in incident channel with timestamp, command, and expected rollback.

3) Validate (20-45 minutes)
- Observe the dashboard panels for: p95/p99 latency, 5xx ratio, model throughput, KV cache hit ratio.
- Run synthetic canary requests to model endpoints to verify correctness and response shape.
- If degradation does not reduce load or error rate in 20 minutes, escalate to SRE lead and consider region failover.

4) Stabilize and cleanup (45-90 minutes)
- Incrementally restore weights or model variants once metrics are stable for 10 minutes.
- Publish a short incident summary to #ops/inference and tag the incident with the actions taken and links to dashboards.

Escalation and ownership

- First responder: inference-oncall (primary) — page SRE oncall roster.
- SRE lead: notify if mitigation unsuccessful after 30 minutes.
- Platform product: notify for any model downgrade that affects SLAs or committed behavior.

SLOs and metric thresholds (operator-friendly)

- Service availability: 99.9% monthly (objective).
- Error budget burn alert: if 1-hour rolling error rate > 0.5% absolute of monthly budget, fire an ops alert.
- Latency SLOs (hosted API): p95 < 350ms, p99 < 1.2s. Alert (page) if p99 > 1.5s for 10m.
- Region degradation trigger: 5xx ratio > 3% for 5m or sustained p95 degradation > 40% above baseline for 10m.

Prometheus alert examples

- Regional 5xx spike:
expr: |-
  sum(rate(requests_total{job=\"inference\",region=~\".*\",status=~\"5..\"}[5m]))
  / sum(rate(requests_total{job=\"inference\",region=~\".*\"}[5m])) > 0.03
for: 5m
labels: {severity=\"page\"}
annotations: {summary=\"Regional 5xx spike for inference service\"}

- p99 latency alert:
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(latency_bucket{job=\"inference\"}[5m])) by (le,region)) > 1.5
for: 10m
labels: {severity=\"page\"}

Dashboards and panels to add to incident view

- Region: p95/p99 latency panels (by slice).
- Error ratio (5xx, 4xx) by slice and model variant.
- Throughput by model and region.
- KV cache hit ratio and TTL distribution.
- Traffic weight changes timeline (audit log).
- Cost signal: 15m token spend rate and forecasted 24h spend at current rate.

Incident channel templates (Slack)

- Channel name: #incident-inference-YYYYMMDD-HHMM (automated).
- First message template:
  - Incident: high regional latency / errors
  - Region: eu-central
  - First responder: @oncall-inference
  - Initial metrics:
    - p95: 860ms (baseline 320ms)
    - 5xx%: 4.2%
  - Actions taken: reduced hosted-free weight to 5% (trafficctl)
  - Expected rollback: revert when p95 < 350ms for 10m
Operator verification checklist

- [ ] Confirm command executed and returned 0 exit code.
- [ ] Dashboard shows at least one target metric improving in 10 minutes.
- [ ] No customer-facing regression in enterprise telemetry.
- [ ] Attach logs and timestamps to incident ticket.

Post-incident retrospective starter (template)

- Summary of events (timeline).
- Actions taken and time to mitigation.
- What worked / didn't work with operator templates.
- Recommended permanent changes (config, autoscaling policy, capacity commitment).
- Owner and ETA for follow-ups.

Appendix A — CLI and script snippets

trafficctl examples:
- Set weight: trafficctl set-weight --slice hosted-free --region us-west --weight 0.05 --reason "latency-surge-2026"
- Show weights: trafficctl get-weights --service inference-router --region us-west
redwoodctl examples:
- Start rolling model switch: redwoodctl rollout --service inference-router --from-model x-large-v2 --to-model x-large-v1 --percent 10 --wait 120s
- Apply slice config: redwoodctl apply-slice-config --file /tmp/slice-override.yaml --region eu-central
kubectl quick checks:
- Health: kubectl -n redwood exec -it deployment/inference-router -- curl -sS http://localhost:8080/health
- Logs (last 200 lines): kubectl -n redwood logs deployment/inference-router --tail=200

Appendix B — Decision matrix (guidance)

- If 5xx > 3% AND enterprise errors increasing: isolate non-enterprise slices first.
- If latency high but errors low: favor model downgrade and cache-warmup.
- If cost spike detected without latency issues: apply token caps for free tiers and enable short term quota.
- If degradation persists > 60 minutes: schedule cross-team war room and consider region failover.

Contacts and ownership

- Oncall SRE: inference-oncall@redwood.ai
- Platform SRE lead: Ethan Park (ethan@redwood.ai)
- Runtime product owner: Sofia Martinez (sofia@redwood.ai)

Related reading

- Observability-driven traffic shaping and fallbacks playbook (internal)
- Runtime cost instrumentation and alerting (dashboards)

Notes

This runbook is intentionally prescriptive and conservative: operators should prefer the smallest-change action that is likely to restore SLOs. Update the operator templates when new trafficctl/redwoodctl flags are released or when SLAs are renegotiated.

title: Perf Canary: Synthetic Prompt Distribution (v0.4)
content:
## Overview
This page defines the **synthetic prompt distribution** used by the production performance canary ("perf-canary"). The canary exists to detect **p95 latency regressions** and **tokens/sec drops** per model (optionally per region/tier/SKU) with minimal noise and zero customer data.

The prompt distribution is intentionally **shape-focused** (token lengths, prefill/decode mix, and request patterns) and uses **template-generated, non-sensitive content**.

**Version:** v0.4 (current)

---

## What changed since v0.3
This revision keeps the overall design and bucket structure, but updates several workload knobs to reduce variance and improve coverage of newer request paths.

Changes:
1. **Request interface mix updated** to include a small, strictly bounded **tool/function calling** shape.
2. **Bucket weights adjusted** to slightly increase mid/long-context coverage (P2/P3) while staying within overhead targets.
3. **Decode tail weight increased modestly** to improve sensitivity to tokens/sec regressions.
4. **Streaming ratio reduced** to limit instrumentation-induced variance in end-to-end metrics (runtime-only metrics remain stream-independent).
5. **Overhead budget target tightened** (see Validation checklist).

Baseline note:
- v0.4 is **not baseline-compatible** with v0.3 for absolute latency; baselines must be recomputed per model family.

---

## Goals
1. Provide a stable, reproducible workload that approximates typical production request shapes:
   - Short chat turns
   - Medium instruction-style requests
   - Longer context (RAG-like) inputs
2. Exercise runtime performance characteristics that commonly regress:
   - Prefill attention (prompt length sensitivity)
   - Decode loop efficiency (generation length sensitivity)
   - Scheduler/queueing behavior (concurrency + mix)
   - Batching behavior (wide distribution of sequence lengths)
3. Keep the workload privacy-safe:
   - No customer prompts
   - No user identifiers
   - No training data excerpts

## Non-goals
- Measuring response *quality* (handled separately via eval harness and prompt sets)
- Matching every customer domain distribution perfectly
- Capturing multi-turn conversation state beyond 2 turns (initially)

---

## Constraints and safety rules
- **No customer data**: prompts are generated from controlled templates and synthetic text blocks.
- **No PII**: templates must not include real person names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, or account identifiers.
  - Exception policy: if a template needs proper nouns for realism, use only names from the internal **synthetic-name allowlist** (non-real, generated) maintained by Applied ML & Evals.
- **No secrets**: no API keys, auth tokens, or internal incident text.
- **Content neutrality**: prompts should avoid disallowed content categories that might trigger model safety filters unevenly across model versions.
- **Reproducibility**: prompt generator must be seedable; canary runs must be replayable.

---

## Workload model
The canary uses a mixture of request "shapes". A shape is defined as:
- Interface: chat, completion, or tool/function calling
- Prefill length bucket (input tokens)
- Target decode length bucket (output tokens)
- System/user template family (synthetic text)
- Generation parameters (temperature/top_p/etc.)

### Request interface mix
- **Chat**: 65%
- **Completion (instruct-style)**: 25%
- **Tool/function calling**: 10%

Rationale:
- Most production traffic is chat-like, but we keep completion coverage for older integrations and to exercise slightly different formatting/tokenization paths.
- Tool/function calling is included at low weight to detect regressions in structured-output formatting and the associated serving path, while keeping variance bounded.

---

## Prefill (input) length buckets
Input lengths are bucketed in **tokens** (post-tokenization). Bucket selection uses fixed weights (below), then the generator samples a specific length uniformly within the bucket range.

| Bucket ID | Token range (inclusive) | Weight | Typical pattern exercised |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| P0 | 16–64 | 0.18 | Short chat turn; low prefill overhead |
| P1 | 65–256 | 0.34 | Common instruction/chat requests |
| P2 | 257–768 | 0.26 | Medium context; batching interactions |
| P3 | 769–2048 | 0.16 | RAG-like context; prefill attention pressure |
| P4 | 2049–4096 | 0.06 | Long-context edge; KV/cache and kernel thresholds |

Notes:
- These ranges are tuned to keep GPU overhead within the perf-canary budget while still catching regressions in long-context kernels.
- Bucket weights are global defaults; specific models may override (e.g., long-context models can increase P3/P4).

---

## Decode (output) length buckets
The canary targets an output token count; the request uses max_tokens and stop conditions such that typical output lands in the intended bucket.

| Bucket ID | Target output tokens | Weight | Typical pattern exercised |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| D0 | 16–64 | 0.22 | Short answers; latency dominated by prefill |
| D1 | 65–256 | 0.45 | Most common generation lengths |
| D2 | 257–768 | 0.27 | Longer responses; decode efficiency and scheduling |
| D3 | 769–1024 | 0.06 | Tail decode; sustained throughput and thermal stability |

Rationale:
- Canary sensitivity to tokens/sec regressions improves when decode lengths include sustained decoding (D2/D3), but we cap the tail to control overhead.

---

## Joint distribution (prefill x decode)
We do not sample prefill and decode independently; we use a constrained joint distribution to reflect reality (very long prompts rarely request extremely long generations).

**Allowed pairs and weights (normalized within each prefill bucket):**
- P0: D0 0.58, D1 0.38, D2 0.04, D3 0.00
- P1: D0 0.26, D1 0.55, D2 0.17, D3 0.02
- P2: D0 0.14, D1 0.48, D2 0.33, D3 0.05
- P3: D0 0.10, D1 0.53, D2 0.32, D3 0.05
- P4: D0 0.14, D1 0.60, D2 0.24, D3 0.02

Rationale:
- Keeps the workload realistic and reduces variance from extremely long end-to-end sequences.
- Ensures the canary hits both prefill-heavy and decode-heavy regimes.

---

## Template families
Templates define the *content* without introducing variability that would overwhelm performance signals.

### Chat templates (65% of traffic)
All chat requests include a system message and a user message.

System message families (selected uniformly):
1. "You are a concise assistant. Answer with bullet points when appropriate."
2. "You are a technical assistant. Prefer clear steps and short explanations."
3. "You are a helpful assistant. If the request is ambiguous, ask one clarifying question."

User message families (selected with weights):
- (0.38) **Structured extraction**: asks to extract fields from synthetic paragraphs (non-sensitive)
- (0.34) **Summarization**: summarize synthetic text blocks (generated lorem-like technical prose)
- (0.16) **Planning**: generate a short plan for a synthetic scenario (no real entities)
- (0.12) **Light reasoning**: simple multi-step reasoning on synthetic facts (bounded)

### Completion templates (25% of traffic)
Prompt is formatted as an instruct-style completion:
- "Instruction: …\nInput: …\nOutput:"

Instruction families:
- Rewrite/shorten
- Create a checklist
- Convert paragraph to JSON-like keys (synthetic fields only)

### Tool/function calling templates (10% of traffic)
Tool calling requests use a single tool with a small schema and bounded output to reduce variance.

Tool family (selected uniformly):
1. **extract_fields_v1**
2. **classify_issue_v1**

Schema rules:
- Maximum 8 keys.
- Values are short strings or small arrays (bounded length), no free-form long text.
- No nested objects in the tool output content (enforced by the generator).

Rationale:
- Exercises structured output paths and serialization without turning the canary into a quality benchmark.

---

## Synthetic text blocks (for prefill length control)
To reach the target prefill bucket, the generator appends one or more synthetic paragraphs from a controlled corpus:
- Neutral, technical-sounding prose (e.g., abstract descriptions of systems, graphs, scheduling)
- Randomized but deterministic token sequences from a whitelist vocabulary

**Important:** The corpus is generated internally and reviewed to ensure it contains:
- No proprietary content
- No customer names
- No copied documentation text

---

## Generation parameters
Defaults (unless overridden per model config):
- temperature: 0.1
- top_p: 0.95
- max_tokens: derived from decode bucket upper bound (upper bound + 8 token slack)
- presence_penalty: 0.0
- frequency_penalty: 0.0
- stop: ["\n\nEND", "<END>"] (template-dependent)
- stream: enabled for 50% of requests
- seed: derived deterministically from (canary_run_id, model, region, shape_id)

Rationale:
- Lower temperature reduces variability in decode length and avoids occasional long rambles that distort tail latency.
- A small max_tokens slack reduces truncation artifacts at bucket boundaries.
- Streaming is included because it exercises buffering/serialization paths, but the ratio is reduced to improve stability of end-to-end metrics.

---

## Concurrency and pacing
Perf-canary runs continuously with a fixed per-target budget.

Default pacing per (model, region, SKU, tier):
- Target request rate: 0.1–0.8 RPS (config-driven)
- Concurrency: 1–6 in-flight (config-driven)

Notes:
- The scheduler is intentionally exercised with overlapping requests, but we cap concurrency to avoid canary-induced queueing dominating signals.
- If the canary is primarily measuring *runtime-only* latency, it will also emit queueing time separately so we can attribute regressions.

---

## What we measure vs what we control
Controlled by this distribution:
- Prefill token count
- Target decode token count
- Request mix (chat vs completion vs tool calling)
- Streaming ratio

Not controlled (and intentionally observed):
- Batching outcomes (batch size distribution)
- Queueing time under normal production load
- Kernel selection outcomes given real hardware + runtime version

---

## Rationale and design notes
### Why these buckets?
- Buckets align to known performance regimes where regressions have historically occurred:
  - Kernel changes around long-context thresholds
  - Scheduler heuristics sensitive to mixed sequence lengths
  - KV cache behavior changes when prefill dominates

### Why not mirror exact customer distributions?
- Customer distributions change over time (product launches, region shifts, SDK versions). The canary needs a stable reference to detect regressions in the serving stack itself.

### Why include a small amount of tool calling now?
- Serving has multiple request pathways with different serialization/validation overhead.
- A low-weight, bounded tool shape increases regression detection coverage without materially increasing noise.

---

## Versioning and change management
- This distribution is versioned as **canary_prompt_dist_version** (e.g., v0.4) and emitted as a metric tag and in canary logs.
- Any change that impacts token lengths, interface mix, or the joint distribution MUST:
  1. Increment the version
  2. Run the perf-canary validation plan in staging
  3. Recompute baselines (or explicitly document baseline compatibility)

Approval required:
- Runtime Perf Suite (owner): Noah Patel
- Applied ML & Evals review (prompt/template safety): Rina Kobayashi
- Scheduling review when concurrency/pacing changes: Sofia Ivanova

---

## Validation checklist (for edits)
1. Tokenizer sanity: measured token lengths fall into intended buckets (p95 within bucket bounds).
2. Decode length stability: measured output tokens are within target bucket >90% of the time.
3. Safety/privacy: no PII strings; templates pass redaction assertions.
4. Variance check: end-to-end p95 variance does not increase materially versus previous version at constant runtime.
5. Overhead: canary stays within regional GPU overhead budget (**<0.4% target**).
6. Tool calling sanity (if enabled): tool outputs remain schema-valid with bounded length; no nested object outputs.

---

## Examples (template snippets)
These examples illustrate structure only. Do not copy production incident/customer text.

**Chat (summarization):**
- System: "You are a technical assistant. Prefer clear steps and short explanations."
- User: "Summarize the following synthetic report into 5 bullets, focusing on performance and reliability:\n\n<synthetic_paragraphs_to_reach_prefill_bucket>\n\nEND"

**Chat (structured extraction):**
- User: "Extract the fields {component, symptom, suspected_cause, mitigation} from the text below. Output as key:value lines:\n\n<synthetic_paragraphs>\n\nEND"

**Completion (checklist):**
- Prompt: "Instruction: Write a 7-step checklist for validating a service rollout in a synthetic environment.\nInput: <synthetic_context>\nOutput:"

**Tool calling (extract_fields_v1):**
- Tool name: extract_fields_v1
- User: "From the synthetic text, extract {service, metric, regression_type, suspected_layer}. Keep values under 12 tokens each.\n\n<synthetic_paragraphs>\n\nEND"

---

## FAQ
**Q: Why include streaming at all?**
A: Streaming exercises buffering/serialization paths and helps ensure that end-to-end instrumentation remains correct across modes. Runtime-only latency metrics should remain comparable.

**Q: Should we add multilingual prompts?**
A: Not in v0.4. Multilingual content can change tokenization behavior and output lengths unpredictably across models. We may add a dedicated multilingual shape set once baselines and variance are well characterized.

**Q: Does tool calling turn this into a quality benchmark?**
A: No. Outputs are schema-bounded and performance-oriented; correctness is not scored here beyond basic schema validity and boundedness.

---

## Ownership
- Primary owner: Runtime Perf Suite (Noah Patel)
- Prompt/template safety review: Applied ML & Evals (Rina Kobayashi)
- Runtime integration: Omar El-Sayed
- Telemetry review: Logan Wright

For changes or questions, post in **#eng-runtime** and tag **@Noah Patel** and **@Rina Kobayashi**.

title: Canary SLA Oracle and Benchmark Gate Specification
content:
Title: Canary SLA Oracle and Benchmark Gate Specification

Summary:
This document defines the design, operational contract, and runbook for the Canary SLA Oracle — a deterministic decision service that evaluates canary releases against a defined set of benchmark gates before permitting progressive rollout. The specification ties release tooling to the benchmarking suite and runtime observability so releases are gated by both fidelity (quality) and operational SLOs (latency, error budget, cost).

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable, auditable gate for canary decisions that combines synthetic benchmark signals with live canary telemetry.
- Reduce false positives/negatives by using weighted evidence and time-windowed aggregation.
- Ensure fast feedback for small canaries while remaining robust for larger traffic ramps.
- Emit human-readable verdicts and machine-readable artifacts for automation (ok/reject/conditional).

Scope:
This spec covers: Canary SLA Oracle behaviour, benchmark gate definitions, data ingestion and enrichment, verdict calculation, tie-breaking, and required observability hooks. It does NOT specify UI/console layouts; those are product deliverables.

Definitions:
- Canary: A controlled subset deployment of a new runtime component, kernel, or model variant.
- Benchmark Gate: A single pass/fail criterion computed from benchmark or telemetry data (e.g., P99 <= 80ms).
- Oracle Verdicts: {ok, reject, conditional, inconclusive}.

Architecture overview:
1) Ingests two data streams in parallel: static benchmark results from the perf-suite and live telemetry from the canary shard(s).
2) Normalizes metrics to canonical units (ms, tokens/sec, error-rate) and tags by route/model/tenant.
3) Runs gate evaluators and a weighted aggregator to compute a single verdict.
4) Emits a signed artifact (JSON) with detailed gate evidence, confidence score, and rollback recommendations.

Gate taxonomy and thresholds (default):
| Gate name | Input source | Unit | Default threshold | Failure mode | Notes |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| latency_p99_path | live telemetry | ms | <= 120 | reject | path is route-specific P99 over 5m window |
| latency_median_change | perf vs baseline | % | <= +10% | conditional | small regressions allowed with review |
| tail_error_rate | live telemetry | errors/1000 | <= 1.0 | reject | counts 5xx and model-failure errors |
| quality_similarity | perf-suite eval | cosine | >= 0.92 | reject | embedding/response-similarity check against baseline |
| cost_per_token_delta | perf-suite and billing | % | <= +15% | conditional | flags large regressions in unit cost |

Aggregation and weighting:
- Each gate produces an evidence object: {gate, status, measured, threshold, weight, rationale}.
- We compute a score S = sum(weight_i * score_i) / sum(weight_i) where score_i = 1 for pass, 0 for fail, 0.5 for conditional.
- Default weights: latency_p99_path=3, latency_median_change=1.5, tail_error_rate=4, quality_similarity=5, cost_per_token_delta=1.
- Verdict mapping: S >= 0.85 => ok; 0.6 <= S < 0.85 => conditional; S < 0.6 => reject; insufficient/conflicting data => inconclusive.

Time windows and sampling:
- Live telemetry: rolling windows of 1m, 5m, 15m; primary decision window is 5m with 15m as confirmation.
- Perf-suite results: treated as single-snapshot evidence with decay function: weight *= e^{-age/48h}.
- Minimum sample floor: for latency/error gates require >= 500 requests in the 5m window or verdict is marked inconclusive.

Data enrichment and canonicalization:
- Normalize percentiles using the runtime's histogram export (OpenMetrics). Convert to ms and apply route-specific knobs (see section on route sensitivity).
- Enrich with: model_variant_id, kernel_commit, instance_type, region, traffic_mix (proportion of streaming/chat/embedding).

Tie-breaking and human override:
- If aggregation yields inconclusive or conditional, the policy allows a human approver to escalate with justification. The Oracle will surface the top three signals that would flip the verdict if they changed.
- Overrides are auditable: approver id, timestamp, justification, and a TTL for the override (default 1 hour).

Runbook: Canary release flow (operators):
1) Author triggers a canary via the release tool with expected traffic fraction and perf-suite job id.
2) Perf-suite runs pre-release benchmarks (synthetic SLOs) and uploads results to the benchmark-store.
3) Release tool marks canary as active; the Oracle begins ingesting live telemetry automatically.
4) Oracle evaluates gates at T+5m and emits initial verdict artifact to the release tool and logs.
5) If verdict == ok => auto-progress to next stage per release policy.
6) If verdict == conditional => hold, notify on-call and product reviewer with evidence bundle.
7) If verdict == reject => trigger automatic rollback policy and create incident for postmortem.
8) If verdict == inconclusive => extend canary for an additional 10m or require perf-suite re-run with larger synthetic load.

Operational alerts and observability hooks:
- Alert: Oracle failure (ingest/compute) => P1 oncall.
- Alert: inconclusive rate > 10% across canaries in last 24h => investigate metric sparsity or perf-suite health.
- Gauges to expose: current_score, gate_pass_rate, evidence_age_seconds, min_sample_count.
- Dashboards: Canary Health (per-release), Gate Violations (heatmap by route), Evidence Drift (time series of quality_similarity).

Example verdict artifact (machine-readable):
```
{
  "release_id": "r-2026-0104",
  "canary_shard": "canary-eu-7",
  "verdict": "conditional",
  "score": "0.72",
  "evidence": [
    {"gate":"latency_p99_path","status":"pass","measured":"95ms","threshold":"120ms","weight":"3"},
    {"gate":"quality_similarity","status":"fail","measured":"0.88","threshold":"0.92","weight":"5"}
  ],
  "timestamp": "2026-06-10T16:12:03Z",
  "artifact_signature": "sha256:..."
}
```

(That JSON is illustrative; the real artifact must be signed and include schema_version.)

Rollout automation examples (CLI snippets):
- Trigger a canary and attach a perf job:
```
redwoodctl release start --component runtime --sha abcd1234 --canary 0.01 --perf-job perf-2026-06-10-phi
```
- Query Oracle verdict:
```
redwoodctl release verdict --release r-2026-0104 --json
```

Quality and calibration process:
- Monthly calibration: update default thresholds and weights against a held-out corpus of releases from the last 6 months.
- Backfill experiments: re-run perf-suite on historical images and compute oracle false-positive/false-negative rates; aim for < 5% FP at current thresholds.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Oracle service owner: eng-serving-runtime - Release Engineering (primary).
- Benchmarking suite ownership: eng-serving-runtime - Perf & Benchmarking team.
- Oncall escalation: runtime oncall rotation.

Testing and release criteria for Oracle service itself:
- Unit tests for gate evaluators and weight decay logic.
- Integration tests against simulated telemetry with deterministic verdict expectations.
- Synthetic canary first-run in staging must show correct artifact emission and signed artifact verification.

Compatibility notes and known limitations:
- Small-traffic tenants: floor on sample counts will cause frequent inconclusive verdicts; teams should use larger synthetic perf-suite runs for such customers.
- Cross-region canaries: network variance will affect latency gates; the Oracle applies region-aware baselines but teams must review region-specific thresholds.
- Model-aware quality gates assume availability of a reference embedding; new-model onboarding must include a reference dataset.

Migration plan for existing gating mechanisms:
1) Run Oracle in shadow mode for two release cycles and compare with legacy canary decisions.
2) Publish discrepancy report and adjust weights/thresholds.
3) Opt-in small set of services for auto-enforcement for 30 days.

Appendices:
A. Route sensitivity knobs table:
| Route type | sensitivity multiplier | recommended median threshold change tolerance |
| api:chat | 1.2 | 8% |
| api:generation | 1.0 | 10% |
| api:embedding | 0.8 | 6% |

B. Benchmark artifact schema (subset):
- perf_job_id (string)
- model_variant_id (string)
- date (ISO8601)
- metrics {latency_p50, latency_p95, latency_p99, tokens_per_sec, quality_similarity, cost_per_token}

C. Related runbooks:
- runtime-upgrade-validation-and-canary-matrix-2026 (detailed canary matrix and roll criteria)
- runtime-deployment-circuit-breakers-and-sla-fallback-playbook-2026 (fallback policies)

Contact and feedback:
For design feedback or to request a change to gating thresholds contact Sofia Martinez (s-martinez@redwood.ai) or open an RFC in the eng-serving-runtime team channel.

Revision history:
- 2026-03-01: Draft created by Sofia Martinez.
- 2026-04-12: Added evidence weighting proposal (reviewed by Liam O'Connor).
- 2026-06-10: Updated default thresholds and added artifact signing requirement (published).

title: End-to-End Fidelity Validation Lab Manual — Runtime Benchmarking & Observability
content:
Summary
-------
This lab manual defines a repeatable, end-to-end validation workflow for runtime fidelity, cost and observability when making changes to serving kernel scheduling, quantization profiles, routing/fallback policies, and telemetry enrichment. The manual is intended for SREs, runtime engineers, and performance QA engineers who need deterministic validation before rollouts to Dedicated/Hosted fleets.

Scope
-----
- Controlled lab and CI testbed exercises covering: kernel scheduler changes, model-variant swaps, quantization profile updates, eviction and warmstart behavior, routing fallback correctness, and telemetry/enrichment validation.
- Focus on observable fidelity (semantic quality), SLO preservation (P99 latency, error rate), and telemetry completeness (span coverage, attribute set).
- Excludes upstream model training or dataset curation; assumes validated model weights.

Goals and Acceptance Criteria
----------------------------
- No observable regression in defined prompt suite: prompt-set pass-rate >= 98% (see Acceptance Checklist).
- Latency SLOs preserved: P50 < 60ms, P95 < 120ms, P99 < 300ms for the configured test shape.
- Telemetry signal completeness: 100% of major request traces contain kernel-orchestrator span + kv-cache span + dispatch-daemon span.
- Automated detection of fidelity regressions via diff-based eval and embedding-similarity thresholds.

Testbed Topology (text diagram)
-------------------------------
Lab cluster (isolated VPC) topology:
- traffic-generator -> runtime-gw (ingress proxy) -> router -> dispatch-daemon -> kernel-orchestrator -> GPU-pool / CPU-fallback nodes
- auxiliary services: kv-cache-service, eviction-controller, telemetry-bridge, metrics-exporter, trace-collector

Required services and minimum versions
-------------------------------------
| Service                | Min version | Purpose                                | Owner |
|------------------------|-------------|----------------------------------------|-------|
| runtime-gw             | 2.4.0       | Ingress routing, rate shaping          | eng-platform |
| kernel-orchestrator    | 1.8.2       | Kernel selection & scheduling          | serving-runtime |
| dispatch-daemon        | 3.1.0       | Request fanout & concurrency shaping   | serving-runtime |
| kv-cache-service       | 0.9.5       | Prefix/KV caching & warmstart hints    | eng-platform |
| eviction-controller    | 1.2.0       | Cross-tenant eviction coordination     | eng-sre |
| telemetry-bridge       | 2.2.0       | Enrich and forward traces/metrics      | eng-platform |
| trace-collector (jaeger)| 1.31.0     | Trace capture for E2E correlation      | eng-sre |

Baseline artifacts
------------------
- Golden prompt-suite: /data/lab/golden-prompt-suite-2026.json (1000 prompts across short/medium/long sequences).
- Golden embeddings snapshot: /artifacts/golden-embeddings-2026.tar.gz (used for semantic diff checks).
- Baseline kernel metric snapshot: s3://redwood-perf/baseline/kernel-metrics-2026-02-01.json

Benchmarks and Metrics to Capture
--------------------------------
- Latencies: P50, P90, P95, P99, tail-99.9 (end-to-end and kernel-only).
- Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec under shaped arrival processes.
- Resource signals: GPU utilization, GPU-memory fragmentation, CPU steal, NIC TX/RX.
- Fidelity: embedding cosine similarity, BLEU-like sequence similarity for deterministic prompts, classification/QA exact match for labeled prompts.
- Observability coverage: % traces with required spans, % requests with sampling_id, % logs with request_id.

Testing Workflows (high-level)
------------------------------
1) Preflight: environment sanity
   - Verify service versions and config (see config-check CLI below).
   - Start trace-collector and telemetry-bridge in debug mode.
2) Baseline capture
   - Run golden prompt-suite against the baseline runtime configuration, store traces/metrics/artifacts.
3) Change under test
   - Apply kernel scheduling change / quantization profile / routing update in isolated test namespace.
4) Controlled replay
   - Replay captured traffic shapes (steady-state, microburst, heavy-tail) and run golden prompt-suite concurrently.
5) Automated fidelity checks
   - Run embedding-similarity diff and per-prompt regression detector.
6) Observability validation
   - Check trace/span coverage and metric cardinality including enriched attributes.
7) Acceptance gating
   - Apply acceptance checklist and sign-off for canary.

Detailed Procedures
-------------------
A. Kernel scheduler change validation (engineer-run)
1. Coordinate with owner and schedule lab window; tag change PR with {lab-validation-needed}.
2. Snapshot baseline artifacts (metrics, traces, outputs).
3. Deploy planner branch to kernel-orchestrator in test namespace: kubectl set image ... --record.
4. Warmstart KV cache hinting: pre-warm top 20 prefixes from golden prompt-suite.
5. Run three workload shapes: steady (r=500 rps), burst (3x for 30s every 5min), tail-heavy (Pareto shape).
6. Capture traces (100% sampling) and metrics at 1s resolution.
7. Run regression detector: python tools/regression_detector.py --baseline s3://... --candidate ./artifacts/candidate-output.json
8. If embedding similarity drop > 0.07 average or > 10 prompts below threshold, abort and file incident.
9. If performance SLOs violated (P99 > 1.5x baseline), revert change and open ticket.

B. Quantization profile update validation (automated pipeline)
1. Pipeline triggers from quantization-profile PR.
2. Build candidate artifacts and deploy to canary pool of 10 GPUs.
3. Run golden prompt-suite with deterministic seeds; capture outputs.
4. Run automatic semantic check: cosine similarity on embeddings (thresholds in acceptance checklist).
5. If any prompt in labeled set loses exact match or similarity below threshold, mark profile as failing.

C. Eviction and warmstart behavior (chaos-style)
1. Start a long-run session workload for warm KV cache builds.
2. Trigger eviction-controller to evict a tenant shard and observe eviction propagation.
3. Verify warmstart hints cause cache warm-up within 60s and P95 latency returns to baseline within 120s.
4. Validate no request leaks or auth errors during handoff.

CLI and Example Commands
------------------------
- Config check: ./tools/lab_config_check.sh --env lab --services runtime-gw,kernel-orchestrator,dispatch-daemon
- Start traffic generator: ./tools/traffic_gen --shape steady --rps 500 --duration 20m --out ./runs/steady-2026-03-01
- Run regression detector: python tools/regression_detector.py --baseline s3://redwood-perf/baseline --candidate ./runs/steady-2026-03-01/outputs.json --report ./runs/report.json

Example config snippet (YAML)
---------------------------
run_id: e2e-lab-2026-03-05
workload_shapes:
  - name: steady
    rps: 500
    duration: 20m
  - name: burst
    rps_profile: "spike:3x:30s:period:5m"
sampling:
  traces: 100%
  metrics_resolution: 1s
fidelity_checks:
  embedding_similarity_threshold: 0.85
  labeled_prompt_exact_match: 0.98

Acceptance checklist (must pass all)
-----------------------------------
- [ ] Regression detector: overall pass (no more than 2% prompts flagged).
- [ ] Latency SLOs: P50/P95/P99 within defined thresholds.
- [ ] Observability: required spans present in >= 99.5% of traces.
- [ ] Resource safety: no GPU memory OOMs; fragmentation delta < 5% vs baseline.
- [ ] No functional errors (auth, 5xx, malformed outputs) above 0.1%.

Signal artifacts and retention
----------------------------
- Traces and metrics for each run stored under s3://redwood-lab-runs/{run_id}/ with retention 90 days.
- Output diffs and reports under artifacts/ in the CI workspace; retain for 30 days.

Failure modes and escalation
---------------------------
- Fidelity regression detected: open a regression ticket (label: perf+fidelity) and notify author + eng-sre.
- SLO breach during lab run: pause test, capture extended traces, and create an incident with severity P2 if breach persists > 15m.
- Observability gap: escalate to eng-platform to verify telemetry-bridge configuration and collector health.

Runbook links and ownership
--------------------------
- Kernel scheduler owner: serving-runtime (oncall alias: #srv-runtime-oncall).
- Eviction-controller owner: eng-sre (alias: #eng-sre).
- Telemetry ingestion owner: eng-platform (alias: #observability).
- Related runbooks: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-deployment-circuit-breakers-and-sla-fallback-playbook-2026

Automation and CI integration
----------------------------
- Recommended: run quantization-profile and small-sample fidelity checks as part of PR gating (fast-path). Full golden-suite runs scheduled nightly or on-demand via the lab pipeline.
- CI artifacts MUST include run_id, git-commit, kernel-orchestrator-image, and quantization-profile-id for traceability.

Appendix: Quick cheat-sheet
--------------------------
- Quick start: tools/lab_bootstrap.sh --run e2e-lab --env lab
- Baseline artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/baseline/
- Who to call: serving-runtime owners (Maya Ortega), eng-sre lead (Leah Thompson), telemetry (Arjun Patel).

Notes and future work
---------------------
- Add synthetic adversarial prompt generator for corner-case fidelity checks (Q3 2026).
- Integrate a lightweight human-in-the-loop review for ambiguous prompt diffs.
- Expand telemetry enrichment assertions to include token-level attributions.

Document history
----------------
- 2026-02-14: Created by Maya K. Ortega.
- 2026-03-05: Updated with quantization pipeline steps and CLI snippets.

title: Real-world Integration Latency Lab Protocol
content:
Summary:
This document defines the lab protocol for measuring and validating real-world end-to-end latency for Redwood's serving runtime when integrated with typical customer stacks. The goal is reproducible, comparable results across experiments and a clear path from measurement to mitigation and runbook updates. This protocol covers test harness configuration, kernel scheduling knobs to exercise, profiling instrumentation, benchmark metrics, acceptance gates, triage steps, and release checklist items.

Why this exists:
- Many microbenchmarks do not expose systemic latency sources (networking, pre/post-processing, SDK client behavior, model-variant switching).
- Product teams need a repeatable integration workflow to validate latency budgets before shipping model variants or scheduler changes.
- Oncall and SRE require deterministic steps to reproduce customer-facing tail latency and to collect the exact traces needed for root-cause analysis.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: Hosted API path, Dedicated pools (single-tenant), and Private deployment reference config. Includes kernel and scheduler toggle exercises, KV cache warmup patterns, and cross-service tracing.
- Non-goal: Microkernel engineering (kernel code changes should be validated in the kernel lab and referenced here).

Owners and contacts:
- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime / Benchmarking (Elena Park)
- SRE escalation lead: Arjun Patel
- Profiling & Observability contact: Sofia Martinez
- Release engineering reviewer: Priya Singh

High-level success criteria (sample SLOs for lab runs):
1) Median p95-p99 delta under controlled synthetic load must be < 1.5x baseline.
2) 99th percentile absolute latency (end-to-end, client-observed) must be < 250 ms for small prompt workloads (<= 128 tokens) on Dedicated rtx-llama-8 profile.
3) No more than 5% of requests may observe > 300 ms extra jitter after model-variant swap during a 30-minute canary exercise.

Test environment matrix (table):
- Hardware: rtx-llama-8, a100-40, a800-64 configurations
- Deployment modes: hosted-api (eu-west1), dedicated-small (8-GPU pool), private-onprem (1-rack)
- Network: local-test VLAN, simulated 50 ms cross-region latency, baseline intra-region
- Client SDK: python-sdk v2.8, go-sdk v1.5

(Represented as a human-readable table in the lab runbook):
| axis | options |
|------|---------|
| hardware | rtx-llama-8, a100-40, a800-64 |
| deployment | hosted-api, dedicated-small, private-onprem |
| network profile | intra-region (10ms), cross-region (50ms), congested (100ms +- 20ms jitter) |
| client load | single-request steady, sustained qps, bursty microbursts (10x baseline) |

Instrumentation and data to collect (mandatory):
- Client-side: request timestamp, sdk version, client region, request size, prompt token count, retry count.
- Edge: ingress latency, TLS handshake times, proxy queue depth.
- Runtime: dispatch latency, kernel selection, batch size, kernel exec time, KV cache hit/miss, memory pressure events.
- Kernel traces: per-kernel wall time, tensor upload/download durations, kernel queuing time, accelerator telemetry (SM utilization, temperature, power).
- Tracing: full distributed trace with unique run_id; ensure trace IDs propagate through edge -> router -> runtime -> kernel.
- Aggregates: per-route p50/p90/p95/p99, concurrency histogram, CPU/GPU tail utilization, retry/backpressure counts.

Profiling playbook integration steps:
1) Baseline capture: run 30 minutes of steady-state single-request-to-queue traffic at 1x production QPS. Collect lightweight traces (1/100 sampling) plus full traces for 1 minute every 5 minutes.
2) Microburst capture: inject 10x QPS for 60s bursts every 10 minutes. Use high-frequency sampling (1/10) during bursts.
3) Model swap: trigger a canary model-variant swap (v1 -> v1-quantized) and capture traces for 30 minutes post-swap with 100% sampling.
4) Kernel-change simulation: toggle scheduler gating parameter (kernel_credit_floor) to stress preemption and run a 15-minute stress profile.
5) KV warm/cold runs: run identical prompts with cold KV (restart runtime between runs) and warm KV (run warmup with 1000 unique requests).

Procedure: running a lab experiment (numbered checklist)
1. Reserve lab environment: use the bench-run booking service (benchctl reserve --env=<env-name> --hours=3). Document reservation id.
2. Deploy benchmark artifacts: push canary model to bench registry and pin runtime image to stable-<sha>.
3. Configure experiment: edit run_config.yaml (see sample below) and upload to bench-run.
4. Start instrumentation collectors: start jaeger, perf-collector, nvtop-exporter, and bench-metrics-shipper. Confirm metrics ingestion in metrics-redwood/baseline-run.
5. Execute baseline and perturbations following the profile above.
6. Export artifacts: traces (JSON), aggregates (CSV), kernel histograms (parquet), and nvml snapshots (tar.gz). Attach to the bench-run ticket.
7. Annotate findings: fill the experiment-summary template and link to related issues.
8. Close reservation and notify reviewers.

Sample run_config.yaml (literal block):
---
run_id: rw-latency-experiment-2026-08
hardware: rtx-llama-8
deployment: dedicated-small
client: python-sdk-2.8
qps_profile: |
  - step: steady
    qps: 50
    duration: 1800
  - step: burst
    qps: 500
    duration: 60
  - step: cooldown
    qps: 50
    duration: 600
sampling: 
  steady: 1/100
  burst: 1/10
  post_swap: 1/1
---

Acceptance gates and triage thresholds:
- Gate A (pre-merge): No p99 regression > 2x baseline on median of 3 independent runs.
- Gate B (canary): < 1% increase in client-visible request failures and p99 within SLO.
- Gate C (release): 3-run streak of passing Gate A and one canary pass after scheduler toggle.

If a gate fails run the triage checklist: (short steps)
1) Re-run the exact experiment with debug sampling enabled (100% traces for 5 minutes).
2) Correlate traces with kernel histograms and NVML snapshots by run_id.
3) Check for scheduler backpressure signals (kernel_credit_balance < 0), dispatcher queue depth > 90th percentile, or KV eviction storms.
4) Narrow to layer (network, dispatch, kernel) and open a priority P0 investigation ticket with attached artifacts.

Known issues to watch for during runs (operational guidance):
- Intermittent nvlink retransmits when multiple A100s are under microburst stress: remediate by toggling cross-gpu coalescing off and retest.
- SDK client-side exponential backoff misconfiguration: ensure client max_retries=2 for lab runs.
- Kernel driver stutters manifested as 10-20ms spikes on p99: capture kernel logs and escalate to kernel-team with trace artifacts.

Kernel scheduling knobs exercised by this protocol:
- kernel_credit_floor: minimum credits to keep a kernel resident.
- preempt_grace_window_ms: time window before allowing preemption of running kernel slices.
- batch_slice_target_ms: target slice duration used by the batch-slicer.
- admission_watermark: soft queue threshold to trigger admission backpressure.

Release checklist tie-ins (before rolling runtime changes):
- Ensure three lab runs across the environment matrix pass acceptance gates.
- Document any scheduler knob changes in the release notes with exact config diffs.
- Attach representative traces and a short remediation playbook for SRE.

Runbook snippet for oncall (short, actionable):
- Symptom: customer complains of increased tail latency after rollout.
- Quick checks: verify canary-run_id in bench-run, check runtime dispatch queue depth, verify kernel_credit_balance and GPU utilization.
- Immediate mitigation: revert scheduler knob to previous value (idempotent config), scale up warm spare pool for 15 minutes, and notify release-owner.
- Collect: full traces for 10 minutes after mitigation and attach to ticket.

Post-experiment analysis and reporting template (bulleted):
- Experiment objective and hypothesis
- Environment and exact artifacts (images, model-sha, run_id)
- Key metrics: baseline p95/p99, post-change p95/p99, CPU/GPU tail util
- Notable traces and causal inference (short narrative)
- Recommended action: rollback, config tweak, kernel bug, or accept

Artifacts and storage policy:
- Store all collected traces and artifacts under s3://bench-archive/<run_id>/ with 90-day hot retention and 2-year cold archive.
- Sensitive data (customer prompts) must be redacted before upload following the data-management template.

Appendix A — Quick CLI snippets:
- Reserve environment: benchctl reserve --env=dedicated-small --hours=3
- Start collection: benchctl collect start --run_id=rw-latency-experiment-2026-08
- Upload artifacts: benchctl upload --run_id=rw-latency-experiment-2026-08 --path=./artifacts

Appendix B — Common troubleshooting queries (examples):
- Find runs with p99 > 300ms: SELECT run_id FROM bench_metrics WHERE metric='p99' AND value > 300 AND date >= '2026-01-01';
- Correlate kernel credit dips with p99 spikes: join kernel_histogram by run_id and timestamp window.

Revision history:
- 2026-03-02: Draft created by Elena Park (initial protocol).
- 2026-05-11: Added KV warm/cold procedure and sampling guidance after SRE feedback.
- 2026-08-15: Updated acceptance gates and added private-onprem environment entries after integration test runs.

Related documents and references:
- Operational workload simulator and signature guide (bench-manifest)
- Profiling observability correlates playbook
- Runbook: graceful-fidelity-staircase-and-degradation-modes

End of document.

title: TP Stress Suite Spec (Multi-GPU Tensor Parallel Reliability + Performance)
content:
## Summary
This document specifies the **TP Stress Suite**: a set of repeatable workloads and pass/fail criteria used to detect **multi-GPU tensor-parallel (TP)** regressions in Redwood’s serving runtime. The suite targets known failure modes under sustained load (mixed prefill/decode, long context, bursty concurrency, cancellation, memory/KV pressure) that have historically produced **request hangs, GPU stalls, and downstream timeouts**.

The suite runs in two modes:
1) **CI smoke + gating** (fast, minimal hardware): catches obvious deadlocks and correctness-breaking changes.
2) **Perf lab + perf-canary** (representative GPUs, longer burn): catches probabilistic stalls, p99 latency inflation, and throughput regressions.

## Goals
- Detect and prevent re-introduction of TP hangs/timeouts (primary).
- Provide early, actionable signals that localize stalls to **compute vs NCCL/collectives vs scheduler starvation**.
- Establish stable, versioned workload definitions (distributions, seeds, thresholds) to make results comparable over time.
- Integrate with existing Redwood pipelines:
  - benchmark-lab repro harness
  - perf-canary scenarios
  - runtime release gating and canary dashboards

## Non-goals
- Model quality/evals (we use fixed prompts purely as workload generators).
- Exhaustive hardware coverage (we prioritize the fleet/hot paths; full coverage remains a lab responsibility).
- Replacing microbenchmarks; this suite complements kernel-level microbench tests.

## Definitions
- **Replica**: one runtime instance serving requests.
- **TP degree (TP=2/4/8)**: number of GPUs participating in one replica’s model partition.
- **Prefill**: prompt processing; **decode**: token-by-token generation.
- **Hang**: request fails to complete without explicit error; typically presents as streaming stuck, stalled NCCL, or scheduler deadlock.
- **Stall detector**: runtime metric indicating lack of progress (heartbeat gap, collective in-flight growth, queue depth growth without completion).

## Suite Overview
The suite is composed of **scenario groups**, each with a workload generator and pass/fail criteria.

### Scenario Groups (required)
1) **Mixed Prefill/Decode (Streaming)**
2) **Long Context + Heavy Prefill**
3) **Bursty Concurrency + Backpressure**
4) **Cancellation / Client Disconnect**
5) **KV Cache Pressure + Compaction Edges**

### Scenario Groups (optional / phased)
6) **Replica churn during sustained load** (drain/restart while traffic continues)
7) **Fault injection** (forced collective timeout to validate watchdog + abort semantics)

## Workload Generators
All generators share these properties:
- Deterministic by default via **seeded randomness**.
- Pluggable distributions for prompt length, output length, think-time, and request interarrival.
- Supports streaming and non-streaming requests.
- Emits structured artifacts:
  - request timeline summary
  - per-rank progress markers
  - runtime metrics snapshot references (Prometheus query links)
  - trace sample IDs (if enabled)

### Generator Interface (conceptual)
Each scenario defines:
- **Model + TP config**: model identifier, quantization profile if relevant, TP degree.
- **Traffic config**: concurrency targets, arrival distribution, duration.
- **Request config**: distributions of prompt lengths and max_new_tokens, streaming on/off.
- **Failure hooks**: cancellation rate, replica restart events, memory pressure toggles.
- **Success criteria**: thresholds and required signals.

### Standard Distributions
Unless overridden per scenario:
- **Prompt length distribution (tokens)**: mixture of short + medium + long
  - 60%: 128–512 (uniform)
  - 30%: 1,024–4,096 (log-uniform)
  - 10%: 8,192–16,384 (log-uniform; only on long-context-capable models)
- **Max new tokens distribution**:
  - 70%: 64–256 (uniform)
  - 25%: 256–1,024 (log-uniform)
  - 5%: 1,024–2,048 (log-uniform; decode stress)
- **Interarrival**:
  - CI mode: fixed-rate to keep variance low.
  - Perf mode: Poisson arrivals with occasional burst windows.

## Scenario Specifications

### 1) Mixed Prefill/Decode (Streaming)
**Purpose:** Reproduce starvation and ordering issues caused by prefill-heavy batches interleaving with streaming decode steps.

**Config (baseline):**
- TP: 4
- Duration: 20 minutes (perf), 5 minutes (CI)
- Concurrency target: 24 in-flight requests per replica (perf), 8 (CI)
- Streaming: enabled
- Prompt length: standard distribution
- Max new tokens: skewed toward short/medium (to keep decode churn high)

**Additional knobs:**
- Decode step budget: enforce continuous decode iterations (avoid all-prefill phases).
- Prefill burst windows: 30s windows with 2x arrival rate every 5 minutes.

**Pass/fail:**
- **Hard fail** if any request exceeds timeout:
  - CI: > 120s wall time
  - Perf: > 300s wall time
- **Hard fail** if stall detectors trigger:
  - per-rank heartbeat gap > 30s (CI) / > 60s (perf)
  - in-flight collective counter monotonic growth without completion for > 30s
- **Soft fail** (regression) if:
  - p99 end-to-end latency increases > 15% vs pinned baseline for same hardware/profile
  - decode tokens/sec decreases > 10% (throughput regression)


### 2) Long Context + Heavy Prefill
**Purpose:** Catch long-context issues that amplify NCCL ordering sensitivity and scheduler backpressure, and stress KV allocation paths.

**Config (baseline):**
- TP: 4 (required), TP: 8 (lab-only where supported)
- Duration: 30 minutes (perf), 8 minutes (CI)
- Concurrency: 8 (perf), 2 (CI)
- Streaming: disabled by default (focus on prefill correctness); optional streaming variant
- Prompt lengths:
  - 50%: 8k–16k
  - 40%: 16k–32k (only for models configured for 32k)
  - 10%: 32k–64k (lab-only)
- Max new tokens: 64–256

**Pass/fail:**
- **Hard fail** on any hang / stall detector trigger.
- **Hard fail** if OOM occurs when below expected headroom thresholds (see “Memory expectations”).
- **Soft fail** if prefill latency p95 increases > 20% vs baseline.


### 3) Bursty Concurrency + Backpressure
**Purpose:** Validate scheduler fairness and load-shedding hooks; ensure we don’t wedge replicas during sudden spikes.

**Config:**
- TP: 4
- Duration: 20 minutes perf, 5 minutes CI
- Baseline arrival: maintain 50% of steady-state throughput target
- Burst: 3x arrivals for 20s, every 2 minutes
- Concurrency cap: set to production-like default; verify we reject/queue correctly

**Pass/fail:**
- **Hard fail** on hang.
- **Hard fail** if queue depth grows without completion for > 60s.
- **Soft fail** if burst recovery time (p95 latency returning to within 10% of baseline) > 90s.


### 4) Cancellation / Client Disconnect
**Purpose:** Catch deadlocks caused by cancellation paths leaving collectives waiting or ranks diverging.

**Config:**
- TP: 4
- Duration: 15 minutes perf, 5 minutes CI
- Streaming: enabled
- Cancellation rate: 2% of requests cancel mid-decode; 1% cancel during prefill
- Cancellation timing: random uniform over request lifetime, seeded

**Pass/fail:**
- **Hard fail** if any cancellation causes:
  - replica wedging (no progress on subsequent requests)
  - watchdog abort storm (excess aborts) exceeding rate limit
- **Soft fail** if cancellation increases error rate > 1% above baseline (excluding intentional cancellations).


### 5) KV Cache Pressure + Compaction Edges
**Purpose:** Exercise fragmentation/compaction interactions with TP and ensure no rank divergence under memory pressure.

**Config:**
- TP: 4
- Duration: 25 minutes perf, 8 minutes CI
- Workload: long-ish prompts + moderate decode to keep KV resident
- Enable KV compaction feature flag(s) per current default
- Memory pressure: keep steady-state at ~80–90% of KV budget through concurrency and sequence choices

**Pass/fail:**
- **Hard fail** if:
  - ranks diverge (detected via per-rank progress mismatch / collective mismatch signals)
  - deadlock or stall detector triggers
- **Soft fail** if compaction causes p99 latency increase > 20% without corresponding throughput gain.


## Hardware + Runtime Matrix
The suite is defined to be portable; execution targets depend on mode.

### CI (gating) targets
- Minimum: TP=2 or TP=4 on a single node, single replica.
- GPU class: smallest available multi-GPU CI runner (team-owned pool).
- Duration constraints: scenarios truncated; focus is hang detection.

### Perf lab / perf-canary targets
Run nightly (or per-release) across representative fleet:
- A100 80GB (TP=4) (primary)
- H100 80GB (TP=4) (primary)
- L40S (TP=2/4 where used in hosted tiers) (secondary)

Each hardware run records:
- driver/CUDA version
- NCCL version
- runtime build SHA
- model + quantization profile

## Metrics and Instrumentation Requirements
Each run MUST emit or link to:
- Request metrics:
  - request_count, success/error rate
  - end-to-end latency p50/p95/p99
  - streaming: time-to-first-token (TTFT) p50/p95/p99
  - decode tokens/sec and prefill tokens/sec
- TP progress / stall metrics:
  - per-rank heartbeat timestamp and gap
  - in-flight collective counters (by type if available)
  - scheduler queue depth and starvation indicators
  - stall reason code counts (compute/comms/scheduler/memory/unknown)
- Resource metrics:
  - GPU SM utilization, HBM usage, PCIe/NVLink (where available)
  - NCCL error counters / timeouts

If traces are enabled in perf mode:
- sampled spans must include rank IDs and collective counters for correlation.

## Pass/Fail Criteria (Global)
A scenario run is **FAIL** if any of the following occur:
- Any request exceeds the scenario timeout (CI: 120s; perf: 300s unless scenario overrides).
- Any stall detector triggers above configured thresholds.
- Any replica enters a non-recovering state (no completions for > 60s under active load).
- Any NCCL error is surfaced (except explicitly-injected fault tests).

A run is a **REGRESSION (non-gating)** if:
- p99 latency regression > 15% vs pinned baseline for that scenario/hardware.
- throughput regression > 10% (tokens/sec) vs baseline.

Baseline comparisons should be pinned to:
- release branch baseline for canary
- last green main build for CI

## Memory Expectations
- Scenarios should be configured to avoid OOM under expected headroom.
- If OOM occurs, the run is considered FAIL unless:
  - the scenario explicitly configures “expected OOM” (not currently used), or
  - the model/profile/hardware combination is marked unsupported in the scenario registry.

## Integration Plan

### Repository / config ownership
- Scenario definitions live as versioned configs in the perf-canary and benchmark-lab repos.
- The runtime repo owns:
  - metric names/labels stability guarantees
  - stall detector semantics and thresholds (feature-flagged where necessary)

### CI Integration (gating)
- Trigger: on changes touching TP scheduling, NCCL/collectives boundary, KV compaction, cancellation paths, watchdog/abort.
- Execution:
  - run a reduced set: Scenario 1 + Scenario 4 (mandatory), plus one of (Scenario 2 or 5) depending on changed area.
  - total runtime target: <= 20 minutes.
- Outputs:
  - junit-style summary + links to logs
  - Prometheus snapshot link (if available)
  - failure bundle with last 2 minutes of per-rank logs

### Perf Lab Integration (nightly)
- Full suite with standard durations.
- Stored artifacts:
  - scenario run metadata (hardware/software/sha)
  - aggregated metrics
  - sampled traces (if enabled)
  - NCCL debug logs only when “debug window” is explicitly enabled via run parameter

### Perf-canary Integration (release)
- Dedicated-first rollout: run on Dedicated canary clusters prior to broad Hosted enablement.
- Gating checklist ties to runtime release ticket:
  - all TP scenarios green on target hardware
  - no new stall reason spikes
  - abort/watchdog rates within limits

## Operational Safety and Logging
- NCCL debug logging is **off by default**. Enable only via explicit “debug window” parameter to avoid performance and data volume issues.
- Logs must avoid customer prompt contents; use synthetic prompts only.
- For any FAIL:
  - capture rank-local logs and runtime structured error codes
  - include the stall reason code summary and last-known progress markers

## Running the Suite (operator-facing)
Required inputs:
- model identifier
- TP degree
- scenario config name
- run mode: ci | perf
- duration override (optional)

Standard run procedure:
1) Select hardware pool and reserve node(s).
2) Deploy runtime build SHA to a single replica with TP enabled.
3) Start scenario generator with seed pinned; record run ID.
4) Monitor dashboards for heartbeat gaps and queue depth.
5) On completion, publish summary + compare to baseline.
6) If FAIL, file/associate a Linear issue and attach failure bundle.

## Ownership and Change Control
- Primary owner: **Marcus Reed** (perf/regression coverage)
- Scenario definitions: **Rina Kobayashi** (repro harness + perf canary)
- CI wiring: **Sahana Iyer** (GPU regression coverage)
- SRE alert alignment: **Aisha Bello**, **Rafael Mendes**

Any change to:
- metric names/labels
- stall detector thresholds
- pass/fail thresholds
- scenario distributions
must be reviewed by at least one of:
- Scheduling lead (Sofia Ivanova) for scheduler-related scenarios
- Kernel lead (Hiro Tanaka) for NCCL/stream-sync scenarios
- SRE reviewer (Rafael Mendes or Aisha Bello) for alertability implications

## Appendix: Recommended Baseline Threshold Table
Use as starting defaults; tune per model/hardware.

- Mixed Prefill/Decode (Streaming):
  - p99 latency regression: 15%
  - tokens/sec regression: 10%
  - heartbeat gap fail: 60s (perf)

- Long Context + Heavy Prefill:
  - prefill p95 regression: 20%
  - heartbeat gap fail: 60s (perf)

- Bursty Concurrency:
  - recovery time > 90s -> soft fail

- Cancellation:
  - replica wedge -> hard fail

## Appendix: Known Failure Signatures to Tag
When failing, include one tag in the run summary (best effort):
- collective_ordering_mismatch
- stream_wait_deadlock
- scheduler_starvation_decode
- kv_compaction_rank_divergence
- cancellation_collective_wait
- watchdog_abort_spike
- unknown_progress_stall

title: Scheduler Experimentation and Observable Fidelity Manual
content:
# Scheduler Experimentation and Observable Fidelity Manual

Summary
-------
This manual documents the recommended process, observability signals, and bench/experiment templates for running scheduler and kernel-selection experiments on the Redwood serving runtime. It ties runtime architecture considerations to scheduler policy changes, prescribes profiling and benchmarking steps, and provides a safe rollout / rollback runbook for production canaries. The intent is to make scheduler experiments repeatable, measurable, and auditable while protecting customer SLOs.

Goals
-----
- Provide a repeatable experiment skeleton for kernel/scheduler changes.
- Define the fidelity and telemetry signals required to qualify a change for canary and global rollout.
- Define bench and replay artifacts to measure cost/latency impact and guard against degradation.
- Standardize rollout criteria, rollback triggers, and owner responsibilities.

Scope and non-goals
-------------------
- In scope: scheduler policy language changes, kernel hinting heuristics, admission controller tuning, telemetry-driven adaptive policies.
- Out of scope: model architecture changes, client-side retry behaviour, or infra provisioning (handled by eng-infra).

Audience
--------
- Runtime engineers implementing scheduler logic and kernel authors.
- SRE and oncall for canary/production validation.
- Applied ML / perf teams running fidelity and cost experiments.

Principal components referenced (service names)
---------------------------------------------
- runtime-coordinator: global experiment controller and policy reconciler.
- kernel-agent: per-node kernel selection and hinting process.
- telemetry-pipeline: trace/metric collector and enrichment layer (ingest + partitioner).
- perf-lab: synthetic benchmark runner and mirror replay harness.
- autoscaler: capacity and burst handling component.

SLOs & safety thresholds (operational baseline)
---------------------------------------------
- Short-seq p95 latency (<= 64 tokens): target 60 ms, hard SLO 120 ms.
- p99 latency (<= 64 tokens): target 120 ms, alert at 200 ms.
- 95th-percentile GPU kernel-run-time variance increase: <= 10% relative to baseline during canary.
- Error rate increase: <= 0.05% absolute over baseline in canary window.
- Cost-per-token delta: treat increases > 8% as economic regression.

Telemetry and observability: required signals
-------------------------------------------
The following signals must be captured and correlated for every scheduler experiment:
1) Request-level traces (span naming: runtime.request -> scheduler.decision -> kernel.dispatch) with the following attributes: model, route, sequence_length, priority_class, admission_decision, kernel_variant.
2) Kernel-level histograms: dispatch_duration_ms, execution_duration_ms, occupancy_pct, tensor_core_util_pct.
3) Queue and admission metrics: queue_depth_by_route, admission_rejections, preemption_events.
4) Cost signals: tokens_generated, gpu_ms_charged, per-request-cost-estimate.
5) Sampling artifacts: 1% full-request-body capture (shadow only, redaction required), 10% top-k token histogram.

Instrumentation checklist (must exist before experiment start)
---------------------------------------------------------------
- runtime-coordinator event emitted for experiment start/end and policy version.
- kernel-agent emits kernel_variant tag with kernel_hash.
- telemetry-pipeline enrichment populates "kernel_variant" and "scheduler_policy_id" fields and writes to perf-lab topic.
- Perf Lab replay mapping for route -> synthetic corpus present (see Appendix B).

Experiment taxonomy and examples
-------------------------------
A. Kernel hinting heuristic change (low blast radius)
- Change: prefer FP16 kernel variant for sequence_length < 128 when occupancy > 45%.
- Risk: reduced numeric fidelity for edge tokens.
- Typical runtime config change: kernel_hint.profile=fp16_aggressive, kernel_hint.min_occupancy=45

B. Admission controller tightening (medium blast radius)
- Change: limit speculative-batch admission for non-premium routes during peak windows.
- Risk: increased latency for eligible batched requests (due to single-run path).
- Runtime config: admission.speculative_batch.enabled=false for routes [chat-api-v2], window=18:00-22:00 UTC

C. Scheduler policy language rewrite (high blast radius)
- Change: integrate economic-priority in policy DSL and add preemption budgets.
- Risk: complex decision pathways may introduce priority inversions.
- Requires perf-lab shadow replay prior to canary and an extended canary window (72h).

Profiling playbook (step-by-step)
--------------------------------
1) Pre-experiment profiling (dev cluster)
  - Run perf-lab synthetic suite: ./perf-lab run --experiment <id> --profile baseline --topology small-mixed.
  - Collect kernel-level traces: ensure kernel-agent trace rate at 100% for dispatched kernels in this run.
  - Generate comparison report: compare dispatch_duration_ms / execution_duration_ms histograms to baseline.

2) Shadow traffic validation (staging)
  - Mirror 10% of production traffic for 2 hours into staging using traffic-mirroring-service.
  - Validate that telemetry-pipeline enrichments and trace correlation tags are present.
  - Run automated fidelity checks: BLEU/ROUGE spot-checks for sample responses when applicable.

3) Canary (production, isolated cohort)
  - Scope: 1% of traffic or a single small region (preferably non-critical).
  - Duration: 24h minimum, extendable based on risk category (see taxonomy).
  - Metrics to monitor live: short-seq p95/p99, error_rate, admission_rejections, kernel_variant_latency_delta, cost-per-token.
  - Automated rollback triggers (see Runbook section).

4) Extended monitoring and rollout
  - If canary stable for window, expand to 10% for 48h and re-evaluate.
  - Run perf-lab long-run cost simulation for 7 days to capture diurnal effects.

Benchmarking suite integration
-----------------------------
- Bench artifacts to generate for every experiment:
  1) Microbench: per-kernel latency/throughput at multiple sequence lengths and batch sizes.
  2) Shadow replay: 24h replay of sampled production surface with kernel_variant toggles.
  3) Cost-sim: per-route cost impact across synthetic and replay workloads.

Sample benchmarking job JSON (perf-lab)
--------------------------------------
{
  "job": "scheduler-experiment-<id>",
  "targets": ["kernel-variants", "routes"],
  "duration": "24h",
  "replay_topic": "perf-lab.replay.scheduler-experiment-<id>",
  "metrics": ["p95_latency","p99_latency","gpu_ms_charged","kernel_dispatch_variance"]
}

(Place this in perf-lab jobs directory and ensure replay_topic is provisioned in telemetry-pipeline.)

Release notes checklist (for runtime release carrying scheduler changes)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
- Summary line describing high-level risk and affected routes.
- List of config flags and default values.
- Canary plan referencing this manual and experiment id.
- Telemetry migration notes (schema changes, new tags).
- Rollback instructions and quick commands.

Known issues and mitigations (experiment-related)
------------------------------------------------
- Issue: kernel_variant tag not propagated to long-term metrics store.
  - Mitigation: add temporary joiner job in telemetry-pipeline to backfill kernel_variant via trace correlation.
- Issue: admission.rejections spike without latency change (indicates over-aggressive admission policy).
  - Mitigation: revert admission window and enable speculative ramp for target routes.
- Issue: Perf-lab replay underestimates tail-latency due to missing network latencies.
  - Mitigation: add network-latency augmentation step to replay harness (see Appendix A).

Runbook: Canary quick actions (operational)
-----------------------------------------
1) Detect: alert triggers when p99 short-seq latency > 150 ms or error_rate delta > 0.05%.
2) Triage: oncall page -> add incident tag `scheduler-experiment-<id>`; notify runtime-policy-owner and kernel-owner.
3) Quick rollback: run (requires runtime-coordinator access):
   - curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     https://runtime-coordinator.internal/api/v1/experiments/<id>/rollback
   - Alternatively: set runtime-coordinator policy_deactivate=true for policy id.
4) Postmortem: collect perf-lab job artifacts, full traces (use runbook `operator-livetrace-collection-and-rollback-playbook-2027`), and open postmortem ticket with severity, timeline, and owner.

Owner and escalation matrix
---------------------------
- Experiment owner: runtime-scheduler team (oncall: @runtime-scheduler).
- Kernel variant owner: kernel-team (oncall: @kernel-oncall).
- SRE escalation: runtime-sre (pager rotation).

Configuration table (recommended starting defaults)
--------------------------------------------------
Parameter | Default | Notes
---------|---------|------
kernel_hint.profile | conservative_fp16 | safe default that prefers stability
kernel_hint.min_occupancy | 50 | percent, reduce aggressive switching below this
admission.speculative_batch.enabled | true | set false only in targeted canaries
admission.max_batch_size | 64 | avoid >64 for short-seq heavy routes
scheduler.preemption_budget_ms | 100 | per-GPU per-minute budget for preemption

Appendix A — Network augmentation for perf-lab replay
----------------------------------------------------
- Add a synthetic latency layer to perf-lab Docker network: tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 8ms 4ms distribution normal.
- Documented in perf-lab job by adding "netem_delay_ms": 8.

Appendix B — Replay mapping example
----------------------------------
- Map production route `chat-api-v2` -> replay corpus `chat-api-v2-2026-11-sampled-24h`
- Replay config snippet: 
  replay_map:
    - route: chat-api-v2
      corpus: chat-api-v2-2026-11-sampled-24h
      sample_rate: 0.12

Appendix C — Useful CLI snippets
--------------------------------
- Start a perf-lab job: perf-lab submit --job-file jobs/scheduler-experiment-<id>.json
- Query canary metrics: curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/query?experiment=<id>&window=1h" | jq .
- Force rollback (runtime-coordinator): kubectl -n runtime exec svc/runtime-coordinator -- \
  -- ./runner rollback --experiment <id> --reason "ops-triggered-rollback"

Document maintenance and ownership
----------------------------------
- This manual is owned by the eng-serving-runtime / runtime-scheduler subteam.
- Update cadence: every major scheduler release or after a canary that resulted in rollback.
- Related pages: add postmortems and perf-lab job ids under related_pages.

If you are about to run an experiment and this manual does not fully answer your questions, open a PR to this doc and tag @Miguel Torres for review.

title: Operational Workload Simulator and Signature Guide
content:
Overview

This document describes the Operational Workload Simulator (OWS): a deterministic, configurable engine used by the eng-serving-runtime team to emulate customer traffic shapes, infer kernel-scheduler interactions, and produce telemetry signatures that feed the benchmarking and autotune pipelines. The OWS is intended for performance experiments, release validation, and as a canonical source of workload descriptors for replay across clouds and local sandboxes.

Goals

- Provide a small set (~8) of canonical workload signatures that cover >90% of production request shapes for text-generation and chat routes.
- Produce reproducible latency/cost buckets for CI and release verification.
- Emit annotated traces and kernel-hint suggestions to accelerate scheduling experiments.
- Be lightweight and portable: runnable in developer sandboxes and CI runners.

Workload signature taxonomy

Each signature is a compact descriptor summarizing the request distribution we want the runtime to see. Signatures are identified by id, human name, and a short rationale. Use the signature ids in experiments and report names.

Signature table (canonical set)

| id | name | request mix | mean tokens | percentile shape | primary risk | use case |
|----|------|-------------|-------------|------------------|--------------|----------|
| sig-llow | Low-latency chat (short-turn) | 90% chat-turn / 10% gen | 32 | tight (P99 ~ P95*1.2) | tail latency | UI chat, assistants |
| sig-lburst | Burst small prompts | 70% tiny / 30% small | 16 | spiky | scheduler warmstart | bot spiking behavior |
| sig-synth | Long generation seq | 100% generation | 1024 | heavy tail | memory pressure | document generation, summarization |
| sig-mix1 | Mixed enterprise | 50% chat / 30% embed / 20% gen | 128 | bi-modal | KV cache churn | multi-tenant enterprise |
| sig-embed | Embeddings heavy | 95% embed requests | 256 | narrow | throughput saturation | embedding pipelines |
| sig-prefetch | Stateful prefetched | 60% chat with KV hints | 64 | moderate | stale KV warmup | sessionized agents |
| sig-lowq | Low-quality cheap tokens | 100% short gen | 8 | narrow | over-batching | telemetry sampling |
| sig-noisy | Erratic unseen shapes | random mix | mixed | unpredictable | kernel thrash | chaos testing |

Simulator architecture (high level)

- Input: YAML workload descriptor (example below) describing arrival process, request templates, sequence lengths, and KV-cache locality.
- Orchestration: single binary (owsctl) schedules clients and records per-request metadata.
- Execution modes: local (single process), distributed (controller + worker), and CI-mode (deterministic RNG seeds).
- Outputs: time-series of latency percentiles, per-token cost estimate, kernel selection log, and full trace bundles (zip of trace.json + kernel-events.csv).

Workload descriptor (example YAML)

-- sample-workload.yaml --
name: long-document-summaries
id: sig-synth
seed: 20260201
arrival:
  distribution: poisson
  lambda: 0.8  # requests/sec per client
clients: 8
templates:
  - type: generation
    model_variants: ["rw-7b-q4f16", "rw-7b-fp16"]
    length:
      distribution: lognormal
      mu: 6.9  # exp(mu) ~ 1000 tokens
    temperature: 0.0
kv_locality: low
session_affinity: false
metrics_to_emit: [latency, kernel_hints, kv_miss_rate]

Kernel-hint mapping and guidance

The simulator emits a preliminary kernel_hint bundle that maps observed sequence-length histograms + concurrency to recommended kernel profile names. Use these hints to seed experimental scheduler policies or to annotate A/B runs. The guideline for interpreting hints is: 

- Hint level: "suggest" | "caution" | "avoid"
- Key signals used: mean_seq_len, tail_seq_len (P95/P99), kv_cache_hit_ratio, avg_concurrency, burst_index (max RPS / mean RPS)

Example kernel hint CSV (excerpt)

signature_id,mean_seq,P95_seq,kv_hit,avg_conc,burst_index,hint_level,recommended_profile
sig-synth,1024,2048,0.23,4,3.4,suggest,large-tile-qkv-fusion
sig-llow,32,48,0.88,16,1.3,avoid,large-batch-optimizations

Mapping rules (summary)

- If mean_seq > 512 and kv_hit < 0.4 -> prefer memory-efficient kernels, enable fragmented-kv-eviction.
- If avg_conc > 12 and burst_index < 2 -> enable continuous-batching aggressive slice.
- If burst_index > 3 and kv_hit > 0.7 -> warmstart fast-path kernels and prefetch KV.

Running experiments (step-by-step)

1. Prepare environment: export OWS_ARTIFACT_DIR=/tmp/ows-runs && mkdir -p $OWS_ARTIFACT_DIR
2. Pick signature YAML: examples/sig-llow.yaml
3. Run locally for quick smoke: ./owsctl run --profile local --config examples/sig-llow.yaml --out $OWS_ARTIFACT_DIR/sig-llow-20260218
4. For distributed: ./owsctl controller --config cluster-controller.yaml & then ./owsctl worker --join-controller http://controller:9000 --config examples/sig-synth.yaml
5. After run completes, generate report: ./owsctl report --input $OWS_ARTIFACT_DIR/sig-llow-20260218 --format html --output report-sig-llow.html
