Repeatability and CI integration

- Use deterministic seeds in CI-mode; the runner will assert histogram equivalence (within tolerance) vs baseline.
- Baseline artifacts are stored in s3://redwood-bench-baselines/ows/ and referenced by signature id and git sha. CI job will fail on >5% regression in P99 latency for P50 traffic.

Telemetry emitted and acceptance criteria

Essential emitted signals:
- latency_p50/p95/p99 (ms)
- per_token_cost_estimate (USD/token)
- kernel_profile_distribution (counts)
- kv_cache_hit_rate
- gpu_utilization and mem_peak (MB)
- trace_bundle_url

Acceptance criteria for pre-release smoke (recommended):
- P50 change from baseline: < 2%
- P95 change from baseline: < 5%
- P99 change from baseline: < 10%
- Per-token cost delta: < 7% (absolute) or flagged for review
- Kernel-profile shift: no more than 2 suggested-profile changes for sig-llow and sig-embed

Experiment matrix and result naming

- Always include signature id + model variant + kernel-profile + run-seed in artifact names, e.g.: sig-synth__rw-7b-q4f16__large-tile-qkv-fusion__s20260201.zip
- Suggested matrix dimensions: signature x model_variant x concurrency x kernel_profile x quant_mode

Telemetry interpretation and correlation playbook (short)

1. Start with latency regressions: correlate P99 spikes with kernel_profile_distribution shifts and kv_cache_hit_rate drops.
2. If kernel events indicate repeated kernel load/unload, check burst_index and device memory fragmentation traces.
3. For throughput regressions, correlate GPU utilization vs avg_concurrency and queue_depth histograms.
4. For cost regressions, inspect per_token_cost_estimate and kernel time breakdown (attention vs decoder vs memcpy).

Troubleshooting checklist

- Symptom: Unexpected P99 increase in local runs
  1) Confirm deterministic seed and workload descriptor unchanged
  2) Check kernel_profile distribution in trace bundle; look for sudden "fallback" profile usage
  3) Inspect worker logs for OOMs / driver warnings
  4) Run with -v debug and attach sampling profiler: ./owsctl run --profile local --config X --debug-sampler

- Symptom: Different behavior in distributed vs local
  1) Verify clock skew and controller/worker time sync
  2) Confirm number of clients and threadpool sizes match (controller overrides matters)
  3) Check network latency histogram between controller and workers; high controller latency can artificially increase burst_index

Ownership and lifecycle

- Owning team: eng-serving-runtime (benchmarking subteam)
- Primary owner: Maya Patel (author)
- Secondary owners: Diego Martinez (kernel experiments), Priya Singh (profiling/telemetry)
- Review cadence: Quarterly; bump major versions for simulation model or schema changes.

Change log (high level)

- 2025-11-12: v0.1 created (initial canonical signatures and runner CLI)
- 2026-01-20: v0.2 added distributed controller, kernel-hint CSV output
- 2026-02-18: v0.3 tightened CI acceptance thresholds and stabilized P95 baseline comparison

Appendices

Appendix A — Common config flags
--threads N          # client threads per worker
--deterministic true # enable deterministic RNG
--emit-trace true    # create per-request trace bundles

Appendix B — Minimal example: quick local smoke
1) git checkout main && git pull origin main
2) ./owsctl run --profile local --config examples/sig-lowq.yaml --out /tmp/ows-quick
3) ./owsctl report --input /tmp/ows-quick --format text

Appendix C — Contact and escalation
- Slack: #eng-serving-runtime-bench (primary channel)
- Pager: eng-sre on-call for infra issues (see oncall roster)
- Pager escalation path: bench-owner -> runtime-sre -> infra-team

If you are adding a new workload signature, add a short rationale, expected badge (latency/cost vs baseline), and at least one representative production trace id in the related_pages field.

title: Fidelity correlation benchmarking playbook
content:
Summary
------
This playbook describes a repeatable process to benchmark correlation between model fidelity (quality) and runtime execution signals (latency, kernel selection, memory pressure, quantization path) across production-like workloads. The goal is to produce actionable correlations that guide scheduler, kernel, and quantization changes without regressing customer-visible quality.

Why this doc exists
-------------------
- Engineers often optimize for cost/latency and see unexpected changes in output quality.
- Quantitative correlation between fidelity metrics and runtime signals helps make safe tradeoffs.
- This playbook standardizes experiment design, telemetry collection, and analysis so that findings can be validated and operationalized.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Audience: runtime engineers, benchmarking owners, SREs, model-onboarding team.
- Scope: inference workloads for text generation and chat; includes model variants, quantized kernels, and multi-tenant scheduling shapes.
- Out of scope: training fidelity analysis, dataset labeling methodology outside of our eval harness.

Key definitions
---------------
- Fidelity: end-to-end task quality measured by an agreed prompt set and evaluation metric (e.g., BLEU, ROUGE, or Redwood QA score).
- Runtime signal: telemetry emitted by the runtime (per-request latency percentiles, kernel variant id, slot preemption count, KV cache hit rate, accelerator occupancy).
- Correlation window: time window used to align telemetry and fidelity observations (default: 1 hour for production mirroring tests, 5–15 minutes for synthetic load tests).

Required tooling and infra
------------------------
- Benchmark runner: benchmarking-and-perf-suite/runner v2.1 (supports traffic shaping and mixed concurrency).
- Eval harness: eval-harness/cli v0.9 for automated fidelity scoring against standardized prompt sets.
- Trace collector: tracing pipeline (OTLP -> internal collector) with the kernel and scheduler annotations enabled.
- Shadow traffic mirror: network mirror that can replay production traffic into an isolated runtime fleet.
- Metrics store: Prometheus + long-term rollup in ClickHouse for hourly aggregates.

Pre-experiment checklist
------------------------
1. Confirm owner: assign an experiment owner and at least one reviewer (SRE + model owner).
2. Select prompt set: choose a representative prompt set from prompt-sets-and-benchmarks labeled with the workload fingerprint.
3. Baseline health: ensure SLAs on baseline fleet (p90 < target latency, error rate < 0.1%).
4. Telemetry sanity: verify trace and metric tags are present: model_version, kernel_variant, scheduling_slot_id, shard_id, quantization_profile.
5. Dependencies: confirm benchmark runner and eval harness versions in the experiment README.

Experiment matrix design
------------------------
Design a factorial matrix to isolate effects. Common factors:
- Model variant: full-precision, 8-bit quantized, mixed-precision.
- Kernel variant: tensor-core fast-path, fallback kernel, sparse-attention kernel.
- Scheduling policy: fairness-first, latency-priority, batch-aggressive.
- Load shape: steady-state low-concurrency, bursty peak, long-sequence heavy.

Matrix example (4x3x3x3 = 108 runs):
| Factor | Values |
|--|--|
| Model variant | fp16, int8, int8+kv
| Kernel variant | fast, fallback, sparse
| Scheduling policy | fairness, latency, burst
| Load shape | steady, burst, long

Data collection and alignment
-----------------------------
1. Start metric capture and trace collection for all candidate fleets.
2. Run the benchmark runner to generate controlled traffic for each matrix cell. Ensure a warmup period of at least 10 minutes to stabilize KV caches and batch patterns.
3. Simultaneously run the eval harness against the same prompt set and collect fidelity scores. For stochastic models run N=5 seeds and aggregate mean/CI.
4. Aggregate telemetry into hourly buckets and align with fidelity scores using the correlation window. Use request IDs or hash(provenance) for per-request joining when available.

Primary metrics to collect (per request)
- latency_ms (p50, p90, p99)
- kernel_variant_id
- kernel_execution_time_ms
- kv_cache_hit (boolean)
- batch_size
- accelerator_util_pct
- quantization_profile
- model_version
- fidelity_score (from eval harness)

Analysis procedure
------------------
1. Exploratory data checks: confirm distributions, missing telemetry, and outliers.
2. Correlation analysis: compute Spearman and Pearson correlations between fidelity_score and each runtime signal. Report 95% confidence intervals.
3. Conditional effects: use stratified analysis (e.g., p99 latency when kv_cache_hit=false) to identify interaction effects.
4. Simple causal checks: run ablated tests (flip single factor while holding others constant) and validate delta fidelity.
5. Regression detection: if any metric change co-occurs with fidelity drop > threshold (see threshold table) escalate to a quality hold.

Thresholds and decision rules
----------------------------
| Signal | Alert threshold | Action |
|--|--|--|
| p99 latency | +20% vs baseline | Investigate scheduler backlog and kernel slow-paths
| fidelity_score | -2.0 points absolute (task-specific) | Block rollout, start joint triage (runtime + model owner)
| kv_cache_hit_rate | -10 percentage points | Check cache affinity and warmstart profiles
| kernel_fallback_rate | > 5% | Evaluate kernel correctness and performance regressions

Recommended default fidelity thresholds (examples):
- Short-form summarization: delta ROUGE-L <= 1.5 absolute
- Q&A fidelity (Redwood QA): delta <= 2 points

Reporting and artifacts
-----------------------
Every experiment must produce a single artifact bundle:
- experiment-manifest.yml (matrix, versions, runner config)
- telemetry-rollup.csv (hourly aggregates)
- fidelity-results.json (per-prompt scores and seed stats)
- analysis-notebook.ipynb (minimum reproducible notebook with the correlation figures)
- triage-log.md (if any thresholds are breached)
Upload artifacts to the experiment bucket: s3://redwood-experiments/fidelity-correlation/{yyyyMMdd}_{owner}_{id}.

Operationalization path
-----------------------
1. If correlations show a safe optimization (e.g., int8 reduces cost with < threshold fidelity delta), prepare a controlled rollout plan.
2. Create a runtime feature flag for the kernel/quantization change.
3. Run a canary with mirrored traffic for 48 hours and validate metrics.
4. Use the Redwood Console route-level QA gating: require fidelity_score check to pass on canary before expanding.

Escalation and triage playbook
------------------------------
1. If fidelity threshold is breached, pause rollout and notify: #runtime-incidents, model-owner, and release manager.
2. Triage steps:
   a. Confirm telemetry alignment and timestamps.
   b. Run targeted replay for failing prompt subset (use experiment-manifest filters).
   c. Check kernel logs for errors or fallback signatures.
   d. Assess whether degradation is deterministic or stochastic across seeds.
3. Rollback criteria: complete rollback if fidelity delta persists after 3 targeted replay attempts or if customers report reproducible failures.

Troubleshooting FAQ
-------------------
- Q: My fidelity score is noisy across runs. A: Increase sample seeds to N>=10 and use median-of-means for robust estimates.
- Q: Kernel variant tags missing in traces. A: Ensure runtime build includes "kernel-annotator" and that trace sampling for the experiment is set to 100%.
- Q: Correlation but no causal signal. A: Run single-factor ablation (hold other variables constant) and verify reproducibility.

Appendix A — sample experiment-manifest.yml
------------------------------------------
experiment_id: fidelity-20260115-aisha
owner: aisha.patel@redwood.ai
matrix:
  model_variant: [fp16, int8]
  kernel_variant: [fast, fallback]
  scheduling: [latency, fairness]
  load_shape: [steady, burst]
runner_config:
  duration_minutes: 120
  warmup_minutes: 15
  concurrency_profile: steady-200
eval_config:
  prompt_set: summarization/clinical-abstracts-v2
  seeds: 5
  metric: rouge_l

Appendix B — example CLI commands
---------------------------------
# start telemetry capture
$ benchctl start-capture --experiment fidelity-20260115-aisha --tags "fidelity,playbook"

# run a single cell
$ benchctl run-cell --manifest experiment-manifest.yml --cell "model_variant=fp16,kernel_variant=fast, scheduling=latency"

# collect eval results
$ eval-harness run --config eval_config.yml --out fidelity-results.json

Ownership and contact
---------------------
- Playbook owner: Aisha Patel (eng: runtime-inference)
- Oncall contact: eng-sre oncall (pager-duty)
- Suggested reviewers for experiments: model-onboarding, eng-sre, kernel-maintainers

Change log
----------
- 2025-11-10: Draft created.
- 2025-12-05: Added matrix example and threshold table after internal review.
- 2026-01-15: Finalized reporting artifact list and canary requirements.

Related reading and links
-------------------------
- quantization-profiles/index
- prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/summarization/README
- runtime-architecture/fidelity-orchestrator-telemetry-contract-runbook-2026

End of document

title: Shadowing & Fidelity Convergence Lab Protocol
content:
Summary

This page documents the lab protocol for running controlled shadow (mirrored) traffic experiments to measure "fidelity convergence" across model variants and kernel scheduling profiles. Fidelity convergence is the process of comparing output quality (task-specific metrics and human-validated checks) between a live production model and candidate variants (quantized, distilled, or alternative kernels) while simultaneously measuring performance and scheduler interactions. The protocol is intended for benchmarking-and-perf-suite engineers, runtime engineers, and applied ML evaluators.

Goals

- Produce reproducible, comparable fidelity metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/EM/accuracy for task datasets; embedding cosine similarity for retrieval) between model variants and production model.
- Measure kernel-scheduler interaction effects: how different scheduler policies (e.g., preemptive-shepherding, batch-slicing, slotting) affect fidelity under load.
- Provide a safe failover and rollback runbook for experiments that impact latency or error budgets.
- Deliver a data artifact package that supports triage: latency histograms, per-token cost, kernel trace events, KV-cache hit/miss rates, and sample outputs.

Scope and Definitions

- Shadowing: replicate a proportion p of production requests and send them to a candidate model variant without altering the client-visible response. Logging and sampling must ensure privacy and PII handling consistent with data policy.
- Fidelity Convergence Threshold (FCT): threshold defining acceptable divergence; default: mean task metric drop <= 1.5% absolute and embedding cosine >= 0.985. Product teams can define stricter thresholds per SLA.
- Kernel Scheduling Profile: a named set of scheduler parameters (slot_size, preemption_timeout_ms, batch_slice_limit) used by the runtime.

Pre-requisites

1. Canary baseline: a validated production canary model id (e.g., model:redwood-v1-canary).
2. Candidate artifact: containerized candidate model + kernel hints (quantization profile id, kernel hint file).
3. Access: experiment-runner service role with read/write to telemetry S3 bucket and the sandboxed runtime namespace.
4. Quotas: ensure shadow traffic rate is limited to <= 10% of production RPS or a configurable safe cap defined in the experiment config.

Experiment Design

1) Select dataset and metrics
- Synthetic corpora: short prompts (<= 64 tokens), medium (128-512), long (512-2048).
- Evaluation datasets: use the canonical task corpus for the product (e.g., ticket-summarization-testset-v3) and a random production-sampled corpus (anonymized).
- Metrics: task accuracy / BLEU / ROUGE, embedding cosine, hallucination rate (via extractor), latency P50/P90/P99, per-token cost, KV-cache hit ratio.

2) Choose shadowing fraction and routing policy
- Default: 5% shadowing with stratified sampling across customers and request sizes.
- Routing policy: mirror -> candidate variant in 'sandbox' pool, with enforced kernel-scheduler profile. If the runtime detects any P99 or error-rate regression beyond thresholds, automatically drop shadow to 0% (see runbook).

3) Kernel schedule matrix (example)
- profile:baseline { slot_size: 16, preemption_timeout_ms: 50, batch_slice_limit: 4 }
- profile:latency-optim { slot_size: 8, preemption_timeout_ms: 20, batch_slice_limit: 2 }
- profile:throughput-optim { slot_size: 32, preemption_timeout_ms: 200, batch_slice_limit: 8 }

Run Steps (numbered)

1. Provision candidate: push candidate model artifact to sandbox registry and register variant in model-catalog under tag experiment/<id>.
2. Prepare experiment config (example YAML below).
3. Run a dry run against replayed traffic for 1 hour to check for obvious crashes and kernel-level OOMs.
4. Start shadow with rate cap; monitor real-time dashboards and automated gates for 60 minutes.
5. Escalate to expanded run if gates pass (see gating criteria).
6. Post-process logs for fidelity metrics, kernel traces, and scheduler attribution.

Example experiment YAML

experiment_id: shadow-fc-2026-02
shadow_fraction: 0.05
routing:
  pool: sandbox
  kernel_profile: latency-optim
datasets:
  - ticket-summarization-testset-v3
  - prod-anon-sample-2026-02
metrics:
  - task_accuracy
  - embedding_cosine
  - p50_latency
  - p99_latency
gates:
  p99_latency_regression_ms: 50
  error_rate_delta_pct: 0.5
  fidelity_drop_pct_absolute: 1.5

Monitoring and telemetry

Required metrics and traces to collect for each request (retention 30 days):
- request_id, route_id, model_variant_id, kernel_profile, token_count, kvcache_hit, batch_id
- latency_ms (end-to-end), compute_ms (kernel-level), gpu_cycles, memory_bytes_allocated
- scheduler_events: enqueue_time, dequeue_time, preempted_flag, slot_alloc_ms
- sampled outputs (1:1000 sampling) with anonymized prompt hash and output hash

Dashboards (required)
- Fidelity Overview: task metric delta, distribution plots, output examples
- Performance Overview: p50/p90/p99 latency split by kernel_profile and request_size bucket
- Scheduler Attribution: preemption counts, slot occupancy heatmap, batch sizes over time

Gating Criteria (automated)

- Gate FAIL if p99 latency increases by > p99_latency_regression_ms OR error_rate increases by > error_rate_delta_pct OR fidelity_drop_pct_absolute exceeded.
- Gate WARN if task metric drop between 1.0% and 1.5% or embedding cosine between 0.985 and 0.99.

Safe Stop & Rollback Runbook (quick steps)

1. If Gate FAIL triggers, experiment-runner will automatically set shadow_fraction=0 and mute candidate variant. Notify oncall (@eng-serving-oncall) via PagerDuty.
2. Run a triage job: collect kernel traces for last 15 minutes, export to /s3/experiments/<id>/artifacts/triage.
3. If regression caused by scheduler policy, revert kernel_profile to baseline and re-run dry replay.
4. If regression is fidelity-related, mark candidate as rejected and create an evaluation ticket with sample outputs and diff table.

Ownership and contacts

- Experiment owner: Priya Shah (applied-ml infra).
- Runtime instrumentation owner: Marco Rivera (eng-serving-runtime).
- Kernel scheduler owner: Yuna Kim (kernel-scheduling team).
- PagerDuty: eng-serving-oncall (primary), eng-sre-backup (secondary).

Data artifacts to publish

- fidelity_report.csv (task metrics aggregated by prompt size and customer cohort)
- kernel_trace.ndjson (annotated scheduler events)
- latency_histograms.json (p50/p90/p99 by bucket)
- sample_outputs.jsonl (anonymized samples with comparator diffs)

Post-experiment analysis checklist

1. Confirm artifact integrity and retention location.
2. Run statistical significance test (paired bootstrap) on primary metric; record p-value.
3. Annotate top 20 divergent samples and assign to an evaluator for manual review.
4. If pass: create rollout proposal including recommended kernel_profile and quantization profile, estimated cost delta, and rollback plan.

Appendix: Quick diagnostic commands

- Start a 1-hour dry replay locally (dev cluster):
  curl -X POST https://experiment-runner.internal/run -d '{"experiment_id":"shadow-fc-2026-02","mode":"replay","duration":"1h"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'

- Export kernel traces for experiment:
  aws s3 cp s3://telemetry/experiments/shadow-fc-2026-02/kernel_trace.ndjson ./kernel_trace.ndjson

- Minimal jq to compute embedding cosine distribution:
  jq -r '.samples[] | .embedding_cosine' artifacts/sample_outputs.jsonl | ./percentile-aggregator --p99

References and related pages

- Performance regression huntbook (see related pages).
- Runtime scheduler telemetry contract (team wiki).

Notes and change log

- 2025-11-12: Initial draft (Priya Shah).
- 2026-01-20: Added gating thresholds and kernel_profile matrix after internal pilot (Marco Rivera).
- 2026-02-15: Updated artifact retention and monitoring list to match new telemetry schema (Yuna Kim).

End of document

title: Service Fidelity Spotlight — End-to-end Benchmark & Kernel Impact Mapping Protocol
content:
Overview

This page defines a repeatable, cross-team protocol for spotlighting service-level fidelity changes (quality vs. cost/latency) and mapping those changes to kernel scheduling and runtime subsystems. Use this protocol when onboarding a new model variant, validating a quantization rollout, or investigating regressions in production SLOs. The goal: produce a minimal, reproducible benchmark and instrumentation bundle that ties observable customer impact to kernel-level signals and actionable runbook steps.

Scope

- Applies to: runtime-dispatcher, kernel-scheduler, kvcache-store, gpu-dispatcher, request-multiplexer, and model-variant-adapter.
- Not covered: client-side SDK behavior, non-inference storage tiers, or billing pipelines (except where cost-per-token is measured).

Success Criteria

- A reproducible benchmark (input corpus + harness) that reproduces the customer-visible regression within ±5% on p95 latency and token-efficiency.
- Mapped kernel signals (GPU occupancy, kernel-duration histogram, warp-stall rate, memory-copy latency) correlated with at least one service-level metric.
- A short remediation runbook with owner and rollback clause that can be executed within a 2-hour operational window.

Quick summary of metrics to capture (minimum):

| Metric | Level | Target window | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p95 request latency (inference path) | service | 60s | end-to-end, excluding client network |
| p99 tail latency | service | 60s | critical for SLO signoff |
| tokens/sec per-GPU | infra | 60s | aggregated by gpu-dispatcher |
| kernel duration (histogram) | kernel | 10s | per-kernel id, percentile buckets |
| GPU occupancy | kernel | 10s | % of active warps/SMs |
| KV cache hit ratio | service | 60s | per-session prefix reuse |
| end-to-end quality delta | application | corpus-run | BLEU/ROUGE/LL-judge score per prompt set |

Bench harness and corpus

1) Choose a narrow corpus that represents the failing surface: typically 200–1000 prompts drawn from production replay (anonymized) or curated prompt set.
2) Define a deterministic run profile: request concurrency, sequence length distribution, and per-request stop tokens.
3) Use the benchmark harness located at infra/bench/harness (team artifact) with the following example invocation: 

# Example CLI (internal lab machine with GPU access)
# runs 500 prompt-replays with concurrency=16 against a local runtime build
./bench/harness \
  --target http://localhost:8080/v1/generate \
  --corpus ./corpora/fidelity-spotlight/replica-2026.jsonl \
  --concurrency 16 \
  --seqlen-dist ./seqlen/prod-trimmed.yaml \
  --collect-kernel-traces /tmp/kernels.trace \
  --tag "fidelity-spotlight-$(date +%Y%m%d)"

Instrumentation checklist (kernel -> service mapping)

- Enable per-kernel tracing: kernel-scheduler must be started with KERNEL_TRACE=1 and trace export to a path with timestamps in nanoseconds.
- Correlate each request id with kernel trace id via the request-provenance header. Ensure request-provenance is present in the harness.
- Capture GPU metrics (SM utilisation, memory bandwidth, PCIe latency) using gpu-exporter at 5s resolution for the run.
- Collect runtime-level traces (request timeline) with trace level=INFO and the following fields: request_id, model_variant, sequence_length, kvcache_hit, chosen_kernel_hint, gpu_node.

Causal kernel-impact mapping procedure (numbered step playbook)

1. Baseline run: execute the bench harness against the previously certified model variant and collect all signals. Label artifact as baseline-<tag>.
2. Test run: execute the harness against the candidate model/quantization/kernel-change. Label artifact as candidate-<tag>.
3. Compute deltas for service metrics (p95/p99, tokens/sec, error-rate, quality delta). If deltas are <= threshold (p95 delta < 7%, quality delta within guardrail), proceed to step 7.
4. If regression observed, run kernel-signal diffing: align kernel traces by request_provenance and compute per-kernel-duration deltas and stall-rates.
5. Identify top-3 kernel IDs with largest duration increase and check associated inputs (sequence length, batch size, kvcache-hit). If top kernels map to attention or fused-matmul kernels, flag possible memory layout or schedule regressions.
6. Cross-check scheduling signals: examine scheduler decisions for these requests — preemption events, slice boundaries, and co-scheduled kernel sets. If scheduler consistently inserts extra preemption/slice boundaries for candidate, add scheduling hypothesis to incident doc.
7. Re-run targeted microbenchmarks for suspect kernels (single-kernel isolations) with 5–10% input perturbations to confirm sensitivity. Document command used and raw kernel profiles.
8. Produce remediation plan: configuration tweak (kernel-flag or scheduler param), model pin, or rollback. Include risk assessment and estimated cost impact.

Example kernel-focused profile snippet (text excerpt)

--- kernel-deltas.txt ---
kernel_id | baseline_p95_ms | candidate_p95_ms | delta_ms | suspected-cause
K_ATT_012 | 3.4 | 6.7 | +3.3 | attention-fused-layout-regression
K_FGEMM_03 | 1.1 | 1.3 | +0.2 | higher batch-padding (sequence skew)
K_COPY_00 | 0.05 | 0.8 | +0.75 | unexpected host->gpu memcpy (eviction)
--- end ---

Profiling playbook excerpts (how to capture good traces)

- Prefer stratified-capture: sample 1 in N requests for full kernel trace but collect light-weight metrics for all (tokens/sec, kv-hit). N depends on cost budget; default N=5.
- For tail investigations, use targeted 100% tracing on a small cohort of requests that hit the fault surface.
- Always correlate traces with the benchmark tag and git SHA of runtime to enable fast bisects.

Benchmark analysis checklist (deliverable items)

- Repro artifacts: corpus, harness args, kernel traces, gpu-exporter TSV, runtime log bundle, and model SHA.
- A concise findings table (1–2 pages) answering: What regressed? Which kernels changed? Which scheduler behavior changed? What is the recommended remediation?
- Estimated rollback cost and performance delta if remediation is applied.

Release notes & labelling template (short)

When a kernel or scheduler change is promoted to canary or prod, include the following in the release note: 

- Change ID: release/kernel-<X> or release/scheduler-<Y>
- Short description: what the change modifies
- Risk summary: p95 impact observed in lab runs (absolute and percent), top kernels affected
- Canary checklist: yes/no (list of required traces and metrics)
- Rollout gates: automatic rollback threshold (p99 increase > 15% or BLEU drop > 2 points)

Known-issues cataloging format (how to add an entry)

When you discover a novel kernel or scheduling-related issue, create an entry in the known-issues catalog with these flattened fields (one-line examples):

- id: KERNEL-2026-0123
- title: unexpected memcpy on model swap causing p99 spikes
- symptom: intermittent p99 spikes when model-variant-adapter performs hot-swap after session affinity change
- kernel_evidence: kernel COPY_00 duration increased by 10x for affected requests
- workarounds: reduce per-node max-connections to avoid hot-swap batching; disable aggressive prefetcher
- owner: Evan Ross

Runbook snippet (emergency mitigation for kernel regressions)

1. Triage: confirm alerts (p99 spike and tokens/sec drop) and fetch latest bench harness run tag.
2. Validate: run a short 5–10 minute harness with request-provenance set to 'triage-<incident>' against a replica canary pool.
3. If kernel duration anomaly reproduced, scale down candidate pool and route traffic to baseline variant (mechanism: runtime-routing annotate route/variant with fallback=true).
4. If routing not available, execute rapid rollback to previous runtime image via k8s rollout undo for runtime-dispatcher.
5. Collect post-mitigation traces and attach to incident ticket.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime oncall team (pager: #infra-oncall).
- Kernel/scheduler engineering owner: Liang Zhou (pager: @liang).
- Escalation path: owner -> eng-sre -> platform-ops -> exec on-call (document chain in incident ticket).

Appendix: useful commands and small configs

# Collect kernel traces (lab only)
export KERNEL_TRACE=1
./runtime/bin/runtime --config ./configs/lab.yaml &> /tmp/runtime.log &
./tools/trace-dump --input /tmp/kernels.trace --format csv --out /tmp/kernels.csv

# Example seqlen distribution YAML (prod-trimmed.yaml)
- bucket: short
  pct: 0.72
  avg: 32
- bucket: mid
  pct: 0.20
  avg: 128
- bucket: long
  pct: 0.08
  avg: 512

# Minimal analysis snippet (python-like pseudocode)
# correlate kernel traces with request ids and compute p95 delta
# load baseline and candidate kernels as CSV
# group by kernel_id and compute percentiles

Next steps and maintenance cadence

- Add a quarterly 'fidelity-spotlight' run to the benchmarking calendar (owner: benchmarking team) to exercise common regression surfaces across recent model changes.
- Maintain a short list of 10 canonical corpora that reflect customer segments. Update every 6 months.
- Revisit tracing cost budget and stratification policy annually.

Contact

For questions, reach out to: Asha Patel (author), Liang Zhou (kernel owner), Carlos Mendez (benchmarking lead).

title: Per-token energy and cost benchmarking for runtime configurations
content:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood's methodology for measuring per-token energy consumption and mapping that to unit cost across common runtime configurations. The goal is to provide reproducible benchmarks that combine power telemetry, token accounting, latency buckets, and scheduler/kernel settings. Use these measurements to: (1) guide model/quantization selection for cost-sensitive workloads, (2) set realistic energy-aware SLOs for Dedicated pools, and (3) feed cost-model inputs for the Console optimizer recommendations.

Scope and motivation:

- Scope: LLM inference CPU/GPU stacks used by Redwood Hosted and Dedicated runtimes. Includes: model variants (fp16/int8/q4f16), sequence lengths 8–2048, batching policies, KV cache hit/miss scenarios, and multi-tenant kernel scheduling modes.
- Motivation: token-level unit cost is traditionally driven by time-on-kernel. We complement that with measured power to capture the true marginal energy cost for chargeback and optimization. This matters for large-scale Dedicated fleets and green/Sustainability metrics.

Owner and contacts:

- Owner: eng-serving-runtime / Performance Team
- Primary contact: ravi.menon@redwood.ai
- Secondary: perf-oncall@redwood.ai

Definitions and conventions:

1) Measurement interval: telemetry window aligned to a request or batch lifecycle. Default: request submission time -> last token emitted + 5ms drain.
2) Per-token energy (ET): measured joules consumed attributable to generating a token. Calculation method described below.
3) Baseline idle power (P_idle): power draw of the node(s) measured with runtime process up but quiescent (no requests, background housekeeping allowed).
4) Attribution unit: single request, or combinable into micro-batches for throughput experiments.

Hardware and software profiles used in this doc:

- GPU types: A100 80GB (nvml), A10G 24GB (nvml), H100 (nvml).
- Node configs: 1xGPU, 4xGPU NCCL-sharded nodes.
- Runtime: redwood-runtime v2.3.1 (includes kernel scheduler v1.8).
- Kernel builds: cuda-12.2 + custom attention kernel v6.1.

Measurement methodology (step-by-step):

1) Prepare test fleet:
   a) Reserve 3 identical nodes for each hardware profile.
   b) Deploy runtime build under test with identical runtime flags except for the variable under measurement (e.g., quantization flag).

2) Calibrate idle power (P_idle):
   a) Remove user traffic and ensure collector is attached (nvml-exporter or node-power-proxy).
   b) Collect power for 120s and store median as P_idle_node.

3) Generate traffic workload:
   a) Use workload runner (perf-runner v1.5) with a representative prompt set. Include: small-chat (len 16), search-snippet (len 128), long-form (len 1024).
   b) For each request profile, run 10,000 requests for stable averages. Use fixed seed for deterministic tokenization.

4) Collect telemetry:
   a) Power telemetry: sample at 100Hz from NVML via node export.
   b) Runtime telemetry: token counts, kernel invocation timestamps, kernel IDs, batch sizes, and KV-cache hit ratio.
   c) Infrastructure telemetry: CPU utilization, PCIe bandwidth counters, GPU memory usage.

5) Compute per-token energy (ET):
   a) For each request window, compute energy_joules = SUM_over_samples(power_sample - P_idle_node) * sample_interval_seconds.
   b) ET_request = energy_joules / tokens_emitted_in_request.
   c) Aggregate across requests to produce mean, median, and 99th-percentile ET per workload bucket.

6) Convert energy to cost:
   a) Input parameters: cost_per_kWh (team finance input), datacenter PUE, currency.
   b) cost_per_joule = cost_per_kWh / (3600 * 1000).
   c) token_cost = ET_request * cost_per_joule * PUE.

Minimum reproducibility checklist (run before publishing results):

- [ ] Node clock sync verified (chrony/ntp).
- [ ] nvml-exporter version logged and consistent across nodes.
- [ ] Workload runner commit hash recorded.
- [ ] Kernel build id and runtime version recorded.
- [ ] P_idle measurement attached.
- [ ] At least 3 nodes per profile used with cross-node variance reported.

Example measurement table (text CSV):

Profile,Model,Quant,Sequence,Mean ET (J),Median ET (J),P99 ET (J),Tokens/s,Mean latency (ms),Token cost (USD*1e-6)
small-chat-16,redwood-7b,fp16,16,0.085,0.078,0.150,4200,2.1,0.32
search-128,redwood-7b,q4f16,128,0.22,0.21,0.40,1800,8.5,0.83
long-1024,open-70b,fp16,1024,1.9,1.8,3.6,110,92,7.2

Observations from initial runs (summary):

- Quantization (q4/q8) reduces per-token energy by 20%–45% depending on GPU and sequence length; savings are largest on memory-bound long sequences where reduced memory traffic reduces PCIe and cache thrash.
- Batch coalescing increases tokens/s but can increase peak power draw; net per-token energy often decreases for medium-length sequences because kernel amortization dominates.
- KV-cache hits reduce ET per token by ~10% for long-form generation due to fewer recomputed attention kernels.
- Scheduler mode matters: ‘‘preemptive-strict’’ reduces tail ET variance by enforcing kernel preemption at a small latency cost; ‘‘greedy-batch’’ yields lower mean ET but higher P99.

Recommended reporting format for dashboards and Console integration:

- Fields to expose per model-config: mean_ET_j, p50_ET_j, p95_ET_j, p99_ET_j, tokens_per_second, mean_latency_ms, token_cost_usd_1e-6, hardware_profile, kernel_build, runtime_version, sample_size.
- Expose an annotation for any measurement where KV-cache behavior is >90% hit or variance on P_idle >5%.

Common pitfalls and mitigations:

- Pitfall: Idle measurement drift due to background system jobs. Mitigation: pin collector to cgroup and exclude telemetry windows where system CPU >5%.
- Pitfall: NVML sampling aliasing with kernel bursts -> undercounting of short spikes. Mitigation: increase NVML sampling to 200Hz for short-burst tests or use direct power-sampling kernel.
- Pitfall: Tokenization differences across tokenizer versions causing token count mismatches. Mitigation: freeze tokenizer commit used for each benchmark and include tokenizer hash in results.

Actionable tuning checklist (for operators):

1) If per-token energy is higher than baseline by >30% for a given model-config:
   - Validate that kernel build matches the recommended kernel list (see "approved-kernels.txt").
   - Check for memory thrashing on GPU (mem_util > 95% for sustained periods).
   - If model is memory-bound, try quantized variant or increase batch size if latency budget allows.

2) If P99 ET is high (>2x mean):
   - Investigate scheduler preemption mode and noisy neighbors.
   - Run single-tenant microbench to isolate kernel scheduling effects.

3) If tokens/s is unexpectedly low after a runtime upgrade:
   - Compare kernel timings across two builds using kernel-trace profile.
   - Rollback to previous kernel candidate if regression persists, and open a kernel-bisect ticket.

How this feeds into product decisions and Console optimizations:

- Pricing: token_cost estimates feed into Dedicated capacity pricing simulations. Use mean token_cost for baseline price and p95 for SLO reserve.
- Autoscaling heuristics: energy-aware policies can prefer lower-energy nodes during non-peak windows to reduce cost without violating throughput SLOs.
- Model recommendations: Optimize will prefer a model/quantization combo that minimizes token_cost while meeting latency SLO.

Example CLI snippets and reproducibility artifacts:

- Start power collector:
  ./tools/node-power-proxy --nvml --sample-rate 100 --out /tmp/power-node-1.csv

- Run workload runner (example):
  perf-runner run --workload small-chat-16 --concurrency 64 --requests 10000 --seed 42 --out /tmp/results-small-chat-16.json

- Compute ET (example one-liner):
  python tools/et_calc.py --power /tmp/power-node-1.csv --telemetry /tmp/results-small-chat-16.json --p_idle 75 --out /tmp/et-small-chat.csv

Telemetry artifact checklist to store with results (artifact names):

- power_samples.csv
- runtime_telemetry.json
- workload_runner_commit.txt
- kernel_build_id.txt
- node_inventory.csv

Ownership and escalation:

- Primary owner for running energy benchmarks: eng-serving-runtime / Performance Team.
- Escalation path: perf-oncall -> runtime-kernel-team -> infra-hw-support.

Appendix A: Example cost conversion parameters (finance input)

- cost_per_kWh = $0.06
- PUE = 1.2
- cost_per_joule = 0.06 / 3,600,000 = 1.67e-8 USD/J

Appendix B: Quick reference table of recommended sampling rates

Telemetry,Recommended sampling
Power (short-burst),200Hz
Power (steady-state),50–100Hz
Runtime events (kernel),event-driven with nanosecond timestamps
Infrastructure metrics,1s

Related reading and links:

- Throughput & latency workload catalog (see related pages)

title: Cost Model Inputs from Serving Runtime Metrics (v1)
content:
## Overview
This document defines the *runtime-exported inputs* required by the Standard Cost Model (SCM) to produce consistent per-request and aggregated cost breakdowns across Console, Optimize, and finance reporting.

The Serving Runtime is the source of truth for:
- Prefill vs decode token accounting (including accepted/emitted vs attempted tokens)
- KV cache behavior (hits/misses, reuse, evictions)
- Batching and scheduling outcomes (batch sizes, queue times, GPU occupancy proxies)
- Quantization execution path identifiers (what actually ran on-GPU)

This page is a contract between Serving Runtime, Telemetry, and the Cost Model service.

### Scope
**In scope (v1):** metrics emitted per request (or per request stage) that the cost model needs to explain cost deltas driven by caching/batching/quantization and to allocate runtime-attributable costs.

**Out of scope (v1):** full kernel-level profilers, per-layer timing breakdowns, and proprietary hardware counters. We prefer coarse but stable identifiers and low-cardinality metrics that can be aggregated safely.

---

## Contract principles
1. **Deterministic semantics:** A metric means one thing across all runtimes and deployment modes.
2. **Low cardinality by design:** Values must be bounded; raw histograms are preferred over unbounded sets.
3. **Stage-aware accounting:** Prefill and decode are first-class stages for both token and time/cost attribution.
4. **Execution-path truth:** The cost model keys off what the runtime *actually executed* (kernel/quant path ID), not what the request asked for.
5. **Backwards compatibility:** New fields are additive. Renames require dual-write for ≥2 releases and a deprecation notice.

---

## Emission model
Runtime emits a single logical record per request with optional stage sub-metrics.

### Required record identifiers
These identifiers must be present on every record so Telemetry can join with platform and billing primitives:
- **request_id**: globally unique within a region; UUID string
- **tenant_id**: Redwood tenant/org identifier
- **project_id**: project/workspace identifier (if applicable)
- **deployment_mode**: hosted | dedicated | private
- **region**: e.g., us-east-1
- **model_id**: catalog model identifier (pinned version)
- **model_revision**: immutable model revision hash or build id
- **runtime_build_id**: runtime binary build/version
- **hardware_sku**: canonical GPU SKU label (e.g., a100-80gb, h100-sxm)

Note: Several of these come from the control plane; however the runtime must *pass through* the identifiers it was scheduled with, so the emitted record is self-contained.

---

## Metrics: tokens & stages
The SCM requires tokens to be attributed to prefill vs decode consistently.

### Definitions
- **prefill_tokens**: number of prompt tokens processed in the initial forward pass for the accepted prompt.
- **decode_tokens_emitted**: number of tokens emitted to the client (including streamed tokens).
- **decode_tokens_attempted**: number of decode steps attempted, including tokens that were later suppressed/rolled back by stop conditions.

In v1 cost breakdowns, Console uses **decode_tokens_emitted** for customer-visible token counts, while internal performance modeling may use **decode_tokens_attempted** to explain compute waste. Both are exported to allow reconciliation.

### Fields (required)
- **tokens.prefill.accepted** (int, tokens)
- **tokens.decode.emitted** (int, tokens)
- **tokens.decode.attempted** (int, tokens)
- **tokens.total.accepted** (int, tokens) = prefill.accepted + decode.emitted

### Fields (recommended)
- **tokens.prefill.cached_reused** (int, tokens)
  - Number of prefill tokens for which KV state was reused from cache (see KV cache section).

---

## Metrics: KV cache
KV cache behavior is the most important runtime-only driver for cost differences across otherwise identical requests.

### KV cache semantic model
We track cache at the request level in terms of:
- **prefix reuse**: how many prompt tokens did not require compute because their KV states were available
- **missed compute**: how many tokens required prefill compute
- **evictions**: how often we had to evict KV blocks, causing lower hit rates and/or recomputation

### Fields (required)
All units and semantics below must be stable across implementations.

1) **kv_cache.enabled** (bool)
- True if the request was eligible to use KV caching (even if hit_rate is 0).

2) **kv_cache.lookup_status** (enum)
- allowed values: disabled | no_key | hit | partial_hit | miss | error
- “partial_hit” indicates some prefix tokens were reused but not the full eligible prefix.

3) **kv_cache.prefix_tokens_eligible** (int, tokens)
- Number of prompt tokens eligible for KV reuse (after normalization, templates, and routing decisions).

4) **kv_cache.prefix_tokens_reused** (int, tokens)
- Subset of eligible prefix tokens whose KV states were reused.

5) **kv_cache.blocks_reused** (int, blocks)
- Count of KV blocks reused (block size is runtime-defined but must be consistent within a runtime_build_id).

6) **kv_cache.blocks_written** (int, blocks)
- New KV blocks written for this request.

7) **kv_cache.evictions** (int, blocks)
- Number of blocks evicted attributable to this request’s execution window.

### Fields (recommended)
- **kv_cache.eviction_reason** (enum): capacity | ttl | policy | fragmentation | unknown
- **kv_cache.cache_namespace** (string, bounded)
  - A small, bounded label (e.g., tenant-scoped vs global) used for debugging hit rate differences. Must not include tenant IDs or unbounded values.

### Validation rules
- prefix_tokens_reused ≤ prefix_tokens_eligible
- lookup_status = hit implies prefix_tokens_reused = prefix_tokens_eligible
- lookup_status = disabled implies kv_cache.enabled = false and all kv_cache.* counts are 0

---

## Metrics: batching & scheduling
Batching and scheduling outcomes influence effective GPU time per token, and are required to explain unit-cost changes as batching configuration changes.

### Concepts
- **request queue time**: time from runtime receiving the request until it is assigned to a batch for prefill
- **continuous batching**: decode steps can be interleaved across requests; this affects decode efficiency metrics

### Fields (required)
1) **scheduler.queue_time_ms** (int, ms)
- Time from request enqueue to first execution (prefill start).

2) **scheduler.prefill_batch_size** (int, requests)
- Number of requests included in the batch for the prefill stage.

3) **scheduler.decode_max_batch_size_observed** (int, requests)
- Maximum number of concurrently active sequences in the decode loop while this request was active.

4) **scheduler.decode_mean_batch_size** (float, requests)
- Mean active batch size across decode steps for this request.

5) **scheduler.tokens_per_step_mean** (float, tokens/step)
- Mean tokens advanced per decode step across the batch while this request was active.

### Fields (recommended)
- **scheduler.prefill_microbatch_count** (int)
  - If prefill is microbatched internally.
- **scheduler.decode_steps** (int)
  - Number of decode iterations observed for this request.
- **scheduler.throttled** (bool)
  - True if scheduler throttling engaged (capacity protection / SLO protection).
- **scheduler.throttle_reason** (enum): gpu_mem | queue_depth | fairness | overload | unknown

### Cardinality constraints
- throttle_reason and lookup_status must be enums with a fixed set.
- No per-request lists of batch composition or other request IDs.

---

## Metrics: latency & runtime time attribution
The SCM uses runtime wall times for reconciliation and drift analysis, and to allocate overhead when configured.

### Fields (required)
- **timing.request_total_ms** (int, ms)
- **timing.prefill_compute_ms** (int, ms)
- **timing.decode_compute_ms** (int, ms)

### Fields (recommended)
- **timing.serialization_ms** (int, ms)
- **timing.network_overhead_ms** (int, ms)
- **timing.runtime_overhead_ms** (int, ms)

Notes:
- “compute_ms” includes time spent executing model kernels and any runtime-managed waits in the execution stream.
- “overhead” fields are for internal diagnostics; the SCM may use them for overhead allocation policies depending on ADR-022 configuration.

---

## Metrics: quantization execution path
The SCM must know what quantization *actually ran* to apply the correct throughput/cost profile and to support Optimize what-if projections.

### Required identifiers
1) **quant.profile_id** (string)
- Stable identifier from the model catalog (e.g., qfp16, int8-awq-v2, fp8-e4m3fn).
- Must match catalog IDs used by Optimize and SCM.

2) **quant.execution_path_id** (string)
- Runtime-chosen execution path identifier. Examples:
  - fp16_tensorcore_v3
  - int8_awq_gemm_v2
  - fp8_mixed_precision_v1
- Must be bounded and versioned by runtime_build_id; avoid embedding raw kernel hashes.

3) **quant.kernel_family** (enum)
- allowed values: fp16 | bf16 | fp8 | int8 | int4 | mixed | unknown

### Recommended identifiers
- **quant.kv_cache_dtype** (enum): fp16 | bf16 | fp8 | int8 | unknown
- **quant.weights_dtype** (enum): fp16 | bf16 | fp8 | int8 | int4 | unknown
- **quant.activations_dtype** (enum): fp16 | bf16 | fp8 | int8 | unknown

### Failure mode requirement
If quantization metadata is missing, runtime must set:
- quant.profile_id = "unknown"
- quant.execution_path_id = "unknown"
- quant.kernel_family = unknown

Do not omit the fields; omission complicates downstream schema negotiation and drift triage.

---

## Request outcome & safety signals
These are used by SCM and Console to avoid attributing costs incorrectly in partial or failed requests.

### Fields (required)
- **outcome.status** (enum): success | client_cancel | timeout | rate_limited | server_error
- **outcome.http_status_code** (int)
- **outcome.retry_count** (int)

### Fields (recommended)
- **outcome.error_class** (enum): none | overload | oom | invalid_request | upstream_dependency | unknown
- **outcome.fallback_taken** (bool)
- **outcome.fallback_reason** (enum): capacity | model_unavailable | policy | safety | unknown

---

## Example payload (runtime → telemetry)
This example shows the shape Telemetry should expect; actual transport may be OTLP attributes + metrics, but fields and semantics must match.

{
  "request_id": "req_7bdf1d2c-4a65-4d0b-b1b4-7c2dbf2d2b33",
  "tenant_id": "tnt_3f2c...",
  "project_id": "prj_91a...",
  "deployment_mode": "hosted",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "model_id": "rw-llama-3-70b-instruct",
  "model_revision": "rev_2026-02-01_8b1c",
  "runtime_build_id": "runtime-1.38.2",
  "hardware_sku": "h100-sxm",

  "tokens.prefill.accepted": 1142,
  "tokens.decode.emitted": 268,
  "tokens.decode.attempted": 270,
  "tokens.total.accepted": 1410,

  "kv_cache.enabled": true,
  "kv_cache.lookup_status": "partial_hit",
  "kv_cache.prefix_tokens_eligible": 900,
  "kv_cache.prefix_tokens_reused": 740,
  "kv_cache.blocks_reused": 185,
  "kv_cache.blocks_written": 95,
  "kv_cache.evictions": 0,

  "scheduler.queue_time_ms": 12,
  "scheduler.prefill_batch_size": 6,
  "scheduler.decode_max_batch_size_observed": 28,
  "scheduler.decode_mean_batch_size": 19.4,
  "scheduler.tokens_per_step_mean": 18.7,

  "timing.request_total_ms": 832,
  "timing.prefill_compute_ms": 241,
  "timing.decode_compute_ms": 523,

  "quant.profile_id": "fp8-e4m3fn",
  "quant.execution_path_id": "fp8_mixed_precision_v1",
  "quant.kernel_family": "fp8",

  "outcome.status": "success",
  "outcome.http_status_code": 200,
  "outcome.retry_count": 0
}

---

## Implementation notes (runtime owners)
### Where to compute these metrics
- Token counts should be emitted from the tokenizer + generation loop with a single canonical counter source.
- Prefill/decode compute times should be measured at the runtime scheduling boundary (not client-side).
- KV cache metrics must be emitted by the cache subsystem, not inferred from prompt hashes downstream.
- Quantization execution path should be emitted by the kernel selection / execution plan component.

### OTLP mapping guidance
- Prefer OTLP **span attributes** for identifiers and enums.
- Prefer OTLP **metrics** for numeric counters/timers, but ensure they can be joined by request_id (trace ID) in Telemetry.
- Avoid high-frequency per-token events; export aggregate per-request values.

---

## Data quality & conformance testing
Telemetry and SCM require conformance checks to avoid silent drift.

### Required checks (CI + staging)
- Prefill/decode tokens must satisfy: total.accepted = prefill.accepted + decode.emitted
- queue_time_ms ≥ 0; compute_ms ≥ 0
- lookup_status enum membership validation
- quant.profile_id must be one of: catalog-known IDs OR "unknown" (alert on unknown rate)

### Recommended runtime perf-suite tests
- KV cache hit/miss scenario replay: verify prefix_tokens_reused behavior across known prompt templates
- Batching scenario replay: verify decode_mean_batch_size monotonicity under controlled load
- Quantization A/B: verify execution_path_id changes when profile changes, and remains stable within a runtime_build_id

---

## Ownership & change process
- **Owning team:** Serving Runtime (Scheduling + Kernel Selection)
- **Primary owners:** Omar El-Sayed (KV cache/prefill-decode), Sofia Ivanova (scheduling), Grace Kim (quantization execution)

### Change policy
- Any semantic change requires an ADR or an addendum to the SCM schema docs.
- Breaking changes require:
  1) Dual-write old+new for at least 2 runtime releases
  2) Telemetry backfill/translation plan (if needed)
  3) Sign-off from SCM service owner (Platform) and Telemetry lead

---

## Open questions / v2 candidates
- Representing *cache warm-rate* explicitly (Optimize request): likely requires aggregate workload metrics rather than per-request fields.
- Differentiating “compute stalled due to memory pressure” vs “scheduler queueing” using additional runtime counters.
- Standardizing microbatch-level visibility without increasing cardinality.

title: Cross-layer capacity probing and fidelity sampling protocol
content:
Overview

This document defines a repeatable protocol for cross-layer capacity probing and fidelity-aware sampling used by the runtime performance and benchmarking teams. The goal is to produce deterministic, signal-rich datasets that drive scheduling, kernel selection, and model-variant routing decisions while preserving production safety.

Goals

- Measure usable capacity and safe degradation points across the full stack (dispatcher -> scheduler -> kernel -> kvcache).
- Correlate fidelity changes (quantization, sharding, batching) with cost and error surface.
- Produce automatable data and thresholds for runtime admission controllers and canary policies.

Scope

- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private runtime variants that use the runtime-dispatcher and kernel-allocator services.
- Focused on core token-generation workloads (chat, standard completion) and embedding workloads where applicable.
- Excludes long-running offline training jobs and third-party accelerator tests unless explicitly scheduled.

Terminology

- Probe: A controlled synthetic traffic pattern used to stress a subsystem.
- Cohort: A grouping of similar requests (seq_len, prompt shape, model variant).
- Fidelity step: A discrete change in model execution (e.g., int8 -> int4, kv cache disabled, half-precision -> full-precision).
- Safe degradation point: The earliest observed point where SLOs are broken for >5% of traffic in a cohort and recovery is non-deterministic.

Ownership

- Author: Jordan Kim (Runtime Performance)
- Primary owners: runtime-performance (eng), kernel-schedulers (eng)
- Observability steward: Priya Nair (Eng Platform)

Required signals & SLOs

Collect the following signals for each probe run:

- request_id (string)
- timestamp (ISO-8601)
- cohort_id (string)
- model_variant (string)
- seq_len (int)
- tokens_generated (int)
- kernel_id (string)
- kernel_latency_ms (float)
- dispatcher_queue_ms (float)
- kvcache_hit (boolean)
- gpu_util_pct (float)
- gpu_mem_used_mb (int)
- host_mem_used_mb (int)
- error_class (string | null)

Minimum SLOs to compare against in probing runs:

- p95 tail latency (generation end-to-end) <= 200 ms for seq_len <= 64 on standard variants.
- p99 <= 800 ms for seq_len <= 64.
- p95 CPU/GPU utilization should not exceed target utilization by more than 12 percentage points for normal ops.

Protocol steps (runbook)

1) Prepare experiment harness

- Create or reuse a synthetic corpus that mirrors the cohort profile (use request-surface-replay tool).
- Configure a probe matrix: cohorts x fidelity-steps x target-utilization (40%, 65%, 85%).
- Pin the runtime image and kernel bundle used for the baseline.

2) Baseline run (no degradation)

- Run each cohort at 40% target-utilization for 30m.
- Record all signals and confirm observability pipes (zipkin/traces, metrics, and probe dataset ingest).
- Validate that baseline SLOs are met; if not, abort and create an action ticket.

3) Fidelity steps and progressive pressure

- For each fidelity change (e.g., int8->int4, reduced KV cache capacity, smaller beam size), run the cohort at target utilizations in increasing order: 40%, 65%, 85%.
- Each run duration: 20m steady-state after 5m warmup.
- If any run breaches p99 latency target or shows >5% error_class != null, mark that combination as degraded.

4) Controlled overload probing

- For candidate safe-degradation points, perform a controlled overload: ramp utilization by +5% per minute until p95 or error thresholds violated or max 100% util reached.
- Capture kernel-level traces for 1 minute windows centered on threshold-crossing events.

5) Automated analysis and threshold extraction

- Run the probe-analyze job to extract: usable_capacity_per_cohort, degradation_onset_util, kernel_breakpoint_map (kernel_id -> seq_len -> latency slope).
- Persist outputs to the benchmarking dataset namespace with tags: commit, runtime-image, kernel-bundle, probe-id.

Data collection schema (text table)

| field | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| probe_id | string | unique id for the probe run |
| cohort_id | string | cohort signature (seq_len_distribution + prompt-type) |
| fidelity_tag | string | description of fidelity step |
| util_target_pct | int | requested target utilization |
| observed_gpu_util_pct | float | observed per-GPU utilization |
| p50_latency_ms | float | generation p50 |
| p95_latency_ms | float | generation p95 |
| p99_latency_ms | float | generation p99 |
| error_rate_pct | float | fraction of requests with error_class != null |

Experiment harness sample config (YAML)

```
probe_id: probe-2026-02-08-crosslayer-01
runtime_image: runtime:v2026.02.01
kernel_bundle: kernels/2026-01-28/optimized
cohorts:
  - id: chat-short
    seq_len_dist: [8, 16, 32]
    qps: 400
fidelity_steps:
  - tag: baseline-int8-kvcache-on
  - tag: int4-kvcache-on
  - tag: int4-kvcache-limited
util_targets: [40, 65, 85]
run_duration_min: 20
warmup_min: 5
observability_endpoints:
  metrics: prometheus.cluster.local:9090
  traces: zipkin.cluster.local:9411
```

Analysis and decision criteria

- Usable capacity: the highest util_target where p95 and error_rate_pct are within SLO thresholds for two consecutive runs.
- Safe degradation point: the util at which p99 is exceeded OR error_rate_pct rises >5% compared to baseline, and the kernel_breakpoint_map shows non-linear latency slope for critical kernels.
- Kernel pin recommendation: if kernel latency slope crosses >2x per additional 10 tokens for a cohort, recommend pinning to alternative kernel_id or fallthrough policy in the scheduler.

Rollout / automation gates

1. Generated thresholds and recommendations are pushed to the staging runtime-operator via the probe-ci pipeline.
2. Staging will run a lightweight canary (10% traffic) for 24h with automatic rollback on SLO breach.
3. If canary is green, a progressive rollout (25% -> 50% -> 100% over 72h) is initiated with telemetry-based automatic pause if p95 rises >10% from baseline.

Safety notes

- Never run overload probes on production serving clusters without explicit SRE approval. Use dedicated probe clusters that mirror topology instead.
- Always include a rollback plan and a pre-created hotpatch image if kernel regressions are suspected.

Troubleshooting common failure modes

- Missing traces: confirm that the probe-runner has write permissions to trace-ingest and that sampling rate is not 0.
- High variance between runs: check sequence-length distribution drift and re-run baseline with matched corpus.
- Kernel OOMs during overload: reduce batch sizes in the probe matrix and capture coredump + kernel telemetry.

Appendix: quick diagnostic commands

- Start a probe-run locally (dev cluster):
  ./tools/probe-runner --config probe-config.yaml --dry-run=false

- Extract probe artifacts:
  gsutil cp gs://benchmarks/probe-2026-02-08-crosslayer-01/*.ndjson ./local/

Related pages

- See runtime-scaling-experiment-protocol-and-benchmark-checklist-2026 for scheduling prerequisites.
- See variance-driven-sampling-and-cost-correlation-playbook-2026 for sampling strategies and cost attribution.

Change log

- 2025-11-12: Document authored.
- 2026-02-08: Added automated analysis step and YAML harness sample.

title: Coordinated Execution: Benchmarks & Sampling Protocol
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines a coordinated execution benchmark and sampling protocol for validating scheduler and kernel interactions across mixed inference workloads. It complements existing per-component tests by providing a reproducible end-to-end measurement harness, standardized metrics, and a lightweight on-call triage flow for anomalies that arise during benchmark runs.

Goals
-----
- Provide an experiment protocol that produces stable, comparable signals for: latency P50/P95/P99, token throughput, per-token GPU time, kernel-switch rate, and KV-cache hit/miss impact.
- Standardize sampling, tracing, and aggregation so regression hunts can compare like-for-like across runtime versions and hardware shapes.
- Offer step-by-step runbook sections for running, interpreting, and responding to benchmark anomalies.

Scope and Non-Goals
-------------------
- Scope: multi-tenant mixed inference profiles (chat + single-turn generation + long-context summarization), scheduler interaction patterns (admission, preemption, handoff), and sampling-based profiling to attribute tail latency to kernel or network layers.
- Non-goals: this is not a replacement for microbenchmarks (kernel unit tests) nor for customer-specific capacity planning; it should be used as a cross-cutting integration verification and regression detector.

Overview of the Protocol
------------------------
1. Define workload cohorts: head (short chat, 8–64 tokens), mid (generation, 64–512 tokens), tail (long-context, 512–4k tokens). Each cohort has an associated QPS target and entropy profile.
2. Synthesize request surface: use the workload corpus generator (see Appendix) to produce deterministic request sequences for each cohort.
3. Run a staged experiment matrix across hardware shapes and kernel build variants. For each cell collect: end-to-end traces (sampled), kernel-level traces (per-dispatch timestamps), and telemetry counters (scheduler signals, admission events, eviction events).
4. Apply the sampling and aggregation rules below to produce a canonical report.

Workload Cohort Definitions
- Head: 100ms target latency, 8–64 tokens, QPS per-cohort: 100–300.
- Mid: 200–500ms target, 64–512 tokens, QPS: 10–50.
- Tail: 500ms–5s target, 512–4k tokens, QPS: 0.5–5.

Key Metrics (aggregation rules)
- Latency: P50/P90/P95/P99 measured end-to-end and kernel-only. Kernel-only = sum(kernel execution windows on device).
- Token throughput: tokens/sec measured per-cohort and aggregated weighted by customer-weighted token shares.
- Kernel-switch rate: number of kernel handoffs per request (normalize by sequence length).
- KV-cache hit ratio and miss latency contribution: report absolute and delta vs baseline.
- Preemption/eviction rate: events per 1k requests.

Sampling & Tracing Rules
------------------------
- Deterministic seed: All synthetic corpora must be generated with a fixed RNG seed per experiment id. Record the seed in the run metadata.
- Stratified sampling: sample 1 in N end-to-end requests per cohort to capture full trace data. N is chosen so that overhead < 2% CPU and <1% GPU time: default N=100 for head, 50 for mid, 10 for tail.
- Kernel-level sampling: enable fine-grained kernel timestamps for 1 in 500 kernel invocations (circular buffer). These traces should be uploaded as compressed artifacts for offline attribution.
- Trace metadata requirements: every trace must include request id, cohort tag, sequence length, model variant id, kernel-variant tag, scheduler-policy snapshot, and node/hardware id.

Telemetry Signals to Collect
- Scheduler: admission decisions, slot allocation, priority buckets, preemption timestamp, backpressure signals.
- Kernel: kernel_id, kernel_variant, start_ts, end_ts, device_mem_used, thread_block_count.
- Network / RPC: inbound queue time, serialization time, outbound flush latency.
- KV-cache: shard_id, hit/miss, fetch_latency, warmup_state.

Experiment Matrix Example (table)
| Dimension          | Values / Notes                      | Default selection |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------|-------------------|
| Hardware shape    | A100x8, A100x4, L40x8, H100x8        | A100x8            |
| Model variant     | fp16, int8-quant, trimmed-ctx       | fp16              |
| Scheduler policy  | latency-first, economic-governor    | latency-first     |
| Load pattern      | steady, poisson-burst, diurnal-saw  | steady            |
| Cohort mix        | 70/25/5 head/mid/tail               | 70/25/5           |

Pass/Fail Criteria (example thresholds)
- Kernel P99 regression: fail if kernel-only P99 increases > 15% vs baseline.
- End-to-end P99: fail if > 25% increase OR absolute > 2s for mid cohort.
- KV-cache miss contribution: fail if miss-induced latency increases > 30ms average.

Investigation & Triage Runbook
------------------------------
1. Validate inputs: confirm RNG seed, cohort mix, and hardware cell match the experiment matrix.
2. Compare traces: aggregate top-3 root cause candidates by per-request kernel-only latency contribution.
3. Check scheduler signals: are admission delays or preemptions elevated? Check admission queue length and priority inversion counters.
4. Inspect kernel histogram: look for new long-tail modes indicating kernel stalls or thermal throttling.
5. Inspect device metrics: GPU SM utilization, PCIe transfer spikes, and nvlink error counters.
6. If kernel-only latency is unchanged but end-to-end regresses, inspect RPC and serialization metrics and network egress congestion.
7. Run targeted microbenchmarks: isolate suspect kernel variant on controlled single-tenant run to confirm reproducer.
8. If reproducer found, create an issue with: run id, seed, failing metrics, top traces (compressed), and suggested hypothesis.

Quick Mitigations (operational)
- Swap scheduler policy to economic-governor for degraded tail pressure scenarios.
- Pin cohort-heavy customers to isolation pool (dedicated capacity) if noisy neighbor observed.
- Temporarily enable kernel hedging for long tail requests (config toggle, see Runtime Flags table).

Runtime Flags & Configuration Table
| Flag name                         | Purpose                                      | Recommended value |
|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| runtime.benchmark.sample_rate    | stratified sampling divisor (per-cohort)     | head:100,mid:50,tail:10 |
| runtime.kernel.trace_window      | kernel-level trace buffer (entries)          | 500               |
| runtime.scheduler.policy         | active scheduler profile                     | latency-first     |
| runtime.kv.prefetch_threshold    | tokens ahead to prefetch                     | 64                |

Release Checklist (when using this protocol for a CVE/regression gate)
- Update canonical baseline artifact (store in artifact repo with run id).
- Run full experiment matrix across two hardware shapes.
- Ensure telemetry upload succeeded and artifacts are checksumed.
- Attach report + top 10 worst traces to PR and tag on-call owners.

Ownership and Contact
---------------------
- Owner: serving-runtime benchmarking team (oncall alias: eng-runtime-bench@redwood.example.com).
- Escalation: if evidence of hardware degradation, escalate to eng-infra GPU fleet team (pager: eng-gpu-fleet).

Appendix A — Example benchmark config (YAML)
```
experiment_id: coordinated-exec-2026-02
seed: 452318
cohort_mix:
  head: 70
  mid: 25
  tail: 5
hardware: A100x8
scheduler_policy: latency-first
sampling:
  head: 1/100
  mid: 1/50
  tail: 1/10
tracing:
  kernel_sample_divisor: 500
  artifacts_retention_days: 14
```

Appendix B — CLI snippets
- Start a run: redwood-bench run --config path/to/config.yaml --out /tmp/run-artifacts --note "perf-tuning-experiment"
- Upload artifacts: redwood-bench upload /tmp/run-artifacts --repo experiments/coord-exec
- Create quick report: redwood-bench report /tmp/run-artifacts --format html > /tmp/report.html

Appendix C — Example failure report template
- Run id: <run id>
- Baseline id: <baseline id>
- Delta metrics: {end_to_end_p99: +X%, kernel_only_p99: +Y%} 
- Top 5 traces (compressed path): /artifacts/<run>/trace-1.gz ...
- Hypothesis: <short description>
- Next steps: <list>

Document history
----------------
- 2025-11-03: created by Aisha Gupta (initial draft).
- 2026-01-12: added stratified sampling defaults and kernel sampling buffer guidance (reviewer: Marco Alvarez).
- 2026-02-10: clarified triage steps and added runtime flags table (reviewer: Nina Park).

title: Microbenchmark suite and variance analysis - 2025
content:
Overview:

This guide documents the microbenchmarking suite we run against the Redwood serving runtime to capture per-kernel and per-path variance characteristics that inform scheduling, batching, and autoscaling decisions. The document explains the test harness, recommended configurations, analysis steps for variance decomposition, example outputs, and actions owners should take when results indicate regressions.

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable, low-noise microbenchmark that isolates kernel execution time, memory-copy overhead, and KV-cache lookup variability.
- Produce variance decomposition reports (P95/P99 variance, coefficient of variation) by sampling across seeds, sequence lengths, and batch shapes.
- Surface kernel scheduling sensitivity (e.g., small-batch vs large-batch tradeoffs) to influence kernel mapper rules.
- Define actionable thresholds and an alerting/playbook for anomalous increases in variance.

Scope and Assumptions:
- Targets: single-GPU and 2-GPU shard topologies on A100 v4 and H100 hardware in our lab cluster.
- Tests are NOT full end-to-end requests (no network latency); they are focused on runtime hotspots (attention, softmax, kv-cache management, CUDA memcpy, decode tokenizer).
- Experiments assume stable host load; noisy host metrics invalidate runs (see run criteria below).

Test harness and repository:
- Harness: redwood/perf/microbench-suite (internal repo). Primary CLI: `rw-microbench run --profile <profile> --repeats 50 --out <dir>`
- Supported profiles: small-decoding, long-prefix-atten, kv-lookup-heavy, tiled-attention, quantized-int8-path.
- Artifact format: JSON lines where each line is {"timestamp","op","duration_ms","gpu_util","memcpy_ms","batch_shape","seed"}.

Recommended lab config (table):
| key | value | notes |
|---|---:|---|
| OS image | ubuntu-22.04+cuda_12.1 | lab standard image |
| Driver | NVIDIA 545.60 | pinned for reproducibility |
| CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES | 0 or 0,1 | set per-run |
| NUMACTL | preferred | bind to local numa when measuring |
| run_isolation | docker --cpuset-cpus + cgroups | avoid background processes |

Run criteria (pre-flight checklist):
1. No active builds or long-running loads on the target host.
2. GPU temperature < 45C and util < 2% for 60s.
3. Node-level interrupts below baseline.
4. Kernel cached artifacts compiled (rw-microbench compile-kernels) to avoid JIT warmups during measurement.

Execution pattern and sampling strategy:
- Repeats: 50 independent repeats per (profile, batch_shape, sequence_length). Each repeat runs 200 iterations internally and reports per-iteration latencies.
- Random seeds: use 5 distinct seeds per repeat group to exercise cache/prefetch variability.
- Warmup: 40 iterations of warmup that are discarded.
- Inter-run pause: 3s jittered +/-1s to reduce systematic alignment with other periodic tasks.

Metrics and derived statistics to compute:
- Mean and median op duration (ms) per op and overall path.
- Stddev and coefficient of variation (CV = stddev/mean).
- Tail variance: difference between P99 and P95, P999 if available.
- Between-seed variance: variance of medians across seeds.
- Cross-batch scaling slope: linearized slope of duration vs batch_size.

Example JSON snippet (collected output):
{
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T14:03:21Z",
  "op": "attn_forward_fused",
  "duration_ms": 0.72,
  "gpu_util": 3.4,
  "memcpy_ms": 0.05,
  "batch_shape": "1x128",
  "seed": "seed-03"
}

Analysis playbook (step-by-step):
1. Aggregate outputs into a single parquet file for fast slicing: `rw-microbench ingest --input <dir> --out runs.parquet`.
2. Produce per-op histograms and summary statistics: `rw-microbench analyze runs.parquet --ops attn_forward_fused,kv_lookup --output analysis/`.
3. Run variance decomposition: `rw-microbench variance-decompose analysis/ --group-by op,batch_shape,seed`. This produces a CSV with columns "op,group,mean,stddev,cv,p95,p99,between_seed_var".
4. Compare current run to baseline (stored in perf-bench-baselines). If CV increases by > 30% for ops with mean > 0.1 ms, mark as suspect.
5. If suspect, capture a flamegraph and kernel trace: `rw-instrument trace-kernels --target <node> --duration 120s --out trace/` (requires perf-admin role).

Thresholds and alerting rules (SRE owners):
- Informational: CV > 0.15 for op groups with mean >= 0.2ms.
- Warning: CV > 0.30 OR P99/P95 ratio > 3 for any op (mean >= 0.1ms).
- Critical: Between-seed variance increases by factor >= 2 AND absolute P99 increase > 25% compared to baseline.
- Alerts route to #runtime-perf and create ticket in PERF backlog with label "microbench-regression".

Common failure modes and triage guidance:
- Symptom: Increased memcpy_ms variance.
  - Likely causes: noisy PCIe bus, concurrent node-level memcpy, or NUMA misbinding.
  - Actions: run `nvidia-smi topo --matrix`, check dmesg for DMA errors, rerun with NUMACTL pinned.
- Symptom: Intermittent long-tail in attn_forward_fused.
  - Likely causes: kernel fallback path triggered due to unsupported shape or quantization mismatch.
  - Actions: verify kernel metadata via `rw-runtime kernel-inspect --op attn_forward_fused` and check kernel selector logs.
- Symptom: Between-seed variance dominates (seed medians jump).
  - Likely causes: cache eviction policy, non-deterministic scheduling, or memory page migration.
  - Actions: increase warmup iterations, run isolating test with only deterministic seeds, capture kernel trace.

Integration with scheduler/kernel-mapper decisions:
- The variance report should be consumed by the kernel-mapper pipeline: when CV for a kernel under small-batch shape exceeds 0.25, prefer a "latency-priority" kernel build for that shape in the next kernel release.
- Autoscaler: if per-request variance for small requests (batch 1) leads to P99 > 2x median, autoscale policy should add a latency-priority shard rather than increase batch size.

Release notes and historical baseline policy:
- Baselines are stored per hardware family and runtime minor version. Name format: baseline-<runtime>-<hw>-YYYYMMDD.
- When a kernel or runtime release is proposed, include a microbench variance report as part of the PR checklist. Changes that increase P99 by >10% require a mitigation plan.

Report example (condensed):
| op | batch_shape | mean_ms | p95_ms | p99_ms | cv | between_seed_var | verdict |
| attn_forward_fused | 1x64 | 0.45 | 0.60 | 1.78 | 0.28 | 0.05 | regressed |
| kv_lookup | 4x256 | 0.12 | 0.14 | 0.16 | 0.08 | 0.01 | ok |

Automated dashboards and artifacts:
- Grafana dashboard: /dashboards/microbench-variance (ingests aggregates exported to perf-metrics).
- Archived artifacts: s3://perf-artifacts/microbench/<run-id>/ with raw jsonl, parquet, flamegraphs, kernel traces.

Operational runbook (when a regression is detected):
1. Triage in #runtime-perf with run-id and attached summary.
2. Reproduce on a clean node using the same profile and seeds. If not reproducible, mark as intermittent and schedule a 24h watch with repeated runs.
3. If reproducible, capture `nvprof`/Nsight trace and attach to ticket.
4. Assign to runtime-kernel team and schedule a debug session.
5. If kernel-level fix is needed, pin a compatible kernel on canary traffic for 48h and run end-to-end smoke tests.

Known limitations and caveats:
- Microbench results do not include host-network variance; use workload-level benchmarks for end-to-end SLO validation.
- Small numeric differences may be introduced by different CUDA/textures driver versions. Always run baselines tied to driver versions.
- Some quantized kernels are non-deterministic across minor CUDA driver bumps; see known-issues/quantization-driver-drift.

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner: Maya Chen (runtime-performance).
- Secondary: Diego Alvarez (kernel-mapper), Priya Nambiar (scheduling).
- SRE escalation: oncall-runtime@s.redwood.com

Appendix A — Quick command reference:
- Compile kernels: `rw-microbench compile-kernels --profile tiled-attention`
- Run full microbench: `rw-microbench run --profile tiled-attention --repeats 50 --seeds 5 --out /tmp/run-202502`
- Ingest + analyze: `rw-microbench ingest --input /tmp/run-202502 --out runs.parquet && rw-microbench analyze runs.parquet --output /tmp/analysis`

Appendix B — Example kernel-inspect JSON (stringified in-line):
{"kernel":"attn_forward_fused","binary":"attn_fused_v3.so","shapes":["1x64","1x128"],"quant_support":["fp16","int8"],"priority":"latency-priority"}

Revision history:
- 2024-11-12: initial draft (Maya Chen)
- 2024-12-05: added thresholds and automation hooks (Diego Alvarez)
- 2025-02-03: clarified between-seed variance analysis and run isolation checklist (Priya Nambiar)

Related reading:
- See throughput-latency-workload-catalog for workload-level baselines.
- See runtime-profiling-playbook-guidelines for flamegraph capture and kernel tracing steps.

title: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype: results summary (runtime-1.18 candidate)
content:
## Summary
This page summarizes benchmark results for the **mixed-workload scheduler prototype** landing behind a feature flag in the **runtime-1.18 candidate**. The goal was to reduce **user-visible p95 tail latency** (especially TTFT for short prompts) under mixed prompt-length distributions without materially regressing throughput or fairness.

**Headline:** Across representative SKUs, the short/long class-based policy reduced **short-prompt p95 TTFT by ~18–41%** in mixed workloads, with **throughput within -0% to -3%** of baseline in most scenarios. Long-request latency increased slightly in some mixes but remained bounded with aging + token budgets. The primary regression observed was **kernel auto-selection instability on L40S** under a long-spike pattern (details below).

---

## Build + test matrix
**Candidate:** runtime-1.18.0-rc3 (scheduler prototype enabled via `scheduler.class_policy.enabled=true`)

**Baseline:** runtime-1.17.4 (existing continuous batching policy)

**Models tested (representative):**
- `rw-llama-3-8b-instruct` (batching friendly, common hosted usage)
- `rw-mistral-7b-instruct-v2` (sensitive to prefill contention)
- `rw-llama-3-70b-instruct` (limited coverage; used for sanity on high compute)

**SKUs / environments:**
- **H100-80GB (PCIe)**: Dedicated pool (us-east), driver 550.x
- **A100-80GB**: Hosted API pool (us-west), driver 535.x
- **L40S-48GB**: Cost-optimized pool (eu-west), driver 550.x

**Workload patterns (from benchmark plan):**
- **80/20 short/long**: 80% short chat-like prompts; 20% long-context prompts
- **50/50 mixed**: equal mix of short and long
- **Long-spike**: short traffic steady with periodic bursts of long-context requests
