1. Admission (onboarding): model artifact is registered with metadata including quantization-friendly flags, tokenization fingerprint, and probe manifest.
2. Shadow validation: run the probe manifest against a shadow fleet (same model version but isolated) for 24–72 hours to gather stability and fidelity metrics.
3. Micro-canary: route 0.1%–1% live traffic, enforce short stability window (30–120 minutes), and evaluate live SLO adherence and fidelity sentinels.
4. Ramp: exponential increase with verification windows (1h, 4h, 24h).
5. Full release: model marked as promoted; retention of shadow tracing for 7 days and periodic probes at 6h cadence.

Lifecycle checklist (must be present in model metadata on admission):
- model_id (artifact tag)
- quant-profile-tag (or "none")
- probe-manifest-location (URI)
- owner:team and pager
- required-metrics (list) and alert thresholds
- rollback-policy (immediate | manual-approval | gradual-fallback)

Probe manifest guidance:
- Each probe entry should include: name, description, expected-response-pattern, sample-size, annotation-template, priority (1–5), and affinity (latency/throughput/quant-sensitive).
- Include negative tests and adversarial perturbations alongside nominal cases.
- Design probes to be deterministic where possible (fixed seeds) and provide a re-seeding policy for stochastic tasks.

Example probe manifest (YAML snippet):
```yaml
probes:
  - name: longcontext-coherence-16k
    priority: 1
    sample_size: 120
    affinity: long-context
    expected_signatures: ["coherence_score>=0.85", "no-truncation"]
  - name: functioncall-stability
    priority: 2
    sample_size: 200
    affinity: function-call
    expected_signatures: ["return_schema_match", "latency_p50<180ms"]
```

Metric bundle and gating table:
The evaluability contract relies on a bundle paired with severity tiers for automated actions. Below is the recommended gate matrix used during micro-canary and ramp stages.

| Metric group | Metric | Canary Gate (0.1–1%) | Ramp Gate (1–25%) | Severity if breached | Action |
|--------------|--------|----------------------:|------------------:|---------------------:|--------|
| Latency | p50 / p95 / p99 (ms) | p95 < 300ms | p95 < 500ms | high | rollback or route-to-fallback |
| Quality | fidelity delta (anchor probes) | delta <= 0.03 | delta <= 0.05 | critical | immediate rollback, alert ML-oncall |
| Stability | response variance index (RVI) | RVI < 0.08 | RVI < 0.12 | high | pause ramp, run extended shadow |
| Cost | token-cost-per-request | < 1.2x baseline | < 1.5x baseline | medium | notify infra, consider quant-profile |
| Safety | sentinel-failure-rate | < 0.001 | < 0.002 | critical | block release, run safety sandbox |

Note: gates are expressed relative to the _baseline_ model/service being replaced. Baseline is recorded at admission-time.

Telemetry contract and required signals:
- Core signals: request_id, model_id, version, tenant_id, route, latency_p50/p95/p99, token_count_in/out, embed_dims (if applicable), kv_cache_hit, quant_profile_used.
- Quality signals: anchor_probe_id, anchor_score, human_rating_sample_id (if available).
- Stability signals: seed, randomness_label, prompt_hash, system_prompt_version.
- Safety signals: sentinel_id, fail_type, content_category_tags.

Automated gating engine behavior (implementation notes):
- Windowing: use rolling windows with both short (15m, 1h) and medium (6h, 24h) perspectives. Triggers must evaluate both absolute and trend-based deltas (e.g., 5% worsening over 1h).
- Aggregation: compute weighted metrics by traffic slice; heavy slices can dominate and should be isolated in evaluation.
- Explainability: when a gate trips, the engine emits a short diagnostic bundle (top-3 contributing slices, diff-of-anchors, sample failed requests).

Quantization and KV-cache considerations:
- Quant-sensitive probes: probe manifest must flag probes that are expected to be sensitive to quantization; for these probes require an explicit quant-fallback policy (e.g., route to FP16 variant or increase beam/temperature adjustments).
- KV-cache-aware ramp: for models using persistent KV caches, shadow validation must simulate realistic session patterns (e.g., average sequence length, churn, re-use rate). Include a KV-cache-hit metric and require no >5% drop compared to baseline in early gates.

Rollout policies (examples):
- Immediate rollback: any safety sentinel breach or fidelity delta > 0.07 during micro-canary triggers an immediate rollback to the last stable model.
- Gradual fallback: if latency breach but fidelity is maintained, apply CPU/GPU autoscaling or route to a quantized-but-tested variant for 10 minutes before rollback.
- Manual approval: model changes that touch embedding schema or function-calling require an explicit product/owner manual approval after ramp-green status.

Runbook: responding to a failing gate (steps):
1. Automated action: system pauses rollout and emits diagnostic bundle to #ml-oncall and #infra-ops.
2. Investigator triage (10–30m): owner inspects diagnostics, checks probe samples, and confirms whether breach is distributional or systemic.
3. Quick mitigation (30–90m): apply fallback routing (route 100% of affected slices to baseline), or increase replica capacity if latency-driven.
4. Root cause (RC) investigation (4–72h): pair with SRE to walk traces, reproduce in shadow, and propose permanent fix (model tweak, prompt rewrite, quant-profile change).
5. Post-incident: record regression tickets, update probe manifest if probe failed to detect the issue, and schedule re-run of the lifecycle.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Ownership: the model owner (ML engineer) is responsible for probe manifest correctness and responding to canary alerts. The platform (serving/runtime) team owns telemetry reliability and automated gating implementation. SRE owns capacity and latency remediation knobs.
- SLAs for evaluability pipeline: 99.9% availability for probe orchestration and 99.95% for telemetry ingestion during rollouts.

Acceptance checklist before full promotion (all must be green):
- Shadow pass: no critical sentinel failures for 72h and fidelity delta <= 0.03.
- Micro-canary pass: no critical breaches in 2 consecutive windows (30m and 2h).
- Telemetry completeness: all required signals present and validated for 24h.
- Rollout policy set: rollback path and fallback variant declared.

Operational examples and CLI snippets:
- Run a probe locally against the shadow fleet:
```bash
rwi eval run --model my-model:v2 --probes probes/longcontext-coherence-16k.yaml --shadow true --window 24h
```
- Query recent gate diagnostics (returns a small JSON bundle):
```bash
rwi eval diagnostics --model my-model:v2 --since 2026-02-28T00:00:00Z
```
(Above CLI returns a zipped bundle; platform UI will render top-10 failed samples inline.)

Appendix: common failure modes and preventive actions:
- Symptom: fidelity delta only in a specific tenant slice. Prevention: add isolation probes per-tenant or cohort and use tenant-aware ramping.
- Symptom: high p99 with stable p95. Prevention: add tail-probing with long sequences and adversarial tokens; consider micro-batching config change.
- Symptom: quantized variant regresses on function-call outputs. Prevention: include structured-output validation probes (schema conformance) in admission.

Questions and next steps:
- Proposed automation: upstream every model artifact with a minimal evaluability contract enforced by CI at merge-time.
- Owners: steward: Aisha Patel (applied-ml); implementation lead: Daniel Kim (eng-serving-runtime).
- Proposed milestones: CI gating POC by 2026-04-01; platform gating beta for internal teams by 2026-06-01.

References and links:
- See also: model promotion guidelines, probe taxonomy index, quantization profile catalog.
- Contact: #applied-ml, #serving-runtime, ml-oncall@redwood.internal

title: Heterogeneous Workload Shadow Orchestration and Telemetry Spec
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a standardized orchestration and telemetry specification for running 'shadow' evaluations across heterogeneous customer workloads (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, multi-turn stateful flows) and across deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private). The goal is to produce actionable, production-realistic signal for model promotion, quantization impact, and regression triage while preserving privacy and minimizing production risk.

Scope: eval harness components, sampling strategies, fingerprinting and workload signatures, capacity-aware routing, telemetry schema, data retention, onboarding steps, and remediation/fast-fail playbook. This is intended for ML Engineers, SREs, and Product owners responsible for model promotion and quality guardrails.

High-level principles

- Non-disruptive: Shadow traffic must not add user-visible latency or affect customer SLOs.
- Representative: Sampling must preserve distributional properties of the target workload (intent mix, sequence length, token distribution).
- Traceable: Every shadow request is tagged with identifiers that tie back to deployment configuration, quant profile, and sampling provenance.
- Cost-aware: Orchestrator must throttle shadow replication under capacity pressure.
- Privacy-first: Use local PII filtering and differential-privacy sampling when required by customer configuration.

Architecture and components

1) Mirroring Proxy (mirrord)
- Deployed as an ingress-layer sidecar or region-edge service.
- Responsible for duplicating production requests to a shadow queue without affecting production response path.
- Tags traffic with: workload_fingerprint, sample_bucket_id, region, model_variant, quant_profile.

2) Shadow Sampler (sampler-service)
- Implements sampling policies (fixed-rate, stratified, capacity-aware, slot-based).
- Maintains per-workload counters and safety budgets.
- Supports on-the-fly rate adjustments via the Control Plane.

3) Replay Store (replay-blob / kafka topics)
- Short-term durable store for shadow payloads (30–90 days depending on retention policy).
- Indexes by fingerprint and sample_bucket.

4) Eval Runner (evald)
- Pulls from Replay Store, executes against target model variant(s) and quant profiles, produces evaluation artifacts.
- Runs both lightweight (latency/throughput) and fidelity evals (semantic-similarity, task-specific metrics).

5) Telemetry Collector (telemetry ingestion layer)
- Central schema-enforced collector that receives delta metrics, logs, and artifacts.
- Emits normalized events to observability pipeline and to the eval dashboard.

6) Audit & Triage UI (eval-console)
- Surface diffs between baseline and candidate variants, grouped by fingerprint slice and quant-profile.
- Provides explainability overlays and links to raw artifacts.

Workload fingerprinting (why and how)

- Fingerprinting objective: group similar requests so shadow sampling preserves within-slice distributions and we can prioritize critical slices.
- Fingerprint components: route_id, intent_hash (top-level classification of user intent), token_length_bucket, device_context (web/mobile/api), language, privacy_flag.
- Implementation: deterministic hash of normalized request headers + canonicalized prompt text (PII redacted).

Sampling strategies

1) Capacity-Aware Stratified Sampling (default)
- Stratify by fingerprint slice (intent + length bucket + language).
- Allocate sampling budget proportional to slice-contribution to production traffic, with minimum floor to ensure coverage of low-frequency critical slices.
- Backpressure: when GPU pools approach 85% utilization, reduce non-critical slice replication by multiplicative decrease.

2) Focused Safety Sampling
- For newly onboarded prompt sets or after model changes, temporarily boost sampling for slices tagged as safety-sensitive by product owners.

3) Weighted Reservoir for Long-Tail
- Maintain a small reservoir of long-tail examples sampled uniformly across customers; useful for regression discovery.

4) Differential Privacy-Constrained Sampling
- Optionally enabled per-customer: samples are drawn in a way that enforces local epsilon budgets; shadow artifacts are tagged and processed under private lanes.

Telemetry schema (key events and fields)

All telemetry events use the eval_event schema v2. Fields below are top-level strings or simple numeric values; evaluators must surface them in dashboards.

- event_type: "shadow_request" | "eval_result" | "model_diff" | "resource_pressure"
- timestamp: ISO8601 string
- request_id: unique id (matches production request)
- workload_fingerprint: string
- sample_bucket_id: string
- route_id: string
- model_variant: string (e.g. redwood-phi-3b-v2)
- quant_profile: string (e.g. q4_0_dynamic)
- deployment_mode: string (hosted|dedicated|private)
- latency_ms: integer (end-to-end execution on shadow path)
- tokens_consumed: integer
- similarity_score: float (-1..1) // semantic similarity to baseline output if applicable
- fidelity_delta: float // positive means candidate improved against baseline on chosen metric
- failure_code: string | null
- privacy_flag: true|false
- capacity_flag: OK | THROTTLED | DROPPED

(Example JSON event)
{
  "event_type": "eval_result",
  "timestamp": "2025-10-22T14:33:12Z",
  "request_id": "r-7f3c2a",
  "workload_fingerprint": "intent=translate;len=short;lang=es",
  "model_variant": "redwood-phi-3b-v2",
  "quant_profile": "q4_0_dynamic",
  "latency_ms": 42,
  "tokens_consumed": 34,
  "similarity_score": 0.92,
  "fidelity_delta": -0.03
}

Acceptance criteria and thresholds

- Latency: shadow RTT should not add > 0.5ms to production P50 or cause more than 0.1% of production requests to breach P99 latency.
- Fidelity regression: for any critical slice, fidelity_delta must be >= -0.02 averaged across a 24h window, otherwise fail promotion.
- Embeddings drift: cosine similarity mean should not drop by > 0.015 on embedding baselines for core slices.
- Reranker NDCG: candidate should not degrade NDCG@10 by more than 0.01 for top-customer slices.

Config table (example)

- job_id: string (eval-job-2025-11-02-01)
- target_variants: [baseline, candidate] (as comma-separated string)
- slices: comma-separated list of fingerprint slices
- sampling_policy: capacity_aware|focused_safety|reservoir
- retention_days: numeric (30|90)
- max_parallel_jobs: numeric
- min_samples_per_slice: numeric

Example eval job YAML (for evalctl)

eval_job: eval-job-hetero-2025-11-02
target_variants: baseline=candidate: redwood-phi-3b-v1, candidate: redwood-phi-3b-v2
slices: intent:translate:len:short, intent:qa:len:medium
sampling_policy: capacity_aware
retention_days: 30
min_samples_per_slice: 100

CLI example

# create a shadow eval job from a sample policy
evalctl create --job eval-job-hetero-2025-11-02 --policy capacity_aware --slices "translate:short,qa:medium" --variants "baseline=redwood-phi-3b-v1,candidate=redwood-phi-3b-v2"

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step)

1) Workload annotation (owner: product/solutions)
- Define critical slices and expected behaviors. Tag prompts that are safety or compliance sensitive.
2) Fingerprint validation (owner: ML infra)
- Run offline fingerprint sampler on representative logs to ensure slice coverage and avoid over-fragmentation.
3) Sampling policy selection (owner: ML Engineer)
- Choose capacity_aware for steady-state workloads; focused_safety for new model releases; reservoir for exploratory audits.
4) Capacity planning (owner: SRE)
- Pre-allocate GPU pools for evald with a target headroom of 30% for burst.
5) Dry-run shadow (owner: ML Engineer)
- Run a 4-hour dry-run at 1% replication, inspect telemetry and ensure no production impacts.
6) Promote to full shadow (owner: product)
- Gradually increase replication to target; monitor fidelity deltas and capacity signals.

Regression triage fast path

If a regression is detected (fidelity_delta < threshold for critical slice):
1) Auto-throttle: Control Plane marks candidate as THROTTLED for new shadow replication.
2) Bisect: Launch a binary search over recent commits/quant profiles using the automated-regression-bisect assistant (see related page).
3) Localize slice: Use the eval-console to iterate on top-10 failing fingerprints and export 500 raw artifacts for human annotation.
4) Remediate: If regression is due to quant profile, revert to previous quant_profile for the slice or pin routing to baseline model_variant; file an incident per incident playbook.

Operational runbooks (runbook excerpt)

- Incident: Shadow-agent causing production latency increase
  1. SRE alert triggers when duplicate-path latency delta > 0.5ms sustained for 5 minutes.
  2. Run: curl -XPOST https://control-plane.internal/shadow/adjust --data '{"action":"throttle","target":"all"}'
  3. Verify production latency returns to baseline; roll back throttling only after 15 minutes of stable metrics.

Ownership and governance

- Ownership: ML Infrastructure owns Mirror Proxy + Sampler. Eval Platform team owns Eval Runner and Telemetry pipeline. Product/Applied ML owns slice definitions and acceptance criteria. SRE owns capacity and incident response.
- Review cadence: Quarterly reviews of fingerprint schema and sampling budgets. Post-release safety window: 14 days with elevated sampling on safety slices.

Privacy and retention notes

- PII redaction: The Mirroring Proxy must run the PII redaction pipeline for any customer with privacy_flag=true before storing payloads.
- Retention: Default retention is 30 days for shadow artifacts; extended retention requires customer consent and security review.

Appendices

A. Example fingerprint canonicalization pseudo-code

1. normalize = remove_dynamic_tokens(request.text)
2. redact = run_pii_redactor(normalize)
3. fingerprint = sha256(route_id + "|" + intent_class(redact) + "|" + length_bucket(redact))

B. Prioritized metric matrix (example)

- safety: false_negative_rate | threshold: < 0.01 | action: stop promotion
- semantic_fidelity: similarity_score | threshold: >= -0.02 | action: investigate if violated
- latency: p99 | threshold: increase < 0.5ms vs baseline | action: throttle shadowing

C. Frequently asked questions

Q: Will shadowing increase costs for the customer?
A: No customer-facing billing changes; internal cost is charged to platform evaluation budget. Customers can opt out per route.

Q: What if the shadow job reveals a reproducible bug?
A: Follow the regression triage fast path and open a public incident if customer-facing.

D. Related documents
- Shadow-to-prod eval continuity guidelines (link in related_pages)
- Heterogeneous hybrid quant deployment guidelines (link in related_pages)

Document change log

- 2024-07-12: Created by Aisha Romero (initial draft).
- 2025-10-18: Added differential-privacy sampling notes and capacity-aware throttling thresholds (review by Marcus Liu).
- 2025-11-02: Finalized acceptance criteria and CLI examples; published.

title: Probe Scheduling for Mixed-Precision Evaluation Orchestration
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines a probe-scheduling strategy and orchestration pattern for running mixed-precision (MPX) evaluation workloads across the eval-harness. It centralizes how probes (synthetic requests, prompt slices, and adversarial cases) should be scheduled, prioritized, and routed to candidate model/quantization variants so we can detect quality regressions and quant-degradation early without overspending GPU cycles.

Goals
-----
- Detect regressions introduced by mixed-precision and quantization changes within 24 hours of a rollout candidate being staged.
- Prioritize probes that historically surface degradations while preserving sampling diversity to catch new failure modes.
- Keep incremental compute overhead <= 12% of production-like dedicated shadow capacity.
- Provide deterministic scheduling outputs for reproducible triage and automated alerts.

Scope
-----
Applies to: eval-harness orchestration, model-onboarding shadow deployments (hosted, dedicated, private), quantization profiles used by production-serving. Excludes: offline batch-only research experiments and one-off ad hoc label collections.

Definitions
-----------
- Probe: a single test case derived from the prompt catalog (single- or multi-turn) with metadata (slice, expected behavior, anchor model output).
- MPX candidate: a model variant that uses mixed-precision kernels (e.g., int8+f16 hybrid) or a quantized artifact targeted for private/dedicated deployment.
- Probe Farm: the eval-harness pool service that schedules probes to worker lanes.
- Priority Score: numeric score used by scheduler to order probes; see algorithm below.

High-level Architecture
-----------------------
1. Probe Catalog (Prompt Sets): persisted in S3 + metadata in the eval database. Each probe has tags: slice, risk_score, cost_estimate, anchor_hash, last_seen_failure.
2. Scheduler Service (probe-scheduler): computes a daily schedule manifest for each MPX candidate.
3. Orchestrator (eval-orch): reads manifests and executes probes on the shadow fleet, collecting telemetry to ingestion topic eval-telemetry-prod.
4. Analyzer (probe-analyzer): computes signal (response stability index, semantic-embedding divergence, length-normalized token-delta) and writes alerts to PagerDuty and regression-triage queue.

Probe Types and Weighting
------------------------
We categorize probes into 4 types with default target proportions for a daily run:
- High-risk regressors (15%): known slices that have produced past regressions (high precision recall).
- Random coverage (30%): uniformly sampled to detect unknowns.
- Adversarial perturbations (20%): syntactic and semantic noise variants.
- Long-context & KV-cache sensitive (35%): multi-turn sequences emphasizing cache stability.

Priority score formula (used to sort queue):
priority = clamp(0.0, 1.0, 0.5 * normalized_risk + 0.3 * age_factor + 0.2 * impact_estimate)
Where: normalized_risk in [0,1] from probe metadata; age_factor = min(days_since_last_run/30,1); impact_estimate derived from upstream product usage weight.

Scheduling Algorithm
--------------------
1. For each MPX candidate, fetch last-run outcomes and compute a reweight table for probes.
2. Reserve N high-priority slots (N = ceil(0.12 * daily_budget_slots)) for probes with last_seen_failure = true.
3. Fill remaining slots by sampling per target proportions with stratified sampling across languages, device types, and traffic cohorts.
4. Annotate schedule with preferred lane (gpu-v2, cpu-sim, or quant-sim) and estimated token-cost.
5. Persist manifest and start execution window.

Operational Runbook: daily execution
-----------------------------------
1. probe-scheduler triggers at 02:00 UTC and emits manifests per candidate.
2. eval-orch pulls manifests and runs probes over a 2-hour window. Long-context probes are rate-limited to spread memory pressure.
3. probe-analyzer runs streaming checks and posts signals:
   - Response Stability Index (RSI) drop > 0.07 -> create regression triage ticket (severity P2).
   - Embedding Cosine Drift > 0.12 on median of slice -> add to regression queue.
   - Token Delta > 20% on top-k token distribution -> flag for quantization failure-mode.
4. If more than 5 distinct probes fail automatic gates for the same candidate, automatically set deployment status to HOLD and notify Model Onboarding channel (@model-onboard).

SLOs and Alert Thresholds
-------------------------
- Coverage: At least 80% of manifest probes must complete successfully within the 2-hour window.
- Latency: median probe execution latency <= 800ms per probe on gpu-v2 lane.
- Detection window: regressions must be detected and a ticket created within 6 hours of detection.

Gates and Automated Actions
--------------------------
- Soft Gate: RSI drop between 0.03–0.07 -> create a low-priority regression ticket; schedule follow-up re-run with expanded adversarial cases.
- Hard Gate: RSI drop > 0.07 or Embedding Drift > 0.12 -> set candidate to HOLD and notify oncall and onboarding owners.
- Emergency Fallback: If an MPX candidate is promoted to dedicated and field telemetry indicates correlated errors, the Routing Service will fallback to the anchor model for 1 hour while triage proceeds.

Promotion Checklist (for MPX candidate)
--------------------------------------
- [ ] All scheduled probes pass soft gates in two consecutive daily runs.
- [ ] No hard gate triggers in the last 7 days.
- [ ] Token-cost delta within expected budget +/- 8%.
- [ ] Shadow-to-field calibration run completed (see 'shadow-rollforward' playbook).
- [ ] Owners and validators listed in onboarding ticket have signed off.

Sample manifest excerpt (YAML)
----------------------------
---
candidate: mpq-model-v3-int8-hybrid
date: 2025-02-10
slots: 1200
reserved_high_risk: 150
probes:
  - id: probe-15033
    slice: billing-invoice-extraction
    type: long-context
    lane: gpu-v2
    expected_anchor_hash: 7f2a9d
  - id: probe-1122
    slice: frontend-dialogue-clarity
    type: adversarial
    lane: quant-sim
    expected_anchor_hash: 9c4b1a

Config table: scheduler tunables
--------------------------------
| key                         | description                                    | default  | notes |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------|----------|-------|
| daily_budget_slots          | total probe executions per candidate per day  | 1200     | scales with candidate priority |
| reserved_failure_slots_pct  | percent reserved for recent failures          | 12       | set to 0 for experimental runs |
| long_context_rate_limit_ms  | per-probe cooldown for long-context probes    | 1500     | avoid GPU memory thrash |
| sample_seed                 | deterministic seed for sampling               | 42       | increment per run for variance |

Telemetry and Metrics (collected per-probe)
--------------------------------------------
- run_id, probe_id, candidate, lane, start_ts, end_ts
- tokens_in, tokens_out, wall_ms, gpu_mem_peak_mb
- response_hash, embedding_vector_id, rsi_score, token_delta_percent
- annotations: human_label (if escalated), triage_ticket_id

Triage Flow and Responsibilities
--------------------------------
- Initial Triage: Model Onboarding -> verify whether difference is expected for quant profile.
- Deep Triage: Applied ML (Regression Squad) -> reproduce with debug flags, compare kernel traces, KV cache traces.
- Ops Action: If a resource bottleneck is suspected (gpu_mem_peak_mb > threshold 90%), engage eng-infra to reprofile.

Owner and Escalation Contacts
----------------------------
- Probe Scheduler (owner): Marco Ruiz (marco@redwood.ai)
- Probe Analyzer (owner): Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Regression Squad Lead: Priya Menon (pri@redwood.ai)
- Oncall: see eng-oncall rota (link internal)

Example CLI commands
--------------------
# Generate schedule for candidate
make run-probe-scheduler CANDIDANT=mpq-model-v3-int8-hybrid RUN_DATE=2025-02-10

# Inspect manifest
aws s3 cp s3://eval-manifests/mpq-model-v3-int8-hybrid/2025-02-10/manifest.yaml -

Appendix: common failure modes and remediation
-----------------------------------------------
1) Token distribution collapse (spike in token_delta_percent)
   - Likely cause: quant kernel top-k instability.
   - Remediation: tighten quantization calibration, run quant-sim with higher precision for top-k.
2) Embedding semantic shift
   - Likely cause: fused kernel numerical drift or tokenizer mismatch for rare unicode.
   - Remediation: run tokenizer normalization pass, add targeted probes for affected Unicode ranges.
3) Intermittent OOM on long-context probes
   - Likely cause: batch packing + long context combinatorics.
   - Remediation: reduce pack size for long-context lane and increase long_context_rate_limit_ms.

Related artifacts and references
-------------------------------
- Scheduler service repo: git@internal:redwood/eval-scheduler.git
- Probe catalog schema: s3://eval-catalog/schema/v2/probe-schema.yaml
- Regression triage template: confluence://applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/triage-ticket-template

Revision history
----------------
2025-01-15 — Dana Kim — initial draft
2025-02-12 — Dana Kim — added automated gate thresholds and sample manifest

title: Interactive streaming + function-call stability eval protocol
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines a repeatable evaluation protocol, harness components, workload recipes, and triage playbook for measuring stability and fidelity of interactive streaming responses when the model invokes function/tool calls. The protocol is specifically targeted at cross-cutting failure modes introduced by quantization, KV-cache interactions, and continuous-batching in production serving. It is intended for applied-ML engineers, runtime owners, and SREs validating model promotions and platform changes that affect streaming or function-call behavior.

Scope
-----
- Model families: decoder-only & encoder-decoder topologies used in Redwood hosted/dedicated/private serving.
- Modes: streaming token-by-token output with optional function/tool call markers, non-streaming baseline for comparison.
- Interventions: quantization changes (8/4-bit paths), KV-cache warm/cold patterns, batching policy changes, streaming buffer/window tuning.
- Excludes: offline embedding-only workloads and strictly batch, non-interactive evaluation.

Goals
-----
1) Detect and quantify stability regressions introduced by runtime changes that affect streaming partial outputs or function-call boundaries.
2) Measure end-to-end fidelity (intent and argument correctness) of function-call outputs across quantized/float variants.
3) Provide deterministic triage steps and thresholds for blocking promotions or triggering rollback.
4) Produce actionable artifacts (diffs, heatmaps, replay bundles) that developers can use to debug.

Definitions
-----------
- Partial-stream divergence: token-level Levenshtein distance between prefix streams produced by baseline and candidate at matched prefix lengths.
- Call-boundary shift: a change in the token index where the model emits the function_call start token (or structured marker). Measured as delta in tokens.
- Argument fidelity: semantic equivalence score for the structured arguments in function calls (using domain-specific equality rules).
- Streaming latency SLOs: p50/p95 of time-to-first-byte and time-between-chunks measured at the API gateway.

Metrics and thresholds
----------------------
Use these primary metrics in the evaluation dashboard and for automated gating:
- Partial-stream divergence (median per-example): acceptable < 0.08 normalized edit distance.
- Partial-stream divergence (95th percentile): acceptable < 0.20.
- Call-boundary shift: median < 3 tokens; 95th percentile < 12 tokens.
- Argument fidelity: exact-match >= 98% for deterministic argument schemas; semantic-score >= 94% for freeform args.
- Streaming latency regressions: p95 time-to-first-byte regression < 25% vs baseline; p95 inter-chunk delay < 200ms.
- Regression alert: any single high-severity sample where partial-stream divergence > 0.6 or argument fidelity < 80% must be considered a blocking failure.

Test harness architecture
------------------------
1) Controller: orchestrates experiments, schedules traffic, applies environment overrides (quant flags, cache priming).
2) Workload generator: replay-based and synthetic workload engines that can produce interleaved streaming clients and function-call stubs.
3) Proxy recorder & replayer: records wire-level chunk timing and payloads (timestamps, chunk sizes, and markers) to enable deterministic replays.
4) Analyzer: computes token-level diffs, boundary shifts, semantic scoring of structured outputs, and produces per-example artifacts.
5) Dashboard: stores metrics, example traces, heatmaps, and links to replay bundles in object storage.

Workload generation recipes
--------------------------
- Real-traffic shadow: sample 72 hours of production streaming sessions (anonymized) with a 1% sampling rate; keep conversation context lengths stratified (0-128, 128-512, 512+ tokens).
- Synthetic edge-probe set: 1,200 queries designed to exercise: long-running partial outputs, multi-step tool invocation, nested JSON output, ambiguous prompt completions, and adversarial truncation.
- Cold-cache churn: attack pattern that alternates sessions across 10,000 unique user prefixes to simulate worst-case KV cache miss rate.
- Burst streaming: simulate 500 concurrent lightweight streaming clients issuing 1–3 requests each, with varied inter-chunk arrival rates.

Experiment config template (YAML)
--------------------------------
```yaml
experiment_name: interactive-stream-fcall-canary-2026-02
baseline_model: redwood-1.0-fp16
candidate_model: redwood-1.0-8bit
workload_sets:
  - name: real_shadow
    duration: 72h
    sample_rate: 0.01
  - name: synthetic_edge_probes
    iterations: 10
interventions:
  - quant_flags: [enable_8bit_kernels]
  - kv_cache: [warm, cold, partial]
  - batching_policy: [continuous, fixed-window]
metrics_to_record: [partial_stream_divergence, call_boundary_shift, argument_fidelity, ttfb_p95, inter_chunk_p95]
analysis_outputs: [per_example_diff, top_100_regressions, heatmap_stream_divergence, replay_bundle_url]
```

Run procedure
-------------
1) Prepare baseline: pin baseline model and capture a 24-hour shadow snapshot to serve as the canonical baseline if not already available.
2) Configure candidate: deploy candidate runtime variant (quant or batching change) to an isolated staging cluster with identical routing rules.
3) Prime caches: run the "warm" phase for 1 hour to stabilize KV-cache state, then run the cold-cache phase by cycling unique prefixes.
4) Execute workload: start the controller; run real_shadow and synthetic_edge_probes concurrently for the configured duration.
5) Collect artifacts: ensure proxy recorder saves chunk timings, structured call outputs, and client-side partial streams to object storage.
6) Analysis pass: run analyzer; generate diffs and heatmaps; compute gating metrics.
7) Decide: compare metrics to thresholds and follow triage guidance below.

Result analysis and artifacts
----------------------------
- Per-example diff bundle (plain text + token-level annotations).
- Call argument table (baseline vs candidate) with semantic similarity scores.
- Heatmap: examples (rows) vs prefix-length (columns) colored by normalized edit distance.
- Timing waterfall per example showing time-to-first-byte and inter-chunk deltas.
- Replay bundle (runnable): includes recorded traffic + runtime recipe to reproduce the trace in a local staging cluster.

Regression triage playbook
-------------------------
If the experiment shows any metric violating the regression alert thresholds:
1) Reproduce the top-10 failing examples with the proxy replayer locally against both baseline and candidate; save logs.
2) Run a narrow micro-benchmark toggling only one intervention at a time (e.g., quant flag only, then cache pattern only, then batching policy only).
3) If the failure is tied to quantization: run the candidate with mixed-precision (FP16 tokens for logits accumulation) and run targeted per-layer profiling.
4) If the failure is tied to KV-cache: compare warm vs cold traces; inspect cache keys, sequence offsets, and KV eviction events.
5) If the failure is tied to streaming chunkization: instrument the runtime to capture internal chunk buffer boundaries and confirm whether function_call markers align with chunk boundaries.
6) Produce a root-cause note with: minimal repro, diffs, profiler flame snapshots, and recommended rollback or mitigation (e.g., fall back to fp16 for model X, increase chunk buffer to 64KB, or adjust batching to preserve deterministic tokenization).
7) Postmortem: tag the release and link to the CI job that introduced the change; propose permanent guardrail (see guardrail suggestions below).

Guardrail suggestions (examples)
------------------------------
- Safety gate: any candidate that increases call-boundary shift at the 95th percentile by > 5 tokens must fail automated promotion.
- Canary window: require a minimum 7-day rolling run of the streaming canary with no blocking regressions before promoting quantized runtime to dedicated clusters.
- Auto-fallback rule: when argument_fidelity < 90% for more than 1% of traffic in the canary, automatically route 10% of traffic to baseline model until triage completes.

Ownership and cadence
---------------------
- Primary owner: applied-ml infra team (OWNERS: @applied-ml-infra).
- Secondary owner: serving-runtime team for instrumentation and replay tooling.
- Run cadence: automated nightly canary runs for non-production changes; full 72-hour runs for any model candidate promotion or runtime kernel change.
- On-call: severity-2 incident for blocking regressions discovered in production within the first 72 hours after release.

Appendix: example CLI commands
-----------------------------
# Start a local replay against candidate runtime (example)
redwood-eval run --experiment interactive-stream-fcall-canary-2026-02 --target candidate --replay-bundle gs://eval-replays/bundle-20260210.tar.gz

# Compute token-level diff summary
redwood-eval analyze --input gs://eval-replays/bundle-20260210 --output gs://eval-results/interactive-canary-20260210 --metrics partial_stream_divergence,call_boundary_shift

Frequently asked questions (short)
---------------------------------
Q: Why test streaming and function calls together?
A: Function-call boundaries are often emitted mid-stream; chunkization and truncation interact with where structured markers appear, which is a source of high-severity regressions.

Q: Can this protocol be used for private deployments?
A: Yes — the harness supports private replay bundles and local staging clusters. Masking/anonymization hooks must be enabled for customer data.

Change log
----------
- 2025-11-12: Created initial draft (Aisha Park).
- 2026-01-15: Added heatmap outputs and gating thresholds (Omar Chen).
- 2026-02-10: Finalized triage steps and canary cadence; published (Lucia Morales).

title: Cost Model Validation Harness (v1) — Golden Datasets, Replay, and Acceptance Criteria
content:
## Purpose
This page defines the validation harness for the Standard Cost Model (SCM) v1. The harness is the shared mechanism to:
- Verify correctness and determinism of per-request cost projections.
- Prevent regressions as schemas/runtime telemetry evolve.
- Quantify and monitor drift between predicted cost and observed spend.
- Provide repeatable evidence for Console/Optimize adoption (and Finance alignment).

The harness is explicitly *not* a billing reconciliation system of record. It is a correctness/regression suite for the cost model spec + implementation.

## Scope
### In scope (v1)
- Golden fixtures for SCM inputs (request + deployment context + runtime/telemetry-derived primitives) and expected SCM outputs.
- Replay runner that executes the Cost Model API/service against fixtures in CI and nightly.
- Acceptance thresholds per output field and per aggregate view (prefill/decode split, cache attribution, overhead allocation).
- Integration points with:
  - Serving runtime perf suite (latency/throughput counters used as SCM inputs)
  - Drift monitoring job (predicted vs observed)

### Out of scope (v1)
- Full invoice reconciliation and RevRec.
- “Exhaustive” model catalog coverage. v1 uses a curated coverage set.
- Customer-facing quality metrics for generation output; only cost-model correctness is validated.

## Definitions
- **Fixture**: A single test case capturing SCM inputs and expected outputs (with tolerances).
- **Golden dataset**: A versioned collection of fixtures representing realistic workload slices.
- **Replay**: Running the SCM compute against fixtures using a pinned schema version and pinned pricing inputs.
- **Observed cost**: Finance-approved spend attribution for a reporting window (e.g., GPU-hours + overhead pools) transformed into comparable primitives.
- **Drift**: Relative error between predicted and observed cost for the same workload slice and window.

## Harness architecture (conceptual)
1) *Fixture builder* produces SCM input payloads from:
   - Sanitized telemetry extracts (token accounting, cache stats, batching stats)
   - Model catalog metadata (model id, quant profile id)
   - Deployment context (hosted/dedicated/private; region; hardware SKU)
2) *Replay runner* calls Cost Model API (preferred) or library entrypoint (fallback) with:
   - schema_version = pinned (e.g., "cost-model/v1")
   - pricing_snapshot_id = pinned (e.g., "2026-02-01")
3) *Comparator* checks outputs against expected values with field-level tolerances.
4) *Reporter* emits:
   - CI pass/fail signal with diffs
   - trend metrics for nightly runs
   - coverage report by scenario

## Golden datasets
Golden datasets are designed to cover the most common and most error-prone dimensions.

### Dataset catalog (v1)
The following datasets must exist for v1 launch.

| Dataset ID | Primary purpose | Size target | Update cadence | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| golden-hosted-chat-baseline | Basic hosted chat requests, no cache | 200 fixtures | Quarterly + on major schema changes | Telemetry & Analytics |
| golden-hosted-streaming | Streaming + partial completions + retries | 100 fixtures | Quarterly | Platform Control Plane |
| golden-dedicated-batch | Batch efficiency + queueing attribution | 150 fixtures | Quarterly | Runtime Scheduling |
| golden-kv-cache-scenarios | Prefix/KV cache hit/miss attribution | 150 fixtures | Monthly until stable | Runtime Scheduling |
| golden-quant-profiles | Quant profile deltas & constraints | 120 fixtures | On new quant profiles | Applied ML |
| golden-overhead-allocation | Overhead allocation behavior per policy | 60 fixtures | On Finance policy update | FP&A |
| golden-cardinality-bounds | Stress tests for bounding/pagination behavior | 40 fixtures | Quarterly | Platform Control Plane |

### Fixture scenario dimensions
Each dataset should intentionally cover:
- Deployment mode: hosted / dedicated / private
- Region: at least 2 regions with different SKU/pricing (e.g., us-east, eu-west)
- Hardware SKU: at least 2 GPU SKUs per deployment mode used in production
- Request shape: prompt length distribution, max_tokens, stop/early_stop
- Cache: kv_cache_hit_rate buckets (0%, ~50%, ~90%), cache warm/cold
- Batching: batch_size buckets (1, 4, 16+) and batch efficiency variations
- Quantization: fp16/bf16 baseline + at least one quant profile id

### Data hygiene and privacy
- Fixtures must not include customer prompts or PII.
- Prompts in fixtures must be synthetic or templated (e.g., "Summarize the following: <DOC_001>").
- Any real telemetry used to derive distributions must be aggregated/sanitized before fixture construction.

## Replay methodology
### Execution modes
- **CI (PR gating)**:
  - Runs a small, fast subset: ~50–100 fixtures total across key datasets.
  - Enforces determinism and strict correctness checks.
  - Runtime budget: 3 minutes wall-clock.
- **Nightly (extended)**:
  - Runs full datasets.
  - Computes drift metrics and trendlines; posts summary to #eng-platform.
  - Runtime budget: 30–45 minutes.

### Pinning and reproducibility
To make comparisons stable, the runner must pin:
- schema_version (e.g., "cost-model/v1")
- pricing_snapshot_id (e.g., "2026-02-01")
- model_catalog_snapshot (e.g., "catalog-2026-02-10")
- runtime-metrics-contract version (for derived fields)

Any change to a pinned artifact requires an explicit update PR to the harness with:
- rationale
- expected diff summary
- reviewer sign-off from owning team

### Calling surface
Preferred: validate via Cost Model API endpoints used by Console/Optimize (to catch serialization/auth/bounds behavior). Fallback: library compute for unit-level invariants.

The harness supports two call patterns:
1) Per-request estimate endpoint (single fixture → estimate)
2) Aggregated breakdown endpoint (workload summary → breakdown)
3) What-if endpoint (baseline + scenario change → projected delta)

## Acceptance criteria
Acceptance thresholds are designed to:
- Be tight where determinism is expected (pure arithmetic on pinned inputs).
- Be tolerant where empirical models/heuristics exist (batch efficiency, cache warm-rate, uncertainty intervals).

### Field-level tolerances (v1)
| Output field class | Examples | Tolerance | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Exact deterministic scalars | token counts, stage attribution totals | 0 (exact match) | Must match exactly with pinned contracts |
| Monetary totals (per-request) | total_cost_usd | ±0.5% or ±$0.0001 (whichever larger) | Accounts for rounding; should normally be tighter |
| Breakdown components | prefill_cost, decode_cost, cache_savings | ±1.0% of component | Component drift must not cancel out to hide errors |
| Overhead allocation | overhead_allocated_usd | Policy-dependent; ±2.0% | Must follow Finance policy doc; review on policy change |
| What-if deltas | delta_total_cost_usd | ±3.0% | Wider due to modeled effects; must also satisfy directionality checks |
| Confidence/uncertainty | ci_low/ci_high | Interval must contain observed value ≥ 90% in nightly backtests | Evaluated on dataset-level, not per fixture |

### Invariant checks (must always pass)
- Non-negativity: all costs >= 0.
- Conservation: total_cost ≈ sum(breakdown components) within rounding tolerance.
- Stage consistency: prefill_tokens + decode_tokens = total_billed_tokens (for schemas that require it).
- Cache accounting: cache_savings cannot exceed baseline prefill+decode cost for identical request.
- Bounded outputs: responses must not exceed documented max list lengths / bucket counts.

### Drift acceptance (nightly/backtest)
Drift is evaluated at the dataset aggregate level (not per-request):
- P50 absolute percentage error (APE) <= 5%
- P95 APE <= 12%
- No single dataset aggregate APE > 15% for 2 consecutive nights

When drift breaches thresholds, the harness must:
- open an issue tagged "cost-model-drift"
- attach the dataset aggregate diff and top contributing scenarios (by cost)

## How perf/eval suites validate SCM projections
### Runtime perf suite integration
The serving runtime perf suite provides the authoritative source for:
- prefill vs decode token attribution
- batch efficiency metrics and queue time counters
- kv cache hit/miss counters
- quantization execution path identifiers

Validation approach:
1) On a fixed set of perf workloads (prompt/response sizes), record runtime metrics.
2) Convert metrics into SCM inputs using the published runtime metrics contract.
3) Ensure SCM output breakdown behaves monotonically with respect to:
   - Increasing batch efficiency should not increase per-token compute cost (holding other vars constant).
   - Increasing kv-cache hit rate should not increase prefill compute cost.
   - Quant profile switching should reflect expected throughput/memory deltas per catalog metadata.

### Optimize “what-if” regression checks
For each supported what-if knob (v1):
- batching policy change
- caching enablement
- quantization profile swap

The harness includes paired fixtures:
- baseline payload
- what-if payload

Required checks:
- Directionality: if a what-if claims cost savings, delta_total_cost_usd must be <= 0.
- Guardrails: projected savings must be bounded by physically plausible limits (e.g., cannot exceed removing all decode compute).
- Confidence sanity: intervals should widen when input uncertainty increases (e.g., unknown warm-rate).

## Tooling and implementation plan
### Repo layout (proposed)
- /cost_model/validation_harness/
  - datasets/
  - fixtures/
  - runner/
  - comparator/
  - reports/

### CLI runner (proposed)
Commands:
- cost-model-validate run --dataset golden-hosted-chat-baseline --env staging
- cost-model-validate run --dataset ci-smoke --env local --use-library
- cost-model-validate report --last-nightly

### CI integration
- PRs touching any of:
  - schema package
  - cost-model service compute
  - telemetry input contracts
  - pricing snapshot logic
  - model catalog quant metadata

…must trigger the CI subset validation.

### Updating goldens
Golden updates must be explicit and reviewed.
Process:
1) Run runner with --update-goldens in a dedicated branch.
2) Generate diff summary (top 20 fixtures by cost change, and reason tags).
3) Obtain approvals:
   - Owning team for affected dataset
   - Finance reviewer if overhead allocation outputs change
4) Merge with a changelog entry referencing the PR/ADR.

## Failure triage playbook (quick reference)
When CI fails:
1) Determine failure type:
   - Schema mismatch/serialization
   - Determinism (non-reproducible output)
   - Numeric regression (cost changed)
   - Bounds/pagination violation
2) Identify affected datasets and scenario dimensions.
3) If regression is expected:
   - update goldens with justification and reviewer approvals
4) If unexpected:
   - bisect by recent changes to telemetry contracts, pricing snapshot, or model catalog
   - validate on staging with same pinned artifacts

## Open questions (tracked for v1 closeout)
- Final tolerance for overhead allocation under partial telemetry (telemetry lag scenarios).
- Whether to require strict matching for quantization deltas per profile, or allow empirical calibration to override catalog metadata.
- How to represent cache warm-rate assumptions in fixtures without reintroducing high-cardinality inputs.

## Owners and contacts
- Harness owner: Leila Farouk (E2E/automation QA)
- Drift/backtesting: Mei Lin (Analytics pipelines), Logan Wright (Telemetry)
- What-if methodology: Jonas Weber (Applied ML)
- Runtime metrics contract: Sofia Ivanova, Omar El-Sayed
- Service/API issues: Ethan Park

## Appendix A: Example fixture (human-readable)
Each fixture records a minimal SCM input payload, plus expected outputs and tolerances. The canonical serialized form lives alongside the dataset.

Example (conceptual):
- Input: hosted, us-east, sku=H100-80GB, model=rw-llama-70b, quant=bf16
- Request: prompt_tokens=1200, decode_tokens=250, streaming=true
- Runtime: avg_batch_size=8, batch_efficiency=0.72, kv_cache_hit_rate=0.55
- Expected:
  - total_cost_usd=… (±0.5%)
  - breakdown: prefill/decode/cache_savings/overhead (component tolerances)

Appendix B: Change log
- 2026-02-22: Added drift thresholds and what-if directionality checks; aligned overhead tolerance to latest Finance guidance.
- 2026-02-10: Expanded dataset catalog to include cardinality bounds and streaming scenarios.
- 2026-01-23: Initial draft.

title: Tenant-aware Probe Fabricator and Isolation Eval Playbook
content:
Summary

Purpose: This playbook describes a reproducible process for fabricating tenant-aware synthetic probes and running isolation-focused evaluations in Dedicated and Private deployments. It is intended for evaluation engineers, SREs, and model-onboarding owners who must ensure tenant isolation, fairness across tenant workloads, and robust regression detection in multitenant serving environments.

Why this exists
- Mixed-tenant production traffic can hide regressions that only trigger when specific prompt structures interact with cache and batching policies.
- Standard global probe sets miss tenant-specific patterns (naming conventions, domain-specific tokens, code fragments, or legal clauses).
- We need a standard way to: generate tenantlike probes, run isolation/pollination experiments, and triage cross-tenant leakage or degradation.

Scope and non-goals
- Scope: Dedicated and Private deployments; evaluation harness integration; tethering to telemetry and canary systems.
- Non-goals: This is not a replacement for customer-provided test suites or legal discovery procedures. Not intended for adversarial red-team escalation without security sign-off.

When to use
1) Onboarding a new tenant into Dedicated or Private (run isolation baseline).
2) After model version rollout that changes caching, KV handling, or quantization profile.
3) When telemetry highlights tenant-specific delta in fidelity or latency.
4) Before offering aggregated shared caches to multiple tenants.

Roles and ownership
- Probe Owner: applied-ml (primary) — responsible for probe design and validation.
- Eval Runner: infra/eval-harness — execute experiments and collect telemetry.
- SRE/Platform: eng-sre — configure isolation controls and provide access to per-tenant traces.
- Onboarding Product Owner: product — signs off on acceptance criteria.

High-level workflow
1) Gather tenant signal: sample spike tokens, prompt templates, and typical sequence lengths from telemetry (7 days).
2) Synthesize probes: produce a catalog of 3 probe families per tenant (Structural, Semantics, Edge) using templates below.
3) Isolation experiment: run experiments in three modes — isolated (only tenant traffic), co-located (tenant + noise from other tenants), and pollination (with intentionally crafted contaminant probes).
4) Measure and compare: fidelity deltas, latency percentiles, KV-cache hit rate, and top-n reranking stability.
5) Triage and remediate: follow regression triage rubric (see Runbook section).

Probe family definitions and templates
- Structural probes: exercise tokenization and sequence boundaries (IDs, markup, code fences). Example template: "<TENANT_ID> || config:

function foo() { /* {{LARGE_IDENTIFIER}} */ }"
- Semantic probes: domain-specific phrasing and slot values (legal clauses, medical terms, product names). Example: "When billing for {{SERVICE_NAME}} on account {{TENANT_ACCOUNT}}, list the exact refund policy."
- Edge probes: adversarial-like inputs (truncated JSON, nested function calls, ambiguous references) intended to expose KV-cache or quantization sensitivity.

Probe generation procedure (numbered)
1. Collect sample corpus: run telemetry export script (example):
   $ python tools/telemetry/export_tenant_corpus.py --tenant-id=TENANT_123 --days=7 --out=tenant123-corpus.json
2. Extract skeletons: apply the skeleton extractor to derive 50 canonical prompt shapes.
3. Instantiate probes: for each skeleton, generate 200 variations by sampling slot values from tenant lexicons, anonymized customer tokens, and synthetic noise.
4. Label probes: tag each probe with metadata: family, seed, expected-fuzzy-output (anchor), token-length, and priority. Use CSV column format: probe_id, family, priority, expected_anchor_hash.
5. Sanitize PII: run the scrubbing pipeline and assert zero matches against PII regex set.

Minimum probe catalog config (ascii table)
| field               | example                     | notes                       |
|---------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------|
| catalog_name        | tenant123-isolation-v1      | semantic versioning         |
| probes_total        | 600                         | 3 families * 200 each       |
| high_priority_count | 60                          | top 10% for regression fast-path |
| scrub_policy        | strict                      | must remove PII             |
| retention_days      | 90                          | local eval artifacts        |

Integration with eval-harness
- Use the harness job type: tenant-isolation. Key runner config (YAML example):

job_type: tenant-isolation
team: applied-ml
run_modes: [isolated, co-located, pollination]
batch_size: dynamic
max_tokens: 4096
telemetry_capture: [latency, tokens, kv_hits, model_scores]

- Priority: run high-priority probes first in smoke phase (15m).
- Determinism: seed RNG and store seed per-run for reproducibility.

Metrics and SLOs (what to track)
- Fidelity delta (anchor-based similarity) — alert if median fidelity drops > 3% relative to isolated baseline.
- Latency: P95 increase > 20% triggers investigation.
- KV-cache hit-rate: drop > 10% relative to baseline is a concern.
- Token-cost delta: > 5% increase requires cost review.
- Cross-tenant leakage indicator: any probe returning content with top-5 tokens originating from other tenant namespace (heuristic) => immediate triage.

Runbook: triage steps for a failing probe suite (numbered)
1) Confirm failure: rerun only the failing probes in isolated mode with same seeds.
2) Capture full trace: collect model logs, KV-tagged traces, batching windows, and GPU allocation snapshot.
3) Classify failure: is it latency, fidelity, or cross-tenant leakage? Use decision tree: 
   - Latency only -> inspect batching and autoscaler logs.
   - Fidelity only -> check quant profile, tokenization diffs, and prompt rewrite logs.
   - Leakage -> check cache eviction and shared-cache config.
4) Quick rollback: if regression is linked to a model variant or quant-profile change, activate fallback to previous variant per rollback playbook.
5) Postmortem and mitigation: document root cause, add probe to regression-suite, and produce a follow-up eval for the remediation.

Escalation matrix
- Severity P1 (production outages, high leakage): Eng-sre oncall -> applied-ml lead -> product oncall.
- Severity P2 (sustained fidelity drop > 5% for a tenant): applied-ml -> model-onboarding -> product.

Security and privacy controls
- All tenant corpora must be anonymized using the internal scrubbing tool before probe generation.
- Probes must not contain verbatim customer PII. Automated checks run during probe ingest.
- Access to per-tenant traces gated by RBAC group: sandbox-eval-access.

Example artifact: probe CSV line (single-line example)
probe_000123,semantic,high,sha256:ab12cd...,345,expected_anchor:Q3JvYyBvZmYK

Acceptance criteria for onboarding
- Baseline (isolated) fidelity >= global baseline - 1%.
- No cross-tenant leakage detected across 3 consecutive runs.
- P95 latency within tenant SLA (configured per-tenant).
- Probe suite reproducibility: identical seeds produce deterministic anchor hashes.

Operational notes and tips
- Use lightweight priming to reduce cost when generating many probe variants (limit context to 512 tokens where possible).
- For large tenants, shard catalogs by domain to keep per-run time bounded.
- Store high-priority probes in the eval-harness hot cache for faster smoke runs.

Appendix: common failure signatures and suggested mitigations
- Failure: sudden drop in anchor similarity with no latency change.
  Mitigation: inspect tokenization layer and recent tokenizer updates; run token-diff utility.
- Failure: fidelity drop only under co-located mode.
  Mitigation: test KV-miss patterns and consider stronger tenant eviction policies or per-tenant cache namespaces.
- Failure: P95 latency spikes when pollination probes are present.
  Mitigation: verify batching policy and consider lowering batch latency SLO for noisy tenants.

Related artifacts and links
- eval-harness: tenant-isolation job spec (internal link)
- KV-cache behavior playbook (see related-pages)
- Onboarding checklist for Dedicated (linked from product-docs)

Contact and ownership
- Document owner: Renee Ortiz (applied-ml)
- Primary runbook maintainers: Marcus Li (infra/eval-harness), Aisha Kumar (eng-sre)

Revision history
- 2025-09-15: initial draft
- 2026-02-10: added pollination mode and acceptance thresholds

title: functioncall-eval-contracts-and-onboarding-checklist-2026
content:
Summary:
This guide defines a standard evaluation contract and an onboarding checklist for models that use function/tool-calling interfaces (a.k.a. functioncall or toolcall). It covers: what to measure, how to construct prompt and probe sets, quantization considerations, quality gate thresholds, and a regression triage fast-path for function-calling failure modes. Use this doc to certify a model (hosted, dedicated, or private) for production traffic that exercises the tool-calling surface.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: applied ML engineers, model infra owners, SREs, platform QA, and product engineers integrating tools.
- Scope: text-only and multimodal models that expose structured function output or tool invocation APIs. Not for purely embedding-only endpoints.

Why this matters:
Function-calling expands app capabilities but creates deterministic integration contracts (JSON schema, sequence-of-calls semantics, and failure/retry behaviors). Failures manifest as malformed JSON, wrong tool selection, missing params, or silent no-op calls — which have higher user-impact than standard free-text regressions. We need a reproducible, automated way to validate these behaviors across model variants, quantized artifacts, and rollout channels.

Evaluation contract (machine-readable):
Every model onboarding request must supply an eval contract json that declares the following fields. This schema is the minimum expected artifact attached to a model card.

Example eval_contract.json:
```
{
  "model_id": "redwood-llamax-13b-v3",
  "interface": "functioncalling-v1",
  "schemas": [
    {"name": "search_file", "json_schema": "{\\\"type\\\":\\\"object\\\",...}", "required_samples": 200},
    {"name": "summarize_page", "json_schema": "{\\\"type\\\":\\\"object\\\",...}", "required_samples": 150}
  ],
  "quant_profiles_tested": ["fp16","int8-ggml"],
  "primary_prompt_set": "/datasets/functioncall/checkout-2026-v1",
  "slo_targets": {"parse_rate": 0.995, "correct_tool_selection": 0.98, "latency_ms_p95": 800}
}
```

Key contract fields (human-readable):
- model_id: canonical model reference used in runtime routing.
- interface: cataloged interface type (functioncalling-v1, functioncalling-v2, toolchain-v1).
- schemas: list of named function/tool schemas with their canonical JSON Schema and minimum sample count for evaluation.
- quant_profiles_tested: quantization artifacts that must be validated (list).
- primary_prompt_set: pointer to the canonical probe/prompt dataset.
- slo_targets: minimal quality/latency thresholds to pass the gate.

Prompt & probe design principles:
1) Intent diversity: For each declared schema, include probes that exercise intent synonyms, misspellings, nested requests, and numeric edge cases.
2) Structural fuzzing: Include syntactic noise that commonly breaks parsers: mismatched punctuation, truncated sentences, and nested JSON in text blocks.
3) Multi-step sequences: For function chains (tool A -> tool B), model must demonstrate correct ordering under simulated session state.
4) Latency-sensitive probes: Tiny-context and long-context variants — measure p50/p95/p99 for both token-generation and post-processing (parse time).
5) Quantization sensitivity: For each probe, run on floating-point baseline and at least two quantized variants to capture divergent behavior.

Sample prompt matrix (short table represented as text):
- schema: search_file | probes: 200 | categories: exact-match, fuzzy-query, truncated-path, escaped-characters
- schema: summarize_page | probes: 150 | categories: long-context, single-sentence, list-based, nested-bullets

Automated checks (must pass to promote to canary):
- Parse success rate (parse_rate): fraction of probes returning syntactically valid JSON matching schema. Target >= slo_targets.parse_rate.
- Tool selection accuracy (correct_tool_selection): fraction of probes that select the expected function/tool. Target >= slo_targets.correct_tool_selection.
- Semantic correctness (semantic_score): automated heuristics + small human annotation sample. Thresholds depend on product (default >= 0.85 for conversational tool workflows).
- Latency SLOs: token-generate + parse <= slo_targets.latency_ms_p95.
- Determinism budget: For deterministic routes, p95 token divergence <= 1.2x baseline variance.

Quality guardrails and blocking failures:
- Blocker: Returning top-level free-text when schema required (e.g., response is plain text instead of JSON) — immediate rollback for canaries.
- Blocker: Incorrect tool invoked when expected tool has security implications (delete/write operations).
- High-severity: Missing required keys in returned JSON across >2% of probes.
- Medium-severity: Parsable but semantically incorrect params (e.g., wrong file id).

Quantization & artifact considerations:
- All quantized artifacts used in production must be part of the eval_contract.quant_profiles_tested list.
- Run the quantized-replay orchestrator (see /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/quantized-artifact-eval-gate-and-rollout-2026) with the same seed and prompt ordering to detect brittle tokenization-induced parse fractures.
- If parse_rate drops by >1% between fp16 and int8 on any schema, trigger conservative rollout (no auto-promote).

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step):
1) Prepare artifacts: model binary, tokenizer config, eval_contract.json, primary_prompt_set (as JSONL), and a human annotation plan.
2) Local smoke: run 100 probe smoke harness with both baseline and quantized artifacts.
   CLI: ```./tools/run_probe_harness --model ./bin/model.pt --prompts prompts.jsonl --out results.jsonl --mode smoke```
3) Full eval: schedule an isolated canary evaluation job on the eval-cluster with the contract. Tag run with model_id and git sha.
4) Review metrics: parse_rate, correct_tool_selection, semantic_score, latency percentiles. Attach the annotated sample.
5) Human validation: sample 200 probes for each schema with a 3-rater majority label for correctness.
6) Security review: for tool calls that touch data stores or external systems, run threat checklist and confirm RBAC/KMS integration.
7) Sign-off: model owner and platform QA MUST approve. Update model registry with signed eval_contract.json.

Canary rollout policy (recommended):
- Canary phase 1 (internal-only): 0.5% of traffic, 24 hours, realtime monitoring for parse_rate and key SLOs.
- Canary phase 2 (gradual escalation): 2.5% traffic, 48 hours with auto-rollback if parse_rate drops by >0.5% or lat_p95 increases by >25%.
- Promote to baseline after 7 days of stable metrics and negative regression on regression-scan.

Regression triage fast-path (if canary or prod shows functioncall failures):
1) Capture failing traces: include request_id, prompt snapshot, tokenizer state, model_variant, quant_profile, and runtime route.
2) Reproduce in isolation: replay using quantized-replay-orchestrator.
3) Bisect by artifact: switch between model versions, tokenizers, and quant artifacts to isolate change.
4) If parse errors only in quantized artifact, tag as QUANT_FAILURE and escalate to infra-quant team.
5) For semantic failures (wrong-tool), run probe-slice amplification to find minimal prompt that flips selection and open a regression issue.
6) Rollback criteria: sustained parse_rate drop >1% over 1 hour OR single catastrophic security-invoking miscall.

Telemetry and dashboards (what to instrument):
- parse_rate (rolling 5m / 1h), correct_tool_selection, semantic_score (approx), p50/p95/p99 latency, error classes (malformed, missing-key, wrong-tool).
- Annotated-sample drift signal: fraction of human labels disagreeing with automated heuristics.
- Quant-profile comparison chart: delta(parse_rate fp16, int8) by schema.

Ownership and escalation matrix:
- Model Owner: primary contact for onboarding, responsible for eval_contract and fixes.
- Eval Platform: owns harness infra and gating automation.
- Quant Team: owns quant artifacts and kernel selection.
- Security: owns high-severity tool-call gating.
- Oncall escalation order: Model Owner -> Eval Platform -> Quant Team -> Security (if data/store impact).

Operational recipes (quick commands):
- Run full contract locally: ```python infra/eval_runner.py --contract eval_contract.json --out results/$(date +%F)-full.json```
- Extract failing slice: ```jq -r '.probes[] | select(.status=="failed")' results.jsonl > failing_slice.jsonl```
- Compare quant artifacts: ```./tools/compare_quant --baseline fp16.bin --compare int8.bin --prompts prompts.jsonl```

Appendix A — Example failure report template (use for triage issues):
- title: [Regression][functioncall] search_file parse-rate drop on canary
- summary: brief description with model_id and canary window
- impact: delta parse_rate, affected routes, user-visible impact
- reproduction: exact commands + env + seed
- artifacts: model binary sha, tokenizer sha, quant profile id
- initial hypothesis: e.g., tokenization drift after new tokenizer mapping
- proposed mitigation: rollback, narrow-canary, or patch

Appendix B — Suggested prompt set naming and storage conventions:
- /datasets/functioncall/{team}-{intentset}-v{YYYYMM} e.g. /datasets/functioncall/search-team-checkout-v202601
- Include companion metadata.json with fields: created_by, sample_counts, schema_coverage, seed, source_revision

Appendix C — References and related playbooks:
- evaluator-interchange-format-and-federation-spec-2026 (interop format for evaluators)
- quantized-artifact-eval-gate-and-rollout-2026 (quant gate and safety thresholds)
- eval-oncall-runbook-for-model-regression-debugging-2026 (oncall playbook)

Revision history:
- 2025-09-15: initial draft by Aisha Patel
- 2025-11-02: added quantization gating rules (review by Diego Morales)
- 2026-02-01: finalized canary thresholds and triage fast-path (review by Priya Krishnan)

title: Multi-Granularity Response Correction Orchestrator
content:
Overview:

This document describes the Multi-Granularity Response Correction Orchestrator (MG-RCO): an automated system and operational runbook for detecting, synthesizing, validating, and rolling out corrections to model outputs at different granularities (token, turn, and conversation/session). MG-RCO is designed to integrate with the eval harness, prompt catalog, model onboarding flows, quantization profiles, and regression triage processes so fixes are safe, measurable, and reversible.

Why we built MG-RCO:
- Persistent long-tail quality issues require targeted repairs at different levels (e.g., tokenization errors vs. conversational context drift).
- Manual patching is slow and risky; a reproducible orchestrator enables faster mean-time-to-fix while preserving production SLOs.
- Corrections must be validated across quantized variants and shadow fleets to avoid regressions introduced by performance optimizations.

Scope and definitions:
1) Granularity levels:
   - Token-level: fixes that alter prompt encoding, tokenization, or scoring of a small lexical pattern (e.g., punctuation handling, Unicode normalization).
   - Turn-level: fixes that affect a single exchange (prompt + immediate response) such as hallucination suppression or instruction tightening.
   - Session-level: multi-turn stateful repairs (context window trimming, memory anchors, persona resets).

2) Correction types:
   - Prompt rewrite: automated or templated prompt modifications applied at request-time.
   - Post-filter/heuristic: deterministic filters that modify or suppress outputs (e.g., remove PII patterns).
   - Model artifact patch: small model re-ranking weights or delta weights applied in runtime (rare, requires rigorous rollout).
   - Eval-driven synthetic label: generated training/eval examples used for model fine-tuning or on-the-fly re-ranking.

Design principles:
- Minimal blast radius: prefer prompt rewrites and post-filters before considering model artifact patching.
- Evaluability: every correction must be covered by an automated eval suite (unit-level + slice-level + mixed-SLO shadowing).
- Quant-compatibility: corrections must be probed against quantization profiles and KV-cache behaviors.
- Observability: clear telemetry for candidate impact, rollback triggers, and SLOs.

System architecture (textual diagram):
- Detection layer: anomaly detectors, probe triggers, and incident inputs (Sentry alerts, eval regressions, customer tickets).
- Orchestrator core: stores correction recipes, coordinates patch generation, runs validation workflows, and coordinates rollouts.
- Evaluator adapters: run correction-aware eval harness jobs (shadow, canary, full-fidelity replay).
- Synthesis engine: template-based rewrite generator + small LLM-based rewriter used with caution (sandboxed).
- Safety & guardrails: static checks, cost budget checks, quant-compatibility checks, and approval gates.

Key integrations:
- Eval harness: MG-RCO registers a validation job type 'correction-validation' that runs the candidate against the canonical probe set plus a targeted slice.
- Prompt catalog: correction recipes are linked to prompt-set IDs; canonicalized templates are versioned in the prompt registry.
- Model onboarding: when a correction requires model artifact changes, MG-RCO triggers a model-onboarding check including preflight probes and shadow promotions.
- Quantization profiles: MG-RCO runs candidate corrections across the active quant profiles for the target model (e.g., int8, q4_0) and fails candidates that show coherence or hallucination regressions beyond thresholds.
- Regression triage: every correction generates a traceable incident ticket containing hypothesis, test matrix, and blame candidates for regression investigators.

Operational runbook: detection to production (numbered steps)
1) Detection & intake:
   - Trigger sources: automated regression alert, probe-sentinel, SLO breach, customer-reported case.
   - Create MG-RCO intake with: input example(s), TLDR of failure class, target service/model, urgency level.
2) Preliminary triage (human-in-loop):
   - Triage engineer assigns granularity and correction preference (prompt rewrite, filter, model patch).
   - If evidence points to quant or KV-cache interaction, mark "quant-sensitive" and notify runtime team.
3) Candidate generation:
   - For prompt rewrites: run template synthesizer + 3 LLM-variant rewrites (sandboxed) and canonicalize.
   - For filters: author a deterministic rule with unit tests.
   - For model patches: create a small re-ranking delta and schedule offline evaluation (requires cross-team pre-approval).
4) Automated validation:
   - Launch correction-validation job in eval harness with matrix: 
     * Baseline model (prod variant) + candidate correction (shadow)
     * Quantized variants (all active quant profiles)
     * Long-context session replay (if session-level)
     * Adversarial prompt suite for the affected slice
   - Pass criteria: no regression on anchor slices, >X% improvement on failure slice, latency increase < 5% absolute, token cost delta within configured budget.
5) Human review and safety gates:
   - Reviewer checklist includes: privacy scan, hallucination regression check, prompt-rewrite bias scan, and cost impact.
   - If any gate fails, mark candidate as 'rework' and loop back to step 3.
6) Canary rollout:
   - Deploy correction as a shadow for 10% of requests (not visible to end-users) and run live evaluators for 48 hours.
   - Monitor MG-RCO dashboard metrics (see Metrics section) and run a scheduled rollback test at 24 hours.
7) Gradual promotion:
   - If canary passes gates (no service-impacting regressions, stable latency/cost), promote to 1%, 5%, 25%, 100% over daily steps with quorum checks at each stage.
8) Post-promotion validation and closure:
   - Run post-promotion audit: tranche sample of live requests replayed through eval harness and recorded.
   - Close the intake with a postmortem if the correction involved model artifact changes.

Acceptance criteria and SLOs for corrections:
- Functional: the failure-slice pass rate increases by at least the configured uplift (default 20% relative).
- Non-functional: 99th-pctl latency increase <= 5% absolute and 95th-pctl latency increase <= 3% absolute.
- Cost: token-cost delta <= 10% for heavy-use endpoints unless compensated by a business case.
- Safety: zero new high-severity safety findings on eval sentinel suite.

Sample correction spec (JSON used by orchestrator, example):
{
  "id": "corr-2026-0892",
  "target_model": "redwood-chat-v2.1",
  "granularity": "turn",
  "type": "prompt_rewrite",
  "recipe_version": "v1",
  "validation_matrix": ["baseline", "q4_0", "int8"],
  "pass_thresholds": {"slice_uplift_pct": "20", "max_latency_p95_pct": "3"},
  "owner": "priya.nair@redwood.com"
}

(Orchestrator fields are stored in the correction registry; the example above is textual only.)

Validation matrix example (table as text):
| Axis | Baseline | Shadow+Correction | Quantized int8 | Long-context replay | Adversarial slice |
|------|----------|-------------------|----------------|---------------------|-------------------|
|Metric: failure-slice accuracy| 0.42 | 0.66 | 0.63 | 0.61 | 0.55|
|Pass?| No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Partial|

Telemetries and dashboards to monitor:
- Correction-intake rate and median time-to-first-triage.
- Correction validation pass/fail counts per model and per quant-profile.
- Canary impact charts: slice uplift, overall quality delta, latency, token-cost.
- Regression triage link: each correction creates a triage artifact with provenance (eval jobs, seed probe IDs).
- Audit trail: who approved, reviewer notes, artifact versions (prompt template id, model id, quant profile id).

Automated rollback rules (examples):
- If production error rate for affected route increases by > 5% RELATIVE within a 30-minute window, auto-rollback.
- If failure-slice regression reaches > 10% relative compared to baseline at canary stage, auto-rollback.
- If cost per 1k tokens rises above the configured cost budget for the route, rollback and notify finance-runbook.

Troubleshooting checklist (common failure modes):
- Candidate passes offline but fails in-shadow: check for telemetry mismatch (tokenization differences, header prompts), verify request canonicalization.
- Quant regressions: run quant-shadow replay harness, inspect KV cache alignment and attention kernel fallbacks.
- Drift reappearance after promotion: schedule probe refresh; consider session-level anchors rather than brittle rewrites.

Governance and change control:
- Low-risk corrections (prompt rewrites + filters) are auto-approvable with two reviewers.
- Medium-risk (synthetic label changes, LLM-generated rewrites) require cross-team approval from Applied ML and Safety.
- High-risk (model artifact deltas) must go through full model-onboarding acceptance, SRE performance sign-off, and security review.

How MG-RCO complements existing playbooks:
- Eval harness: runs the canonical correction-validation jobs and contributes new job types and example seeds.
- Prompt sets: canonical prompt templates are versioned and mapped to correction recipes to preserve provenance.
- Model onboarding: when a patch crosses into model artifacts, MG-RCO invokes the onboarding acceptance matrix (preflight probes, shadow promotion).
- Quantization profiles: MG-RCO requires per-profile passes and stores results in the correction artifact.
- Regression triage: every failed candidate generates a triage artifact that is consumable by the regression huntbook team.

Ownership and contacts:
- Runbook owner: Priya Nair (Applied ML)
- Runtime / Quant contact: Jonah Baker (Serving Runtime)
- Evaluator and probe infra: Alex Chen (Eval Infrastructure)
- Emergency rollback pager: eng-sre oncall (see internal pager rota link)

Appendix A — Example CLI commands:
- Create intake: redwood-mgro intake create --title "Chat hallucination on payments" --examples-file ./examples.json --urgency P2
- Run quick validation: redwood-mgro validate --id corr-2026-0892 --matrix baseline,q4_0 --timeout 2h
- Promote to canary: redwood-mgro promote --id corr-2026-0892 --stage canary --percent 10

Appendix B — Quick decision heuristics table (text):
- If failure pattern is syntactic and deterministic -> prefer filter.
- If failure pattern requires context rewriting but is stable -> prefer prompt rewrite.
- If failure pattern is model-internal (semantic hallucination not fixed by prompt) -> model artifact path (requires onboarding).

Related pages and artifacts:
- Link to canonical prompt registry: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/prompt-registry-index (internal)
