- Provide a stable API endpoint for the triage dashboard to stream new manifest entries (schema URL: /internal/eval-manifest/v1).

Operational playbook: from failure detection to remediation
1) Detection: auto-heuristics mark candidate failures and assign confidence.
2) Prioritization: failures are ranked by severity x user-impact metric (e.g., active sessions affected).
3) Human review: annotators label top N for the day where N is set by SRE/product trust thresholds.
4) Root-cause analysis: triage uses model_version diffs, quant profiles, and workload fingerprints to hypothesize cause.
5) Remediation: roll forward/rollback, quant profile adjustments, prompt-template patches, or retraining tasks.
6) Postmortem: document actions, mitigation latency, and regression test additions.

Sample labeling example (annotator checklist)
- Prompt id: pf_2026_00021
- Raw prompt (redacted): "List the founding year of OpenCo and provide citations."
- Model output: "OpenCo was founded in 2008. See Journal of AI, 2009."
- Quick checks: KB lookup suggests founding year is 2012 -> FactError, severity=medium, repeatability=sometimes. Justification: "Founding year mismatch with public registry (link provided)."

Metrics and dashboards to expose
- Failure rate per 1000 prompts by category (rolling 7d)
- Median time-to-label for queued items (goal < 6 hours for high severity)
- IAR trendline and adjudication backlog size
- Cross-model delta matrix: how frequently a failure appears in variant pairs (useful for quant causality)

Governance and lifecycle
- The taxonomy is intentionally small. We will revisit quarterly. Any proposal to add a new top-level category requires a 2/3 vote from applied-ml, model-onboarding, and product trust leads.
- Maintain an examples corpus of ~2k labeled prompts (balanced across categories) used for annotator onboarding and heuristic tuning.

Appendix A: quick-reference decision flow
- heuristics confident? -> auto-label -> persist
- heuristics low confidence -> human queue -> label/adjudicate -> persist
- severity high -> escalate to oncall/model-owner and attach replication bundle

Appendix B: recommended JSON schema snippet for the manifest (single-row example)
{
  "prompt_id": "pf_2026_00021",
  "source": "prod:chat-assist",
  "seed_text": "[REDACTED]",
  "model_version": "gpt-redwood-v2-quant8",
  "failure_category": "FactError",
  "severity": "medium"
}

Contacts and ownership
- Primary owner: Morgan Reyes (applied-ml)
- Secondary reviewers: Nadia Chen (model-onboarding), Aakash Patel (eval-harness)
- Adjudication pool: annot-leads@redwood-inference.internal

Revision history
- 2026-01-18: Draft published and circulated to reviewers.
- 2026-02-10: Finalized taxonomy and IAR targets after calibration round.

References
- See also: edgecase-probe-generator-and-labeling-guidelines-2026 (prompt-sets-and-benchmarks) and causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026 (regression-triage) for linked procedures and crosswalks.

title: Hybrid Shadow Federation and Probe Retention Protocol
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines a company-wide protocol for running hybrid shadow evaluations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments using a federated orchestration model, with a strong focus on privacy-aware probe retention and telemetry aggregation. It standardizes: probe manifest formats, federation coordination patterns, privacy budget enforcement (DP), retention tiers, aggregation windows, and operational runbooks for triage and promotion.

Scope
-----
Applies to:
- Evaluation harness teams (shadow/eval orchestrator)
- Model onboarding and quantization teams (model owners)
- Platform & infra (orchestration connectors)
- Privacy & legal for DP/retention policies
- Customer Success for private deployment constraints

Not in scope:
- Non-eval production logs (use observability standards)
- Long-term archival of raw PII-laden user content beyond defined retention windows

Goals and success metrics
------------------------
Primary goals:
1) Provide consistent, low-latency shadow evaluation across environments while preserving tenant isolation.
2) Limit retention of raw probe payloads without sacrificing actionable triage signals.
3) Enable cross-tenant, cross-region federated aggregation for fleet-level signal analysis.

Success metrics (monthly):
- Shadow orchestration success rate >= 99.0% (jobs launched and results returned within expected window).
- Aggregate fidelity-preservation score <= 0.03 MRR delta for promoted models vs baseline on evaluation slices.
- Privacy budget overage events = 0 (epsilon budget violations).
- Mean time to first-triage (probe anomaly) <= 4 hours.

System architecture (overview)
----------------------------
1) Probe Fabric: central registry of probe manifests (immutable IDs) and lightweight shards delivered to orchestrators.
2) Local Shadow Engine: runs inside each deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private) that executes probes, applies local DP mechanisms, and emits telemetry.
3) Federation Coordinator: central or regionally replicated controller that aggregates pre-processed telemetry from Local Shadow Engines.
4) Aggregation Layer: deterministic, privacy-aware reducers that compute slice-level metrics and produce evaluated artifacts (reports, diffs, alerts).

Key properties:
- Immutable probe manifests allow reproducible runs.
- All raw payloads are treated as sensitive by default; local pre-processing removes or hashes candidate PII before any external transfer.
- The federation supports pull-based and push-based modes depending on private deployment networking constraints.

Probe manifest schema (human-readable)
-------------------------------------
Each manifest must be stored in the Probe Fabric and include the following fields:
- probe_id: string (immutable)
- created_by: engineer name or service
- description: short text explaining intent and slice
- input_template: single-line template with placeholders
- expected_labels: list of label names used by evaluators
- priority: low|medium|high
- retention_tier: raw|redacted|aggregate
- max_runtime_seconds: integer
- seed_policy: seed|randomized|deterministic-with-seed
- dp_policy_id: optional reference to a DP policy (see Privacy section)

Example manifest (YAML snippet)
------------------------------
manifest:
  probe_id: "pf-2026-0012"
  created_by: "maya.chen"
  description: "multi-turn coherency slice: long-context, system prompts"
  input_template: "<SYSTEM> \nUser: {question} \nAssistant:"
  expected_labels: ["coherence_score","toxicity_flag"]
  priority: medium
  retention_tier: redacted
  max_runtime_seconds: 30
  seed_policy: deterministic-with-seed
  dp_policy_id: dp-epsilon-0.5-std

Privacy, retention and DP enforcement
-------------------------------------
Retention tiers (policy):
- raw: raw request + raw response (allowed only for limited ops debugging and audited by privacy). Max retention 7 days.
- redacted: PII removed or replaced, text minimally redacted (stable identifiers hashed). Maximum retention 90 days.
- aggregate: only statistical aggregates or bucketing retained. Maximum retention 365 days.

Default policy: all probe runs default to redacted unless explicitly approved for raw by Privacy and the model owner.

Differential privacy enforcement:
- All telemetry leaving a private deployment must apply the local DP shim (Laplace or Gaussian depending on the metric) before transmission.
- Standard privacy policies: dp-epsilon-0.5-std (per-probe epsilon = 0.5), dp-epsilon-2.0-experiment (per-probe epsilon = 2.0, requires approval).
- Federation Coordinator validates DP policy IDs on ingestion and rejects telemetry without a valid DP header.

Telemetry fields and schema (table)
----------------------------------
| field_name | type | description | retention_tier | allowed_in_private_pull? |
| probe_id | string | manifest ID | aggregate | yes |
| run_id | string | unique run UUID | aggregate | yes |
| model_variant | string | model version tag | aggregate | yes |
| slice | string | evaluation slice name | aggregate | yes |
| latency_ms | int | end-to-end run latency | aggregate | yes |
| token_count | int | tokens consumed | aggregate | yes |
| fidelity_delta | float | metric delta vs baseline | redacted | yes |
| raw_response_hash | string | SHA256 of response after redaction | redacted | yes |
| annotation_flags | list | labels from annotators | redacted | no (annotator PII removed) |
| dp_policy_id | string | policy id applied locally | aggregate | yes |

Federation modes and networking patterns
----------------------------------------
1) Push-mode (hosted & dedicated): Local Shadow Engine pushes pre-aggregated telemetry to Federation Coordinator via HTTPS with mutual TLS.
2) Pull-mode (private / VPC): Federation Coordinator cannot reach the private network. Local Shadow Engine exposes an authenticated pull endpoint; coordinator fetches aggregated bundles on schedule.
3) Hybrid: Local Shadow Engine pushes to a customer-controlled mirror S3 / bucket. Federation Coordinator consumes from the mirror in read-only mode.

Operational runbook: shadow-run-create -> monitor -> triage
----------------------------------------------------------
1) Create probe manifest in Probe Fabric. Tag retention_tier and dp_policy.
2) Schedule a shadow run via the eval-orchestrator CLI (example below).
3) Local Shadow Engines acknowledge within 60s, run probes, and emit local metrics.
4) Federation Coordinator aggregates within the configured window (default 15 minutes) and computes slice-level metrics.
5) If aggregate fidelity_delta > threshold (0.05) on any high-priority slice, auto-open a triage ticket and page the eval-oncall.
6) For privacy flags or DP violations, Federation marks run as failed and notifies Privacy team; no further aggregation occurs.

CLI example (eval-orchestrator)
-------------------------------
# launch a single-run against a manifest across all reachable environments
eval-orchestrator run --manifest pf-2026-0012 --deadline 1800 --priority medium --notify-team eval-team

Config snippet for federated push (JSON)
---------------------------------------
{
  "federation_mode": "push",
  "endpoint": "https://federation.redwood.internal/v1/ingest",
  "mTLS_cert": "/etc/ssl/fed-client.pem",
  "aggregation_window_minutes": 15
}

Canary and promotion criteria
----------------------------
Promotion to staged-serving must satisfy both quality and operational gates:
- Quality: aggregated fidelity_delta <= 0.02 across critical slices (intent, safety, coherence) with p-value < 0.05 vs baseline.
- Cost/latency: 95th percentile latency increase <= 10ms and token cost delta <= 3%.
- Stability: no more than 2 regression incidents in the last 14 days.
- Privacy: no DP policy violations and retention tier is compatible with target environment.

Escalation and triage ownership
-------------------------------
- Probe steward: owns manifest lifecycle and labeling (assigned by applied-ml).
- Eval-oncall: primary responder for any fidelity/regression alerts.
- Privacy-eng: owns DP policy approvals and investigations.
- Infra-platform: responsible for federation endpoints and mTLS rotation.

Triage checklist (first responder)
---------------------------------
1) Verify the run_id and manifest ID.
2) Check Federation ingestion logs for DP header and reject reasons.
3) Examine slice-level metrics; identify top 3 regressions by impact.
4) If raw payload is required for debugging, request Privacy approval with a justification ticket (include hash of response and time window).
5) If regression is operational (latency/throughput), escalate to infra-platform.

Audit and compliance
--------------------
- All manifest creations and edits are immutably logged in Probe Fabric (write-once audit log retained 3 years).
- DP policy changes require dual approval (Privacy + Applied ML lead) and are recorded.
- Random spot checks: Privacy team runs monthly audits on raw-release approvals.

Operational metrics and dashboards to build
-----------------------------------------
- Shadow job success rate by environment (hosted/dedicated/private)
- Probe retention counts by tier and age histogram
- DP policy compliance rate and most common rejected runs
- Slice-level fidelity_delta heatmap (rolling 7d)
- Mean time to first triage and triage backlog size

Appendix A: Example DP header (HTTP)
-----------------------------------
X-DP-Policy-Id: dp-epsilon-0.5-std
X-DP-Epsilon: 0.5
X-DP-Algorithm: gaussian

Appendix B: Minimal troubleshooting commands
-------------------------------------------
# check local shadow engine status\kubectl -n eval get pods -l app=local-shadow-engine -o wide
# tail federation ingestion logs\stern federation-ingestor -n infra

Appendix C: Change log
-----------------------
- 2025-09-02: initial draft (Maya Chen)
- 2025-10-14: added DP policy table and retention tiers (Arjun Patel)
- 2026-01-15: clarified pull-mode for private deployments and added CLI examples (Lena García)

Notes and open questions
------------------------
- Should redacted tier include automated named-entity replacement vs hashing? Proposal: hashing by default; replacement optional with explicit approval.
- Investigate lightweight homomorphic aggregation for certain safety counts to reduce DP noise while preserving utility.

References
----------
- Probe Fabric spec (internal): /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/probe-fabric-spec
- Privacy budgeting playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails/probe-privacy-budget-and-annotation-retention-playbook-2024

Contact
-------
For questions or approvals, contact Maya Chen (maya.chen@redwood.ai) or the Applied-ML oncall channel (#eval-oncall).

title: Synthetic Workload Profiles and Stress Test Protocol for Inference and Quantized Models
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a reusable set of synthetic workload profiles and a stress-test protocol for validating inference correctness, latency SLOs, cost-accuracy tradeoffs, and quantization stability across Redwood Inference runtimes (hosted, dedicated, private). It is intended for applied ML engineers, runtime owners, and SREs who run large-scale pre-production and canary tests.

Purpose and goals:
- Provide a canonical library of synthetic traces that emulate real customer workloads (short chat, long-compose, retrieval-augmented prompts, embedding bursts).
- Surface regressions caused by quantization (INT8/INT4), KV-cache interactions, batching and kernel selection.
- Verify latency and tail behavior under sustained load and cold-cache scenarios.
- Standardize pass/fail criteria and triage steps for regression alerts.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers onboarding new models or quantization profiles.
- Runtime and serving teams validating kernel optimizations.
- SRE and test-automation teams running nightly stress suites.

Prerequisites and test environment:
1) Test cluster: dedicated test pool named `stress-test-pool` (A100/80GB or A10G depending on profile).
2) Services: `inference-service`, `runtime-proxy`, `batcher`, and `metrics-exporter` running with test tags.
3) Dataset seeds: production-sampled seed files in `s3://redwood-evals/seeds/2026/` (obfuscated customer ids).
4) Canary model artifacts: model vX.Y quantized variants (FP16, INT8, INT4) stored in model registry with tags `canary` and `quant-test`.

Test profiles (table):
| profile_id | short_name | description | typical_seq | QPS | target_95p_latency |
|-----------:|------------|-------------|------------:|----:|------------------:|
| P1 | chat-short | Multi-turn chat with short replies, token lengths 8-64 | 8-64 tokens | 100 qps | <= 120 ms |
| P2 | compose-mid | Single-turn compose with 256-token output distribution | 64-256 tokens | 30 qps | <= 300 ms |
| P3 | long-context | Long context (news article ~2048 tokens) with KV cache stress | 1024-4096 tokens | 5 qps | <= 1.2 s |
| P4 | embed-burst | Embedding bursts: 512-dim embeddings, small inputs | 1-32 tokens | 500 qps | <= 80 ms |
| P5 | mixed-realtime | Mixed traffic: 70% P1, 20% P2, 10% P4, respecting burstiness | variable | 150 qps | P1-95p <= 150 ms |

Profile generation rules:
- Use production distribution percentiles: sample prompt lengths from P0/P25/P50/P75/P95 distributions.
- Inject content diversity: include code, tables, conversational tokens, and multilingual samples in 12% of traces.
- Cache state simulation: for P3 run with a warm cache (90% KV hit) and a cold-cache run (0% KV hit) to measure delta.

Config template (YAML) for harness (example):
```yaml
profile: P3
model: open-mistral-v1-canary
variant: int8
duration: 1800 # seconds
qps: 5
concurrency: 20
seed_file: s3://redwood-evals/seeds/2026/long-context-seed.jsonl
headers:
  X-Test-Run: synthetic-stress-2026-02
metrics_exporter: prometheus://metrics-exporter:9090
```

Execution steps (canonical run):
1) Provision `stress-test-pool` and ensure cluster autoscaling disabled for test.
2) Deploy canary model variant to `inference-service` with tag `canary/stress/2026-02`.
3) Start `metrics-exporter` and validate Prometheus scrape targets: `batcher`, `runtime-proxy`, `inference-service`.
4) Run baseline FP16 P1-P5 profiles for 30 minutes each, capture APM traces and tokens breakdown.
5) Run quantized variants (INT8, INT4) with identical seeds; run both warm-cache and cold-cache modes.
6) Run long-duration soak (>= 3 hours) for P5 mixed-realtime profile to measure degradation patterns.
7) Upload artifacts: raw responses, latency histograms, token counters, and cost model inputs to `s3://redwood-evals/results/<run-id>/`.

Key metrics to collect (labels map to Prometheus metrics):
- request_duration_seconds{quantization,profile,model_version} (Histogram)
- token_generated_count_total{model_variant}
- kv_cache_hit_ratio{profile}
- batch_size_distribution{profile}
- gpu_utilization_percent{node}
- runtime_fallback_count_total (counter)

Pass/fail and alert thresholds:
- Functional correctness: BLEU/ROUGE/stability checks against FP16 baseline. Fail on > 3% drop in semantic consistency (task-dependent).
- Latency: 95th percentile must be within 20% of FP16 baseline for the same profile and hardware OR within the absolute thresholds in the profile table.
- Error budget: if runtime_fallback_count_total increases by > 2x baseline across a run, mark as failed.
- Cost delta: unit token cost projected > 1.4x compared to FP16 indicates regression for cost-sensitive tiers; flag for product review.

Triage playbook (ordered):
1) Reproduce: re-run failing profile with same run-id and extended logging enabled.
2) Check metrics: examine kv_cache_hit_ratio, batch_size_distribution, and gpu_utilization. Low KV hit or smaller batch sizes indicate workload skew.
3) Kernel mismatch: inspect runtime logs for kernel selection warnings (tagged `kernel-selector.warn`). If present, escalate to serving-runtime team.
4) Quantization degradation: run small targeted eval suite (100 deterministic prompts) to compute semantic drift. If drift concentrated on numeric or code outputs, tag as `quant-numbering-regression`.
5) Fallback & OOM: if runtime_fallback_count_total > threshold, collect heap profiles and GpuMem logs, open internal ticket `RUNTIME-FTB-<run-id>`.
6) Communication: add regression summary to the nightly evaluation digest and notify `#applied-ml-evals` with subject `STRESS-FAIL <profile> <model> <run-id>`.

Ownership and cadence:
- Test owner: applied-ml team (owner contact: evelyn.cho@redwood.ai).
- SRE support: eng-sre on-call for `stress-test-pool`.
- Nightly runs: automated P1-P3 smoke every night at 02:00 UTC. Full synthetic stress suite (all profiles) runs weekly on Saturday 03:00 UTC.
- Gate for rollout: all canary model releases require a successful synthetic stress run against P1-P5 before traffic migration.

Automation and artifact retention:
- Harness lives in `repo: infra/eval-harness` under `synthetic-profiles/`.
- Results retained for 90 days in S3; summarized metrics pushed to TSDB.
- CI integration: Pull requests that modify quantization profiles must reference a `stress-test-run-id` demonstrating non-regression.

Interpreting results (examples):
- Scenario A (INT8 shows +15% 95p latency only for P3 cold-cache): likely KV-cache alignment or slower INT8 kernel for long sequences. Next step: run `kernel-benchmark --seq 2048 --variant int8` and compare micro-benchmarks.
- Scenario B (INT4 shows semantic drift on code snippets but latency OK): revert INT4 for canary and open issue against `applied-ml/quantization` for targeted post-training calibration.

Appendix A — Useful CLI snippets:
- Start run: `python tools/run_synthetic.py --config configs/P3-int8.yaml --out s3://redwood-evals/results/$(date +%s)-p3/`
- Collect traces: `kubectl logs -l app=inference-service -n stress-test --since=2h > inference-service-logs.gz`
- Query metrics example: `promql: rate(request_duration_seconds_sum{profile=\"P1\",model_variant=\"int8\"}[5m])`

Appendix B — Known limitations and future work:
- Current seeds underrepresent streaming token-by-token patterns used by low-latency SDKs; plan to add P6 streaming profile Q3 2026.
- Does not currently simulate multi-tenant noisy neighbors; a separate noisy-neighbor harness is scheduled for H2 2026.

Related pages and references:
- See quantization stability audit playbook for KV-cache specific guidance.
- See serving-simulation-eval-harness for microbench orchestration examples.

Change log:
- 2025-09-10: Initial draft and canonical profile list (E. Cho).
- 2025-11-02: Added P5 mixed-realtime and cost gating rules (M. Ruiz).
- 2026-02-15: Updated pass/fail thresholds and added INT4 semantic-drift guidance (A. Patel).

title: Operational Eval Sweep and Prioritization Framework
content:
SUMMARY
This document describes the Operational Eval Sweep and Prioritization Framework (OESPF), an opinionated set of processes and configuration conventions to run continuous, cost-aware evaluation sweeps across production workloads, quantized artifacts, and prompt perturbations. The framework balances risk (quality regressions) and cost (eval compute) with clear prioritization and automated handoffs into regression triage.

Scope
- Applies to eval orchestration performed by eval-orchestrator and probe-farm for hosted, dedicated, and private model variants.
- Covers sweep definition, priority scoring, scheduling policies, telemetry collection, alert thresholds, and integration points for triage/runbooks.
- Not a replacement for unit-level evals or offline researcher experiments.

Goals
1) Surface high-impact regressions early with minimal eval spend.
2) Ensure repeatable priority decisions across workloads and teams.
3) Provide deterministic handoffs to the regression-triage playbooks when thresholds are exceeded.

Definitions
- Sweep: a single, parameterized pass of probes (a set of prompts + seeds) run against a model or artifact.
- Probe: individual synthetic or sampled request used for evaluation.
- Priority Score: numeric score (0-100) used to order sweeps for execution.

Sweep types and use cases
1) Smoke Sweep (high-priority, low-cost): 50 probes per workload; run on every model push to hosted. Purpose: fast fail detection.
2) Sensitivity Sweep (medium-priority): targeted perturbation families (paraphrase, tokenization noise, slot-shuffle); 200 probes. Purpose: detect semantic instability and tokenization sensitivity.
3) Quant-sensitivity Sweep (high-cost, targeted): runs only for artifacts flagged by quant-profile changes; includes per-layer microbenchmarks and 1k prompt subset.
4) Regression Probe Sweep (on-demand): triggered by telemetry anomaly or customer report; merges production traces with synthetic probes.

Priority scoring algorithm (example)
Priority = round(min(100, 0.4*Risk + 0.3*CustomerImpact + 0.2*ArtifactChangeScore + 0.1*ResourceUrgency))
Where:
- Risk: model lineage delta score (0-100) from model-watcher.
- CustomerImpact: weighted by active routes using model (0-100).
- ArtifactChangeScore: 0-100 based on quantization delta or kernel changes.
- ResourceUrgency: incremental based on backlog age and SLA commitments.

Scheduling policies
- Real-time queue: priority >= 80 -> scheduled within 30 minutes.
- Batch queue: priority 40-79 -> scheduled during next nightly slot.
- Low queue: priority < 40 -> opportunistic execution when idle.
- Quotas: team-level daily compute budgets enforced by eval-orchestrator.

Config schema (YAML example)
```yaml
sweep_name: sensitivity-2026-10
model_variant: redwood/gptx-7b-q4f
type: sensitivity
probe_count: 200
priority_overrides:
  customer_critical: true
schedulers:
  queue: batch
  retry_policy:
    max_attempts: 2
    backoff: exponential
stability_checks:
  coherence_threshold: 0.88
  semantic_shift_alert_delta: 0.05
telemetry_exports:
  prometheus_metrics: [eval_duration_seconds, probe_failure_count, response_coherence]
  storage: s3://eval-results/prod-sweeps/
```

Concrete thresholds and SLOs
- Eval completion SLO: 99th percentile eval_duration_seconds < 300s for real-time queue.
- Alerting rule: raise a "sweep-regression" when response_coherence drops by >= 5% relative to baseline AND semantic_shift >= 0.04 on >= 10 probe slices.
- Escalation: Critical if customer_impact >= 80 and quality delta >= 3% on high-traffic routes.

Telemetry and observability
- Instrumentation: eval-orchestrator emits traces (trace_id), per-probe metrics, and artifacts (serialized responses).
- Prometheus metrics: eval_queue_length, eval_success_count, eval_failure_count, eval_duration_seconds_bucket.
- Dashboards: "Operational Eval Health" (per-model, per-route) and "Sweep Priority Backlog".

Failure modes and mitigations
- Stalled sweeps: watchdog kills runs exceeding 2x expected duration; auto-requeue with reduced probe_count.
- Probe flakiness: if probe_failure_count > 10% for a sweep, mark as unstable and quarantine probe family.
- False positives (semantic metric drift): require 2 consecutive sweep confirmations within 48h before automated rollbacks.

Integration with regression triage and oncall
1) When a sweep crosses the "sweep-regression" alert rule, eval-orchestrator creates a ticket in regression-triage with: sweep_id, top failing slices, baseline snapshot, and a link to artifacts in S3.
2) The regression-triage playbook (see related_pages) is responsible for bisect steps, suspected root-cause tags (quant-rollback, prompt-shift, model-weight-drift), and recommended mitigations.
3) Oncall flow:
   - Pager triggers for Priority >= 90 + customer_impact >= 80.
   - Runbook steps: confirm alerts, gather signatures (traces, sample diffs), run a narrow canary rollback, and notify CS if customer routes were affected.

Operational runbook (short run steps)
1) Verify sweep artifacts: `aws s3 ls s3://eval-results/prod-sweeps/<sweep_id>/`
2) Check dashboard slices and top-failing prompts.
3) If failure confirmed: open regression-triage ticket and tag as `high-priority`.
4) Apply mitigation: temporary model pin or automatic fallback to parent model variant via smart-routing.
5) Follow up: schedule a quant-sensitivity sweep after any rollback to verify health.

CLI snippets
- Kick off a one-off sensitivity sweep:
  `rwd-evalctl start-sweep --model redwood/gptx-7b --type sensitivity --probes 200 --priority 65`
- Query sweep status:
  `rwd-evalctl get-sweep --id sweep-202610-abc123 --format json`

Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: Applied ML Platform (Maya Singh) — applied-ml@redwood.ai
- Escalation: Runtime SRE (oncall alias: runtime-sre@redwood.ai)

Change log
- 2025-09-30 (Maya Singh): Initial draft and rollout of priority algorithm.
- 2026-02-18 (Maya Singh): Added quant-sensitivity gating rules and confirmed telemetry export schema.

Appendix: Examples of prioritization decisions
- Example A: A small quant change (ArtifactChangeScore 30) for a model used by 3 enterprise routes (CustomerImpact 80) -> Priority ≈ 62 -> Batch queue but with customer_critical override can promote to Real-time.
- Example B: Kernel-level update (ArtifactChangeScore 70) + high lineage drift (Risk 75) -> Priority ≈ 78 -> Nightly batch but with auto-accelerate if backlog_age > 24h.

References
- model-watcher lineage scoring (internal doc)
- regression-triage playbook (related_pages)
- eval-orchestrator v3 API spec (internal)

title: anchored-fallback-probe-assembler-and-quant-safety-cookbook-2026
content:
Summary:
This cookbook describes a repeatable, runtime-aware process for assembling anchored fallback probes that are designed to detect and triage quality regressions introduced by quantized deployments and runtime fallbacks. The procedure ties together probe curation, priming strategies, quant-compatibility scoring, and an automated fallback activation plan for production rollouts.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers building eval harnesses and onboarding models
- Runtime engineers responsible for quantized rollback and fallback policies
- QA and SRE teams who run shadow and canary evaluations

Why this doc exists:
Quantization and fallback policies reduce cost but introduce subtle coherence and function-call regressions. Existing probe factories generate broad coverage; this cookbook focuses on probes that a) are anchored to stable behavior signatures, b) exercise fallback handoffs end-to-end, and c) include quant-compatibility metadata so triage can rapidly isolate causes.

Scope and definitions:
1) Anchored probe: a synthesized test case that includes a canonical prompt, expected behavior signature (anchor), and a small set of tolerated variability patterns. Anchors can be tokens, semantic embeddings, or function-call schemas.
2) Fallback path: a runtime route where requests switch to a different model/variant (e.g., full-precision -> 8-bit quant -> smaller model) due to capacity, latency, or policy.
3) Quant-compatibility score (QCS): a scalar score (0–1) estimating how likely a probe's expected anchor survives a target quant profile. QCS integrates per-token coherence loss, functioncall-stability, and embedding cosine drift.

High-level workflow:
- Step 0: Preflight checks (ownership, telemetry hooks)
  1. Confirm owner and monitoring hooks are present in the probe manifest.
  2. Ensure the runtime emits fallback traces (model_variant, quant_profile, kv_cache_state, latency_ms).
- Step 1: Anchor selection
  1. Select a stable reference set from production seed traffic (top 500 high-frequency prompts for target service slice).
  2. Filter for probes with deterministic anchors: functioncall schemas or canonical JSON outputs, short canonical completions, or high-confidence embeddings (embedding cosine > 0.95 across seeds).
- Step 2: Synthesis with priming variants
  1. For each anchor, generate 6 primed variants: neutral, historical-context (short), historical-context (long), noise-perturbed (syntactic), adversarial-lexical, and multimodal-placeholder (if applicable).
  2. Label each variant with meta: token_count, expected_anchor_type, intent_category, latency_budget.
- Step 3: Quant-compatibility assessment (offline)
  1. Run each variant through the quant-sim sandbox: FP16, INT8, hybrid-quant profiles used in production.
  2. Compute QCS = weighted_sum(embedding_drift_score * 0.5, functioncall_stability * 0.3, token_coherence * 0.2).
  3. Mark probes with QCS < 0.6 as high-risk (candidate for pre-deployment triage).
- Step 4: Fallback path simulation (shadow)
  1. Mirror candidate probes through the shadow mesh with configured fallback policies enabled (simulate capacity degradation and latency SLO violations).
  2. Capture traces and compare anchor hits vs baseline.
- Step 5: Acceptance, remediation, and rollout gating
  1. If > 3% of production-priority probes drop below anchor-match threshold, fail rollout.
  2. For failing probes: attempt prompt-rewrite priming (see Appendix A) and re-evaluate QCS.
  3. If rewrite cannot recover anchor, schedule quant-hold for that model and file regression ticket (Triage label: quant-fallback-critical).

Probe manifest schema (text table):
| field | type | example | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| id | string | probe-anch-2026-0001 | unique probe id |
| anchor_type | string | functioncall | token | embedding | json-schema |
| canonical_prompt | string | "Summarize the quarterly revenue for Q3." | prompt used for generation |
| priming_variants | list | neutral,long-context,noise | comma-separated in manifest |
| qcs_scores | list | fp16:0.92,int8:0.58,hybrid:0.71 | used to gate deployment |
| owner | string | analytics-team | oncall and owner contact |
| rollout_action | string | hold|rollout|rewrite | decision after evaluation |

Operational thresholds and SLOs:
- Anchor-match threshold: 0.85 (primary signal for semantic anchors).
- Functioncall-stability SLO: 99.5% for high-criticality probes (billing, auth, legal).
- QCS gate for canary: median QCS >= 0.75 across canary probe set.
- Canary rollback rule: if latency increase > 2x AND anchor-match drop > 1.5%, rollback immediately.

Example CLI snippet (probe-synth tool):
# synthesize anchored probes from seed logs
redwood-probe synth --seed-log s3://redwood-prod/seed-2026-02-15.jsonl --anchor-type functioncall --variants 6 --out probes/anchored-2026.jsonl

Quant-sim config (YAML example):
quant_profiles:
  - name: int8-baseline
    kernels: auto
    calibration_steps: 2048
  - name: hybrid-bert-optim
    kernels: hetero
    per_channel: true

QCS calculation (pseudocode):
- embedding_drift = 1 - cosine(e_baseline, e_quant)
- token_coherence = 1 - (levenshtein(baseline_text, quant_text) / max_len)
- functioncall_stability = fraction_identical_calls
- qcs = clamp(0,1, 1 - (0.5*embedding_drift + 0.2*(1-token_coherence) + 0.3*(1-functioncall_stability)))

Triage playbook (short flow):
1) Alert triggers: Canary QCS median < 0.75 OR production probe anchor-match regression > configured slice threshold.
2) Pager and channel: Notify applied-ml-oncall and runtime-oncall with runbook link.
3) Initial investigator: confirm signal with shadow replay.
4) Hypothesis sprint (30 minutes): check quant_profile drift, kernel mismatch, tokenization shift, and prompt slicing artifacts.
5) If runtime fallback implicated: capture full KV cache capture and escalate to runtime-kernel team.
6) If quant profile implicated: revert quant profile and trigger mixed-precision fallback.

Remediation patterns (ranked by expected velocity):
- Pattern A (fast): prompt-rewrite priming (append explicit function call schema + example).
- Pattern B (moderate): per-slice quant-hedge (keep FP16 for slices with low QCS).
- Pattern C (heavy): model re-quantization with per-channel calibration; schedule out-of-hours rollout.

Appendix A — Prompt-rewrite templates:
- Functioncall example:
  "You must respond in JSON with fields: {\"action\":string, \"items\":array}. Example: {\"action\":\"list\",\"items\":[\"a\"]}. Now: <USER PROMPT>"
- Embedding anchor example: include a short anchor sentence to bias embedding: "Anchor: financial-summary-v2" appended to the prompt.

Appendix B — Canary composition guidance:
- Canary set size: minimum 200 anchored probes covering at least 5 priority slices.
- Sampling: stratified by tenant weight and intent category (responses that include function calls weighted x3).
- Evaluation cadence: continuous shadow with hourly aggregated QCS and daily human spot checks for high-impact slices.

Ownership and runbook links:
- Probe synthesis: Applied ML Eval Platform (oncall: @m-chen).
- Quant-sim sandbox and kernels: Serving Runtime Kernel Team (oncall: @e-summers).
- Regression triage board: Regression Triage (label: quant-fallback-critical).
- Runbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/field-eval-fast-path-and-rollback-playbook-2025

Appendix C — Example incident timeline (realistic template):
- T+0 min: Canary QCS drop detected (median => 0.62). Pager fired.
- T+10 min: Shadow replay confirms anchor failures on int8 baseline but not FP16.
- T+25 min: Prompt-rewrite attempted for top-10 failing probes: partial recovery.
- T+40 min: Quant hold applied to canary cohort; rollout aborted.
- T+72 hours: Quant re-calibration completed and rolling canary resumed with per-slice hedges.

Notes and caveats:
- QCS is a heuristic. Always pair automated gates with human spot checks on high-impact slices.
- Embedding drift metrics are sensitive to tokenization changes; include tokenization_version in probe manifests.
- When possible, prefer mixed-precision hedging over full rollback to preserve cost benefits.

Maintenance and next steps:
- Quarterly: refresh anchor set from latest production traffic and re-evaluate QCS thresholds.
- Next iteration: add synthesized natural-language paraphrase families using LMs constrained to low-divergence decoding; evaluate impact on QCS stability.

End of document."

title: functioncall-emergent-regression-simulator-2026
content:
Overview

This document describes the Functioncall Emergent Regression Simulator (FERS) — a reproducible harness and failure-library designed to synthesize and stress emergent failure modes for function-calling models during shadow, canary, and quantized rollouts. FERS is intended to detect behavioral regressions that do not appear in standard prompt suites: e.g., degraded function argument extraction, hallucinated tool endpoints, corrupted JSON shapes, and latent tokenization-induced misalignment under quantization.

Goals

- Provide a catalog of synthetic failure generators targeting functioncall interfaces.
- Define a runtime harness (eval-meson) that can inject failures into shadow traffic and produce deterministic failure traces.
- Supply acceptance criteria and automated triage signals to gate rollouts (shadow -> canary -> prod) for models with functioncall usage.
- Standardize remediation and rollforward steps for regressions discovered by the simulator.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to models exposed via Redwood API's chat/functioncall surface and internal rerankers that emit structured payloads.
- Intended for model onboarding, quant migration, and canary validations across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Not intended as a replacement for human annotator evaluations; FERS augments evaluator workflows by surfacing falsifiable, reproducible failure traces.

Definitions

- Failure generator: deterministic or stochastic transformer that mutates prompts, responses, or function signatures to simulate a class of regression.
- Anchor probe: a canonical prompt-and-response pair used for day-zero comparison and SLI calculation.
- Emergent regression: behavior change that appears only under composite conditions (e.g., long context + quant + functioncall).

Failure-library (catalog)

Below is an excerpt of the curated failure generators. The full library is in repo: git://infra/eval-meson/fers/failure-library.

| id | target | description | intensity knobs | expected signal |
|----|--------|-------------|-----------------|----------------|
| FCF-01 | function-args | Drop a random required arg from the model-invoked JSON payload | drop_rate (0.0-1.0) | increase in missing-arg errors; schema-violation count up |
| FCF-02 | json-escape | Inject mis-escaped control characters into string args | char_freq, char_set | parser exceptions or silent truncation |
| FCF-03 | endpoint-halluc | Replace real tool names with plausible-but-invalid endpoints | substitution_map_size | 4xx/5xx tool routing anomalies; increased fallback triggers |
| FCF-04 | token-shift | Shift token boundaries to simulate tokenization drift (quant-sensitive) | shift_window, seed | coherence drop on long-context slices; KV-cache misses |
| FCF-05 | type-corrupt | Replace numeric args with strings and vice-versa | corruption_rate | type-mismatch traces in downstream services |

Design and architecture

High-level components: eval-meson (harness), probeforge (probe generator), sidecar-evaluator (per-tenant evaluator-sidecar), and synth-catalog (failure library).

- eval-meson: Gateway that replays or mirrors shadow traffic and coordinates injection via a pluggable failure step graph. Supports deterministic seeds for reproducible traces.
- probeforge: DSL for composing multi-step probes (priming -> invoke -> verify). Probe definitions are stored as YAML manifests and can target live shadow traffic, synthetic sessions, or archived traces.
- sidecar-evaluator: Runs near the serving tier (dedicated/private) and evaluates functioncall stability at socket-level to catch protocol anomalies before they hit upstream tooling.
- synth-catalog: Versioned package of failure generators with semantic versioning. Each generator includes a risk score and recommended mitigation patterns.

Operational flow (high level)

1) Author creates a probe manifest in probeforge (see example below).
2) eval-meson schedules the probe against a shadow cohort or synthetic session set.
3) Failure generators run according to configured intensity; traces are recorded to S3 and the eval-meson results store.
4) Automated analyzers compute SLI deltas vs. anchors and emit triage tickets if thresholds are breached.
5) Triage flow routes to the model-oncall and quant-steering desk with recommended rollback/mitigation actions.

Probe manifest example (YAML)

---
name: invoice-extraction-longcontext
mode: shadow
seed: 20260610-invoice-001
steps:
  - priming: file://probes/primers/invoice-context-12k.txt
  - call: { model: gpt-4x-functioncall-v0, max_tokens: 256, function: extract_invoice }
  - failure_inject:
      id: FCF-04
      params: { shift_window: 128, seed: 42 }
  - verify: { schema: file://schemas/invoice-v2.json, allow_missing_fields: false }

Running the simulator (CLI examples)

# Run a single probe against archived trace set
$ eval-meson run --probe invoice-extraction-longcontext --archive s3://eval-archives/tenant-a/2026-06-01 --seed 42

# Schedule a multichoort run with increasing intensity
$ eval-meson schedule --manifest ./manifests/quant-compat-multi.yaml --cohorts tenant-a,tenant-b --ramp 0.1:0.5:1.0 --notify --deadline 2026-06-20

Acceptance criteria and gating rules

All rollouts that include functioncall-capable models must pass the following checks in the shadow stage before canary:

- Anchor coherence SLI: delta <= 1.5% against promoted baseline on the anchor probes after 1000 probe runs.
- Schema conformance: no more than 0.2% schema violations on critical fields (invoice_id, total_amount) across the shadow cohort.
- Tool stability: < 0.5% increase in tool fallback rate when endpoint-hallucation generators are enabled at intensity=0.25.
- Token-shift sensitivity: coherence p95 drop < 2% under FCF-04 intensity=0.5 for long-context probes.

If any single gating rule fails, the model must not proceed to canary and the model owner must open a regression investigation within 1 business day.

Monitoring, alerts and triage signals

Primary signals produced by FERS:

- SLI delta per-anchor (numerical): stored as time-series metric ers.anchor.delta_{probe_name}
- Schema violation rate (percentage) ers.schema.violation_{model}_{schema}
- Tool fallback increment ers.tool.fallback_delta_{model}
- Reproducibility score (0-1): fraction of injected failures that reproduce across seeds (low score indicates non-deterministic failure)

Alerting thresholds (examples):

- P0: schema violation rate >= 1% sustained for 5 minutes -> page oncall + create incident ticket.
- P1: anchor SLI delta >= 3% for 30 minutes -> notify model owner and schedule regression run.
- P2: reproducibility score < 0.3 on high-severity failure generators -> send to evaluation desk for manual analysis.

Automated triage rules

- If schema violation rate > 0.5% && reproducibility >= 0.75 -> auto-open a regression-investigation ticket with attached failure traces and suggested blame candidates (quant, tokenizer, prompt-preprocessor).
- If token-shift sensitivity triggers with low tool fallback changes -> flag quant as likely cause and pin a quant_shadow cohort for deeper replay.

Investigation and remediation checklist (numbered runbook)

1. Confirm reproducibility: re-run failing probe with seed and verify failure trace (eval-meson replay --trace <id>).
2. Compare traces across promoted baseline and candidate model; capture tokenization diffs.
3. If tokenization drift suspected, run token-shift diagnostic (probeforge diagnostics token-diff).
4. If quant-sensitive: route to quant-steering; run mixed-precision shadow with FCF-04 intensity sweep.
5. If function-arg or JSON corruption: run sidecar-evaluator at socket level and check intermediate tool ingress logs.
6. Apply mitigations: prompt-rewrite, schema-relaxation (short-term), or quant rollback (if severity high).
7. Re-run gated probes and ensure all acceptance criteria pass before resuming rollout.

Owner and escalation matrix

- Library owner: Sasha Kim (applied-evals).
- Harness owner: Marcus Liu (eval infra).
- Quant desk: Diego Ramirez (applied-ml).
- Oncall: model-oncall rotation (see team wiki for schedule).

Change controls and release cadence

- synth-catalog updates require a PR with: description of new generator, risk score, two reviewers, and reproducibility report (>= 10 deterministic seeds).
- Minor patch releases (catalog patch) on a two-week cadence. Major changes that affect gating thresholds require sign-off from quant desk and evaluation committee and a 1-week canary run across two tenants.

Appendix A — Example failure trace snippet (trimmed JSON)

{
  "probe_id": "invoice-extraction-longcontext",
  "seed": 42,
  "failure_gen": "FCF-04",
  "events": [
    {"t":"2026-06-10T12:01:02Z","stage":"call","tokens_before": 10234},
    {"t":"2026-06-10T12:01:03Z","stage":"inject","desc":"shifted tokens at 100-228"},
    {"t":"2026-06-10T12:01:04Z","stage":"verify","result":"schema_violation","field":"total_amount"}
  ]
}

Appendix B — Quickcheck list before submitting a promo PR

- [ ] Add anchor probe + baseline results to PR description.
- [ ] Include reproducibility score and failure traces for all enabled generators.
- [ ] Confirm no schema regressions on critical fields (invoice_id, user_id, total).
- [ ] Run token-shift diagnostic at intensity 0.5 and include report.

Contacts and references

- Eval harness repo: git://infra/eval-meson
- Failure library index: git://infra/eval-meson/fers/failure-library/index.yaml
- Probe DSL docs: confluence://applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/probe-dsl-reference-2025

Changelog

- 2026-02-15: Initial draft by Sasha Kim.
- 2026-04-02: Added token-shift generator and acceptance thresholds (reviewers: Anya Patel).
- 2026-06-10: Finalized gating rules and automation triage flows (publish).

title: Quantization Shadow Fidelity Simulator and Regression Hypothesis Bundle
content:
Overview

This document describes the Quantization Shadow Fidelity Simulator (QSFS) — a lightweight, modular evaluator used by the eval-harness to predict behavioral deltas introduced by quantized model artifacts before production rollout — and the accompanying Regression Hypothesis Bundle (RHB) for structured triage if the simulator surfaces risk. QSFS is intended for use during model-onboarding, quantization-profile generation, and pre-rollout canary design.

Why we built QSFS

- Reduce time and cost: simulate large-scale quantized behavior deterministically on small reference workloads rather than running full shadow fleets.
- Improve triage velocity: provide prioritized hypotheses and signal extraction to accelerate root cause identification for regressions tied to quant artifacts.
- Standardize handoffs: produce an artifact (RHB) consumed by regression teams, SRE, and model owners with uniform fields and triage runbooks.

Scope and non-goals

- In-scope: sequence-level fidelity simulation for text generation and reranking models (causal and encoder-decoder), token-level divergence metrics, prompt-conditioning sensitivity, and KV-cache interaction emulation.
- Out-of-scope: full GPU kernel performance estimation, detailed latency/throughput microbenchmarks, or end-to-end production traffic replay (use shadow-fleet or production mirror for that).

High-level architecture

QSFS consists of three coordinated modules:

1) Probe Fabricator: selects and prepares workload slices (priming context, few-shot examples, edge-case seeds).
2) Quantized Emulator: runs a quantized-inference deterministic emulator that applies quant noise models and cache-decay approximations to a floating-point baseline.
3) Analyzer & Hypothesis Composer: produces fidelity metrics, diffs, and structured hypotheses (RHB).

Each module can be executed independently in the eval-harness pipeline or as a single command. Ownership: eval-harness team owns the code; applied-ml stewards the probe catalog.

Probe Fabrication and Selection

- Inputs: workload fingerprint, slice definitions, probe budget, and tenant constraints.
- Strategy: stratified sampling across context lengths (short/medium/long), priming density (0/1/5 shots), and token-entropy buckets.

Probe types generated:

- Baseline-stability probes: produce deterministic seeds used for consistency checks.
- Quant-stress probes: perturbations (token swap, suffix truncation, numeric precision stressors).
- Edge semantic probes: adversarially generated prompts targeting critical functionality (e.g., code generation, instruction-following).

Simulator configuration (table)

| parameter | description | default | notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| quant_profile | identifier for quant recipe (e.g., q4f, q8a) | q4f-default | maps to quantization-profiles catalog |
| seed_set | probe catalog id | small-core-100 | use larger for release candidate |
| kv_cache_modeling | none | "approximate" | options: none, approximate, exact-sim |
| temperature | sampling temp for stochastic probes | 0.0 | 0.0 forces deterministic sampling |
| rerun_count | number of emulator passes per probe | 3 | aggregate variance budget |
| divergence_threshold | alert-level for token-level divergence | 0.06 | used to generate RHB alerts |

Execution procedure (step-by-step)

1. Prepare context: map service-level workload fingerprint (from eval-mesh) to seed_set and override priming where necessary.
2. Run floating-point baseline (FP32 or BF16) to generate canonical outputs and internal trace (logits, top-k tokens per step).
3. Run Quantized Emulator against the same probes. If kv_cache_modeling=="exact-sim", emulate cache reads/writes; else apply cache-decay model.
4. Compute fidelity metrics: token-divergence (KL and token-mismatch rate), response-syntactic-distance (BLEU/ROUGE heuristics), and functioncall-structure-delta (for tool-calling).
5. If any metric breaches configured thresholds, auto-generate an RHB and escalate per policy.

Fidelity metrics and thresholds (examples)

- Token mismatch rate: fraction of sample tokens not in FP baseline top-1 (Alert if > divergence_threshold).
- KL over logits: mean KL across steps (Alert if > 0.18).
- Response structure flip: % of probes where functioncall schema or JSON validity changed (Alert if > 0.02).
- Latent-behavior drift: embedding cosine drift of final states (Alert if > 0.12).

Regression Hypothesis Bundle (RHB) schema

The RHB is a standardized artifact produced as a JSON-LD (consumed by issue trackers and triage dashboards). The key fields listed below must be present in the bundle; simplified here for human review.

Table: RHB fields and triage actions

| field | example | triage owner | action on fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| title | "q4f -> q4f-v2: functioncall fidelity regression on payments prompts" | model-owner | assign model regression ticket |
| probe_ids | ["seed-123","seed-54"] | applied-ml | reproduce locally |
| primary_signal | "token-mismatch-rate" | applied-ml | run targeted stress probes |
| delta_snapshot | "/artifacts/q4f/v2/compare-2026-02-10" | SRE | pull logs & kernel traces |
| top_hypotheses | ["quant-rounding-bias", "kv-cache-loss"] | applied-ml | prioritize by score |
| suggested_mitigations | ["increase precision for attention kernels", "use cache-stabilizer rewrite"] | model-owner | patch & re-run QSFS |
| impact_estimate | "0.6% requests downgraded for payments flow" | product | decide rollout delay |
| blocker_flag | "true" | release_coord | block rollout if true |

Hypothesis scoring and prioritization

- Each hypothesis scored by: signal-strength (0–1), reproducibility (0–1), surface-risk (0–1). Composite score = weighted sum (0.5*signal + 0.3*repro + 0.2*risk).
- Triage guidelines: focus first on hypotheses with composite score > 0.6 and reproducibility > 0.7.

Automated escalation rules

- If blocker_flag==true OR top_hypothesis composite score > 0.8 -> auto-create high-priority regression incident and tag SRE/model-oncall.
- If token-mismatch-rate > 2x divergence_threshold across critical probes -> notify product & customer-success.

Integration points with existing pipelines

- eval-harness: QSFS is a pluggable stage in pre-promotion pipelines. Use the eval-harness adapter to surface metrics to the eval-mesh and metrics-store.
- quantization-profiles catalog: QSFS reads canonical quant recipes; results write back suggested profile adjustments.
- regression-triage: RHBs are posted to the regression queue with labels: quant-shadow, simulator, auto-rhb.

CLI examples

# Run a quick smoke sim against a small seed set
redwood-qsf simulate --profile q4f-default --seed-set small-core-100 --kv-cache-modeling approximate --temperature 0.0 --runcount 3 --out-dir /tmp/qsf/run-042

# Generate RHB and upload to triage queue
redwood-qsf package-rhb --in /tmp/qsf/run-042 --title "q4f-v2 smoke" --upload --notify applied-ml

Promotion checklist (pre-release gate)

1. QSFS run completed with rerun_count >= 3 for release-candidate seeds.
2. No metric breaches OR documented mitigations in RHB.
3. Mitigation verification run shows reduction in relevant signals by >= 50%.
4. RHB accepted by model owner and SRE.
5. Release coordination updated (if blocker_flag true, release blocked until root cause resolved).

Operational roles and SLAs

- QSFS owner: eval-harness team. Response SLA for triage requests: 24 business hours.
- Model owner: respond to RHB assignments with initial ack within 8 business hours.
- Applied-ML: investigative owner for hypotheses with reproducibility >= 0.7.

Failure modes and mitigation patterns (short list)

- Non-reproducible drift (low reproducibility score): increase rerun_count and switch kv_cache_modeling to exact-sim.
- Cryptic embedding drift: run embedding-level saliency probes and per-layer quant-activation histograms.
- Functioncall schema flips: add precision guard for decoder logits and widen functioncall-token threshold.

Appendix A — Example RHB snippet (human-readable)

{
  "title": "q4f-v2: rerank drift for billing prompts",
  "primary_signal": "token-mismatch-rate",
  "divergence": 0.083,
  "top_hypotheses": ["attention-scale-truncation","quantized-softmax-loss"],
  "suggested_mitigations": ["upgrade attention kernel to q8a for critical layers","apply softmax smoothing"]
}

Note: the actual RHB artifact is a structured JSON-LD object; the snippet above is for readability in this doc.

Related pages and references

- Quantization profile catalog and naming conventions: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024
- Shadow-to-prod continuity guidelines: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/shadow-to-prod-eval-continuity-guidelines-2026
- Regression triage playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026

Change history

- 2025-11-12: Draft created (Maya Patel).
- 2025-12-15: Incorporated Evan Chen feedback: added kv_cache_modeling modes.
- 2026-02-10: Published: added automated escalation rules and RHB schema (Sofia Ramos review).

Contact and feedback

For questions, suggested improvements, or to add a seed set to the QSFS catalog, open a ticket in the eval-harness board or DM @Maya.Patel on internal chat.

title: Annotation Credit Allocation and Entropy Stewardship Framework
content:
Overview

This document defines the Annotation Credit Allocation and Entropy Stewardship Framework: a policy and lightweight algorithm for (1) budgeting human annotation credits across probe classes, (2) prioritizing probes by information gain (entropy) relative to unit annotation cost, and (3) integrating these signals into the eval-harness scheduling and probe-rotation systems used by Redwood Inference evaluation teams.

Why this matters

- Annotation budgets are finite and shared across many eval initiatives (shadow validation, production-sampled sentinels, regression triage).
- Not all probes produce equal information: low-entropy probes rarely surface new failure modes but can consume substantial annotation dollars.
- Quantization, caching, and model variants change response distributions; we need an adaptive allocation that preserves coverage while minimizing annotation spend.

Goals and success criteria

- Increase per-dollar entropy captured (bits per USD) by 20% within the first quarter of rollout.
- Reduce annotation spend on low-yield probe classes by at least 30% while maintaining minimum coverage thresholds for critical slices.
- Ensure the eval-harness scheduler can enforce per-tenant credit allocations and emergency top-ups with minimal human intervention.

Principles

1) Entropy-first prioritization: prioritize probes ranked by expected information gain (entropy delta) normalized by annotation cost.
2) Minimum safety coverage: critical safety slices always reserve a fixed credit floor independent of entropy ranking.
3) Rotational freshness: include a percentage of low-entropy probes in every batch to detect distribution drift that entropy estimators may miss.
4) Transparency & auditability: every credit allocation decision is logged and inspectable; budgets and heuristics stored in the eval config.

Key definitions

- Probe: a single input sent through the eval-harness (synthetic or production-sampled).
- Entropy score: estimated Shannon entropy (or surrogate) of model responses for a probe family before annotation.
- Annotation credit: unit of human labeling budget; configurable per-label type (binary, multi-class, multi-annotator).
- Cost per credit: USD-equivalent based on vendor rates and internal labor overhead.

Metrics tracked

- BitsPerDollar: total estimated information gain (bits) collected divided by USD spent on annotation.
- YieldRate: fraction of annotated probes that triggered new actionable findings (regression, safety alert, calibration failure).
- CoverageFraction: percent of critical slices that have at least N annotated probes in 30-day window.
- DriftSignalRate: rate of probes where entropy estimator disagreed with human labels by >threshold (used to tune estimator).

Allocation algorithm (operational procedure)

1) Daily probe cataloging:
   - The eval-harness aggregates candidate probes into families and computes a running EntropyEstimate for each family. EntropyEstimate uses a lightweight ensemble of predictive models (softmax entropy, edit-distance diversity, and embedding-dispersion).
2) Cost normalization:
   - Map label types to CreditUnit and USD cost (example: binary=1 credit=$0.60, 3r consensus multi-class=3 credits=$2.10).
3) Priority score computation:
   - For each family: Priority = (EntropyEstimate * FamilyWeight) / ExpectedCostPerProbe. FamilyWeight encodes product impact, regulatory sensitivity, and SLA exposure (see table below).
4) Apply hard floors and ceilings:
   - Reserve CriticalFloor credits: all families with label 'safety' or 'regulatory' get at least 5% of total daily credits.
   - Cap per-family spend to MaxPercent (default 20%) unless emergency flagged.
5) Sampling and rotation:
   - Select probes for annotation by sampling in proportion to Priority, but inject RotationLowEntropyFraction (default 10%) of low-priority families uniformly to maintain freshness.
6) Dispatch and logging:
   - Send selected probes to annotation backend with metadata and expected adjudication policy. Write allocation decisions to the probe-allocation ledger (timestamp, family_id, priority_score, credits_allocated, owner).

Table: default family weights and thresholds (example)

| Family label     | FamilyWeight | Critical? | Minimum daily credits | Notes |
|------------------|--------------|-----------|-----------------------|-------|
| safety           | 3.0          | yes       | 50                    | Regulatory and user-safety slices |
| user-facing      | 1.2          | no        | 20                    | High product exposure |
| backend-parser   | 0.8          | no        | 10                    | Non-critical but useful |
| long-context     | 1.5          | no        | 15                    | Historically high entropy |
| rare-edge        | 1.8          | yes       | 25                    | Low frequency but high impact |

Embedding the framework in eval-harness

- Config integration: add a new top-level field in eval-recipe YAML: annotation_allocation:
  - total_daily_credits: int
  - rotation_low_entropy_fraction: float
  - critical_floor_percent: float
  - family_weights: map
  - cost_map: map

Example YAML snippet:

annotation_allocation:
  total_daily_credits: 2000
  rotation_low_entropy_fraction: 0.10
  critical_floor_percent: 0.05
  family_weights:
    safety: 3.0
    user-facing: 1.2
    backend-parser: 0.8
    long-context: 1.5
    rare-edge: 1.8
  cost_map:
    binary: 0.6
    multi_class_3: 2.1
    multi_annotator_consensus: 3.5

Operational runbook: emergency top-up and regression triage

1) Trigger: regression triage or P1 production incident requires immediate re-labeling of a suspect probe family.
2) Immediate action:
   - Owner toggles emergency_flag for family_id in eval console. This bypasses MaxPercent cap and bumps FamilyWeight to EmergencyWeight (default 10x).
   - System allocates EmergencyCredits from a reserved pool (configurable).
3) Post-mortem allocation reconciliation:
   - Annotators' spend is reconciled to real budget. If reserve used, product manager reviews the spend and approves rebalancing of future daily credits.

Integration with quantization profiles and model variants

- When a model variant or quant-profile is promoted to staging, run a CalibrationSweep: sample N probes from top-priority families and recompute EntropyEstimate under the variant. If BitsPerDollar drops below VariantThreshold, flag for extended human review and delay rollout.
- For quantized models that reduce response diversity, the EntropyEstimate should include kernel-aware priors (we store a small per-model variance multiplier in the model catalog).

Telemetry and dashboards

Expose the following dashboards in the eval console:
- BitsPerDollar over time (by family, by model variant)
- AnnotationSpend vs Budget (rolling 7d)
- CoverageFraction heatmap (slices x tenants)
- DriftSignalRate and top families with estimator-human disagreement

Ownership and teams

- Document owner: Aisha Patel (Applied ML)
- Primary implementer: Eval-harness team (eng-applied-ml)
- Annotation operations: DataOps / LabelOps
- Product stakeholder: Feature reliability PMs

Rollout plan (phased)

1) Pilot (2 weeks): enable for 3 families (safety, long-context, user-facing) with a 10% of annotation volume and manual review of allocations.
2) Beta (6 weeks): expand to 25% of families and integrate with annotation backend automatic dispatch. Measure BitsPerDollar and YieldRate.
3) GA (quarterly cadence): full rollout with SLOs on BitsPerDollar and CoverageFraction and automated emergency top-ups.

Audit and governance

- Ledger retention: allocation ledger retained 2 years.
- Monthly review: AnnotationOps and Applied ML review allocation patterns and update family_weights if needed.
- Approval process: any change to CriticalFloor or EmergencyReserve requires sign-off from Product Reliability and Security.

Appendix: sample SQL for BitsPerDollar calculation

-- pseudocode SQL (for analytics team)
SELECT
  family_id,
  SUM(entropy_bits) as total_bits,
  SUM(usd_cost) as total_usd,
  CASE WHEN SUM(usd_cost) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(entropy_bits)/SUM(usd_cost) END as bits_per_dollar
FROM probe_annotation_results
WHERE annotated_at >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 30 DAY)
GROUP BY family_id
ORDER BY bits_per_dollar DESC;

Notes, known limitations, and future work

- Entropy estimates are approximations; early tuning required per-family. Track DriftSignalRate closely during the pilot.
- This framework assumes stable annotation unit costs; vendor churn can invalidate thresholds quickly.
- Future: integrate active learning models for per-probe annotation decisioning and experiment with variable consensus (dynamic annotator counts) to further optimize cost-per-bit.

Related pages and links

- Probe telemetry compression and scheduling (see: ../eval-harness/probe-telemetry-compression-scheduling-playbook-2026).
- Probe curation and annotation charter (see: ../prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/probe-curation-stewardship-and-annotation-charter-2026).

Revision history

- 2025-11-04: Drafted by Aisha Patel.
- 2025-12-10: Pilot config examples added; reviewers Jonah Kim and Mariana Lopez.
- 2026-02-18: Updated with emergency top-up workflow and SQL; published.

title: Promotion Readiness: Cross-Stage Synthetic Simulation & Quantization Safety Playbook
content:
Summary

This playbook defines a combined evaluation and safety protocol used to decide when a model artifact can be promoted from evaluation (canary/validation) into production routing. It coordinates three corridors of checks: 1) synthetic user simulation to validate behavioral and distributional stability, 2) quantization & kernel-sensitivity safety checks for performance-preserving transforms, and 3) lightweight runtime smoke and canary procedures to exercise operational invariants. The goal is deterministic, reproducible promotion decisions tied to explicit pass/fail signals and rollback criteria.

Scope and Use Cases

- Applies to any model promotion that will be served by Redwood runtime variants where quantized or variant kernels (FP16/INT8/QLoRA-style) are in the promotion path.
- Intended for models with expected production throughput above 1 qps/customer or with regulatory/data-sensitivity constraints (customer PII handling).
- Not required for experimental sandbox promotions under 24h unless flagged by product as critical.

Definitions

- Promotion: the act of moving a model from staging/canary to a production route where customer traffic is served.
- Synthetic Actor: a deterministic user-simulation profile used to exercise prompts and contexts representative of production usage.
- Quant Safety Check: a set of deterministic tests that validate output fidelity and KV-cache integrity across quantized kernels.

Ownership and Roles

- Model Owner (primary): ML engineer who produced the model artifact and is responsible for test bundles, prompt sets, and baseline metrics.
- Eval Owner: engineering squad responsible for running the synthetic actor harness and interpreting results.
- Runtime Owner: infra/runtime team responsible for quantization tooling, kernel selection, and performance baselining.
- Release Approver: product or platform PM with final sign-off for non-emergency promotions.

Acceptance Criteria (summary table)

- For each criterion below the format is: Criterion | Pass Threshold | Primary Signal | Escalation
  - Behavioral stability | Delta <= 1.5% on core pass-rate metrics across prompt-slices | aggregate pass-rate time series (7k sample window) | Auto-fail -> regression-triage
  - Semantic drift | Embedding cosine shift < 0.06 median across intent clusters | embedding distribution KL (staging vs baseline) | Review required
  - Exact-match integrity for CI prompts | 100% for deterministic QA prompts | golden-answer diff report | Auto-fail
  - Quantized fidelity | Top-1 response similarity >= 95% (ROUGE-L or BLEU for fixed tasks), and human-annotated quality delta <= 0.5 on sampled prompts | batch-diff + human spot-check | Rollback & quant-retry
  - KV-cache parity | no cache corruption observed in 10k simulated long-context requests | kernel log parity + checksum | Runtime rollback
  - Latency and tail | p99 < target_latency and p99_tail_spikes < 10% over baseline | telemetry time-series | Canary throttling

Design: Synthetic Actor Harness

- Purpose: emulate real user behavior without shipping customer data. Synthetic actors combine prompt skeletons, variable slot content generators, and timing distributions.
- Actors are stored as JSON bundles: {actor_id, intent_weight, prompt_templates[], context_length_dist, slot_generators[]}. Example actor fragment below.

Example actor JSON (representative):

{
  "actor_id": "support_search_v2",
  "intent_weight": "0.18",
  "prompt_templates": [
    "User: {{query}}\nAssistant:",
    "Given the following product description: {{desc}}\nSummarize:"
  ],
  "context_length_dist": "poisson(λ=64)",
  "slot_generators": ["wiki-snippet-sampler", "customer-nounizer-v2"]
}

- Scenario catalog (must cover):
  1) Short-form Q&A (<=64 tokens) - 40% weight.
  2) Long-context summarization (>=1024 tokens) - 25% weight.
  3) Multi-step instruction with tool-calls emulation - 10% weight.
  4) Edge adversarial variants (typos, hallucination probes) - 15% weight.
  5) Rare-entity and numeric reasoning - 10% weight.

- Execution: run 3 independent seeds per actor with deterministic RNG to allow diffs. Collect full traces including prompt, logits (sample), KV-cache checksums, and returned tokens. Store artifacts in the eval artifact bucket with the tag: promotion/<model>:<sha>.

Quantization & Kernel Safety Checks

- Purpose: verify that quant transforms and kernel selections do not induce unacceptable semantic/functional regressions.
- Automated checks:
  - Layer-wise output delta: run a 500-sample micro-batch and compute per-layer L2 and cosine delta vs baseline FP32. Thresholds: median L2 < 1e-3, cosine > 0.999.
  - End-to-end behavioral delta: use the synthetic actor prompt set, compute pass-rate deltas and embedding shifts.
  - KV-cache replay: for long-context runs, serialize and replay KV-cache through quantized kernels and validate checksums.
  - Failure-mode detector: fuzz a subset of kernels with perturbed inputs to detect NaNs/inf or divergence outliers.

- Tooling commands (example):
  - Quant bake: 
    redwood-quant bake --model model.tgz --profile int8-s90 --output quantized/model-int8.tgz
  - Layer compare: 
    redwood-compare-layers --base model_fp32 --candidate model_int8 --samples 500 --out report.html

Runtime Smoke Test Suite

- Purpose: exercise operational invariants (metrics, logs, tracing) before opening production traffic.
- Keys:
  - Load profile: synthetic actors at 1x, 5x expected qps for 10 minutes each.
  - Observability checks: ensure traces propagate, token-level billing counters accurate, request IDs preserved.
  - Telemetry asserts: no more than 0.2% errors, p95 latency regression < 10% of baseline.

Canary Promotion Procedure (numbered)

1) Artifact upload: Model owner uploads artifact, test bundles, and promotion metadata to the staging registry.
2) Preflight: CI runs unit tests, deterministic QA prompts, and the synthetic actor harness end-to-end. Reject on auto-fail signals.
3) Quant safety pass: Runtime Owner runs quant checks and signs off or files quant-issue ticket.
4) Smoke run: Deploy to isolated canary pool (1% traffic) with synthetic traffic overlay and 30m observation window.
5) Rollout phases: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% by automated policy, each stage gated by acceptance criteria evaluation window (30m for small models, 60m for L>8k contexts).
6) Monitoring guardrails: automated rollback triggers include: behavioral stability fail, KV-cache parity fail, p99 latency > threshold, or error rate spike > configured delta.
7) Post-promotion audit: collect artifacts, diff reports, and human spot-check on 200 sampled prompts.

Automated Alerting and Rollback Rules

- Alert channels: PagerDuty to Runtime on severity=1 (KV-cache corruption), Slack #runtime-ops for severity=2, email to model-owner for degraded quality signals.
- Auto-rollback thresholds (examples):
  - Behavioral pass-rate drop >= 2% absolute in sliding 10m window -> automatic rollback.
  - KV-cache checksum mismatch (any) during canary -> immediate rollback and incident start.
  - p99 latency > baseline_p99 * 1.5 for 10 minutes -> gradual throttle and rollback if persists.

Data and Artifact Retention

- All synthetic-run artifacts and diff reports for a promotion must be retained for 90 days under eval-artifacts/<model>/<sha> with TTL tags.
- Human annotation records from the spot-check should be stored with reviewer id and comments.

Failure & Triage Process

- If automated checks fail, create a regression ticket with: title, failing signals, links to artifacts, investigator assignment. Use label: regressions/promotion.
- Regression triage steps:
  1) Reproduce in isolated environment (runtime owner + model owner).
  2) Run layer-diff and kernel-fuzz tests.
  3) If quant-related, attempt quant-profile fallback (e.g., int8->int8-s95 or int16) and re-run harness.
  4) If behavioral, escalate to applied-ml for annotation and root-cause.

Auditability & Sign-off

- Each successful promotion must include the following artifacts in the promotion ticket: artifact SHA, synthetic-run summary report, quant-compare report, smoke-run telemetry snapshot, human spot-check results, release approver signature.
- The Release Approver records the promotion decision and any exceptions in the promotion ticket.

Appendix: Example Eval Command Sequence

1) Bake quant candidate
   redwood-quant bake --model s3://models/foo/sha.tgz --profile int8-s90 --output /tmp/foo-int8.tgz
2) Run harness
   redwood-eval run --actors actors/catalog.json --model /tmp/foo-int8.tgz --out artifacts/foo/sha --seeds 3
3) Layer compare
   redwood-compare-layers --base s3://models/foo/fp32 --candidate /tmp/foo-int8.tgz --samples 500 --out artifacts/foo/layer-report.html

Appendix: Minimum Required Test Bundle (table-like list)

- Deterministic QA prompts: 1k prompts (must include golden answers).
- Actor prompt set: 10k produced prompts across actor catalog.
- Long-context replay corpus: 2k sequences >= 3k tokens each.
- Kernel fuzz harness: 5000 micro-batches designed to expose NaNs/inf.
- Human spot-check: 200 prompts sampled from failing/edge slices.

References and Links

- See: ../model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026.json for baseline promotion policies.
- See: ../quantization-profiles/kv-cache-quant-stability-audit-playbook-2025.json for detailed KV-cache checks.

Notes and Rationale

- Combining synthetic actors with deterministic quant checks reduces dependence on scarce human annotation while still surfacing high-risk regressions. The thresholds above were chosen based on historical regressions observed in Q1–Q3 2025 where early quantized promotions without KV checks produced silent corruption in long-context flows.

Contact

- Primary: Ava Chen (Model Owner liaison) — ava.chen@redwood.ai
- Runtime on-call: see #runtime-oncall rota

Change log

- 2026-02-10: Initial draft.
- 2026-02-17: Added quant-fuzz details and example commands (reviewer: Priya Kapoor).
- 2026-03-01: Updated acceptance thresholds and canary windows after cross-team review (reviewers: Diego Martinez, Liam O'Neill).

title: Evaluator Onboarding and Certification Curriculum - 2026
content:
Purpose

This page defines the official Redwood Evaluation Team curriculum for onboarding, certifying, and re-certifying evaluators who operate the eval harness, curate prompt/probe suites, and run shadow/federated experiments across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. The curriculum is designed to: 1) shorten time-to-productivity, 2) reduce annotation and probe creation variance, 3) ensure consistent use of quantification and regression triage tools, and 4) codify the certification gates that allow an evaluator to approve production shadow runs.

Audience

- New evaluators joining the Applied ML group.
- ML engineers responsible for shadow validation and probe orchestration.
- Cross-functional reviewers (SRE/product) who sign off on production gating.

Overview and outcomes

At the end of the curriculum, an evaluator will be able to:
- Operate the Eval Harness CLI and submit reproducible probe runs (eval-mesh).
- Compose probe families that cover calibration, drift, long-tail, and quant-sensitivity slices.
- Run a shadow-to-prod migration with the Probe Migration Checklist and pass the certification exam.
- Diagnose regressions using the Regression Investigation Playbook and bootstrap a quant-fallback experiment.

Structure

The curriculum has three phased tracks that must be completed in sequence:

1) Foundations (2 weeks) — orientation, tooling, safety basics
2) Applied Labs (3 weeks) — hands-on probe design, shadow runs, annotation calibration
3) Certification and Audit (1 week) — exam, live run approval, pairing audit

Each phase contains lectures, reading, a set of hands-on tasks, and acceptance criteria. Evaluators are paired with a "steward" (senior evaluator) for at least one full shadow lifecycle.

Phase 1: Foundations (2 weeks)

Goal: Ensure the evaluator understands the platform, core telemetry, and quality guardrails.

Mandatory reading and videos:
- "Eval Harness Primer" (internal video, 35m)
- "Quality Guardrails: SQC mapping" (doc)
- "KV-cache behavior and quant sensitivity" (paper summary)

Access & setup checklist:
1. Request access to eval-mesh and probe-fabricator via internal ticket (Tool-Access-202).
2. Verify RBAC: membership in group redwood-evaluators and read access to eval-telemetry.
3. Complete online safety course (security-and-compliance/module-eval-safety).

Local environment quickstart (required):
- Install evaluator-cli: pip install redwood-evaluator-cli==0.6.1
- Configure credentials: evaluator configure --profile sandbox --region us-west-2
- Run a smoke probe: evaluator run --probe-id sample/smoke-001 --mode dry-run

Acceptance criteria (foundations):
- Can run a dry-run without errors and retrieve telemetry IDs.
- Pass a short quiz (min score 80%) covering SLOs, confidentiality rules, and probe privacy budget.

Phase 2: Applied Labs (3 weeks)

Goal: Practice probe authoring, slice definition, annotation calibration, and shadow execution across quantized and unquantized model variants.

Core modules and exercises:
A. Probe Design Lab (3 exercises)
- Exercise 1: Build a calibration probe family for the "fewshot-summarization" workflow. Deliverables: JSON probe manifest, expected anchors, and acceptance tests.
- Exercise 2: Create a long-context cohesion probe that stresses KV cache boundaries. Deliverables: token-length distribution, expected failure modes, and a seed corpus.
- Exercise 3: Design a perturbation probe to surface quant-induced hallucination modes. Deliverables: perturbation matrix and repair template.

B. Annotation Calibration & Economics (2 exercises)
- Calibrate three annotators using the Annotator Calibration Toolkit. Target inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff alpha) >= 0.75 for high-signal slices.
- Run an annotation budget exercise: plan cost for 5k judgments across three slices and optimize for efficiency (heuristic: prioritize high-impact seeds).

C. Shadow Run Execution (live pairing with steward)
- Perform an end-to-end shadow run against model family: rwin-13b (float16), rwin-13b-q4 (quant), and rwin-7b (fallback).
- Follow the Shadow Run Checklist (see table below) while steward pairs for run sign-off.

Shadow Run Checklist (table)

| Step | Responsible | Artifact | Threshold/Notes |
