|------|-------------|----------|-----------------|
| Probe manifest review | Evaluator + Steward | manifest.yaml | All probes have anchor coverage >= 90% |
| Dry-run verification | Evaluator | smoke logs | No runtime errors; 95th latency < 1.2x baseline |
| Annotation plan approved | Evaluator | annotation-plan.md | Annotator QA plan included; privacy budget specified |
| Metric contract set | Evaluator | eval-contract.json | Primary metric and delta budget defined (see Metric Contracts) |
| Run approval | Steward | run-id | Steward signs after drift/fidelity checks |

Metric Contracts (example)
- Primary metric: Response Coherence (rc_score) computed by evaluator-metrics v1.4
- Acceptance gate: rc_score delta >= -0.015 relative to baseline OR pass compensating slice checks
- Latency SLO: p95 infer latency <= 240ms for 128-token average length on dedicated pool

Commands and example manifests

Example manifest manifest.yaml (snippet):

```
probe_family: summarization_calibration_v2
model_targets:
  - rwin-13b
  - rwin-13b-q4
slices:
  - name: anchor_examples
    seed_source: corpus/summaries/anchor-2025
    expected_pass_rate: 0.92
  - name: long_context_priming
    seed_source: corpus/long/slice-a
    expected_pass_rate: 0.88
```

Run command (example):
- evaluator run --manifest manifest.yaml --priority normal --dry-run=false --telemetry-tag evaluator/onboarding/$(whoami)

Acceptance criteria (applied labs):
- Manifest and probe families reviewed by steward.
- Shadow runs produced telemetry and produced pass/fail slices as predicted for >= 3 of 4 probes.
- Annotator calibration passes (alpha >= 0.75) for primary slices.

Phase 3: Certification and Audit (1 week)

Goal: Demonstrate independent run ownership and the ability to approve a shadow run for promotion to canary stage.

Components:
1) Written exam (open book) — 60 minutes, passing score 85%. Topics: metric contract writing, privacy budget, probe manifest conventions, rollback criteria.
2) Practical exam — run ownership: the candidate must design and execute a configuration that flips on a new quantized variant via the staging mesh and demonstrate the ability to trigger a safe rollback.
3) Audit pairing — candidate does a live run while a cross-team reviewer (SRE or Product) monitors.

Practical exam rubric (summary):
- Correctness of probe manifests: 30 pts
- Metric contract defensibility and thresholds: 25 pts
- Annotation pipeline and QA: 20 pts
- Rollback and mitigation plan: 25 pts
- Passing threshold: >= 80/100

Certification outcomes and badges
- Certified Evaluator — full sign-off: allowed to approve shadow runs for canary (limited to one model family until first three live canaries are monitored). Badge granted in HR profile and redwood-evaluators group.
- Provisional Evaluator — passed practical but needs two additional steward-signed runs to be upgraded.

Re-certification and continuing education (annual)
- All certified evaluators must re-certify yearly by: 1) completing a 4-hour update on new tooling/metrics, and 2) passing a short practical re-cert exercise.
- If a major change (e.g., new quant scheme, new KV cache architecture) is introduced, temporary re-cert drives may be required: stewards will notify via #eval-ops.

Operational integrants and run governance

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: Applied ML — Eval Team (owner_team: engineering)
- Steward role: senior evaluator assigned per-model-family; contact via steward-oncall rotation
- Escalation path: evaluator -> steward -> model-owner -> SRE -> oncall-exec

Approval gates for promotion to production canary:
1. Metric contract satisfied within delta budgets.
2. No high-severity slice failures (severity defined in Failure Taxonomy doc).
3. Annotation QA completed and auditable.
4. SRE performance smoke tests passed (p95 latency within agreed SLA).

Tooling references and troubleshooting

- evaluator-cli docs: internal link /tools/evaluator-cli (version 0.6+ required)
- eval-mesh run logs: run logs available in Kibana under index eval-mesh-logs-*
- Telemetry quick query (example):
  curl -s "https://telemetry-api.internal/v1/query" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"run_id":"<RUN_ID>","metrics":["rc_score","latency_p95"]}' | jq

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Symptom: p95 latency spike in quant variant
  Mitigation: trigger fallback to non-quant variant and file a performance incident; capture runtime kernels and attach to triage ticket.
- Symptom: Annotator drift (Krippendorff alpha < 0.6)
  Mitigation: pause annotation, recalibrate annotators using gold set, re-run sample.
- Symptom: Metric contract violation on minority slice
  Mitigation: Evaluate slice-specific compensating checks; if multiple high-priority slices fail, rollback.

Appendix A — Suggested onboarding schedule (4-week calendar)

Week 0: Pre-boarding
- Access requests, install CLI, watch primer video.
Week 1: Foundations
- Read docs, pass quiz, complete dry-run.
Week 2: Probe design exercises (pairing begins)
Week 3: Shadow runs, annotation calibration (steward pairing)
Week 4: Exam week, certification practical and audit, final sign-off

Appendix B — Minimum telemetry and artifacts retained for audits

- Probe manifest (manifest.yaml) — retained indefinitely in repo eval-manifests
- Run logs and telemetry snapshots — retention 180 days for certified runs; compressed snapshot stored 2 years for canary promotions
- Annotation samples and gold sets — retention 2 years, redacted of user PII where applicable

Appendix C — Quick reference: Metric contract template (eval-contract.json)

```
{
  "metric": "rc_score",
  "baseline_model": "rwin-13b",
  "delta_budget": -0.015,
  "slice_overrides": {
    "long_context_priming": -0.02
  },
  "latency_p95_ms": 240
}
```

Contacts and next steps

- Curriculum owner: Sana Malik (Applied ML) — sana@redwood.ai
- Steward coordinator: Diego Ferns — diego@redwood.ai
- To enroll: create a ticket in TEAM-TRAINING queue with subject "Eval Onboarding Enrollment".

Revision history
- 2025-09-15: Created by Sana Malik (foundations and lab design)
- 2025-11-02: Added quant-sensitivity probe exercises (Lina Zhou)
- 2026-01-12: Finalized certification rubric and retention policy (Diego Ferns review)

End of document

title: Entropy-driven probe generation and prioritization playbook
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes an entropy-driven workflow for generating, scoring, prioritizing, and sampling evaluation probes (short input prompts, dialog seeds, or workload traces) using live telemetry signals. The approach is designed to surface rare or unstable behaviors while balancing evaluation cost and annotation bandwidth. Use this playbook when you need continuous, targeted coverage of model failure modes, drifting slices, or capacity-sensitive corners of production traffic.

Goals:
- Discover high-utility probes from production telemetry with minimal human effort.
- Prioritize probes that maximize information about model regressions (quality delta), quantization sensitivity, and latency anomalies.
- Provide deterministic scoring and an auditable pipeline from telemetry to evaluator-runbooks.

When to use this playbook:
- Integrating new model variants into Dedicated/Private canaries.
- Creating targeted prompt sets to stress quantized variants or KV-cache behavior.
- Triaging intermittent production regressions where labeled examples are scarce.

Definitions and components:
- Probe: A single input example (prompt + metadata) used in an eval job.
- Probe Farm: service name "probe-farm" (k8s: namespace eval-tools) that stores candidate probes in ClickHouse (table: probes.catalog).
- Eval Orchestrator: "eval-orchestrator" that schedules evaluator-sdk jobs and reports results to the eval-metrics topic in Kafka.
- Telemetry signals: metrics and logs sourced from prod (Prometheus, traces, and structured logs forwarded to ClickHouse/Clickhouse-materialized views).

Signal taxonomy and mapping (table):
| Signal name             | Source         | Frequency | Interpretation                                      | Weight (default) |
|-------------------------|----------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| token-error-rate        | eval-metrics   | 1m        | Token-level hallucination/safety sentinel hits     | 0.30             |
| response-entropy        | probes.agg     | 5m        | High entropy = diverse/confused outputs            | 0.20             |
| lat99                  | prometheus     | 1m        | 99th percentile latency for model route            | 0.10             |
| kv-cache-miss-rate      | prod-kv-metrics| 1m        | Cold starts and cache eviction sensitivity         | 0.10             |
| user-friction-score     | product-telemetry | realtime| Product-derived signal (errors, retries, cancels)  | 0.20             |
| annotation-gap-score    | probe-farm     | on-demand | Low historical labels for this workload slice      | 0.10             |

Scoring and prioritization algorithm (high level):
1) Candidate extraction: pull candidate inputs from prod trace windows using producers: structured-log extractor, trace-sampler, and request-diff job. Default window: last 72 hours. Query examples:
   - ClickHouse: SELECT request_id, prompt, session_id, route, model FROM prod.requests WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 72 hour AND route IN ('chat', 'completion') AND tokens > 8 LIMIT 200000;
2) Enrich candidates: join telemetry signals (token-error-rate, response-entropy, lat99, kv-cache-miss-rate, user-friction-score) into the candidate row.
3) Compute raw priority score:
   priority_raw = sum(w_i * normalized(signal_i)) - penalty(privacy, pii, customer_sensitive)
   where normalized(signal_i) uses rolling 7-day z-score bounded to [0,1].
4) Diversity adjustment: apply an embedding-based de-duplication (service: probe-farm/embed-index) that attenuates score for near-duplicates within the last 30 days using cosine similarity threshold 0.85.
5) Cost gating: apply heuristics to limit high-cost probes (length > 4096 tokens or multimodal attachments) unless explicitly labeled as high-priority.
6) Final priority buckets: HOT (top 0.5%), WARM (0.5%-5%), COLD (remaining).

Sampling and resampling policy:
- HOT probes: sample 100% into nightly evaluator runs (priority queue). Annotate with reason codes (e.g., TOKEN_ERR_SPIKE, HIGH_ENTROPY, KV_EVICT).
- WARM probes: sample 5% daily with stratified sampling across routes and customers (by tenant-hash).
- COLD probes: reservoir sample 0.05% weekly for long-tail drift detection.
- Resampling rule: if HOT probe receives a failing eval result (quality delta > regression threshold), clone and expand neighborhood by retrieving 50 nearest embedding neighbors and promote top-10 by rescored priority.

Annotation schema and labeling contract:
- label: {"category": string, "severity": one of [critical, major, minor], "notes": string, "annotator": string, "timestamp": ISO8601}
- Required fields: category, severity, annotator. Optional: customer_consent_id if sample contains customer-provided content.
- Labeler SLA: initial triage within 48h for HOT probes; 7 days for WARM. Use the "annotate-probe" internal UI (path: /tools/probe-annotator).

Privacy and safety gating:
- PII detection: run pii-scanner (lambda) at extraction time. Any probe with PII flag set must be redacted or moved to restricted bucket and requires security review (owner_team: security).
- Customer-sensitive sampling: probes tagged tenant_sensitive are only eligible for Private/Dedicated shadow evals when customer opt-in exists.

Integration with eval harness and CI/CD:
- Eval job naming: entropy-probe-YYYYMMDD-{bucket}
- Example CI trigger (GitOps):
  curl -X POST "https://eval-orchestrator.internal/api/v1/run" -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_TOKEN" -d '{"job": "entropy-probe-20260212-HOT", "model": "rwd-1.3-quantized-v2", "probe_source": "probe-farm:HOT"}'
- Result consumer: eval-orchestrator writes to Kafka topic eval-results; a consumer (eval-ingest) populates eval-results.clickhouse and alerts via ops-alerts when regression_count >= 3 for a model variant.

Canary gating and rollout policy (recommended):
1) Run nightly HOT evals against both float and quantized candidates.
2) If a critical category regression is detected (delta > 0.08 in task-level accuracy or safety-sentinel spike > 2x baseline), block canary rollout and trigger regression triage playbook (see related pages).
3) For non-critical but actionable regressions, schedule a focused micro-canary (2k qps shadow) and run expanded probe neighborhoods.

Operational runbook (incident-light):
- Owner: applied-ml/evals team oncall (primary: @applied-evals)
- If probe pipeline stops producing HOT candidates for >24h:
  1. Check probe-farm deployment status: kubectl -n eval-tools get pods -l app=probe-farm
  2. Validate ClickHouse connectivity and recent ingestion: SELECT count(*) FROM probes.catalog WHERE created_at >= now() - INTERVAL 1 hour;
  3. Check telemetry ingestion: kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group telemetry-collector
- If scoring anomalies (scores all zero): check z-score windowing job (cron: score-normalizer) and restart: kubectl -n eval-tools rollout restart deployment/score-normalizer

Metrics, SLOs and dashboards:
- Metric: HOT probe discovery rate — SLI target: 1000 HOT candidates/day (SLO: 95% monthly).
- Metric: annotation turnaround for HOT probes — SLO: 48h 95th percentile.
- Metric: regression detection lag — time from first failing prod example to HOT promotion — SLO: < 24h 90th percentile.
- Dashboards: Grafana dashboard id: eval-entropy-001 (panels for signal distribution, HOT arrival rate, and annotation backlog).

Example JSON candidate (stored in probes.catalog):
{
  "probe_id": "pf-20260212-000123",
  "prompt": "Write a short explanation of differential privacy in simple terms.",
  "route": "completion",
  "tokens": "48",
  "response_entropy": "0.88",
  "token_error_rate": "0.032",
  "kv_cache_miss": "0.12",
  "priority_raw": "0.78",
  "priority_bucket": "HOT",
  "extraction_window": "2026-02-12T03:14:00Z"
}

FAQ (short):
Q: How do we avoid overfitting probes that repeatedly fail for the same annotate pattern?
A: We decay priority for probes that have stable failing labels beyond a half-life of 21 days and upweight neighbors instead.

Q: Can product teams request targeted probes?
A: Yes. Submit to /tools/probe-requests with tenant, route, and rationale. Requests are treated as manual HOT promotions after security review.

Ownership and contact:
- Primary owner: applied-ml-and-evals
- Secondary: eng-serving-runtime (integration for kv-cache signals)
- Oncall alias: ops-evals@redwood.ai

Related pages:
- /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-orchestrator-integration-spec-2025
- /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/kv-cache-quant-stability-audit-playbook-2025

Revision history:
- 2025-10-03: created by Marisol Alvarez
- 2026-02-12: updated scoring normalization and added cost gating (Marisol Alvarez)

End of document.

title: Slice Drift Sentinel and Quant Hedging Playbook
content:
Overview

This playbook describes the Slice Drift Sentinel system and the Quant Hedging policy used across Redwood's eval harness to maintain user-visible fidelity while maximizing cost savings from quantized deployments. It covers detection signals, thresholds, automated hedging (fallback) rules, how to allocate cost 'shields' to high-risk slices, and the operational runbook for regression triage and rollback.

Motivation

- Quantized model variants decrease serving cost but occasionally produce regressions that are slice-specific (e.g., domain jargon, long context).
- We need automated, explainable controls to detect quality shifts at slice granularity and to migrate affected traffic to higher-fidelity variants with minimal manual intervention.
- The sentinel also provides cost accounting so product teams can accept controlled quality trade-offs.

Scope

Applies to: hosted and dedicated inference fleets, hybrid private deployments where telemetry is available.
Not covered: full retraining workflows, human annotation pipelines (see related pages).

Key concepts

- Slice: a workload partition (intent, tenant cohort, locale, prompt family) defined in the probe registry.
- Sentinel score: a composite signal combining fidelity delta, confidence calibration shift, and embedding drift (0-100).
- Quant hedging: automated rule set that routes a percentage of slice traffic to a higher-precision variant when sentinel score exceeds thresholds.
- Cost shield: per-slice budget to allow temporary hedging without blowing team-level cost targets.

Telemetry and metrics

Primary metrics (per slice, computed hourly):
- fidelity_delta_pct: relative drop in oracle-aligned metric (e.g., BLEU/QA-F1/Instruction-adherence) vs baseline (rolling 7d).
- topk_confidence_shift: change in average model token confidence or logit gap.
- embedding_drift_cosine: mean cosine distance between recent embeddings and baseline centroid.
- user_apdex_change: change in product Apdex correlated with quality signals.
- hedged_traffic_pct: percent of slice routed to higher fidelity.

Detection algorithm (high level)

1. Compute normalized z-scores for fidelity_delta_pct, confidence_shift, embedding_drift using slice historical window (90th percentile to reduce noise).
2. Sentinel score = weighted sum: 0.5*fidelity_z + 0.3*confidence_z + 0.2*embedding_z, clipped to 0-100.
3. Apply hysteresis: require sentinel score > threshold for 3 consecutive hourly bins before triggering hedging.
4. Raise severity levels: informational (20), guarded (40), hedging (60), immediate rollback (85).

Quant Hedging Policy (config example)

policy_name: slice_quant_hedge_v1
priority: high
thresholds:
  informational: 20
  guarded: 40
  hedging: 60
  rollback: 85
actions:
  guarded: notify-steward, increase-probe-frequency
  hedging: route-percent: 25; 50; 100 by step; duration: 2h-auto-evaluate
  rollback: immediate-shift-to-fp16, open-incident
cost_shield:
  default_monthly_credits_usd: 1500
  per_slice_max_pct_of_shield: 20
  auto-replenish_policy: manual

Policy semantics

- Hedging ramps are conservative: start with 25% traffic to higher-fidelity for 2 hours, evaluate fidelity_delta and user_apdex; if improved, escalate to 50% then 100%.
- Shielding prevents unlimited hedging: when a slice's cumulative hedging cost exceeds its allocated shield, the policy falls back to alert-only and requires steward approval.

Cost accounting model (table)

Slice metric | baseline cost/token | hedged cost/token | expected monthly delta
--- | ---: | ---: | ---:
default-chat | 0.0012 | 0.0025 | +$320
enterprise-forms | 0.0020 | 0.0040 | +$1,200
longcontext-recalls | 0.0009 | 0.0021 | +$480

Onboarding checklist for a new slice

1. Register slice in probe registry with owner, intent, and canonical prompt set.
2. Define baseline (rolling 14d) fidelity metric and target SLO.
3. Assign cost shield and steward approver.
4. Enable sentinel telemetry and probe frequency (default: 60 probes/hour).
5. Run synthetic shadow evaluation for 48 hours to collect initial embedding centroid.
6. Approve policy (slice_quant_hedge_v1) or provide overrides.

Runbook: when sentinel reports hedging trigger

1. Alerting: PagerDuty notify to slice steward, include sentinel diagnostics link and current metrics.
2. Triage steps (ordered):
   a. Review probe examples that contributed most to fidelity_delta (top 10 failing probes).
   b. Check config diff: model variant, tokenization, prompt-presets, quant profile.
   c. Inspect runtime errors and kernel fallbacks in last 2 hours.
   d. If hedging succeeded (fidelity_delta reduced by >= 40%), keep hedging and reduce probe aggressiveness after 12h.
   e. If no improvement, escalate to model-onboarding team for rollback to baseline model or retrain.
3. Communication: post a summary to the slice incident page and tag owners.
4. Post-incident: run regression-bisect playbook and create an action item with expected ETA.

CLI and API examples

- Query current sentinel score for slice 'enterprise-forms':
  curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' 'https://internal-api.redwood.ai/sentinel/v1/slices/enterprise-forms/score'

- Apply a temporary hedging override (requires steward token):
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $STEWARD_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"slice":"enterprise-forms","action":"hedge","route_percent":50,"duration_minutes":120}' https://internal-api.redwood.ai/sentinel/v1/overrides

Monitoring queries (prometheus-like pseudo)

- fidelity_delta_pct (1h avg) by slice:
  avg_over_time(fidelity_delta_pct[1h]) by (slice)
- sentinel_score recent:
  max_over_time(sentinel_score[3h]) by (slice)
- hedged_traffic_pct to detect cost pressure:
  sum(rate(hedged_traffic_pct[1h])) by (slice) > 0.15

Escalation and rollback criteria

- Immediate rollback: any slice with sentinel_score >= 85 and fidelity_delta_pct > 15% sustained for 1h.
- Steward approval required when hedging cost exceeds 50% of slice cost shield.
- Postmortem required if rollback occurred and customer impact > 5% of monthly queries.

Ownership and SLAs

- Sentinel core service owner: eng-servables-team (on-call rotation).
- Eval-harness integration owner: applied-ml-team.
- SLA: sentinel scoring available within 5 minutes of probe completion 99.9% of the time.

Related artifacts and links

- Probe registry: /tools/probe-registry
- Quant profile manifests: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles
- Regression bisect playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026

Change log

- 2026-02-10: initial published version, v1 policy and thresholds.
- 2026-02-25: adjusted hedging ramp to include 2h evaluation window after internal pilot.

Appendix: Example failure case

- Symptom: enterprise-forms slice shows fidelity_delta_pct = 22% and embedding_drift_cosine = 0.19; sentinel_score = 67.
- Automated action: hedge 25% -> 50% over 4h, fidelity_delta improved to 9% after 2h, hedging kept at 50% and steward notified.
- Outcome: no rollback, post-incident action to add targeted probes for form-parsing intent.

For questions or to request a shield increase, contact the applied-ml steward channel or open a ticket with owner-team.

title: Multi-seed aggregation and variance budgeting for eval stability
content:
Purpose
-------
This document defines the Multi-seed Aggregation and Variance Budgeting protocol (MAVB) used by Redwood's eval harness to quantify output stochasticity, attribute variance to sources (prompting, model nondeterminism, quantization, runtime caching), and set actionable variance budgets for production rollouts and regression triage.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all internal evaluation runs that influence model promotion, quantization decisions, or production rollouts (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Intended for use by applied-ML, model-onboarding, runtime, and SRE teams.
- Covers generation (chat/text), reranking, and embedding stability analyses where multiple random seeds or sampling strategies are relevant.

Definitions
-----------
- Seed run: One execution of an evaluation workload with a single RNG seed and fixed runtime settings.
- Seed ensemble: A set of N seed runs used to measure variance for a given workload slice.
- Variance budget: A pre-defined acceptable range (σ or interquartile range) for metric fluctuation attributable to nondeterminism.
- Attribution buckets: "prompt variance", "model stochasticity", "quantization impact", "runtime cache/batching".

Roles & Ownership
-----------------
- Evaluation Owner (Applied-ML): defines workload slices, target metrics, and baseline model.
- Runtime Owner (Serving Runtime): provides reproducible runtime configs and documents non-deterministic behaviors.
- Onboarding Lead (Model Onboarding): approves variance budgets for model promotion and signs off on triage.
- Regression Lead (Regression Triage): coordinates bisecting and blames assignment when variance exceeds budgets.

High-level protocol summary
---------------------------
1. Define workload slices (by prompt-type / user-slice / sequence length / language / quantization profile).
2. For each slice, run a seed ensemble of N runs (default N=7; N minimum = 5 for preliminary checks).
3. Compute per-metric aggregation (mean, median, stdev, IQR, bootstrap CI) across seeds.
4. Compare against the variance budget table; if exceeded, run attribution steps and trigger triage.
5. Record all raw seed traces, RNG seeds, runtime config, and KV-cache state hash in the eval store.

Determining ensemble size (N)
-----------------------------
- Small slices or quick smoke tests: N = 3–5 (informational only).
- Standard production slices: N = 7 (balance of power and cost).
- High-sensitivity slices (legal, safety): N = 15+ and use stratified sampling across RNG engine settings.
- Guidance: choose N such that 95% bootstrap CI of the primary metric width <= half the variance budget.

Aggregation methods and rationale
---------------------------------
- Use median as the primary central tendency for skewed generation metrics (e.g., ROUGE, BLEU for few-shot outputs).
- Report both stdev and IQR; prefer IQR for heavy-tailed distributions.
- Provide bootstrap percentile CI (1k resamples) for each metric and seed-aggregated score.
- For binary pass/fail checks (safety filters), report the proportion across seeds with Clopper–Pearson 95% CI.

Variance budgeting table (example)
----------------------------------
| Slice category            | Primary metric         | Variance budget (IQR) | Notes |
|--------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|-------|
| Short FAQ prompts (<64)  | answer-accuracy @1     | <= 3% points           | typical low variance |
| Long-context summarization | ROUGE-L               | <= 5 pts IQR           | cache-sensitive |
| Multi-lingual short prompts | BLEU (en→xx)         | <= 4 pts IQR           | cross-tokenization noise |
| Safety filter pass rate   | pass-rate (%)         | <= 1.5% points         | high-sensitivity |
| Embedding cosine (µ)      | mean cosine           | <= 0.005               | quantization-sensitive |

Attribution workflow
--------------------
1. If variance budget exceeded, re-run the seed ensemble with controlled toggles:
   - Fix RNG engine to deterministic mode (if supported).
   - Disable prefix/KV cache.
   - Run on a reference model binary (unquantized) and then on the quantized artifact.
   - Switch sampling strategy to greedy to isolate sampling noise.
2. For each toggle, compute delta in metric stdev/IQR. Attribute percent of variance explained to each bucket.
3. If quantization explains > 60% of excess variance, fail quantization promotion and open a quant-triage ticket.
4. If runtime cache/batching contributes > 30%, create a runtime investigation with traces and GPU scheduling logs.

Regression triage playbook (short)
----------------------------------
1. Tag the failing eval run and mark related traces as P0 for triage.
2. Run an automated bisect across commits and model checkpoints using the eval harness (see CLI below).
3. For suspected infra/runtime causes, reproduce on a minimal dedicated node with identical runtime config.
4. If model change suspected, request an annotated diff of token-level outputs across seeds and an error-slice report.
5. Document conclusion in the regression tracker with blame attribution and corrective action (rollback, quant-tune, prompt-harden).

Practical examples and CLI
-------------------------
Example eval config (YAML) used by the harness:

```yaml
name: long-summary-xlang
baseline_model: redwood-open-7b-v2
slices:
  - name: long-docs
    length_range: [1024, 8192]
    prompt_template: templates/long-summary-v2.jinja
seeds: 7
sampling:
  method: top-p
  p: 0.92
  temperature: 0.8
runtime_config:
  kv_cache: enabled
  batch_size: 8
  quant_profile: q4_0
output_metrics:
  - rouge_l
  - readability_score
  - latency_ms
```

Run command (eval harness):

$ eval-harness run --config long-summary-xlang.yaml --store /evals/mavb/2026-02-15

Bisect command (example):

$ eval-harness bisect --config long-summary-xlang.yaml --commit-range abc123..def456 --seeds 5 --report /tmp/bisect.html

Data retention and artifact requirements
---------------------------------------
- Keep raw seed outputs and RNG seeds for 90 days for general audits; 365 days for safety-critical slices.
- Save runtime traces (trace ids) including kernel selection logs, KV-cache hashes, and batching metadata in the eval store.
- Attach quantization artifact id and build metadata when running quantized profiles.

Alerting thresholds and play-trigger rules
-----------------------------------------
- Automated alert when primary metric IQR exceeds budget on three consecutive runs for the same slice.
- PagerRule: if safety-filter pass-rate variance > budget, page Regression Lead and Safety Owner.
- Generate a "variance-drift" ticket automatically when long-term drift exceeds 2x budget over 30 days.

Integration with model onboarding and Optimize
---------------------------------------------
- Model onboarding adds variance budgets to the promotion checklist. The onboarding job fails if high-sensitivity slices exceed budgets.
- Redwood Optimize can suggest alternative quant profiles when quantization-attributed variance is detected; attach suggested profiles to the quant-triage ticket.

Quick reference checklist
-------------------------
- [ ] Define slices and primary metric
- [ ] Choose N seeds (≥5 for production)
- [ ] Run seed ensemble and compute IQR/CI
- [ ] Compare to variance budget table
- [ ] If exceeded: run attribution toggles
- [ ] If still failed: trigger regression triage
- [ ] Record findings and attach raw traces

Appendix A — Example report output (CSV columns)
------------------------------------------------
run_id, seed, slice_name, metric_name, metric_value, runtime_config_id, quant_artifact_id, kv_cache_hash, trace_id

Appendix B — Troubleshooting tips
---------------------------------
- High variance but low mean change: likely sampling noise — increase seeds or fix to greedy for diagnostic runs.
- Variance concentrated in long-context slices: look for KV cache fingerprint mismatches or tokenization boundary issues.
- Quantization large jumps in specific tokens: run token-level log-prob difference across seeds and check for Outlier Token Instances (OTIs).

Related pages
-------------
- See also: Stochastic Eval Replay and Determinism Protocol (link above), Quantization Failure Modes and Recovery Playbook, Regression Bisect Assistant.

title: Operational probe economics and priority contract
content:
Overview

This document defines the operational contract between evaluation owners (model teams, product teams, and the eval platform) for probe prioritization, sampling budgets, and the per-probe cost accounting model used by the Redwood eval harness. It codifies: how probes are scored for execution priority, how budget allocation works across workloads (hosted/private/dedicated), and the runbook for triaging cost-driven failures or regressions that originate from probe scheduling and sampling.

Scope

- Applies to all probes scheduled through the eval harness (shadow, continuous, and targeted stress probes)
- Covers cost accounting for compute + annotation + human review components of probes
- Defines telemetry and alerting thresholds used by SRE and the evaluation platform team

Definitions

- Probe: a single unit of evaluation (input prompt + expected checks + metadata) run against one or more model variants.
- Probe cost: an estimated USD cost for executing a probe in a specific mode (hosted / dedicated / private), including token compute, IO, and annotation overhead.
- Priority score: numeric score used by the scheduler to rank pending probes for execution.
- Sampling contract: a signed agreement (documented here as config) that specifies the target sample rate and SLA for a probe family.

Principles

1) Transparently measurable economics: every scheduled probe must attach a probe_cost estimate and cost_breakdown metadata (compute_tokens, warmup_tokens, annotation_minutes).
2) Workload-aware fairness: priority score should reflect both customer-facing impact (severity) and marginal economic utility (information gain per dollar).
3) Safety-first triage: probes that are safety or compliance critical always have a higher base priority and an independent execution budget.

Priority scoring model (operational formula)

PriorityScore = base_factor * severity_weight + lambda * (info_gain_estimate / probe_cost) - penalty_adjustments

Where:
- base_factor: 100 for safety/compliance probes, 50 for production regression probes, 20 for exploratory/ad-hoc probes.
- severity_weight: integer [1..5] assigned by the owning team (must justify)
- info_gain_estimate: expected fraction (0..1) of new failure modes discovered; derived from historical probe novelty and slice coverage
- probe_cost: estimated USD cost for the probe in target execution mode
- lambda: scaling constant (default 25) tuned quarterly by the eval platform team
- penalty_adjustments: negative modifiers for duplication, recent failures with no new signal, or owner throttles

Operational sampling contract (YAML config example)

teams must submit a sampling contract YAML to the eval platform to guarantee run capacity and to encode cost limits. Example: 

---
probe_family: "payment-intent-fuzzy-parsing"
owner: "payments-ml"
priority_category: "production-regression"
target_sample_rate_per_day: "500"
monthly_cost_cap_usd: "2500"
safety_critical: "false"
modes: ["shadow", "continuous"]
retention_days: "90"
# required fields: justification, contact, SLAs for annotation
justification: "Covers high-frequency parsing errors observed in Q4"
contact: "payments-ml@redwood.com"
annotation_sla_days: "3"
---

Contract enforcement rules

- Contracts are evaluated at the start of each scheduling epoch (midnight UTC). If run queue demand exceeds capacity, probes are ranked by PriorityScore subject to monthly_cost_cap_usd.
- If a probe_family exceeds its monthly_cost_cap_usd, the scheduler will: 1) pause exploratory probes, 2) reduce sampling rate proportionally for non-safety probes, and 3) notify the owner via email and slack.
- Owners may petition for temporary burst capacity by opening a ticket with the evaluation platform; approval required from platform + finance for > $5k burst.

Telemetry, dashboards and SLIs

Minimum telemetry emitted per probe run:
- probe_id, probe_family, execution_mode, model_variant, start_ts, latency_ms_median, tokens_consumed, warmup_flag, run_cost_usd, result_status (pass/fail/error), info_gain_signal (0..1)

Key dashboards and SLOs:
- Probe-cost burn rate (daily / monthly) — alert if projected monthly spend > budget by 10% (pager duty: eval-finance)
- Sampling fairness index — Gini coefficient of executed probes per family; alert if Gini > 0.6 for 72 hours
- Critical-probe-latency SLO — 95th percentile exec latency < 1200ms for shadow runs; breach triggers oncall paging
- Novelty throughput SLI — number of unique new failure signatures per 1000 probes; used in quarterly platform tuning

Alerting thresholds and ownership

- Budget breach (projected monthly overspend > 10%): owned by evaluation platform (alerts to eval-finance and owner team)
- Safety probe failure spike (> 5x baseline in 1 hour): owned by SRE + safety lead; immediate mitigation: pause model rollout and notify product security
- Scheduler backlog growth (> 5000 pending probes for > 6 hours): owned by platform infra (investigate worker saturation, DB locks, or networking)

Annotation and human review economics

- For probes requiring human annotation, the annotation_minutes estimate must be provided. The platform will aggregate annotation demand weekly and provision annotator capacity.
- Annotation SLAs: default 3 business days. If annotation backlog > 2x SLA, owner must provide additional capacity or the platform will reduce non-critical sampling.

Runbook: high-level steps for cost-driven probe failure

1) Alert fires: budget-breach or backlog.
2) Triage owner and platform leads review the probe_family cost_breakdown in the dashboard.
3) If overspend is due to an unexpected hot slice: run immediate targeted diagnostics (run 100 blind replicates with token caps, check info_gain).
4) Temporary mitigation options (in order):
   a) throttle sampling rate (by 50%)
   b) switch execution_mode to cached/replica (uses lower-cost model variant)
   c) pause exploratory probes within the family
   d) request burst capacity through ticketing flow
5) If mitigation fails, escalate to SRE and Finance for emergency funding or rollback of model rollout.

Regression triage tie-in

When regression detectors fire (see regression-triage handbook), the platform will:
- Reserve a 10% emergency probe budget to re-run failing slices at higher fidelity (multi-seed, quant-aware).
- Tag those probe runs with regression_investigation=true so they bypass normal cost throttles for up to 48 hours.
- Require a one-page triage summary from the owning team within 5 business days documenting root cause and remediation plan.

Model onboarding checklist (contract items)

Every model onboarding must include:
- A signed sampling contract for any production-facing probe families
- Probe_cost benchmarks for all target execution modes (hosted, dedicated, private)
- Quantization impact notes (expected delta in info_gain per token)
- A synthetic probe suite for quick smoke checks (<=100 probes)

Appendix: example probe run CLI and YAML

# CLI example to schedule a probe family (evalctl)
evalctl submit --family payment-intent-fuzzy-parsing --mode shadow --rate 100/day --contract-file ./payment-sampling.yaml

# Example run payload (JSON)
{
  "probe_id": "probe-20260215-001",
  "probe_family": "payment-intent-fuzzy-parsing",
  "input": "{\"order\": 1234, \"text\": \"Charge me $1,200.00 for item ABC\"}",
  "expected_checks": ["canonical_amount_parsed", "currency_normalized"],
  "probe_cost_estimate_usd": "0.015"
}

Appendix B: tuning cadence and governance

- The eval platform will review lambda (scaling constant) and the priority model every quarter in the Eval Platform Forum. Changes to the contract require sign-off from platform lead, finance, and representatives from three active owner teams.

Ownership and contacts

- Evaluation Platform (owner): eval-platform@redwood.com
- Finance (cost approvals): eval-finance@redwood.com
- SRE (critical probe escalation): sre-oncall@redwood.com
- Safety & Compliance: safety-compliance@redwood.com

Related artifacts and references

- Probe curation charter: ../prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/probe-curation-stewardship-and-annotation-charter-2026.json
- Cost budgeting framework: ../eval-harness/eval-cost-slice-prioritization-and-resource-budgeting-2026.json

Change log

- 2026-02-15: initial published version (Sanjay Patel)
- 2026-03-01: clarified penalty_adjustments and added sampling contract example (Mariela Gomez)

title: Hybrid slice-eval and quant-aware prompt-rewrite playbook
content:
Summary

This playbook defines the hybrid slice-driven evaluation workflow that combines: (a) stratified slice evaluation across production-like prompt distributions, and (b) quantization-aware prompt rewrites used as a lightweight mitigation for quality regressions introduced by lower-precision model variants. The goal is to detect, triage, and (where safe) automatically mitigate quality regressions caused or amplified by quantization and runtime interactions without blocking throughput or availability.

Why this exists

- Quantized model variants and mixed-precision rollouts reduce cost but can cause localized failure modes on specific prompt slices (e.g., numeric tables, code, multi-step reasoning).
- Existing holistic evals hide slice-level failures; owners need a repeatable way to detect degradations, diagnose root cause (model vs prompt sensitivity vs cache interaction), and apply minimal interventions such as prompt rewrites or routing rules.

Scope and exclusions

- In scope: text generation and chat endpoints, embeddings when downstream quality depends on prompt framing, integration with the eval-harness for batch and shadow runs, quant profiles (int8/int4/hybrid) handled by the runtime.
- Out of scope: training-time fixes, privacy-preserving DP transforms (see privacy-first-shadow-eval elsewhere), large-scale dataset relabeling.

Ownership and contacts

- Playbook owner: Applied ML — Maya Chen (author)
- Runtime integration: Serving Runtime Team — Diego Ramos
- Quant profiles and verification: Inference Research — Harpreet Kaur
- Pager/contact for urgent regression: #ml-regressions (Slack) and oncall-applied-ml rotation

Definitions and key metrics

- Slice: a subset of prompts defined by label rules (regex, metadata, token patterns, language, prompt-template).
- Prompt rewrite: deterministic transformation applied to the user prompt before inference (e.g., explicit context headers, answer-format anchors, numeric formatting).
- Quant variant: model binary compiled to a specific quant profile (e.g., fp16, int8, int4).

Primary metrics collected per slice per variant:

- Slice Success Rate (SSR): percent of responses passing a slice-specific acceptance check (boolean or thresholded semantic similarity).
- Response Stability Index (RSI): normalized similarity between reference (gold) and response distribution across seeds (0-100).
- Per-token latency and tail-p99 latency (ms).
- Token-economic delta: tokens generated and kv-cache reuse percentage.
- Human-review CTR: for slices flagged, rate of escalation to human review.

Acceptance thresholds (example)

- SSR drop tolerated: <= 2% drop vs baseline for low-risk slices; <= 0.5% drop for high-safety slices (PII extraction, compliance prompts).
- RSI decrease tolerated: <= 5 points.

Prerequisites

1) Registered slice catalog: a YAML file per product listing slice_id, label_rules, owner, risk_level, acceptance_checks. Example:

---
- slice_id: numeric-table-extraction
  label_rules:
    - "prompt contains 'table' AND regex '\\d+\\.\\d+'"
  owner: fin-nlp-team
  risk_level: high
  acceptance_check: "column-extraction-f1 >= 0.92"
---

2) Eval harness integration: a job type that can run an eval across multiple model binaries and quant-profiles and emit per-slice metrics.
3) Canary traffic mirror: ability to run shadow runs at production sampling rates and attach telemetry to trace IDs.

High-level workflow (summary)

1) Slice sampling: generation of representative prompts for each slice from prod logs (time-windowed) with stratified sampling to maintain distributional weighting.
2) Baseline run: run chosen reference binary (usually fp16) to generate gold outputs and metric baselines.
3) Quant sweep: run each quant profile against the same prompt set; collect per-slice metrics and difference deltas.
4) Detection: automatic rules flag slices with metric regressions above acceptance thresholds.
5) Triage: triage path splits into (A) root cause: quantization artifacts vs prompt-sensitivity vs cache/latency-induced failure; (B) automatic mitigations: prompt rewrite heuristics, routing to higher-precision variant, cache TTL adjustments.
6) Canary release: if mitigation is accepted, create a canary route with mitigation enabled for a small % of production traffic and monitor RTT metrics before promotion.

Detailed step-by-step procedure

1) Build slice set
   - Run slice-extractor CLI: `rwd-slice-extract --window 7d --min-usage 100 --out slices/quarterly.yaml`
   - Ensure each slice includes at least 500 examples or mark as low-sample and schedule for synthetic augmentation.

2) Generate rewrites
   - For each flagged slice, produce candidate prompt rewrites. Rewrites follow these rules:
     a) Do not change user intent (strictly prefix/suffix or formatting fixes).
     b) Keep token overhead < 20 tokens or mark as acceptable if latency budget allows.
     c) Explicit annotations only when helpful (e.g., \"OutputFormat: JSON; Fields: name, price\").

   - Example rewrite ruleset (text):
     - numeric-table-extraction: prefix \"Task: extract table columns as CSV. Numeric fields keep 2 decimals.\"
     - code-synthesis: append \"Provide only code in a fenced block, include no explanations.\"

3) Run quant-aware A/B evals
   - Eval config YAML (example):

     eval_job:
       name: quant-sweep-run-2026-02
       prompt_set: slices/quarterly.yaml
       seeds: [42, 123, 256]
       models:
         - model: redwood-open-20b
           binaries: [fp16, int8-q4, int4-hybrid]
       acceptance_checks_path: /checks/slice_checks.py

   - Kick off: `rwd-eval run --config eval-job.yaml --output results/quant-sweep-2026-02`

4) Automated detection rules (examples)
   - flag when SSR drop > threshold AND RSI drop > 4 points
   - flag when p99 latency increases > 20% correlated with quant profile changes

5) Triage checklist (on flagged slice)
   - Verify reproducibility: run single-seed debug with full logs and KV-cache disabled to rule out cache-induced nondeterminism.
   - Compare tokenization: ensure no tokenizer mismatch between binaries.
   - Inspect logits divergence: runtime team to provide top-k softmax drift report for problem prompts.
   - If divergence concentrated in early tokens, suspect prompt sensitivity or rewrite mismatch.

6) Mitigation decision matrix
   - If divergence is due to quant rounding in numeric formatting -> apply controlled prompt rewrite and re-run quant sweep for the slice.
   - If divergence persists across rewrites -> route slice to higher-precision variant (routing config change).
   - If high latency introduced by mitigation -> prefer routing to dedicated capacity instead of longer prompt rewrites.

7) Canary rollout and monitoring
   - Create route: `route_rule: if slice_id == numeric-table-extraction -> model_variant: int8-q4-mitigated; weight: 5%`
   - Monitor for 24-72 hours: SSR, RSI, p99 latency, human-review CTR.
   - Promotion criteria: no SSR regressions beyond tolerance, stable RSI, and no rise in human-review CTR.

Operational integrations and observability

- Dashboards: per-slice comparison panel showing baseline vs variant for SSR, RSI, latency, token-economics.
- Alerting: auto-ticket (Jira) creation when a high-risk slice is flagged; include reproduction artifacts and candidate rewrites.
- Audit logs: every applied rewrite or routing rule must include owner, justification, and link to eval run id.

Safety and guardrails

- Do not apply prompt rewrites that change semantics for PII or legal/compliance slices. Those must be routed to higher-precision binaries only.
- For restricted slices, require explicit approval from Security/Trust owners before any automated mitigation is promoted.

Example artifacts (copyable)

- Minimal slice YAML entry:
  - slice_id: code-synthesis
    label_rules:
      - "prompt contains 'write a function' AND language == 'python'"
    owner: platforms-dx
    risk_level: medium
    acceptance_check: "exact_code_match_rate >= 0.70"

- Prompt rewrite example (JSON as string):
  {
    "slice_id": "code-synthesis",
    "rewrite": "Append: 'Return only code. No explanation.'",
    "token_overhead": "5"
  }

To promote as standard

- When a slice-level mitigation demonstrates consistent improvement across three independent production-like windows and meets promotion thresholds, create a promotion PR to the `slices-catalog` repo and tag the runtime team for binary changes if necessary.

Appendix: triage playbook checklist (quick reference)

1) Confirm sample parity between baseline and quant-run.
2) Reproduce with KV-cache disabled.
3) Run tokenization and logits-diff diagnostics.
4) Try constrained prompt rewrite (<=20 tokens).
5) If resolved, run canary (5-10% traffic) for 24-72 hours.
6) If unresolved, escalate to model-onboarding and inference-research with artifacts.

Related pages and references

- See eval-harness/throughput-fidelity-tradeoff-matrix-and-acceptance-protocol-2026 for promotion thresholds and tradeoff guidance.
- See quantization-profiles/heterogeneous-hybrid-quant-deployment-guidelines-2026 for binary labeling conventions.

End of document

title: Anchored Shadow Fleet: Qualification & Exposure Manifest
content:
Summary:
This document defines the qualification, exposure accounting, telemetry contract, and operational playbook for anchored shadow fleets used in Redwood's eval harness. Anchored shadow fleets are stable, versioned shadow cohorts (a small percentage of traffic mirrored to candidate model variants) with explicit exposure budgets and automated qualification checks that gate promotion to canary or full rollout.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers running shadow experiments
- SRE and runtime owners who operate fleet infrastructure
- Product teams approving promotions for production features

Goals:
- Provide deterministic qualification criteria for shadow cohorts so promotion decisions are auditable.
- Standardize exposure accounting (how we measure and cap risk) across private/dedicated/hosted environments.
- Define the minimum telemetry required from runtime and evaluator sidecars.
- Offer a runbook for common failure modes and rollback steps.

1) Definitions and scope
- Anchored shadow fleet: a named group of replicas running a candidate model that receives mirrored traffic (no live responses to users) with trace-level linkage back to origin request and a stable exposure budget.
- Exposure: the fraction of user traffic (or probe volume) mirrored to the shadow fleet normalized to an impact score (see Exposure Scoring).
- Qualification window: a contiguous time period (default 72 hours) used to compute qualification metrics unless otherwise specified.
- Promotion gates: the set of checks that must pass for a shadowed model to advance to canary.

2) Exposure scoring (how to account risk)
Exposure Score = traffic_fraction * request_risk_weight * feature_sensitivity_factor
- traffic_fraction: fraction of requests mirrored (e.g., 0.01 for 1%).
- request_risk_weight: default 1.0; increased for high-sensitivity endpoints (payments, auth) to 5.0.
- feature_sensitivity_factor: computed from product-level taxonomy (0.5–2.0).
Thresholds:
- Low exposure: score < 0.05 — eligible for quick qualification.
- Medium exposure: 0.05 <= score < 0.2 — requires extended probe sets and a human reviewer.
- High exposure: score >= 0.2 — blocked; requires legal/security approval and dedicated privacy budget.

3) Telemetry contract (required signals)
Provide the following fields on each mirrored request event via the evaluator sidecar or shadow logging pipeline:
- request_id (string)
- origin_route (string)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- model_variant (string)
- latency_ms (number)
- tokens_in / tokens_out (numbers)
- scorer_metrics: {fidelity_delta, hallucination_flag, embedding_cosine}  -- scorer_metrics may be JSON-encoded string in logs if necessary
- kv_cache_hit (bool)
- quant_mode (string)
- exposure_tag (string)
Minimum ingestion SLA: telemetry packets must be available in the eval datastore within 5 minutes of generation for 95% of events.

4) Qualification matrix (automated checks)
Automated tests are run over the qualification window. All thresholds are configurable per-service but defaults are below. 
Table: Qualification checks and default thresholds
| Check name | Metric | Default threshold | Failure severity |
| ---------- | ------ | ----------------- | ---------------- |
| Latency tail | 95th latency (ms) | <= runtime_slo*1.5 | high |
| Token cost delta | mean tokens_out delta | <= +10% | medium |
| Fidelity delta | evaluator_fidelity_score delta | >= -0.03 | high |
| Hallucination rate | % responses flagged | <= 0.5% | high |
| Embedding drift | mean cosine drop | >= -0.02 | medium |
| Error rate | 5xx or sidecar failures | <= 0.1% | high |
| Quant-sensitivity | slice-level fidelity delta when quant mode != baseline | <= -0.05 | high |

Pass criteria: No high-severity failures; at most one medium failure provided a mitigations plan is in place and reviewer signs off.

5) Shadow cohort construction and anchoring
Steps to create an anchored shadow fleet:
1. Define the cohort name and exposure budget in the Fleet Registry. Example: anchored-shadow-primer-2026, exposure budget 0.02.
2. Register model artifact with the Model Registry and attach a promotion policy.
3. Create evaluator sidecar spec that declares scorer metrics, probe sets, and sampling strategy.
4. Attach a stable anchor: an immutable probe set of 10k golden samples corresponding to critical slices (payments, localization, multi-turn). Anchoring ensures deterministic drift checks across promotion windows.
5. Enable mirrored traffic rule in the routing layer with traffic_fraction <= configured max.
6. Activate data retention and redaction policy for any customer-identifying fields.

Example evaluator sidecar snippet (YAML):
---
sidecar:
  name: anchored-eval-01
  probes:
    - path: /probes/anchored-primer-10k.jsonl
  required_metrics:
    - fidelity_delta
    - hallucination_flag
  upload_endpoint: s3://eval-ingest/anchored-shadow/
  telemetry_window_minutes: 4320
  reporting_interval_seconds: 300

6) Promotion workflow (shadow -> canary)
1. Automated qualification runs at the end of the qualification window. A validation report is posted to the Fleet Registry.
2. If automated gates pass, schedule a human review (Reviewer group: Applied-ML Oncall + Product Owner).
3. Human reviewers inspect: golden anchor diffs, telemetry sample traces, cost impact estimate, and privacy checklist.
4. If approved, create canary plan with explicit rollout percentage and rollback policy.
5. Record approval in the promotion audit log and tag the model artifact with promotion:canary.

7) Runbook: common failure scenarios and mitigation
Scenario A — Fidelity delta breach on a single critical slice:
1. Pause further shadow exposure by setting traffic_fraction=0 for the cohort.
2. Run slice-localizer to identify prompt families causing the regression.
3. If a quick prompt rewrite mitigates (>50% improvement on retry), prepare a patch candidate and restart a shortened qualification window.
4. Otherwise, revert shadow fleet to previous model artifact and schedule a deep regression triage.

Scenario B — Telemetry ingestion lag > 10 minutes:
1. Notify infra-sre channel and open an alert runbook.
2. Switch to secondary logging endpoint for short-term buffering (edge-aggregator -> s3).
3. Recompute metrics once backlog recovered; extend qualification window by backlog window length.

Scenario C — Quant-sensitivity failure at scale:
1. Isolate quantized replicas and run deterministic probe replay against baseline float artifacts.
2. If reproducible, tag artifact with quant-failure and prevent promotion.
3. Initiate quant remediation (re-tune per-slice quant profile) under Applied-ML ownership.

8) Audit and reporting requirements
- Every promotion decision must have an accompanying report: automated validation output, human reviewer comments, sample traces (10 positives/10 negatives), and exposure accounting.
- Audit retention: reports retained for 540 days.
- Weekly summary: Fleet Registry should export a CSV of active anchored shadows, exposure totals, and open failures for the Platform Review meeting.

9) Implementation checklist (operators)
- [ ] Create Fleet Registry entry with owner, exposure_budget, anchor_set_id
- [ ] Register sidecar and confirm telemetry contract endpoints
- [ ] Upload anchor set to eval-db and mark as immutable
- [ ] Configure routing mirror with safety caps and privacy redaction
- [ ] Run initial qualification (dry-run flag) and verify automated report generation

10) Appendices
A. Example query: compute exposure burn rate (SQL):
-- daily exposure burn per cohort
SELECT cohort, sum(traffic_fraction * request_risk_weight * feature_sensitivity_factor) as daily_exposure
FROM shadow_cohort_events
WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '1 day'
GROUP BY cohort;

B. Config table (defaults):
| param | default | notes |
| exposure_budget | 0.02 | Max allowed exposure score over qualification window |
| qualification_window_hours | 72 | Sliding window for automated checks |
| telemetry_latency_sla_seconds | 300 | 95th percentile ingest latency |
| anchor_sample_size | 10000 | Minimum golden probe set size |
| retention_days | 540 | Promotion report retention |

C. Ownership and contacts:
- Fleet Registry owner: eng-platform@redwood.com
- Applied-ML lead: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.com)
- Runtime/SRE oncall: see /eng-sre/runbooks/oncall-rotation

If you are implementing a new anchored shadow fleet or modifying exposure rules, follow the Implementation checklist and schedule a pre-qualification review with Applied-ML. For any high-exposure experiments contact Security for a privacy budget lift and Legal for customer-data approvals.

Document history:
- 2026-03-02: Created by Aisha Patel
- 2026-06-08: Added quant-sensitivity section after cross-team incident
- 2026-10-12: Clarified telemetry SLA and retention periods

title: Eval Data Provenance and Reproducibility Standard
content:
Summary:

This standard defines the metadata, process, and automated checks required to ensure evaluation datasets and synthetic prompt collections used in Redwood Inference evaluation harnesses are traceable, auditable, and reproducible. It applies to all evaluation artifacts consumed by the eval-orchestrator and offline evaluation pipelines (interactive, batch, and shadow).

Scope and goals:

- Scope: ground-truth datasets, prompt playlists, synthetic generators, sampled mirrors of production traffic, and any derived evaluation artifacts used for model promotion, regression triage, or quality guardrails.
- Goals:
  - Produce a minimum provenance record for every eval artifact that permits exact rehydration in CI and on private/dedicated deployments.
  - Provide a reproducibility score and gating rules for model promotion and rollout.
  - Automate metadata capture, enforcement, and lineage visualization.

Definitions:

- artifact: any dataset, prompt set, synthetic generator output, or evaluation manifest.
- dataset_id: stable identifier for the upstream source (e.g., redwood/datasets/intent-probes-v2).
- snapshot_sha: git or object-store SHA for the exact file(s) used.
- manifest_uri: location in object storage or dataset registry.
- schema_hash: deterministic hash of the record schema (order + field names + types).
- provenance_level: low|standard|strict (see "Provenance Levels" below).

Provenance levels and requirements:

1) low (ad-hoc experiments)
- Required fields: dataset_id, created_by, timestamp, manifest_uri
- Recommendation: include seed when sampling
- Not allowed for promotion or production guardrails

2) standard (typical evals and benchmark runs)
- Required fields: dataset_id, snapshot_sha, manifest_uri, schema_hash, sample_strategy, seed, eval_suite_version, creator_contact
- Metadata must be stored in the central data-catalog entry and linked from the eval run
- Automated lint must pass (metadata-lint >= v1.3)

3) strict (promotion and safety-critical checks)
- All standard fields plus: lineage (upstream datasets used), annotation_guides_version, annotator_ids (or k-anonymized certificate), access_control_audit_uri, differential_privacy_parameters (if applied), reproducibility_score
- Required to use reproducibility_score >= 0.90 for model promotion to hosted or dedicated clusters

Minimal metadata schema (required keys):

| field | description | example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| dataset_id | canonical dataset name in data-catalog | redwood/datasets/intent-probes-v2 |
| snapshot_sha | SHA of the gzipped manifest or git tag | sha256:2a4b... |
| manifest_uri | s3 or gs URI pointing to the manifest | s3://redwood-evals/manifests/intent-probes-v2/2026-01-08.jsonl |
| schema_hash | deterministic hash of field names and types | hsh:8f12... |
| sample_strategy | full|stratified|random|production-mirror | stratified:user_segment |
| seed | integer seed for sampling/synth | 42 |
| eval_suite_version | semantic version of eval suite used | 2026.01.1 |
| creator_contact | owner email or oncall | nadia.chen@redwood.ai |
| provenance_level | low|standard|strict | standard |

Mandatory fields must be present as top-level keys in the artifact manifest and also as labels in the data-catalog entry. Implementations that fail to populate these keys should be rejected by eval-ci pre-submit checks.

Reproducibility score and computation:

The reproducibility_score is a number in [0.0, 1.0] that represents the confidence that an artifact + pipeline can be deterministically re-executed and yield equivalent evaluation outputs (accounting for known non-determinism). It is computed as a weighted average of:

- metadata_completeness (30%): fraction of mandatory keys present and valid.
- binary_stability (30%): whether binaries (evaluator, model surrogate) used are pinned with SHAs or immutable container digests.
- sample_determinism (20%): sampling seeds present and non-random components pinned.
- environment_pin (20%): runtime environment pinned (e.g., python packages, CUDA driver, runtime container digest).

Thresholds:

- < 0.6: exploratory only, cannot be used in regression triage or gated promotions.
- 0.6–0.89: acceptable for nightly bench and internal experiments.
- >= 0.90: eligible for promotion to canary/dedicated and for use in safety guardrails (strict artifacts require >=0.90).

Automation and enforcement:

- metadata-lint (CLI): runs on any manifest changes. Usage:
  - metadata-lint validate manifest.json --schema eval-provenance-v1
  - metadata-lint compute-score manifest.json
  - Exit codes: 0 pass, 2 warnings, 3 failure
- eval-ci (GitHub/GitLab integration):
  - Pre-merge hook validates manifest presence and reproducibility_score >= 0.6 (project config may raise this)
  - Promotion pipeline requires reproducibility_score >= 0.90 and provenance_level strict
- data-catalog (service: redwood-data-catalog): automatic registration API
  - POST /v1/artifacts register payload -> returns artifact_id and visual lineage graph link
- lineage-visualizer: internal service used by SRE and QA to render upstream/downstream dependencies

Promotion and gating workflow (numbered steps):

1. Author creates or updates evaluation manifest and pushes to the repo or uploads manifest to s3 with manifest_uri.
2. metadata-lint runs locally; author fixes schema or missing keys.
3. On PR, eval-ci validates manifest and computes reproducibility_score. PR blocked if score < team-configured threshold.
4. After merge, eval-orchestrator picks manifest and runs smoke evaluation.
5. If smoke passes and score >= 0.90, QA triggers strict-level human review (security/data-privacy).
6. Upon approval, artifact is marked in data-catalog as promotable and can be used in canary/regression suites.

Promotion checklist (must pass all items):

- metadata-lint: pass (exit 0)
- reproducibility_score >= 0.90
- smoke evaluation: no numeric regressions > 3% relative to baseline on key slices
- privacy review: DP parameters or annotator attestations present if data-sensitive
- storage: manifest_uri accessible with read-only service principal (audit log must show at least one access)

Operational considerations and edge cases:

- Large production mirrors: for privacy, store only stratified subsamples with schema_hash and random_seed, and store an access-controlled pointer to the full mirror.
- Synthetic generators: store generator commit hash, config, temperature/parameters, and random seed. If generator is non-deterministic (e.g., uses True RNG), mark provenance_level low unless additional determinism is introduced.
- Third-party datasets: require evidence of license and a scanned license_id field in manifest; provenance_level strict requires license_caveats documented.

Examples (manifest snippet):

{
  "dataset_id": "redwood/datasets/intent-probes-v2",
  "snapshot_sha": "sha256:2a4b...",
  "manifest_uri": "s3://redwood-evals/manifests/intent-probes-v2/2026-01-08.jsonl",
  "schema_hash": "hsh:8f12...",
  "sample_strategy": "stratified:user_segment",
  "seed": "42",
  "eval_suite_version": "2026.01.1",
  "creator_contact": "nadia.chen@redwood.ai",
  "provenance_level": "strict",
  "reproducibility_score": "0.93"
}

CLI quickstart for authors:

1) Create manifest: cp samples/manifest-template.json manifest.json && edit fields
2) Validate: metadata-lint validate manifest.json --schema eval-provenance-v1
3) Compute score: metadata-lint compute-score manifest.json
4) Register: curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data @manifest.json $DATA_CATALOG/register

Monitoring and alerts:

- Metrics exposed by eval-orchestrator: provenance_checks.total, provenance_checks.failed, reproducibility_score.avg (per-team metric).
- Alert: provenance_checks.failed > 5 in 1h -> page oncall-eval (pagerduty)
- Reports: weekly digest to applied-ml-and-evals channel with top failing keys and artifact churn

Ownership, support, and exceptions:

- Owner: Applied ML platform (team lead: Nadia Chen)
- Reviewers: Marcus Alvarez (SRE), Priya Kapoor (ML Research), Ethan Rivera (Privacy)
- Exceptions: requests for exceptions to the strict level must be submitted via the data-exceptions workflow and include a compensating controls checklist.

Appendix: example metadata-lint rule highlights:

- schema_hash must be computed using the deterministic_hasher tool (sha1 of field-name:type list)
- manifest_uri must be reachable by the CI runner and return 200 for HEAD
- snapshot_sha should be a 64-char hex (sha256) or a container digest (sha256:...)

Related pages and references:

- Evaluator interchange format: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/evaluator-interchange-format-and-federation-spec-2026
- Promotion playbook: /applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026
- Metadata tooling repo: git://git.redwood.ai/platform/metadata-lint (internal)

Revision history:

- 2025-11-20: initial draft (Nadia Chen)
- 2025-12-15: added reproducibility_score algorithm and thresholds (Marcus Alvarez)
- 2026-02-10: clarified strict level privacy requirements and added CLI quickstart (Priya Kapoor)

title: Multimodal Long‑Context Probe Orchestration and Telemetry Guide
content:
Summary:
This guide describes the probe orchestration and telemetry design for evaluating multimodal models on long‑context workloads. It covers synthetic probe generation, traffic stitching (real + synthetic), telemetry event schema, annotation guidance, privacy constraints, and a step-by-step orchestration playbook for staging -> shadow -> production evaluation. The goal is repeatable, auditable evals that reveal subtle long‑context regressions without significantly impacting production latency or costs.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: applied ML engineers, evaluation engineers, model onboarding owners, and SREs who run shadow/replica evals.
- Scope: multimodal inputs (text + images, video frames, document pages), sequence lengths from 2k to 200k tokens/frames, and workloads that exercise cache/KV behavior and prefix reuse. Not a model training guide.

Motivation and objectives:
- Detect quality regressions that only appear with long coherent context or multimodal grounding (e.g., reference tracking across thousand‑token spans).
- Measure worst‑case and average latency, KV cache miss effects, and token‑level fidelity for long context.
- Provide reproducible telemetry that supports causal triage (see regression triage playbooks).

Definitions:
- Probe: an input (text + optional media) designed to exercise a specific failure mode (forgetting, hallucination, coherence loss, cache invalidation).
- Stitch: the process of combining real customer traffic with synthetic probes in a way that preserves request distribution properties for evals.
- Shadow run: live inference of candidate model behind production routing, with outputs logged but not surfaced to users.

Probe generation pipeline (high level):
1. Collection and slicing:
   - Collect anonymized long‑context sessions from consenting customers or synthetic simulators.
   - Slice sessions into anchors (prefixes) and probes (target continuations) with metadata: anchor_length, last_accessed_kv_size, media_count, modality_mix.
2. Synthesis and augmentation:
   - Generate synthetic continuations using calibrated LLMs with varying temperature and instruction templates to cover edge behaviors.
   - Insert controlled perturbations: coreference swaps, repeated entity aliases, injected contradictions, and repeated image references.
3. Prioritization and sampling:
   - Score probes by risk (semantic drift probability), rarity (frequency in corpus), and resource impact (expected token cost).
   - Create evaluation batches balancing high‑risk low‑frequency probes with representative samples.
4. Annotation:
   - Human labelers annotate ground truth for intent, expected entity continuity, acceptable tolerance windows, and failure tags (e.g., misattribution, drop-off, hallucination).

Telemetry event schema (single flat JSON line per event):
- event_id: string (UUID)
- probe_id: string
- session_anchor_hash: string (HMAC with eval key)
- model_version: string
- route: string (internal route id)
- input_length_tokens: integer
- input_media_count: integer
- context_kv_size_bytes: integer
- start_timestamp: ISO8601
- end_timestamp: ISO8601
- latency_ms: integer
- tokens_generated: integer
- cache_hit_ratio: float (0.0-1.0)
- failure_tags: list[string] (may be empty)
- output_digest: string (sha256 of normalized output)
- annotation_verdict: string (match|partial|mismatch|not_applicable)
- annotation_notes: string
- cost_usd_estimate: float

Table: recommended thresholds and alerting rules
| Metric | Warning threshold | Critical threshold | Alert owner |
| Latency 95th | > 1200 ms | > 2000 ms | eng-serving-runtime |
| Cache hit ratio (median) | < 0.6 | < 0.4 | eng-serving-runtime |
| Mismatch rate (slice) | > 3% | > 7% | applied-ml |
| Token generation cost (avg) | > $0.015/token | > $0.03/token | finance-legal |

Annotation and labeling guidelines:
- Labelers must be provided the anchor, probe, and model output side‑by‑side.
- Use the tolerance window concept: a model can satisfy a probe if the required entity/intent appears within N tokens/frames (N determined per probe type).
- Assign failure_tags using the canonical taxonomy: {forgetting, misattribution, contradiction, hallucination, truncation, multimodal-mismatch}.
- For multimodal references, require linkability: the output must reference the correct image/frame id from the anchor.

Privacy and data handling:
- All session_anchor_hash values must be HMACed with an evaluation key stored in the secrets manager; do not store raw PII.
- Synthetic probe generation must not be seeded with customer‑owned textual content unless explicit consent exists.
- Telemetry retention: raw events retained for 30 days in hot storage, 365 days in compressed audited archive. Access requires applied-ml-team role.

Shadow orchestration playbook (stepwise):
1. Prepare candidate probe set and priority lanes (critical, representative, low-risk).
2. Create a shadow deployment: route 0.1-1% of mirrored traffic to shadow cluster for a 24‑48h smoke test.
3. Run combined replay: for heavy long‑context probes, use replay worker to flood the shadow cluster with synthetic sequences at controlled throughput to exercise KV cold/warm states.
4. Collect telemetry and annotations asynchronously; do not add blocking to live requests.
5. Run automated checks: mismatch rate per slice, latency degradation per model_version, cache behavior drift.
6. If checks pass, expand to 5–10% traffic with extended probes for 7–14 days.
7. Final promotion gating: pass SLOs, reviewer signoff (applied‑ml + SRE), and privacy checklist.

Traffic stitching and replay constraints:
- Stitching must preserve inter‑arrival time distributions for representative lanes; synthetic bursts allowed for stress lanes but tagged as such.
- Maintain separate telemetry tags: stitched=true|false, synthetic=true|false, stress_test=true|false.
- Use replay windows to avoid violating customer rate limits or user‑facing SLAs.

Quality gates and rollbacks:
- Hard gates: 95p latency regression > 20% on representative lanes triggers immediate rollback.
- Soft gates: mismatch rate increase > 0.5% triggers investigation workflow but may not auto-rollback.
- Rollback procedure: revert route config, mark model_version as quarantined, create regression ticket with probe references and primary telemetry digests.

Operational considerations and ownership:
- Ownership: applied-ml owns probe catalog and annotation quality. eng-serving-runtime owns runtime telemetry and alerting. eng-sre coordinates shadow routing and safe rollout windows.
- SLOs for eval infra: telemetry ingestion 99.9% within 30s, probe replay worker availability 99% monthly.

Troubleshooting quick list:
- If cache_hit_ratio drops unexpectedly: check KV eviction logs, recent infra changes, and quantized kernel rollouts.
- If annotation backlog grows: spin up labeler elastic workers, throttle synthetic generation, and prioritize critical lanes.
- If output_digest collision rate spikes: confirm normalization pipeline and dedup heuristics.

Examples and snippets:
- Telemetry ingestion CLI (example):
  rinf telemetry ingest --source replay-worker --file probes_batch.json --env staging

- Minimal synthetic probe JSON (single line example):
  {"probe_id":"probe-20241115-001", "anchor":"[doc pages 1-14] ...", "continuation_instruction":"Answer with the list of referenced figures and their captions."}

- Example analysis query (pseudo-SQL):
  SELECT probe_id, model_version, AVG(latency_ms) as p95_latency, SUM(failure_tag='forgetting') as forgetting_count
  FROM telemetry_events
  WHERE stitched=false AND synthetic=false AND start_timestamp >= '2025-01-01'
  GROUP BY probe_id, model_version

Release notes and iteration plan:
- v1.0 (2024-11): baseline probe types, telemetry schema, and shadow playbook.
- v1.1 (2025-01): added multimodal linkability checks, cost_estimate fields, and privacy hardening.
- Next: integrate automatic root cause attribution hooks with regression bisect tool.

Appendix: canonical probe taxonomy (short):
- Coherence-lapse: long-range entity consistency failures.
- Multimodal-mismatch: incorrect image/frame grounding.
- KV-thrash: performance and correctness failures caused by KV cache churn.
- Intent-drift: model shifts intent interpretation mid-session.

Contacts and escalation:
- Applied ML oncall: applied-ml-oncall@redwood.ai
- Eng serving runtime: runtime-ops@redwood.ai
- Evaluation owner: Maya Thompson (maya@redwood.ai)

Related documents and references:
- See eval mesh and workload fingerprinting for scheduling ties.
- See regression triage playbooks for incident investigation linkage.

Document history:
- 2024-11-15: created by Maya Thompson
- 2025-01-08: expanded telemetry schema and added release notes

title: Ensemble calibration and explainable trust scoring
content:
SUMMARY
  -------
  This playbook describes a standard, reproducible pipeline for (1) calibrating evaluator ensembles, and (2) producing an explainable per-response trust score used by downstream routing, canary gating, and alerting. The document covers terms, data and probe requirements, model-agnostic calibration recipes (temperature scaling, isotonic regression), ensemble aggregation strategies, explainability primitives (feature contributions, provenance tokens), verification tests, and operational runbook items.

  WHY THIS EXISTS
  ----------------
  As Redwood supports heterogeneous model variants (full precision, quantized, KV-cache-optimized) and multiple evaluator models (ML-based quality predictors, heuristics, human raters), teams need a single canonical scoring contract that:
  - Produces well-calibrated probabilities that map to real-world error rates (e.g., P(failure) ~ observed failure frequency).
  - Is robust across workload slices and domains (multilingual, multimodal, long-context).
  - Yields explainable signals that can be surfaced in dashboards and used for triage/rollback decisions.

  SCOPE
  -----
  - Applies to evaluator ensembles used in shadow-eval, canary gating, and automated rollback pipelines.
  - Not intended for training production generation models; only for downstream evaluators and meta-decision systems.

  KEY TERMS
  ---------
  - Trust score: calibrated probability in [0,1] that an evaluated response meets the acceptance criterion for a slice (higher = more trustworthy).
  - Ensemble: logical combination of multiple evaluators (model-based, heuristic, human label) producing one trust score.
  - Calibration: post-hoc transform to align predictive probabilities with empirical frequencies.
  - Slice: workload partition defined by intent, language, prompt family, or tenant.

  ACCEPTANCE CONTRACT
  -------------------
  For an ensemble to be promoted to production gating, the following targets must be met on the holdout probe set for each critical slice:
  - Brier score <= 0.12 (weighted by slice importance)
  - Reliability diagram slope within 5% of ideal across 10 probability buckets
  - Predictive-AUROC >= 0.86 for binary failure detection
  - 95% bootstrap CI on predicted failure rate width <= 0.04
  If any threshold is missed, the ensemble must be flagged for remediation and follow the regression triage runbook (see related_pages).

  DATA & PROBE REQUIREMENTS
  -------------------------
  1) Probe composition
     - Minimum 500 examples per critical slice; for low-volume slices use stratified resampling and synthetic augmentation (see section on augmentation heuristics).
     - At least 3 independent human annotations per probe; retain raw annotator IDs and timestamps.
     - Annotator calibration: Cohen's kappa >= 0.7 against anchor gold set.
  2) Feature telemetry recorded
     - evaluator_scores: raw per-evaluator logits/probabilities
     - input_metadata: model_variant, context_length, client_tier, tenant_id (redacted if required)
     - provenance_tokens: contiguous token ranges identified as high-influence by the evaluator (optional for privacy-sensitive slices)

  ENSEMBLE ARCHITECTURE PATTERNS
  ------------------------------
  We recommend the following logical patterns depending on use-case:
  - Weighted mean (fast, interpretable): trust = sum(w_i * p_i) / sum(w_i). Use when evaluators are independent and have stable per-slice reliability.
  - Calibrated stacking (meta-learner): train a small logistic/regression stacker on holdout probes to combine outputs and covariates (context length, language). Use when evaluators have complementary strengths.
  - Conservative gating (safe-by-default): if any evaluator reports p_failure > 0.95, force trust <= 0.05 (fail-fast). Useful for high-risk financial/legal slices.

  CALIBRATION RECIPES
  -------------------
  Apply transforms per-slice when possible; global calibration is acceptable for homogenous workloads.

  1) Temperature scaling (logits required)
     - Fit a single scalar T on validation set by minimizing negative log likelihood (NLL).
     - Implementation: use Adam (lr=0.01) with 1000 steps; early stop if val NLL doesn't improve for 50 steps.
     - CLI example:
       python tools/calibrate_temperature.py --logits logs/ensemble_logits.pkl --labels probes/labels.csv --out calibrated/T.pkl
  2) Isotonic regression (probabilities)
