     - Non-parametric; useful for small datasets where monotonicity is expected.
     - Use sklearn.isotonic.IsotonicRegression with out_of_bounds='clip'.
  3) Platt scaling (sigmoid)
     - Logistic transform; faster than isotonic for small feature sets.

  EXPLAINABILITY & SIGNALS
  ------------------------
  Provide the following artifacts per scored response:
  - top_contributors: list of evaluator IDs with contribution delta to trust score (format: evaluator_id|delta)
  - highlight_spans: token ranges that shifted the score > threshold (store as start:end indices)
  - calibration_bucket: one of {0.0-0.1,...,0.9-1.0}
  Example JSON payload (trimmed):
  {"trust_score": 0.12, "top_contributors": ["e1|+0.05","heuristic-mismatch|+0.03"], "highlight_spans": ["12:27"]}

  VERIFICATION & TESTS
  --------------------
  Run these checks after calibration:
  - Reliability diagram generation for each slice and archive image in artifact storage (see artifacts/docs/reliability/).
  - Brier decomposition (calibration vs refinement) and automated triage rules:
    - If calibration component > 60% of Brier score, prioritize calibration-focused fixes (more probe data or isotonic).
  - Synthetic adversarial sweep: apply 3 perturbations per prompt family and assert trust delta < 0.2 for stable slices.

  OPERATIONAL PIPELINE
  --------------------
  1) Ingest new probes -> store raw telemetry in eval-fs.
  2) Run per-evaluator scoring (batch) -> persist logits/probs.
  3) Fit calibration transforms per-slice -> save artifacts to model-registry under namespace "eval-calib/{ensemble}/{date}".
  4) Recompute ensemble scores on validation probes and produce report (automated PR to owners).
  5) If acceptance contract passes, mark artifact as promotable and publish trust scoring config to routing service.

  MONITORING & ALERTING
  ---------------------
  Dashboard widgets (Redwood Console):
  - Slice-level mean trust and 7d trend
  - Calibration drift metric (Kullback-Leibler of bucketed histograms) per slice
  Alerting rules:
  - P1: calibration drift > 0.08 over 24h for any slice -> PagerDuty to eval-oncall
  - P2: drop in predictive-AUROC > 0.07 vs baseline -> Slack to #eval-notify

  ROLLOUT CHECKLIST FOR PROMOTION
  -------------------------------
  - [ ] Holdout probes archived and checksums recorded
  - [ ] Calibration artifacts uploaded to model-registry
  - [ ] Explainability artifacts validated on 200 examples
  - [ ] Runbook entry created linking to ensemble config and owner contacts

  TROUBLESHOOTING COMMON FAILURE MODES
  -----------------------------------
  - Low Brier but high false negative rate on minority slice:
    - Action: increase probe representation, retrain slice-aware stacker, or use conservative gating.
  - High calibration component (isotonic overfitting):
    - Action: switch to temperature scaling or regularize isotonic with monotone bin merging.
  - Annotator drift:
    - Action: refresh anchor gold set; run annotator re-certification workflow.

  OWNERSHIP & CONTACTS
  --------------------
  - Primary owner: applied-ml team (Maya Chen)
  - Evaluator infra owner: eng-platform (Arjun Patel)
  - Oncall: eval-oncall rotation (see People Directory)

  REFERENCES & ARTIFACTS
  ---------------------
  - Notebook: notebooks/ensemble_calib/reliability_report.ipynb
  - Tooling: tools/calibrate_temperature.py, tools/isotonic_pipeline.py
  - Related pages: see top of doc

  APPENDIX: QUICK CONFIG EXAMPLE
  -----------------------------
  pipeline: "ensemble-trust-v1"
  slices:
    - id: "billing-critical"
      calibrator: "temperature"
      min_probe: 1000
      weight: 1.5
    - id: "web-chat-longcontext"
      calibrator: "isotonic"
      min_probe: 500
      weight: 1.0

  NOTES
  -----
  - This playbook is intentionally conservative. Use the conservative-gating pattern for data-sensitive slices (finance, healthcare) by default.
  - Revisit calibration cadence quarterly or after any major model variant roll.

  CHANGELOG
  ---------
  2027-03-05: Initial published playbook and verification rules (Maya Chen).

title: Real-time Rerank Eval and Quant Fallback Operational Spec
content:
Summary:
This operational spec defines the evaluation harness, probe generation, metric thresholds, and automated fallback procedures for deploying quantized model variants of the real-time rerank pipeline (service name: rerank-service). The goal is to allow safe promotion of quantized rerankers into production traffic with automated detection and graceful fallback to full-precision variants when quality or latency SLOs degrade.

Scope:
- Applies to rerank-service endpoints behind the inference gateway (route: /v1/rerank).
- Covers shadow evaluations, canary rollout, automated monitoring, and rollback.
- Includes quantized variants (int8/4-bit hybrid) and mixed-precision fallbacks.
- Excludes offline batch re-ranking jobs and non-rerank ranking pipelines.

Key terminology:
- Probe: a synthetic or sampled request used to measure quality and latency.
- Shadow run: mirrored traffic evaluated against target model without affecting user responses.
- NDCG-delta: change in NDCG@10 versus baseline model.
- Quant-gatekeeper: the component that decides whether to route requests to quantized variant.

Stakeholders and ownership:
- Service owner: Search & Ranking team (primary oncall: @search-ranking-oncall).
- Eval harness owner: Applied ML (owner: Priya Nair).
- Observability: Eng Platform (dashboards: rerank/quantization-eval).
- Rollout approvals: Product + Applied ML for market-impacting models.

SLOs and acceptance criteria (must be met in shadow + canary phases):
- Latency SLO (production): P95 <= 50 ms for single-query rerank at 128 tokens, P99 <= 120 ms.
- Latency impact (quantized vs baseline): P95 delta <= +10 ms.
- Quality SLO: NDCG@10 delta >= -0.007 (i.e., loss must be < 0.007 absolute).
- Hallucination / safety sentinel: flagged rates must not increase by >0.2% absolute.
- Tokenization fidelity: OOV token rate change < 0.05%.

Metric telemetry and thresholds to publish to the console:
- ndcg_at_10, ndcg_delta, rerank_latency_ms_p95, rerank_latency_ms_p99, tokens_generated, hallucination_signal_rate, oov_rate, quant_error_rate.
- Alert rules (examples):
  - high-quality-delta: trigger if ndcg_delta < -0.007 for 5m rolling window AND sample-size >= 2000.
  - latency-regression: trigger if rerank_latency_ms_p95 increase > +12 ms vs baseline for 10m.

Probe synthesis strategy (how we create test traffic):
1) Seeded shadow probes: sample 10% of production queries with user-consented telemetry flags and mirror to shadow-sequencer.
2) Synthetic perturbations: augment real queries with adversarial paraphrases and long-context extensions to stress KV-cache and quantization.
3) Rare-slice amplification: upsample low-frequency slices (locale=en-IN, conversational multi-turn) to reach minimum statistical power.

Probe composition and size guidance:
- Minimum per evaluation window: 5k probes across slices.
- Recommended slice allocation: 60% head queries, 30% medium-tail, 10% longtail/edgecases.
- Time windows: rolling 1h for latency, rolling 24h for quality stability before canary promotion.

Quant-sensitivity test matrix (example):
| Variant | Bits | KV cache enabled | Target SLO notes | Acceptance delta |
| Baseline | fp16 | yes | Reference | 0.0 |
| int8-ldq | 8 | yes | Expected minimal fidelity loss | ndcg >= -0.005 |
| hybrid-4+8 | mixed | yes | aggressive cost trade | ndcg >= -0.007 and latency <= +8ms |
| int4-edge | 4 | limited | experimental, only shadow | ndcg >= -0.01 and manual review |

Automated evaluation pipeline (high-level):
1) build-artifact: produce quantized model artifact and push to artifact repo (artifact tag: rerank/{model}:{quant-profile}:{sha}).
2) smoke-run: run local throughput + deterministic-output checks (tool: evaluator-sdk smoke-run).
3) shadow-run: replay probes via shadow-sequencer to quant variant. Collect metrics to telemetry-ingest and evaluator-db.
4) aggregation: compute slice-level metrics (ndcg, latency percentiles, hallucination rate).
5) gate decision: quant-gatekeeper consults rules engine and posts recommended action to rollout-service.

Example CI job config (YAML):
job_name: rerank-quant-eval
cron: "*/30 * * * *"
steps:
  - name: download-artifact
    run: |
      aws s3 cp s3://artifacts/rerank/${MODEL_TAG}.tar.gz .
  - name: run-shadow
    run: |
      evaluator-sdk run --config configs/rerank-shadow.yaml --artifact ${MODEL_TAG} --out /tmp/results.json
  - name: upload-results
    run: |
      curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_API_TOKEN" -F results=@/tmp/results.json https://eval-orchestrator.internal/api/results

Rollout & canary process (step-by-step):
1) Shadow-only (48h): quant variant must pass shadow acceptance across all high-priority slices.
2) Micro-canary (0.5% traffic for 6h): route 0.5% user traffic through quant-gatekeeper with real-time comparison telemetry collected.
3) Ramp (0.5 -> 5 -> 20%): increase only if quality and latency remain within thresholds at each checkpoint (24h windows at each stage).
4) Full promotion: require stakeholder sign-off and documentation of observed deltas and mitigation plan.

Automated fallback & rollback behavior:
- If alert high-quality-delta or latency-regression fires during canary/ramp, quant-gatekeeper will automatically route new requests to baseline for the affected region + model and open a high-priority incident.
- Fallback TTL: immediate re-route for 60 minutes; the rollout-service pauses ramps until manual review.
- For transient anomalies (blips <5m with <1% probes affected) hold and continue monitoring; do not auto-rollback unless condition persists for 10m and sample-size > 500.

Triage playbook for failures (oncall steps):
1) Acknowledge pager and pull up rerank/quantization-eval dashboard.
2) Confirm which slices triggered the alert and query sample IDs.
3) Run evaluator-sdk isolate --slice <slice_id> --artifact <artifact_tag> to reproduce locally.
4) If quant-error suspected, trigger auto-fallback (rerankctl fallback --artifact <artifact_tag> --region <region>).
5) Postmortem: capture root cause, affected slice, mitigation steps, and rollback timeline.

Example CLI snippets (for oncall):
# Check recent ndcg deltas
curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/api/metrics?name=ndcg_delta&service=rerank-service&window=1h" | jq .
# Trigger a targeted fallback
rerankctl fallback --model rerank_v2026 --profile hybrid-4+8 --slice locale=en-IN

Evaluation report template (required before full promotion):
- Artifact tag:
- Shadow window (start/end):
- Probe volume by slice:
- NDCG@10 baseline vs quant (table):
- Latency P95/P99 comparison (table):
- Safety sentinel comparison (table):
- Known limitations & edge cases:
- Recommended action (promote / widen shadow / rollback):

Privacy and data handling:
- All shadow probes must follow the privacy budget policy: PII redaction enabled, retention 7d for probe payloads, annotation artifacts stored with encryption at rest.
- Rare-slice amplification must not include user-identifiable content — use redacted proxies or synthetic variants.

Testing checklist before on-call signoff:
- [ ] Smoke-run passed with deterministic checks.
- [ ] Shadow-run completed with required probe counts per slice.
- [ ] No slice-level ndcg_delta breaches for 24h.
- [ ] Latency regression within limits for 24h.
- [ ] Documentation of expected cost delta and deployment runbook.

References and related pages:
- evaluator-sdk README: internal link (evaluator-sdk docs).
- Quant profile playbooks (see related_pages above).
- rerank-service runbook: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/rerank-service-runbook-2025.json

Appendix: quick troubleshooting matrix
- Symptom: increased ndcg_delta on locale=en-IN only -> Action: inspect tokenization differences between artifacts, run tokenization-diff tool, verify vocab alignment.
- Symptom: P95 latency increase -> Action: check batching behavior, KV-cache hit rate, and hardware scheduling (gpu-util).

Contact list:
- Applied ML (owner): priya.nair@redwood.ai
- Search & Ranking oncall: search-ranking-oncall@redwood.ai
- Observability: monitoring@redwood.ai

Document changelog:
- 2026-02-08: Created initial spec (Priya Nair).
- 2026-03-01: Added automated fallback TTL rules and updated acceptance thresholds (reviewers: Ethan Chen, Maya Ortiz).

title: Probe Pruning and Adaptive Sampling Playbook
content:
Summary

This playbook defines the probe pruning and adaptive sampling system used by the Eval Harness to keep continuous evaluations cost-effective while preserving signal for regression detection. It formalizes: probe scoring, pruning thresholds, an adaptive sampler that reallocates budget to high-variance slices, scheduler policies for burst/steady modes, and a safe rollout path for any changes.

Motivation

Large-scale continuous evaluation produces a long tail of low-value probes (very stable slices, duplicated semantics, or highly correlated prompts) that consume budget and increase noise in alerting. By pruning probes and adaptively sampling, we achieve:
- 30–60% reduction in probe execution cost for stable workloads
- Faster regression detection on volatile slices
- Lower false-positive alert rates from noisy low-variance probes

Scope

This document applies to:
- The Eval Harness scheduler (service: eval-sequencer)
- Probe catalog artifacts (probe registry and metadata)
- Continuous monitors and alerting rules tied to eval-sentinels

Not in scope: manual one-off experiments, offline research-curated benchmark runs.

Definitions

- Probe: a single stimulus (prompt + context) executed against a model variant and recorded with outputs and telemetry.
- Slice: logical grouping of probes (e.g., language, intent, length bucket).
- Stability score: running statistic (0..1) where 1 == perfectly stable across N recent runs.
- Importance score: business-weight multiplier (0.1..10) assigned by owners.

High-level architecture

1) Probe registry enriches probes with base metadata (slice, created_at, owner_team, importance).
2) Eval-sequencer assigns probes to worker queues according to adaptive-sample policy.
3) Pruner service periodically marks probes as "prune_candidate" based on scoring rules and retention config.
4) Audit logger records all prune actions and supports rehydration for 90 days.

Key metrics and thresholds (recommended defaults)

- Metric: Stability score (rolling 30-day window)
  - Thresholds: stable if >= 0.98, semi-stable if 0.95–0.98, unstable if < 0.95
- Metric: Sample variance (per-slice)
  - Action: reallocate +20% budget to slices with variance in top 10%
- Metric: Duplicate similarity (embeddings cosine)
  - Prune if cosine >= 0.995 to a higher-ranked probe in same slice
- Minimum retained probes per slice: 50 (unless slice cardinality < 50)

Pruning ruleset (ordered)

1) Structural deduplication: within a slice, group probes with embedding cosine >= 0.995 and keep the highest-importance/most-recent item.
2) Stability floor: for probes with stability >= 0.99 and age > 21 days, mark prune_candidate.
3) Low-importance culling: importance <= 0.2 and stability >= 0.97 -> prune if slice has > minimum retained probes.
4) Manual holdouts: probes with flag "do_not_prune" are preserved.

Adaptive sampling algorithm (overview)

The adaptive sampler reallocates probe budget per scheduling epoch (default 24h) based on per-slice signal. Steps:
- Compute per-slice priority = mean(importance * max(1, variance_score * 10)) * recent_violation_factor
- Normalize priorities to available budget (tokens / probe cost estimate)
- Ensure hard floor: every slice must receive >= 1% of epoch budget unless explicitly disabled

Pseudocode:

for each epoch:
  load slices S
  for s in S:
    compute importance_s, variance_s, violation_factor_s
    priority_s = importance_s * max(1, variance_s * 10) * violation_factor_s
  scale priorities so sum(priority) == epoch_budget
  assign probes to queue respecting per-slice minimums and per-probe dedup constraints

Scheduler policies

- Steady mode: evenly distributed probes across 24h with jitter; used for baselining.
- Burst mode: directed execution for top-K priority slices when on-call triage requests immediate re-eval or after new model rollout. Burst windows capped at 2h and require SRE approval.
- Canary mode: small fraction (default 2%) of new probe templates are exercised for 72h before being added to main catalog.

Configuration example (YAML snippet)

# eval-sampler-config.yaml
epoch_period: 24h
min_slice_budget_pct: 0.01
min_probes_per_slice: 50
stability_window_days: 30
dedup_cosine_threshold: 0.995
burst_mode_max_window: 2h
canary_fraction: 0.02
prune_scan_interval: 48h
prune_retention_days: 90

Rollout and change control

Any change to pruning thresholds or adaptive sampler weights must follow this path:
1) Draft change proposal in the eval-harness repo with benchmarks (description, config diff, expected savings/risks).
2) Submit PR and tag reviewers from applied-ml-and-evals and eng-sre.
3) Run controlled experiment (A/B) for 7 days: 10% traffic on new config vs 90% control. Record: detection latency for seeded regressions, cost delta, alert noise.
4) If experiment meets pass criteria (<=5% degradation in detection latency, >=10% cost improvement, no increase in high-severity alerts), schedule staged rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 7 days with monitoring gates.
5) Post-rollout retrospective and update playbook if necessary.

Pass/fail gate checklist for A/B

- Regression detection latency: no more than 5% worse than control
- Alert precision on top-10 slices: not decreased by >3 percentage points
- Cost per epoch: >=10% improvement expected; if less, require product sign-off
- No increase in customer-facing incidents attributed to eval changes

Operational runbook (quick actions)

- If critical slice goes missing from schedule:
  1) Query pruner audit logs: "pruner.events?probe_id=<id>"
  2) Rehydrate probe from archival store (rehydrator CLI): "rehydrator restore --probe <id> --reason emergency"
  3) Temporarily mark slice as "holdout" in probe registry and set min_slice_budget_pct to 0.05
- If adaptive sampler is starving a high-importance slice:
  1) Pause prune job: "kubectl scale deployment/pruner --replicas=0 -n eval"
  2) Manually bump importance for affected slice in registry UI or via API
  3) Re-run epoch with debug logging enabled and capture schedule plan

Observability and alerts

Monitor these dashboards and alerts:
- Dashboard: Eval Sampling Overview (latency, cost, per-slice budget allocation)
- Alert: eval-sampler:budget-deviation > 25% for 2 epochs -> paged to applied-ml-oncall
- Alert: prune:unexpected-retention-drop when retained_probes_count < 60% expected -> pager
- Alert: canary-failures: > 3 seeded-regressions missed in 72h -> paged to product-owner and applied-ml-oncall

Data retention and auditability

- Pruner decisions are logged in audit store for 90 days.
- Full probe artifacts (inputs, outputs, embeddings) retained for 365 days for investigations.
- Rehydration API supports re-executing archived probes against historical models for reproducibility.

Safety & false-positive mitigation

- Never prune a probe used in a currently open incident ticket.
- Prioritize retention of probes tagged as regulatory or compliance-critical.
- For any prune action that would drop a probe with importance >= 5, require two approvers (applied-ml lead + product).

Troubleshooting checklist

- Symptom: sudden drop in per-slice probe count
  - Check prune job logs for recent sweeps and decisions.
  - Verify dedup threshold change in config history.
- Symptom: missed seeded regression in canary
  - Inspect canary fraction; confirm canary traffic was delivered.
  - Increase canary_fraction to 5% for next experiment if flakiness persists.

Ownership and contacts

- System owner: applied-ml-and-evals team (oncall: applied-ml-oncall rotation)
- Pruner service owner: runtime-quality squad (primary: Marcus Nguyen)
- Scheduler owner: eval-platform squad (primary: Aisha Patel)
- SRE escalation: eng-sre oncall (see runbook for page routing)

Appendices

A. Example dedup query (CLI)

# Find duplicates within slice=faq
probe-embeddings search --slice faq --similarity-threshold 0.995 --output csv | head -n 50

B. Example schedule inspection API

GET /api/v1/scheduler/plan?epoch=2026-02-09T00:00:00Z
Response fields: slice_id, assigned_probes, estimated_cost_tokens, priority_score

C. Change log
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft and internal review (Priya Shah)
- 2026-01-05: Added burst/canary policies and safe rollout gates (Liam O'Connor)
- 2026-02-10: Tightened dedup cosine default to 0.995 and clarified rehydration retention (Sofia Martinez)

If you have questions, file an issue in the eval-harness repo and tag @applied-ml-and-evals.

title: Baseline Telemetry Anchoring and Eval Seed Management
content:
Overview

This document defines Redwood's baseline telemetry anchoring approach and a standardized eval seed management lifecycle. It is intended for ML engineers, SREs, and applied ML owners responsible for evaluation stability, promotion gating, and regression triage. The goal is to reduce spurious variance in continuous evals and make failure modes easier to diagnose by controlling seed sources, telemetry baselines, and anchoring strategies across private/dedicated/hosted targets.

Why this matters

- Small changes in RNG seeds, tokenization seeding, and probe sampling can inflate perceived variance and trigger false positive regressions.
- Anchored telemetry provides a persistent baseline that is resilient to benign nondeterminism while still surfacing meaningful quality regressions.
- Standardized seed management enables reproducible replays for triage and quantization regression investigations.

Scope and assumptions

- Applies to production-facing eval harnesses, long-running shadow evals, and nightly synthesis jobs used for model promotion decisions.
- Does not replace deterministic unit tests or model-level determinism efforts — it complements them by controlling sampling and anchoring at the eval orchestration layer.
- Assumes eval platform can accept explicit RNG seeds and deterministic dataset shuffling parameters.

Key concepts and definitions

- Anchor set: a small, curated subset of probes used as a stable reference point (typical size: 500–2,000 probes depending on workload).
- Seed manifest: a versioned file that enumerates RNG seeds, shuffle salts, and the indices used to sample anchors and dynamic probes.
- Telemetry anchor vector: the vector of baseline metric values (e.g., BLEU, ROUGE, semantic-similarity, latency median) computed over the anchor set for a given model artifact and promotion point.
- Seed rotation window: controlled cadence for refreshing the seed manifest (default: quarterly for anchors, weekly for synthetic probes).

Guidelines and requirements

1) Anchor set creation and stewardship
   - Ownership: each product or workload team must nominate an anchor steward (primary + backup).
   - Composition: anchors must cover: 
     * 60% high-frequency, high-impact real traffic slices
     * 25% edge / long-tail / adversarial seeds identified from incidents
     * 15% synthetic stress probes (long context, function calls, multimodal where applicable)
   - Annotation: each anchor must have a metadata row (probe id | slice | origin | rationale | sensitivity flag). Use the anchor manifest template in the examples section below.

2) Seed manifest format and storage
   - Format: JSONL or CSV with columns: manifest_version, seed_id, rng_seed, shuffle_salt, probe_indices, created_by, created_at, role (anchor|dynamic|synthetic).
   - Storage: manifests are stored in the eval bucket under path: s3://redwood-evals/manifests/{team}/{workload}/{manifest_version}. Lock each manifest with an immutable tag once used for a promotion gate.

3) Telemetry anchoring calculation
   - Metric computation: compute telemetry anchor vector using the exact seed manifest and the same model runtime config (quant, kv-cache policy, batch config).
   - Aggregation: report median and 10/90 percentiles for latency; mean and std for quality metrics where meaningful.
   - Baseline window: maintain a rolling baseline history for the last 6 promotion points. Use EWMA with alpha=0.2 to smooth short-lived fluctuations.

4) Seed rotation and freshness policy
   - Anchor rotation: rotate anchor indices no more frequently than every 90 days unless a triggered incident requires emergency replacement. Document reason and vote in the rotation changelog.
   - Dynamic seed refresh: dynamic probe seed manifests may be refreshed weekly for sampling diversity; each refresh must have a different manifest_version and be recorded in telemetry.

5) Promotion and gating protocol
   - Promotion gate input: automated promotion jobs must reference an immutable manifest_version. The gate compares the new candidate telemetry anchor vector against the preserved baseline vector.
   - Acceptance criteria: candidate model must not show a statistically significant degradation on more than N slices in the anchor set (N defaults to 2 for 500-1k anchor size). Use bootstrap resampling (B=1,000) and require p > 0.05 for no-regression.
   - Quality-coverage check: if a candidate improves aggregate metrics but worsens a high-sensitivity anchor (sensitivity flag set), require a product sign-off.

6) Reproducible replay for triage
   - Repro command: provide the exact CLI and environment file to replay an anchor run. Example: 
     
     eval-run --manifest s3://redwood-evals/manifests/vision-team/recommendation/v3-manifest-2026-01-12.jsonl \n       --model-ref model-registry://prod/recommendation/v2.3.1 \n       --runtime-config runtimes/quantized-gpu.yaml \n       --replay-output /tmp/replays/replay-20260210-001.jsonl

   - Determinism checklist:
     1. Use the exact manifest_version.
     2. Use pinned model artifact digest (not tag).
     3. Use the same runtime image and kernel revision.
     4. Record and compare seed hash between original and replayed runs.

Operational playbooks

- Daily smoke: the eval platform posts a daily anchor vector summary to #eval-telemetry. On-call evaluator checks for any drift >2x EWMA sigma on critical anchors.

- Regression triage fast path:
  1. Triage engineer compares candidate anchor vector to baseline and runs reproducible replay using the manifest_version.
  2. If replay reproduces regression, attach replay artifacts to a regression issue and assign to model owner.
  3. If replay does not reproduce, escalate to platform SRE to check runtime/kernel/version mismatch, quant artifact mismatch, or nondeterministic RNG sources.

- Emergency anchor replacement: when anchor probes are found compromised (PII leak, invalidated by product change), the steward can replace up to 10% of anchors outside regular rotation. Log a post-hoc review within 48 hours.

Metrics, SLOs and alerts

- Anchor stability SLO: 99% of daily anchor vector differences must be within the EWMA 3-sigma band across a 30-day window.
- Alerting: create PagerDuty alert when:
  * a single critical anchor drops by >5% absolute in quality or increases latency by >50% p95, or
  * more than 3 anchors cross the statistical regression threshold during a promotion attempt.

Examples and templates

- Anchor manifest snippet (JSONL row):
  {"manifest_version": "anchor-v1-2026-01", "seed_id": "anchor-0001", "rng_seed": "9823749283", "shuffle_salt": "slt-04", "probe_indices": "[13,56,234,1021]", "created_by": "aisha.patel@redwood.ai", "created_at": "2026-01-10", "role": "anchor"}

- Example telemetry anchor table (text table):
  | probe_slice | metric | baseline_value | candidate_value | delta | sensitivity | action |
  | high-frequency-search | semantic-sim | 0.842 | 0.835 | -0.007 | high | product-review |
  | long-context-chain | pass-rate | 0.912 | 0.885 | -0.027 | critical | block-promotion |

- Runtime config YAML excerpt (used for replay):
  image: gcr.io/redwood-eval-images/eval-runtime:2026-01-28
  kernel_rev: k1.7.3
  quant_profile: 8bit-lora-v2
  kv_cache_policy: preserve-full

Roles and responsibilities

- Anchor steward (team): maintains anchor set, manages seed manifest lifecycle, documents rotation rationale.
- Model owner: validates candidate regressions and approves or rejects promotion after triage.
- Eval platform SRE: ensures manifest immutability, provides replay tooling, and diagnoses nondeterministic platform causes.
- Applied ML ops: monitors anchor SLOs and coordinates cross-team investigations.

Change log and governance

- All manifest changes require an entry in the manifest-changelog.md and a 2-person review (steward + product or senior ML engineer).
- Governance board: triage council meets monthly to review anchor slippage trends and approve exceptional rotations.

Appendix: small reproducibility checklist

- Confirm manifest_version and seed hash
- Confirm model digest (sha256) and runtime image digest
- Confirm quant/precision flags used in the original run
- Re-run replay with debug telemetry enabled (token-level hashes, deterministic RNG) for 3 runs and compare inter-run variance

Related artifacts and references

- eval-provenance spec (linked in related_pages)
- regression-impact-index (linked in related_pages)
- Replayer CLI docs: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/replayer-cli

Contact and ownership

For questions or to nominate an anchor steward, contact: aisha.patel@redwood.ai or join #eval-telemetry on Slack.

title: Eval snapshot & checkpoint strategy for reproducible replay and rollback
content:
Overview
--------
This document defines Redwood's standardized approach to taking, storing, and using evaluation snapshots and checkpoints across the eval harness, prompt/benchmark sets, model onboarding flows, quantization experiments, and regression triage. The objective is to ensure exact, auditable replays of eval runs for: root-cause analysis, regression bisecting, audit reviews, and safe rollbacks to previously validated artifacts.

Audience
--------
- Applied ML engineers running batch and interactive evals
- Platform and SRE teams supporting storage and replay infra
- Model onboarding owners and QA engineers
- Incident responders in regression triage

Goals
-----
1) Guarantee bit-for-bit replay of any eval or benchmark run within the retention window.
2) Minimize size and operational cost of snapshots while preserving required fidelity.
3) Provide clear CLI and API primitives for taking snapshots, restoring checkpoints, and executing replay jobs.
4) Integrate snapshot metadata with model promotion gates and quantization profiles.
5) Ensure snapshots are discoverable and usable for automated regression bisect tooling.

Scope and non-goals
------------------
- Scope: eval-harness executions (both scheduled and ad-hoc), prompt set executions, quantization experiment runs, on-boarding shadow runs, and regression-triage reproductions.
- Non-goal: long-term cold archival (>1 year) — archival policy is handled by compliance with separate retention exports.

Key concepts and definitions
---------------------------
- Snapshot: a compact, self-describing artifact that contains inputs (prompts, seed, config), deterministic RNG state, environment pin (container image + runtime hash), model artifact id & weights checksum, and optional KV-cache prefix samples.
- Checkpoint: periodic model-serving state during long-running evals (e.g., warm-up cache snapshots, per-shard KV state) used to accelerate partial replays.
- Replay Job: an execution that consumes a Snapshot/Checkpoint and runs the eval in a controlled, deterministic environment, producing an identical token stream and telemetry.
- Fidelity Modes: `minimal`, `prompt-plus-config`, `full` — controls how much auxiliary telemetry and KV data are stored.

Snapshot manifest (required fields)
-----------------------------------
All snapshots must include a top-level manifest with the following fields:

| field | required | type | description |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| manifest_version | yes | string | semantic version of snapshot schema (e.g. "1.0.0") |
| snapshot_id | yes | string | UUID v4 |
| created_by | yes | string | username or service principal |
| created_at | yes | YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ | UTC ISO timestamp |
| run_type | yes | string | {batch, interactive, shadow, quant-experiment, triage} |
| model_artifact_id | yes | string | model identifier + pinned weights checksum (sha256) |
| model_variant | yes | string | e.g. `fp16-q8_0` or `gptx-7b` |
| prompt_set_id | conditional | string | if the run consumed a named prompt set |
| seed | conditional | int | RNG seed used for deterministic ops |
| fidelity_mode | yes | string | {minimal,prompt-plus-config,full} |
| artifacts | yes | list[string] | signed URLs or storage keys for payloads (prompts, kv-dumps, logs) |
| env_hash | yes | string | container image digest / runtime artifact hash |
| checksums | yes | list[string] | checksums for each artifact |

Example manifest (JSON snippet)
------------------------------
{  "manifest_version": "1.0.0",  "snapshot_id": "7f3e2c4a-2d4a-4f1a-b8d3-9a1e4b0d1c2f",  "created_by": "applied-ml/eval-scheduler",  "created_at": "2026-02-09T21:41:12Z",  "run_type": "batch",  "model_artifact_id": "redwood/gptx-7b@sha256:abcd...",  "model_variant": "fp16-q8_0",  "prompt_set_id": "semantic-anchoring-v2",  "seed": "420420",  "fidelity_mode": "prompt-plus-config",  "artifacts": ["s3://eval-snapshots/7f3e2c4a/prompts.ndjson", "s3://eval-snapshots/7f3e2c4a/response-headers.json"],  "env_hash": "registry.redwood.local/runtime:sha256:ff12...",  "checksums": ["prompts.ndjson:sha256:...", "response-headers.json:sha256:..."]}

Storage and retention rules
--------------------------
- Default retention: 90 days for `prompt-plus-config` and `minimal`; 180 days for `full` fidelity snapshots.
- Snapshots must be stored in the region where the run originated to respect data residency.
- Size caps: single snapshot <= 5GB for `minimal`, <= 50GB for `full`. If a run would exceed caps, the harness must reject with an explainable error and suggest `prompt sampling` or `trim-kv` options.
- All artifacts must be content-addressed and checksummed. The manifest contains signed URLs valid for 7 days; long-term access requires the snapshot_id reference to the object store.

When to take a snapshot (triggering policy)
-------------------------------------------
1) Mandatory triggers:
   - Production model promotion candidate runs (all fidelity modes must be `full`).
   - Any run that triggers a promo gate failure (quality guardrail alert).
2) Recommended triggers:
   - Quantization profile generation and cross-workload transfer tests.
   - Shadow/on-boarding validation runs.
   - End-of-week scheduled benchmark sweep.
3) On-demand: manual snapshot via CLI/API for ad-hoc triage.

Snapshot creation CLI examples
----------------------------
# Create snapshot for a scheduled job (minimal fidelity)
redwood-eval snapshot create --job-id=job-1234 --fidelity=minimal --output=s3://eval-snapshots/

# Create a full snapshot including KV caches (may be large)
redwood-eval snapshot create --job-id=job-1234 --fidelity=full --include-kv --encrypt-kms=projects/redwood/kms/key1

Deterministic replay constraints
--------------------------------
To guarantee identical token streams across replay runs, replays must satisfy: 
- Same model artifact checksum and variant.
- Same runtime env_hash and compatible GPU/CPU instruction set.
- RNG seed fixed and deterministic software paths (no telemetry-based randomization).
- Disk/networked artifact fetch must use checksummed content; any cache layers must be either replayed from checkpoint or disabled.

Integrations with other subsystems
---------------------------------
- Eval Harness: snapshot APIs are first-class primitives; every harness job exposes `snapshot.create`, `snapshot.list`, `snapshot.replay` endpoints.
- Model Onboarding: onboarding playbooks must reference snapshot_id for final promotion meetings. Promotion pipeline will fail if no `full` snapshot exists for the final regression sweep.
- Quality Guardrails: alerts generated by the guardrail service should attach `snapshot_id` when present so triage can immediately replay the offending run.
- Quantization: quantization experiments must store both pre- and post-quant snapshots with `fidelity=prompt-plus-config` to facilitate difference comparisons.

Regression triage runbook (short)
---------------------------------
1) Intake: from guardrail alert or customer ticket, capture snapshot_id from alert.
2) Quick replay (minimal fidelity): run `redwood-eval snapshot replay --id=<snapshot_id> --fidelity=minimal --dry-run` to confirm reproducibility.
3) If mismatch observed, perform `redwood-eval snapshot replay --id=<snapshot_id> --fidelity=full --attach-kv` and collect diffs of token stream and logits.
4) Bisect: if recent commits are suspected, use `snapshot-bisect` tool which replays the snapshot across candidate model_artifact_ids to find first differing artifact.
5) Escalate: if bisect identifies a regression, open a regression triage ticket with `snapshot_id`, diffs, and the bisect result.

Example bisect command
----------------------
redwood-eval bisect --snapshot=7f3e2c4a-... --candidates=redwood/gptx-7b@sha256:[a..z] --metric=semantic-similarity --threshold=0.85

Recording telemetry and audit fields
-----------------------------------
During snapshot creation, the harness must record and attach:
- SLOs and latencies observed (p99, p50), token counts, error rates
- Resource footprint (GPU memory, batch-size distribution)
- Guardrail evaluation results (pass/fail + trigger details)
- Operator notes (free text)
These fields should also be surfaced in the snapshot manifest under `artifacts` as small JSONs.

Safety, privacy, and PII handling
--------------------------------
- If prompts or responses contain PII, snapshot creation must mark `confidentiality: restricted` and the snapshot must be encrypted with customer KMS if requested.
- By default snapshots redact auth headers and full customer identifiers but retain hash pointers for traceability.

Operational metrics and SLOs for snapshot service
------------------------------------------------
- Snapshot create latency: 90% <= 120s for `minimal`; 90% <= 20m for `full` (large KV dumps).
- Snapshot list API: 99% <= 500ms.
- Replay success rate: 99.9% (replays that finish and validate checksums).
- Storage cost budget: snapshot storage should not exceed 4% of eval infra spend (tracked monthly).

Ownership and escalation
-----------------------
- Primary: Applied ML (eval-harness) team (oncall: eval-harness@redwood.com).
- Secondary: Platform infra (storage and KMS).
- For replay failures that block customer-facing rollouts, escalate to Eng SRE with priority P0.

Open items and roadmap
----------------------
- Binary diff format for optimized KV snapshots (Q2 2026).
- Cross-region snapshot replication for multi-region promotion tests (Q3 2026).
- Tight integration with regression bisect assistant (ML-powered) to suggest likely commit candidates.

Appendix A — Example minimal replay manifest (ndjson)
----------------------------------------------------
{ "prompt": "Summarize the following email: ...", "seed": 420420, "context_hash": "sha256:..." }
{ "response": "In summary, ..." }

Appendix B — Troubleshooting checklist
-------------------------------------
- If replay fails with env mismatch: verify `env_hash` and pull container image digest.
- If token stream differs: ensure seed was recorded and that quantization bit-level parity was preserved.
- If KV-cache-dependent behavior differs: re-run with attached `--attach-kv` and check timestamps.

References
----------
- See eval harness API docs: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/evaluator-interchange-format-and-federation-spec-2026
- Model onboarding acceptance matrix: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/holistic-acceptance-matrix-for-model-promotion-2026
- Regression investigation handbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026

Contact
-------
For questions about the snapshot schema or to request exceptions, contact the Applied ML team: applied-ml@redwood.com

title: Hybrid Probe Fabrication and Traceability Guide
content:
Summary
---
This document defines a repeatable process for fabricating evaluation probes (synthetic examples), anchoring them to production traffic, and tracking provenance so that mixed synthetic/real evals (hybrid fusion) are auditable and actionable. It is intended for ML engineers, evaluation owners, and SREs running the eval-orchestrator and probe-farm services.

Motivation
---
Teams increasingly rely on hybrid evaluation runs that mix synthetic probes with shadowed production samples to stress-test models across quality and latency SLOs. Without a standard fabrication and provenance process, regressions are hard to triage, sample bias proliferates, and remediation is slower. This guide specifies design patterns, metadata, sampling rules, and triage playbook steps to address those gaps.

Scope
---
- Applies to: probe generation for text-only and multi-turn chat workloads evaluated by eval-orchestrator and shadow-sequencer.
- Not covered: human labeling details (see label-runbook), legal data-retention constraints (see security-and-compliance).

Key Principles
---
1. Anchoring-first: Every synthetic probe must have at least one anchor (production-derived exemplar) or a documented rationale for synthetic-only creation.
2. Deterministic provenance: Probes are immutable artifacts with stable IDs, creation metadata, and hash signatures.
3. Reproducible fusion: Hybrid runs must record fusion policy and the exact seed set used for sampling.
4. Minimally invasive: Probes should not alter production routing or customer-visible metrics.

Definitions
---
- Probe: A single evaluation input (prompt + context + optional metadata) used by the eval-harness.
- Anchor: A production-derived exemplar (anonymized) that a probe is designed to mimic or stress.
- Fusion policy: A declarative rule that defines how many probes vs. production samples are mixed, with weighting and prioritization.
- Provenance record: Machine-readable metadata that accompanies a probe through creation, storage, and evaluation.

Fabrication Procedure (step-by-step)
---
1) Identify target slices
   - Use telemetry-driven hotspot reports from probe-farm: top failing slices by semantic-stability and kv-cache-miss-rate.
   - Prioritize slices with high traffic and high business impact (example: chat-assistant/checkout).
2) Select anchors
   - Query shadow-logs for exemplars matching slice criteria (service: product-signal-collector).
   - Anonymize PII using scrub-tool v2.1; retain conversational structure and token positions.
3) Draft synthetic probe variants
   - Create at least three perturbation families: lexical swaps, priming (few-shot adjustments), and coherence breaks.
   - For prompt templates, parameterize slots and list expected valid continuations.
4) Run local micro-simulation
   - Use evaluator-adapter local runner with flag --seed=<stable-seed> and --kv-warmup=3. Confirm deterministic artifact hash.
5) Review and sign-off
   - Submit a probe bundle for review via the probe-review workflow (label: probe-eval-needed). Reviewer checklist: anchor match, privacy scrub, coverage matrix.
6) Publish to probe-farm
   - Upload via CLI: probectl publish --bundle <bundle.tgz> --provenance-json <meta.json>

Anchoring Strategy and Examples
---
- Soft anchor: probe captures distributional properties (length, role sequence, topic) but not lexically identical content.
- Hard anchor: probe is a close paraphrase of a production exemplar used to reproduce a specific failure mode.

Example: Hard-anchor mapping
- Anchor id: PROD-2025-08-17-9f1b
- Probe id: PROBE-HARD-2026-00042
- Rationale: Reproduces truncated completion observed for long-context checkout flow.

Provenance Metadata Schema (required fields)
---
All probe bundles must include a provenance file named provenance.json. Required fields: probe_id, created_by, created_at (UTC), anchor_ids (list), bundle_hash (SHA256), semantic_slice (string), privacy_level (one of 'anonymized' or 'synthetic-only'), fusion_compat (policy id), seed (string). Optional: notes.

Telemetry and Sampling Configurations
---
Attach a sampling manifest for hybrid runs. Example (yaml-like):

fusion_policy:
  name: 'balanced-weighted-1:3'
  description: '1 probe for every 3 shadowed production samples; prefer probes when slice-specific failures present'
  weights:
    probes: 0.25
    production_shadows: 0.75
  max_probe_replication: 4
  kv_warmup: 2
  latency_priority: true

Operational thresholds (used by eval-orchestrator):
- semantic-stability drop alert: greater than 3.0 percentage points relative to baseline
- 95th latency regression: greater than 20% relative increase or absolute > 250ms
- coherence-index (CI) drop: greater than 2.5 points

Runbook: Investigating a Hybrid Run Regression
---
1) Triage summary (owner: eval-oncall)
   - Fetch run snapshot: evalctl snapshot --run-id <id>
   - Evaluate top failing slices by semantic-stability and error-classification tags.
2) Confirm provenance
   - For each failing probe, open provenance.json and validate bundle_hash against artifact storage.
   - If probe is anchored: retrieve anchor exemplar via safe-anchor-retriever --id <anchor_id> and verify anonymization.
3) Reproduce locally
   - Re-run probe bundle with same seed and kv warmup to check determinism: evaluator-run --bundle <bundle> --seed <seed> --replay-mode deterministic
   - If non-deterministic, tag with 'non-deterministic' and escalate to runtime-team.
4) Quick mitigation (if quality regression impacts customers)
   - Roll back to previous model variant via rollout-service. Document rollback in incident ticket.
5) Deep analysis
   - Compare attention maps, token-level logprobs, and KV-cache hit profiles across failing probes and anchors using probe-analysis-tool --run <run-id> --diff anchors.

Failure modes specific to hybrid fusion
---
- Anchor leakage: synthetic probe accidentally contains customer-identifying tokens. Mitigation: automated scrub and manual reviewer confirmation.
- Overfitting to anchor templates: probes too similar to anchors produce false positives; require perturbation families >= 3.
- Sampling bias: fusion policy skew causes undercoverage of critical production traffic. Mitigation: periodic calibration against production holdout.

Promotion and Acceptance Criteria
---
A probe bundle or hybrid-run may be used for promotion when all of the following are met:
- At least 90% of artifact hashes reproduce deterministically in local replay.
- Semantic-stability baseline is within 1.5 percentage points of anchor baseline for the same slice.
- Privacy scan returns zero PII flags.
- Two reviewers have approved via probe-review workflow.

Tooling and CLI snippets
---
Publish a bundle:
  probectl publish --bundle ./checkout-probes-v1.tgz --provenance ./provenance.json --tags 'slice:checkout,owner:payments'
Run a hybrid sim locally:
  eval-orchestrator local-run --fusion-manifest ./fusion.yaml --bundle ./checkout-probes-v1.tgz --seed 42
Fetch anchor exemplar (anonymized):
  safe-anchor-retriever get --id PROD-2025-08-17-9f1b --redact true

Ownership and SLAs
---
- Probe fabrication and provenance storage: probe-stewardship team (rotating on-call).
- Eval runs and immediate triage: eval-oncall (SLO: acknowledge within 1 business hour).
- Audit retention for provenance records: 365 days by default (configurable).

Appendix A - Example provenance (text)
---
{ 'probe_id': 'PROBE-HYB-2026-0042', 'created_by': 'maya.chen', 'created_at': '2026-02-03T18:12:09Z', 'anchor_ids': ['PROD-2025-08-17-9f1b'], 'bundle_hash': 'e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924...', 'semantic_slice': 'multiturn-checkout', 'privacy_level': 'anonymized', 'fusion_compat': 'balanced-weighted-1:3', 'seed': '42', 'notes': 'Hard-anchor for truncated completions observed in holiday spike' }

Appendix B - Reviewer checklist
---
- Anchor mapping present and valid (if required)
- Provenance JSON signed and hash matches artifact store
- Privacy scan clean
- Perturbation families >= 3 and coverage matrix attached
- Fusion policy documented

Related pages and references
---
- evaluator-adapter integration docs (/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/evaluator-adapter-patterns-for-private-and-dedicated-2026)
- probe-farm API reference (internal link: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/probe-farm-api)

Revision history
---
- 2025-11-13: Draft created (Maya Chen)
- 2025-12-07: Added fusion policies and telemetry thresholds (Arjun Patel)
- 2026-02-08: Clarified provenance schema and reviewer checklist (Sofia Martínez)

If you have questions or want a live walkthrough, create a ticket and tag @probe-stewardship.

title: Continuous Safety Evaluation Pipeline and Integration Guide
content:
Summary

This page describes the Continuous Safety Evaluation Pipeline (CSEP): a reusable, CI-integrated eval harness designed to catch safety regressions, distributional drift on prompt sets, and quantization-induced failure modes across model rollouts and runtime changes. CSEP unifies prompt selection, metric computation, alerting thresholds, and triage handoffs so that model owners and infra teams can act quickly and reproducibly.

Goals

- Provide a lightweight, actionable pipeline that runs on PRs and nightly schedules.
- Surface both absolute safety violations and relative regressions against a pinned baseline.
- Make triage deterministic: every failing run produces a standardized artifact bundle for forensics.
- Integrate with release gating (canary/rollout) and the model onboarding checklist.

When to use this guide

- New model onboarding (quantized variants included).
- Model or runtime upgrades (e.g., kernel changes, new batching).
- Prompt set expansions or production prompt redistributions.
- Regression investigations triggered by monitoring alerts.

High-level design

CSEP is composed of four stages:

1) Prompt selection and sharding
- Use the prompt catalog (see prompt-sets directory) to pick: safety-critical prompts, high-frequency production prompts, and targeted adversarial cases.
- By default: 60% safety suite, 30% prod-sampled, 10% adversarial.
- Shards are created deterministically using a seed tied to pipeline run id so reruns are idempotent.

2) Execution harness
- Runs requests against specified model variants (float32, int8/quantized, and fallback variants).
- Supports hosted API and dedicated/private endpoints via a unified runner CLI.
- Tracks timing (p95/p99), token counts, and the raw responses.

3) Metric aggregation and regression tests
- Safety metrics include: toxic-span rate, disallowed-instruction triggers, hallucination proxies (entity-mismatch rate), and policy-classifier score distributions.
- Quality metrics include: BLEU/ROUGE-style comparisons when references available, embedding-distance drift (cosine), and length-conditioned perplexity proxies.
- Two comparison modes: absolute thresholds and relative delta to baseline.

4) Artifact generation and alerts
- Pipeline produces a triage bundle: run metadata, raw responses, diffed examples (baseline vs candidate), prompt shards, and a reproducible run config (YAML).
- If checks fail, the pipeline opens a ticket in our tracker with severity and attaches the bundle.

SLOs and thresholds (recommended defaults)

- Safety-critical trigger rate (absolute): <= 0.005 (0.5%) across safety suite.
- Relative safety regression: candidate increase > 30% versus baseline -> fail.
- Prod prompt acceptance drop: mean acceptance (automated classifiers + sample human check) drop > 10% -> warn.
- Token-latency regression: p95 increase > 20% -> warn; p99 increase > 30% -> fail.
- Quantized variant hallucination proxy: relative increase > 15% -> fail.

Note: thresholds are tunable per-customer workload; the pipeline should set the thresholds from the model certification profile stored in the model registry.

CI integration and flow

1) Pull Request checks (fast mode)
- Runs a lightweight shard (4–8 safety prompts, 8 prod-sampled) against candidate and baseline short-circuit.
- Time budget: 5 minutes.
- Outcome: pass/warn/fail comment on PR with summarized metrics and links to full artifacts.

2) Merge/Pre-release (full nightly mode)
- Runs full safety suite + production set + quantization sweep.
- Schedules on the release branch; failure blocks canary rollout.

3) Canary gating
- Canary deploy accepts traffic at 1% if CSEP green. Canary monitored with production telemetry and small quick re-run of CSEP against live traffic-sampled prompts.

Configuration examples

Example pipeline YAML (simplified):

```yaml
pipeline: csep-nightly
version: 1.2
seeds: [20260128]  # deterministic sharding seeds
models:
  - baseline: rwd-v1-34b-fp32
  - candidate: rwd-v2-34b-qat-int8
shards:
  safety_suite: 1200
  production_sample: 5000
  adversarial: 300
cases:
  - name: safety-checks
    checks:
      - toxic_span_rate: {threshold: 0.005, compare: absolute}
      - policy_score: {threshold: 0.85, compare: relative}
```

Runner CLI snippets

- Run a single-model quick pass locally:

  ./csep-runner --model rwd-v2-34b-qat-int8 --shard safety_quick --out ./artifacts/run-2026-01-28

- Run against hosted API with credentials:

  API_KEY=redwood_XXXX ./csep-runner --endpoint=https://api.redwood.ai/generate --config pipeline-nightly.yaml

Artifact bundle contents

Each failed or warning run archives a zip with:
- run-metadata.txt (model ids, commit hashes, seeding, timestamps)
- run-config.yaml (reproducible pipeline config)
- examples/ (CSV with prompt, baseline output, candidate output, metric scores)
- diffs/ (annotated examples highlighting safety failures)
- logs/ (runner logs, low-level request/response traces)
- system-metrics.json (throughput/latency samples for the run)

Triage process (step-by-step)

1) Auto-classify severity
- Severity assignment ruleset maps the failed check to severity: safety-absolute-fail -> Sev1, large relative drift on safety -> Sev1, latency p99 fail -> Sev2, minor prod acceptance warn -> Sev3.

2) Create ticket and assign owner
- Ticket template pre-populated with triage bundle link and suggested owners based on affected model and runtime tags.

3) Reproduce and isolate
- Owner runs the pipeline with narrower scopes: quant-only, kernel-only, prompt-subset, and hardware-variant. Use the deterministic seed to guarantee consistent sharding.

4) Patch/mitigation options
- Immediate rollback to pinned baseline (automated option in deployment pipeline).
- Deploy model with safety filters enabled (policy classifier / response sanitizer) as a temporary mitigation.
- Adjust rollout to 0% and run debugging harness with debug logs (with PII redaction).

5) Postmortem and remediation
- Owner files a short RCA within 72 hours with attachments from the bundle and a remediation plan.
- If root cause is quant/compilation related, schedule a kernel/infra retro and flag the runtime owner.

Quantization-specific checks

- Include paired runs: quantized vs fp32 with identical seeds and input order.
- Compute per-example drift score: embedding cosine drop and policy-score deviation.
- Flag examples where policy score crosses the safety threshold in the quantized model but not in fp32.
- Maintain a per-model quant-tolerance profile saved in model registry.

Operational considerations and cost

- Nightly full runs are costlier; gate them to run only on release branches or when model metadata indicates a high-impact change.
- Use caching for deterministic prompts and prefix-KV where possible to reduce compute costs for repeated runs.
- Archive artifact bundles for 90 days by default; configure S3 lifecycle for longer retention when required for audits.

Ownership and contacts

- Pipeline owner: Applied ML Team (owner contact: priya.nair@redwood.ai)
- Runtime/Kernel owner: Eng Serving Runtime (owner contact: marcos.li@redwood.ai)
- Security & Policy classifier: Security team (owner contact: evelyn.carter@redwood.ai)

Appendices

A: Prompt selection heuristics
- Sampling weights for production prompts should be proportional to 95th-percentile request frequency buckets to ensure heavy-tail coverage.
- Adversarial cases are periodically seeded from the adversarial lab and fuzzers; keep a rotating pool to avoid overfitting the classifier.

B: Example quick checks for PR pipelines (shell snippet)

```bash
# run a quick safety shard in CI
./csep-runner --shard safety_quick --model ${CANDIDATE_MODEL} --baseline ${BASELINE_MODEL} --timeout 300 --output ./ci-artifacts/${CI_BUILD_ID} || exit 1
# summarize and upload artifacts
./csep-summarize --input ./ci-artifacts/${CI_BUILD_ID} --upload s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/${CI_BUILD_ID}
```

C: Monitoring dashboards to create
- CSEP nightly failures by model family (time series)
- Per-check false positive rates (based on sampled human verification)
- Quantization degradation heatmap (model x metric)

D: Related pages and resources
- Model onboarding checklist (link: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/production-model-certification-checklist-2026)
- Prompt catalog index (link: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/production-prompt-catalog-and-stress-bench-2025)

If you are implementing this pipeline and need the runner binary or Helm charts for the on-prem variant, contact the pipeline owner (priya.nair@redwood.ai) or open an infra request ticket in the infra backlog.

title: Longtail Continuous Scan Playbook for Production Evals
content:
Summary

This playbook describes the Longtail Continuous Scan (LCS) process: an automated, prioritized, and privacy-conscious approach to running small, frequent, and broad-spectrum evaluations of models in production-like conditions. LCS targets tail distributions and low-frequency prompt slices that commonly surface quality regressions after deployments, quantization, or major prompt/handler changes.

Scope

- Applies to Redwood studio-managed models and verified open-model variants used in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Covers evaluation orchestration, slicing, scheduling, metric thresholds, alerting, and first-response triage for long-tail failures.
- Excludes heavy offline human-labeling efforts (those are handled by the annotation pipeline documented separately).

Objectives and SLOs

- Detect regression signals originating from: model updates, quantization changes, routing fallback, KV-cache invalidation, and prompt-surface changes.
- Time-to-detect: median 6 hours from the first anomalous tail observation.
- Time-to-triage (initial owner assignment): 2 hours after a severity-2 alert.
- False-positive rate target: < 12% for automated alerts after calibration.

Glossary

- Longtail slice: A prompt/user pattern with low request volume but high business risk (e.g., legal disclaimers, financial templates, multi-step instructions).
- Scan job: A configured run of LCS that samples prompts, model variants, and runtime settings.
- Seedset: Curated minimal prompt examples used to bootstrap a slice.

Architecture overview

1) Controller: Scheduler service that farms jobs to the eval harness.
2) Runner pool: Ephemeral workers that execute model calls (can run against hosted endpoints, dedicated pools, or shadow VPC endpoints).
3) Aggregator: Time-series store and comparator that computes stability metrics and drift signals.
4) Alerting layer: Rule engine that applies thresholds and enriches signals with provenance to emit alerts to PagerDuty/Slack.

Scan types and when to run them

- Smoke Scan (hourly): 100 weighted prompts across high-priority slices. Fast checks for immediate regressions after traffic-shaping or small rollouts.
- Focus Scan (every 6 hours): 500 prompts concentrated on business-critical low-volume slices and recent failing seeds. Includes edge-case adversarial prompts.
- Exploration Scan (daily): 3k prompts sampled stratified by locale, token-length buckets, user-agent signals, and model-quantization variant. Used for drift discovery and slice expansion.

Prioritization and budgeting

- Each customer and route is assigned a priority weight (0-10) by product owners. Priority influences sampling probability.
- GPU budget caps: LCS jobs cannot exceed 8 GPU-hours per region per day by default; request increases via capacity requests.

Data handling and privacy

- Do not store raw customer prompt text unless explicitly consented. All LCS jobs use pseudonymized prompt keys and salted hashing.
- Seedsets that contain customer data must be tagged "PII-sensitive" and routed to a private shadow cluster with KMS-protected logs.
- Logs kept for debug: sanitized prompt hash, token counts, model variant, latency, and top-3 token-probability deltas. Retention: 30 days by default.

Evaluation metrics and thresholds

Primary metrics (automatic):
- Response Stability Index (RSI): measures distributional shift over n-gram/embedding space. Threshold: RSI delta > 0.12 triggers a warning; > 0.25 triggers an incident.
- Semantic Recall (SR): fraction of ground-truth keyphrases present in model outputs for structured tasks. Threshold: drop > 6% (relative) triggers a high-priority alert.
- Safety-Trigger Rate (STR): rate of policy-flagging tokens per 1k responses. Threshold: absolute STR > 4 and increase > 2x baseline triggers immediate review.

Secondary metrics (profiling):
- Median latency (ms), 95th percentile latency, kv-cache hit ratio, and truncated-output rate.

Regression detection heuristics

- Multi-evidence consensus: an alert requires at least two metric classes to exhibit degradation (e.g., RSI + SR), unless the metric is a safety hit.
- Rolling-window confirmation: short blips are suppressed using a 3-sample exponential smoothing prior to alerting.
- Model-variant correlation: anomalies that correlate only with a single variant (e.g., quantized-int8) tag the alert as "quant-suspect".

Triage playbook (first 6 steps)

1) Alert enrichment: The aggregator appends last-known rollout id, model-commit, quant-profile id, and route config.
2) Owner assignment: PagerDuty integration assigns the alert to the model-owner rotation.
3) Immediate checks (automated):
   a) Verify model-commit changed in the last 24 hours.
   b) Check KV cache flush events or recent cache eviction logs.
   c) Examine autoscaler events and pod restarts for the model cluster.
4) Canary rollback: If the regression aligns to the canary rollout id and the rollback window is open, trigger automated rollback to prior canary snapshot.
5) Shadow replay: Launch focused shadow-run against previous known-good variant for 200 seeds. Compare diffs and attach to the ticket.
6) Human review: If automated checks are inconclusive, assign to applied-ml for semantic review and label impacted slices.

Detailed triage checklist (owners should follow):
- Verify reproducibility using the seedset with deterministic RNG.
- Re-run with and without quantization to isolate numeric sensitivity.
- Re-run with cached KV disabled to test cache-sensitivity regressions.
- If safety flags increased, run the safety-deep-eval (1000 synthetic adversarial prompts) before public rollback.

Observability, alert templates, and runbook snippets

Alert template (Slack / PagerDuty summary):
- Title: LCS Alert: {metric} regression on {route} (severity {1|2|3})
- Body: One-line summary, metric deltas, affected model-variants, last rollout id, link to aggregator graph, and link to reproduction job.

Suggested Grafana panels:
- RSI time-series with slice decomposition (lines per locale/token-length).
- SR per variant as bar-chart with error bands.
- Top-10 diffs in token-probability mass as a table.

Automation recipes and example configs

Example LCS job config (YAML, abbreviated):

```
job_id: lcs.focus.20260305
priority_weight: 8
slices:
  - id: legal-disclaimer
    seedset: s3://lcs/seeds/legal-v3.csv
    sample_ratio: 0.6
  - id: financial-templates
    seedset: s3://lcs/seeds/finance-v2.csv
    sample_ratio: 0.3
variants:
  - model: rdx-gpt-13b
    quant_profile: quant-int8-a
  - model: rdx-gpt-13b
    quant_profile: fq-16
budget:
  max_gpu_hours: 2
  max_concurrent_workers: 6
output_policy: hash-only
```

CLI example to kick off a Focus Scan against a private endpoint:

$ rdx-eval run --job-config s3://lcs/configs/lcs.focus.20260305.yaml --target private-shadow --concurrency 4 --tags longtail,focus

Onboarding checklist for a new model into LCS

1) Register model variant and quant profiles with the aggregator catalog.
2) Provide initial seedsets for priority slices (min 40 seeds per slice).
3) Configure run-time limits and private-vpc access if seeds contain customer-derived patterns.
4) Run a baseline Exploration Scan and upload baseline metric snapshots to the baseline store.

Ownership and escalation

- LCS Controller: eng-infra (owner: Priya Gupta)
- Aggregator & rules: applied-ml (owner: Arjun Patel)
- On-call triage: model-owner rotation (list maintained in Oncall Playbook)

Related pages and artifacts

- Seedset schema: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/seedset-schema-spec-2025
- Safety deep-eval: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/continuous-safety-eval-pipeline-and-integration-guide-2026
- Quantization safety checklist: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-failure-modes-and-recovery-playbook-2026

Appendix: sample alert payload (JSON)

{
  "alert_id": "lcs-20260305-8fb2",
  "route": "/api/v1/generate",
  "metric": "RSI",
  "delta": "0.31",
  "top_slices": ["legal-disclaimer", "long-form-instructions"],
  "variants": ["rdx-gpt-13b:quant-int8-a"],
  "links": {"repro_job": "https://internal.redwood/eval/12345"}
}

This playbook will be revised as LCS matures; for questions or improvement proposals, contact the owners listed above.

title: dynamic-slice-creation-and-priority-scheduling-2026
content:
summary:
Operational playbook for automatically generating evaluation slices from telemetry and assigning dynamic priorities to each slice for scheduling in the eval harness. Reduces manual slice engineering, improves coverage of regressions in long-tail traffic, and integrates with existing promotion and rollback gating.

body:
Overview
========
This document defines the dynamic slice creation and priority scheduling system used by the Eval Harness. The goal is to automatically synthesize actionable evaluation slices from production telemetry, score them by risk/impact, and schedule them into the evaluation queue with appropriate cadence and resource allocation. This complements static slice catalogs and reduces time-to-detection for regressions appearing in the long tail.

Motivation
----------
- Static prompt slice catalogs are brittle and require continuous manual maintenance.
- Many regressions surface first in telemetry hotspots or newly emerging user behavior.
- We need a reproducible, auditable pipeline that:
  - translates telemetry signal into candidate slices,
  - ranks candidates by an explainable priority score,
  - schedules slices to the eval harness under capacity constraints, and
  - surfaces actionable reports for triage and remediation.

Scope
-----
This playbook covers:
- Slice candidate generation (signals, heuristics, constraints)
- Priority scoring function and weighting defaults
- Scheduler rules for the eval mesh/orchestrator
- Integration steps for model onboarding and promotion gating
- Monitoring, alerts, and troubleshooting
It does NOT cover human annotation workflows or label pipelines beyond basic sample labeling used for slice verification.

Definitions
-----------
- Candidate slice: a compact selector describing a subset of requests (e.g., metadata + prompt signature + token-length bucket).
- Slice fingerprint: deterministic string used to deduplicate candidates.
- Hotspot: continuous telemetry region exceeding configured thresholds (e.g., error-rate > 2x baseline or latency p95 > SLO).
- Priority score: numeric 0-100 determining scheduling urgency.

Data Sources and Signals
------------------------
Primary signals used to generate candidates:
1. Error telemetry: response errors, function-call failures, safety sentinel hits.
2. Latency anomalies: p50/p95/p99 shifts per model/route/region.
3. Semantic drift indicators: embedding drift, response embedding distance to historical buckets.
4. Volume surges: sudden increase in request share for a specific route or customer.
5. Customer-reported incidents and support tickets (ingested via tag).
6. Canary eval deltas: small canary sets that exhibit performance regressions.

Candidate Generation Algorithm (high level)
-----------------------------------------
1. Ingest normalized telemetry windows (default: 24h, configurable).
2. Identify hotspots by applying per-route baselines and outlier detection (median absolute deviation).
3. For each hotspot, extract candidate selectors:
   - route_id, model_family, customer_tier, locale, device_type, prompt-template-hash, token-length-bucket, top-3 tokens prefix.
4. Generate fingerprint: SHA1(route_id + model_family + template_hash + token_bucket).
5. Deduplicate candidates by fingerprint; keep top-N variants per hotspot (default N=10).
6. Enrich candidates with sample examples and initial lightweight labels (if available).

Priority Scoring (explainable formula)
-------------------------------------
We use a linear combination of normalized signals to produce a 0-100 priority score. Default weights (tunable):
- Impacted volume weight (w_vol) = 0.30
- Error severity weight (w_err) = 0.30
- Model divergence weight (w_div) = 0.20
- Customer SLA sensitivity weight (w_sla) = 0.10
- Freshness / growth weight (w_growth) = 0.10

Score computation (pseudocode):

score = round(100 * clamp( w_vol * norm(volume_percentile) + w_err * norm(error_z) + w_div * norm(embedding_shift) + w_sla * sla_flag + w_growth * growth_rate, 0, 1))

Where:
- norm(x) maps a signal into [0,1] using historical percentiles.
- error_z is z-score relative to model-route historical error mean.
- sla_flag is 1 for enterprise customers with SLA, 0 otherwise.

Priority tiers (operational):
- 80-100: Critical — schedule as high-frequency slot, notify on-call triage.
- 60-79: High — schedule daily batch, include in weekly regression digest.
- 30-59: Medium — schedule weekly with lower resource priority.
- 0-29: Low — schedule opportunistically, aggregated sweeps.

Scheduler Rules and Quotas
--------------------------
- Eval Mesh capacity is expressed as concurrent slice slots per hour.
- By default, 40% of capacity reserved for Critical/High tiers, 40% for Medium, 20% for Low.
- Per-customer cap: no more than 10% of total slots to a single customer unless approved by CS.
- Model-family cap: prevent majority of slots going to a single model family (default 50%).
- Aging policy: slices that do not surface issues within 4 weekly runs are downgraded automatically.

Scheduler pseudo-workflow:
1. Pull prioritized candidate queue, sorted by (priority_score, recency, uniqueness).
2. Apply quota constraints and backpressure.
3. Allocate to eval runners with appropriate resource profile (e.g., long-context -> larger GPU mem).
4. Launch evaluation with attached telemetry replay or synthetic generator.
5. Capture artifact: eval result, failure trace, example requests, and metrics.
6. If eval triggers regression gates, escalate via regression triage (see "Triage handoff").

Integration with Model Onboarding and Promotion Gates
----------------------------------------------------
- New model versions should be shadowed for 72h with an elevated slice sampling weight to detect early regressions.
- Promotion requires no Critical-tier slices failing and < 10% of High-tier slices flagged in the last 7 days.
- The slice system exports a promotion summary: top failing slices, sample counts, error types, impact estimates.
- Use this export as part of the Model Promotion Checklist (link to onboarding page).

Example: scheduling API call (CLI)
--------------------------------
```bash
redwood-evalctl schedule-slice \
  --fingerprint sha1:abc123def \
  --priority 87 \
  --runner-type gpu-large \
  --timeout 3600 \
  --examples-file /tmp/slice-examples.json
```

Promotion decision table (example)
---------------------------------
| Metric | Threshold | Action |
|---|---:|---|
| Critical slices failing | >0 | Block promotion, immediate triage |
| High slices failing | >10% | Hold promotion, require mitigations and re-eval |
| Medium slices failing | >25% | Require justification for promotion |
| Regression severity (avg) | >= 0.7 (on 0-1 scale) | Block and open priority incident |

Monitoring, Alerts, and Dashboards
----------------------------------
Key dashboards to build and monitor:
- Candidate generation volume by route/model (24h, 7d)
- Priority distribution histogram and slot utilization
- Recent failing slices table (with links to artifacts)
- Time-to-detection for newly created slices
Alerting thresholds (examples):
- New Critical-tier slice created with error_rate > 5%: page on-call (P1).
- >3 Critical slices fail within 24h for a single model family: open incident.

Ownership and Roles
-------------------
- Ownership: Applied ML (owner) — maintains heuristics, scoring weights, and integration.
- On-call: Eval Platform SRE — handles scheduling failures, runner capacity issues.
- Triage: Model Quality team — receives failing slice artifacts and coordinates fixes.
- Product/CS: notified for customer-impacting slices.

Rollout Plan
------------
1. Prototype phase (2 weeks): run candidate generator in read-only mode; produce candidates and scored outputs to a review queue.
2. Pilot (4 weeks): enable scheduling for non-critical tiers and a small model subset.
3. Gradual ramp (6 weeks): expand to full model fleet and enable high-priority scheduling.
4. GA: enable promotion gating and integrate with release pipelines.

Operational SLOs for the system
-------------------------------
- Candidate latency: new candidate discovered and scored within 15 minutes of telemetry window close (SLO 90%).
- Scheduling success: scheduled candidates start running within 10 minutes of allocation (SLO 95%).
- Artifact availability: evaluation artifacts available for triage within 10 minutes of job completion (SLO 99%).

Troubleshooting and Runbook (quick)
----------------------------------
Problem: Candidate queue is empty despite high telemetry volume
1. Check ingestion pipeline latency: kafka_consumer_lag > 0?
2. Confirm hotspot detector thresholds were not misconfigured (path: /config/slicing/hotspot-thresholds.yaml).
3. Verify fingerprinting service is healthy; look for rate-limiting errors.

Problem: Scheduler failing to allocate slots
1. Inspect the eval-mesh capacity dashboard; check for node drains.
2. Verify per-model caps are not saturated.
3. Check runner pod logs (/var/log/eval-runner/*).

Auditing and Safety
------------------
- Every candidate and scheduling decision is logged to the audit index with: fingerprint, input signals, score breakdown, scheduled-run-id, and owner.
- Slice fingerprints that involve customer PII are redacted; if redaction removes determinism, use deterministic surrogate keys.
- Security review required for any change that increases sampling for customer data beyond a configured threshold.

Appendices
---------
A. Example candidate JSON (simplified)
```json
{
  "fingerprint": "sha1:abc123def",
  "route_id": "chat-completion:v2",
  "model_family": "redwood-rlf-13b",
  "selectors": {"locale":"en-US","token_bucket":"64-128","template_hash":"t3_4f"},
  "signals": {"volume_pct":0.021,"error_z":2.7,"embedding_shift":0.35},
  "priority_score": 88
}
```
B. Default thresholds (config path: /config/slicing/defaults.yaml)
| key | value | notes |
| hotspot_window | 24h | sliding window used for detection |
| max_candidates_per_hotspot | 10 | prevents explosion |
| critical_threshold | 80 | priority >= this is critical |

C. Links and references
- Eval harness: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026
- Regression triage playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-01-15: Created by Aisha Patel (prototype spec).
- 2026-02-10: Updated scoring weights and scheduler quotas after pilot feedback.

title: Evaluation Provenance Ledger and Mixed-Precision Rollout Manifest
content:
summary:
Defines a canonical provenance ledger format for evaluation artifacts and prescribes a guarded rollout checklist for mixed-precision (quantized) deployments. The goal is reproducible artifact lineage, rapid triage of regressions introduced by precision changes, and clear telemetry to drive safe rollouts.

body:
Overview
This document defines the evaluation provenance ledger (EPL) schema, storage conventions, and an operational manifest for rolling mixed-precision model variants (e.g., FP16 -> INT8 or hybrid quant) through our eval and shadow environments before production promotion. It bridges eval-harness outputs, model-onboarding checkpoints, and runtime telemetry used by regression triage.

Scope
- Applies to all evaluations and probes used for model promotion, shadow validation, and regression bisecting for mixed-precision and quant-migration efforts.
- Covers: provenance records produced by the eval-harness, artifact storage paths, hash and signing conventions, telemetry fields required by triage runbooks, and the staged rollout checklist.
- Excludes: training data lineage (handled by Data Platform) and customer PII transformation rules (see privacy sandbox docs).

Why a ledger matters
- Reproducibility: Every eval artifact must map to an immutable record so a failing probe can be replayed against the exact artifact and runtime.
- Triage speed: Standardized fields let the regression-hunting automation correlate anomalies to runtime/kernel/quant changes.
- Auditing: Rollout manifest provides a compact audit trail for mixed-precision migrations required by compliance.

EPL (Evaluation Provenance Ledger) record format
- Each evaluation run MUST emit an EPL record and push it to the artifacts index. The record is a small YAML/JSON metadata file stored next to artifacts. Example (YAML):

  eval_id: "epl-2026-000124"
  timestamp: "2026-02-09T21:16:03Z"
  probe_set_id: "priming-cohort-v3"
  model_suite: "redwood-small-7b"
  model_commit: "6a3b9c2"
  model_build_tag: "redwood-small-7b:2026-02-01"
  quant_profile_version: "qpv-2026-01-15-int8-hedge-v2"
  runtime_fingerprint: "runt-fw-1.8.2+kernels-2026-01-20"
  runtime_bin_sha: "sha256:4f9a8e..."
  seed_and_rng: "seed=20260209-42"
  dataset_hashes:
    - "prompts:sha256:ab12..."
    - "labels:sha256:9f3d..."
  batch_profile: "microburst-16-lowlatency"
  kv_cache_config: "enabled,cache_ttl=30m"
  host_gpu_arch: "nvidia-h100-80gb"
  docker_image: "redwood/eval-runner:v1.27"
  artifacts_url: "s3://eval-artifacts/epl-2026-000124/"
  metrics_summary:
    - "embedding_stability:0.012"
    - "coherence_delta:-0.03"
    - "latency_p95_ms:128"
    - "token_cost_delta_per_1k:0.74"
  signature: "sig:v1:base64..."

Notes on the record format and constraints:
- All hashes use sha256 and are hex-prefixed.
- quant_profile_version must reference a formal quant profile artifact from the quant registry.
- runtime_fingerprint encodes serving runtime major/minor, kernel set date, and any experimental flags.
