- signature is an HMAC-SHA256 over the canonicalized YAML; signing key is the eval-harness service key (rotated quarterly).

Storage and naming conventions
- Artifact path template: s3://eval-artifacts/{year}/{model_suite}/{eval_id}/
- EPL metadata is saved as metadata.yaml next to artifacts and copied into the artifacts index database.
- Retention: metadata kept indefinitely; large artifacts kept for 90 days by default, with TTL extensions for promoted runs.

Searchable index fields (required)
- eval_id, model_suite, model_commit, quant_profile_version, probe_set_id, timestamp, host_gpu_arch, runtime_bin_sha, artifacts_url.
- Index entries MUST include a small metrics vector (embedding_stability, coherence_delta, latency_p95_ms) for fast queries.

Rollout manifest: staged promotion for mixed-precision variants
Purpose: Reduce blast radius when deploying quantized variants and ensure each stage is reversible with traceable provenance.

Rollout stages (numbered checklist)
1) Local dev & micro-evals
   - Owner: model-onboarding team
   - Run: full EPL metadata produced for the quant profile against a mini-probe set (N=500).
   - Acceptance: no coherence_delta worse than -0.05; embedding_stability <= 0.02.
2) Shadow (isolated shadow mesh)
   - Owner: eval-harness + serving-runtime
   - Run: shadow traffic replay for 48 hours with replica ratio 1:1000; collect EPL and streaming telemetry.
   - Acceptance: pass functional sentinels (safety/hedge tests), latency_p95 within 1.25x baseline, no token_cost_delta > +1.5x.
3) Canary (tenant-limited rolling canary)
   - Owner: platform ops
   - Run: 48–72 hours, ramp to 3% traffic segmented by low-risk tenants; EPL records must link to each canary snapshot.
   - Acceptance: per-tenant quality thresholds: NPS-equivalent probe acceptance rate >= 98%, embedding drift < 0.03, no SEV on functioncall stability.
4) Multi-tenant confidence window
   - Owner: product + platform
   - Run: 7 days at 10–20% traffic; additional human-in-the-loop review for flagged probes.
   - Acceptance: no priority regressions, ops runbook readiness validated.
5) Full promotion
   - Owner: release lead
   - Run: promote artifact tag to catalog and mark EPL provenance as promoted (promoted=true). Update retention policy to 1 year.

Rollback triggers (automated)
- Any SEV-level alert mapped to the promoted artifact_runtime_bin_sha within the last 2 hours.
- embedding_stability delta > 0.05 vs baseline for 5-minute rolling window.
- sustained latency_p95 > 2x baseline for > 10 minutes.

Rollback procedure (numbered)
1) Mark artifact as blocked in the model catalog and set promoted=false.
2) Trigger automated routing policy: shift traffic to the last known good commit according to EPL history.
3) Notify stakeholders: #ops-oncall, model-owner, product. Include eval_id and artifacts_url in message.
4) Open regression investigation ticket and attach EPL metadata, telemetry snapshot, and failing probe list.

Triaging with the EPL: a step-by-step example
1) Detection: alert for rise in functioncall failure rate. Alert payload includes runtime_bin_sha and recent eval_ids.
2) Correlate: query the artifacts index for eval runs with matching runtime_bin_sha and quant_profile_version within the last 7 days.
3) Reproduce: fetch metadata.yaml and artifacts_url for the top candidate eval_id, reproduce the run locally using docker_image and seed_and_rng.
4) Isolate: run the same probe set under FP16 and the candidate quant profile; collect metric diffs.
5) Hypothesis: if failure maps to a kernel mismatch, escalate to kernel team; if mapping to quant_profile_version, use quant rollback checklist.

Telemetry fields required by regression automation
- eval_id (string)
- runtime_bin_sha (string)
- quant_profile_version (string)
- host_gpu_arch (string)
- probe_set_id (string)
- embedding_stability (float)
- coherence_delta (float)
- functioncall_error_rate (float)
- latency_p95_ms (float)
- token_cost_delta_per_1k (float)

Operational playbook snippets
- Quick repro CLI (example):
  docker run --rm -v /tmp/artifacts:/artifacts redwood/eval-runner:v1.27 \
    --eval-id epl-2026-000124 --probes /artifacts/prompts.json --model-tag redwood-small-7b:2026-02-01 \
    --quant-profile qpv-2026-01-15-int8-hedge-v2 --seed 20260209-42 --out /artifacts/replay_result.json

- Checking a provenance record: (jq-friendly example)
  aws s3 cp s3://eval-artifacts/2026/redwood-small-7b/epl-2026-000124/metadata.yaml - | yq e . - && jq .metrics_summary replay_result.json

Security and signing
- All EPL records for canary or promoted runs MUST be signed by the eval-runner service using the eval-harness key.
- Access to artifact buckets requires role-based ACLs: read for platform and model-onboarding; write only by eval-harness service principal.

Governance and review cadence
- Every quarter, the model-onboarding and quant teams run a review of promoted EPL records and collect lessons into a quarterly migration report.
- Any promoted quant profile with two or more production incidents in a quarter must be paused and triaged under the cross-team incident process.

Appendix: Example queries and dashboards
- Minimal dashboard panels to create in Grafana:
  - "EPL Promotions": count of promoted=true by week, filterable by model_suite and quant_profile_version.
  - "Embedding Stability Heatmap": avg embedding_stability by probe_set_id and quant_profile_version.
  - "Runtime Fingerprint Error Correlation": time-series of functioncall_error_rate annotated with runtime_bin_sha changes.

- Helpful index queries (Elasticsearch-style):
  POST /epl-index/_search
  {"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"term": {"runtime_bin_sha": "sha256:4f9a8e..."}}, {"range": {"timestamp": {"gte": "now-7d/d"}}}]}}}

Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: Aisha Patel (Applied ML - Eval Harness)
- Secondary: Diego Morales (Model Onboarding)
- Oncall escalation: see /oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process for paging details.

Change log
- 2026-01-12: Draft created (Aisha Patel).
- 2026-01-28: Added signing and storage constraints (reviewer: Maya Chen).
- 2026-02-10: Added rollout acceptance numbers and automation-triggered rollback rules (reviewer: Liam O'Connor).

Related references
- quant-profile registry: /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles (internal index)
- model catalog tagging guidelines: /product-docs/requirements/model-catalog-tagging
- regression triage runbook: /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/eval-oncall-runbook-for-model-regression-debugging-2026

If you are implementing EPL emission in a new eval runner, open a PR that includes: schema validation tests, signing integration, and at least one sample metadata.yaml for a real probe run.

title: Runtime Shadow Rehearsal and Localized Probe Synthesis Playbook
content:
Summary

This playbook defines the runtime "shadow rehearsal" pattern: an operationalized workflow that (1) synthesizes localized evaluation probes targeted at tenant cohorts, locales, and latency bands; (2) runs those probes in a low-risk shadow mesh against quantized and mixed-precision artifacts; and (3) performs cost-aware rehearsal passes that validate quality, latency, and coherence before a real rollout. The goal is to detect regressions and quant-induced degradations earlier while bounding evaluation cost and preserving tenant privacy.

Scope

- Applies to model promotion and quantized rollouts for text generation and multi-turn chat services (service names: eval-orch, shadow-mesh, rehearsal-runner).
- Covers probe generation, seed selection, rehearsal execution, gating metrics, and rollback triggers.
- Intended for on-prem, private VPC, and hosted Dedicated deployments.

Why this pattern

- Longtail and locale-specific regressions often escape coarse global evals. Localized probes increase sensitivity to per-tenant failure modes.
- Running rehearsals against quantized artifacts in a shadow mesh simulates production mixing without impacting production traffic.
- Cost-aware caps and staged rehearsal passes allow teams to validate risk under budget constraints.

High-level components

1) Probe Fabricator (probe-fabricator)
   - Responsible for localized probe synthesis: locale-aware lexical meshes, few-shot priming templates, and context anchors.
   - Inputs: seed traffic fingerprints, tenant taxonomy, priming registry, localization lexicons.
2) Shadow Mesh (shadow-mesh)
   - Lightweight runtime that replays probes against quantized variants and the nominal FP32 baseline.
   - Provides instrumentation (response_coherence, fidelity_delta, q_loss, latency_p95, token_emissions).
3) Rehearsal Runner (rehearsal-runner)
   - Orchestrates rehearsal passes, enforces cost caps, aggregates metrics, and writes rehearsal artifacts to eval-orch ledger.
4) Gating Engine
   - Applies SLOs and guardrail rules. Produces pass/fail verdicts and recommended rollout decisions.

Localized probe synthesis strategy

- Taxonomy partitioning: split the tenant base into cohorts along three orthogonal axes: locale (en-US, en-GB, fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP), intent surface (support, search, compose), and latency band (fast p95 < 150ms, medium 150–500ms, slow > 500ms).
- For each cohort generate probes across these buckets:
  - 40% anchor probes (real user anonymized seeds sampled from last 90 days)
  - 40% synthetic perturbations (paraphrases, tokenization edgecases, punctuation/noise injection)
  - 20% adversarial variants (contrastive prompts designed to stress hallucination and instruction-following)
- Probe counts per rehearsal pass are configurable; default targeted sample: 1k probes per cohort for small services, 10k for high-volume services.

Privacy and provenance

- Anchor probes must be redacted and hashed before leaving telemetry storage (hash-salt per rehearsal job). Raw PII is never exported.
- Provenance metadata attached to each probe includes cohort_id, seed_hash, probe_type, and priming_template_id.

Rehearsal execution modes (staged passes)

1) Dry-run (low-cost smoke)
   - Run: 1–2% of full probe set, quant variants only, no baseline comparison.
   - Purpose: surface obvious failures and infra incompatibilities. Cost cap: $X/day (set by team).
2) Contrast-pass
   - Run: 20% sample, run against FP32 baseline and quant variant(s). Compute fidelity_delta metrics and delta-significance tests.
3) Full-rehearsal
   - Run: 100% probe set, cohort-balanced. Includes heavier metrics (token-level divergence, functioncall stability).

Gating metrics and thresholds

We compute both statistical and decisionable thresholds. Primary signals:

- fidelity_delta (KL-style scoring + templated semantic similarity): fail if cohort mean fidelity_delta > 0.12 and throughput-corrected CI excludes zero.
- response_coherence (annotator-simulated score 0–1): fail if cohort P90 < 0.70 and drop vs baseline > 0.08.
- q_loss (quantization artifact score): fail if absolute q_loss increase > 0.05 and correlated with token_emission anomalies.
- latency_p95: fail if latency_p95 increase > 2x and exceeds target SLO band for that cohort.
- embedding_stability (for retrieval/rerank): fail if cosine shift > 0.06 on average for critical slices.

Decision matrix (simplified)

- If any cohort fails fidelity_delta AND response_coherence -> abort rollout for that cohort and open regression ticket.
- If only latency_p95 regression observed but coherence preserved -> engage ops throttling + capacity reroute and run narrow replay.
- If q_loss is high but coherence preserved for anchor-probes -> schedule quant-tuning pass and run targeted micro-rehearsal.

Runbook: step-by-step rehearsal for a scheduled quant rollout

1) Preflight (owner: ModelOnboard Team)
   - Create rehearsal job in eval-orch: include cohort list, probe budget, quant-variant ids, and expected cost cap.
   - Run quick smoke locally with rehearsal-runner dry-run mode: run command below.
2) Dry-run review (owner: Release Lead)
   - Confirm no infra errors in shadow-mesh logs, check instrumentation counters (request_e2e_errors < 0.5%).
3) Contrast-pass (owner: Evaluation Engineers)
   - Run contrast-pass, collect fidelity_delta, response_coherence, and q_loss.
4) Analysis (owner: Applied ML)
   - Run automated delta-significance test (see CLI step). Produce report, tag failing cohorts.
5) Decision (owner: Release Lead + Product)
   - If no failing cohorts -> proceed to phased production rollout.
   - If some cohorts fail -> open triage (link created) and either rollback quant artifact or schedule micro-tunings.
6) Post-rehearsal monitoring (owner: SRE)
   - Enable rehearsal-derived sentinels for 72 hours post-rollout and maintain elevated sampling of failed cohorts.

CLI examples

# Start a dry-run rehearsal (example)
rehearsal-runner start --job-id rjr-20260712-01 --cohorts en-US:support:fast,de-DE:compose:medium --mode dry-run --probe-budget 200 --quant-variant qv-2.1 --cost-cap 200

# Run contrast-pass and upload report
rehearsal-runner start --job-id rjr-20260712-02 --mode contrast --probe-budget 2000 --quant-variant qv-2.1 --baseline mv-1.0 --report-bucket s3://eval-orch/reports/rjr-20260712-02

YAML rehearsal job manifest (example)

job_id: rjr-20260712-02
owner: model-onboard
cohorts:
  - id: en-US-support-fast
    locale: en-US
    intent: support
    latency_band: fast
    probe_target: 1000
  - id: de-DE-compose-medium
    locale: de-DE
    intent: compose
    latency_band: medium
    probe_target: 1000
quant_variants:
  - qv-2.1
baseline: mv-1.0
mode: contrast
cost_cap_usd: "1500"
retention_days: "30"

Interpretation and reporting

- Reports include cohort-level summaries, ranked failure slices, example failing probes, and suggested remediation actions. Attachments include raw witness tokens (hashed) and aggregated diff visualizations.
- Use the provided report template (report-template-v2) for consistency.

Cost control and budgeting

- Rehearsal-runner enforces a hard cost cap at job-level. If cost consumption reaches 90% of cap during a mid-pass, execution pauses, and a partial report is emitted for review.
- Default cost guidance: small service full-rehearsal ~ $800–1,200; large service ~ $4k–8k depending on probe complexity and annotator simulation.

Integration with quant profiles and eval-harness

- Rehearsal jobs reference quant profile IDs from the quantization catalog. Rehearsals must include quant metadata (bitwidth, kernel-profile, stash-policy).
- The probe-fabricator consults the eval-harness priming registry to select few-shot templates, ensuring parity between rehearsal prompts and production priming.

Failure triage and escalation playbook

1) Triage run (owner: Applied ML)
   - Label failing probes by failure mode (hallucination, truncation, functioncall-mismatch, tokenization-error).
2) Cross-team incident (owner: Release Lead)
   - If multiple cohorts fail fidelity_delta or coherence -> declare a Rehearsal Incident (severity: S2) and run causal regression investigation.
3) Rollback policy
   - Immediate rollback recommended when anchor-probe P90 coherence drops below 0.6 for >3 cohorts or when similarity drift >= 0.18 with statistical significance.

Postmortem artifacts and follow-ups

- Create a rehearsal incident dossier containing: rehearsal job manifest, cohort failure matrix, top 50 failing probes, annotator sample, and timeline of actions. Attach to the central incident tracker and link to model-promote PR.
- Follow-ups commonly include: micro-quant-tune, priming-template adjustment, or probe-corpus augmentation.

Ownership and contacts

- Probe Fabricator: Applied ML (owner: Priya Natarajan)
- Rehearsal orchestration: Platform Eval (owner: Marcus Holt)
- Gating & artifacts: ModelOnboard (owner: Sofia Alvarez)
- SRE & post-deploy monitoring: Platform SRE (owner: Liam Chen)

Appendices

A) Metrics table (columns: metric, description, alert-threshold, owner)

metric | description | alert-threshold | owner
fidelity_delta | semantic divergence vs baseline | >0.12 cohort mean | Applied ML
response_coherence | simulated annotator coherence 0–1 | cohort P90 < 0.70 | Evaluation
q_loss | quant artifact amplitude | absolute increase > 0.05 | ModelOnboard
latency_p95 | 95th percentile E2E latency | >2x baseline for cohort | SRE
embedding_stability | avg cosine shift per slice | >0.06 | Retrieval Team

B) Delta-significance command (example)
# runs bootstrap CI test comparing metric streams
python tools/delta_test.py --baseline reports/mv-1.0/metrics.json --variant reports/qv-2.1/metrics.json --metric fidelity_delta --alpha 0.05 --output reports/delta-ci.json

C) Quick checklist before scheduling a full rehearsal

- [ ] Manifest created and reviewed, probes budgeted and redaction confirmed.
- [ ] Quant variant artifacts uploaded to artifact store and kernel-profile declared.
- [ ] Shadow mesh capacity validated and can accept N concurrent rehearsal workers.
- [ ] Cost cap set and billing owner notified.
- [ ] Reviewers assigned and report template linked.

Related links and references

- See: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook-2026 for quant fallback patterns.
- See: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/shadow-to-prod-eval-continuity-guidelines-2026 for end-to-end shadow orchestration.

Document revision history

- 2026-02-10: initial draft (S. Alvarez)
- 2026-04-02: added cohort taxonomy and cost guidance (Marcus Holt)
- 2026-07-12: finalized gating thresholds and rollout runbook (S. Alvarez, Priya N.)

title: Evaluator Backpressure and Priority Fairness Playbook
content:
Overview

This playbook documents the design and operational procedures for the distributed evaluator backpressure subsystem and priority-fairness scheduler used by Redwood's Eval Mesh. It targets evaluator-sidecar and orchestrator components responsible for running probes, scoring outputs, and returning telemetry while respecting product SLAs and evaluator resource constraints.

Goals
- Prevent evaluator overload during spikes in probe load or slow downstream services.
- Ensure tenant and slice priority classes receive fair shares of evaluation budget.
- Provide deterministic and observable behavior for on-call engineers.
- Make graceful degradation decisions (deferred probes, sampled execution, degraded fidelity) explicit and reversible.

Scope
- Applies to: eval-orchestrator, evaluator-sidecar, probe-priority-agent, and the probe-queue services running in the Eval Mesh.
- Not in scope: probe generation policies and annotation pipelines (handled by Probe Fabrication).

Background and Motivation
- We run heterogeneous probes (shadow traffic, synthetic seeds, long-context functioncall tests) across a fleet of evaluators. Peaks (e.g., model rollouts, heavy shadow validation) can saturate CPU/GPU and cause unexpected increases in latency and cost.
- Previous incidents (see incident-2025-eval-thundering.json) showed cascading failures when thousands of long-context probes simultaneously retried after transient KV-cache warmup failures.

Design Principles
1) Observable decisions: every backpressure action must emit an event with reasoning tags (reason, affected_slice, priority_class, resource_util).
2) Predictable fairness: priority classes map to weight buckets; allocation follows weighted fair queuing with bounded latency targets.
3) Multi-tier degradation: prefer fidelity reduction (e.g., use draft evaluator config -> sample fewer seeds) before dropping high-priority probes.
4) Recovery-first rollbacks: automated scaling/backpressure policies must be paired with an explicit rollback and a health-check gating policy.

Key Terms
- priority_class: {gold, silver, bronze, infra}.
- probe_token: logical unit charged against a probe budget.
- soft_limit: policy threshold that triggers degradation; not an immediate reject.
- hard_limit: reject threshold requiring immediate shedding.

Architecture and Components
- eval-orchestrator: central controller that assigns probes to evaluator pools and updates policies via /api/v1/policy-sync.
- evaluator-sidecar: local agent on evaluator hosts that enforces per-host queueing, backpressure decisions, and emits telemetry to eval-metrics-service.
- probe-queue: Redis-backed sharded queue used for short-lived probe bursts.
- probe-priority-agent: service that converts business priority into scheduling weights and budgets.

SLOs and Operational Thresholds
- Probe completion SLO (P95): 2.5s for short probes (<512 tokens), 95s for long probes (>=4096 tokens) in gold class for hosted evaluation.
- Queue wait soft_limit: host CPU util >= 70% or queue length > 250 -> trigger soft degradation.
- Queue wait hard_limit: host CPU util >= 92% or queue length > 1000 -> reject non-infra probes.
- Backpressure event emission: 100% of decisions must emit to eval-metrics-service with keys: decision_type, priority_class, queue_len, cpu%, mem%.

Priority Class Weights (default)
- gold: weight 8
- silver: weight 4
- bronze: weight 1
- infra: weight 12 (reserved for infra-critical probes)

Backpressure Strategy (high level)
1) Admission Control: evaluator-sidecar applies per-priority leaky-bucket admitting tokens at rate = base_rate * weight.
2) Soft Degradation: when soft_limit hit, execute in this order:
   a) Reduce sample rate by 50% for bronze/silver probes.
   b) Convert >1K-token long probes to trimmed probes (context pruning rules applied).
   c) De-prioritize functioncall-heavy probes by requeueing with lower routing priority.
3) Hard Reject: when hard_limit triggered, reject bronze probes first, then silver; gold and infra should remain unless host is dangerously saturated.
4) Circuit Breaker for downstream dependencies: if downstream scorer latency > 2x baseline for 30s, temporarily pause new probes that require that scorer and route to fallback scorer.

Detailed Procedure: Host-side Enforcement (evaluator-sidecar)
1) Monitor: collect per-host CPU%, GPU util (if present), queue_length, avg_probe_latency (sliding 1m).
2) Evaluate thresholds in order: if cpu% >= 92% OR queue_length > 1000 -> hard_limit path. Else if cpu% >= 70% OR queue_length > 250 -> soft_limit path.
3) Soft Limit Actions (atomic):
   - Emit event: POST /telemetry/backpressure with payload: {host,reason,queue_len,priority_sampled}.
   - Apply adaptive sampler: for priority_class in [bronze, silver], set sample_rate = max(0.1, current * 0.5).
   - Trim contexts: call local priming microservice to apply configured context_trim_rules (see config table).
4) Hard Limit Actions (atomic):
   - Reject policy: return HTTP 429 with X-Backpressure-Reason header.
   - Requeue infra probes to dedicated infra pool when possible.
   - Trigger autoscaler webhook: POST /ops/autoscale-requests with reason "evaluator_hard_limit".

Configuration Matrix (reference)
| config_key | default | description | recommended change for model-rollout |
|------------|---------|-------------|------------------------------------|
| host_soft_cpu_pct | 70 | host-level soft CPU threshold | +5 during slow rollout warmup |
| host_hard_cpu_pct | 92 | hard limit for host-level CPU | unchanged |
| queue_soft_len | 250 | soft queue length | lower to 200 for high-contention tenants |
| queue_hard_len | 1000 | hard queue length | unchanged |
| base_rate_per_weight | 10 probes/s | base admission rate per weight | increase in steady-state after scaling |

Examples: CLI and Policy YAML
- Query current host backpressure state
  $ rmeshctl host-status --host eval-host-12 --format json

- Example policy (eval-orchestrator/policies/prod-priority-policy.yaml)
  ---
  priority_weights:
    gold: 8
    silver: 4
    bronze: 1
    infra: 12
  host_soft_cpu_pct: 70
  host_hard_cpu_pct: 92
  queue_soft_len: 250
  queue_hard_len: 1000
  base_rate_per_weight: 10

Telemetry and Dashboards
- Metrics emitted: eval.backpressure.decisions.count, eval.backpressure.rejected.count, eval.queue.length, eval.latency.p95.short_probes, eval.priority.share.
- Alert rules (SRE):
  - P1: eval.backpressure.rejected.count > 500 in 5m -> Incident (pager)
  - P2: eval.queue.length.avg > 750 for 15m -> Slack alert (#eval-ops)
  - P3: eval.priority.share.gold < 60% for 10m when gold load > 1000 -> Ops review.

Runbook: On-call Steps for P1
1) Acknowledge pager and open incident channel.
2) Query eval-orchestrator /api/v1/pools to identify affected pools.
3) Run: rmeshctl drain-pool --pool-id <pool> --grace 120s to stop new probes to pool.
4) If root cause is autoscaler lag, trigger manual scaling: POST /ops/autoscale-requests with scale_delta +2 nodes.
5) If immediate relief required, flip policy to emergency-priority-policy (feature flag) which: reduces bronze sample to 5% and routes gold to dedicated pool.
6) Record decision in incident timeline and emit retrospective tags for regression triage.

Operational Play Scenarios
- Gradual Model Rollout: pre-warm evaluators for 10m, then ramp probes at 10% per minute while observability confirms p95 latency < SLO. If soft_limit hits, pause ramp and investigate probe-type mix.
- Sudden Spike (Third-party scorer outage): circuit-break scorer calls; route light-weight scoring fallback; mark affected probes with tag scorer_fallback=true for later replay.

Testing and Validation
- Unit tests for admission controller deterministic behavior across weight combinations.
- Chaos tests: inject evaluator-sidecar CPU pressure and verify soft->hard transitions are logged and observable.
- Shadow rollouts: deploy new backpressure policy to 10% of evaluators for 48h before full rollout.

Rollout Checklist
1) Create policy PR in eval-orchestrator (include traffic simulation results).
2) LGTMs from reviewers (Evan Morris, Lina Fernández).
3) Canary deploy to canary-pool (10% fleet) and monitor priority_share, rejected.count, p95 latency for 48h.
4) Gradual ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 12h observation windows.
5) Post-rollout audit and update playbook with lessons learned.

Ownership and Contacts
- Policy owners: Priya Khandelwal (applied-ml), Marcus Li (infra).
- On-call rotation: eval-oncall (see roster).
- Escalation: if autoscaler fails to add capacity within 15m, escalate to infra-sre lead (pager).

Appendices
A. Context trimming rules (example)
- remove backreference sentences beyond 1024 tokens unless anchor markers exist.
- collapse multi-turn persona prompts to last 2 turns for trimmed probes.

B. Event schema (telemetry/backpressure)
- decision_type: soft_degrade | hard_reject | sampler_adjust | route_shift
- reason: cpu | queue_len | downstream_latency
- priority_class: gold | silver | bronze | infra
- host: hostname
- queue_len: integer
- cpu_pct: float

C. FAQ
Q: How do we treat long-context (>16k) probes during soft-limit?
A: Prefer trimming with context_trim_rules and, if trimming insufficient, sample at 10% and enqueue for background replay once load decreases.

Document History
- 2026-01-12: Created by Priya Khandelwal.
- 2026-02-20: Added runbook steps and CLI examples after triage of incident-2026-eval-spike.

Related reading
- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/operational-probe-economics-and-priority-contract-2026.json
- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/telemetry-driven-prompt-surgeon-and-repair-playbook-2025.json

title: Contextual Slice Replay Orchestration and Anchoring Playbook
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes the orchestration pattern we use to reliably replay workload slices through the eval harness and to anchor slice-level baselines across model promotions, quantization changes, and serving runtime updates. It combines deterministic replay, stochastic resampling, and anchor scoring so teams can detect, localize, and triage regressions with high signal-to-noise and consistent instrumentation.

Purpose:
- Provide a reproducible, operationalized pattern for slice extraction, replay orchestration, and anchor creation.
- Ensure slice baselines are portable across environments (shadow, dedicated, hosted) and model variants (float, quantized).
- Reduce regression triage time by surfacing causal candidates and providing pre-baked diffs for human review.

Scope:
- Applies to: interactive generation and chat workloads, embedding batches with context metadata, and reranking pipelines where per-request context affects outputs.
- Not in scope: low-level kernel tuning, hardware provisioning, or privacy-incompatible datasets (see privacy-first-shadow-eval page for those).

Key definitions:
- Slice: a named subset of traffic defined by metadata predicates (intent, language, client_id, prompt_template, context_window).
- Replay Job: an orchestrated execution of a slice through a target model/config combo in the eval harness.
- Anchor: a compact summary of prior-run outputs and metrics used as a stable baseline for monitoring and comparison.
- Anchor Score: multidimensional metric vector (accuracy proxy, semantic drift, response-stability-index, token-cost) used to detect changes.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Slice owner: product/feature team that defines the slice semantics and acceptance criteria. (Primary contact required)
- Eval harness owner: eng applied-ml team — maintains replay infra, scheduler, and artifact storage.
- Regression triage owner: model reliability squad — drives investigation workflows and rollbacks.

Data and artifact requirements:
- Inputs: canonicalized request objects (JSONL), tokenizer metadata, KV-cache seeds for long-context tests, and deterministic RNG seeds where sampling is allowed.
- Outputs: model responses (text/structured), logits or top-k token distribution (when available), embedding vectors, and per-request telemetry (latency, cost, route).
- Storage: run artifacts are persisted in the eval-artifacts bucket under /slices/{slice_name}/{run_id}/ with an index.json manifest.

Slice definition matrix (example):
| Slice name | Predicate | Purpose | Min sample | Owner |
| Critical-invoice-phrases | language=en AND intent=invoice AND prompt_template=invoice-summarize | Business-critical NLU checks | 500 | BillingFE |
| Low-resource-lang-zh | language=zh AND client_tier=free | Coverage for low-resource tokens | 200 | i18n |
| Long-context-chats | context_tokens>2048 AND interaction_type=chat | KV cache and attention stability | 300 | ConversationalAI |

Replay orchestration procedure (step-by-step):
1. Slice registration: feature team registers slice in the Slice Registry with predicate, sample window, and TTL. Include a canonical prompt set (30–200 examples) and an acceptance rubric.
2. Sampling and seeding: the harness sampler pulls N requests according to the slice window and injects deterministic RNG seeds and KV-cache seeds. For stochastic anchors, include M resamples per request (default M=3).
3. Environment mapping: map the target run to a model artifact (sha or model-id), quant-profile (if any), runtime image, and routing policy.
4. Dry-run validation: run a small pilot (10–20 requests) to validate tokenization parity and that no privacy flags are triggered.
5. Full replay: schedule the replay job on the eval cluster. Use priority queues for critical slices. Capture raw outputs, metadata, and system telemetry.
6. Anchor computation: compute anchor vectors (see Anchoring & Baselines) and persist alongside run artifacts.
7. Diff and alerting: compute delta vs. anchor and run automated checks. If thresholds exceeded, create a regression ticket with pre-populated findings.

Anchoring and baseline procedures:
- Anchor types:
  - Snapshot anchor: full-run anchor created at release cut and stored permanently.
  - Rolling anchor: windowed anchor computed over the latest X runs (default X=7) for stable slices.
  - Synthetic anchor: for small slices, generated by augmentation and weighted sampling.
- Anchor content: for each request store response hash, embedding centroid, top-5 token distributions, stability score, and cost per request.
- Anchor scoring (example calculation):
  - Response-stability-index (RSI) = fraction of requests with normalized similarity >= 0.85 (cosine for embeddings, BLEU/ROUGE/SemSim for text)
  - Semantic-drift = 1 - average cosine(embedding_current, embedding_anchor)
  - Token-cost-delta = (tokens_current - tokens_anchor)/tokens_anchor
- Anchor retention policy: Snapshot anchors retained indefinitely. Rolling anchors retained 90 days. Synthetic anchors retained 30 days.

Metrics, thresholds, and automated checks:
- Primary alarm triggers (per-slice):
  - RSI drop >= 0.10 => create P2 regression ticket.
  - Semantic-drift increase >= 0.08 => auto-run triage (bisect by model and quant-config).
  - Token-cost-delta >= 0.20 AND RSI drop >= 0.05 => flag for cost-quality tradeoff review.
  - Latency increase > 25% p50 or p95 breach => route to infra runbook.
- Evaluation metrics to compute per-run: RSI, semantic-drift, top-token-shift (KL divergence), fidelity score (task dependent), and end-to-end correctness (if labeled).

Integration with quantization profiles and runtime variants:
- Label each replay job with quant_profile_id and runtime_image. Store quantization metadata (bit-width, per-channel/per-tensor, calibration dataset id).
- Recommended workflow when testing quantized variants:
  1. Run float baseline anchor (if not present).
  2. Run deterministic quantized replay with identical seeds.
  3. Compute paired diffs and generate per-request failure indicators.
  4. If divergences exceed thresholds, run targeted per-layer micro-benchmarks and create a quant-failure case.
- Crossworkload guidance: for heterogeneous slices (e.g., embeddings + generation), anchor each signal type separately and compute a composite anchor score.

Regression triage fast-path (operational playbook):
1. Auto-classify: harness computes candidate root causes using heuristics (config mismatch, tokenizer drift, quantization delta, prompt template change, model version).
2. Automated bisect: run binary bisect across commits or model snapshots to narrow to a 1–2 commit window.
3. Localize to dimension: use per-request diffs to determine if failure is concentrated in prompts, languages, or client IDs.
4. Escalate: if auto-classify confidence < 0.7, escalate to model reliability squad with artifacts attached.
5. Rollback/mitigation: if slice is business-critical and impact > P1 thresholds, perform rollback to last snapshot anchor and notify SRE.

CLI / API examples:
- Create replay job (curl):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    https://eval-api.redwood.internal/v1/replay-jobs \
    -d '{"slice":"long-context-chats","model_id":"rwd-llama-70b-v2","quant_profile":"q8-perchannel-v2","sample_size":300,"seeds":{"deterministic":true}}'

- Example manifest (index.json) snippet stored with artifacts:
  {
    "run_id": "20260120-longcontext-01",
    "slice": "long-context-chats",
    "model_id": "rwd-llama-70b-v2",
    "quant_profile": "q8-perchannel-v2",
    "artifact_paths": ["responses.jsonl","topk.jsonl","metrics.json"]
  }

Rollout checklist for slice anchoring in release pipelines:
- [ ] Snapshot anchor exists for current main release.
- [ ] Canonical prompt set verified and annotated with acceptance rubric.
- [ ] Quant profiles and runtime labels included in job metadata.
- [ ] Low-latency dry-run passed.
- [ ] Automated checks and thresholds configured in monitoring.
- [ ] Regression triage playbook contact and runbook links attached.

Operational notes and best practices:
- Prefer deterministic seeds for regression-sensitive slices; allow stochastic resamples for robustness checks.
- Keep canonical prompt sets small (30–200) but representative; control for label imbalance.
- When possible, compute embedding-centroid deltas rather than raw text diffs for multilingual stability.
- Annotate expensive slices with cost-owners; include token-cost delta in decision heuristics.

Troubleshooting quick reference:
- Tokenization mismatch: run token-compare tool and inspect tokenizer version differences; common fix: pin tokenizer artifact in env mapping.
- Large semantic-drift with no conf change: check upstream prompt rewrite or client-side template changes.
- Quant-induced hallucination: escalate to quant team; run per-layer fp32-vs-quant attribution tests.

References and related pages:
- Eval mesh and workload fingerprinting (internal) - for slice fingerprinting primitives.
- Quant profile synthesis and safety playbook - for quant test patterns and thresholds.
- Regression triage playbooks - for escalation and incident handling steps.

Appendix: example threshold table
| Metric | Warning | Action | Owner |
| RSI drop 0.05–0.10 | Create P3 ticket, run extended resample | Feature team + Eval harness |
| RSI drop >= 0.10 | Create P2 ticket, bisect | Model reliability squad |
| Semantic-drift 0.04–0.08 | Run embedding pair analysis | Applied-ML |
| Semantic-drift >= 0.08 | Auto-trigger bisect and escalate | Model reliability squad |

Contact:
- Primary: Marisol Chen (marisol@redwood.ai) — Eval harness owner
- Secondary: Diego Alvarez (diego@redwood.ai) — Model reliability

Document history:
- 2026-01-15: created by Marisol Chen
- 2026-02-10: updated thresholds and quant integration section

title: workload-mirroring-fork-and-eval-scenario-library-2026
content:
Overview:
This document defines a curated library of workload mirroring and synthetic fork scenarios, the process to synthesize them for offline and shadow evaluation, and the acceptance criteria used during model onboarding and quantization qualification. The goal is to provide a consistent, repeatable set of adversarial and production-proximate scenarios to validate latency, correctness, cache behavior, token economy, and regression risk across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Motivation and scope:
- Motivation: Many regressions and cost surprises arise from rare workload interactions (prefix-skew, irregular KV-cache reuse, long-context fragmentation, or mixed function-calling loads). A compact scenario library reduces surprise by exercising these corner cases during promotion and before rollouts.
- Scope: This playbook covers generation, execution, metrics, and triage for: production traffic mirroring, synthetic forks of sessions, quantization-aware shadow runs, latency/failure injection, and multi-tenant noise stress. It does not replace end-to-end customer integration testing; rather it complements field tests and unit-level evals.

Key concepts and terminology:
- Mirror: A passive copy of production requests routed to a non-production endpoint without affecting responses to users.
- Fork: A diverging variant of a mirrored request where inputs are perturbed (e.g., prompt rewrite, tokenization noise) to create stress cases.
- Shadow-run: Active execution of models in parallel to production that can run expensive computations (e.g., quantized variants) and collect trace/outputs for offline comparison.
- Fidelity-weighted score (FWS): Composite measure combining semantic similarity, token delta, and downstream metric impact to rank regressions.

Scenario taxonomy (summary table):
| ID | Name | Primary risk vector | Intended use | Run mode |
| S001 | Prefix-skew chaining | Prefix reuse + KV eviction | Shadow-run + offline diff | Mirroring/Fork |
| S002 | Long-context fragmentation (L-16k) | Memory blowup, kernel change | Performance and latency SLO test | Shadow-run |
| S003 | Mixed-stream tool-calls | Function call-heavy interleaving | Correctness + structured output | Mirroring/Fork |
| S004 | Quantized-roundtrip stress | Quantization numerical drift | Compare quant profiles to fp16 | Quant-aware shadow |
| S005 | Burst+cold-cache | Sudden traffic burst with empty KV | Autoscaling and throughput | Mirroring with traffic shaping |
| S006 | Tokenization adversarials | Unusual unicode / whitespace | Model stability and token economy | Fork + synthetic perturbations |
| S007 | Multi-tenant interference | Noisy co-tenants, rate limit backpressure | Isolation and fallback behaviors | Mirroring in dedicated pools |
| S008 | Latency injection & retry storms | Network lag + client retries | Fallbacks and idempotency | Mirroring with fault-injection |
Each scenario in the library includes: a description, input perturbation recipe, traffic shaping parameters, collection hooks, and acceptance thresholds.

How to synthesize a forked workload (step-by-step):
1) Select base mirror stream: choose a representative 24–72 hour production shard identified by workload fingerprinting (use eval-harness tool `stream-select --fingerprint <id>`).
2) Define perturbation recipe: select from the recipe catalog (examples below). Compose multiple perturbations with probabilistic weights. Keep total perturbation probability <= 15% for realism.
3) Add environment modifiers: latency profiles, error injection rates, and KV cache warm/cold flags.
4) Run small-scale pilot: 1–2% of stream to validate instrumentation and ensure no PII leakage.
5) Scale to shadow-run: execute full scenario in a non-customer-facing environment and collect traces.
6) Compute acceptance metrics and produce a FWS report. If FWS exceeds thresholds, open regression ticket and follow triage playbook.

Perturbation recipe examples (text-form snippets):
- token_squeeze: replace 20% of whitespace sequences with alternate U+00A0 non-breaking spaces and re-tokenize to surface tokenization edge cases.
- prefix_repeat: append a 16-token repeated prefix to 10% of requests to stress KV cache eviction heuristics.
- function_shuffle: for requests with tool calls, randomly reorder call sequence in 5% of cases to validate structured output determinism.
- quant-scale: multiply logits by a small scalar (0.98–1.02) at generation time to mimic quantization bias during shadow inference.

Metrics and acceptance criteria:
- Latency SLO impact: median latency increase <= 10% and p99 <= 1.5x baseline for production-like scenarios.
- Token delta: average token count deviation <= 3% unless scenario intentionally tests truncation.
- Semantic drift (bert-sim): mean embedding cosine similarity >= 0.92 compared to baseline; exceptions must be documented.
- FWS threshold: any scenario with FWS >= 0.35 requires blocking investigation; 0.20–0.35 is warning and needs owner signoff.
- Error amplification: increased downstream error-rate (e.g., malformed JSON tool call) by > 0.5% must be triaged.

Integration with model onboarding and quantization profiles:
- Promotion gates: For a model or quant profile to be promoted to Dedicated/Private, it must pass the scenario set mapped to the workload tier (see promotion matrix below).
- Promotion matrix (text):
  - Tier: critical-customer routes -> must pass S001, S003, S004, S008 and have FWS < 0.20 on each.
  - Tier: high-throughput public API -> must pass S002, S005, S006, S007 with latency/p99 criteria.
  - Tier: internal tools -> must pass S001 and S006 with semantic drift checks.
- Quant-aware shadow runs: run quantized profile side-by-side with fp16 for at least three independent seeds and compute token-level divergence and downstream metrics. Automate this in CI with `eval-harness run-quant-shadow --seeds 3 --compare-to=fp16`.

Execution patterns and tooling (examples):
- CLI: capture and mirror a production shard
  - `capture-stream --start 2026-01-01T00:00Z --end 2026-01-02T00:00Z --fingerprint=cust-ml-3`
  - `mirror-run --stream captured/2026-01-01 --target shadow/prod-s001 --mode fork --perturbations token_squeeze,prefix_repeat --scale 0.25`
- YAML scenario definition (example snippet):
  - name: "S001-prefix-skew-chaining"
  - base_stream: "captured/2026-01-01"
  - perturbations:
    - token_squeeze: {prob: 0.1}
    - prefix_repeat: {prob: 0.05, repeat: 16}
  - env_modifiers: {latency_profile: "tail-200ms", kv_warm: false}
  - acceptance: {fws: 0.2, median_latency_pct: 1.10}

Observability and data collection:
- Required traces: request_id, route, model_name, model_hash, token_count_in/out, kv_cache_hit_rate, kernel_variant, gpu_utilization, embedding_vector (optional hashed), and deterministic seed used.
- Tagging: add labels `scenario_id`, `mirror_origin`, and `perturbation_set` to all telemetry to enable quick filtering in the Console.
- Storage: keep shadow outputs and traces for 30 days in standard eval retention; increase to 90 days for scenarios that are part of an ongoing regression investigation.

Triage playbook (on FWS breach):
1) Assign owner from the model-onboarding team and tag incident as "eval-regression".
2) Reproduce: run the scenario across three independent seeds and collect full logs.
3) Bisect: narrow to perturbation combinations. Use `eval-harness bisect --scenario S001 --split perturbation` to automate.
4) Localize: identify whether drift is due to tokenization, sampling, quantization, or kernel selection (kernel traces and token deltas are primary signals).
5) Mitigate: possible mitigations include pinning an older quant profile, adjusting KV cache eviction policy for the route, or routing to a higher-fidelity model variant for affected tenants.
6) Roll-forward/rollback: follow the standard release runbook for promotion or emergency rollback.

Failure modes and recommended countermeasures (summary):
- False positives from synthetic perturbations: reduce perturbation intensity and validate against control mirror.
- PII leakage risk when mirroring: always run mirror captures through the PII-filter pipeline. Abort if PII ratio > 0.1% in pilot.
- Overloading non-prod infra: use rate limits and circuit breakers in mirror-run to preserve cluster stability.

Ownership and operational responsibilities:
- Library owner: Applied ML & Evals team (primary contact: maya.chen@redwood.example).
- Onboarding owner: Model Onboarding team must map new routes to scenario tiers during acceptance.
- SRE support: Eng SRE provides capacity and alert integration for shadow-run clusters.
- Review cadence: Quarterly review of scenario catalog and thresholds; immediate add when a new regression vector is discovered.

Appendix: sample FWS computation (pseudocode):
- FWS = w1*(1 - mean_cosine_similarity) + w2*(normalized_token_delta) + w3*(downstream_error_impact)
- default weights: w1=0.5, w2=0.3, w3=0.2

Appendix: small JSON example of a mirrored request (single-line for logging):
{"request_id":"r-1234","route":"/v1/chat","model":"redwood-13b-fp16","input":"Translate to French: Hello world","scenario_id":"S006-tokenization-adversarial"}

Related pages and references:
- See CI integration docs in eval-harness for automated gates.
- Cross-reference: performance standards and observability-standards for kernel and tracing requirements.

Change log:
- 2025-09-15: Created initial scenario taxonomy and synthesis procedure.
- 2025-11-02: Added quant-aware shadow-run steps and CLI examples.
- 2026-01-10: Tightened FWS thresholds and clarified retention policy.

Contact: Maya Chen (Applied ML & Evals) — please raise comments on this page or ping #applied-evals on slack for urgent requests.

title: Tokenization Robustness Testbed and Operational Procedures
content:
Overview

This page documents the Tokenization Robustness Testbed: a repeatable, automated evaluation harness and operational playbook for detecting, triaging, and preventing tokenization and byte-level drift across model onboarding, quantization, and runtime upgrades. The testbed focuses on mismatches between expected token sequences and runtime tokenization behavior, errors introduced by tokenizer-regression after merges, and failure modes that cause silent semantic changes (e.g., whitespace-sensitivity, Unicode normalization, byte-order-mark handling).

Why this matters

- Tokenization changes are a frequent, low-signal source of downstream quality regressions (classification label shifts, hallucination triggers, changed prompt completions).
- Quantized kernels and low-level runtime changes can subtly change token boundary behavior; these are often missed by standard semantic-only evals.
- For enterprise customers operating in regulated domains, tokenization determinism is part of certification and audit.

Scope and non-goals

- In scope: tokenizer behavior across model variants and runtime kernels, tokenizer + quantizer interactions, cross-locale Unicode normalization, and token-level privacy filters.
- Out of scope: overall semantic evaluation (covered by regular eval harness), dataset labeling policies, and user-facing prompt rewriting features.

Architecture and components

- eval-orchestrator: schedules runs, stores artifacts to S3-compliant storage (service: eval-runner).
- token-fuzzer: generator of edge-case input (emoji sequences, ZWJ clusters, bidi text, BOM prefixed inputs, mixed normalization).
- tokenizer-checker: deterministic reference tokenizer (pinned to model-catalog version) used as ground truth for token sequence comparisons.
- runtime-prober: executes tokenization inside the redwood-runtime and quantized kernels (service: simserv).
- analyzer: computes metrics, diffs, and triage signals, pushes alerts to Prometheus/Alertmanager and creates Jira tickets if thresholds cross.

Test definitions and canonical metrics

- Tokenization Mismatch Rate (TMR): fraction of inputs where runtime token sequence != reference token sequence. Alert threshold: 0.5% on a 10k sample (SLO: <0.1%).
- Boundary Shift Count (BSC): average number of tokens with different boundaries per mismatched input. Alert if mean BSC > 1.2 for failing sample set.
- Normalization Drift Rate (NDR): percent of inputs whose normalized form differs between reference and runtime normalization. Alert: >0.2%.
- Byte-Order Anomalies (BOA): count of inputs that gain or lose nonprinting bytes (BOM, ZWJ). Any nonzero BOA in production branch triggers immediate rollback candidate.

Config and requirements (reference)

| Parameter | Value | Rationale | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Sample size per run | 10,000 | Balanced sensitivity vs cost | Applied ML infra |
| Fuzzer variants | 24 families | Unicode, whitespace, markup, escaped JSON, long-repetition | Applied ML team |
| Run cadence | nightly + pre-merge on mainline | Detect regressions early and nightly drift | Eng-SRE |
| Retention | 90 days artifacts, 365 days metadata | For triage and audit | Data-Platform |

Test families (examples)

1. Unicode normalization bank: NFD vs NFC, mixed combining marks, sequenced modifiers.
2. Whitespace and delimiter stress: repeated spaces, nonbreaking spaces, soft hyphens.
3. Markup-edge cases: HTML entities, nested tags, incomplete XML.
4. Embedding/escape combos: JSON-escaped text, serialized protobuf fragments.
5. Long-tail concatenations: repeated rare tokens to stress KV cache and quant boundaries.
6. Locale-specific bidi and RTL stress tests.

Procedure: running a validation sweep (engineer-facing)

1. Prepare environment
   a. Checkout stable reference tokenizer: git checkout tags/tokenizer-ref-2025-11-01
   b. Ensure eval-orchestrator is pointed to the correct bucket: export EVAL_BUCKET=s3://redwood-evals/tokenization-testbed

2. Start a pre-merge check (CI integration)
   - CI step triggers `tokenization-check --ci --build $PR_BUILD --target runtime`
   - CI receives artifact with TMR and BSC. If TMR > 0.5% the PR blocks and posts a triage card.

3. Nightly full sweep
   - Cron job: `eval-orchestrator run --suite tokenization-robustness --size 10000`
   - Artifacts stored at: s3://redwood-evals/tokenization-testbed/YYYY-MM-DD/<run-id>/

4. Alerting and automated actions
   - If TMR > 0.5% or BOA > 0: Alertmanager fires `RED-TOK-DRIFT` pager with run artifacts link.
   - If NDR > 0.2% but TMR < 0.5%: create low-priority Jira labeled `token-normalization` for follow-up.

On-call triage playbook

1. Acknowledge alert and locate run artifacts. Primary responder: Applied ML oncall (rotation in Eng-SRE).
2. Reproduce locally: run `runtime-prober --model $MODEL --input-file artifacts/inputs.json --dump-tokens` and compare with `tokenizer-checker --input artifacts/inputs.json` using the provided `diff-tokens.py` tool.
3. Determine root cause categories (select one):
   - Tokenization code change in tokenizer library (e.g., upgrade to new tokenizers binding).
   - Runtime kernel rounding or quantization effect that changes bytewise input handling.
   - Preprocessor change in ingestion layer (e.g., trimming, normalization).
   - Model packaging issue (wrong tokenizer artifact bundled).
4. Mitigation steps by category:
   - Tokenizer library change: revert or pin dependency; hotfix and trigger pre-merge checks.
   - Runtime kernel effect: roll to previous kernel variant in Dedicated and Private pools; create rollback run.
   - Ingestion preprocessor: patch normalization to align with reference behaviour; prepare minor release.
   - Packaging issue: repackage model with correct tokenizer and promote via shadow deployment.
5. Post-incident: create a regression ticket, attach artifacts, and schedule a postmortem if production customers were impacted.

Rollout and canary guidance

- Always run tokenization-check suite as part of model promotion pipeline (shadow stage).
- For runtime upgrades, run the testbed across 3 environments: dev (nightly), canary (10% traffic), and prod (full). Canary must pass TMR < 0.1% for 48 hours before wider rollout.

Integration with other evals and quant profiles

- The testbed emits per-input tags that downstream semantic evals can use to stratify failures (e.g., 'ZWJ-cluster', 'escaped-json'). This guarantees we can correlate semantic regressions to tokenization families.
- Before quantized promotion, run quant-tuner with tokenization-check enabled. Some quantization profiles (see quantization-profiles/kv-cache-quant-stability-audit-playbook-2025) modify byte handling for speed; these must be validated explicitly.

CLI examples and helper scripts

- Snapshot command to run a focused suite against a runtime image: 

```
eval-orchestrator run --suite tokenization-robustness --size 2000 --runtime-image redwood/runtime:canary-2026-01-15 --output ./artifacts/run-$(date +%F).tar.gz
```

- Quick local comparator: 

```
python tools/diff-tokens.py --ref artifacts/ref_tokens.json --hot artifacts/runtime_tokens.json --report out/report.html
```

Artifact format (recommended)

- inputs.jsonl: newline-delimited inputs with metadata tags.
- ref_tokens.jsonl: token lists from tokenizer-checker.
- runtime_tokens.jsonl: token lists from runtime-prober.
- metrics.json: small JSON with TMR, BSC, NDR, BOA values.

Example metrics.json content:

```
{ "run_id": "2026-02-03-01", "tmr": "0.0034", "bsc": "0.76", "ndr": "0.0012", "boa": "0" }
```

Ownership and SLAs

- Primary owner: Applied ML (tokenization testbed subteam).
- Secondary owner: Eng-SRE (alerting and infra).
- SLO: Nightly run completion within 2 hours of start 99% of the time.
- Alerting SLA: Critical tokenization pager must be acknowledged within 15 minutes.

Operational notes and limitations

- Synthetic fuzzers do not guarantee coverage of customer data distributions; any flagged regression must be verified against production customer seed sets before major rollbacks.
- Determinism requirement: tokenization-checker is pinned by hash in the model-catalog entry; ensure model packaging scripts include tokenizer-hash metadata.

Related pages and artifacts

- Serving simulation harness and orchestration: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/serving-simulation-eval-harness-2026
- KV-cache quant stability audit: /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/kv-cache-quant-stability-audit-playbook-2025

Revision history

- 2025-11-18: Initial draft by Priya Nair.
- 2026-01-10: Added BOA handling and quick comparator script (review: Ethan Cole).
- 2026-02-03: Published with updated SLOs and integration notes (review: Lena Schmidt, Marcus Lee).

title: Telemetry-driven Eval Prioritization and Hotspot Triage
content:
Summary
This document describes a telemetry-first system for prioritizing offline and online evaluation jobs and a structured hotspot triage playbook for high-impact model behavior regressions. It targets the evaluator orchestration layer and SRE/Applied-ML engineers who run and act on model quality telemetry for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Motivation
- The eval backlog grows faster than evaluation capacity. Manual triage leads to missed regressions and wasted compute on low-impact slices.
- Telemetry (production errors, user rejections, SLA anomalies) is an early indicator of quality regressions but needs automated translation into eval work.
- We need a deterministic, auditable prioritization pipeline that: (1) converts telemetry to eval tasks, (2) assigns cost-aware priority, and (3) feeds actionable triage runbooks to on-call and ML engineers.

Goals and non-goals
- Goals:
  - Surface the top-K evaluation tasks that reduce user-impact most per compute dollar.
  - Ensure high-recall capture of hotspots without overwhelming evaluators.
  - Provide an operator-facing triage checklist with concrete rollback/fallback actions.
- Non-goals:
  - This is not a model promotion gate (that remains the model-onboarding pipeline).
  - It does not supersede security or privacy reviews for customer data.

Principles
1) Signal-first: prioritize signals with clear business impact (error rates, retention drops, user-text flags).
2) Cost-awareness: include token/throughput cost estimates in prioritization.
3) Explainability: each prioritized eval job must include the telemetry-derived rationale and suggested slices.
4) Fast feedback: support micro-canaries and quick smoke evals (<30m) before full-scale runs.

Telemetry signals (inputs)
- Production traces: streaming error labels (500-series), latency p99/p50 spikes, timeouts.
- User feedback: explicit thumbs-down, A/B experiment metrics (CTR/retention deltas).
- Quality analytics: semantic drift detectors, embedding-distance anomalies, stability score drops.
- Routing & capacity: fallback events (requests routed to cheaper model variants).

Signal enrichment steps
1) Attach context: request metadata (model version, route, top-k prompts), tenant_id, and sequence length buckets.
2) Cluster related events: temporal proximity (5–15m windows), similar prompt fingerprints (edit distance or embedding cosine > 0.92).
3) Score impact: compute an impact score (0–100) combining user count, error severity, and retention delta.

Priority scoring algorithm (overview)
- Inputs: impact_score, estimated_eval_cost (core-hours or token-cost), urgency_multiplier (customer SLA tier), seasonality_factor.
- Priority = (impact_score * urgency_multiplier * seasonality_factor) / (1 + log(1 + estimated_eval_cost))
- Normalization: scale to 0–100 and bucket into: critical (>80), high (60–80), medium (30–60), low (<30).

Eval task generation
1) Auto-slice suggestion: generate 3–7 candidate slices using clustering (intent, length, locale, prompt-token prefix).
2) Quick smoke: spawn a 30m micro-eval on a 500–2k sample (approx 5–20k tokens) to confirm signal.
3) Full evaluation: if smoke fails, schedule full eval with stratified sampling across traffic segments.

Hotspot triage playbook (operator steps)
1) Acknowledge: Owner (on-call ML or SRE) acknowledges the prioritized task in the evaluation dashboard within 30 minutes for critical tasks.
2) Run smoke eval: launch the micro-sample smoke eval. If pass -> mark as false-positive and document reasoning.
3) If smoke fails: run a targeted full eval job and fetch comparison baselines (previous model version and quantized variant).
4) Determine root cause categories (choose one primary):
   - Model drift / distribution shift
   - Quantization-induced degradation
   - Serving KV-cache/latency artifact
   - Prompt-processing bug (pre/post-processing mismatch)
   - Data corruption / formatting errors
5) For each root cause, follow the remediation checklist below.

Remediation checklists (short)
- Model drift:
  - Compare top-k token distributions and embedding centroids versus baseline.
  - Re-run eval with increased context/contextual shots.
  - If confirmed, create model-promotion hold ticket; notify product and release manager.
- Quantization-induced degradation:
  - Re-run on full-precision replica and mixed-precision replicas.
  - If degradation isolated to q4/q8 profile, revert to higher-fidelity profile for affected routes and open quant-team ticket.
- KV-cache / latency artifact:
  - Check per-token latency, cache hit rates, and request-shard mapping.
  - Warm caches for affected routes and schedule a controlled roll-forward.
- Prompt-processing bug:
  - Replay raw request through offline preprocessing; compare outputs.
  - Patch preprocessor and deploy a canary.
- Data corruption:
  - Validate ingestion pipelines and normalization; block bad batches and backfill missing fields.

Escalation and rollback policy
- Critical priority: if a full eval shows regression (>5% degradations on primary metric for top-tier customers), perform an emergency rollback to the last certified model and notify Incident Response.
- High priority: consider partial route-level fallback to a previous variant; schedule a postmortem if rollback is performed.

Operational configurations (table)
| Config name | Default | Range | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| smoke_eval_sample_size | 1000 | 500–5000 | sample count for micro-evaluations |
| smoke_eval_duration | 30m | 5m–120m | duration limit before automatic cancel |
| eval_cost_threshold_usd | 200 | 50–2000 | above threshold requires manager approval |
| critical_priority_threshold | 80 | 70–100 | score threshold for critical routing |
| max_parallel_smoke_jobs | 20 | 1–100 | global concurrency cap |

Automation and tooling hooks
- Orchestration: eval-orch service (internal) integrates with telemetry bus and can enqueue tasks into the evaluator fleet.
- Dashboard: "Eval Hotspots" view shows live prioritized queue, rationale, sample prompts, and quick-run buttons.
- CLI examples:
  - Queue a micro-smoke: evalctl run --slice-id S12345 --mode smoke --sample 1000
  - Fetch rationale: evalctl show --task T98765 --rationale

Metrics and SLOs for the pipeline
- Time to acknowledge (critical): 30 minutes (target 90th percentile).
- Time to smoke result: 45 minutes from enqueue (including scheduling).
- False positive rate for prioritized tasks: <20% (measured quarterly).
- Coverage: >95% of telemetry events with impact_score >= 40 must surface a prioritized eval job or a documented suppression rule.

Ownership and contact list
- Primary owner: Applied ML - Eval Orchestration (team lead: Aisha Patel)
- Secondary owner: Serving Runtime Reliability (team lead: Miguel Santos)
- Pager rotations and on-call: see /confluence/eng-oncall/oncall-rotations for links.

Audit and compliance notes
- All eval jobs spawned from customer traffic must log the minimal request fingerprint and must not store PII in evaluation payloads. The eval-orch enforces scrubbing policies described in the privacy contract.

Appendix: example prioritized payload (human-readable)
- Alert ID: ALERT-2026-1421
- Rationale: p99 latency spike for route /chat/stream; 12k impacted users, 0.7% retention drop over 1h window
- Suggested slices: long-context > 1024 tokens, locale: en-US, intent: summarization
- Estimated eval cost: $340 (full), $28 (smoke)
- Priority score: 87 (critical)

Related work and references
- See evaluator interchange format and federation spec for task serialization.
- See drift detection and embedding stability guidelines for signal extraction patterns.

Revision history
- 2026-01-12: Initial draft by Eleanor Ruiz.
- 2026-02-10: Added smoke eval parameters and CLI examples (reviewers: Miguel Santos).
- 2026-03-01: Published after review; added escalation thresholds and audit notes.

title: Distribution Stability Eval and Response Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook describes Redwood's standardized process for evaluating distribution stability (inputs, embeddings, outputs) and the operational response for detected deviations. It is intended to connect evaluation harness outputs, production telemetry, and remediation actions so teams can act consistently across model types and deployment modes.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers maintaining model quality
- SREs and platform engineers managing observability and alerts
- Owner teams performing model rollouts and post-deployment verification

High-level goals:
- Detect meaningful distribution changes with low false-positive rate
- Maintain model calibration within expected bounds for customer-facing metrics
- Provide automated safe mitigations and clear handoffs for human investigation

Core signals we monitor (defaults):
- Token-level PSI: alert if PSI > 0.25 over 24h window
- Embedding median cosine shift: alert if median shift > 0.08 over 1h window
- Token KL divergence: alert if KL > 0.5 on sampled prompts
- Scalar calibration gap: alert if absolute gap > 0.06 on labeled validation tasks
- Feedback-derived error rate: alert if 7-day rolling error-rate > 2x baseline
- Traffic anomalies: 3-sigma change in route traffic or sudden spike in latency

How the eval-harness integrates:
1) Scheduled stress evaluations: the eval-harness runs daily stress sweeps and produces artifacts (sampled prompts, metrics CSVs, and summary HTML). These artifacts are uploaded to s3://redwood-eval/harness-artifacts/{model_version}/date/.
2) Shadow sampling: during rollouts, the harness collects 14-day shadow traffic and computes baseline distributions to register with the model registry.
3) Scenario suites: teams author scenario YAMLs that the harness runs to simulate edge cases; scenario outputs are stored alongside baseline artifacts.

Signal computation and aggregation:
- Aggregation windows: 1h for embedding medians, 4h for token-level checks, 24h for PSI and calibration summaries.
- Sampling policy: default 1% of traffic for embeddings snapshots; up to 10% for flagged routes. Prioritize enterprise tenants and newly introduced route_tags.
- Storage & retention: raw sampled embeddings in Parquet (hourly), aggregated metrics in ClickHouse (90-day TTL), and full harness artifacts preserved for 90 days in S3.

Detectors and algorithms (recommended set):
- PSI with adaptive bucketing for token categories and prompt length buckets.
- Median cosine shift with trimmed mean to reduce sensitivity to outliers.
- KL divergence for token outputs computed on stratified prompt sets.
- MMD with RBF kernel on embeddings for workloads with continuous shifts.
- Confidence calibration metrics: ECE (expected calibration error) and class-wise calibration for classification-like tasks.

Alert lifecycle and severity classification:
- Warning (P2): metric exceeds investigation threshold (e.g., PSI > 0.15) but under page threshold. Logged to Slack channel with link to harness artifact.
- Page (P1): metric exceeds page threshold (e.g., PSI > 0.25 OR calibration gap > 0.06) and impacts high-priority tenant or high-traffic route. Triggers PagerDuty.
- Critical (P0): sustained degradation for >4 hours, customer-facing failures, or safety guardrail violations. Requires immediate cross-team war room.

First-response checklist (0-30 minutes):
1) Confirm alert details and sampling window. Attach harness artifact and recent sampled inputs.
2) SRE: validate system health (latency, error rates, GPU/memory utilization, recent deploys).
3) Applied-ML owner: review sample outputs in the harness UI and check calibration dashboard.
4) If correlated with recent deploy, consider immediate rollback or traffic-pin to previous version.
5) If systemic input shift (e.g., sudden change in prompt shape), update sampling filters and tag incident for retraining consideration.

Automated mitigations (safe-by-default):
- Traffic pin: rollback traffic split to previous model_version for impacted routes for up to 2 hours unless manually cleared.
- Apply latest-calibration: post-hoc calibration transform can be injected in runtime for scalar outputs if artifact exists and owner approves.
- Fallback model route: switch to conservative model variant when safety guardrail triggers.
- Throttle non-critical routes: reduce background sampling and batch sizes to preserve capacity.

When to retrain or fine-tune:
- If calibration plus small corrective data does not restore metrics in 72 hours, plan for targeted fine-tuning.
- Sample requirement guidance: collect minimum 5k validated examples for small distribution shifts; 20k+ for broader domain shifts. Prioritize label quality and tenant representation.
- Retraining options: domain-adaptive fine-tuning, LoRA-style adapters, or retrieval-augmented fine-tuning depending on task and data characteristics.

Onboarding checklist for new model versions (minimum gating):
- Telemetry schema validated and test messages flowing into telemetry topics.
- 14-day shadow evaluation via eval-harness with stress scenarios executed.
- Baseline distributions and calibration artifacts registered in the model registry.
- Drift detectors configured and initial thresholds set; PagerDuty routing updated with owner contacts.

Example commands and quick references:
- Run a daily stress sweep: redwood-eval-harness run stress-sweep --model {model_version} --suite default --out s3://redwood-eval/harness-artifacts/{model_version}/
- Generate a drift report: redwood-eval-harness report-drift --model {model_version} --window 24h --algorithms psi,median-embedding,kl --out ./drift-report.pdf
- Inspect last calibration artifact: redwood-model-registry get-calibration --model {model_version} --latest

Ownership and escalation contacts:
- Primary: applied-ml oncall (applied-ml@redwood.com) — analysis, calibration artifacts, scenario ownership.
- Platform/SRE: eng-sre oncall (eng-sre@redwood.com) — telemetry, alerting, and rollback automation.
- Product/security: looped in for high-impact or regulated-customer incidents.

Post-incident workflow:
- Postmortem required within 7 days for incidents that triggered manual mitigation or customer impact. The postmortem must include timeline, root cause hypothesis, sample artifacts, corrective actions, and updated thresholds.
- Store postmortem artifacts under /incidents/distribution-stability/{incident_id}/ and link to model registry entry.

Maintenance and exercises:
- Quarterly stability drills: run a simulated shift (synthetic prompts + embedding perturbation) and validate detection time and false positive rate.
- Monthly threshold review: applied-ml and eng-sre review detector thresholds for top 10 models by traffic.

Appendix: decision heuristics summary:
- If metric is marginally above threshold but no customer impact: monitor and increase sampling for 24h.
- If correlated with new deploy: prefer rollback + forensic harness run over immediate retraining.
- If calibration-only fix succeeds: publish new calibration artifact and monitor for 72h before closing incident.

Document history:
- 2025-09-20: Created (Diego Alvarez)
- 2025-11-12: Added severity tiers and automated mitigation policies (Priya Nair)
- 2026-01-28: Updated sampling guidance and onboarding checklist (Jared Lim)

title: Experimental Priming Sandbox and Relabeling Playbook
content:
Summary
This playbook documents the Experimental Priming Sandbox: a repeatable, auditable environment for generating, validating, and relabeling priming examples (few-shot anchors, system prompts, and priming templates) before they reach onboarding or shadow fleets. It focuses on safety, cross-tenant isolation, quantization compatibility checks, and a human-in-the-loop relabeling loop to reduce noisy anchors that cause downstream regressions.

Goals
- Provide a lightweight, reproducible sandbox that mirrors production serving characteristics for priming artifacts.
- Detect priming-driven regressions early (semantic drift, hallucination amplification, quant sensitivity).
- Supply an annotated relabeling pipeline that respects annotator privacy and yields high-quality anchors for shadow/onboard promotion.

When to use this sandbox
1. Introducing a new priming family (new few-shot template / system prompt) for a model-suite.
2. Migration of a service to a quantized runtime where priming sensitivity is unknown.
3. Investigating regressions traced to prompt-anchor families in regression triage.
4. Routine pruning and refresh of priming registry prior to major rollout.

Ownership and roles
- Sandbox Owner: Applied ML Platform (primary) — responsible for infra, access control, and monitoring.
- Priming Steward: Service/feature owner — provides candidate priming artifacts and acceptance criteria.
- Annotator Lead: Quality/Labeling — runs relabeling rounds and signs off on dataset quality.
- Evaluator: Applied ML Eng — configures eval harness scenarios and quant checks.
- Security Reviewer: InfoSec (on restricted or customer-sensitive priming artifacts).

High-level workflow
1. Candidate registration: Priming Steward registers new artifacts in the priming registry with metadata (description, expected intents, negative examples, provenance).
2. Synthetic amplification: The harness expands edge cases and counterfactual variants (noise/shuffling, paraphrase, long-context) to probe sensitivity.
3. Shadow simulation: Run priming candidates against a mixed-fidelity shadow mesh (float32 reference + quantized variants) using service-like request traces.
4. Metric collection: Record coherence, hallucination indicators, functioncall stability, token-efficiency, and divergence between float/quant variants.
5. Relabeling loop: Low-confidence or high-disagreement responses are queued for annotators. Relabel results update artifact scores and provenance.
6. Promotion gate: If artifact passes thresholds and annotator sign-off it moves to shadow fleet; otherwise iterate or retire.

Acceptance criteria (promotion gate)
- Coherence score >= 0.85 (service-specific baseline).
- Cross-fidelity divergence (KL-like coherence delta) <= 6% relative.
- No amplification of hallucination markers on anchor-augmented probes (regression delta <= 0.5%).
- Annotator agreement >= 80% on relabeled items.
- Latency overhead <= 5% at p95 when using anchor in production runtime profile.

Sandbox resource configuration (example table)
| Resource | Purpose | Typical size | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Priming harness job | Generate variants and run evals | 2 vCPUs, 8 GB, ephemeral GPU 1xA10 | Short lived, autoscale per queue |
| Shadow mesh | Mixed-fidelity model runners | 4 GPUs (2 float, 2 int8) | Use representative model weights |
| Annotation queue | Human labeling UI + storage | 4 vCPUs, 16 GB, 50 GB storage | S3 bucket with TTL for PII redaction |
| Telemetry store | Probe & telemetry retention | 8 vCPUs, 32 GB DB | Retention 90 days for sandbox artifacts |

Key diagnostic metrics captured
- Per-probe coherence, intent-preservation score, hallucination-signal count.
- Fidelity delta: token-level log-prob divergence between float32 and quantized run.
- Functioncall stability score (normalized rank variance for function results).
- Annotator disagreement (fraction of items needing second pass).
- Priming amplification index: response-length/novel-token expansion over baseline.

Step-by-step: Running a priming experiment
1. Register candidate: Use the priming-registry CLI. Example metadata payload (YAML):

```yaml
name: onboarding-help-template-v2
owner: payments-checkout
intent_tags: ["helpfulness","safety:tokenization"]
description: >-
  Compact few-shot to disambiguate payment error remediation steps.
negatives: ["billing-lookup"]
provenance: manual-author:priya/2026-01-10
```

CLI command: primingctl register --file candidate.yaml

2. Launch synthetic amplification: primingctl expand --candidate onboarding-help-template-v2 --modes paraphrase,noise,context-elongation --samples 500

3. Schedule shadow run: primingctl trigger-shadow --candidate onboarding-help-template-v2 --mesh float32,int8 --trace sample-trace-202601 --deadline 2h

4. Inspect results dashboard: Open Sandbox -> Experiments -> onboarding-help-template-v2. Review fidelity delta heatmap and functioncall variance table.

5. Queue relabeling: primingctl queue-annotate --threshold divergence>0.06 --annotator-group payments-anchors

6. Annotator workflow: Annotators use the Sandbox Labeler UI. Labeling instructions: preserve intent, flag hallucination, quantify response utility (0..3). Include free-text rationale.

7. Promotion or retire: Evaluator reviews metrics + annotator summary and executes primingctl promote --candidate onboarding-help-template-v2 if gate satisfied. Otherwise primingctl retire --candidate ...

Relabeling policy and privacy controls
- Annotators must never see raw user PII. Sandbox must apply deterministic redaction plus synthetic mask where live traffic is used.
- For customer-sensitive artifacts, require Security Reviewer approval (confidentiality: restricted).
- Relabel decisions and comment history are immutable and stored for 1 year for audit.

Quant-compatibility checks (automated)
- Token-level log-prob comparison across float32 and target quant modes. Report the 95th percentile divergence.
- Identify prompts where quant causes rank inversion for critical tokens (functioncall names, entity identifiers).
- Run targeted micro-benchmarks: repeated long-context with anchored priming to detect KV cache misalignment.

Troubleshooting common failure modes
- High fidelity delta but low annotator disagreement: often cosmetic phrasing differences. Apply normalization (whitespace/casing) and re-evaluate.
- High annotator disagreement: re-run with expanded paraphrase set and add an adjudicator pass.
- Latency regression on p95: try shorter anchors, move heavy examples to background priming, or apply prompt condensation (template compression).

Rollback and incident integration
- Any promoted priming artifact must have a rollback artifact (previous anchor version or empty anchor) and a rollback plan in the promotion ticket.
- If a regression is detected in production tied to priming, follow Regression Triage Playbook: create an incident, capture sample traces, run targeted sandbox replay, and escalate to Model Onboarding for root-cause.

Operational runbooks (quick steps)
- Emergency disable: primingctl disable --candidate <id> (immediate removal from live routing).
- Fast replay: primingctl replay --trace <trace-id> --candidate <id> --to float32,int8 --out /tmp/replay.json
- Extract disagreement set: primingctl exports failures --candidate <id> --min-agreement 0.6 --format ndjson

Housekeeping and lifecycle
- Sandbox artifacts older than 180 days are archived unless actively referenced in onboarding tickets.
- Quarterly priming audit: Priming Steward must run an audit report and retire anchors with low utility (usage < 0.1% and negative impact on fidelity).

Appendix: Example experiment JSON output (trimmed)
```json
{
  "candidate": "onboarding-help-template-v2",
  "runs": [
    {"mesh":"float32","coherence":0.89,"hallucination":0.01},
    {"mesh":"int8","coherence":0.82,"hallucination":0.012}
  ],
  "fidelity_delta": 0.074,
  "annotator_agreement": 0.81
}
```

References and links
- Priming registry spec: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/priming-registry-manifest-2025
- Regression triage: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024
- Quant checks: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-output-degradation-detect-and-repair-protocol-2026

Contact
- For questions or access requests contact: applied-ml-platform@redwood.ai or Priya Nambiar (priya@redwood.ai)

title: Model launch evaluation gates (Hosted API catalog)
content:
# Overview
