This page defines the required evaluation gates for launching a new model into the Hosted API model catalog. The goal is to ensure we can safely serve the model, meet product quality expectations, and detect regressions after launch.

# Ownership and signoff
- Gate owner (quality): Applied ML (Onboarding + Evals)
- Required signoff: Applied ML + Product (for model positioning)
- Optional signoff: Customer Success (if a launch is for a named account)

# Required evaluation suites
All Hosted API catalog launches must pass *all* suites below. Each suite must be run on the candidate model build (exact weights + tokenizer + runtime config) and logged in the eval harness.

## Suite A: Internal prompt set regression
- Source: `prompt-sets/hosted-api/core-regression`
- Metrics: win-rate vs current default in family; structured output adherence for required schemas
- Pass criteria:
  - Overall win-rate >= 50% vs baseline (no regression)
  - Any critical prompt tagged `p0` must not regress
- Artifact: eval harness run link + summary paragraph

## Suite B: Public benchmark sanity
- Source: curated public tasks (e.g., MMLU subset, GSM8K subset, HumanEval-lite)
- Purpose: catch obvious misconfigs, broken tokenizer, prompt formatting issues
- Pass criteria:
  - No single task drops > 5% absolute vs upstream reported numbers *after adjusting for our settings*
  - If upstream numbers are unavailable, compare vs adjacent model sizes in family and explain outliers
- Artifact: table of scores + notes

## Suite C: Safety and policy screening (lightweight)
- Source: policy prompts + refusal behavior checks
- Pass criteria:
  - No increase in disallowed content generation on policy set
  - Refusal templates must be compatible with Redwood policy layer
- Artifact: pass/fail summary + any required policy config notes

## Suite D: Tool/function calling compatibility (if applicable)
- Required when the model is marketed for tools/function calling
- Pass criteria:
  - JSON schema conformance >= 99% on tool-calling prompt set
- Artifact: schema validation report link

# Required documentation artifacts
A launch packet must include:
1. Eval harness run URLs for all required suites
2. A one-paragraph risk assessment (what could go wrong in prod)
3. A recommended default inference config (temperature/top_p/max_tokens defaults)
4. Known limitations (e.g., cannot do reliable tool calling; poor multilingual)

# Escalations and exceptions
- Exceptions must be approved by the Applied ML gate owner and recorded as a label `eval-exception` on the Linear ticket.
- If Suite A fails on any `p0` prompt, do not ship.

# Post-launch monitoring requirement
For the first 7 days after GA:
- Enable quality canary (1% traffic shadow to baseline, where possible)
- Watch `quality_regression_alerts` dashboard and error budget burn
- File a follow-up ticket if any metric crosses thresholds (see Platform runbook)

# Related pages
- Hosted API model intake
- Hosted model performance bar
- Hosted model rollout and fallback runbook

title: Cross-Stage Evaluation Contracts and Explainability Protocol
content:
Overview
====
This document defines the cross-stage evaluation contracts we use to move models from onboarding to production, and introduces a standard protocol for surface-level explainability checks that must be run as part of automated evals. It ties together eval-harness integration points, prompt set sampling, quantization verification, quality guardrail assertions, and regression-triage signals so each stage can be automatically verified and quickly diagnosed when metrics regress.

Scope
----
- Applies to: model-onboarding, quantization-profiles, eval-harness CI, and regression-triage pipelines.
- Environments: qa, staging, dedicated, hosted-preview.
- Consumers: model-owners, applied-ml engineers, SRE oncall for inference services, product owners for quality gates.

Goals and principles
----
- Define machine-readable contracts between stages (onboarding -> quantize -> canary -> prod).
- Surface explainability signals that are cheap to compute and provide high signal for prediction drift or harmful behavior.
- Ensure evals are deterministic where required and probabilistic where useful (sampling-based prompt tests).
- Provide runbook scaffolding for regression-triage that ties specific metrics to likely root causes.

Evaluation Contract (machine-readable)
----
We require every model candidate to publish an evaluation artifact that conforms to this contract: a YAML file located with model artifacts and a final results JSON produced by the eval harness. Minimal contract fields: model_id, model_variant, dataset_refs, date, top_level_metrics, explainability_signals, quant_profiles_tested, artifact_uri.

Example eval_contract.yaml
```
model_id: redwood-llama-7b-v2
model_variant: quantized-4bit-llm
date: 2026-02-01
dataset_refs:
  - promptset: prompt-catalog-v2026/semantic-diversity
  - stress-suite: stress-long-context-2026
top_level_metrics:
  rouge_l: 0.72
  perplexity: 12.6
  safety_score: 0.98
explainability_signals:
  token_shap_top5_fraction: 0.12
  attribution_entropy: 1.9
quant_profiles_tested:
  - q4_2pass
  - q8_mixed
artifact_uri: s3://redwood-evals/2026-02-01/redwood-llama-7b-v2/eval.json
```

Evaluation metric sanity table (examples)
| metric | target | type | alert threshold | owner |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| latency_p95 (ms) | <= 90 | perf | > 120 | infra-serving |
| end_to_end_loss | <= 0.45 | quality | > 0.55 | applied-ml |
| safety_score | >= 0.95 | safety | < 0.92 | safety-team |
| token_shap_top5_fraction | <= 0.25 | explain | > 0.40 | applied-ml |

Prompt set sampling & annotation protocol
----
1. Sample strategy: stratified by intent, length, and entity density. For production promotion we require: 3k stratified samples for functional evals, 500 adversarial prompts, and 200 long-context prompts (>= 2k tokens).
2. Annotation schema: JSONL with fields: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_behavior, critical_flags[], severity_bucket, rubric_scores{}. Use the rubric to capture hallucination, relevance, and toxicity on 1-5 scales.
3. Inter-annotator agreement: target Cohen's kappa >= 0.6 for critical_flags on any new prompt set release. If lower, run a calibration pass with lead annotators.

Explainability checks (fast, automated)
----
We require the eval harness to compute a set of lightweight explainability signals for each prompt batch. These are intended to be inexpensive and informative for triage:
- Token-level SHAP surrogates (approximate via influence functions over last-layer embeddings).
- Attribution entropy: per-response Shannon entropy over normalized positive/negative attribution weights.
- Top-k token concentration: fraction of total attribution mass in top 5 tokens.
- Context-sensitivity delta: compare attributions with and without the first 128 tokens of context to detect over-reliance on prefix.

Example explainability CLI run
```
python -m redwood_eval.run \
  --config eval_contract.yaml \
  --explainability --explain-backend=approx-shap \
  --output artifacts/redwood-llama-7b-v2/
```

Quantization verification overlay
----
When quantized variants are evaluated, include these checks in the same eval run:
- Quant delta test: run a 500-sample micro-benchmark comparing logits distribution statistics (mean, std, KL divergence) between float32 baseline and quantized model. Alert if KL > 0.08 on critical benchmarks.
- KV-cache fidelity: for a set of 200 sequences with repeated prefixes, verify identical next-token top-1 for >= 98% of steps.
- Determinism smoke test: run the same seed twice (batching shapes changed) and assert token-sequence equality on deterministic modes.

Regression triage signals and automated prioritization
----
Signal sources: CI eval runs, prod telemetry (latency, safety alerts), user-reported tickets, and canary guardrail violations. Each signal is scored and routed by the triage service:
- Score = w1*metric_delta_zscore + w2*production_impact + w3*heurstic_severity_flag
- Priority buckets: P0 (immediate), P1 (next-day), P2 (backlog)

Triage checklist (fast path)
1. Reproduce: rerun the eval contract locally with the same artifact_uri.
2. Compare: run a diff between top_level_metrics and explainability_signals against the last-passing artifact.
3. Narrow: check quantization overlay (if quantized) and KV-cache fidelity.
4. Hypothesize: map metric pattern to likely causes using the table below.
5. Escalate: attach artifacts and open postmortem if P0.

Common metric patterns -> likely causes
- latency_p95 jump + p50 stable -> scheduling/queueing regression or catastrophic batching drop. Owner: infra-serving.
- safety_score drop + explainability token concentration increase -> model shift (training data drift) or prompt amplification. Owner: safety/applied-ml.
- hallucination rate up + attribution_entropy increase -> quantization precision loss in output head. Owner: applied-ml + runtime kernel team.
- perplexity up + KV-cache mismatch on repeat prefixes -> KV-cache invalidation bug or rollout of incompatible model variant. Owner: serving-runtime.

Runbook snippet for P0 safety regression
1. Mark canary as fail and rollback to last-passing model: `redwoodctl rollout cancel && redwoodctl rollout promote --model-id <last-good>`
2. Disable serving fallback to newer variant: `redwoodctl config set fallback_policy=disabled --scope=canary`
3. Capture artifacts: export model eval artifacts, explainability traces, and last 1k offending prompts.
4. Notify: `#sre-oncall`, `safety@redwood.com`, and the model-owner.

Integration with CI and release gates
----
- Presubmit: small smoke eval (200 samples, explainability on) must pass.
- Merge gate: full eval_contract.yaml run for PRs that touch model code or quant profiles.
- Promotion: gating by evaluation artifact review + manual spot checks (random 1% of prompts).

Operational responsibilities and ownership
----
- applied-ml: owns eval_contract spec, quality metrics definitions, and explainability algorithm maintenance.
- infra-serving/runtime: owns latency and cache fidelity SLOs integrated into the contract.
- safety-team: maintains safety_score rubric and approves any change to critical_flags semantics.
- SRE: owns triage automation and routing.

Onboarding checklist for new model owners
----
1. Create model repo scaffold with eval_contract.yaml and a basic prompt subset.
2. Run presubmit smoke: `pytools eval run --smoke --output /tmp/eval` and attach results.
3. Configure quant profiles to test (q8_mixed, q4_2pass).
4. Submit to the model-onboarding pipeline and request a model review.

Audit and compliance notes
----
- All eval artifacts must be retained for 180 days in the evaluation bucket for audit and postmortem.
- Explainability outputs are considered internal derivatives and must not be exported to customer-visible logs unless redacted.

Appendix: JSON schema (summary) for eval results
```
{
  "model_id": "string",
  "variant": "string",
  "eval_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "metrics": {"metric_name": "number"},
  "explainability": {"signal_name": "number"},
  "quant_tests": ["string"],
  "artifacts": ["uri"]
}
```

Contacts
----
- Document owner: Marina Kolesnikov (applied-ml)
- Triage escalation: SRE pager (see internal SRE runbook)
- Safety contact: safety@redwood.com

Revision history
----
- 2025-11-20: created (Marina Kolesnikov)
- 2026-01-12: added quantization overlay details (Luis Ortega)
- 2026-02-08: clarified explainability signals and CI integration (Priya Anand)

title: Cascade Probe Resilience and Repair Playbook
content:
SUMMARY
This page describes detection, emergency mitigation, and long-term prevention for cascading failures in the eval harness probe pipeline. We define failure modes that commonly cause large-scale evaluation regressions, provide an emergency runbook to restore safe continuity, and list durable design changes and configuration standards to prevent recurrence.

Scope
- Applies to the eval-harness execution plane (probe generator, sequencer, shadow router, and annotator ingestion queue).
- Includes interactions with: quantized shadow artifacts, KV cache warmup probes, and external annotator workers.
- Does NOT cover model training pipeline bugs or user-facing product incidents unless they are caused by an eval probe cascade.

Why this matters
- A single overloaded probe generator or stalled annotation queue can amplify into systemic false-positive regressions, wasted compute, and production instability for private/dedicated shadowing.
- Detecting and containing cascades early preserves evaluation fidelity, reduces noise for oncall, and keeps rollout gates (canaries, quant rollbacks) actionable.

Symptoms (observable metrics)
- Probe-failure-rate (probe.errors / probe.total) > 5% for 30m.
- Sequencer queue latency (p95) > 10s or steady growth for 15m.
- Annotation backlog > 10k unprocessed items AND ingestion rate falling > 30% vs baseline.
- Spike in duplicate probes / replays (indicates retry storm).
- Sudden divergence between shadow and synthetic control probes (indicates quantization or cache mismatch).

Common root-cause patterns
1. Backpressure amplification: downstream annotator lag triggers probe retry policy which pushes more load upstream.
2. Retry storms: aggressive retry policy (low jitter, high concurrency) + transient infra failure -> exponential traffic.
3. Quantization-induced behavioral skew: quantized model variant returns unexpected tokens and triggers extra post-processing or longer traces.
4. Sequencer scheduling inversion: priority inversion where low-priority bulk probes starve critical control probes.
5. Resource exhaustion: ephemeral node OOM or GPU out-of-memory causing probe workers to exit repeatedly and restart.
6. Telemetry blindspots: missing sampling of failed probe payloads, preventing root-cause attribution.

Emergency mitigation runbook (fast path)
Run this immediately when alerts indicate a spike matching the symptoms above. The goal is to stop amplification and buy time for a careful rollback/repair.

Ownership: eval-platform oncall (primary), model-onboarding (secondary), infra-sre (escalate when node-level OOMs are present).

Immediate steps (0–15 minutes)
1) Acknowledge pager and post incident stub in #eval-incidents with tags: cascade, severity:high.
2) Throttle probe ingestion: flip the sequencer rate-limit toggle to 20% of normal via the admin console OR run:

   # temporarily reduce probe rate to 1/5
   curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/eval/sequencer/rate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"target_fraction":0.2,"reason":"cascade-mitigation"}'

3) Disable aggressive retries: change probe retry policy to exponential backoff with jitter and caps. Apply the emergency policy:
   - base: 1s, factor: 2, jitter: true, max_retries: 3, max_backoff: 300s

4) Pause non-essential shadow experiments: set shadow-router tag multipliers to 0 for low-priority experiments.

5) Open a telemetry capture window for failed probes: enable full payload logging for the failing probe family for 15 minutes, write logs to a quarantined S3 prefix: s3://eval-debug/quarantine/<incident-id>/

6) If annotation backlog > 50k, spin up temporary annotator workers (runbook for autoscale: infra-sre) OR toggle manual expedited labeling for high-priority slices.

Stabilization checks (15–60 minutes)
1) Confirm probe-failure-rate trending down to < 1% and queue latency p95 below 5s.
2) Validate that retry counters are not growing and duplicate probe counts fall.
3) If quantized variant involved, temporarily pin evaluation routing to the float reference or last-known-good quant artifact.

Rollback / repair decisions (60–240 minutes)
- If rollback to last-known-good brings system back to healthy levels, schedule a postmortem and leave the rollback in place until root cause fixed.
- If the cascade is caused by a specific probe family, disable that family and create a prioritized mitigation ticket.

Post-incident diagnosis (post-stabilization)
- Collect the quarantined payloads, probe logs, and a compressed execution trace from the sequencer for the incident window.
- Run the automated bisect script against probe artifacts (see related: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/automated-regression-bisect-and-blame-assistant-2026).
- Classify root cause into one of the patterns above and tag the incident with: root_cause_pattern, estimated_impact_tokens, affected_models.

Long-term prevention (design and configuration changes)
1) Default retry-safety policy (applied to all probe agents):
   - max_retries: 3
   - base_backoff_s: 0.8
   - max_backoff_s: 300
   - jitter: true
   - circuit_breaker_threshold: 10 failures / 60s per probe-family

2) Sequencer safety knobs:
   - prioritized control probe lane (reserved QPS 50) that cannot be backfilled by bulk probes.
   - soft-ttl on probes: default 48 hours; probes older than TTL are tombstoned.

3) Probe family metadata enforcement: every probe must declare: owner, priority (critical/high/normal), expected-cost-tokens, safe-fallback-route. The sequencer rejects unlabeled probe families.

4) Annotation autoscale thresholds: proactively provision extra workers when backlog > 5k for 10m, with a hard cap tied to budget alerts.

5) Shadow routing durability: automatic pin-to-reference when divergence metric (shadow_vs_reference_coherence) falls below 0.85 for two consecutive windows.

6) Telemetry coverage: sample 100% of failing probe payloads for first 10m of a failure, then 5% afterwards. Ensure redaction pipeline before storage.

Operational SLOs and alert thresholds (proposal)
- Probe success rate: 99.5% over 24h for control probe families.
- Sequencer queue latency p95: < 5s.
- Annotation backlog: < 5k unprocessed with smoothing window 1h.
- Automatic circuit-breaker trips: manual review required after 3 trips in a 7-day window.

Config reference (table)
| config_key | recommended_default | rationale |
|-----------|---------------------|-----------|
| probe.ttl_hours | 48 | Prevents stale probes from amplifying long-tail issues |
| probe.max_retries | 3 | Limits retry storms while preserving transient resilience |
| sequencer.control_qps | 50 | Reserved QPS for critical control probes |
| annotator.autoscale_backlog | 5000 | Trigger autoscale before latency degrades |
| retry.jitter | true | Breaks synchronization between failing workers |

Example emergency policy snippet (YAML)
apiVersion: eval/v1
kind: EmergencyPolicy
metadata:
  name: cascade-mitigation-2026
spec:
  sequencer:
    target_rate_fraction: 0.2
  retryPolicy:
    base: 1s
    factor: 2
    jitter: true
    maxRetries: 3
    maxBackoff: 300s

Ownership and escalation matrix
- eval-platform-oncall: primary (pager)
- model-onboarding: secondary (model-related failures)
- infra-sre: node-level resource exhaustion and autoscale failures
- applied-ml: assists with probe design and quant failure analysis

Post-incident actions (must be completed within 5 business days)
1) Fill incident template: link to logs, root-cause classification, and remediation plan.
2) Create a changelog entry in the probe family registry with the action taken and retention policy changes.
3) Run a targeted smoke eval against the affected family after fixes and collect before/after coherence scores.

Pre-deployment checklist for new probe families
1) Declare probe metadata (owner, priority, expected_token_cost, fallback_route).
2) Run local burst test: 10k probes at scaled intervals to verify sequencing and ttl handling.
3) Nightly shadow run for 48h with metrics gated (success rate >= 99.7%).
4) Quantized artifact check: run quant-sensitivity probe suite and ensure shadow_vs_reference_coherence >= 0.9.

Appendix A — Useful diagnostic commands
- Inspect sequencer queue: kubectl logs deploy/sequencer -n eval --since=1h | jq '.queue_stats'
- Toggle rate limit: curl -X POST https://admin.internal/eval/sequencer/rate -d '{"target_fraction":0.2}'
- Capture failed probe payloads (one-off): aws s3 cp s3://eval-logs/failure-window/<id> ./ --profile eval-debug

Appendix B — Example incident timeline (illustrative)
1) 12:03: spike in probe-failure-rate to 8%
2) 12:07 sequencer p95 queue latency rising to 18s
3) 12:12 admin toggles rate to 20% and disables aggressive retries
4) 12:25 queue latency down to 4.2s; failure-rate falling to 0.9%
5) 15:00 rollback of quantized artifact to float reference; proxy pinned to last-known-good

Related reading and links
- Probe lifecycle and TTL enforcement: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/probe-lifecycle-annotation-economics-playbook-2026
- Quant failure modes and repair: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-output-degradation-detect-and-repair-protocol-2026
- Automated bisect and blame assistant: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/automated-regression-bisect-and-blame-assistant-2026

Document maintenance
- Owner: eval-platform team
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any incident categorized as cascade.
- Last review: 2026-02-18

End of document

title: Representative Session Trace Fabricator and Eval Seeding Blueprint
content:
Summary:
This document defines the 'Session Trace Fabricator' — a standardized toolkit and procedure for synthesizing representative long-session traces used to seed evals, stress benches, and shadow workloads across model-onboarding, quantization safety checks, and regression triage. It centers on reproducibility, tenant realism, and quantization compatibility without relying on customer PII.

Scope:
- Audience: ML engineers, evaluators, model-onboarding teams, QA owners, and applied-research.
- Use cases: seeding eval meshes, generating long-context stress profiles, priming registries, creating canary/shadow traffic for quant-aware rollouts, and constructing synthetic probes for rare-slice failure modes.

Goals:
- Produce representative sessions that preserve request/response distributions, multi-turn persistence patterns, and function-call behavior while removing sensitive data.
- Ensure generated traces are annotated with fidelity metadata (fidelity_score, priming_vector, quant_compat_flags).
- Provide a repeatable CLI and API for scaled trace generation.

Definitions:
- Session Trace: ordered list of user/system messages, model responses, functioncalls, and associated telemetry (latency, token counts).
- Priming Vector: compact descriptor that encodes the prompt-anchoring context used when fabricating the session (template id, few-shot examples, locale).
- Quant Compatibility Flags: per-trace flags indicating likely sensitivity to quantization (high/medium/low) computed by the Quant Sensitivity Module.

Design Overview:
1) Components:
   - Trace Templates: YAML templates that encode intent flows (e.g., multi-step booking, nested functioncalls, policy reasoning).
   - Session Sampler: probabilistic sampler that mixes templates with real traffic-derived fingerprints.
   - Sanitizer: deterministic redactor + privacy transformer to remove PII and maintain statistical properties.
   - Annotator: attaches provenance fields, priming_vector, and quant_compat_flags.
   - Output Formatter: emits traces to JSONL, parquet, or the Eval Asset Registry.

2) Trace Template spec (summary):
   - id: short string
   - description: one-line
   - intents: ordered list of intent names and branching probabilities
   - example_user_turns: 2–6 canonical utterances per intent
   - expected_function_patterns: optional (e.g., call sequence: [search, enrich, book])
   - context_length_profile: distribution (mean, 90p)

Example template (YAML excerpt):
| id: booking-nested-3step
| description: user searches, asks clarifying q, then books with payment fragment
| intents:
|   - { name: search, p: 0.45 }
|   - { name: clarify, p: 0.35 }
|   - { name: confirm_payment, p: 0.20 }

Operational Procedure (step-by-step):
1. Create or select templates for the target workload slice. Record template id and steward.
2. Configure session sampler parameters: target_token_dist, multi_turn_depth, functioncall_rate, locale_mix.
3. Run fabricator in dry-run mode: samples=100, output=synthetic-dryrun.jsonl.
4. Sanitize outputs; run automatic privacy checks (PII-score < 0.01 threshold).
5. Annotator computes quant_compat_flags using the quant-sensitivity model and writes metadata.
6. Seed eval harness: register traces in eval asset registry with tags (service, slice, quant_risk).
7. Run targeted evals (smoke -> fidelity -> cost) and compare to seed acceptance criteria.

CLI examples:
- Dry run (100):
  redwood-eval-fabricator generate --template booking-nested-3step --samples 100 --mode dryrun --out /tmp/booking-dryrun.jsonl

- Produce and register with metadata:
  redwood-eval-fabricator generate --template billing-edgecase-guard --samples 5000 --locale en-US --register --tags "quant-risk:high,service:billing"

JSON trace example (one-line placeholder):
{
  "session_id": "fabric-20260203-0001",
  "template_id": "booking-nested-3step",
  "turns": [
    {"role":"user","text":"I need a flight to SFO next Tuesday"},
    {"role":"assistant","text":"Do you prefer morning or evening?"},
    {"role":"user","text":"Morning, and a window seat please"},
    {"role":"assistant","function_call": {"name":"search_flights","args": "{...}"},"text":"Searching..."},
    {"role":"assistant","text":"I found a 9:10am option, proceed to payment?"}
  ],
  "telemetry": {"tokens_total": 142, "approx_latency_ms": 320, "kv_cache_deltas": "low"},
  "metadata": {"priming_vector":"pv_3f2a","quant_compat_flags":"medium","fidelity_score":"0.88"}
}

Quantization Compatibility Matrix (example — text table):
| workload_profile | quant_risk | suggested_fallback | test_scope |
| booking-heavy     | medium     | per-turn 8-bit fallback | shadow-run with mixed-precision |
| functioncall-dense| high       | disabled static-quant for fcall path | canary with querier-only |
| chat-short        | low        | aggressive 4-bit allowed | unit-run |

Acceptance criteria for seeds (minimum):
- Fidelity score >= 0.75 for functional slices (function-call correctness).
- Token distribution KL < 0.07 compared to production fingerprint for the same slice.
- PII-score < 0.01 after Sanitizer.
- Quant-sensitivity: no more than 5% of generated traces flagged as 'high' for low-priority slices.

Seeding the eval mesh (recommended staging flow):
1. Register traces in the Eval Asset Registry with labels: slice, priming_vector, template_id, created_by.
2. Assign to eval lanes: smoke, fidelity, cost, stress.
3. Run smoke in a small cohort (10% jobs) -> inspect sample outputs and metrics.
4. Promote to fidelity lane if smoke pass; run side-by-side against current production model for coherence and functioncall accuracy.
5. Run quant-aware shadow with mixed-precision candidates.
6. If discrepancy > thresholds, open an onboarding ticket with Model Onboarding and Quant teams and attach sample failing traces.

Telemetry and Metrics to collect on fabricated traces:
- sample_coherence: automated scorer vs anchor outputs (0–1).
- token_histogram: distribution vector to compute KL divergence.
- functioncall_recall: fraction of expected fcall sequences matched in output.
- quant_perturbation_sensitivity: delta in fidelity when switching precision.
- privacy_artifact_rate: redaction events per session.

Regression triage playbook (when seeded evals fail):
1. Triage owner (assigned by test-run) collects: failing trace id, model version, eval lane, metric deltas.
2. Re-run the trace under deterministic seeds (seed id logged) to rule out nondeterminism.
3. Compare outputs across: baseline unquantized, candidate-quant, and candidate-unquantized.
4. If failure is quant-sensitive, tag with quant_failure_mode: {lossy-tokenization, kv-cache-inconsistency, functioncall-mismatch}.
5. If failure maps to prompt-priming variance, check priming_vector: run ablation by swapping few-shot examples.
6. Escalate to Model Onboarding if root cause is model drift or decoder-regression; include 10 failing traces and annotated diffs.
7. For infra-induced regressions (latency/timeouts), attach telemetry spans and hand to runtime team runbook 'eval-failure-runtime-handoff'.

Rolling to production: checklist (must be completed before seeding canary):
- [ ] Templates reviewed by a second SME and documented with stewardship.
- [ ] PII-score verification and privacy audit signed off.
- [ ] Quant-compatibility review: flags evaluated and mitigation plan defined.
- [ ] Seeds registered and smoke/fidelity lanes passed.
- [ ] Canary run executed with traffic shadowing and automatic rollback hooks enabled.
- [ ] Post-carry forward plan for trace retirement and storage TTL set (default 90 days).

Ownership and contacts:
- Fabricator library (code + CLI): eng/eval-platform (owner: Avery Chen).
- Quant sensitivity model: research/optimization (owner: Marco Delgado).
- Privacy/Sanitizer: security-and-compliance (contact: Priya Rao).

Appendix A — Sanitizer rules (high level):
- Deterministic redaction: emails, phone numbers, IPs -> replace with consistent tokens.
- Name hashing: replace name spans with hashed pseudo-identifiers preserving count statistics.
- Numeric bucketing: replace high-precision numbers with bins (e.g., amounts -> <$10, $10-100, >$100).
- Sampling-only linking: do not attempt to reconstruct cross-session customer ids in synth traces.

Appendix B — Recommended storage schema (JSONL fields):
session_id, template_id, created_by, created_at, turns, telemetry, metadata.tags, metrics (coherence, token_kld, quant_sens).

Appendix C — Example test plan snippet (for model onboarding):
1) Objective: ensure new model M_x maintains functioncall fidelity on booking-nested-3step traces.
2) Seeds: 5k booking-nested-3step traces, priming_vector variants=3.
3) Success: functioncall_recall >= 0.95, fidelity_score_delta <= 0.03 vs baseline.
4) Fallback: if quant-perturbation_sensitivity > 0.08, route booking slice to dedicated unquantized pool.

Related reading and links:
- See the Eval Asset Registry README for registration APIs.
- See Quant Sensitivity Module design doc for the quant_compat_flags algorithm.

Change log:
- 2025-11-12: initial draft and internal review.
- 2026-02-03: added quant compatibility matrix and triage playbook updates.

Contacts for feedback: avery.chen@redwood.ai, priya.rao@redwood.ai

title: Synthetic User Simulation and Long-tail Eval Protocol
content:
Overview
This document defines the Synthetic User Simulation (SUS) framework and the Long-tail Evaluation Protocol (LTEP) used by Redwood Inference to validate model behavior and serving correctness across rare, compound, and emergent input patterns. The intention is to produce repeatable, auditable simulations that exercise production routing, caching, KV behavior, quantized execution, and fallback logic.

Goals
- Provide a reproducible harness for generating realistic long-tail user requests and multi-turn sessions.
- Measure model and serving stability across compound perturbations (tokenization, prompt templates, kv-cache state, quant noise).
- Produce artifact outputs for triage: deterministic traces, synthetic user IDs, seed manifests, and per-slice metrics.
- Integrate with CI and the eval mesh to block model promotions on regressions of defined slices.

Scope and non-goals
- Scope: multi-turn chat, few-shot templates, embedding drift probes, reranking workloads, and long-context summarization flows.
- Non-goals: full user privacy simulation (do not attempt to rehydrate PII); SUS must use synthetic/generated entities only.

Definitions and terminology
- Session: ordered sequence of user messages and system/tool calls intended to mimic a single interaction.
- Slice: a labeled subset of sessions sharing attributes (e.g., nonstandard tokenization, mixed languages, deep-turn > 40).
- Perturbation: synthetic modification applied to inputs (typos, injection tokens, sentence shuffling, prefix truncation).

High-level architecture
1. Seed Catalog: canonical prompt templates, persona generators, and locale distributions.
2. Perturbation Engine: applies deterministic/noisy transforms to seeds with reproducible RNG seeds.
3. Session Mixer: composes multi-turn sequences, optional tool calls, and stateful KV cache interactions.
4. Runner: executes sessions against target model variants via the eval mesh and records full traces.
5. Analyzer: computes per-slice metrics and produces regression/quality reports.

Example evaluation slices (recommended)
- Tokenization-edge: mixed-encoding, zero-width joiners, and emoji-heavy input.
- Deep-context: session length >= 40 user/system turns; tests KV reuse efficiency.
- Few-shot-template-variance: permutations of demonstration order and answer-key formats.
- Quant-noise-probe: identical prompt executed on fp16, int8, and q4 profiles to surface divergence.
- Cross-lingual/romanization: code-switched tokens and transliteration fallbacks.

Metrics and thresholds
- Semantic-consistency-score (SCS): aggregated BERTScore-type metric compared to golden replies; pass threshold >= 0.82 for critical slices.
- Latency-90 (L90): 90th percentile token-end latency; must be <= 220ms for hosted SLO workloads, <= 350ms for dedicated background workloads.
- Token-delta drift (TDD): percent token count variance vs baseline <= 12% for deterministic prompts.
- Output-stability-index (OSI): fraction of identical deterministic outputs across N=5 seeds; must be >= 0.9 for inference-readiness slices.
- Regression-alert: any delta in SCS > 0.03 or OSI drop > 0.08 triggers triage.

Artifact outputs (required)
- session-trace-<seed>.json: full request/response with headers and timing.
- seed-manifest.csv: seed_id, template_id, RNG_seed, slice_tags.
- metric-report-<model>-<variant>.csv: per-slice metrics and baseline deltas.
- failure-bundle.tar.gz: representative traces, model logs (if available), and runtime config.

Experiment configuration table (example)
| field | description | example |
|---|---|---|
| model_variant | model tag under test | redwood-7b-v2-qat-q4 |
| batch_policy | batching mode | continuous-batch-128 |
| kv_mode | KV cache policy | enable-local, preload-prefix=128 |
| quant_profile | quantization configuration | q8_256_tile_sparse |
| seed_set | synthetic seed catalog version | sus-seedset-v1.4 |
| rng_seed | numeric seed for perturbation reproducibility | 20260202 |
| run_id | unique run id | sus-run-2026-02-02-01 |

Run procedure (step-by-step)
1. Provision: allocate an eval runner in the desired environment (hosted/dedicated/private). Ensure the runner has network egress to the eval mesh.
2. Prepare artifacts: pull seed-set (sus-seedset-v1.4) and perturbation configs.
3. Start run: ./sus-runner --config sus-config.yaml --run-id sus-run-2026-02-02-01 --parallelism 32
4. Monitor: watch L90 and OSI in the run dashboard; abort run if L90 > 600ms for >5 minutes.
5. Collect: when complete, gather session traces and metric-report CSVs. Upload to artifacts store and link to run id.
6. Evaluate: Analyzer computes deltas vs baseline and generates regression-alerts if thresholds breached.

Example sus-config.yaml (inline)
---
model_variant: "redwood-7b-v2-qat-q4"
batch_policy: "continuous-batch-64"
kv_mode: "preload-prefix=64"
quant_profile: "q4_opt_level_2"
seed_set: "sus-seedset-v1.4"
perturbations:
  - name: typo-insert
    rate: 0.12
  - name: emoji-injection
    rate: 0.05
  - name: prefix-truncation
    max_prefix_len: 512
parallelism: 24
retries_on_failure: 2
output_bucket: "s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/sus/${run_id}/"
---

Failure triage checklist
1. Confirm reproducibility: re-run top failing session with identical rng_seed and model_variant.
2. Compare quantized vs fp baseline: run same seed on fp16 to determine if quantization is primary cause.
3. Inspect tokenization: re-tokenize inputs with dev tokenization tool; compare token boundaries and special token insertion.
4. KV-cache sensitivity: replay session with cache-warmup and cache-cleared modes.
5. Network/runtime noise: confirm CPU/GPU contention and host telemetry (GPU SM utilization, NVLink errors) during failing run.

Integration and gating rules
- Every model promotion to staging must include 3 SUS runs: short-smoke (1k sessions), deep-context (5k sessions, mixed slices), and quant-fidelity sweep (10k sessions across quant profiles).
- Promotion gating: no critical slices with regression-alerts, and aggregate SCS within 0.02 of baseline.
- If gating fails, attach failure-bundle and open a regression ticket with priority tag: regress/auto-block.

Dashboarding and alerting
- Expose per-slice SCS, OSI, L90 and TDD on the eval mesh dashboard.
- Alert channel: #eval-regressions with automated triage summary and link to failure-bundle.
- Weekly digest: long-tail drift trends and top 10 failing seeds.

Ownership and maintenance
- Primary owner: Applied ML — Eval Harness (owner: Nina Patel).
- Secondary owner: Serving Runtime (owner: Evan Morales) for infra and runner reliability.
- Maintenance cadence: seed-set refresh quarterly or after major model architecture changes.

CI integration
1. Add SUS run step to model promotion pipeline (nightly for candidate builds).
2. Store artifacts in immutable storage; reference run_id in promotion PRs.
3. Fail fast: if automated triage marks run as 'block', the promotion pipeline must stop and assign to oncall owner.

Privacy and data hygiene
- All synthetic seeds must be generated from safe-name and safe-entity tables. No PII, real email addresses, or real phone numbers are permitted.
- Seed manifests must include a lineage field that states generator version.

Appendix: quick CLI examples
- Launch single-session replay (developer): ./sus-runner --replay session-trace-20260202-0001.json --model redwood-7b-v2-qat-q4 --output ./replay-output.json
- Run quant sweep: ./sus-runner --config quant-sweep.yaml --sweep-profiles [fp16,q4,q8] --run-id quant-sweep-2026-02-02

References
- eval-harness/promotion-readiness-synthetic-quant-safety-playbook (internal)
- prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/edgecase-probe-generator-and-labeling-guidelines-2026 (internal)

Change log
- 2025-09-18: Document created (Nina Patel).
- 2025-12-07: Added quant-noise-probe slice and artifact naming conventions (Evan Morales).
- 2026-02-02: Formalized CI gating rules and thresholds; published.

title: Runtime slice profiling and quant stress sandbox playbook
content:
Overview

This playbook describes the runtime slice profiling and quant stress sandbox used to detect and triage behaviour regressions introduced by quantization or runtime kernel changes. It combines continuous lightweight slice profiling in production shadow runs with an isolated, reproducible sandbox for aggressive quant and kernel stress tests. The goal is early detection of coherence regressions (hallucinations, factual errors, repetition) and degradations in token-level quality before promotion to Dedicated or Hosted fleets.

When to use

- Before promoting a model or quant profile from staging -> production.
- After kernel or compiler upgrades that affect attention/kv-cache behaviour.
- When a regression slice is flagged by the continuous eval or customer report.
- During cross-workload quant rollouts (heterogeneous hardware deployments).

Definitions and key concepts

- Slice: a defined subset of prompts (or probe families) representing a workload characteristic (e.g., long-context summarization, multi-turn code editing, low-resource language QA).
- Profiling fingerprint: a compact runtime signature (avg seq length, attention pattern entropy, kv cache miss rate, token generation distribution) used to route probes to suitable stress profiles.
- Stress sandbox: isolated environment (ephemeral cluster) configured to run quant/kernels at edge-case settings (mixed precision, simulated memory pressure, randomized kernel selection) against a slice.
- Coherence score: composite metric combining BLEU/ROUGE-style overlap for deterministic tasks, embedding cosine stability, repetition penalty, and annotator pass-rate for safety checks.

High-level architecture

1. Profiling agents (lightweight sidecar) emit slice-extracted telemetry from shadow/prod shadowed requests.
2. Central profiler aggregates slice fingerprints and computes trend signals (weekly delta, z-score).
3. Automated triggers forward problematic slices to the stress sandbox queue.
4. Stress sandbox runs parametrized experiments and produces a reproducible report with artifacts (model config, quant artifacts, random seeds, output samples, metric deltas).

Ownership and SLAs

- Owner: Applied ML - Evaluation Engineering (primary), Runtime (secondary).
- On-call: eval-oncall rotation (see runbook link in related_pages).
- Target detection latency: new regression signal surfaced within 48 hours of slice delta crossing threshold.
- Sandbox experiment turnaround: standard queue 8 hours, expedited 2 hours for P1 regressions.

Runbook: step-by-step procedure

1) Signal detection and prioritization
   1.1. Profiling aggregator flags slice S with coherence z-score <= -2.0 or embedding stability drop >= 12%.
   1.2. Pager and Slack alert created in #eval-regressions with slice diagnostic summary and link to telemetry dashboard.
   1.3. Triage owner assigns severity (P1/P2/P3) based on user impact and prevalence.

2) Reproduce in sandbox (automated)
   2.1. Create a sandbox job via CLI:
       redwood-sbx run --slice-id S --model vX.Y --quant-profile qZ --seeds 42,117 --kernels auto
   2.2. Default sandbox config (if omitted) runs 3 quant levels: FP16, INT8-dynamic, INT8-static with mixed-kernel randomized scheduler.
   2.3. The job collects: token-level perplexity, coherence_score, embedding_stability, latency distribution, kv cache hit/miss, and sample outputs.
   2.4. Sandbox stores artifacts in s3://redwood-eval-sbx/<job-id>/ and annotator tickets if human review needed.

3) Analysis and decision matrix
   3.1. If coherence_score delta > 8 points relative to baseline and embedding stability drop > 10%, mark as quant-induced regression.
   3.2. If latency tail (p99) increases > 40% but coherence unchanged -> likely kernel scheduling change; inform Runtime.
   3.3. If kv cache miss rate increased > 5% and repetition rises -> investigate attention-kernel changes and context trimming heuristics.

4) Mitigation paths
   - Automatic: route affected traffic to fallback model variant (pinned non-quantized or higher-precision profile) via Smart Routing policy for affected tenants for 24–72 hours.
   - Rollback: revert quant profile promotion in Dedicated/Private via deployment rollback playbook.
   - Fix-forward: iterate quant tuning (calibration set re-run, per-slice bias correction) and re-run sandbox experiments.

Telemetry schema and dashboarding

All profiler events use the eval-telemetry schema:
- event_type: profiling_sample
- timestamp: RFC3339
- slice_id: string
- model_version: string
- quant_profile: string
- seq_length: integer
- kv_cache_hit_rate: float (0-1)
- token_entropy: float
- coherence_score: float (0-100)
- embedding_cosine: float
- latency_ms_p50/p90/p99: integers
- replica_kernel: string

Dashboard views (must exist for every model/major slice):
- Slice longitudinal view: coherence_score, embedding_cosine, kv_cache_hit_rate, p99 latency over 90 days.
- Heatmap: slice x quant_profile coherence delta.
- Sandbox job explorer: artifact links and per-run metric deltas.

Acceptance criteria and promotion gates

Use this table (expressed in text):

| Gate | Metric | Allowed delta | Action if exceeded | Owner |
|------|--------|---------------|---------------------|-------|
| CanPromoteQuant | coherence_score (slice-level) | <= 4 points drop | Block and require sandbox re-run with recalibration | Applied ML |
| CanAutobumpKernel | p99 latency | <= 25% increase | Manual review by Runtime + perf tests | Runtime |
| CanA/BRoute | embedding stability | <= 6% drop | A/B route with 5% traffic and monitor 48h | Product |

(When a gate is failed, the promotion pipeline should annotate the model record with gate failure and link to sandbox job.)

Sandbox configuration example (YAML)

---
job_name: stress-slice-S-2026
slice_id: "S-longform-summarization-v2"
model_version: "redwood-llm-v2.1"
quant_profiles:
  - id: fp16
  - id: int8-dyn
  - id: int8-static
kernel_scheduler: randomized-mix
seeds: [42,117,2025]
metrics: [coherence_score,embedding_cosine,token_entropy,kv_cache_hit_rate,latency_p99]
annotation_required: true
output_bucket: "s3://redwood-eval-sbx/"
priority: expedited
---

Triage checklist (quick)

- [ ] Confirm slice provenance and sample reproducibility.
- [ ] Run sandbox job with accelerated seeds.
- [ ] Compare deltas to gate thresholds.
- [ ] If quant-induced, mark rollout blocked and open ticket (runtime + applied-ml).
- [ ] If kernel-induced, escalate to Runtime with kernel+perf artifacts.
- [ ] If ambiguous, add to human review queue for annotator labeling (target 48h).

Common failure modes and diagnostics

- Mode: Coherence drop only for long-tail prompts
  - Likely cause: quantization-sensitive attention heads or tokenizer edge cases.
  - Diagnostic: isolate top-k tokens with high perplexity; re-run per-head ablations in sandbox.

- Mode: Deterministic repetition increases
  - Likely cause: KV cache eviction or seed/temperature mismatch across kernels.
  - Diagnostic: compare kv_cache_hit_rate and seed consistency; verify deterministic kernel path.

- Mode: Latency regressions without quality loss
  - Likely cause: new kernel selection or scheduling policy.
  - Diagnostic: p99 heatmap broken down by kernel and sequence length.

Communication and escalation

- For P1 regressions: open incident in PagerDuty, notify Runtime lead and Applied ML manager, schedule emergency triage call within 1 hour.
- For P2: asynchronous triage in #eval-regressions, assign owner and target 48h remediation.
- Prepare a short executive summary for customer-impacting incidents including: affected slices, estimated % of traffic, action taken (route/rollback), and ETA for fix.

Appendix: sample CLI snippets and analysis utilities

- Run a quick sandbox experiment:
  redwood-sbx run --slice-id S-longform-summarization-v2 --model redwood-llm-v2.1 --quant-profile int8-dyn --seeds 42

- Fetch sandbox artifacts:
  aws s3 ls s3://redwood-eval-sbx/<job-id>/ --human

- Quick coherence delta computation (Python):
  from statistics import mean
  baseline = [ ... ] # list of baseline coherence scores
  run = [ ... ]
  delta = mean(run) - mean(baseline)
  print(f"coherence delta: {delta}")

Related pages and resources

- Probe generation and slice definition canon: /applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/slice-prioritization-and-annotation-bidding-playbook-2026
- Quant profile synthesis guide: /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024
- Runtime kernel rollout runbook: /eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/kernel-rollout-and-rollback

Revision history

- 2025-09-18: Created by Maya Patel — initial draft.
- 2026-03-11: Added telemetry schema and automated trigger thresholds.
- 2026-12-03: Formalized acceptance gates and expedited sandbox SLA; reviewers Ethan Grant, Lina Zhou.

If you have questions or want access to the sandbox, contact Applied ML Eval infra in #eval-infra or email eval-infra@redwood.ai.

title: Probe Dependency Graph and Orchestration Manifest
content:
Overview

Purpose: Define the Probe Dependency Graph (PDG) concept, data model, orchestration manifest, and operational procedures for coordinating evaluation probes across shadowing, quantization migration, and regression triage. The PDG ensures probes run in dependency-aware order, minimizes redundant work, and encodes quality/latency constraints for mixed-SLO workloads.

Scope: This doc covers the PDG schema, node/edge semantics, orchestration priority rules, example manifests, runtime integration points with the eval harness, and a step-by-step runbook for probe incidents and migrations. It applies to: evaluator teams, model-onboarding engineers, and the runtime/CI owners.

Why a PDG?
- Probes increasingly depend on the outputs of other probes (e.g., priming templates, cached KV artifacts, quant-safety classifiers). Without explicit dependency management, we see wasted compute, nondeterministic scheduling, and triage complexity during regressions.
- PDG centralizes dependency metadata so the eval engine can reuse intermediate artifacts, schedule co-located runs, and generate clear blame paths for regressions.

Key concepts

1) Node types (table)
| node_type | purpose | critical_fields | owner |
| probe | Primary evaluation probe (prompt+seed+slice) | id, slice_id, cost_estimate, expected_latency_ms | evaluator |
| transformer | Artifact producer (priming template generator, tokenizer shim) | id, image, cache_key | evaluator |
| quant-job | Quantization candidate run (per-model/per-profile) | id, profile, quant_level | applied-ml |
| kv-cache | Generated cache snapshot used by downstream probes | id, model_version, ttl_sec | infra |
| aggregator | Combines probe outputs into metrics (e.g., coherence, fidelity) | id, metric_list, window_size | applied-ml |

2) Edge semantics
- depends_on: downstream node must wait for upstream to complete successfully.
- uses_cache: downstream can reuse upstream artifacts; orchestration may skip run if cache is fresh.
- optional_if_failed: if upstream fails, downstream can run a degraded flow (e.g., fallback prompt) but must be tagged in manifest.

3) Contract rules
- Each node declares SLO tags: latency_budget_ms, budget_tokens, fidelity_min (0-1).
- Orchestrator enforces a soft-deadline; nodes that miss latency_budget_ms are flagged and the scheduler may deprioritize their dependents.
- Cost_estimate is required (USD/minor_units) to support eval budgeting and probe eviction.

PDG Manifest: YAML example\n# Example PDG manifest (annotated)
version: v1
manifest_id: pdg-example-card-promotion-2027
description: PDG for card-promotion ranking probe set with quant shadowing
nodes:
  - id: tkn-priming-v1
    type: transformer
    image: gcr.io/redwood/primers/tkn-priming:202701
    cache_key: primer/tkn-v1/sha256:abcd
    owner: evaluator
    outputs: [kv-cache:primer-tkn-v1]
  - id: probe-ranking-a
    type: probe
    slice_id: ranking-promo-A
    depends_on: [tkn-priming-v1]
    expected_latency_ms: 120
    cost_estimate: 0.003
    fidelity_min: 0.85
    owner: evaluator
    optional_if_failed: true
  - id: quant-shadow-low
    type: quant-job
    profile: int8-dynamic
    depends_on: [probe-ranking-a]
    owner: applied-ml
    expected_latency_ms: 500
    cost_estimate: 0.02
edges:
  - from: tkn-priming-v1
    to: probe-ranking-a
    relation: uses_cache
  - from: probe-ranking-a
    to: quant-shadow-low
    relation: depends_on

Integration points
- Eval Orchestrator API: POST /eval/orchestrate with manifest_id and run_policy (immediate | scheduled | canary). The orchestrator returns run_id and a plan with task-level ETA estimates.
- Cache registry: PDG nodes that declare outputs must register artifacts into the central cache service under the manifest namespace. The registry stores artifact provenance and TTL.
- Telemetry hooks: each node emits standardized spans (pdg.node.start/stop) and a final pdg.node.result with fields: status, tokens_used, wall_ms, artifact_refs (if any).

Scheduling and priority algorithm (high-level)
1. Topological sort by depends_on edges. Nodes in the same rank are prioritized by a score: score = w1*(1-fidelity_min) + w2*(cost_estimate_norm) + w3*(latency_penalty) where weights are configured per-origination (default w1=0.6,w2=0.25,w3=0.15).
2. If a node's cache_key exists and artifact is fresh (TTL not expired), skip the producer node and link the artifact ref into the plan.
3. For mixed-SLO runs (some nodes with tight latency_budget_ms, others with high-fidelity), the scheduler builds two passes: a fast-pass (best-effort low-latency nodes) and a quality-pass (full fidelity).
4. Canary policy: when running quant-shadow jobs, orchestrator schedules canary runs limited to 1% of traffic-mapped probes and pins a regression-watch window. Canary failures trigger an early abort and notify the regression triage channel.

Operational runbook

Trigger conditions:
- PDG orchestrator reports node failures > 5% in 10-minute window for any manifest
- Canary quant-shadow failure (quality drop > fidelity_min - 0.1)
- Cache registry reports corrupted artifact checksum

Immediate steps (1-5):
1) Triage lead acknowledges the alert in PagerDuty and opens a PDG incident (link to incident template).
2) Run "pdg-cli plan-status --manifest pdg-example-card-promotion-2027" to get live plan.
3) If failures are isolated to a transformer/kv-cache node, mark dependent probes as degraded: run "pdg-cli rerun --node probe-ranking-a --degraded-template=ranking-fallback-v1".
4) For quant canary failures, immediately set quant-shadow to suspend: "pdg-cli set-policy --manifest <id> --quant-shadow=paused" and notify applied-ml on Slack #applied-ml-quant.
5) Collect artifact refs and attach to the incident: use the telemetry hook to download pdg.node.result spans and attach the first-failure logs.

Post-incident analysis
- Owner: evaluator team lead.
- Deliverable within 3 business days: incident summary with root-cause hypothesis, affected slices, regressions scores, and a remediation plan (rollback, patch, or new probe).
- If root cause relates to model changes, create a regression ticket and schedule a re-run of the PDG with the previous model version pinned.

Rolling out PDG-driven workflows (checklist)
1. Create manifest and validate with 'pdg-cli validate --manifest <file>'. Validation checks: circular dependencies, required SLO tags, cost estimates, and TTLs.
2. Run locally in dry-mode: 'pdg-cli plan --manifest <file> --dry-run'. Confirm that topological order aligns with expectations.
3. Canary schedule: tag manifest with 'canary: true' and define canary_target_percent. Start with 0.5%-1% and observe fidelity metrics for 48 hours.
4. Promote to scheduled daily runs once stability metrics (fidelity variance < 0.02, failure rate < 0.5%) are met for 72 hours.
5. Archive old manifests and ensure cache eviction policies are configured to avoid stale artifacts.

SLOs and alert thresholds
- Probe success rate: 99.5% per 24h window.
- Artifact freshness (kv-cache TTL): default 6 hours, must be <= 24 hours.
- Canary fidelity regression: alert if fidelity delta >= 0.05 over baseline.
- Scheduling latency: 95th percentile plan-to-start <= 30s for immediate runs.

Ownership and escalation
- Manifest author: evaluator team (primary).
- Orchestrator service owner: runtime infra (pager: infra-oncall).
- Quant jobs: applied-ml (pager: applied-ml-oncall).
- Incident triage: evaluator lead -> applied-ml lead -> runtime infra if artifact corruption suspected.

Migration notes for model-onboarding and quantization teams
- When onboarding a quant profile, attach a PDG manifest that includes both the production probe node and corresponding quant-shadow node. This guarantees an atomic relationship between the probe and its quant candidate.
- Ensure quant-job nodes declare a backward-compatibility flag: 'fallback_to: {model_version}' so rollbacks are automated.

Metrics dashboard (recommended widgets)
- PDG run rate (daily) split by manifest owner.
- Node-level failure heatmap (by node_type and slice).
- Cache hit ratio for transformer nodes.
- Canary fidelity delta timeseries per manifest.

Examples and troubleshooting scenarios
1) Scenario: Priming transformer runs unexpectedly slow during a spike.
   - Symptoms: downstream probes show increased latency and partial timeouts.
   - Quick fix: instruct orchestrator to skip transformer with 'pdg-cli override --skip tkn-priming-v1 --manifest <id>' and attach fallback primers.
   - Longer fix: scale transformer horizontally and increase cache TTL for the high-traffic slice.

2) Scenario: Quant canary passes locally but fails under shadow load.
   - Action: pause global quant rollout, run targeted long-tail probes from the PDG (use 'pdg-cli replay --manifest <id> --slice longtail-99') and collect per-slice fidelity.

Appendix A — PDG CLI quick reference
- pdg-cli validate --manifest <file>
- pdg-cli plan --manifest <file> [--dry-run]
- pdg-cli orchestrate --manifest <file> --policy {immediate|scheduled|canary}
- pdg-cli rerun --node <id> --manifest <id> [--degraded-template <id>]
- pdg-cli set-policy --manifest <id> --quant-shadow {running|paused}

Appendix B — Backwards compatibility and provenance
- All artifacts registered by PDG nodes must contain an immutable provenance blob: producer_image, manifest_id, commit_sha, and timestamp. This enables deterministic replay for regression triage.

Related pages and artifacts
- See the PDG schema repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/pdg-schema (link internal).
- Integration tests: CI job 'eval/pdg-integration' must pass before manifest promotion.

Contact
- Doc owner: Aisha Kumar (aisha@redwood.com)
- Evaluator contact: Marco Li (marco@redwood.com)
- Applied-ML contact: Sofia Ramirez (sofia@redwood.com)

Acknowledgements
Thanks to the evaluator platform, runtime, and applied-ml teams for prototyping the PDG proofs-of-concept and providing early feedback.

title: Synthetic Mosaic Eval Cookbook: Priming + Canonicalization + Quant-Fallback
content:
Overview

This document describes the "Synthetic Mosaic" evaluation pattern: a composable approach that combines localized priming, canonicalization, and quant-fallback probes to produce robust, cost-aware onboarding signals for edge and mixed-precision LLM services (multilingual, function-call capable). The goal is to detect quality regressions and quantization sensitivity across low-frequency slices while keeping eval cost bounded.

Who this is for
- ML engineers running model onboarding and quant migration for production services.
- Evaluation owners responsible for probe portfolios and telemetry contracts.
- SREs operating mixed-precision fleets and canary rollouts.

Why we need a Mosaic pattern
- Rare-intent and multilingual slices often fail silent quality checks because synthetic probes don’t capture priming/context artifacts.
- Quantization and KV-cache interactions cause subtle coherence regressions only visible under particular priming and canonicalized inputs.
- Running exhaustive full-fidelity evals is cost-prohibitive; we need a low-cost hedging strategy that surfaces high-risk slices for deeper inspection.

Key concepts and definitions
- Mosaic probe: a small, intentional bundle of related probes for a target slice combining (a) primed variants (localized priming), (b) canonicalized transformations (standardized inputs), and (c) quant-fallback comparisons (float baseline vs quantized variant).
- Localized priming: repeatable short-context priming patterns representative of real user prompts (e.g., product-specific examples, local date/time formats, code snippets).
- Canonicalization: deterministic normalization applied to inputs (token-level normalization, whitespace/casing rules, function-call structure canonicalization) to reduce noise and isolate model changes.
- Quant-fallback probe: paired evaluation where the same probe is executed against a float baseline and the intended quantized runtime to measure fidelity delta and emergent failure modes.

Scope and applicability
- Target services: any text-generation or function-call endpoint that will run mixed-precision or quantized models. Works for multilingual and few-shot scenarios.
- Not intended for: high-frequency ad-hoc prompts (use live telemetry probes instead) or purely embedding-only services.

Design components
1) Probe family composition
   - For each service slice, synthesize 6–12 mosaic probes grouped into three cohorts: Primed (4), Canonical (4), Edge-variants (2).
   - Primed cohort: same prompt stem with 3 distinct priming templates (e.g., product example, short narrative, structured list).
   - Canonical cohort: normalized transformations (strip extraneous punctuation, standardize dates to YYYY-MM-DD, canonicalize function-call JSON ordering).
   - Edge-variants: long-context and truncated-context variants to stress KV-cache behavior.

2) Lightweight fidelity scoring (cost-aware)
   - Use a two-stage scoring pipeline: (A) cheap lexical/semantic heuristics (BLEU-lite, token overlap, function-call schema match) and (B) selective human or heavy automated eval for flagged probes.
   - Flagging thresholds are configured in the rollout table below.

3) Quant-fallback delta measurement
   - Execute mosaic probes against float-baseline (f32 or established gold) and quant-target (q4/nn) and calculate: token-level edit distance, function-call schema delta, hallucination indicator score, and perplexity ratio.

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step)
1. Identify service slices for coverage: list top-50 rare-intent slices by traffic fraction <= 0.5% but high business impact.
2. For each slice, synthesize a mosaic probe family (6–12 probes) following the composition rules. Document priming templates.
3. Run baseline executions against the established float-certified model and record reference outputs.
4. Run quant-target executions (same seed/temperature) and collect diffs.
5. Compute cheap heuristics and apply the flagging policy.
6. For flagged probes, schedule a micro-human review or heavy automated eval (semantic embedding similarity + annotator pass).
7. Produce a per-slice decision: promote, require model tweak, adjust quant profile, or block rollout.

Rollout policy and stages
- Shadow (0%): execute mosaic probes in shadow to collect telemetry for 48h. No traffic routing.
- Micro-canary (1–2%): route a tiny traffic shard; enforce synchronous quant-fallback probe runs and fast alerting.
- Canary (10%): require zero flagged probes for 24h before ramp beyond 10%.
- Ramp (25–100%): continuous monitoring with weekly re-eval of mosaic probes.

Config table: flagging thresholds and recommended actions

| Metric | Warning threshold | Action (automated) | Action (human) |
|--------|-------------------:|--------------------|----------------|
| Token edit ratio (quant vs float) | > 0.12 | mark probe flagged | detailed human review |
| Function-call schema mismatch rate | > 2 mismatches / 10 probes | block function-call rollout | annotate and escalate to model-owner |
| Hallucination indicator (heuristic) | > 0.15 | alert on slice | pair with semantic eval |
| Latency delta (quant vs float) | > 20% increase | flag perf regression | SRE triage |
| Cost delta (tokens/response) | > 30% increase | evaluate batching/priming tweak | cost-owner review |

- Notes: thresholds are intentionally conservative for canary stages and can be relaxed for low-risk slices.

Commands & eval harness snippets
- Example invocation (local evaluator CLI):

  ./evalctl run --suite mosaic --slice-id auth-email-rare --model baseline-f32 --model-compare q4a --seeds 42 --out results/auth-email-mosaic.json

- Minimal YAML config (mosaic probe family):

  suite: mosaic
  slice_id: auth-email-rare
  probes: 8
  priming_templates:
    - "You are a helpful assistant. Example: {product} handles ..."
    - "Short explain: {question}"
  canonicalization:
    date_format: YYYY-MM-DD
    strip_whitespace: true
  quant_targets: [q4a, q8_0]

Monitoring and alerts (metric -> alert rule)
- alert: mosaic_flag_high
  condition: flagged_probes(slice) >= 2 within 1h
  severity: P2
  runbook: follow Troubleshooting section, escalate to model-owner and SRE if function-call mismatch present.

- alert: quant_fidelity_regression
  condition: aggregate_token_edit_ratio > 0.10 over 1k probes
  severity: P1
  runbook: immediate rollback candidate and postmortem.

Troubleshooting and typical failure modes
1) Many canonical probes flagged but primed probes OK
   - Likely: canonicalization rules overly aggressive; re-check tokenization boundary handling. Re-run with less aggressive normalization.
2) Primed probes fail but canonical pass
   - Likely: priming artifacts interact with decoding policy. Test with temperature=0 and deterministic seeds. Consider priming rewrite to shorter anchors.
3) Function-call semantics diverge after quantization
   - Run schema-preserving canonicalization (stable key ordering) and increase float baseline sample size. If mismatch persists, block rollout for function-call routes.
4) High latency delta with quant target
   - Confirm execution backend uses optimized kernels; check kernel selection logs and hardware affinity. If hardware mismatch, route to dedicated capacity.

Operational responsibilities
- Probe synthesis and maintenance: Applied ML (probe-stewards) — primary: Priya Nair.
- Eval executions and scoring pipeline: Eval infra team — primary: Lucas Kim.
- Rollout decisions and business impact signoff: Service owners and product manager.
- SRE on-call for perf regressions: Eng SRE rotation.

Acceptance criteria for promotion
- Zero P1-flagged probes in Canary for 24h.
- Aggregate token edit ratio across mosaic suite < 0.08.
- Function-call schema match >= 99% on the mosaic probes.

Appendix: Example probe templates
- Primed example (support ticket): "Customer: I received a duplicate invoice dated 2025-12-11 for order #12345. Please summarize and next steps."
- Canonical example: "Invoice inquiry | ORDER_ID: 12345 | DATE: 2025-12-11"
- Edge (long context): 3x concatenated previous messages to replicate long-session context.

Related pages and references
- See the Eval Mesh fingerprinting guide for workload selection heuristics.
- See Model Promotion Playbook for cross-team signoff requirements.

Review cadence
- Probe portfolio review quarterly and after any major quant profile change.
- Emergency re-eval whenever a production regression is detected.

Contact
- Document owner: Maya Chen (applied-ml).
- For runbook escalations: ping #eval-oncall and #sre-performance.

Change log
- 2026-02-15: Created initial cookbook.
- 2026-03-01: Added rollout thresholds and YAML snippets.

title: Test Amplification and Latent Failure Detection
content:
Summary:
This document describes our standard for generating amplified test collections from a small set of real failures (latent or observed) to uncover related regressions and emergent failure modes across model variants, quantization profiles, and serving configurations. It bridges the eval-harness, prompt set curation, model onboarding and regression triage processes by describing a repeatable pipeline, danger taxonomy, recommended mutation strategies, and concrete CI / runtime checks to catch latent failures earlier in the lifecycle.

Why we need test amplification:
- Hand-labeled or in-field failures are often sparse. Small seeds may hide families of correlated failures that only appear under slightly different prompts, context truncation, or KV-cache conditions.
- Amplification reduces expensive human annotation by generating prioritized synthetic variants that trigger edge behaviors.
- It helps map failure surfaces across deployment axes: model family, sequence length, batch size, quantization format (int8/4/FP16), and routing fallbacks.

Intended audience:
- Applied ML engineers owning eval harness integration and model onboarding
- Runtime engineers validating quantization/latency trade-offs
- SRE and QA teams running pre-release gating suites
- Solutions engineers investigating customer-exposed regressions

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- A documented amplification pipeline that converts a seed corpus (N >= 5 failing examples) into a prioritized test bundle of 200–2,000 variants within 24h.
- Amplified tests must include metadata: mutation type, expected failure signal (classification/semantic divergence/unsafe output), trigger conditions (seq_len, kv_cache_percent), and reproducibility flags.
- CI gates must detect statistically significant degradation at pre-defined thresholds (see SLOs table).

SLOs and alert thresholds (recommended):
- Latent Failure Coverage: amplification should increase unique failure triggers by >= 3x relative to seed set in a single run (target: 3x–10x).
- Regression detection sensitivity: if model A → model B causes a mean response-stability-index (RSI) drop > 5% on amplified bundle, block promotion and raise P1 review.
- Quantization amplification check: any amplified test that flips a safety classifier label (safe → unsafe) or changes top-1 intent should be flagged as a critical regression.

Failure taxonomy (for labeling amplified tests):
1) Semantic drift — generated variant changes desirable intent despite surface similarity.
2) Safety flip — content becomes policy-violating after transformation or quantization.
3) Hallucination spike — previously factual response is now fabricated or inconsistent.
4) Truncation sensitivity — longer or shorter context changes answer in unacceptable ways.
5) Cache-dependent nondeterminism — responses diverge when KV cache reuse is simulated.
6) Tokenization edgecases — whitespace/punctuation/emoji changes tokenization and triggers an error or change in behavior.

Amplification strategies (ordered by priority):
1. Orthographic and punctuation perturbations
   - Add/remove punctuation, swap hyphens vs em-dash, normalize unicode.
   - Example: "state-of-the-art" → "state of the art", add zero-width space.
2. Context slicing and prefix variation
   - Prepend neutral sentences, repeat tokens, truncate at common tokenization boundaries to simulate windowing.
3. Shot/anchor perturbations
   - Insert or remove few-shot examples, scramble example order, or substitute placeholders with semantically-similar distractors.
4. Numeric and unit transformations
   - Convert units, change date formats, replace numbers with words, shift magnitude (e.g., 1,000 → 1000).
5. Adversarial paraphrasing (semantic-preserving)
   - Use templated paraphrasers with controlled diversity (e.g., back-translation only when quality score > 0.85).
6. KV-cache and incremental decoding simulation
   - Re-run prompt with parts of previously generated tokens pre-filled into cache to surface cache-boundary bugs.
7. Mixed-mode quantization toggles
   - Simulate int8/int4 artifacts on candidate models using fast emulator or sliced inference harness to reveal quantization-specific failures.

Automated pipeline (high level):
1) Seed selection: accept seed failures from bug tracker, field telemetry, or offline evals. Seeds must include failing_response, expected_response, trace_id, and context snapshot.
2) Mutation generation: apply amplification strategies producing labeled variants and collect provenance.
3) Filtering & scoring: run lightweight filters (toxicity, token-length bounds, trivial duplicates). Score variants according to novelty (embedding distance from seed), syntactic variance, and model sensitivity (probe with a fast model).
4) Prioritization: select top-K for full-run depending on test budget and desired coverage.
5) Full-run evaluation: execute amplified bundle across target matrix (model versions, quant profiles, serving configs). Capture metrics: RSI, safety_class, topk_intent_changes, latency, token_count.
6) Triage and triage metadata: generate triage deck with failing examples grouped by failure taxonomy and suggested root causes (quantization, prompt-windowing, prompt-template mismatch).

Runbook: Amplify-to-Triage — step-by-step
1. Create a ticket in the regression board with seed examples and desired target matrix.
2. Run amplification CLI: redwood-eval amplify --seed-file seeds.json --budget 1000 --strategies "orthographic,paraphrase,cache" --out amplified.ndjson
   - Example: redwood-eval amplify --seed-file /var/lib/seeds/field-failures.json --budget 500 --out /tmp/amplified.ndjson
3. Validate amplified.ndjson: use the provided validator to check metadata and duplicate ratio: redwood-eval validate /tmp/amplified.ndjson
4. Submit amplified bundle to CI gate: redwood-ci run-amplified --bundle /tmp/amplified.ndjson --matrix "stable-v2,stable-v3|int8|kv100,kv10"
5. If CI flags regressions: open a regression triage session, attach the generated triage deck, and assign owners.
6. For high-severity safety flips: immediately block promotion and notify Security/Policy via the escalation channel.

Amplified bundle format (required fields) — example ndjson line (single-line JSON per test):
{
  "id": "amp-20260112-0001",
  "seed_id": "seed-42",
  "mutation": "orthographic:dash-normalized",
  "mutation_description": "dash replaced with spaces",
  "expected_signal": "semantic-divergence",
  "notes": "from field-incident #1234",
  "provenance": "amplify:v1"
}
(Our validator requires each amplified item to include at least id, seed_id, mutation, and provenance.)

Filtering heuristics and budgets:
- De-duplication threshold: normalized-levenshtein < 0.15 => drop.
- Toxicity filter: use safety-model v3 to pre-filter expected unsafe variants unless the seed is unsafe.
- Budget allocation: 50% orthographic/context, 25% paraphrase, 25% cache/quant tests by default. Adjust per workload.

Integration points with existing systems:
- Eval harness: amplified bundles are a first-class artifact. Use the eval-harness runner with --amplified flag and provide matrix yaml.
- Model onboarding: require amplified-bundle smoke tests before promotion to staging. Add an entry to the model promotion checklist: "amplified test run (K=500) with zero critical safety flips".
- Quality guardrails: wire amplified failure counts into the response-stability-index dashboard and create an alert when growth rate > 2x/week.
- Quantization profiles: add a per-profile amplification pass to detect quant-specific failure modes and store fingerprints in the quant profile registry.

Example evaluation matrix YAML (text table):
- models: [stable-v2, stable-v3, experimental-quantized-v1]
- quant_profiles: [fp16, int8_fast, hybrid4]
- kv_cache_percent: [0, 10, 100]
- seq_lengths: [64, 512, 2048]

Triage decision rubric (quick):
1) Critical safety flip or P0 customer-impacting behavior → immediate rollback/hold and cross-team incident.
2) High semantic regressions on high-frequency seed slices → revert or prioritize hotfix.
3) Low-frequency hallucination increase < 10% → schedule a targeted eval and shadow rollout.
4) Quant-only diff: treat as quant regression; either tune quant profile or mark as acceptable with documentation.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Applied ML (eval-harness) team: maintain amplification tool, mutation library, and validator.
- Runtime/Quant team: supply fast emulators for quanted inference and validate model-specific failure fingerprints.
- SRE/QA: operate CI gates and define budget for full-run amplification checks.
- Product / Solutions: prioritize seed list and annotate customer-critical seeds.

Operational knobs and configuration examples:
- amplification.config (YAML text example):
  strategies: [orthographic,paraphrase,cache,quant_toggle]
  budget: 800
  dedup_threshold: 0.15
  prioritize_by: [novelty,seed_frequency]
  safety_filter: true

Common pitfalls and mitigations:
- Over-amplification (noise): enforce novelty scoring and cap mutations per seed to 50.
- Synthetic variants that are invalid downstream: validate for required context signatures before including in full run.
- Amplification bias: monitor distribution across language, tokenization patterns, and user geographies to avoid skew.

Metrics to collect (telemetry suggestions):
- Amplified-to-failure ratio (unique failing variants / total amplified)
- Time-to-triage (amplified bundle processed to triage ticket creation)
- Regression false positive rate (CI flag that is not reproducible in field)
- Per-model quant flip rate (safety or intent flips attributable to quant profile)

Appendix: useful commands and quick snippets
- Generate an amplified bundle: redwood-eval amplify --seed-file seeds.json --budget 500 --strategies all --out amplified.ndjson
- Validate bundle: redwood-eval validate amplified.ndjson --schema amplify-v1
- Run in CI: redwood-ci run-amplified --bundle amplified.ndjson --matrix matrix.yaml --notify-on-fail # triggers triage job

References and related reading:
- See eval-harness smoke-and-fidelity-eval-workflow for CI integration notes.
- For regression bisect automation, see automated-regression-bisect-and-blame-assistant.

Glossary:
- Amplification: automated generation of synthetic test variants from seed failures.
- RSI (response-stability-index): internal metric that aggregates semantic and token-level divergence across runs.
- Quant flip: a change in a model response category attributable to quantization (FP16 → int8, etc.).

Contact and escalation
- Primary owner: Maya Chen (applied-ml) — maya@redwood.ai
- Escalation channel: #amplified-regressions (PagerDuty on-call forwarded for critical safety flips)

Change log:
- 2025-11-08: created initial draft.
- 2025-12-10: added quant-toggle strategy and example ndjson format.
- 2026-01-12: updated SLOs and added triage rubric after pilot runs.

title: Shadow Orchestrator for Cross-Modal Stress Testing and Shadow Drift Detection
content:
Overview
========
This playbook describes the Shadow Orchestrator: an orchestrated, repeatable pipeline for running cross-modal (text + image + long-context) shadow tests against production traffic to detect regressions, quantization sensitivity, and early drift. The goal is to exercise the full serving stack and evaluation harness without impacting live responses.

Why this exists
---------------
- Catch subtle cross-modal regressions that only appear under production request composition (multimodal prompts, long context + tool calls).
- Measure behavior differences introduced by model promotions, quantization profiles, or runtime kernel changes.
- Provide a fast, audit-friendly path for risk-aware promotion decisions.

Scope
-----
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments where shadowing of selective traffic is supported.
- Supports: text-only, text+image, and long-context (>4k tokens) shadow runs.
- Not intended for full load performance benchmarking (use dedicated perf suite).

Key components
--------------
1) Orchestrator controller: schedules shadow runs, enforces traffic fraction, and records run metadata.
2) Probe generator: synthesizes cross-modal probes from prompt catalog and production anchors.
3) Shadow sequencer: replays requests into shadow model variants while preserving KV cache warmup policy.
4) Telemetry collector: aggregates semantic metrics, token deltas, latency/throughput, and KV-cache hit rates.
5) Comparator & alerting: computes divergence metrics and raises triage alerts when thresholds are exceeded.

Run definitions and config (example)
----------------------------------
- run_type: cross_modal_shadow
- traffic_fraction: 0.5%  # percent of qualifying requests to fork to shadow path
- probe_mix: [ real-anchors: 70%, synthetic-probes: 30% ]
- variants: [baseline: "v3.1-quant32", candidate: "v3.2-q4f", fallback: "v3.1-quant32"]
- kv_cache_policy: warmup=2 requests, preserve_prefix=true
- telemetry: semantic_similarity=cosine-sbert, token_perturb=edit-distance-tokenized

YAML example for orchestrator (use with CLI)
--------------------------------------------
run_id: crossmodal-2026-02-20-01
selector:
  sources: ["web-api", "mobile-sdk"]
  modalities: ["text", "image", "long-context"]
  min_tokens: 20
  max_tokens: 8192
probes:
  anchor_sampling: {window_hours: 72, sample_rate: 0.001}
  synthetic_rules: ["image-caption-variants", "noisy-instruction-perturbs"]
variants:
  baseline: "models/redwood-v3.1-quant32"
  candidate: "models/redwood-v3.2-q4f"
  fallback: "models/redwood-v3.1-quant32"
schedule:
  parallelism: 8
  batch_size: 16
  max_runtime_minutes: 180
