  - List past runs: redwood-eval list --pipeline aef --model <sha>
  - Fetch artifacts: redwood-eval fetch --run-id <id> --dest ./artifacts
- JSON example of a slice flag record:
```json
{"slice_name":"billing-intent","anomaly_score":0.82,"flag_reason":"accuracy_delta:-0.07","run_id":"aef-20260301-strat-42"}
```

Related policies and pages:
- See prompt-coverage matrix and drift repair guide for how to define slices and minimum coverage targets.
- See regression triage canonical runbook for incident escalation templates.

Revision history:
- 2026-02-18: initial published by Ava Chen.
- 2026-03-01: clarified heavy-simulation gating and added cost knobs by request of reviewers.

Contact:
- Playbook owner: Ava Chen (ava.chen@redwood.ai)
- Platform on-call: applied-ml-platform@redwood.com

title: Shadow Sequencer and Fallback Orchestration Playbook
content:
Summary
-----
This playbook documents the Shadow Sequencer pattern and fallback orchestration used by the eval harness to safely validate new model variants (including quantized and trimmed kernels) across live workloads. It prescribes sequencing rules, sampling policies, telemetry contracts, and incident-runbook steps to keep production SLOs intact while maximizing signal for model onboarding and regression triage.

Audience
--------
- Applied ML engineers running model onboarding and continuous evals
- Serving runtime engineers integrating shadow pipelines
- SRE and platform teams responsible for routing and fallbacks

Goals
-----
1. Collect high-fidelity shadowed request/response pairs for evaluation without impacting user-perceived latency or correctness.
2. Provide deterministic sequencing and prioritization so limited eval capacity focuses on the most informative traffic slices.
3. Automate safe fallback to production variants on degradation (quality or latency).
4. Integrate with quantization and KV-cache-aware on-device evaluation flows.

Terminology
-----------
- Shadow request: a copy of a production request routed to an eval model for offline scoring and telemetry.
- Sequencer: the service that decides which production requests to shadow and at what priority. (service: eval-sequencer)
- Shadow bus: asynchronous pipeline that delivers shadow traffic to eval environments with metadata. (service: shadow-bus)
- Fallback policy: policy that triggers automatic rollback or traffic diversion when a health gate fails.

Architecture overview
---------------------
1. Production ingress -> routing layer (redwood-router).
2. redwood-router emits a sampling key and forwards the request to production model variant.
3. eval-sequencer subscribes to routing metadata and decides shadow eligibility using the Sequencing Policy DB (see configs).
4. Eligible requests are serialized and posted to shadow-bus (Kafka topic: shadows.v1) with encryption and a metadata envelope.
5. Shadow consumers (dedicated eval-pools, private shadow runners) pull and run model variants; results written to eval-store and linked back to the originating request id for later comparison.

Sequencing policy (high level)
-----------------------------
- Priority classes (in descending order):
  - P0: production slow-paths and SLA-critical endpoints (sample rate: 0.1% default)
  - P1: high-business-value cohorts (paid customers, sample rate: 1%)
  - P2: high-entropy prompts (identified by probe classifier, sample rate: 5%)
  - P3: heavy compute or long-context examples (sample rate: 0.5%)
- Global budget: max 3% of total QPS can be shadowed into any single eval-cluster to avoid resource interference.
- Adaptive throttle: sample rates are dynamically lowered if the eval-cluster CPU/GPU utilization > 75% for 5m window.

Sequencing config table (editable YAML snippet)
------------------------------------------------
| key | meaning | recommended value |
|-----|---------|-------------------|
| sequencer.default_rate | baseline sampling | 0.01 |
| sequencer.priority_p1_rate | paid customers | 0.01 |
| sequencer.max_cluster_shadow_pct | cap per cluster | 0.03 |
| sequencer.cpu_util_throttle_pct | throttling threshold | 0.75 |

(Example YAML for a sequence rule)
```yaml
- id: p1_paid_customers
  match: request.customer_tier == \"paid\"
  sample_rate: 0.01
  priority: P1
  destinations: [\"eval-dedicated-a\", \"eval-private-vpc\"]
```

Security and privacy controls
-----------------------------
- All shadow payloads are hashed at ingress and PII fields redacted according to the redaction ruleset (service: pii-filter).
- Shadow bus messages are encrypted with customer-scoped keys; private deployment shadows can be configured to never persist in central eval-store.
- For regulated customers, use DP-mode: add Laplace noise to numeric telemetry and strip verbatim user content before storage.

Telemetry and SLOs
------------------
- Critical SLOs that must not be violated by shadowing:
  - P99 production latency change: <= +1.5ms attributable to shadowing hooks.
  - Error budget: shadow subsystem must not cause >0.1% increase in 5xx rate.
- Observability outputs:
  - metric: eval.shadowed_requests_count (tags: priority, destination, model_variant)
  - metric: eval.shadow_processing_lag_seconds (95th)
  - log: shadow-envelope-{request_id} includes: request_id, sampling_key, model_variant, seq_rule, cluster_id

Quality gates and automated fallback triggers
-------------------------------------------
We evaluate shadow-run results weekly and in near real-time for the following gates. Any failure above thresholds triggers one of the fallback actions below.

Quality gates (examples)
- Token-level degradation: LM_delta_bleu > 0.12 vs baseline for customer-critical prompts
- Latency regressions: 95th percentile increase > 15% for the model variant under test
- Regression alerts per 10k shadowed requests > 3

Fallback actions (ranked)
1. Circuit-breaker: stop all new shadowing for the failing variant for 30 minutes.
2. Auto-rollforward: if degradation persists and a compatible fallback exists (quantized->float or small->large), route canary traffic to fallback variant with gradual ramping.
3. Live rollback: for Dedicated or Private deployments with observed customer impact, automatically switch traffic away from the failing variant at the routing layer and create incident.

Operational runbook (incident scenario: spike in token degradation)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Triage: PagerDuty -> oncall-eng (eval). Confirm spike via grafana: eval.quality.regression_rate (5m).
2. Identify sequencer keys correlated with regressions via:
   - CLI: rcli seq-query --from 2026-03-02T09:00Z --to 2026-03-02T09:30Z --filter=regression=1
3. Stop shadowing for the implicated variant:
   - curl -XPOST https://eval-sequencer/api/v1/rules/disable -d '{"rule_id":"<id>"}'
4. If spike persists > 30m, enable fallback route to previous stable variant:
   - rcli routes update --route-id prod-chat --fallback-variant redwood-gpt-3b-stable --weight 100
5. Postmortem: capture root-cause, model diff, and submit to regression-triage workspace.

Integration checklist for model onboarding
----------------------------------------
- Ensure the model is registered in model-catalog with the following metadata: variant_id, quant_profile, kv_cache_compatibility, expected_latency_ms.
- Attach an eval-suite that includes: production prompt slices, adversarial probes, and a small human-labeled gold set for P1 customers.
- Verify shadow-run: run 1k synthetic shadow requests using the shadow-runner utility:
  - shadow-runner --variant <id> --sample-size 1000 --emulate-headers
- Confirm telemetry: eval.shadowed_requests_count > 1000 and eval.quality.sentinal_pass == true

Operational tips (best practices)
--------------------------------
- Prefer deterministic hashing for stable slice selection to enable reproducible comparisons.
- Use higher sampling for rare high-value slices (e.g., B2B integrations) and lower sampling for generic low-value traffic.
- For quantized variants, annotate messages with quant_profile to enable downstream analysts to compare like-for-like.

Example CLI snippets
--------------------
- Create a new sequencing rule:
  rcli sequencer create --name p2_high_entropy --match-file p2_match.json --sample-rate 0.05 --destinations eval-dedicated-a
- Disable shadowing for a variant immediately:
  rcli shadow disable --variant-id ql-6b-quant-v2

----------------------

- Runtime integration: Jin Park (serving-runtime)
- SRE contact: Aisha Khan
- Oncall escalation: eval-oncall@redwood.com

Related pages

    \"model_variant\": \"redwood-gpt-3b-quant-v2\",

title: Latency Sensitivity Eval Protocol for Routing and Fallback Policies
content:
Summary:
This document describes the evaluation protocol used to measure and qualify model variants and serving configurations for latency-sensitive workloads. The goal is to produce an operational signal that directly informs traffic routing and automatic fallback policies in Redwood's smart routing layer. It covers metric definitions, workload synthesis, test harness configuration, pass/fail thresholds, and an incident triage runbook for latency regressions.

Background and motivation:
- Many customer-facing features require a sub-100ms median response time or predictable tail latency to maintain UX.
- Model choices (size, quantization), runtime kernel selection, KV-cache hit patterns, and batching behavior all interact to create latency regressions that are invisible to token-count-only evaluations.
- Automated routing and fallback should be driven by a reproducible eval signal that closely mimics production request characteristics.

Scope:
- Applies to: model variants intended for low-latency endpoints (chat-completion, single-turn generation with short context), runtime tunables that affect single-request latency (batching, prefetch, kernel/path selection), and routing/fallback policy parameters.
- Excludes: large-batch throughput-only benchmarks, long-context (> 8k) full-document generation stress tests (covered by separate bench).

Key definitions and metrics:
1) Per-request P95 latency: end-to-end time from API ingress to first-byte-of-response (ms).
2) Cold-start latency: latency when no warm worker has the model loaded or KV cache is empty (ms).
3) Steady-state latency: median and P95 after warmup period (ms).
4) Amplification factor (AF): ratio of P95 under production-mixed traffic to P95 under synthetic single-client baseline. Used to quantify sensitivity to interleaving workloads.
5) SLO delta: change in SLO attainment compared to baseline model/config (percentage points).

Minimum SLOs used by this protocol:
- Target median (50th): <= 80ms for short-chat endpoints (configurable per product).
- Target P95: <= 180ms.
- Acceptable cold-start: <= 400ms.
- AF threshold for auto-rollback: > 1.5 triggers investigation; > 2.0 blocks rollout.

Test corpus and traffic profiles:
- Primary prompt set: 1k anonymized short-turn prompts sampled from production (max tokens: 64). Prompts are stratified by client product, region, and token distribution.
- Adversarial prompt subset: 200 prompts with long-token prefixes, syntactic noise, and content that stresses decoding loops.
- Synthetic client mix: a multi-client interleaving generator with 50 concurrent virtual clients, configurable think-time distribution (exponential mean = 200ms).
- Background noise profile: 10% of requests are long-context (> 2048 tokens) to simulate multi-tenant interference.

Harness configuration (example YAML):
---
harness: latency-sensitivity-v1
clients: 50
think_time_ms_mean: 200
prompt_set: s3://redwood-evals/latency/short-chat-1k-v2.json
model_variant: rwinf-7b-q8
batch_policy: continuous
kv_cache_mode: enabled
warmup_requests: 500
measurement_window_sec: 600
collect: [p50, p90, p95, p99, mean, throughput, cpu, gpu_util, memory]
---

Execution steps (numbered procedure):
1. Provision test cluster matching the target deployment class (hosted/dedicated/private). Use the infra profile documented in /confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/test-cluster-profiles.
2. Pre-load models and warm KV caches using warmup_requests. Confirm worker processes are up and the model is resident in GPU memory.
3. Start the synthetic client generator with the primary prompt set and background noise profile.
4. Run for measurement_window_sec (recommended 10 minutes for small variants, up to 30 minutes for larger configs).
5. Aggregate metrics and compute AF relative to baseline. Baseline is the currently promoted model+config for the route.
6. If metrics cross thresholds defined under 'Pass/fail criteria', mark the run as failed and trigger the triage workflow.

Pass/fail criteria and gating rules:
- Hard fail: P95 > 200ms OR AF > 2.0 OR cold-start > 600ms.
- Soft fail (requires engineering review): P95 between 180-200ms OR AF between 1.5-2.0 OR median degradation > 10%.
- Canary gating: For canary rollouts, combine this harness signal with production real-user telemetry for 1 hour before advancing traffic if any soft-fail metrics present.

How latency signals map to routing and fallback policies:
- If hard fail: route traffic away from the model variant immediately (automatic rollback) and mark variant unhealthy in the routing registry.
- If soft fail: reduce traffic to variant by 50% and add a retry fallback (fast-path to baseline variant) for requests with strict latency budget.
- If AF indicates susceptibility to multi-tenant interference: set conservative batching knobs and enable per-customer QoS isolation in Dedicated deployments.

Quantization and kernel interaction notes:
- Always run the harness for both float and quantized builds. Quantization may improve median latency but can worsen P95 due to kernel path mismatches.
- Record kernel selection logs (kernel_id, torch/llvm path) and include in eval artifact. Use the profiling-playbook to map slow paths back to kernel candidates.

Artifact and reporting requirements:
- Each run must produce a single artifact tarball with: harness-config.yaml, raw-metrics.jsonl, aggregated-summary.csv, kernel-selection.log, and reproducer-script.sh. Upload to s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/latency/<run-id>/.
- Create a Confluence run summary page using the template in /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/run-summary-template. Required fields: run-id, cluster-profile, model-variant, pass/fail, owner, link to artifacts.

Incident triage runbook (when a promoted variant shows a latency regression in prod):
1. Immediate mitigation (first 5 minutes): increase routing weight to baseline model; if autos-rollback is enabled, the router will reduce traffic automatically. Notify on-call via Slack channel #prod-latency.
2. Collect traces: enable request tracing for affected route and collect first-byte timing, kernel selection trace, and KV-cache hit logs for a 5-minute window.
3. Re-run harness with identical cluster profile and collect AF. If AF reproduces: escalate to serving-runtime oncall.
4. If AF does not reproduce: capture production request samples (privacy-preserving sampling; redact PII) and run through the harness with identical concurrency/think-time distribution.
5. Postmortem: owner creates a postmortem page including root cause hypothesis, timeline, and remediation (config change, kernel patch, model rollback). Link to regression triage playbook and schedule a follow-up regression test after remediation is applied.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Eval owner: Applied ML Evaluations team (primary contact: Elena Gupta).
- Serving runtime owner: eng-serving-runtime (contacts: Marcus Lee).
- Platform & routing owner: eng-platform (contacts: Tara O'Connell).
- On-call: per the oncall rota in /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/oncall-rotations.

Checklist before promoting a model/config (pre-promotion verification):
- [ ] Pass latency harness under target cluster profile
- [ ] Quantized and float builds evaluated and artifacts uploaded
- [ ] Canary: run 50% traffic for 1 hour with live telemetry and no hard-fail events
- [ ] Kernel-selection review for uncommon slow-paths
- [ ] Owner sign-off and release notes recorded

Appendix: example CLI commands
- Run harness locally (short smoke test):
  ./eval-harness run --config harness-config.yaml --dry-run=false --warmup 100 --window 60

- Upload artifacts:
  aws s3 cp artifacts/<run-id>.tar.gz s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/latency/<run-id>/ --acl private

- Query aggregated metrics (jq):
  cat aggregated-summary.csv | jq -R -s -c 'split("\n") | .[1:-1] | map(split(","))'

References and related pages:
- /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook
- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026
- /confluence/eng-platform/rollouts/canary-deployment-guidelines

Revision history:
- 2025-11-15: created initial draft (Elena Gupta)
- 2025-12-10: added AF metric and gating rules after review
- 2026-02-03: tightened P95 thresholds for short-chat endpoints and clarified artifact requirements

title: Quantized Replay Orchestrator: Spec and Runbook
content:
Summary:
This document specifies the Quantized Replay Orchestrator (QRO): an eval-harness component used to replay production or synthetic traffic against quantized model variants in a controlled, auditable manner. The QRO is intended for: pre-promotion safety checks, longtail stability checks for quantized kernels, and regression triage when inference drift is suspected after quantization or runtime changes.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Provide deterministic replay behavior for token-level and example-level traces.
  - Measure delta metrics (quality, latency, token cost) between float baseline and quantized variants.
  - Surface regressions that are functionally actionable (prompt-level failure modes and statistically significant output shifts).
- Non-goals:
  - This is not a replacement for live A/B canaries; QRO is a controlled offline/nearline analysis tool.

Scope and When to Run:
- Scope: models served by Redwood serving runtime (gpt-family and encoder-decoder variants) running in hosted, dedicated, or private deployments.
- Run triggers (choose one or more):
  1. Before promoting a quantized build to staging/dedicated pools.
  2. After kernel or runtime changes that affect attention/KV cache.
  3. On regression alerts flagged by continuous evals or field reports.
  4. Weekly longtail scans on a stratified subset of traffic.

Architecture (text diagram):
- Components:
  - Ingress: replay-worker fleet (containerized) that pulls traces from Replay Store.
  - Replay Store: S3-backed event store with schema-ed traces (request metadata, tokenization, deterministic RNG seed).
  - Controller: qro-controller (orchestrates batches, model mapping, quant profiles).
  - Normalizer: request normalizer that ensures identical tokenization and prefix padding between baseline and variant.
  - Metrics Collector: emits QA metrics to /internal/metric/v1 and detailed artifact storage to Replay Store (per-example diff blobs).
  - Comparator: post-process job that computes deltas and significance tests.

Operational SLOs and Targets:
- Correctness: replay determinism >= 99.95% (same tokenized input and RNG seed produces matching deterministic non-deterministic ops when configured).
- Coverage: scheduled scan should process >= 95% of target trace sample within target window (default 24h for weekly scans).
- Latency: single-example replay time not an SLO (batch throughput target: 300 examples/s per 8xA100 equivalent pool when running non-streaming scoring).
- Alert thresholds (comparator outputs):
  - Mean lexical divergence (BLEU-like) drop > 3.0 pts -> P1 review.
  - Mean embedding cosine drop > 0.04 -> P1 review if correlated with user-reported regressions.
  - Median per-token latency increase > 20ms -> perf investigation (P2).

Data and Trace Format (table represented in text):
- Required fields in each trace record (newline-separated table-like block):
  - trace_id: string (uuid)
  - timestamp_utc: ISO8601
  - client_id: string (anonymized)
  - model_baseline: string (model:version)
  - model_variant: string (quantized profile id)
  - prompt: raw text
  - token_ids: list<int> (BPE ids) encoded as comma-separated string
  - seed: int
  - metadata: JSON-stringified map (app_version, region, route)
  - expected_answer (optional): text for labeled prompts

Configuration example (YAML snippet):
---
controller: 
  concurrency: 64
  batch_size: 8
  retry_policy: 
    max_retries: 2
    backoff_ms: 500
model_mapping: 
  baseline: gpt-3.5-infer-float:v1
  variants: [gpt-3.5-infer-q8:profile-2026-01, gpt-3.5-infer-q4:profile-2026-01]
sampling: 
  strategy: stratified
  strata: ["high_latency_routes","low_latency_routes","rare_intents"]
  sample_count: 10000
artifact_paths: 
  replay_store: s3://redwood-replay-store/2026/qro/
  diffs: s3://redwood-replay-diffs/
---

Example CLI commands:
- Submit a run: 
  ./qro submit --config configs/qro-staging.yaml --run-id qro-2026-02-03-staging
- Stream metrics (dev):
  ./qro tail-metrics --run-id qro-2026-02-03-staging | jq .
- Collect artifacts locally: 
  aws s3 sync s3://redwood-replay-diffs/qro-2026-02-03-staging ./artifacts

Comparator outputs and required follow-up:
- Output files produced per run (artifact naming):
  - summary.json: high-level statistics and pass/fail flags
  - per-example-diffs/{trace_id}.ndjson: token alignment and lexical diffs
  - statistical-report.html: auto-generated report with charts and significance tests
- Pass/fail rules (automated gate):
  1. Block promotion if ANY of the following are true:
     - >0.5% of labeled prompts flip classification label
     - BLEU drop > 3.0 pts and p-value < 0.01
     - Embedding drift above threshold and median confidence drop > 0.05
  2. If blocked, assign to regression-triage queue (see triage checklist).

Triage checklist (for humans):
1. Review summary.json and top 50 per-example diffs by severity.
2. Check tokenization mismatches: ensure normalizer used identical token vocab.
3. Run deterministic replays for failing examples with higher verbosity: 
   ./qro inspect --trace-id <trace_id> --verbosity debug --runs 10
4. Check for runtime-only causes: kernel changes, attention precision flags, and KV cache boundary conditions.
5. If quantization is implicated, run float vs quant with identical seed and compare logits: 
   python tools/compare_logits.py --float ./artifacts/float_logits --quant ./artifacts/quant_logits --trace-id <id>
6. If failure is correlated with specific prompt patterns, add to prompt-catalog bugset and tag for future evals.

Integration with model onboarding and quality guardrails:
- This run should be attached to the model promotion PR as an artifact. Link the summary.json under the PR checklist item: "QRO run attached and PASS/FAIL status".
- For Private deployments, export only aggregated metrics (no identifiable prompt text) unless customer consent is present. Use DP sanitizer: tools/dp_sanitizer --input artifacts --output s3://redwood-privacy-archive/

Quantization-specific considerations:
- deterministic rounding differences: enable "stable-quant" mode when comparing small-decimal logits.
- KV caching: ensure replay worker simulates the exact cache warmup pattern (prefix lengths, streaming vs non-streaming).
- Mixed-precision fallbacks: compare variant with and without mixed-precision to isolate kernel regressions.

Owner and escalation paths:
- QRO owners: Applied ML - Eval Infrastructure team (primary: @applied-ml-eval).
- On-call escalation: first contact: Marcus Li (applied-ml-eval oncall), then Eng SRE rotation, then Runtime team lead.
- Pager conditions: failed scheduled run (>= 95% sample not processed), or comparator encountering internal errors (exception rate > 5%).

Run cadence and reporting:
- Ad-hoc for promotions, weekly longtail scans (by default Saturdays 02:00 UTC), and immediate runs after kernel merges affecting quant routines.
- Reports are published to the Eval Dashboard under: Evaluations > QRO > last-30-days. The summary.json is auto-imported and emailed to model owners.

Troubleshooting (short playbook):
- Problem: Many tokenization mismatches
  - Check tokenizer version in controller config (tokenizer_version). Re-run with tokenizer snapshot.
- Problem: Non-deterministic diffs across repeated runs
  - Verify RNG seed handling; set seed_override in config to force stable runs.
  - Confirm runtime flags: disable async-sampling and approximate top-k in the replay job.
- Problem: Large embedding drift for non-semantic prompts
  - Confirm embedding model version match and remove whitespace-normalization differences.

Privacy and compliance notes:
- Do not include un-sanitized customer-identifiable content in public artifacts. For enterprise customers, follow the Private deployment export policy and obtain Data Export Approval ticket.

Appendix A: Example minimal config (inline JSON)
{ 
  "run_id": "qro-minimal-2026-02-03",
  "baseline": "gpt-3.5-infer-float:v1",
  "variants": ["gpt-3.5-infer-q8:profile-2026-01"],
  "sample_count": 1000,
  "stratify_by": "route",
  "artifact_bucket": "s3://redwood-replay-diffs/qro-minimal-2026-02-03"
}

Appendix B: Quick link references:
- Quant-profile synthesis playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024
- Shadow deployment eval playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/shadow-deployment-eval-playbook-for-private-and-dedicated-2026
- Regression triage handbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026

Notes and change log:
- 2026-01-12: Initial draft (Daniela Kim)
- 2026-02-03: Updated comparator thresholds and added DP sanitizer instructions (Daniela Kim)

Ownership and contacts:
- Doc owner: Daniela Kim (Applied ML, Eval Infrastructure)
- Primary contact: Marcus Li (applied-ml-eval oncall)

title: Synthetic Seed Generation and Resampling Protocol for Eval Stability
content:
Overview

This document specifies Redwood's canonical protocol for generating synthetic seeds used by eval harnesses and for performing repeatable resampling during stress, stability, and regression tests. The goal is to reduce nondeterministic noise in eval results while preserving representative diversity across workloads and model variants. This protocol is intended for all eval-related automation (CI evals, nightly stress runs, private/dedicated shadowing, and benchmark suites).

Why we need a standardized seed/resampling protocol

- Eval instability is a major root cause of false positives in regression alerts and wasted developer time.
- Synthetic seeds and resampling policies control two orthogonal factors: reproducibility (exact-repeat debugging) and statistical representativeness (variance in distributional tests).
- Without standardization, teams use ad-hoc RNGs and sample sizes that lead to inconsistent F-score drift, noisy A/B comparisons, and fragile quantization verification.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to: eval-harness pipelines, prompt-set generators, synthetic workload producers, and model-onboarding testbeds.
- Out of scope: production request routing, customer data sampling (handled by data-management policies).

Key definitions

- seed: A 64-bit integer used as the root for deterministic PRNG chains.
- deterministic run: An eval execution that, given the same seed and config, must produce byte-for-byte identical synthetic inputs and stable metric computations (modulo model stochasticity when sampling is enabled).
- resample window: The policy time interval after which new synthetic seeds are introduced into continuous evals (e.g., daily, weekly).

Ownership and responsibilities

- Eval Platform (team): maintain the seed service, canonical RNG libraries, and automation for resampling. Owner: @eval-platform.
- Applied ML / Evals (team): define per-workload seed distributions, target sample sizes, and required statistical tests. Owner: @applied-ml.
- Model Onboarding Engineers: request additional deterministic seeds for debugging and certify new seed sets during model promotions.

Protocol: Seed generation and cataloging

1) Canonical RNG and format
   - Use the platform canonical PRNG: xoshiro256++ initialized from a 64-bit master seed. Implementations exist in Redwood's eval-sdks (python and go) at git:redwood/eval-sdks (module: redwood.eval.rng).
   - Seed metadata record (stringified JSON) must include: seed_id, seed_value (decimal), created_by, created_at (ISO-8601), tags (list), and checksum. Example: {\"seed_id\":\"sd-20260214-17\",\"seed_value\":\"9571623412341234\",\"created_by\":\"eval-platform\",\"created_at\":\"2026-02-14T17:23:00Z\",\"tags\":[\"nl-fewshot\",\"stress\"],\"checksum\":\"sha256:...\"}.

2) Seed catalog service
   - All seeds must be registered in the seed-catalog (internal HTTP API: seed-catalog.redwood.svc.cluster.local).
   - Seed records are immutable; if a seed is revoked, mark status=deprecated with a deprecation_reason.

3) Namespacing and tag schema
   - Use a three-part tag schema: workload-type (e.g., \"nl-classification\"), purpose (e.g., \"canary\", \"stress\"), and geography/locale (optional, e.g., \"en-US\").

4) Entropy and diversity constraints
   - For each synthetic workload generator, maintain a mapping of entropy budgets (percentiles of prompt template parameterization). The eval team must define minimum coverage constraints (e.g., template coverage >= 95% over canonical prompt set).

Resampling policy and cadence

- Static evals (on PR): use fixed seed sets pinned in the PR config file. Re-run behavior must re-use the same seeds until the PR author updates the config.
- CI nightly/every-24h stress: rotate N seeds per workload where N depends on workload variance (see table below).
- Weekly/Canary pool: refresh 20% of the pool every week; full pool refresh every 12 weeks or when prompt-set changes exceed a threshold.

Resampling cadence table

| Eval type | Pool size (min) | Refresh policy | Rationale |
|-----------|-----------------|----------------|-----------|
| PR/unit (deterministic) | 8 | pinned per PR | Fast short runs; reproducibility prioritized |
| CI/nightly stress | 128 | rotate 8 seeds/day | Capture diversity; limit noise per run |
| Production shadow | 512 | rotate 64 seeds/day | Extensive coverage for real traffic emulation |
| Long-tail detection suite | 2048 | stratified monthly resample | Find edge-case regressions |

Statistical guidance and thresholds

- Minimum effective sample size (ESS): each eval-run must compute ESS for weighted metrics; ESS < 30 flags low-confidence.
- Metric variance threshold: 95th percentile rolling variance (7-day window) per-metric must remain below workload-specific thresholds. If variance > threshold, trigger triage flow.
- Regression alerting: require both (a) metric delta >= critical_delta and (b) p-value <= 0.01 using the recommended bootstrap test. Avoid single-run-based alerts.

Configuration examples

- YAML example for an eval job that consumes seed-catalog:

job_name: stress-qa-nl
workload: nl-generation
seed_pool: seed-catalog:tag=\"nl-generation,stress,en-US\"
pool_size: 128
rotate_per_run: 8
metrics: [bleu,rouge2,semantic-similarity]
critical_delta: 0.06
variance_thresholds:
  bleu: 0.02
  semantic-similarity: 0.015

CLI examples

- Create a new seed and register: 
  redwood-seed create --tags nl-generation,stress --created-by automated-resampler --output-json | curl -X POST \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data @- https://seed-catalog.internal/api/v1/seeds

- Pull seed pool for job: 
  redwood-seed list --tags \"nl-generation,stress,en-US\" --limit 128 --format csv

Deterministic debug mode

- For failures that require exact replay, request the seed_id and run with --deterministic --seed-id <seed_id> flags. Deterministic runs use the same RNG chain and template parameterization, ensuring byte-for-byte identical synthetic inputs.

Integration with other eval concerns

- Quantization tests: tag seeds used for quant-eval as \"quant-sanity\"; keep a small dedicated pool (min 64) that is never rotated during a quant certification run to isolate numeric instability from sampling noise.
- Regression triage: link seed_id in regression tickets. The triage playbook should include steps to re-run failing workloads with the exact seed and with a nearby neighborhood of +/- 10 seeds to determine whether the failure is seed-specific or systematic.
- Prompt coverage: every resample must compute prompt-template coverage delta and fail if coverage falls below 90% of the canonical set.

Failure modes and runbook pointers

- Symptom: high day-to-day metric variance without code or model changes.
  - Quick checks: verify seed-catalog returned the expected pool; check for unintended stochastic sampling flags; confirm PRNG library version.
  - If seed drift suspected: pin to earlier seed_id and re-run. See runbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/promotion-readiness-synthetic-quant-safety-playbook-2026

- Symptom: single-seed outliers causing regression alerts.
  - Triage: re-run with deterministic seed; run neighborhood of seeds (+/- 10); if only one seed fails, mark seed as flakey and deprecate in seed-catalog, then expand pool to maintain coverage.

Monitoring, dashboards, and SLOs

- Dashboards to create:
  - Eval Stability Overview: per-workload rolling variance, ESS, seed-pool utilization.
  - Seed Health: seed success rate, flakiness per-seed_id (failures/total runs), average runtime impact.

- SLOs:
  - Per-run ESS >= 50 for nightly stress (target) and ESS >= 30 (minimum).
  - Per-workload 7-day variance under threshold defined in workload config (default 0.03).
  - Seed catalog API 99.9% availability with 200ms median latency.

Rollout and updates

1) New seed sets must go through a staged rollout: 
   - Stage A (canary): 5% of nightly runs for 7 days, monitor variance and coverage.
   - Stage B (gradual): 25% for 14 days.
   - Stage C (full): 100% after no significant anomalies.
2) If any monitoring alert fires during canary, rollback to previous seed pool and open an incident with applied-ml and eval-platform.

Appendix: quick checklist for model-onboarding engineers

- [ ] Request private deterministic seeds for debugging (include seed_id in PR).
- [ ] Verify that quant-eval tag pool is used for numeric regressions.
- [ ] Run neighborhood resamples when investigating flaky failures.
- [ ] Record seed_id in the promotion ticket and note any deprecations.

References and related docs

- seed-catalog API: https://seed-catalog.internal/docs
- eval-sdks (rng implementation): git:redwood/eval-sdks#rng
- Promotion readiness playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026

Contact

- For platform issues: eval-platform@redwood.internal
- For policy or coverage questions: applied-ml@redwood.internal

Change log

- 2025-11-12: Draft created (Amelia Chen).
- 2026-01-21: Added integration notes for quantization pools (reviewer: Priya Kapoor).
- 2026-02-18: Finalized resampling cadence table and SLOs; promoted to published.

title: Probe Resynthesis & Budget Simulator: operator manual
content:
Summary:

This page describes the Probe Resynthesis & Budget Simulator (PRBS): an operational tool and set of procedures used by Applied ML to synthesize realistic probe sets from live telemetry, simulate evaluation budget allocation, and surface candidate probe-resynthesis strategies that minimize cost while preserving slice coverage and detection power. PRBS is intended to reduce manual probe curation overhead, accelerate probe replenishment for drifting slices, and provide an auditable simulation trail for budget-driven prioritization during onboarding, shadow validation, and regression triage.

Why PRBS exists:

- We observe expensive manual annotation cycles when longtail prompt slices drift or when quantization/timeout changes require fresh probes.
- Teams need to reason about trade-offs between probe volume, annotation cost, and detection latency for regressions.
- PRBS provides deterministic simulations using historical telemetry + a workload-cost model to recommend resynthesis policies.

Scope and applicability:

- Applies to: eval harness teams, model onboarding, regression triage, and the quality guardrails workflows.
- Not for: production inference routing, customer-facing A/B decisions, or one-off handwritten benchmarks.

High-level workflow (operator view):

1) Ingest: pull telemetry fingerprint snapshots from Eval-Mesh (daily/weekly cadence).
2) Fingerprint synth: cluster pockets of drift and generate seed anchors using the inkling heuristic (see config table).
3) Resynthesize: produce candidate probes for each slice using the selected synthesis policy (seeded paraphrase, adversarial-noise, or hybrid).
4) Simulate: feed synthesized probes into the cost simulator with target annotation rates, expected annotator agreement, and quantization noise models.
5) Score & prioritize: output ranked actions (resynthesize X, retire Y, escalate Z), with estimated cost, expected recall improvement, and detection latency.
6) Promote: selected probe batches are committed to the probe registry and scheduled for annotation.

Key concepts and definitions:

- Probe: an input-record (prompt + metadata) used by eval harnesses to exercise model slices.
- Slice: a semantically grouped set of probes (e.g., financial-instruction, multi-turn-customer-support, low-resource-language).
- Resynthesis policy: algorithmic rule used to generate new probes from seeds (paraphrase, noise-perturbation, translation-backtranslate).
- Budget simulation: deterministic calculation of annotation cost and expected detection performance given probe set composition.

Operational SLOs and thresholds:

- Probe coverage SLO: 95% of active high-priority slices must have >= N_min probes (N_min depends on slice criticality; see table).
- Detection latency SLO: median time to detect a 5% fidelity regression for high-priority slices <= 72 hours under normal resynthesis cadence.
- Budget adherence: recommended resynthesis plan must remain within the monthly eval budget +/- 10% unless approved by Eval PMO.

Parameter table (common configs):

| parameter_name | default | notes |
|---|---:|---|
| resynthesis_window_days | "14" | window of telemetry used to seed resynthesis |
| seed_per_slice | "10" | number of seed anchors sampled per slice |
| target_annot_per_probe | "1" | number of annotations per probe for majority-label tasks |
| annotator_unit_cost_usd | "0.75" | default annotator cost used in sim |
| critical_slice_threshold | "0.05" | fraction of traffic to mark slice as critical |
| quant_noise_factor | "0.03" | conservative estimate for token-level degradation under int8 quant |

(Use these values as starting points; teams may override at the slice-level in the PRBS config.)

Command-line quickstart:

1) Fetch telemetry snapshot:
$ prbs fetch --snapshot-date 2026-02-01 --out snapshots/2026-02-01.json\n2) Run resynthesis simulation with hybrid policy:
$ prbs simulate --snapshot snapshots/2026-02-01.json --policy hybrid --budget 5000 --out sims/hybrid-2026-02-01.json
3) Review top recommendations:
$ prbs summarize --sim sims/hybrid-2026-02-01.json --top 20

The tool emits a CSV with recommended probe actions and an audit JSON for reproducibility (store audit files in s3://redwood-evals/prbs-audit/).

Example policy YAML (annotated):

policy_name: hybrid-resyn-1
resynthesis_window_days: 14
seed_selection:
  method: stratified
  per_slice: 10
synthesis_generators:
  - paraphrase
  - adversarial-noise: {max_perturb: 0.12}
  - backtranslate: {langs: ["fr","es"]}
scoring:
  cost_weights: {annotation: 0.6, detection_power: 0.3, freshness: 0.1}

(Operators copy this YAML into the PRBS policy registry when creating new strategies.)

Integration points and telemetry signals:

- Eval-Mesh snapshot: primary source for per-slice telemetry (latency, tokens, error-rates, fidelity).
- Registry: probe-registry (write access for promotion).
- Annotator pipeline: annotation-queue service (submit batches).
- Evals billing: cost-accounting ledger to reconcile simulated vs actual spend.
- Regression triage: output recommendations create work items in the Regression Board with links to probe batches.

Scoring heuristics (how candidate batches are ranked):

- Detection power estimate: measured as expected lift in slice-level signal-to-noise given additional probes; computed via bootstrap on historical slice variance.
- Cost estimate: annotator_unit_cost_usd * probes * target_annot_per_probe + labeling overhead (10%).
- Freshness score: inverse of median age (days) of probes in slice.

Decisioning matrix (example):

1) If cost per expected-detection > $1200 and slice traffic < critical_slice_threshold => defer resynthesis.
2) If detection latency expected > 72h and slice is critical => escalate to Eval leads and request emergency annotation credit.
3) If quant_noise_factor > 0.05 and slice shows coherence-sensitive tokens => prefer paraphrase + backtranslate hybrid (higher diversity).

Procedure: from simulation to production promotion (numbered steps for operators):

1. Run prbs simulate with the latest snapshot.
2. Review sims/*/summary.csv and open the top-N predicted actions.
3. Validate 3 representative synthesized probes per candidate batch via the human-in-the-loop QA quickcheck (2 annotators).
4. Approve or reject candidate batches in the web UI; approved batches are automatically enqueued for annotation.
5. After annotation, wait for the annotation-completion webhook and run prbs reconcile --batch <id> to update the registry and cost ledger.
6. If the annotated batch triggers a regression detection improvement < expected, file a follow-up triage with the regression-triage template.

Onboarding checklist (model/service teams):

- [ ] Register slice taxonomy with Eval-Mesh and link to PRBS slice IDs.
- [ ] Provide criticality tiers for slices (low/medium/high).
- [ ] Set monthly eval budget and escalation contacts.
- [ ] Run a baseline PRBS sim and review recommendations with Applied ML lead.

Failure modes and mitigations:

- Mode: Synthesized probes are syntactically valid but semantically irrelevant -> Mitigation: tighten seed-selection (higher similarity threshold) and increase human QA sample size to 5 per batch.
- Mode: Simulator underestimates annotation latency -> Mitigation: add per-region latency slack and tie annotation SLA to live queue metrics.
- Mode: Excessive churn in probe registry -> Mitigation: apply retire-after policy for probes older than 540 days and introduce probe-stability gating.

Auditability and reproducibility:

- Every simulation run produces an audit bundle: {snapshot-id, policy-id, seed-rng-seed, scoring-hash}. Store audit bundles in S3 and attach to regression board tickets.
- Use prbs replay --audit <id> to reproduce the exact candidate set.

Quality guardrail interactions (short):

- PRBS must be run against the same eval contracts used by quality-guardrails (fidelity thresholds, sentinel tests). Candidate probe batches that reduce sentinel coverage by > 5% are auto-rejected.
- If quantization profiles are in play, PRBS will simulate quant_noise_factor effects and surface batches with high sensitivity for manual review.

Observability and dashboards to monitor (owners):

- PRBS-run-rate (ops) - how frequently sims run per week.
- Probe-recommendation-accept-rate (product) - percent of recommended batches approved.
- Sim-vs-actual-cost-delta (finance) - monthly reconciliation metric.
- Slice-detection-latency (SRE) - median detection time for top-50 slices.

Ownership and escalation contacts:

- Tool owner: Applied ML - Eval Orchestration (team alias: #applied-ml-eval).
- Primary oncall for PRBS failures: eval-harness oncall (see oncall rota).
- Budget escalation: Eval PMO (eval-budget@redwood.ai).

Appendix: quick triage checklist for regression incidents related to probe gaps:

1) Confirm whether the failing slice has recent PRBS recommendations (search audit bundles).
2) If yes, check whether recommendations were approved/enqueued for annotation and whether annotation completed.
3) If annotation incomplete and slice is critical, escalate for emergency annotation credit and run an interim limited-synthesis with max_perturb=0.05.
4) If annotation complete but detection power did not improve, open a root-cause with hypothesis: (a) seed selection bias, (b) insufficient diversity, (c) quantization collapse.

References and related docs:

- Eval budget ledger: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-budget-accounting-ledger-and-cost-attribution-2026
- Regression triage quickstart: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/eval-oncall-runbook-for-model-regression-debugging-2026
- Probe registry spec: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/probe-curation-stewardship-and-annotation-charter-2026

Contact for questions: Asha Menon (asha@redwood.ai) and the #applied-ml-eval Slack channel.

Change log:
- 2025-08-12: Initial draft and prototype scripts (Asha Menon).
- 2025-11-04: Added hybrid policy defaults and quantization simulation (review: Liam O'Connor).
- 2026-02-15: Updated adjacency to annotation queue webhook and tightened SLOs (review: Priya Patel).

title: Evaluation Asset Retirement and Reuse Guidelines
content:
Summary
This page defines the approved lifecycle for evaluation assets (probes, prompt sets, annotated labels, synthetic probe families, and replay snapshots) at Redwood Inference. It standardizes criteria for retiring, archiving, and safely reusing assets across eval-harness, prompt-sets, model-onboarding, quality-guardrails, and quantization workflows.

Scope
- Applies to all evaluation artifacts stored in: eval-mesh, probe-registry, evaluator-backup-s3, and local evaluator worker caches.
- Covers asset retirement, archival format, metadata enrichment, privacy redaction, reuse approval, and deletion windows.
- Does NOT change production data retention for customer telemetry (see security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention).

Definitions
- Probe: A single input+expected-output evaluation case recorded in the probe-registry.
- Asset: Any file or dataset used for evaluation: prompts, labels, annotation logs, shadow-replay bundles, quantization sample sets.
- Retirement: The status assigned when an asset is no longer part of active evaluation schedules.
- Archive: Long-term storage location for retired assets that may be reactivated after review.

Why this matters
- Storage and compute costs for the eval fleet are non-trivial — stale assets increase evaluator scheduling churn and probe noise.
- Reusing old assets without proper metadata/PII handling risks regressions and compliance violations.
- A clear flow reduces friction for model-onboarding and incident triage teams needing historical probes.

Retention & Retirement Rules (summary table)
| Asset class | Active window | Retirement trigger | Archive TTL | Final deletion |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| Regular probe (small) | 180 days since last use | < 3 executions in 90 days OR superseded by newer slice | 730 days | 1095 days after retirement |
| Annotated label bundle | 365 days | Freeze-requested by steward OR annotation drift detected | 1825 days | 2555 days |
| Shadow-replay snapshot | 90 days | Snapshot older than service model-major-version OR not used in last 30 days | 365 days | 730 days |
| Quant sample set | 180 days | Quant tuning completes OR failing fidelity thresholds | 1095 days | 1460 days |
| Synthetic probe family | 365 days | No active experiments referencing family | 1825 days | 2555 days |

Ownership and roles
- Probe steward (primary): owns the probe set lifecycle. Typical steward: service product lead or SRE.
- Evaluator steward (applied-ml): approves reuse and signing of archived assets.
- Security review (security team): required for archives that contain real user traffic variants.
- Data privacy owner (people-ops / security): final signoff for any PII removal claims.

Retirement procedure (for probe stewards)
1. Evaluate usage: run the asset-usage-report for the asset id (see CLI below). If conditions match retirement triggers, create a Retirement Request ticket in the Evaluation Board.
2. Metadata audit: confirm asset has required metadata fields: owner, steward, original-source, label-schema, sampling-seed, and last-used-timestamp. Missing fields: populate before proceeding.
3. PII/redaction check: if asset.source == "live-traffic" run pii-scan and then redact-tool. Attach redaction report to ticket.
4. Freeze: set probe-registry.status = "frozen" and stop scheduling in eval-mesh (automated step via retire-agent).
5. Archive: run archive-pack command to bundle and push to probe-archive-s3 with manifest.json.
6. Signoff: Evaluator steward + security (if live traffic) must sign retirement request within 5 business days.
7. Move to final: after signoff, probe-registry updates status -> "archived" and archival TTL starts.
8. Deletion: When archive TTL expires, artifact-ledger emits delete candidate. Data privacy owner schedules automated wipe unless exception is granted.

CLI & Examples
- Asset usage report (returns JSON):
  - cli: ./evalctl asset-usage --asset-id sha256:0a12b3 --window 90
- Freeze and archive example:
  - cli: ./evalctl retire --asset-id sha256:0a12b3 --reason "superseded-by:probe-family-2026-v2"
  - On success: {"status":"queued","archive_location":"s3://probe-archive/2026/sha256-0a12b3.tar.gz"}
- Example manifest.json (bundled with archive):
  - {"asset_id":"sha256:0a12b3","steward":"service-abc","schema_version":"v2","pii_redacted":true,"labels":64}

Archive format and minimal manifest fields
- Archive must be compressed tarball (.tar.gz) with the following top-level entries: data/, manifest.json, provenance.txt, checksum.sha256.
- manifest.json minimal required keys (string or number): asset_id, steward, created_at, original_service, schema_version, label_count, pii_redacted, retention_policy, related_assets (list of asset_ids).

Privacy & Redaction guidance
- If asset derives from live traffic, automatic redaction is required for: email addresses, IP addresses, national IDs, payment tokens, and user identifiers. Use redaction level: "high" for assets intended for external sharing.
- Redaction tool: pii-scan + redact-tool chain. Commands: 
  - ./pii-scan --input data/ --output reports/scan.json
  - ./redact-tool --input data/ --rules redaction-level-high.yml --output data-redacted/
- Store redaction report inside provenance.txt. Security must approve any export of archived assets to third parties.

Reuse & Rehydration (bringing an archive back to active)
- Trigger: a model-onboarding or regression-hunt runbook requests rehydration.
- Required approvals: Evaluator steward + probe steward must approve. Security approval if archived asset had "pii_redacted":false.
- Rehydration steps (automated API):
  1. ./evalctl rehydrate --archive s3://probe-archive/2026/sha256-0a12b3.tar.gz --target-namespace onboarding-shadow
  2. System performs integrity check (checksum.sha256) and validates manifest schema.
  3. Reinserted assets receive new asset-id version and are scheduled into eval-mesh with label:rehydrated=true and a 14-day probation period (limited traffic window).

Exceptions and emergency retention
- emergency-retain tag: used by oncall during an incident when asset must survive beyond TTL for diagnosis.
- Authorization: Incident commander + Evaluator steward must record justification in the Retirement Request ticket. Emergency-retain auto-expires after 90 days unless extended.

Telemetry & SLOs for asset management system
- archive-pack success rate >= 99% over 30 days (owner: evaluator-ops).
- manifest completeness >= 98% (no missing required manifest keys).
- average rehydration time <= 12 minutes for archives < 2GB.
- probe-registry list latency < 200ms p95.

Monitoring and alerts
- Alert: archive-pack-failure when > 1% fail in a 1-hour window -> paging to evaluator-ops.
- Alert: manifest-missing-fields when an archival job includes missing required fields -> email to steward and ticket created.

Audit and compliance evidence
- Every archive push must create an entry in artifact-ledger: {asset_id, steward, action:archive, actor, timestamp, checksum}. Ledger entries are immutable and retained for 7 years.
- Quarterly audit: security + applied-ml review a sample of 5% of archives for adherence to redaction and manifest requirements.

Examples of common workflows and decisions
- Reuse during model-onboarding: prefer rehydrating an archived annotated label bundle over creating a new annotation job if label_count >= 500 AND last-annotation-quality >= 0.87 (evaluated on the annotation-quality job).
- Quant migration: prefer new quant-samples when quant-tuning target model architecture changes. If reusing, run quant-shadow-sanity and compare fidelity delta < 1.5% before accepting.

Open questions / planned improvements
- Automate manifest enrichment via heuristics in evalctl to reduce manual steward work.
- Add retention analytics dashboard in Redwood Console (owner: product-telemetry).

Appendix: Quick commands & policy links
- Quick CLI: 
  - ./evalctl asset-usage --asset-id <id> --window 90
  - ./evalctl retire --asset-id <id> --reason <text>
  - ./evalctl rehydrate --archive <s3-url> --target-namespace <ns>
- Related docs:
  - /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/probe-serialization-replay-index-fingerprint-spec-2026.json
  - /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/personal-data-retention-standards-2025.json

If you are a probe steward and need help: ping #eval-ops or file a ticket in the Evaluation Board with component:probe-registry and label:retirement.

title: Persona Bias Probing and Anchor Eval Framework
content:
Overview

This document defines the Persona Bias Probing and Anchor Eval Framework (PBAEF), an evaluation harness designed to: 1) detect persona-conditional bias and safety regressions, 2) provide stable anchor baselines for longitudinal calibration, and 3) integrate with Redwood’s eval orchestration for automated triage and alerting. It combines structured persona variants, targeted adversarial perturbations, and anchor-controlled scoring so that changes in model weights, quantization, or serving configuration can be attributed precisely.

Goals and scope

- Primary goals:
  - Surface persona-dependent failure modes (bias, toxicity, hallucination) across representative workloads.
  - Provide anchor baselines that remain stable across model promotions and deployments to detect relative regressions.
  - Integrate with regression triage playbooks to shorten mean time to detect and resolve quality regressions.
- Scope:
  - Focused on text generation and instruction-following models used in customer-facing chat and assistant flows.
  - Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; quantization-specific guardrails included.
  - Not intended for large-scale safety certification alone — complement to Safety Sandbox.

Definitions

- Anchor prompt: a fixed stimulus (prompt + context) selected to be stable, low-variance, and semantically neutral; used as a baseline to detect drift.
- Persona variant: systematic rewrites of a core prompt that inject persona cues (age, occupation, dialect, religion, gender presentation) while preserving informational intent.
- Bias delta: relative change in a bias metric between current run and anchor baseline (reported as percent).
- Calibrated score: metric value adjusted for known sampling variance using the anchor population.

Design principles

1) Anchoring: each report contains both (a) a set of anchor prompts and (b) the active persona-variant suite. Anchors are rerun at every promotion and on nightly pipelines to control for infrastructure-induced variance.
2) Orthogonality: persona attributes are varied orthogonally to content intent (e.g., same question phrased for different persona labels) to isolate persona effects.
3) Parsimony: test suites are compact (100–500 examples per workload) to enable frequent runs without large compute cost.
4) Explainability: every flagged regression provides diffs, exemplar generations, and likely causal signals (quantization change, kernel switch, batch-size change).

Suite composition and generation procedure

1) Core intent corpus: 250 canonical prompts covering common product intents (summarization, code generation, customer support, policy clarification). Prompts are stored in the canonical prompt repo.
2) Persona matrix: 10 persona attributes x 5 values each (50 variants). Each core prompt is paired with 8 persona variants sampled with stratified coverage.
3) Adversarial perturbations: for each persona-variant pair, apply 3 perturbations from the adversarial prompt suite (lexical noise, sarcasm marker insertion, indirect question phrasing).
4) Anchor set: 40 prompts chosen for low semantic ambiguity and historical stability. Anchors include deterministic seeds and fixed tokenization to reduce runtime nondeterminism.

Metric definitions and thresholds

- Safety toxicity rate: percent of outputs flagged by safety classifier >= 0.5. Threshold: regression if increase > 0.4 percentage points AND bias delta > 25% relative.
- Demographic parity difference: absolute difference in positive/negative sentiment across persona groups. Threshold: alert if > 6 points (0–100 scale) relative to anchors.
- Hallucination rate: percent of outputs containing fabricated named facts (verified by reference extractor). Threshold: regression if increase > 3 points and persists across 3 consecutive nightly runs.
- Response divergence score (RDS): KL-style divergence between persona-conditioned token distributions and anchor distribution. Threshold: alert if RDS increases by > 0.15.

Anchoring and calibration methodology

- Anchors are executed in the same job as the active suite and are used to compute a calibrated score: calibrated_score = observed - anchor_mean + historical_anchor_mean.
- For short-lived infra variance (noisy GPUs, quant kernel jitter) we apply a rolling 7-run median to anchor_mean before raising alerts.
- When calibrating across quantized variants, anchors include both float32 and quantized runs to produce per-precision baselines.

Integration with eval orchestration and CI

- Orchestrator job: eval-orchestrator:run-persona-pbaef triggers PBAEF. Job parameters:
  - model_id (string)
  - precision_profile (enum: fp32, q4_0, q8_0)
  - run_type (smoke|nightly|promotion)
- Execution schedule:
  - Promotion gate: full PBAEF suite on canary and 10% production shadow during canary window.
  - Nightly: compact persona sample + anchors.
  - Post-quantize: run full persona + quant anchors after any quantization pipeline.
- Output artifacts: JSON results, exemplar CSV, annotated diffs, and a JIRA ticket template if thresholds breached.

Regressions triage playbook (high level)

1) Alert ingestion: monitoring posts an alert to #eval-alerts with model_id, metric, delta, and link to artifacts.
2) Auto-classify probable cause: triage-bot analyzes recipe — flags likely causes: quantization, kernel swap, model weight change, config change, or upstream prompt repo change.
3) Run bisect: if weight change suspected, run binary promotion-bisect using model binary snapshots. If quant change suspected, run precision A/B with anchors.
4) Human review: assign to owner (see Ownership table) and open a focused investigation doc.
5) Fix and verify: apply patch (config revert, model rollback, quant recompile) then re-run PBAEF smoke and anchored checks.

Ownership, SLAs and run frequency

- Ownership table:
  - Eval harness orchestration: Evaluations Platform (team-evals-platform@redwood.com)
  - Persona prompt maintenance: Applied ML / Prompting (team-applied-ml@redwood.com)
  - Incident triage: Model Reliability (team-model-reliability@redwood.com)
- SLAs:
  - Nightly anchored run completes within 2 hours for the compact suite.
  - Full promotion run completes within 6 hours.
  - Alert triage owner acknowledged within 1 business hour.

Example commands and snippets

- Trigger a promotion run (CLI):
  rwi eval run --suite persona-pbaef --model redwood-bert-v2 --precision q4_0 --run_type promotion --notify "#eval-alerts"

- Example result JSON (simplified) included as artifact:
  {
    "model_id": "redwood-bert-v2",
    "run_id": "2026-02-10-01",
    "metrics": {"toxicity_rate": "0.7%", "hallucination_rate": "2.1%", "rds": "0.12"},
    "anchors": {"toxicity_rate": "0.3%", "rds": "0.05"}
  }

Config and storage requirements (table-like text)

- Job memory: 16 GB recommended for compact run; 64 GB for full run.
- Token budget: compact suite ~ 1M tokens, full suite ~ 8–10M tokens.
- Artifact storage: results and exemplars stored in s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/{model}/{run_id}/ (retention 90 days by default).

Annotation and labeling guidance

- For human review of exemplar outputs:
  1) Labelers must follow the Persona Annotation Instructions (link in related pages).
  2) Use the structured labels: safety_flag, hallucination_flag, persona_conflict, sentiment_score (0–100), rationale (text).
  3) Margin cases escalate to senior annotator.

Reporting and dashboards

- The PBAEF dashboard (Grafana panel) surfaces: anchored metric trends, per-persona slices, exemplar counters, and incident history. Widget thresholds mirror the alerting rules above.
- Weekly digest: automated report emailed to product owners and reliability leads summarizing top regressions and persistent persona slices.

Maintenance and evolution

- Anchor refresh policy: evaluate anchors quarterly. Replace anchors only after cross-eval verification that the candidate anchor is stable across 5 recent model snapshots.
- Persona taxonomy updates: applied-ml owns taxonomy revisions; changes must be registered in the prompt repo and communicated to evals-platform 2 weeks prior to rollout.

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigations

- Kernel-level tokenization jitter: mitigation — include tokenization-stable anchors and force tokenizer version pinning in promotion runs.
- Quantization-induced terse answers: mitigation — run targeted RAG and prompt-length ablations and update quant profiles.
- Prompt repo drift (unchanged intent but reworded prompt): mitigation — maintain canonical intent IDs and map new prompt text to ID for traceability.

References

- See also: smoke-and-fidelity-eval-workflow-2025, prompt-coverage-matrix-and-annotated-drift-repair-guide-2024.
- Contact: team-applied-ml@redwood.com for taxonomy questions; team-evals-platform@redwood.com for orchestration issues.

End of document.

title: Evaluation lifecycle for Private & Dedicated deployments: integration, promotion, and monitoring playbook
content:
summary:
A cross-functional playbook describing the end-to-end evaluation lifecycle for models promoted to Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments. Covers integration points with the eval harness, deployment acceptance gates, post-promotion observability, regression triage triggers, and rollback criteria tailored for constrained/private environments.

body:
Purpose

This playbook defines the evaluation lifecycle and operational controls required to safely promote and operate models in Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments. It is intended for applied-ML engineers, release engineers, SRE, and solutions engineers who onboard customer-specific inference workloads.

Scope

- Applies to any model variant promoted from staging to Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.
- Covers integration with the eval harness, prompt set validation, quantization/kv-cache stability checks, and monitoring/alerting templates.
- Does NOT replace deployment infra runbooks (see eng-private-deployments/* for network and packaging specifics).

Key principles

1) Evaluate in-situ: run a representative eval harness against the exact runtime (quantization, kernel set, sequence length distributions) that will be used in the target deployment.
2) Define acceptance gates that combine quality, latency, and stability—do not rely solely on aggregate metrics.
3) Observe for asymptotic regressions post-promotion with an elevated monitoring window before relaxing to standard SLOs.
4) Automate rollbacks where conservative criteria are violated; require human triage for borderline failures.

Pre-promotion checklist (must pass all items)

- Model artifact verification:
  - SHA256 of model files matches signed artifact manifest.
  - Config (tokenizer, special_tokens, model config) validated against onboarding matrix.
- Eval harness integration:
  - Run full eval harness with the target runtime binary and config. Include unit prompt sets (safety, hallucination, regressions), customer prompt samples, and stress workloads.
  - Generate the standardized report: eval-report-<model>-<runtime>-<date>.json and upload to artifact store.
- Latency & throughput baselines:
  - P50/P95/P99 token latency baselines measured at target batch sizes and sequence lengths.
  - Maximum sustainable throughput (tokens/sec) at 95th percentile latency budget.
- Quantization & KV-cache checks (if applicable):
  - Run quant-stability-suite (see CLI snippet below) across representative context lengths (0, 512, 2048).
  - Validate KV-cache warm-up behavior: 1000 warm-up sequences, then measure subsequent steady-state latencies and output KL divergence vs FP16 run.
- Regression detection vector:
  - Compare top-level metrics vs baseline using the regression-delta thresholds in the table below.

Acceptance thresholds (example - teams should tune per workload)

| Metric | Acceptance threshold | Measurement window | Action if violated |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Quality Delta (composite score: accuracy+hallucination penalty) | <= 2% relative drop | 1000 eval prompts | Block promotion; open triage | 
| Embedding cosine change (mean) | <= 0.015 absolute | 2000 samples | Block promotion; run embedding recalibration | 
| P95 latency | < 1.6x baseline (target infra) | 1 hr synthetic traffic | Block promotion / capacity review |
| Token error rate (malformed tokens) | < 0.1% | 10k tokens | Block promotion |
| KV-cache hit stabilization | Reach >85% hit rate within 200 warm-up sequences | Warm-up run | Investigate caching policy/priming |

Automated CLI snippets

- Run quant stability suite:
  ```bash
  redwood-eval quant-stability --model ./artifacts/model-v3.q4_0 --runtime /opt/redwood/runtime-dedicated --prompts ./tests/kv-cache-warmup.txt --out ./reports/qstab.json
  ```

- Launch in-situ eval harness against private runtime (example uses ephemeral test node in customer VPC):
  ```bash
  eval-harness run --runtime-endpoint https://10.0.0.12:8443 --auth-token-file ~/.secrets/customer-token --suite canonical,safety,customer-sample --out ./reports/promote-eval.json
  ```

Promotion procedure (recommended automated pipeline)

1) CI gating: push artifact to staging. CI triggers eval-harness + quant-stab + perf-bench suites.
2) If all automated gates pass, create a promotion candidate in the deployment service and run a canary (1-2 nodes) for 24 hours with synthetic traffic at 10% of expected peak.
3) Canary monitoring window: elevated alerts enabled (see alerting templates). If any critical alert fires, automatic rollback to previous model; open regression ticket.
4) If canary is healthy, gradually ramp to target capacity with staged rollout (25% -> 50% -> 100%), each stage at least 2 hours or 10M tokens, whichever is later.

Post-promotion monitoring & elevated observation window

- Observation window: first 72 hours post-promotion are considered elevated. During this time:
  - Data retention: keep full request/response traces and KV-cache logs.
  - Sampling: increase prompt sampling to 5% of traffic routed to the promoted model for manual evaluation queues.
  - Alerts: use stricter thresholds (see alerting template).

Alerting templates (examples to add to monitoring stacks)

- Critical alert (SEV 1): Quality composite drop > 3% relative over 1 hour OR P95 latency > 2x baseline for > 10 minutes. Pager to SRE + applied-ML oncall.
- High alert (SEV 2): Embedding mean shift > 0.03 OR token error rate > 0.5% for 30 minutes. Notify product owner + release engineer.
- Medium alert: Elevated KV-cache miss rate > 30% for 1 hour. Create ticket for performance team.

Alert routing and ownership

- Pager rota: SRE primary -> applied-ML secondary during first 72 hours. After 72 hours, revert to standard routing.
- Incident ownership: the team that owns the model (owner_team in model manifest) is primary for triage. SRE owns rollback execution and infra traces.

Regression triage flow (on alert or automated detection)

1) Triage lead assigned (automatically by pager duty runbook).
2) Collect artifacts: eval-report, perf-bench outputs, recent traces (last 6 hours), sampling set (200 examples flagged by monitoring).
3) Quick checks (first 30 minutes): verify artifact integrity, confirm whether problem exists in staging, compare kernel/driver versions between staging and prod nodes.
4) Isolation: if steady-state latency or quality regressions are observed, shift traffic to a compatible fallback model variant (automated via routing policy).
5) Deep diagnosis: run the regression-forensics suite (see related doc) and annotate failing prompts; open a regression ticket with label regression/severity.

Rollback criteria (automatic)

- Any SEV1 alert during promotion/canary should trigger automatic rollback.
- If more than 5% of sampled prompts show quality regressions beyond the acceptance threshold within 4 hours, rollback.
- If P95 latency exceeds 2x baseline for 20 consecutive minutes under measured load, rollback.

Sampled prompt policies for private deployments

- Customer prompt sampling: collect 1 in N requests (configurable, default N=200) but redact PII and store only model inputs and outputs for evaluation. Use the builtin redaction library before storage.
- Synthetic edge-case prompts: maintain a local prompt-store per deployment with 500 targeted adversarial prompts for regular replay tests.

Quantization-specific guidance

- For on-prem hardware with diverse kernels, always include a kernel compatibility matrix in the promotion artifact.
- When enabling aggressive int4 quantization: require a double-run regression check where outputs from the quantized path are compared against FP16 baseline using semantic and token-level metrics.
- If deterministic replay differs frequently, pin the runtime to the exact kernel revision used in successful evals.

Operational artifacts to attach to promotion ticket

- eval-report-<model>-<runtime>-<date>.json
- perf-baseline-<model>-<runtime>-<date>.csv
- quant-stab-report.json
- kernel-compat-matrix.yaml
- signed-artifact-manifest.txt

Related pages

- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/serving-simulation-eval-harness-2026 (integration example)
- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/kv-cache-quant-stability-audit-playbook-2025 (stability checks)
- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/model-regression-forensics-playbook-2026 (forensics runbook)

Appendix: example monitoring rule (Prometheus-style pseudo-yaml)

```yaml
alert: EvalQualityRegression
expr: |
  (sum(rate(eval_quality_drop_total[15m])) / sum(rate(eval_checks_total[15m]))) > 0.03
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Composite eval quality drop >3% over 15m"
  runbook: https://confluence.internal/runbooks/eval-quality-regression
```

Owner and contact list

- Playbook owner: Ava Chen (applied-ML infra) - ava.chen@redwood.ai
- SRE lead: Diego Ramirez - diego.ramirez@redwood.ai
- Quantization SME: Priya Menon - priya.menon@redwood.ai

Revision history

- 2026-01-12: Created (Ava Chen)
- 2026-02-05: Added quantization warm-up guidance and KV-cache thresholds (Priya Menon)
- 2026-03-02: Expanded regression triage flow and automated rollback criteria (Diego Ramirez)

title: Multi-tenant Canary Eval: Privacy Anchoring & Probe Design Playbook
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines a reproducible, privacy-preserving approach for running multi-tenant canary evaluations of model and serving changes. It describes probe design, anchoring strategies, acceptance criteria, telemetry schema, and rollback procedures tailored for shared evaluator fleets and tenant isolation constraints.

Why this doc exists
- Multi-tenant canaries enable fast feedback but increase privacy risk and cross-tenant interference.
- We need deterministic, auditable probes that exercise production traffic slices while bounding leakage and differential privacy (DP) exposure.
- This playbook standardizes the orchestration (evaluator-orch, canary-operator), probe provenance (probe-store), and decision gates used by model promotion and runtime rollouts.

Scope and audience
- Audience: Applied ML engineers, evaluation owners, SREs operating the evaluator fleet, privacy-compliance reviewers.
- Scope: Canary evaluation of model binaries, quantization variants, routing policies, and KV-cache configurations in environments that host multiple tenants. Not intended for offline-only evals or external benchmark runs.

Key definitions
- Probe: A synthetic or sampled input designed to exercise a targeted failure mode or slice. Probes carry provenance metadata (seed_id, tenant_guard, probe_ttl).
- Anchor probe: A small subset of probes designated as high-trust references (no PII, stable expected outputs) used to detect drift or regressions without exposing tenant data.
- Privacy anchor: A probe or probe-set paired with DP noise parameters and an access policy used to bound leakage across runs.
- Canary slice: A set of tenants or traffic percentage routed to the candidate model variant during the canary window.

Goals and acceptance criteria
- Detect regressions in fidelity (semantic delta, BLEU/ROUGE proxies, task-specific accuracy) within the canary window.
- Maintain isolation: no probe should reveal PII or customer-identifiable artifacts.
- Privacy budget: per-candidate canary epsilon <= 2.0 for public-anchor aggregates; delta <= 1e-6. For tenant-level metrics, use aggregated reporting only.
- Latency and reliability SLOs: p95 latency delta <= 20ms; error-rate delta <= 0.5 percentage points.

Ownership and roles
- Eval owner: creates canary config, defines probe set and success / failure thresholds. (Team: applied-ml)
- Canary operator: schedules the canary via canary-operator and coordinates telemetry capture. (Team: eng-platform)
- Privacy reviewer: verifies that the probe-set and DP parameters meet the privacy policy. (Team: security-and-compliance)
- SRE: monitors infra signals and executes rollback if infra thresholds are violated. (Team: eng-sre)

Probe design principles
1) No-PII-by-construction: All anchor probes must be synthetic or redacted. For sampled probes from production, apply automated redaction and a secondary human privacy review for any sample used as an anchor.
2) Slice coverage: Build probes to cover long-tail slices (rare intents), latency-sensitive paths, and heavy-token sequences. Prioritize probes flagged by the stability index and production-hotspot telemetry.
3) Deterministic seeds & provenance: Store seed_id, generator version, and fixture parameters in probe-store. Each probe run must be reproducible using these fields.
4) Anchors vs. field probes: Keep anchor probes stable across promotions and use field probes for exploratory detection. Anchors are permitted in automatic gating; field probes require manual review if they signal failure.

Probe categories and examples
- Anchor synthetic: templated multi-turn tasks with fixed random seed (e.g., code-refactor instruction templates).
- Sanitized sample: production user query with PII redacted and paraphrase applied.
- Stress probe: artificially long context, heavy function-calls, or many-shot priming.
- Cache-sensitive probe: sequences designed to stress KV cache reuse patterns.

Telemetry schema (table)
Columns to capture per-probe-run:
- run_id (string)
- probe_id (string)
- seed_id (string)
- tenant_guard (string, e.g., "public_anchor" | "tenant_agg")
- model_variant (string)
- route (string)
- tokens_in (int)
- tokens_out (int)
- latency_ms (float)
- p95_latency_ms_by_route (float)
- semantic_score (float)  # per-task similarity metric
- error_tag (string, optional)
- dp_noise_eps (float, optional)
- sample_timestamp (ISO8601)
- provenance_sha (string)

Minimum retention: 90 days for aggregate metrics; probe input text retention limited to 30 days for sanitized samples unless explicitly approved by privacy.

Differential privacy guidance
- Use Gaussian mechanism for aggregate telemetry where we report counts, averages, or semantic-score histograms.
- Default per-run epsilon: 0.5; allow up to 2.0 for tightly-scoped internal canaries only after Privacy review. Report epsilon and delta in telemetry headers.
- DP implementation checklist: prove mechanism via unit tests, attach randomness source (kms-wrapped seed), and include reproducible audit logs.

Canary orchestration: step-by-step
1) Prepare probe-set and canary-config in evaluator-orch repository. Canary-config fields:
   - model_variant: identifier (e.g., redwood-model-x-v3-q4)
   - traffic_percentage: 1-5% initially
   - tenant_selectors: explicit tenant list or hashed namespace selectors
   - duration: 2h default for multi-tenant canaries
   - metrics_and_thresholds: list of metric keys and thresholds
2) Run privacy pre-check: privacy reviewer approves probe-set and DP params.
3) Schedule canary via canary-operator: attach canary-config and probe manifest.
4) Start telemetry capture: canary-operator toggles evaluator-orch telemetry API and streams to probe-ingest pipeline.
5) Monitor primary gates (automated) for the canary window:
   - Quality gate: semantic_score delta <= 0.02 (relative) on anchor set
   - Latency gate: p95_latency delta <= 20ms
   - Error gate: 4xx/5xx increase <= 0.5pp
6) If all gates pass for the stable window (configured contiguous 30 minutes), promote model to broader rollout.
7) If any gate trips, mark canary as failed and escalate to evaluation owner + SRE.

Automated gate thresholds (default)
- anchor_semantic_delta_pct <= 2%
- anchor_confidence_drop >= 5% triggers manual triage
- p95_latency_delta_ms <= 20ms
- top-10-slice-degradation > 3% triggers failure

Rollback and remediation flow (triage playbook)
1) Automated rollback: canary-operator immediately routes traffic back to baseline variant and records the rollback event (run_id, triggered_gate, top failing probes).
2) Post-rollback triage steps (ordered):
   a) Capture failing probe set snapshot and delta metrics.
   b) Reproduce failure locally using probe-store seeds and evaluator-orch local-run mode.
   c) Check quantization/serving differences: kernel fallbacks, heterogenous device dispatch, and cache warming state.
   d) If failure is model-quality: run the regression triage checklist and notify applied-ml on-call.
   e) If failure is infra: route to SRE incident playbook (latency or memory errors).
3) Report: create a canary-incident ticket with attached artifacts: telemetry export, probe snapshots, provenance_sha, and privacy approval stamp.

Operational best practices and tips
- Canary window sizing: for multi-tenant shared fleets prefer shorter windows (1–2 hours) with repeated micro-canaries instead of one long run.
- Tenant selection: prefer hashed namespace selectors to avoid tenant identity in configs. Example selector: tenant_hash_mod(1024) in range [0..10) to pick ~1% of tenants.
