  1. If tenant_privacy_flag == true -> probe_type = synth if allowed by compliance policy, else skip.
  2. Compute volume_score = min(1, log10(weekly_request_volume+1)/5).
  3. Compute failure_score = clamp((week_over_week_failure_delta / baseline_failure_rate), 0, 10).
  4. TailScore = 0.6*failure_score + 0.3*(1-volume_score) + 0.1*slice_failure_contribution.
  5. Map TailScore to p with piecewise mapping:
     - TailScore >= 6 -> p = min(0.5, base_p * (1 + (TailScore-6)/10))
     - 3 <= TailScore < 6 -> p = min(0.2, base_p * (1 + (TailScore-3)/8))
     - TailScore < 3 -> p = base_p * 0.3
  6. base_p is a system-wide floor (default 0.01) configurable via sampler-config.
- Probe_type selection: if weekly_request_volume < 100 and privacy flag allows, prefer synth with probability 0.85.

Synth-probe generation rules:
- Input features used (non-identifying): request size histogram, token-length percentiles (10/50/90), endpoint mix distribution, common intent-tags (anonymized), response-length distribution.
- Privacy constraints: no raw user messages or PII allowed. All synth probes must be produced from aggregated and differentially-noised statistics (Laplace noise, epsilon=1.0 default).
- Probe schema (examples):
  - id: tspo-{tenant_id}-{YYYYMMDD}-{seq}
  - metadata: tenant_anon_bucket, endpoint_mix, token_profile, generated_seed_id
  - inputs: [priming_text_stub_1, priming_text_stub_2] (synthetic stubs derived from template library)
  - expected_metrics: p95_latency_range, coherence_score_target, rerank_accuracy_floor

Cost projection and budget gating (table):
| Item | Unit cost (tokens) | Expected units/week | Weekly cost est | Notes |
|------|--------------------:|---------------------:|----------------:|-------|
| Live-shadow probe | 0.00012 | 500 | $0.06 | full-fidelity model on Dedicated mesh
| Synth-probe (quant) | 0.00002 | 2,000 | $0.04 | quantized runtime via shadow-quant pool
| Batch eval compute | 0.00008 | 1,000 | $0.08 | nightly batch replay for aggregates
| TOTAL (example) | - | - | $0.18 | adjustable via orchestration rate-limits

Operational runbook (oncall action steps):
1. Alert trigger: Coverage SLO degrade (coverage < 95%) or projected monthly cost > 6% of eval budget.
2. Immediate actions:
   a. Open TSPO dashboard -> confirm affected tenant list and recent TailScore trends.
   b. If coverage degraded due to sampler regression, toggle sampler to "fallback-uniform" via sampler-config (CLI):
      - CLI: curl -X POST $SAMPLER_ADMIN/switch -d '{"mode":"fallback-uniform", "base_p":0.05}'
   c. If cost overrun predicted, reduce orchestrator throughput: PATCH /probe-orch/config {"max_rps": 0.1 * current}.
3. Escalation path: if toggles do not restore thresholds within 30 minutes, page ML-Platform oncall and include probe-registry manifest.

Monitoring and alerts:
- Key metrics to expose in Redwood Console:
  - tspo.coverage_ratio (per-slice, per-tenant) — alert if < 0.95 for 24h window.
  - tspo.projected_monthly_cost — warn at 80% of cost SLO, critical at 100%.
  - tspo.synth_quality_index (BLEU/coherence proxies) — degrade if synths diverge from small live-sample baseline by > 12%
  - tspo.sampler_decision_tail_variance — alert if variance jumps > 3x week-over-week.
- Dashboards: Sampling heatmap (tenant vs TailScore), Orchestrator throttle slider, Probe artifact registry viewer.

Rollout and safety gates:
1. Canary: pilot TSPO on a single service domain with 5% of tenants (mix of top, mid, tail) for 2 weeks.
2. Acceptance criteria for promotion:
   - No more than 0.5% increase in false-positive regression signals (measured by human-annotated checks)
   - Cost projection remains below 4% of monthly eval budget for the pilot domain
   - Synth-probe privacy audit completed by security (checklist item in Probe Registry record)
3. Gradual ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with at least 72 hours at each step to observe telemetry.

Troubleshooting common failure modes:
- Symptom: sudden spike in sampler_decision_tail_variance after sampler release.
  - Likely cause: configuration parameter change in base_p or feature skew.
  - Mitigation: revert to previous sampler-config tag, and run offline calibration against historical week.
- Symptom: synth_quality_index drop > 15%.
  - Likely cause: template library drift or incorrect noise parameters.
  - Mitigation: run synth-audit tool to compare synths to small live holdout and roll forward updated templates.

Ownership and contacts:
- Service owners:
  - sampler-tspo: maya.chen@redwood.com (owner)
  - synth-probe-gen: arjun.patel@redwood.com
  - probe-orch: sofia.morales@redwood.com
  - cost-estimator: infra-costing@redwood.com (team)
- Oncall rotation: ML-Platform Pager (see /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/pager-rotations).

Appendix A: Example CLI snippets
- Trigger a dry-run synth generation for tenant 0xabc:
  - curl -X POST $SYNTH_ADMIN/generate -d '{"tenant_id":"0xabc","dry_run":true}'
- Queue a probe batch via orchestrator (YAML example):
  - apiVersion: v1
    kind: ProbeBatch
    spec:
      tenant_bucket: tail-2025-q4
      batch_size: 200
      fidelity: quant
      schedule: "cron(0 3 * * MON)"

Appendix B: Sampler config (sampler-config.yaml) example
- base_p: 0.01
- max_live_fraction: 0.5
- synth_preference_threshold: 100
- noise_epsilon: 1.0
- cost_budget_percent: 0.06

Appendix C: Related artifacts and further reading
- Probe Registry: S3://probe-registry/tspo/ (index is internally accessible)
- Shadow mesh playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/shadow-to-prod-eval-continuity-guidelines-2026
- Privacy audit checklist: /confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/probe-privacy-checklist-2025

Change log:
- 2025-09-15 (Maya Chen): Initial draft and sampler algorithm proposal.
- 2025-11-12 (Arjun Patel): Added synth privacy noise defaults and CLI examples.
- 2026-01-20 (Sofia Morales): Finalized runbook steps, added cost projection table and rollout gates.

title: Cohort-driven Shadow Validation Playbook
content:
Overview:

This playbook describes a repeatable, cohort-driven approach to shadow (non-production) validation that combines traffic mirroring, cohort stratification, and statistical evaluation to detect drift, regressions, or QoE degradations before a model rollout. It is intended for use by ML Engineers, Product Reliability, and SRE when validating model variants (quantized models, finetunes, or new topologies) against real traffic slices.

Goals:
- Expose subtle, slice-specific regressions that aggregate metrics miss.
- Provide deterministic acceptance gates with clear thresholds and statistical tests.
- Keep validation cost-bounded by adaptive sampling and prioritized cohorts.

Scope and Non-Goals:
- Scope: live shadowing and replay for text-generation and embedding endpoints; cohort metrics for latency, token cost, response-stability, and semantic fidelity.
- Non-Goals: synthetic adversarial fuzzing (see separate fuzz playbook) and complete production failover automation.

Definitions:
- Shadow traffic: duplicated requests sent to a candidate model without impacting production responses.
- Cohort: a named subset of traffic defined by request attributes (customer_id, route, prompt-template, language, token_count, session_age).
- Response-stability-index (RSI): composite metric measuring output drift against baseline using embedding cosine similarity, edit distance, and semantic score.

When to run a cohort-driven shadow validation:
- Before a model promotion that affects >5% of production request volume.
- When introducing cross-workload optimizations (e.g., new quant profile, KV-cache changes, batch scheduling).
- After detecting slice-specific degradations in continuous telemetry.

Ownership and Roles:
- Requesting owner: Feature/Model owner (creates cohorts and success criteria).
- Shadow operator: SRE / Infra (sets up mirroring, monitors resource usage).
- Evaluator: Applied ML / Quality (runs statistical tests, interprets slice failures).
- Approver: Product owner or Reliability lead (approves promotion or rollback).

High-level Workflow (stepwise):
1) Define cohorts (3–10 per run):
   - Use historical telemetry to choose meaningful slices (high-value customers, long-context, multimodal inputs).
   - Example cohort definitions: "high-long-context-english" (tokens > 2048), "enterprise-integration-route" (route = /api/v1/generate && customer_tier = enterprise).
2) Choose sampling policy and budget:
   - Default: mirror 10% of cohort traffic for 72 hours or until 5,000 requests per cohort are collected, whichever comes first.
   - For sensitive cohorts, reduce to 1–2% with extended duration.
3) Configure shadow routing (example manifest):
   - Provide network-level mirroring rules and candidate endpoint. See appendix for JSON/YAML snippets.
4) Instrument telemetry and tagging:
   - Ensure every mirrored request is tagged with: cohort_id, shadow_run_id, baseline_model, candidate_model, sample_rate.
   - Log raw prompts, token counts, latency, final cost estimate (tokens * model_cost_rate).
5) Compute per-cohort metrics (real-time and batch):
   - Latency P95 and P99 (ms).
   - Token cost delta (%).
   - RSI (median per cohort) and drift fraction (percent responses with RSI < threshold).
   - Functional correctness checks: reranking loss, presence/absence of required fields for structured outputs.
6) Statistical evaluation and thresholds:
   - For continuous metrics (latency, cost): use bootstrap confidence intervals with 10k resamples. Gate if candidate P99 > baseline P99 + 20% and p < 0.01.
   - For semantic/fidelity metrics (RSI): require median RSI >= baseline median - 0.03 and two-sided Mann-Whitney U test p > 0.05.
   - For categorical regressions (required fields missing): Fisher exact test, require failure rate delta < 0.5 percentage points with 95% CI.
7) Adaptive triage and probe amplification:
   - If a cohort shows borderline failure (0.01 < p < 0.05), automatically increase sampling for that cohort by up to 5x for an additional 24 hours.
8) Runbook actions on failures:
   - Soft fail (slice flagged): pause promotion, notify owners, request focused remediation (prompt-tune, quant-fix, dataset augmentation).
   - Hard fail (critical customer slice degraded or functional correctness violated): immediate rollback path and incident creation.
9) Promotion decision and documentation:
   - Successful run: produce a validation artifact containing per-cohort summaries, raw probe examples (anonymized), and final decision. Attach to release ticket.

Metric and Alerting Configuration (table):
| Metric | Aggregation | Gate | Action on breach | Ownership |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Latency P99 | per-cohort | > baseline + 20% (p<0.01) | Pause promotion, trigger perf triage | SRE |
| Token cost delta | median % | > +15% | Cost review, consider quant profile | Finance/Feature owner |
| RSI median | median similarity | < baseline - 0.03 (MWU p<0.05) | Quality investigation, escalate | Applied ML |
| Required-field loss | failure rate | delta > 0.005 absolute | Immediate rollback for critical routes | Product |

Sampling and Budgeting Guidelines:
- Minimum sample per cohort for significance: 500 requests. If unavailable, mark cohort as "insufficient data" and schedule an extended run.
- Budget cap per run: token budget defined in run config (default 10M tokens). Operator may truncate tests if budget exhausted and annotate results.

Data Privacy and Redaction:
- Always redact PII before storing mirrored requests. Use the pipeline redaction rules: replace emails, SSNs, API keys, and long identifiers with deterministic tokens.
- For enterprise customers with confidentiality flags, request explicit authorization before mirroring; otherwise exclude those cohorts.

Operational Playbook (quick steps):
1) Create run ticket with cohort definitions and success criteria.
2) Request SRE to enable mirror manifest with run_id and sample_rate.
3) Confirm telemetry tags are present in the mirror stream.
4) Validate that baseline and candidate endpoints are reachable.
5) Monitor dashboards (per-cohort) for first 6 hours. If any hard fails occur, follow hard-fail incident checklist.

Promotions, Canary Integration and Rollout Path:
- If all cohorts pass: promote candidate to canary (5–10% production, canary duration 48–96 hours) with continuous cohort monitoring.
- If a small number of low-impact cohorts fail: consider targeted mitigations (prompt templates, per-route fallback) and rerun shadow validation.

Appendix A — Example Shadow Routing YAML:
```yaml
shadow_run_id: cohort-shadow-2025-09
mirror_rules:
  - route: /v1/generate
    sample_rate: 0.1
    cohorts: [high-long-context-english, enterprise-integration-route]
candidate_endpoint: https://shadow-candidate.internal:8443/generate
baseline_endpoint: https://prod-model.internal:8443/generate
storage: s3://redwood-shadow-archive/cohort-shadow-2025-09/
```

Appendix B — Example cohort SQL (for data-team):
```
SELECT request_id, customer_id, route, token_count, language, timestamp
FROM request_logs
WHERE token_count > 2048 AND language = 'en' AND timestamp BETWEEN '{{start}}' AND '{{end}}';
```

Appendix C — CLI snippets:
- Start run: redwood-shadow run start --id cohort-shadow-2025-09 --manifest ./shadow.yaml
- Increase sampling for cohort: redwood-shadow run update --id cohort-shadow-2025-09 --cohort high-long-context-english --sample-rate 0.5
- Archive results: redwood-shadow artifacts bundle --id cohort-shadow-2025-09 --out ./artifacts.tar.gz

Troubleshooting common issues:
- Low sample counts: increase sample_rate for affected cohorts, extend window, or create synthetic probe generator limited to the target cohort patterns.
- High resource usage on candidate host: coordinate with SRE to throttle mirror throughput or scale candidate pool; prioritize critical cohorts.
- Inconsistent telemetry tags: stop the run, patch instrumentation, and restart to ensure validity of per-cohort aggregates.

Audit and Reporting:
- Every shadow run must attach an artifact containing anonymized examples (<=100 per failed cohort), a per-cohort metric CSV, and the approval decision.
- Maintain a run index (spreadsheet or internal DB) with run_id, start/end times, outcome, and link to artifacts for 12 months.

Notes and rationale:
- Cohort-driven validation focuses our signal-to-noise on high-value slices rather than aggregate metrics that can mask regressions. Adaptive sampling reduces cost while enabling focused amplification where it matters. Statistical gates balance sensitivity and false positive rates to avoid unnecessary rollbacks.

Contact and escalation:
- Primary owner: Maya Chen (applied-ml)
- SRE shadow contact: Diego Alvarez
- On-call escalation: Pager duty "model-eval-oncall"

End of playbook.

title: Probe Curriculum and Adaptive Priority Scheduler
content:
Overview

This document describes the Probe Curriculum and Adaptive Priority Scheduler (PCAPS), a deterministic + stochastic scheduling layer for the eval-harness that prioritizes probes for continuous evaluation based on value (quality signal), cost, and reliability impact. PCAPS replaces the static TTL/fixed-priority queues with a curriculum-driven, budget-aware orchestrator to surface regressive or high-risk slices earlier while respecting eval budget and SLOs.

Goals
- Increase early detection rate for meaningful regressions (precision > 0.8 for P1 regressions in production-like shadow runs).
- Bound evaluator spend to a configurable daily budget while maximizing expected information gain.
- Smooth probe churn to avoid bursty load on the eval fleet and model-serving clusters.
- Provide transparent, auditable priorities and deterministic replay for postmortem triage.

When to use this document
- Onboarding new probe families into the evaluation mesh.
- Operationalizing continuous shadow or canary evals against a new model variant.
- Implementing cost-constrained, risk-focused probe sampling for private/dedicated deployments.

Scope and non-goals
- Scope: scheduling, scoring, and integration hooks into eval-orchestrator and probe-queue. Includes telemetry contract and rollout steps.
- Non-goals: model-side instrumentation, long-term labeling workflows, or annotator economics (see separate docs).

Architecture summary
- Components:
  - probe-fabricator: generates and mutates probe candidates from seed sets and telemetry anchors.
  - probe-priority-service: computes a score for each probe based on curriculum rules, risk signals, and cost model.
  - probe-queue: a tiered queue (hot, warm, cold) enforced by the scheduler.
  - eval-orchestrator: consumes probes from probe-queue and dispatches to evaluator workers.
  - backfill-manager: maintains probe budget and triggers historical replays.

Scoring function (design)
- Score(probe) = alpha * IG(probe) + beta * Risk(probe) - gamma * Cost(probe) + delta * FreshnessBoost
  - IG(probe): estimated information gain (expected reduction in uncertainty for target slices). Derived from historical detection rates and slice entropy.
  - Risk(probe): production telemetry signal (e.g., 95th-response-lag, error-rate spike probability, semantic-failure-probability).
  - Cost(probe): expected evaluator compute cost (tokens * model_cost_per_token * quant_penalty).
  - FreshnessBoost: a small time-decay bonus for recently observed production anomalies.
  - alpha/beta/gamma/delta are tunable per-curriculum profile.

Curriculum profiles
- Defensive (SLO-first): maximize Risk, high gamma to constrain cost. Use for mission-critical services.
- Exploratory (coverage-first): maximize IG, moderate gamma. Use for new-model onboarding.
- Cost-limited (budget-first): strong cost penalty and aggressive batching suggestions. Use for low-cost shadow environments.

Operational parameters (table)
- The table below lists default parameters used in prod rollout. Operators can override per-tenant or per-model.

Parameter | Default | Notes
---|---:|---
daily_eval_budget_usd | 1200 | Soft budget; backfill-manager enforces a hard cap with graceful pause.
hot_queue_capacity | 5k probes | Highest priority; targets P0/P1 signals.
warm_queue_capacity | 20k probes | For ongoing coverage and re-eval.
cold_queue_capacity | 200k probes | Low priority, best-effort sampling.
max_batch_tokens | 25k | Aggregation target used by probe-queue to group probes for efficient eval.
priority_decay_window_days | 7 | After this window, FreshnessBoost -> 0.
replay_retention_days | 90 | How long synthetic/historical probes are kept for deterministic replays.

Probe lifecycle (numbered procedure)
1. Fabrication: probe-fabricator creates candidate probes from seeds, telemetry anchors, and adversarial mutators. Each probe is annotated with metadata: seed_id, slice_id, telemetry_anchor, estimated_tokens, provenance_hash.
2. Scoring: probe-priority-service computes Score(probe) and assigns a TTL and suggested batch affinity.
3. Enqueue: probe is placed into hot/warm/cold tier according to score thresholds.
4. Dispatch: eval-orchestrator pulls from hot first, respecting batch and SLO constraints; warm as capacity allows; cold when spare budget exists.
5. Result ingestion: evaluator workers emit structured results (labels, evaluator_metrics, cost). backfill-manager updates cost ledger and recalculates IG for related probes.
6. Retire or recycle: probes are retired after exceeding retries or after replay_retention_days. Reuse is allowed for high-IG probes under a different model variant.

Priority thresholds (example)
- hot: Score >= 0.72
- warm: 0.35 <= Score < 0.72
- cold: Score < 0.35
Thresholds are configurable and should be tuned during the canary rollout (see rollout steps).

Telemetry contract (JSON schema described in text)
- Each evaluator result MUST include the following fields: probe_id, model_variant, tokens_consumed, evaluator_time_ms, label_set_id, confidence_estimate, failure_class (none|semantic|safety|latency|runtime), trace_id.
- Telemetry should be exported to eval-metrics-store with the tag set: {model:variant, env:shadow|canary|prod, tenant}.

Cost model examples (YAML)
- sample_cost_profile:
    model_cost_per_token_usd: 0.0000009
    quant_penalty: 1.15
    avg_tokens_expected: 180
    min_tokens_floor: 16

- sampler_config:
    budget_window: daily
    budget_usd: 1200
    prefer_batching: true
    batch_min_utilization: 0.6

Integration points
- eval-orchestrator: implements a single API endpoint POST /v1/probes/claim which accepts a max_tokens budget and returns a batch. The scheduler must honor this contract.
- shadow-sequencer: when shadowing live traffic, the probe-priority-service listens to anomaly hooks and boosts FreshnessBoost for related probes.
- probe-audit-log: every score change emits an audit entry to enable deterministic postmortem replay.

Runbook: incident scenarios and mitigation (short playbook)
1) Unexpected budget exhaustion mid-day
  - Trigger: backfill-manager emits budget_exhaustion alert.
  - Immediate action: switch scheduler to cost-limited curriculum (owner: eval-platform oncall).
  - If critical production regressions suspected: temporarily raise hot_queue_capacity and create a manual emergency queue with must-run probes.
2) Hot queue starvation (latency backlog)
  - Trigger: hot_queue_latency_p95 > 3 minutes for 10m window.
  - Action: throttle warm/cold dispatch, enable aggressive batching, and spin up ephemeral evaluator workers (runbook: eng-sre procedure).
3) Priority inversion (low-risk probes running before high-risk)
  - Trigger: audit logs show score misassignment for >100 probes in 1h.
  - Action: ingest audit logs to simulate scoring, run deterministic replay, roll back priority-service to previous release.

Failure modes and mitigations
- Overconfident IG estimates: enforce conservative floor to reduce weight on IG during first 48 hours of a new curriculum.
- Cost underestimation for quantized artifacts: add quant_penalty per model and monitor cost drift metric: quant_cost_ratio > 1.25 triggers mitigation.
- Probe duplication loops: dedupe by provenance_hash; if >3 duplicates in 1h, mark probe family as noisy and reduce fabrication rate.

Rollout plan (canary -> ramp)
1. Internal canary (week 0): enable PCAPS in eval-staging with 10% of the evaluator pool; validate scoring reproducibility with deterministic seeds. Acceptance criteria: no increase in eval latency p95 > 5% and IG uplift >= 15% vs baseline.
2. Shadow pilot (weeks 1–2): route 1% production anomalies into PCAPS; track detection lead-time and false positive rate.
3. Tenant pilot (weeks 3–6): enable cost-limited curriculum for 3 non-critical tenant projects; monitor budget adherence and ROI (regressions detected per $1k spent).
4. Full rollout (week 8): enable for all internal services; provide a toggle per-model for external tenants.

Promotion checklist
- Unit tests for scoring function and curriculum selection.
- Telemetry schema validated by eval-metrics-store team (schema id: eval.telemetry.v3).
- Load test: sustained 10k probes/minute ingestion with 95th latency < 500ms for scoring API.
- Security review for probe content (no PII in probes).

Observability and dashboards
- Score distribution dashboard: histogram by curriculum and model_variant.
- Budget burn-down: daily and rolling-7d with per-tenant drilldown.
- Probe churn report: fabricated vs retired vs recycled counts.
- Regression catch rate: ratio of detected regressions to total labeled failures per week.

Open questions and future work
- Multi-model joint probes: how to compute IG when a probe should be evaluated across many model families?
- Reinforcement-style curriculum updates: can we use evaluator outcomes to automatically tune alpha/beta/gamma?
- Pod-aware scheduling: incorporate hardware-aware batching benefits into Cost(probe) for TPU/GPU heterogeneity.

Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: Applied ML infrastructure (owner contact: aisha@redwood.ai).
- Oncall: eval-platform (pager duty: ENG-EVAL-PLT).
- Reviewers: Ravi Patel (Evaluation team), Marta Gomez (SRE).

Appendix: example CLI
- Claim a batch (developer flow):
  curl -X POST https://eval-orchestrator.internal/v1/probes/claim -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"max_tokens": 12000, "preferred_curricula": ["defensive"]}'

- Inspect a probe score:
  curl https://probe-priority-service.internal/v1/probes/score?probe_id=abc123

Appendix: deterministic replay snippet (pseudo-code)
- python replay.py --probe-ids path/to/probe_ids.txt --model model:canary-v42 --replay-window 2026-01-01:2026-02-01 --deterministic-seed 42

References and cross-links
- See eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026 for probe seed taxonomy.
- Related: quality-guardrails/response-stability-index-calibration-and-deployment-2026 for stability gating.

Document change log
- 2025-11-02: Created (Aisha Kapoor).
- 2026-01-18: Added cost model examples and updated daily budget defaults (Ravi Patel).
- 2026-02-14: Added production rollout acceptance criteria and deterministic replay snippet (Marta Gomez).

title: Annotator calibration for long-context streaming evals (playbook)
content:
Summary

This playbook describes the end-to-end process for calibrating human annotators used in long-context, streaming-style evaluations. It covers selection and priming of annotators, creation of streaming-specific judgment tasks, inter-annotator agreement (IAA) targets, drift detection, telemetry required, and automated remediation steps. The goal is to ensure that annotation quality meets the fidelity requirements of production-facing long-context features (e.g., multi-turn chat with >8k tokens, streaming function-calls, and KV-cache sensitive prompts).

Why this matters

- Long-context streaming evals amplify small annotation inconsistencies because judgments depend on earlier context and partially observed responses.
- Low annotator calibration increases variance in eval metrics and can mask regressions introduced by quantization, KV-cache changes, or prompt rewrites.
- Well-calibrated annotators reduce false-positive regression alerts and speed up triage in the regression playbooks.

Scope

- Applies to internal and partner annotation vendors used for streaming, long-context, and multi-turn eval workloads.
- Does NOT replace safety or legal review for user-sensitive data; see privacy-first-shadow-eval docs for sensitive pipelines.

Owners and escalation

- Ownership: Applied ML — Evaluations (primary), Runtime Reliability (secondary)
- Day-to-day steward: Ivy Chen (applied-ml)
- Escalation: If IAA falls below thresholds for two consecutive weekly sweeps, notify the Evaluations oncall and open an investigation ticket (SOP ID: EVAL-AUD-34).

Definitions and success criteria

- Judgement unit: A single streaming session fragment: includes the conversation prefix up to the turn, the partial response (possibly streaming), and the intended evaluation prompt instructions.
- IAA (Krippendorff's alpha for ordinal labels; Cohen's kappa for binary): Target >= 0.7 for ordinal 3+ labels, >= 0.8 for binary pass/fail for production slices.
- Annotator latency: Median annotation time per judgment unit \u003c= 75s for full 8k-token session fragments (instrumented).
- Drift window: 7-day rolling metrics. Significant drift if metric moves >2.5 standard deviations from baseline.

Prep: tooling and data setup

- Create streaming judgment tasks in the Evaluator UI with the following config fields:
  - session_id (string), prefix_tokens (int), response_stream_chunks (list), expected_behavior_tags (list), quality_sentinels (list).
- Telemetry to capture per judgment unit (minimum):
  - prefix_token_count, response_token_count, stream_chunk_count, chunk_interarrival_ms, annotator_id, annotator_latency_s, annotator_confidence_score, gold_label_id(optional), anchor_probe_flag.
- Provide annotators with a streaming playback widget that can: pause/replay by token range, show temporally-aligned function-call traces, and reveal metadata (model version, quantization profile, KV-cache state).

Calibration procedure (step-by-step)

1) Seed-phase (10 hours ceiling) — establish initial calibration:
   a) Select seed probe set: 500 judgment units across the top 10 production slices (mix of short, medium, long contexts).
   b) Each candidate annotator labels the full seed set.
   c) Compute IAA and per-slice confusion matrices.
   d) Pass criteria: overall IAA >= 0.7, no production slice IAA \u003c 0.6. Those who fail receive focused retraining and re-test on 100 new seed units.

2) Anchoring-phase (daily run, ongoing) — keep annotators anchored to golden examples:
   a) Inject 5–10% anchor probes each day (randomized) with previously adjudicated labels.
   b) Track anchor agreement by annotator (daily) and by slice (rolling 7-day).
   c) Auto-suspend annotator from live tasks if anchor agreement \u003c 85% in a rolling 48-hour window.

3) Drift detection and triage (weekly):
   a) Compute per-slice metrics: label distribution, average annotator confidence, median annotation time, anchor-agreement, and IAA.
   b) Flag slices with any of:
      - IAA drop \u003e= 0.1 absolute vs baseline,
      - anchor agreement \u003c 85%,
      - median annotator latency increase > 2x baseline (could indicate task confusion).
   c) Triage steps (ordered):
      1. Re-run a 100-probe adjudication on the flagged slice.
      2. If adjudicated labels disagree with current anchors, create a re-anchoring batch and notify steward.
      3. If disagreement is between annotators only, schedule focused retraining and a 50-probe retest.

4) Continuous quality regression guardrail (integration with eval harness):
   - For every model promotion or quantization change, require a shortform shadow evaluation against an anchored probe set (min 1,000 units) where annotator anchor agreement must remain within +/-2% of baseline.

Guidance for long-context specifics

- Context trimming: Provide explicit priming guidelines to annotators on how to mark relevance when past context exceeds 16k tokens; allow annotators to mark earliest token ranges they used when judging.
- Streaming partial-response judgments: Use a 3-stage label flow: preliminary-pass (after first N tokens), mid-pass (after chunk M), final-pass (full response). Capture timestamps and final label must be used for scoring.
- Function-call fidelity: Expose function-call traces inline; ask annotators to rate (0–2) fidelity of function semantics and argument completeness.

Example task template (JSON snippet)

{\n  "task_id": "stream-annot-0001",\n  "session_id": "s-53042",\n  "prefix_tokens": 6200,\n  "stream_chunks": ["chunk-1", "chunk-2", "chunk-3"],\n  "instructions": "Rate helpfulness (0-3) after full response. Mark if any earlier context changed your judgment.",\n  "anchors": ["anchor-123"]\n}

Automation and dashboards

- Required dashboards (Grafana/Looker):
  - Annotator Health: per-annotator anchor agreement trend, median latency, tasks_completed/day.
  - Slice Quality: per-slice IAA, label distribution delta, anchor coverage.
  - Shadow Promotion Gate: pass/fail for promotions; show detailed diff of anchor labels.

- Alerts (PagerDuty for Evaluations oncall):
  - P1: Overall test-suite IAA \u003c 0.65 for 24h -> create incident.
  - P2: Any production slice anchor-agreement \u003c 80% for 48h -> run triage playbook.

Adjudication and dispute workflow

1. If two annotators disagree on an anchor probe, route to an adjudicator (senior annotator) with context and both judgments.
2. Adjudicator records decision and rationale in the adjudication UI (required).
3. Update the anchor set if adjudicator verdict differs from current anchor; create re-anchoring job for impacted annotators.

Training materials and shrinkage planning

- Create a 60–90 minute calibration module covering: long-context priming, streaming playback usage, function-call traces, and example edge cases.
- Maintain a rolling pool of 1.5x annotators for critical slices to absorb shrinkage.

Rollout checklist for a new streaming eval (pre-launch)

1. Confirm instrumentation captures stream_chunk timestamps and annotator metadata.
2. Run seed-phase with at least 8 annotators and reach pass criteria.
3. Create anchor set (min 500 judged units) and enable automatic injection.
4. Configure dashboard and alerts.
5. Run a dry-run shadow promotion with a known-good model to validate guardrail thresholds.

Failure modes and mitigations

- Symptom: sudden spike in median annotation time. Mitigation: sample recent tasks and check for task UI regressions or unclear instructions.
- Symptom: IAA collapse only on very long contexts. Mitigation: split tasks into two judgment types (context-summarization + judgment) and re-assess.

Related artifacts and links

- Streaming playback widget design doc: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/streaming-playback-widget-design (internal)
- Anchor probe manifest schema: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/evaluator-interchange-format-and-federation-spec-2026
- Regression triage playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/model-regression-forensics-playbook-2026

Appendix: Minimal telemetry schema (CSV header)

session_id,prefix_token_count,response_token_count,stream_chunk_count,chunk_interarrival_ms,annotator_id,annotator_latency_s,annotator_confidence,label,anchor_flag,model_version,quant_profile

Contact

For questions or to request re-anchoring support, contact Ivy Chen (applied-ml) or file a ticket in the Evaluations backlog (component: eval-anchors).

Revision history

- 2026-01-12: Created (Ivy Chen)
- 2026-02-03: Added automation alerts and failure-mode mitigations (reviewers: Asha Gomez, Liam O'Neill)

title: Eval Fleet Prioritization and Probe TTL Policy
content:
Summary:

This document defines the Eval Fleet Prioritization and Probe TTL (time-to-live) Policy used by the eval orchestration system. It standardizes how probes (synthetic and live) are prioritized, how long they remain in active scheduling queues, and how allocation decisions are made when fleet capacity is constrained. The goal is to maximize coverage of high-risk slices while respecting cost, latency, and privacy budgets.

Scope:
- Applies to all eval jobs that run on the central eval fleet and shadow fleets used for Dedicated and Private onboarding.
- Covers probe prioritization signals, TTL semantics, eviction rules, allocation algorithm, and operator runbook steps.
- Does NOT change label taxonomy for probes or annotation contracts (see probe curation docs).

Motivation:
- Eval fleet capacity is finite and heterogeneous (GPU types, quantized vs FP16 runtime, CPU-only spot pools).
- Historically we observed probes starving critical slices during promotion windows and unnecessary retention of low-value probes that consume bookkeeping and storage.
- A standardized TTL + priority policy reduces noise, ensures rapid turnover during incidents, and enables reproducible promotion gating.

Principles:
1. Safety-first: safety, privacy and production regression probes always outrank exploratory probes.
2. Recency matters: more recent user-derived probes (telemetry anchors) get temporary priority boosts for 48–168h.
3. Cost-awareness: probes with high token budgets or heavy multimodal payloads should have explicit cost tags and limited parallelism.
4. Deterministic eviction: eviction must be explainable; use ranked signals to evict the lowest-value probes when capped.

Priority signals (ordered):
1) Safety / sentinel flag (boolean) -> highest priority
2) Production-impact score (0.0–1.0) computed from traffic fraction and severity mapping
3) Recency boost (hours since ingest) capped at 168h
4) Slice coverage delta (how many slices the probe uniquely covers)
5) Probe execution cost estimate (tokens * expected passes) — lower cost favored for equal score
6) Owner/team SLA (e.g., oncall vs research)

TTL semantics:
- Default TTLs (active scheduling window):
  - Sentinel probes (safety/regression sentinels): 90 days
  - Production-impact probes: 30 days
  - Telemetry-derived probes (live traffic seeds): 7 days (recency boost active for first 48h)
  - Exploratory/internally-generated probes: 3 days
  - Low-cost micro-probes (single-turn, <50 tokens): 1 day

- TTL behavior:
  - TTL starts at probe creation (ingest time).
  - When a probe is marked for "retention" by a reviewer, TTL is extended per retention policy (max 180 days) with audit fields recorded.
  - If a probe is executed successfully in the latest evaluation pass and is tagged by a failing-slice trigger, TTL is automatically extended by +14 days to allow follow-up annotations.

Eviction rules (queue-level):
1. Maintain per-device-class caps (e.g., A100 pool, T4 pool, CPU pool). Each cap defined in fleet config.
2. When cap exceeded, sort queued probes by composite priority score (see score calc). Evict lowest until under cap.
3. Evicted probes move to a short-lived tombstone (48h) where they can be reinstated by owner without re-ingest. After 48h they are archived and must be re-created.

Composite priority score (example formula):
score = 100 * safety_flag + 50 * production_impact + recency_boost + 10 * unique_coverage - cost_penalty - team_penalty

- "safety_flag" = 1 or 0
- production_impact in [0,1]
- recency_boost = max(0, 48 - hours_since_ingest) / 48 * 20 (for telemetry-derived probes)
- unique_coverage = integer count bounded to [0,3]
- cost_penalty = log(1 + estimated_token_cost) * 5
- team_penalty = 0 for oncall teams, 5 for research, 10 for external contractors

Allocation algorithm (high-level):
1. For each device class, maintain 3 priority queues: high, medium, low.
2. Periodically (every 30s) pop from high, then medium, then low until utilization target met or queues empty.
3. If utilization < target and high queue empty, migrate eligible medium -> high by dynamic boost (based on SLA windows).
4. Respect parallelism limit per probe (default 3 concurrent executions).

Example fleet config (YAML snippet):

fleet_caps:
  a100: 1200
  t4: 600
  cpu: 2000

default_ttls:
  sentinel: 90d
  production: 30d
  telemetry: 7d
  exploratory: 3d
  micro: 1d

queue_intervals:
  scheduling_tick_sec: 30
  tombstone_retention_h: 48

priority_weights:
  safety: 100
  production_impact: 50
  recency_scale: 20
  coverage_scale: 10
  cost_penalty_scale: 5
  team_penalty_defaults: "oncall:0,research:5,external:10"

Operational runbook (quick actions):
1. If the fleet reports sustained queueing > 5m for production-impact probes:
   a. Run `rbac eval-priority promote --tag production --duration 2h` to temporarily boost production queue.
   b. Notify oncall and escalate capacity additions (see capacity playbook).
2. If tombstone count grows > 10% of queued probes:
   a. Run `rbac probe-audit --since 7d --low-score` to identify low-value churn.
   b. Coordinate with probe owners to reduce re-ingestion.
3. For urgent safety sentinels failing in shadow:
   a. Pin the sentinel to an isolated high-priority pool: `fleet pin --probe-id <id> --pool safety-isolated`
   b. Extend TTL: `probe set-ttl --id <id> --days 14` and open a regression ticket.

SLOs and monitoring (recommended metrics):
| Metric | Target | Alert threshold | Owner |
|--------------------------------------------------------------|----------------|---------------------|-----------|
| median_probe_queue_wait | < 60s | > 300s for 5m | eval-platform-sre |
| pct95_production_probe_wait | < 120s | > 600s for 5m | eval-platform-sre |
| tombstone_ratio | < 0.05 | > 0.1 | eval-harness-product |
| avg_probe_execution_cost | baseline per workload | +50% delta vs baseline | cost-ops |

Data retention and audit:
- All TTL mutations, retention votes, and manual re-instantiations are recorded in the probe audit table (retention:audits) for 365 days.
- Archive policy: archived probes and payloads retained 540 days for internal reproducibility; after that payloads are sanitized and only metadata retained for 3 years.

Rollout and migration plan:
1. Stage 0 — Feature flag off (2 weeks): Simulate priority scoring in dry-run mode and emit metrics to `eval.priority.dryrun`.
2. Stage 1 — Soft enforcement (1 week): Enforce per-pool caps but do not auto-evict; instead notify owners of candidate evictions.
3. Stage 2 — Hard enforcement (2 weeks): Enable auto-evict and tombstone lifecycle.
4. Stage 3 — Monitoring-only extension (ongoing): After 1 month, evaluate thresholds and adjust TTLs.

Owner and contacts:
- Policy author: Liam Chen (Applied ML infra)
- Primary owner: eval-platform-sre@redwood.com
- Escalation: oncall-eval (PagerDuty)

FAQ (short):
Q: Can I request permanent retention of probes used in long experiments?
A: Yes, use the retention workflow in the probe UI. Requests are subject to audit and a maximum 180-day extension; exceptions require product approval.

Q: How are cost estimates computed?
A: Cost = tokens * passes * runtime_factor. The runtime_factor is derived from historical benchmark of the probe type and model variant.

Related pages and references:
- Probe scheduling and priority internals (internal link to code repo)
- Probe curation and annotation contracts
- Fleet capacity and scaling playbook

Change log:
- 2026-01-10: Initial draft created.
- 2026-01-28: Added tombstone lifecycle and retention extension rules after review.
- 2026-02-15: Finalized score formula and rollout plan; published.

Appendix: Example priority calculation (worked example)
- Probe A: sentinel=1, production_impact=0.8, hours_since_ingest=12, unique_coverage=2, estimated_token_cost=120, team=oncall
  score = 100*1 + 50*0.8 + (max(0,48-12)/48*20) + 10*2 - log(1+120)*5 - 0 = 100 + 40 + 15 + 20 - (log(121)*5)
  log(121)≈4.8 -> cost_penalty≈24 -> score≈151
- Probe B: sentinel=0, production_impact=0.6, hours_since_ingest=200, unique_coverage=0, estimated_token_cost=20, team=research
  score = 0 + 50*0.6 + 0 + 0 - log(21)*5 - 5 ≈ 30 - (3.04*5) -5 ≈ 30 - 15.2 -5 ≈ 9.8

This demonstrates how sentinels maintain a large margin over exploratory probes.

End of document.

title: Tenant Journey Fabricator and Labeling Pipeline — SUJG Spec
content:
Overview

This document defines the Tenant Journey Fabricator (SUJG — Synthetic User Journey Generator) and the downstream labeling pipeline used to produce high-quality, privacy-aware synthetic probes for long-tail coherence, context-fading, and multi-turn continuity evaluation. The SUJG is designed for per-tenant fidelity: it fabricates realistic multi-turn sessions that match a tenant's traffic fingerprint (intent distribution, mean-turn-length, context-repeats, entity density) without retaining PII. The output drives shadow evals, stress benches, and targeted annotation passes used during model onboarding, quantization validation, and regression triage.

Goals

- Provide reproducible, tenant-specific synthetic sessions that exercise coherence and memory failure modes at scale.
- Preserve privacy by design: no synthetic output should be reverse-engineerable to real user data.
- Produce labeled artifacts (gold/baseline, difficulty, failure-mode tags) that feed eval harnesses and automated triage.
- Support quantization-aware scenario generation so we can expose quant-induced degradation in realistic contexts.

Scope

Applies to: hosted, dedicated, and private evaluation pipelines. Not intended for generating production training data. This spec covers generation, anonymization, sampling weighting, labeling schema, storage/retention rules, and operational runbook for SUJG jobs.

Key Definitions

- Session: ordered list of turns (user + assistant) representing a multi-turn interaction.
- Fingerprint: statistical descriptor of tenant traffic (turn length distribution, intent mixture, token entropy, modal entities).
- Difficulty band: coarse label (easy/medium/hard) based on token ambiguity, required memory horizon, and branching factor.
- Quant scenario: parameter set for simulating quantized artifact (bitwidth, per-layer scheme, KV-cache perturbation profile).

Architecture Summary

1) Input: tenant fingerprint + seed set (non-sensitive templates) + sampling policy.
2) Generator: hybrid recipe combining template expansion, stochastic paraphrase model, and generative continuity seeding.
3) Anonymizer: differential-preserving redaction + entity-synthesis model that substitutes real tokens with synthetic analogs.
4) Augmentor: applies perturbations (typos, code formatting noise, multilingual fragments, context truncation) to produce robustness cases.
5) Labeler: heuristic + human-in-the-loop triage that assigns failure-mode tags and difficulty bands.
6) Export: artifacts published to eval-mesh and private shadow clusters per tenant.

Operational Config Table (example)

| Field | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| job_id | Unique scheduler id | sujg-2026-09-26-7321 |
| tenant_id | Tenant namespace | tenant-acme-corp |
| session_count | Total sessions to synthesize | 50,000 |
| mean_turns | Average turns per session | 6 |
| seed_templates | Template set label | helpdesk-FAQ-v2 |
| quant_scenarios | Quant scenario list | q8-hybrid,q4-neg10 |
| privacy_mode | anonymization level | strict (DP epsilon=0.5) |
| retention_days | Storage TTL | 30 |
| label_kickoff | Human review threshold | sample 0.5% or all failures |

Fingerprinting and Sampling Policy

- Fingerprints are computed from 30 days of tenant telemetry (requests sampled at 1%). Stored fingerprint fields: intent_histogram (top-20 intents), avg_token_length, pct_multilingual, mean_entity_count, context_reuse_rate.
- Sampling policy aims to allocate evaluation budget across: common (70%), rare-intent (20%), stress-scenarios (10%). Rare-intent and stress-scenarios are oversampled by a factor derived from the tenant's SLA-critical intent list.

Privacy and Anonymization

- All templates and seeds must be scrubbed of PII before consumption by SUJG. The anonymizer uses two steps: deterministic redaction (email, phone, SSN regex) then entity synthesis (replace with synthetic names, numerics, domains).
- Differential-privacy guardrail: aggregated outputs must satisfy DP target for tenant exposures. Default epsilon=0.5, delta=1e-6; configurable per-tenant by compliance.
- Local execution: for Private deployments the entire SUJG can run inside the customer's VPC. In-hosted mode, only fingerprint metadata (no content) leaves the tenant boundary.

Quantization-aware Scenarios

- Each session can be stamped with one or more quant scenario tags. The augmentor will simulate common quant failure modes: rounding noise on logits, KV-cache mismatch for long-context, softmax saturation drift.
- Example quant manifest (JSON snippet):

{"quant_scenario": "q8-hybrid", "per_layer_override": ["attn:8bit", "ffn:16bit"], "kv_noise_std": 0.002, "simulate_kv_eviction": true}

Labeling Schema

- Labels (single-turn and session-level): coherence_break, hallucination_entity, context_forgetting, repetition_loop, truncated_reasoning, formatting_loss, code_incorrectness.
- Difficulty score: 0-100 integer; derived deterministically from token ambiguity metrics + branching factor estimate.
- Human review buckets: auto-pass (confidence >= 0.95 & difficulty <= 20), sampled-check (0.6-0.95), full-review (confidence <= 0.6 or labeled failure).

Labeling Pipeline Steps

1) Auto-label: run deterministic heuristics + classifier model. Persist labels with confidence scores.
2) Sampling: pick sessions according to label_kickoff policy for human review. Use stratified sampling over difficulty bands.
3) Annotation: annotators use a guided UI showing session, model outputs (reference model + candidate model), quant scenario, and suggested labels.
4) Reconciliation: two annotators per item; disagreement sends to adjudicator.

Quality Gates and Promotion Criteria

- Per-tenant acceptance for model promotion to canary: degradation in labeled failure rate <= 1.5x baseline across top-10 intents, and median coherence index drop <= 6 points.
- Quant-fallback criteria: if q8 scenario increases critical intent failure rate by >3x, gate requires either rollout with reduced token budget OR fall back to higher-precision variant.

Integration Points

- Export format: NDJSON with fields [session_id, tenant_id, turns, labels, quant_scenario, difficulty, seed_template, fingerprint_tag]. Example line:

{"session_id":"s-0001","tenant_id":"tenant-acme","turns":[{"u":"How do I reset my password?","a":"To reset..."}],"labels":["coherence_pass"],"quant_scenario":"q8-hybrid","difficulty":12}

- Registry: SUJG jobs register with eval-mesh via /api/v1/sujg/register (POST). CLI example:

# register job
curl -X POST https://eval-mesh.internal/api/v1/sujg/register -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_KEY' -d '{"job_id":"sujg-2026-09-26-7321","tenant_id":"tenant-acme-corp"}'

Operational Runbook (operator steps)

1) Start a job
   - Submit fingerprint and seed_template set in the job UI or CLI. The system will estimate cost and required label budget.
2) Smoke test (minimum 100 sessions)
   - Validate anonymization (run SAMPLE_VALIDATION script)
   - Ensure no PII regex matches on export sample.
3) Ramp to full (progress 10% -> 50% -> 100%)
   - Monitor: generation throughput, label_confidence_histogram, failure_rate_by_intent.
4) Failure handling
   - If anonymizer flags >0.01% PII hits in sample, pause job and run redaction audit.
   - If human review disagreement > 20% in a day, reduce auto-label confidence threshold and re-run sampling.
5) Completion
   - Export NDJSON to secure bucket, notify eval-mesh, trigger shadow-scheduler to replay sessions against candidate models.

Monitoring and Alerts

- SLOs for SUJG job: job completion within SLA = 48h for up to 100k sessions (target 95th percentile).
- Key metrics to instrument: sessions_per_minute, anonymizer_pii_hits, label_confidence_median, human_disagreement_rate, quant_failure_delta_by_intent.
- Pager thresholds (example): anonymizer_pii_hits_rate > 0.0001 => pager to Privacy Eng; human_disagreement_rate > 0.2 => alert to QA leads.

Failure-mode Triage Template

1) Capture: job_id, sample session_id(s), tenant_id, quant_scenario, label set.
2) Reproduce: run session through local generator seeded with seed_id and fingerprint snapshot.
3) Isolate: toggle anonymizer, toggle augmentor perturbations, compare outputs.
4) Root cause hypotheses: seed leakage, paraphrase model hallucination, classification drift, quant-noise amplification.
5) Remediation: tighten redact regex, expand seed templates, retrain auto-label classifier, add quant-stability probe to eval harness.

Ownership and Contacts

- SUJG service owner: Asha Patel (eng-applied-ml). Pager: eng-applied-ml-oncall.
- Labeling operations: Sophie Nguyen (annotation-leads).
- Privacy guardrail contact: Daniel Park (security & privacy).

Appendices

A. Seed template example (YAML)
---
- id: helpdesk-001
  description: common password reset flow
  user_prompts:
    - "I forgot my password"
    - "How do I change my password?"
  expected_slots: [account, method]
---

B. Sample anonymizer regexes
- email: /[a-z0-9._%+-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+\.[a-z]{2,}/i
- phone: /\b(\+?\d{1,3}[- .]?)?(\d{3}[- .]?){2}\d{4}\b/

C. Quick CLI snippets
# run local generator for tenant fingerprint snapshot\python -m sujg.run --tenant tenant-acme-corp --seed helpdesk-001 --count 500 --out sample.ndjson

# validate anonymization sample
cat sample.ndjson | python -m sujg.validate_anonymization --pii-regex-list defaults.txt

D. Change log
- 2025-09-15: initial spec (Asha Patel).
- 2025-11-02: added DP guardrail and quant scenario schema (Marco Liu).
- 2026-02-04: revised labeling buckets and runbook thresholds (Sophie Nguyen).

Related pages and references

- Eval mesh schema reference: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/evaluator-interchange-format-and-federation-spec-2026
- Privacy & annotation retention: /applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails/probe-privacy-budget-and-annotation-retention-playbook-2024

End of document

title: Latency-Quality Slice Optimizer Playbook
content:
Overview

Purpose
- Provide a repeatable, slice-driven evaluation and promotion workflow that balances latency SLOs and output quality when deploying quantized or heterogeneous model variants.
- Reduce regressions by combining targeted slice benchmarking, telemetry contracts, and automated gating.

Scope and audience
- Applies to model onboarding, private and dedicated deployments, and hosted canary rollouts.
- Intended for ML engineers, serving runtime owners, SREs, and product owners.

Definitions
- slice: a named subset of production traffic grouped by intent, length, or feature flags.
- latency SLO: 95th percentile server-side model generation latency budget for a route.
- quality delta: measured expected change in task-specific metric vs baseline model.

Key SLOs and thresholds
- Global production latency SLO: p95 <= 180 ms for interactive text routes.
- Quantized candidate guardrail: quality delta <= 2.5% relative drop on primary slice metric OR absolute metric delta defined per slice.
- Regression alarm: any slice with quality drop > 5% or p95 latency increase > 30% triggers immediate rollback.

Slice catalog (example)
- onboarding-guidance: short instruction following prompts, expected median tokens 12. Primary metric: accuracy@top1.
- long-context-support: multi-turn doc summarization, median tokens 1200. Primary metric: coherence score.
- embeddings-search-q: short queries for vector similarity, median tokens 8. Primary metric: embedding cosine stability.
- api-batch-worker: high-throughput noninteractive batch calls. Primary metric: throughput and tail latency.

Telemetry and signals required
1) Per-slice quality metrics (task metric, confidence distribution, top-k disagreement).
2) Per-slice latency histogram and p50/p95/p99.
3) Token economy: generation tokens and input tokens per request.
4) Feature tags: model variant id, quant profile id, hardware type, route id.
5) Drift indicators: prompt fingerprint rate change, anchor-response divergence.

Evaluation harness configuration examples
- When adding a new candidate, create a harness job with the following attributes:
  - deterministic seed sets for 3 replicate runs
  - slice weightings matching production traffic fractions or importance weights
  - synthetic amplification for rare slices until N=500 example coverage

YAML snippet for an eval job (illustrative)
```
job_name: latency_quality_slice_eval
model_variant: candidate-v2
replicates: 3
slices:
  - name: onboarding-guidance
    weight: 0.35
  - name: long-context-support
    weight: 0.25
  - name: embeddings-search-q
    weight: 0.25
  - name: api-batch-worker
    weight: 0.15
metrics:
  - name: primary_task_metric
    compare: relative
  - name: p95_latency_ms
    compare: absolute
augmentation:
  rare_slice_min_examples: 500
```

Promotion gating and automated policy (high level)
1. Run harness with baseline model and candidate concurrently. Produce per-slice report with confidence intervals and p95 latency.
2. Apply gate rules in order: safety checks -> latency gates -> quality gates -> cost appreciations.
3. If all gates pass, schedule canary rollout with 5% traffic for 4 hours and expanded telemetry retention.
4. If any gate fails, run targeted regression triage (see Runbook) and block promotion until triage resolves causes and a new candidate is evaluated.

Gate examples
- Safety checks: zero high-severity safety sentinel hits across 3 replicates.
- Latency gate: p95(candidate) <= max( p95(baseline) * 1.15, absolute_slo )
- Quality gate: per-slice primary_task_metric delta >= -2.5% for critical slices, >= -5% for noncritical slices.

Regression triage runbook (summary)
1. Triage kickoff: create incident in tracker, tag model id and quant profile. Notify owner_team and oncall.
2. Reproduce: run harness with failing slice example set and deterministic seed. Capture full token-level diffs and KV-cache traces.
3. Isolate: compare candidate vs baseline on short micro-benchmarks: 1) tokenizer alignment, 2) decoding detokenized mismatch, 3) top-k logit shifts.
4. Test hardware sensitivity: replay eval on alternate device types and with and without kernel fallback.
5. If quantization suspected: run full-precision shadow and mixed-precision variants to narrow failure mode.
6. Repair options: prompt rewrite, quant profile relax, small fine-tune, or rollback. Document chosen remediation path and validation evidence.

Runbook snippets and CLI examples
- Trigger a slice evaluation run: rci eval run --job latency_quality_slice_eval --model candidate-v2 --slices onboarding-guidance,long-context-support
- Fetch per-slice report: rci eval report --job-id 0xabc123 --format table
- Promote to canary: rci rollout create --model candidate-v2 --percent 5 --duration 4h --observability retention=72h

Operational best practices
- Keep slice definitions small and orthogonal: prefer intent-based slices over ad hoc query buckets.
- Maintain a slice ownership map and ensure one owner per slice.
- Refresh rare-slice seed sets monthly or when production distribution changes > 10%.
- Archive long-context examples with token boundaries and session context to enable deterministic replay.

Ownership and escalation
- Playbook owner: Applied ML Eval Platform team (contact: maya.chen@redwood.ai).
- Primary oncall: eval-platform-sre rotation.
- Escalation: after 30 minutes unresolved, escalate to runtime-performance team lead and product owner.

References and related artifacts
- See evaluation orchestration policy and quant profile synthesis doc in related pages for integration details.
- Repository: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness (eval job templates and YAML schemas).

Change log
- 2026-01-18: initial draft and adoption for Q1 model promotions.
- 2026-02-12: tightened latency gate formula and added rare slice amplification guidance.

Appendix: example slice acceptance table
- For each slice provide: slice_name, primary_metric, acceptance_threshold, p95_latency_threshold, owner. Maintain this table in the slice registry.

End of document

title: Confidence Calibration and Annotator-Anchoring Feedback Loop Protocol
content:
Overview

This document defines the Confidence Calibration and Annotator-Anchoring Feedback Loop Protocol (the "protocol") for Redwood Inference evaluation pipelines. The protocol standardizes how model-assigned confidence scores are calibrated, how annotator reference anchors are created and maintained, and how automated relabel/recalibration triggers propagate into the eval-harness and production monitoring. The goal is to keep measured quality aligned with customer-facing uncertainty estimates and enable automated, auditable adjustments to evaluation labels and thresholds.

Audience
- Applied ML engineers
- Evaluator/operators
- QA and annotation leads
- Model onboarding owners

Motivation
- Models often report uncalibrated logits that misrepresent real-world correctness probabilities, causing mis-routed fallbacks and incorrect SLO decisions.
- Annotator judgments drift over time; we need conservative anchoring to maintain consistent ground truth while allowing controlled updates.
- Automated relabeling with poor controls can silently degrade eval quality; the protocol enforces checks, telemetry gates, and human review windows.

Key definitions
- Confidence score: normalized [0,1] probability output attached to a response or label.
- Anchor set: a curated subset of labeled examples used as stable reference for annotator decisions.
- Calibration transform: the mapping applied to raw model scores (e.g., temperature scaling, isotonic regression).
- Recalibration window: a time-bounded batch of data used for recalibration; default = 7 days.

High-level flow
1) Ingest: live/prod-sampled telemetry routed into the eval-harness with metadata (route, model_version, prompt_shard, token_count, response_id).
2) Score bucketing: responses bucketed into deciles of raw score and further stratified by slice (language, length, intent).
3) Anchor sampling: select per-slice anchor candidates (see Anchor selection rules).
4) Annotate & adjudicate: anchors are double-annotated and adjudicated; results persist to the anchor registry.
5) Calibration fit: for each model_version+slice, fit candidate calibration transforms and compute calibration metrics (ECE, Brier, calibration curves).
6) Gate & deploy: if transforms improve ECE by >= 15% and do not reduce recall on safety sentinel slices by > 1%, they are promoted following the Rollout policy.
7) Continuous monitoring: live checks compare predicted confidence vs. anchor-derived empirical frequency; drift beyond thresholds triggers a recalibration investigation ticket.

Anchor selection rules
- Size: target 2k examples per major slice (language x intent), minimum 250 for low-volume slices.
- Staleness: anchors older than 90 days must be reviewed before use.
- Diversity: anchors must cover top 10 tokens length deciles and include at least 10% adversarially generated probes.
- Ownership: each anchor set has an owner (applied-ml engineer or annotation lead).

Calibration methods and recommended defaults
- Temperature scaling (TS): fast baseline; recommended first-step.
- Isotonic regression (IR): non-parametric; use when TS residuals are large and sample size > 1000.
- Platt scaling: logistic variant for binary-convertible tasks.
- Dirichlet calibration: for multi-class probability vectors where class-count > 5.
- Ensemble calibration: blend transforms across time windows for smoother behavior.

Recommended default pipeline (YAML example)
config: |
  pipeline:
    sample_rate: 0.01  # 1% production sampling or min 5000/day
    recalibration_window: 7d
    calibration_methods: ["temperature_scaling","isotonic_regression"]
    anchor_target_per_slice: 2000
    ece_improvement_threshold: 0.15
    safety_recall_drop_threshold: 0.01
  outputs:
    promoted_transform_registry: "/eval/calibration/transforms"
    anchor_registry: "/eval/anchors"

Metrics and thresholds
- ECE (expected calibration error): primary metric. Target: ECE <= 0.03 for high-volume slices, <= 0.06 for low-volume.
- Brier score: auxiliary check for probabilistic fidelity.
- Reliability diagrams: visual artifacts retained for 180 days.
- Anchor stability index (ASI): fraction of anchor labels unchanged after re-annotation; target > 0.92.
- Drift signal: 3-sigma deviation in predicted vs empirical frequencies across three consecutive windows triggers investigation.

Rollout policy (promotion steps)
1) Dry-run: candidate transform applied to a 0% production dry-run traffic but evaluated in the eval-harness; compare metrics.
2) Shadow deploy: apply transform within shadow-routing path for 2–3 days; measure downstream decision differences.
3) Canary: route 1–5% real traffic; require metric checks to hold for 48h.
4) Gradual ramp: 5→25→100% over 24–72h with automatic abort on metric regression.

Human-in-the-loop and automated relabeling
- Automated relabeling allowed only if all of: anchor ASI >= 0.95, model_version stable for 14+ days, and adjudicated sample passes QA audit.
- When automated relabel occurs, create audit entry: {response_id, old_label, new_label, reason, evidence_anchor_ids, operator}.
- All automated relabels appear for 7 days in the annotation review queue for spot checks.

CLI examples
- Export candidate anchors for a slice:
  rdl eval export-anchors --model v2.3 --slice "en+intent:faq" --out anchors.csv
- Fit temperature scaling on anchors:
  rdl eval fit-calibration --method temperature --anchors anchors.csv --out transform_v2.3_ts.json
- Simulate promotion impact:
  rdl eval simulate-promotion --transform transform_v2.3_ts.json --metrics ece,brier --window 7d

Operational runbook (short)
- Trigger: alert CALIBRATION_DRIFT_HIGH fires.
- Initial responder: applied-ml oncall (pager).
- Actions:
  1) Triage alert dashboard; confirm which slice(s) exceeded threshold.
  2) Pull recent anchors and run fit-calibration locally; note deltas in ECE.
  3) If automated transform candidate passes gates, open rollout ticket and follow Rollout policy.
  4) If anchors show ASI < 0.9, pause automated relabeling and open annotation audit.
  5) Document actions and mark incident for postmortem if remediation > 12h.

Governance and ownership
- Applied-ML team: maintain calibration code and transform registry.
- Annotation team: maintain anchor registry and adjudication process.
- Observability: provide dashboards and daily health checks.
- Security: review anchor exports for PII; exports must be scrubbed per data-management policy.

Appendix: audit table (example columns)
- response_id | model_version | raw_score | calibrated_score | anchor_id | label_before | label_after | annotators | adjudicator | audit_reason | timestamp

Notes and caveats
- Calibration on synthetic/staged traffic may not generalize to production customer prompts — always validate on production-sampled anchors.
- For heavy-tailed score distributions, consider stratified isotonic fits to avoid overfitting high-score regions.
- Changes to scoring that affect user-facing behavior must coordinate with Product (change advisory).

Related artifacts and links
- Calibration dashboard: /dashboards/eval/calibration-overview
- Anchor registry UI: /tools/anchors
- Eval-harness CLI repo: git@redwood:eval-harness.git

Revision history
- 2025-11-12: created by Sofia Kwan
- 2025-12-04: added automated-relabel governance (reviewer: Diego M. Alvarez)
- 2026-02-03: adjusted ECE thresholds and rollout timing after field trial (reviewer: Priya Nair)

title: Ensemble evaluation orchestration and weighting guidelines
content:
Overview
=======

Purpose
-------
This document specifies a standard for orchestrating ensemble-style evaluations in Redwood's eval harness. It covers how to configure multi-metric evaluation jobs, how to compute a single acceptance score from heterogeneous metrics, recommended weighting strategies, and the operational rules used for model acceptance, canary rollouts, and automated rollback triggers. The goal is consistent, explainable production decisions across different product use-cases (chat, summarization, reranking, embeddings).

Background and motivation
-------------------------
Teams frequently need to combine multiple eval signals (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE-like n-gram overlap, semantic similarity, safety pass rate, latency percentiles) into a single decision for model promotion or rollback. Without a standard approach:
- teams create ad-hoc weights that are hard to justify
- comparisons across workloads are inconsistent
- drift or slice regressions are missed when only aggregate metrics are considered

Scope
-----
This guide applies to:
- All evaluation jobs run through eval-harness-runner and eval-orch services.
- Post-training checks that feed Redwood Optimize and model-onboarding pipelines.
- Production acceptance gates tied to rollout automation in the deployment orchestration layer.

Terminology
-----------
- eval job: a single run that produces a set of metrics for a model version on a prompt set.
- slice: an orthogonal data subset (e.g., low-resource queries, long-contexts, legal-phrasing).
- metric vector: the set of scalar metrics produced by one eval job.
- ensemble score: a normalized, weighted aggregation of metrics used for acceptance decisions.

High-level orchestration
-----------------------
1) Eval job submission: developers submit an eval job YAML to eval-orch. Jobs declare model id, dataset id, slices, metrics, and desired aggregations.
2) Parallel runners: eval-harness-runner scales horizontally to execute slices in parallel. Per-slice results are written to metric-store with a unique job id.
3) Post-processing: a standardized post-processing step normalizes raw metrics, computes slice-level z-scores or bounded transforms, and produces the ensemble score.
4) Decision hooks: the ensemble score is compared against the configured acceptance matrix (thresholds and weights). If the score passes, the model progresses to canary rollout; otherwise it triggers triage.

Orchestration diagram (text)
---------------------------
- user -> eval-orch -> queue (kafka) -> runner pool -> metric-store (timeseries + artifacts) -> postproc -> decision-service -> deployment-orch

Weighting and aggregation strategies
----------------------------------
We provide three canonical strategies. Choose the simplest that satisfies your product requirements; prefer reproducibility over complexity.

1) Equal-weight normalized aggregation (default)
- Use when metrics are commensurate after normalization (e.g., all are percentages or bounded scores).
- Steps: compute per-metric min/max clipped to historical percentiles (5th/95th), rescale to [0,1], average.
- Pros: simple, transparent.
- Cons: can under- or over-emphasize rare but critical metrics.

2) Priority-weighted aggregation
- Use when one metric is safety-critical (e.g., toxicity, hallucination rate).
- Steps: assign integer priority weights (example: safety=5, accuracy=3, latency=1), normalize weights to sum to 1, compute weighted sum of normalized metrics.
- Documentation: every priority weight must have an author and justification recorded in the eval job metadata.

3) Dynamic frequency-weighted aggregation (recommended for customer-facing embeddings/reranking)
- Use when production slice frequencies differ significantly from training/test distributions.
- Steps: estimate slice frequencies from production telemetry (last 30 days), compute per-slice weight proportional to frequency, and combine slice-level metric aggregates into a global metric before normalization.
- Important: frequency estimates are clipped to [0.01, 0.5] per slice to avoid domination by a single slice.

Normalization and transforms
---------------------------
We standardize on the following transforms before aggregation:
- bounded metrics in [0,1] (no transform)
- unbounded error metrics (e.g., MSE): apply inverse transform 1/(1+log(1+value)) then rescale to [0,1]
- latency percentiles: map P50/P95 to score = 1 - min(latency / latency_slo, 1) (SLOs stored in product-config)
- safety/failure rates: use 1 - rate so higher is better
- For metrics with heavy tails, use winsorization at 99th percentile prior to normalization

Scoring formula (canonical)
--------------------------
Given normalized metrics m_i in [0,1] and weights w_i that sum to 1:
ensemble_score = sum_i w_i * m_i

When combining slices, compute slice_score_j first (per-slice aggregation across metrics), then global_score = sum_j slice_weight_j * slice_score_j where slice_weight_j is chosen per weighting strategy.

Config examples
--------------
Example eval job YAML (submit to eval-orch):

---
job_name: "chat-v2-ensemble-eval"
model_id: "m-redwood-chat-v2-2026-03"
dataset_id: "chat-production-sim-2026-01"
metrics: ["semantic-similarity", "toxicity_rate", "response_length_variance", "p95_latency_ms"]
slices: ["all", "long_context_>2048", "low_english_proficiency"]
weighting_strategy: "dynamic-frequency"
weights: {} # optional for dynamic; required for priority-weighted
postproc:
  normalization: "percentile-clip-5-95"
  latency_slo_ms: 150
notify_on_fail: ["ml-evals@redwoodeval.internal"]
---

Example postproc snippet (pseudo-YAML) for priority-weighted:

weights:
  semantic-similarity: 0.4
  toxicity_rate: 0.4
  p95_latency_ms: 0.2
normalization: "1/(1+log(1+value))"

Acceptance matrix and thresholds
--------------------------------
Acceptance matrices must be checked into model-onboarding metadata and include:
- minimum safety pass rate by slice (e.g., safety >= 0.995 on all slices),
- global ensemble_score threshold (default 0.82),
- latency SLO tolerances (P95 <= configured SLO),
- allowed per-metric regressions from baseline (e.g., no more than 2% drop in semantic-similarity).

Default baseline policy (applies if team does not provide custom matrix):
- safety pass rate >= 0.998 on all slices
- ensemble_score >= 0.80
- no metric regressions > 3% compared to production baseline
- canary rollout limited to 5% traffic for 48 hours with monitoring hooks

Canary and rollback rules
------------------------
Canary rollout: on pass, deployment-orch will deploy model to canary cluster at 5% traffic. During canary the following automated checks run every 15 minutes:
- Production sampler run: compare online metrics with eval predictions for a random sample of requests (1 per 1000 requests or at least 1000 samples/day).
- Alert conditions: ensemble_score drop > 0.05 vs baseline OR safety failure spike > 0.01 absolute OR P95 latency increase > 25% -> trigger rollback.

Automated rollback sequence (executed by deployment-orch):
1) Pause canary traffic.
2) Demote model from canary and switch traffic to previous stable model.
3) Create incident and assign to on-call owner of model-service (see runbooks).
4) Persist failing eval artifacts and logs under job id for triage.

Regression triage flow
---------------------
1) Triage owner reviews per-slice deltas and pulls failing examples (eval-harness provides direct links).
2) If failure is dataset-related (label drift), tag dataset and schedule augmentation.
3) If failure is model-related (systematic hallucination/safety), open ModelRegression ticket with: baseline artifacts, counterexamples, per-slice metrics, and suggested mitigation (prompt tuning, quantization rollback, smaller context window).
4) For performance regressions, check runtime config (quantization profile, batching settings) and revert to last-known-good profile if needed.

Operational considerations and do's/don'ts
----------------------------------------
Do:
- Record weight justifications in job metadata.
- Use production frequency data for dynamic weighting when available.
- Always include safety metrics as separate slices (do not absorb safety into a single aggregate without explicit weight).
- Keep acceptance matrices in model-onboarding for auditability.
Don't:
- Hard-code weights in deployment scripts without provenance.
- Use raw latency numbers directly without mapping to SLO-based scores.
- Rely solely on aggregate scores; always require per-slice checks for safety and critical business slices.

Metrics and observability
------------------------
- metric-store: stores per-job, per-slice metrics with job_id and model_id tags.
- dashboards: ensemble-over-time, per-slice-breakdown, canary-sampler-comparison.
- alerts: configured in deployment-orch and routed to ml-evals and eng-sre channels.

Ownership and SLAs
------------------
- Eval orchestration (eval-orch, runner): team = applied-ml (owner: Priya Menon).
- Post-processing & scoring library: team = applied-ml, SLAs for processing of a single job <= 30 minutes for medium datasets (<=100k examples).
- Decision-service and deployment hooks: team = eng-platform.

Required artifacts for onboarding a new model using ensemble evals
----------------------------------------------------------------
- eval job YAML and historical weight justifications (checked into model PR)
- acceptance matrix (JSON) checked into model-onboarding metadata store
- baseline production metrics snapshot (timestamped)
- list of critical slices and slice definitions

Appendix: example of normalized score calculations
------------------------------------------------
Given metrics: semantic_sim=0.78 (higher better), toxicity_rate=0.002 (lower better), p95_latency_ms=120 (SLO=150)
Transform toxicity: 1 - toxicity_rate = 0.998
Transform latency: 1 - min(120/150, 1) = 0.2
Assume weights [0.5, 0.3, 0.2] -> ensemble_score = 0.5*0.78 + 0.3*0.998 + 0.2*0.2 = 0.39 + 0.2994 + 0.04 = 0.7294

Links and references
--------------------
- eval-harness-runner README: internal link (eval-harness-runner)
- model-onboarding checklist: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/production-model-certification-checklist-2026
- regression triage playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/model-regression-forensics-playbook-2026

Contact and escalation
----------------------
For questions about weighting strategy or to request new slice definitions, open an issue in the Applied-ML backlog and assign to the evals owner (Priya Menon). For production incidents related to canary rollouts, follow eng-sre oncall escalation documented in: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/oncall-escalation.

Change log
----------
- 2026-02-15: initial published draft by Priya Menon.
- 2026-03-01: clarified dynamic weighting clipping rules; added default baseline policy.

title: Probe Reshaper and Quant-Routing Manual
content:
Summary

This document defines the Probe Reshaper component of the Eval Harness: a runtime subsystem that transforms incoming evaluation probes (prompt + context bundles) to improve stability under mixed-quant deployments while preserving privacy constraints and probe fidelity. The Reshaper sits in the eval ingress path and cooperates with the Quant Routing policy engine to decide target variants (fp16, q4, q8_0, etc.), prompt rewrites, and when to fall back to higher-fidelity evaluation.

Goals

- Reduce false-positive regressions caused purely by quantization-induced prompt sensitivity.
- Maintain probe privacy (avoid leaking tenant metadata) during on-host transformations and routing decisions.
- Provide deterministic, auditable transformations so eval results are reproducible.
- Minimize additional latency and token-cost overhead across the eval fleet.

Scope and Non-Goals

- In scope: runtime probe normalization, token-level rewrite heuristics, routing decisions to quantized artifact variants, per-probe fidelity annotations, audit logging and provenance metadata.
- Out of scope: model training, core quantizer development, human annotation workflows (except where annotations are needed for rollback debugging).

Terminology

- Probe: an evaluation input consisting of prompt text, metadata (tenant_id, slice_id), and optional attachment(s).
- Reshaping: a deterministic transformation applied to a probe (canonicalization, priming normalization, token-preserving rewrites).

Design overview

1) Ingress flow (high level):
- EvalOrchestrator -> ProbeReshaper -> QuantRoutingPolicy -> ShadowDispatcher -> Runner (target variant)

2) Two-layer decision model:
- Static eligibility checks (probe size, tenant opt-outs, confidentiality flags).
- Dynamic sensitivity estimation (fast SIMD tokenizer pass + learned sensitivity model) that assigns a QuantRiskScore.

Probe Reshaper responsibilities

- Canonicalize whitespace, normalize non-semantic Unicode (NFKC), and normalize date/time mentions into token-short forms when appropriate.
- Apply deterministic priming compression for long-context probes using the PrimingCompact pattern (keeps anchors and last N-turns intact).
- Execute token-preserving obfuscation for tenant-identifying strings (email, org names) when tenant requests privacy gating. Obfuscation is reversible only within the audit enclave (KMS-protected key) and replaced with a stable placeholder for the runner.
- Emit a provenance blob: {reshaper_version, seed, deterministic_hash, transformations_applied} appended to probe metadata for downstream reconciliation.

Quant Routing policy

Routing decisions are the joint output of: static rules, quant risk score, and traffic cost budget. The routing policy maps to target variant IDs and optional fidelity gates (e.g., force high-fidelity when a quality probe fails).

Policy matrix (example)

| QuantRiskScore | ProbeLengthTokens | TenantTier | RouteRecommendation |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 0-0.15 | <512 | any | q8_0 (fast) |
| 0.15-0.45 | <1024 | standard | q4 + priming-compact |
| 0.45-0.80 | any | standard | shadow-first: run on q8_0 with synchronous high-fidelity replay on fp16 if variance > threshold |
| >0.80 | any | enterprise | fp16 (no quant) |
