This blueprint defines a production-ready system for dynamically scoring and synthesizing evaluation probes ("probes") across the eval-harness. The goal is to prioritize limited human annotation and synthetic probe generation capacity toward probes that maximize signal for quality regressions, quantization fragility, latency-related failures, and customer-impacted slices.

Motivation
----------
- Probe budgets are constrained: annotation and compute cost mean we cannot exhaustively evaluate all slices continuously.
- Static prioritization leads to stale signals: workload drift, model updates, and quant changes shift the set of important probes.
- We need a unified, explainable scoring function that combines telemetry, model-change sensitivity, and business impact to 1) rank existing probes for evaluation and 2) seed new synthetic probes automatically where coverage gaps exist.

Scope
-----
This document covers:
- The priority scoring feature set and weight defaults.
- Algorithms for dynamic probe scoring.
- Synthetic-probe seeding heuristics and templates.
- Integration points: eval-harness scheduler, probe fabricator, and telemetry ingestion.
- Rollout plan, monitoring, and ownership.

Out of scope: human annotation UI and billing flows (see probe-curation-stewardship page).

Priority scoring design
----------------------
We represent each probe (existing or synthetic candidate) with a feature vector computed from telemetry and metadata. The final priority score is a weighted, normalized sum of feature contributions with a small stochastic exploration component (epsilon-greedy) to avoid blind spots.

Core features and default weights
(used to compute score = sum(weight_i * normalized(feature_i)))

| Feature name | Signal source | Purpose | Default weight |
|-------------|---------------|---------|----------------|
| Recent-Failure-Rate | eval telemetry (last 7d) | Prioritize probes with rising failure rates | 0.28 |
| Exposure | production shadow/sample rates | Ensure probe matches real traffic slices | 0.14 |
| Model-Change-Sensitivity | diff-of-eval-metrics pre/post model build | High sensitivity means likely regression | 0.20 |
| Quantization-Delta | replays across quant profiles | Detect probes that degrade under quant | 0.12 |
| Customer-Impact | tenant mapping / SLA score | Business-critical slices score higher | 0.10 |
| Latency-Tail-Exposure | p95/p99 per-slice | Latency sensitive prompts prioritized | 0.08 |
| Exploration-Bonus | random seed / novelty | Ensure coverage and avoid stagnation | 0.08 |

Normalization: each feature is normalized to [0,1] using clip-to-99.9th percentile and min=0 baselines computed over a sliding 30d window.

Telemetry ingestion and feature computation
------------------------------------------
- Inputs: eval results, production shadow traffic samples, per-tenant usage, quantized-replay outputs, model promotion diffs.
- Storage: feature aggregates stored in the eval-metrics-store as daily rollups (table: eval_probe_features).
- Freshness: features must be recomputed within 2 hours of new eval telemetry arrival for high-severity slices; otherwise stale flags are set.

Example SQL to compute Recent-Failure-Rate (simplified)
```
SELECT probe_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'fail' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS recent_failure_rate
FROM eval_results
WHERE occurred_at >= now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY probe_id;
```

Scoring pseudocode
------------------
```
features = fetch_features(probe_id)
score = 0
for name, weight in WEIGHTS.items():
  score += weight * normalize(features[name])
# add small randomized exploration
score = (1 - EPSILON) * score + EPSILON * random_uniform(0, 0.2)
return score
```

Dynamic weight tuning
- Default weights above are starting points. We run weekly bayesian optimization using historical detection throughput (true positives for real regressions found) as objective, constrained to maintain interpretability (max single-weight <= 0.4).
- All weight changes require a canary run and sign-off by the evaluation-steering panel.

Synthetic probe synthesis (seeding)
----------------------------------
When the scorer indicates coverage gaps (low exposure but high model-change-sensitivity or quantization-delta), the fabricator will generate candidate synthetic probes. There are two families of synthesis: template-driven and mutation-driven.

Template-driven synthesis
- Use curated prompt templates per product domain (customer-support, code-assist, summarization). Templates include placeholder slots with type constraints (numeric, name, code-snippet).
- Fill slots from a synthetic-lexicon derived from production anonymized tokens and prohibited-list filtering.
- Example template: "User asks to summarize the following transcript: [TRANSCRIPT_SNIPPET]" with TRANSCRIPT_SNIPPET length sampled from heavy-tail distribution to stress context window.

Mutation-driven synthesis
- Take high-value probes and apply controlled mutations: token-level paraphrase, meaning-preserving swap, adversarial perturbations (typos, punctuation changes), and context truncation/extension.
- Each mutation has an associated risk score; only mutations with acceptably low semantic drift are used for production seeding.

Synthesis quality controls
- Semantic similarity gate: new synthetic probe must score >= 0.65 cosine similarity in embedding space to an anchor family when mutation-driven, to avoid generating irrelevant tests.
- Privacy gate: all placeholder substitutions must pass PII detection; any candidate flagged is dropped and logged.
- Diversity cap: limit synthetic probes per fingerprint cluster to 3 per week to avoid overfitting.

Scheduler integration and lanes
----------------------------
We integrate scoring outputs into the eval-harness scheduler which supports lanes: real-eval (human-annotated), synthetic-eval, and stress-eval. Lanes have capacity budgets and SLOs.

- Allocation rule: allocate top-K scored probes to lanes according to a configurable split (default: 40% real, 40% synthetic, 20% stress).
- Backpressure: if annotation backlog > 48h, reduce real-eval allocation by 50% and move budget to synthetic-eval.
- Preemption: high-priority probes (score > 0.85) preempt lower-priority scheduled runs in the next 2-hour window.

Config example (JSON stored in config-store):
```
{
  "lane_split": {"real": 0.4, "synthetic": 0.4, "stress": 0.2},
  "annotation_backlog_threshold_hours": 48,
  "preemption_score_threshold": 0.85,
  "max_synth_per_cluster_per_week": 3
}
```

Monitoring, alerts, and SLOs
---------------------------
- Accuracy of regression catch: target 80% of production-impacting regressions detected by probes within first 24h of model promote (SLO). Measurement: retrospective mapping of incidents to earliest probe alert.
- Freshness: 95% of high-severity probe features recomputed < 2h after telemetry ingestion.
- False positive rate: keep manual triage FP rate < 30% for top-50 scored probes.

Key alerts
- Feature computation lag > 2h for > 5% of high severity probes -> page eng-eval-oncall.
- Spike in synthetic-probe rejection due to privacy gate -> notify security and evaluation-steering.
- Rapid weight drift during auto-tuning -> open ticket for manual review.

Operational runbook (quick steps)
-------------------------------
1. Incident: "probe storm" where too many probes spike score simultaneously.
   - Identify root cause: check model-change-diff, recent deploys, telemetry anomalies.
   - If model-induced, trigger a temporary freeze on synthetic seeding and escalate to model-owner.
2. Annotation backlog > 72h:
   - Increase synthetic-eval allocation and throttle non-critical probes (score < 0.35).
   - Notify annotation ops to scale reviewers.
3. Privacy gate failures:
   - Toggle synthesis off for affected templates, escalate to security to review lexicon and filters.

Rollout plan
------------
- Phase 0 (Lab): 2 weeks. Run scoring offline against historical evaluation data to calibrate weights and measure detection uplift.
- Phase 1 (Canary): 1 week. Enable scoring for 5% of eval-harness traffic; only surface suggestions (no auto-seed) to annotation queue.
- Phase 2 (Pilot): 3 weeks. Enable auto-seeding into synthetic lane for 10% capacity with manual triage for seeds.
- Phase 3 (GA): Gradual ramp to default lane_split over 4 weeks.

Ownership and governance
------------------------
- Primary owners: evaluation-platform (feature compute & scheduler) and probe-fabrication team (synthesis and template maintenance).
- Stakeholders: model-onboarding, applied-ml, security, customer-success.
- Governance: weekly evaluation-steering review of scoring metrics and any weight changes; quarterly privacy audit of synthetic lexicon.

Risk assessment
---------------
- Overfitting to synthetic probes: mitigate with diversity caps and embedding-similarity gating.
- Privacy leaks from lexicon: mitigate with PII detection and security audits.
- Annotation fatigue: mitigate with dynamic lane-splits and backlog-driven throttles.

Appendix A — Example feature table (schema for eval_probe_features)
| column | type | description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| probe_id | text | stable probe identifier |
| recent_failure_rate | float | fraction failures in last 7d |
| exposure | float | sample rate in production shadow |
| model_change_sensitive | float | normalized delta metric |
| quant_delta | float | worst-case change across quant profiles |
| customer_impact_score | float | 0-1 mapped from SLA tier |
| latency_tail | float | p99 normalized |
| last_feature_refresh | timestamp | when this row was computed |

Appendix B — Example mutation policy (short)
- Allowed mutations: paraphrase (preserve semantics), punctuation perturbation, token insertion of stop-phrases.
- Disallowed: replacement of entity types (e.g., identities) unless anonymized via lexicon.

References and related docs
--------------------------
- eval-workflow-optimizer-for-mixed-slo-scenarios-2026: scheduling and allocation patterns.
- probe-curation-stewardship-and-annotation-charter-2026: governance for human annotation.
- quantized-replay-orchestrator-spec-2026: replay infrastructure for quant_delta signal.

Contact
-------
For questions or to request a canary slot, ping @Maya Chen and the evaluation-platform Slack channel (#eval-platform).

title: Counterfactual Traffic Synthesis and Stability Protocol for Eval Harness
content:
Summary:

This document defines a reproducible protocol and tooling approach for generating counterfactual and synthetic traffic to stress-test model serving and evaluation infrastructure. The protocol focuses on producing stable, explainable variations of live traffic for: 1) regression detection, 2) caching/kv-cache sensitivity tests, 3) quantization/precision shock tests, and 4) routing and fallback validation across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Why this exists:
- Live traffic is the gold standard but cannot always be replayed (privacy, PII, consent) or deterministically modified.
- Random synthetic traffic misses critical corner cases and distributional shifts.
- Counterfactual traffic (systematically altered real or simulated requests) bridges the gap: it preserves semantics while enabling controlled perturbations to probe failure modes.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: applied-ML engineers, SREs, model-onboarding owners, and QA.
- Scope: eval harness integrations (eval-mesh), synthetic traffic service (traffic-synth), and downstream triage runbooks.
- Excluded: labeling guidelines for human annotators (handled in prompt-sets-and-benchmarks).

Key definitions:
- Counterfactual Traffic: requests derived from canonical examples with targeted perturbations (e.g., role swaps, locale swaps, long-context insertion).
- Synthetic Shadow: traffic generated to imitate structural properties (token length, entity density) of a production route without using PII.
- Amplification Factor: multiplier applied to rare-slice traffic to increase statistical power when evaluating regressions.

High-level architecture:
- eval-mesh: orchestrates eval jobs and routes to target serving endpoints (hosted/dedicated/private).
- traffic-synth: independent microservice that composes counterfactuals and emits injections to eval-mesh or canary proxies.
- kv-cache-proxy: optional inline proxy to emulate and flush customer KV cache behaviors.
- quant-simulator: module that wraps model variants (float32->int8 quant) to compare outputs without changing live model binary.

Design principles:
- Determinism where possible: seeds + cataloged perturbation rules produce repeatable traffic.
- Observability-first: every synthetic request carries trace metadata (synth.catalog, perturbation.seed, amplification.id).
- Minimal fidelity loss: preserve original semantic intent of examples to avoid false positives.
- Safety and privacy: no PII copied from production; use token-level anonymization + synthetic named entities.

Catalog of perturbation families (examples):
1) Entity-level swaps: replace named entities with same-type synthetic tokens (e.g., COMPANY_X -> COMPANY_SYNTH).
2) Context elongation: insert benign long context passages to stress KV cache and long-context execution path.
3) Role inversion: flip question/answer framing to catch degenerative behavior in instruction-following models.
4) Locale and formatting: switch date/number formats, RTL language insertion, and timezone offsets.
5) Adversarial punctuation/noise: insert seldom-used unicode or tokenization traps.
6) Quantization stress: force sequences known to amplify FP error (dense numerical tables, alignment tokens).

Sampling strategies:
- Stratified-Aware Sampling: sample from production strata (route, customer-tier, model-version) proportionally, then amplify rare slices by Amplification Factor (AF).
- Edge-Amplify: identify slices with <1% frequency and apply AF 50–200x for statistical power.
- Counterfactual Pairs: always generate a (control, perturbed) pair to compute delta metrics per request.

Configuration table (recommended defaults):
Route/Workload Config YAML (example):
---
name: marketing-chat-route
seed_corpus: s3://eval-corpora/marketing-seed-v2.jsonl
perturbation_families: [entity_swaps, context_elongation, locale_swaps]
sample_strategy: stratified-aware
amplification_factors: {rare_slice: 100, default: 1}
batch_size: 128
duration: 2h
send_mode: shadow (no client-visible effects)
observe_metrics: [latency_p50, latency_p95, rsi, match_rate, token_delta]
---

CLI & examples:
- Generate a reproducible counterfactual run locally (dev):
$ traffic-synth run --config configs/marketing-chat-route.yaml --seed 42 --dry-run

- Push a 2-hour shadow stream to eval-mesh for canary:
$ traffic-synth run --config configs/marketing-chat-route.yaml --seed 20260214 --duration 2h --send-mode shadow --target eval-mesh:9090

- Quick curl to submit single counterfactual pair to eval-mesh (JSON):
curl -X POST https://eval-mesh.internal/api/v1/ingest -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"trace_id":"synth-0001","seed":123,"control":{"prompt":"Summarize quarterly results."},"perturbed":{"prompt":"Summarize quarterly results with extra accounting table appended."},"tags":{"family":"context_elongation","amplification":"1"}}'

Metrics and acceptance criteria:
- Response Stability Index (RSI): median absolute token-wise divergence between control and perturbed outputs. Alert if RSI > 0.12 for any amplified slice.
- Latency SLO regression: no more than +10% increase in route p95 latency under synthetic load vs baseline for burst sized up to batch_size*4.
- Semantic match_rate: fraction of perturbed outputs that preserve required intent labels (e.g., intent classification) — target > 0.92 for production promotion.
- Token delta: expected token increase per perturbation family; validate against a 3-sigma envelope built from historical runs.

Experiment / promotion checklist (canary procedure):
1) Local dry-run: run --dry-run and validate traces and perturbation coverage.
2) Shadow targeted canary (1% production RPS equivalent): send to eval-mesh -> observe metrics for 2h.
3) Amplified slice validation: for each rare slice with AF>1, ensure RSI < threshold and match_rate > 0.92.
4) Cross-model comparison: run quant-simulator variants (FP32 vs quant) on same stream and compute per-token delta; flag if > 0.08 for high-sensitivity routes.
5) Rollout decision: if all acceptance criteria pass, mark model as promotion-ready in onboarding matrix.
6) Post-promotion scan: run an overnight full-shaped synthetic sweep (AF=10 for rare slices) and collect stability artifacts.

Triage playbook (when synthetic run flags a regression):
1) Attach run metadata and open a regression issue with tag: eval:counterfactual. Include: config, seed, amplification id, and example (control, perturbed, model outputs).
2) Reproduce with same seed in dev environment. If non-deterministic, capture run logs and escalate to runtime team.
3) Bisect by perturbation family: run traffic-synth with single family enabled to isolate failure mode.
4) Run quant-simulator for quant regressions; if behavior diverges only in quant variant, escalate to model-ops + quant teams.
5) If divergence correlates with KV-cache eviction patterns, enable kv-cache-proxy with deterministic TTL=0/1 toggles to reproduce.
6) Document root cause, mitigations (e.g., prompt normalization, tokenizer glue fixes, caching TTL changes), and remediation timeline.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Traffic-synth: owned by applied-ml (oncall: applied-ml@redwood.internal) — SLA: 99.5% availability for dev runs.
- Eval-mesh ingestion: owned by eng-platform (oncall: eng-platform@redwood.internal) — SLA: 99.9% for evaluation ingestion.
- Triage and model promotion decisions: model-onboarding team.

Observability and artifacts to capture for every run:
- Trace ID list and sampling map (CSV).
- Per-request control/perturbed outputs (ndjson).
- Metric timeseries for RSI, latency percentiles, match_rate.
- Token-level diffs for top-k diverging examples.
- Run manifest (config + git sha + synth version).

Privacy & safety controls:
- No PII rule: any seed corpus coming from production must pass scrubbing + synthetic-entity-replacement before ingestion.
- Safety review checkpoint: any amplification >100x on slices with user-visible outputs requires a safety review from Research safety lead.

Appendix A — Example perturbation rule (JSON):
{
  "id": "entity_swap_company",
  "description": "Swap organization entities with synthetic names preserving token-length distribution.",
  "patterns": ["ORG", "COMPANY"],
  "replacement_pool": ["AcmeSyn", "BetaWorks", "NovaGrid"],
  "seeded": true
}

Appendix B — Common failure signatures and quick remediation:
- High RSI with low token delta: likely a model policy/decoding change. Remediation: check decoding params, temperature, and any soft-prompt patches.
- High token delta + latency spike: batching/backpressure interaction; remediate via batch tuning and autoscaling policy.
- Failures isolated to quant-simulator: investigate quant profile, re-run per-workload quant-tuner.

Links and references:
- eval-harness overview: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/serving-simulation-eval-harness-2026
- Regression triage handbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026
- Quant profiles: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024

Contact:
- Primary author: Aisha Malik (aisha@redwood.internal)
- Applied-ML oncall: applied-ml@redwood.internal

Revision history:
- 2025-11-12: initial draft
- 2026-01-20: added quant-simulator integration and RSI acceptance thresholds
- 2026-02-14: finalized canary checklist and privacy controls

title: Micro-Canary Eval Orchestrator and Fast-Fail Protocol
content:
Summary:

This page describes the Micro-Canary Eval Orchestrator (MCEO), a lightweight evaluation and monitoring pattern designed to detect and triage regressions from deployment events with minimal cost and low latency. The MCEO sits inside the eval-harness and is intended for fast-turnaround verification of change windows (model rollouts, quantization patches, prompt rewrites, routing rules). It complements full-stage shadow and production evaluations by catching high-signal, high-impact regressions within minutes.

Goals:
- Detect degradations that materially affect customer-facing slices within the first 1–30 minutes after a change.
- Provide deterministic fast-fail criteria and an automated mitigation/rollback trigger path.
- Keep compute and annotation cost < 3% of a full CI eval run for typical models.
- Produce actionable telemetry and a standardized triage packet for oncall and model teams.

When to run MCEO:
- Canary rollouts of new model versions or quantized artifacts.
- Prompt/template updates that change structured outputs (JSON schema changes).
- Configuration changes affecting routing, batching, or KV cache behavior.
- Emergency quick checks after hotfixes.

Architecture and Components:
1) Orchestrator service (lightweight):
   - Responsible for scheduling micro-canary jobs, collecting results, and evaluating thresholds.
   - API endpoints: POST /microcanary/start, GET /microcanary/status, POST /microcanary/abort.
   - Owner: eval-harness team.

2) Mini-workload generator:
   - A curated subset of 50–500 prompts per canary (adaptive by model type). Prompts are drawn from the production prompt catalog with stratified sampling across high-impact slices.
   - Includes payloads to exercise streaming, function-calling, and embeddings where relevant.

3) Fast-eval telemetry collector:
   - Lightweight traces (latency p50/p95/p99), token counts, model logits summary, embedding cosine drift, structured-validation failures.
   - Event tags: change_id, rollout_id, model_revision, quant_profile, route.

4) Decision engine (rule + ML hybrid):
   - Rule checks: absolute thresholds (latency > X ms, structured-fail rate > Y%) and delta thresholds (metric_regression > Z% relative to baseline).
   - ML assistant: an anomaly detector that ingests short-term windows to suppress noisy false positives for low-volume slices.

Canary Configuration (example in JSON):
```
{
  "canary_name": "microcanary-frontend-nl-2026-02-10",
  "model_revision": "redwood-v2.3-quant-a8",
  "sample_size": 120,
  "max_duration_minutes": 20,
  "slices": ["billing-clarity", "multi-turn-support", "json-schema-output"],
  "thresholds": {
    "p95_latency_ms": 500,
    "structured_validation_fail_rate": 0.025,
    "embedding_cosine_drop": 0.08
  },
  "rollback_action": "auto-rollback-on-critical",
  "notify_channels": ["#canary-alerts", "pagerduty:ml-canary-signal"]
}
```

Operational Runbook (step-by-step):
1) Schedule: trigger via CI/CD pipeline or manually from Console > Eval Harness > Micro-Canary.
2) Start: Orchestrator reserves a micro-slot against dedicated eval capacity (or falls back to burst pool).
3) Execute: the mini-workload generator issues requests to the target endpoint with recording enabled.
4) Collect: telemetry is streamed to the fast-eval collector (ingest retention 48 hours).
5) Evaluate: Decision engine runs rule checks then ML anomaly suppression.
6) Resolve:
   6.1) If no thresholds exceeded: mark canary success, annotate change with canary_id and attach summary.
   6.2) If thresholds exceeded but non-critical (e.g., minor p95 drift < configured hard-fail delta): open a P0 investigation ticket but do not auto-rollback.
   6.3) If critical thresholds exceeded (structured-validation_fail_rate >= critical threshold OR p95 latency >= emergency threshold): trigger configured rollback action and fire PagerDuty.

Fast-Fail Criteria (examples):
- Critical: structured_validation_fail_rate >= 5% for any high-impact slice OR p95_latency_mm >= 2000 ms for streaming endpoints.
- High: structured_validation_fail_rate in [2.5%, 5%) AND regression from baseline > 40%
- Medium: embedding_cosine_drop between 0.05 and 0.08 for production embedding-using routes (requires manual review).

Telemetry and Triage Packet (what gets produced on failure):
- Canary metadata (canary_name, change_id, timestamp, model_revision).
- Compact telemetry snapshot (latency histogram, token distribution, top 5 prompts with worst regressions).
- Response diffs: golden baseline vs candidate response for top N failures (text diffs and structured-JSON diff).
- Minimal reproduction bundle: 10 representative requests and full raw responses, links to logs and a short human-friendly summary.

Escalation and Ownership:
- First responder: oncall SRE for eval-harness (15-minute ack SLA).
- Second line: owning model/product engineer who deployed change.
- If auto-rollback occurred: postmortem owner is the deploying team; SRE helps restore telemetry overlays and triage data.

Checklist for Deploying a Canary Configuration:
1) Verify slice coverage includes at least one high-impact customer intent.
2) Confirm sample_size maps to at least 10 requests per slice.
3) Set thresholds relative to recent baseline (use last-7-days median).
4) Attach rollout_id and change_id to telemetry.
5) Add reviewer(s) in the canary config for manual overrides.

Integration with Other Eval Stages:
- Shadow stage: MCEO should run before shadow-to-prod promotion. If a micro-canary fails but shadow is green, treat as high-priority investigation (possible sampling mismatch).
- Full CI eval: results of MCEO are included in the release artifact and stored for 90 days for regression analysis.
- Regression triage: MCEO failure packets automatically create a regression triage ticket with a standardized template.

Best Practices and Gotchas:
- Keep canary prompts stable across short windows to avoid noisy drift. If prompts must change, version them with canary config.
- Be conservative with auto-rollback on low-signal slices; use ML suppression to reduce false alarms.
- Watch for caching-related flakiness. If canary interacts with KV cache, run a cache-warm step before measurement.
- For quantization rollouts, include deterministic prompt seeds to surface numeric instabilities.

Metrics to Monitor (SLO / alerting suggestions):
- Canary success rate (target >= 99% per day).
- False-positive rate of auto-rollbacks (target < 2% monthly).
- Time-to-detect (target median <= 5 minutes).
- Triaged regression-to-fix time (target median <= 6 hours for critical).

CLI examples:
- Start a canary: 
  curl -X POST https://eval-orch.internal/microcanary/start -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"canary_name":"canary-quick-2026-02","model_revision":"redwood-v2.3"}'

- Abort: 
  curl -X POST https://eval-orch.internal/microcanary/abort -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"canary_name":"canary-quick-2026-02"}'

KPI Reporting and Dashboards:
- Dashboard panels: canary health over time, top failing prompts, rollback events, time-to-detect histogram.
- Daily digest: aggregated micro-canary outcomes and a short list of notable regressions delivered to the model-onboarding and SRE channels.

Ownership and Implementation Notes:
- Owner: eval-harness team (PM: Priya Nair; Eng lead: Aaron Lim).
- Implementation language: Python orchestration, Go lightweight worker for request issuing.
- Data retention: 48 hours for raw responses, 90 days for summarized canary artifacts.
- Security: all micro-canary payloads must follow PII redaction rules and use customer-scrubbed prompt catalog for production-like corpora.

Open questions / roadmap items:
- Integrate a learned baseline instead of a static short-window median for slice baselines.
- Support micro-canaries in private deployments (VPC-safe runners).
- Add A/B micro-canaries to test routing changes that use weighted variants.

Appendix A — Canary Config Field Reference:
- canary_name (string): unique id.
- model_revision (string): model artifact tag.
- sample_size (int): number of requests.
- slices (list[string]): logical slices to exercise.
- thresholds (map): rule thresholds.
- rollback_action (string): none | manual-notify | auto-rollback-on-critical.
- notify_channels (list[string]): slack/pagerduty endpoints.

Appendix B — Example Triage Ticket Template (auto-populated):
- title: [MICRO-CANARY][FAIL] {canary_name} {model_revision}
- description: short summary + top failing prompts + links to replication bundle.
- severity: critical | high | medium.
- attachments: telemetry snapshot, diffs, reproduction bundle.

If you are implementing or modifying MCEO, please coordinate with the eval-harness owners and add new canary names to the canonical registry: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/canary-registry.

title: Cold-start Bootstrap Sampling Protocol for New Model Onboarding
content:
Summary:
This document defines the Cold-start Bootstrap Sampling Protocol used when introducing a new model (or a major model variant) into Redwood’s serving and eval pipelines. The protocol standardizes: initial sample selection, staged evaluation rounds, statistical stability tests, quantization compatibility checks, and automated gating for promotion to shadow or canary stages.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to any new model version or architecture introduced to Redwood’s Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Intended for the first 0–30 days after a model is first integrated into our eval-harness.
- Not a substitute for safety or policy reviews — those must be executed in parallel per the safety-sandbox process.

Goals:
1) Obtain representative, reproducible quality metrics with minimal cost.
2) Detect early regressions vs. production baseline and historical models.
3) Ensure quantization/latency/kv-cache interactions are covered in the cold-start window.
4) Provide a deterministic gating signal for promotion to longer-running shadow evaluation.

Ownership and roles:
- Author: Amina Chowdhury (Applied ML) — maintains protocol definitions and templates.
- Eval-runner Owner: team that operates the eval-harness (eng-applied-ml).
- Onboarding Owner: model on-call / model steward from Research or Inference.
- Security Reviewer: security-and-compliance for privacy-sensitive sampling.

Key definitions and metrics:
- Bootstrap round: one discrete evaluation pass against a sampled workload slice. Typical rounds: R0..R3.
- Cold-start window: first 7 days (configurable up to 30d) after first integration.
- Stability Index (SI): normalized variance measure of primary quality metric across repeated rounds. Lower is more stable.
- Regret Rate: proportion of samples where the new model performs below baseline threshold.
- Latency SLO breach rate: percent tokens/requests exceeding configured latency SLO for the deployment tier.

Sampling strategy (high level):
1) Seed selection: combine stratified production slices + synthetic stress probes. Use stratification keys: product-route, language, user-intent, sequence-length-bucket.
2) Warmup quota: reserve 20% of eval budget for short context / prefix-heavy samples to exercise KV cache path.
3) Edge coverage: 10% of samples are adversarial/edge prompts from the edgecase-probe inventory.
4) Randomization: apply deterministic seed per-model (model-id + date) to allow replayable sampling.

Recommended sizes: (table representation)
- R0 (sanity): 200 samples (fast), focus on smoke checks and integration.
- R1 (bootstrap): 2,000 samples, stratified coverage across 5 primary slices.
- R2 (stability): 10,000 samples, multi-seed (n=3) aggregation.
- R3 (safety/quant): 1,000 targeted stress probes including quantized replay.

Example sampling config (YAML):

sampling_config:
  model_id: "new-model-2026-03"
  seed: 123456
  rounds:
    - name: R0_sanity
      size: 200
      slices: ["prod-top-10-routes", "sanity-templates"]
    - name: R1_bootstrap
      size: 2000
      stratify_by: ["route","lang","len_bucket"]
    - name: R2_stability
      size: 10000
      multi_seed: 3
    - name: R3_quant_compat
      size: 1000
      probes: ["kv-cache", "quant_roundtrip", "streaming_fncall"]

Procedures (step-by-step):
1) Integration and smoke (Owner: Onboarding Owner)
   a) Deploy model artifact to eval-harness using reproducible image/tag.
   b) Run R0; verify end-to-end integration, tokenization parity, and no fatal errors.
   c) Confirm logging hooks (token-level telemetry, model_version tag) are flowing to the sandbox metrics cluster.

2) Bootstrap evaluation (Owner: Eval-runner)
   a) Execute R1 with the sampling_config. Capture metrics: acceptability_score, bleu/bert_score (where applicable), SI, latency_p50/p95, token_cost_estimate.
   b) Aggregate results and compute Regret Rate vs baseline_model using pre-registered baseline_id.
   c) If Regret Rate > 5% OR SI > 0.08, create an automated triage issue and stop further automatic promotion.

3) Stability sweep (Owner: Applied ML/Onboarding)
   a) Run R2 across multi-seeds. Compute SI and confidence intervals for primary metrics.
   b) If metric variance decreases below configured thresholds (SI <= 0.05), mark as stable; else, require additional data or targeted prompt repairs.

4) Quantization compatibility (Owner: Runtime + Applied ML)
   a) Run R3 using quantized artifacts (int8/int4 profiles) and hybrid-run modes.
   b) Run quantized-replay-orchestrator to compare floating-point outputs to quantized outputs. Report: accuracy_delta, token_pattern-divergence, kv-cache-hits-diff.
   c) Block promotion if accuracy_delta on critical slices > 1.5% or if streaming toolcall regressions observed.

Gating and promotion matrix:
- Gate to shadow: pass R0 + R1 with Regret Rate <= 3% and Latency SLO breach <= 1%
- Gate to canary: stability confirmed (R2) AND quant compat verified (R3) AND no critical safety flags
- Manual review required for any of: high SI, privacy-sensitive sample failures, or high-cost per-token delta

Statistical tests and thresholds:
- Use bootstrap resampling (n=1,000) to compute 95% CI on primary metrics.
- SI = sqrt(Var(metric))/mean_metric; require SI <= 0.05 for promotion beyond canary.
- For paired comparisons vs baseline, use Wilcoxon signed-rank if non-normal; require p < 0.05 for claiming superiority.

Telemetry and instrumentation checklist:
- Event tags: model_id, eval_round, sample_id, slice_key, seed_id, response_hash.
- Metrics emitted: primary_quality_metric, latency_ms, tokens_generated, kv_cache_hit, quant_mode, seed.
- Traces: sample-level traces stored for failing samples with full prompt + response + trace_id.

Automation and CI integration:
- CI job: onboarding/coldstart/<model_id> triggers R0 and R1 on PR to model-integration repo.
- Nightly job: schedule R2 runs for any model in cold-start window until stability achieved or 30d elapsed.
- Alerting: failing gating creates a ticket with triage tags: [eval-fail, coldstart, model_id].

Failure modes and triage notes:
- Symptom: high Latency p95 with normal p50 -> likely sequence-length distribution mismatch; inspect len_bucket distribution and KV cache warmup fraction.
- Symptom: large accuracy_delta only in quantized runs -> check quant-profile (per-workload-quant-tuner) and retry with hybrid-quant.
- Symptom: high Regret Rate on a single route -> isolate route slice, run focused R3 stress probe, and open targeted prompt surfacing task.

Reporting and handoffs:
- Standard deliverables after R2: evaluation report (PDF), failing-sample manifest (CSV), dashboard link, and triage tickets.
- Handoff to Reliability: if latency SLO breach persists at canary, open canary-blocker and assign to eng-serving-runtime.

Appendices:
A. Example CLI to run a round (eval-harness runner)

# Run bootstrap round 1
redwood-eval run --model new-model-2026-03 --round R1_bootstrap --out results/R1_new-model-2026-03.json

B. Minimal result schema (JSON lines)
{
  "sample_id": "s-1234",
  "route": "generate-summary",
  "lang": "en",
  "prompt": "<text>",
  "response": "<text>",
  "primary_metric": 0.83,
  "latency_ms": 120,
  "kv_cache_hit": true
}

C. Quick checklist for model stewards:
- Verify instrumentation tags are present in first-run logs.
- Confirm synthetic stress probes cover streaming/function-call paths.
- Validate quantization artifacts with runtime team before R3.

Related documents and references:
- Inference readiness matrix (see related_pages)
- Quant-profile synthesis playbook
- Edgecase probe generator

Revision history:
- 2025-11-02: initial draft and internal review.
- 2026-01-10: added SI definition, gating thresholds tuned after pilot.
- 2026-02-14: formalized quantization gating and automation CI jobs.

Contact:
- For questions, open a PR on the eval-harness repo and tag @amina or ping #applied-ml on Slack.

title: Compact Priming Fallback Orchestrator and Regression Fastpath
content:
Summary

This playbook describes the Compact Priming Fallback Orchestrator (CPFO): an end-to-end pattern for generating and serving highly compressed prompt priming for edge clients while preserving evaluation fidelity, integrating quantization-aware fallbacks, and providing a rapid regression fastpath for operational incidents. The target audience is model-onboarding engineers, eval harness owners, runtime operators, and SREs who manage mixed-precision/edge-serving fleets.

Goals

- Reduce average token cost for long-primed edge requests by >= 35% without exceeding fidelity delta budgets.
- Maintain 99th percentile generation latency SLOs for edge-tail workloads (see Metrics).
- Provide a deterministic, low-latency rollback and regression triage path when fidelity or hallucination error increases.

When to use

Use CPFO when:
- Clients attach long priming contexts (>= 512 tokens) frequently and budget/cost is material.
- Deployments use mixed-precision quantized model variants (int8/4bit) where prompt sensitivity may vary.
- You need to shadow edge traffic in private or dedicated deployments for continuous fidelity monitoring.

Architecture (text diagram)

Edge Client -> Compact-Priming Service -> Shadow-Orchestrator -> Runtime Router -> {Quantized Variant, Full FP Variant} -> Eval-Mesh (telemetry sink)

Components and responsibilities

- Compact-Priming Service: token-aware compressor that produces a compact priming representation and a reconstruction hint. Outputs: compressed_prompt, reconstruction_meta. Owned by: eng-developer-experience.
- Shadow-Orchestrator: fabric that duplicates requests into shadow lanes with configurable ratio and fidelity anchors. Owned by: eval-harness team.
- Runtime Router: policy engine (latency-first, cost-first, hybrid) that selects model variant. Owned by: serving-runtime.
- Eval-Mesh: long-term storage and continuous evaluators that compute fidelity deltas, embedding drift, and hallucination scores. Owned by: applied-ml-and-evals.

Design details

1) Prompt compression algorithm (overview)
- Input: priming text, tokenized.
- Steps:
  1. Identify high-entropy windows via n-gram frequency sketch (k=5).
  2. Preserve named entities and functioncall signatures (heuristics + regex whitelist).
  3. Replace low-impact adjectives and boilerplate with canonical placeholders.
  4. Serialize compressed representation as a small delta patch: {anchors, tokens, compress-hints}.
- Output constraints: final compressed token footprint <= 0.45 * original for target slices.

2) Quantization-aware priming profiles
- Profiles: conservative (use int8 fallback only), aggressive (allow int4/packed quant), reconstruction-first (prioritizes fidelity).
- Each profile includes: acceptable fidelity delta (ROUGE/embedding distance), recommended shadow rate, and quant hedge policy.

Configuration table (example)

| profile | fidelity_budget | recommended_shadow_rate | runtime_policy | quant_hedge_threshold |
|---------|-----------------|-------------------------|----------------|-----------------------|
| conservative | <= 0.02 embedding-dist | 10% | prefer fp32 -> int8 fallback | 1.5x fidelity-cost |
| aggressive   | <= 0.05 embedding-dist | 2%  | cost-first, allow int4 | 2.0x fidelity-cost |
| reconstruction-first | <= 0.01 embedding-dist | 20% | preserve anchors -> fp32 | 1.2x fidelity-cost |

Shadow orchestration flow (operational steps)

1. Enable CPFO for a tenant: set profile, shadow_rate, and priming_max_tokens in tenant config.
2. For each incoming edge request: generate compressed_prompt; send live request to runtime per policy.
3. Fork a shadow request to eval-mesh with full uncompressed priming and to a quant-shadow pool.
4. Compare live response vs shadow baseline asynchronously; compute fidelity metrics and publish to topic eval.metrics.cpfo.{tenant}.
5. If fidelity deltas exceed profile thresholds for N=5 consecutive probes, trigger regression fastpath.

Regression fastpath (triage playbook)

Immediate detection triggers: fidelity delta high, hallucination score > threshold, functioncall mismatch.

Fastpath steps (numbered):
1. Auto-quarantine: temporarily disable compression for affected tenant-route (API flag). Timebox: 30m.
2. Promote FP baseline: route traffic to non-quantized variant and set shadow_rate=100% for 10 minutes.
3. Capture artifacts: request/response pairs, tokenization diffs, compressed->reconstructed text, model logits (if available).
4. Oncall steps (SLO 15 minutes to initial triage):
   a. Run automatic delta classifier (script: tools/cpfo/delta_check.py --tenant $ID).
   b. If classifier maps to 'compression-failure', create a triage ticket in the regression board and tag as cpfo-compression.
   c. If classifier maps to 'quant-degradation', escalate to runtime/quantops.
5. Rollback path: if an immediate rollback is required, flip runtime_policy to 'prefer fp32' and reduce shadowing for cost.

Metrics and SLOs (text table)

- SLOs:
  - Latency: p95 end-to-end generation < 420ms for edge small prompts, p99 < 900ms for cold starts.
  - Fidelity: average embedding-distance increase <= profile budget (see config).
  - Cost: tokenized priming cost reduction target >= 35% within 30 days of rollout.
- Signals to monitor:
  - eval.metrics.cpfo.{tenant}.embedding_delta (gauge)
  - eval.metrics.cpfo.{tenant}.hallucination_score (gauge)
  - runtime.latency.tail (histogram)
  - quantops.fallback_rate (counter)

Rollout checklist

1. Lab validation: run 1k synthetic probes with both compressed and full priming; assert fidelity budgets.
2. Shadow stage: enable profile at 5% shadow rate for 48 hours; monitor metrics.
3. Canary stage: 1% live traffic (compressed) with 100% shadowing for 24 hours.
4. Gradual increase: double live traffic every 24 hours until 25% or target cost.
5. Full rollout: set runtime_policy and monitor for 14 days.

Ownership and runbooks

- Compact-Priming Service: eng-developer-experience; Pager: compact-priming-pager; Runbook: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues/compact-priming-runbook (link).
- Shadow-Orchestrator: eval-harness; Pager: eval-shadow-pager; Runbook: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/shadow-orchestrator-runbook (link).
- Runtime Router & Quantops: eng-serving-runtime; Pager: runtime-quantops.

CLI & config examples

Example tenant config (JSON):
{\n  "tenant_id": "tenant-acme",\n  "profile": "conservative",\n  "priming_max_tokens": 768,\n  "shadow_rate": 0.10,\n  "runtime_policy": "latency-first"\n}

Quick triage command (for oncall):
$ ./tools/cpfo/triage.sh --tenant tenant-acme --since 15m

Postmortem guidance

- Every regression fastpath incident must include: cause hypothesis, artifacts collected, mitigation applied, and a reproduction notebook.
- If root cause is compression logic, open an onboarding ticket to dev-ex with a failing seed set and mark affected probes as "do-not-compress" until fix.

Security and privacy notes

- Compressed artifacts retain anchors only; do not store full sensitive content in the compressed cache. For regulated tenants enable dp-redaction prior to compression.
- Shadow traffic must be stored to the tenant's private bucket when using Redwood Private.

Related resources

- See: quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook (recommended reading)
- Eval harness shadow consistency checker (for seed determinism checks)

Appendix: heuristics checklist for compression

- Preserve functioncall identifiers and argument shapes.
- Never compress numeric sequences that look like hashes/IDs.
- Favor preserving sentence-level anchors for step-by-step instructions.

This document is maintained by the applied-ml-and-evals and eng-developer-experience cross-functional guild. For questions, tag #cpfo in internal Slack and ping the document reviewers.

title: Cohort-driven Eval Scheduling and Priority Protocol
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the cohort-driven evaluation scheduling and priority protocol used by Redwood's eval-orch service to allocate evaluator resources, reduce noisy variance across workloads, and ensure high-value experiments get stable, timely runs. It describes how cohorts are defined, how priority scores are computed, resource windows and backfill rules, integration with caching/quantization-aware profiles, and operational runbooks for common scenarios.

Why this exists

- Reduce cross-workload interference that causes unstable eval signals (especially for latency-sensitive and quantized workloads).
- Make scheduling decisions reproducible and auditable so regressions can be traced to scheduling artifacts rather than model changes.
- Balance cost, timeliness, and statistical fidelity when allocating constrained evaluator capacity.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to eval runs managed by eval-orch (interactive and batch evaluators) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private eval fleets.
- Covers cohort construction, priority computation, preemption/backfill policies, telemetry signals used for autoscaling, and required annotations on eval requests.
- Does NOT cover model acceptance criteria (see production-model-certification-checklist) or user-facing rollout policies.

Definitions

- Cohort: A grouping of eval jobs that share workload characteristics (latency sensitivity, sequence-length distribution, quant profile, dataset type, and customer tier).
- Priority Score: A computed numeric score used to order job execution. Higher means run earlier.
- Evaluator Pool: Logical group of workers with similar hardware and kernel profiles (e.g., a100-40g-int8-pool).
- Fidelity Band: Statistical group that indicates required sample size and stability budget (low/medium/high).

Cohort construction rules

1) Mandatory tags on every eval request (API/SDK):
   - workload_type: {chat, completion, embedding, rerank}
   - seq_len_bucket: {short:<128, medium:128-1024, long:>1024}
   - quant_profile: {fp16, int8, q4_0, q4_1}
   - latency_sensitivity: {low, medium, high}
   - customer_tier: {self_serve, commercial, enterprise}

2) Cohort assignment algorithm (pseudo):
   - Step A: Bucket by evaluators_supported_hardware and quant_profile.
   - Step B: Sub-bucket by latency_sensitivity + seq_len_bucket.
   - Step C: Tag with fidelity_band using heuristics: high fidelity for enterprise & regression triage jobs; medium for feature-tracking; low for exploratory.

Priority score calculation

Priority score (PS) is a weighted linear combination:

PS = W_tier * TierScore + W_latency * LatencyScore + W_fidelity * FidelityScore + W_staleness * StalenessScore - W_cost * EstimatedCostRank

Where:
- TierScore: self_serve=10, commercial=30, enterprise=60.
- LatencyScore: low=5, medium=20, high=50.
- FidelityScore: low=5, medium=25, high=45.
- StalenessScore: monotonic hours since request submission normalized to [0,10].
- EstimatedCostRank: cost rank of the run on normalized scale [0,10].
- Default weights: W_tier=1.0, W_latency=1.2, W_fidelity=1.4, W_staleness=0.6, W_cost=0.8.

Notes: weights are tunable via eval-orch config; score is clipped to [0,100]. Priority ties are broken by request id timestamp.

Resource windows and capacity allocation

- Each Evaluator Pool exposes N concurrent slots (configured per-pool).
- Pools are partitioned into: baseline_capacity (70%), burst_capacity (20%), preemptible_backfill (10%).
- Baseline capacity honors enterprise SLAs and scheduled high-priority cohorts. Burst capacity serves transient spikes for commercial workloads. Backfill runs lower-priority & exploratory evals and may be preempted.

Preemption and backfill rules

1) Preemption is allowed only for backfill jobs. Baseline and burst slots cannot be preempted without explicit approval.
2) When a higher-priority job (PS delta >= 15) is queued and there is no free baseline slot, eval-orch will attempt to reclaim a backfill slot.
3) Preempted jobs receive an attempt to checkpoint partial results to the artifact store; if checkpointing fails, they are marked for fast-resume (see runbook).

Cache & quantization-awareness

- Cohorts maintain a small KV cache affinity window (default 15 minutes) per pool to preserve KV-cache hotness and reduce cold-start noise.
- Quantization profile mismatches between requested eval and pool hardware lower the effective PriorityScore by 10 points to avoid noisy mismatch runs.

Fidelity bands and statistical budgets

Table: Fidelity band definitions

| Fidelity | Min samples | Max variance budget (std) | Run window (hours) | Typical use-cases |
|----------|-------------|---------------------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| Low      | 250         | 0.15                      | 72                  | exploratory dev, feature probes |
| Medium   | 1,000       | 0.07                      | 48                  | performance tracking |
| High     | 5,000       | 0.02                      | 24                  | regression triage, release gating |

Example YAML eval-orch job config

```yaml
job_id: "eval-2026-0009"
workload_type: "chat"
seq_len_bucket: "medium"
quant_profile: "int8"
latency_sensitivity: "high"
customer_tier: "commercial"
fidelity_band: "medium"
priority_overrides: null
requested_pool: "a100-40g-int8-pool"
expected_sample_count: 1200
max_run_time_hours: 12
annotations:
  team: "search-ranking"
  experiment: "rerank-quant-int8-v2"
```

Telemetry signals and SLOs (what eval-orch tracks)

- Queue latency P95 <= 2 hours for baseline capacity cohorts.
- Job start P95 <= 1 hour after dequeuing.
- Checkpoint success rate >= 99% for runs > 30 minutes.
- Preemption noise rate (jobs preempted more than once) < 0.5%.
- Fidelity convergence: median variance/day reduction >= 30% for medium/high bands.

Operational procedures and runbooks

1) Fast resume for preempted runs
   - Trigger: job preempted and checkpoint saved to artifact store.
   - Steps:
     1. Verify checkpoint exists in s3://eval-artifacts/<job_id>/checkpoint/ .
     2. Requeue job with resume=true and original priority.
     3. Monitor memory and kv-cache warming metrics for first 5 minutes.
     4. If failure to resume, mark job as resume_failed and notify owner (Slack group: #eval-ops).

2) Handling runaway variance in a cohort
   - Trigger: variance > band threshold for 3 consecutive runs.
   - Steps:
     1. Quarantine cohort (stop scheduling new medium/high runs to the same pool).
     2. Spawn diagnostic shadow runs on isolated pool (a100-debug-pool) with identical seeds.
     3. Collect kernel-level traces and KV-cache hit rates.
     4. Open an incident in Incidents Jira (component: eval-orch) and assign to Applied ML on-call.

3) Emergency rebalancing (SLA breach imminent)
   - Trigger: enterprise SLA breach predicted within 15 minutes due to capacity loss.
   - Steps:
     1. Pause all backfill jobs immediately.
     2. Drain burst capacity and move eligible jobs to preemptible nodes.
     3. If still insufficient, execute cross-region fallback policy (route to compatible pools in another region).

Integration points and hooks

- eval-orch -> telemetry-pipeline: emits job lifecycle events (queued, started, checkpointed, preempted, completed).
- eval-orch -> optimizer-service: requests cost estimates and suggested batching parameters.
- eval-orch -> evaluator-agent: gRPC control plane for running and checkpointing jobs.
- eval-orch -> kv-cache-service: affinity hints for cache warmup.

Metrics and dashboards to create

- Evaluator Pool: concurrent usage, slot occupancy by cohort, burst/backfill ratio.
- Job lifecycle: queue latency distribution, preemption counts, resume success rate.
- Cohort health: variance over time, sample completion rate, checkpoint success.

Ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: Applied ML Platform (team alias: applied-ml-eval-platform@redwood.com).
- On-call for eval-orch: eng-sre rotation (see eng-sre/oncall-rotations).
- Incident escalation: Applied ML lead (Marco Hernandez) -> Eng Platform manager (Lena Ortiz).

Change history

- 2026-01-18: Initial published version (Aisha Patel).
- 2026-02-02: Adjusted default weights and added cache affinity window (reviewers: Marco Hernandez, Rina Sato).

Appendix: common troubleshooting commands

- List queued jobs: `curl -sS https://eval-orch.internal/api/v1/jobs?state=queued | jq .`
- Drain backfill on pool: `eval-orch ctl drain --pool a100-40g-int8-pool --mode backfill`
- Force resume job: `eval-orch ctl resume --job eval-2026-0009`
- Inspect checkpoint: `aws s3 ls s3://eval-artifacts/eval-2026-0009/checkpoint/`

References

- production-model-certification-checklist-2026 (model acceptance)
- quantization-profiles/kv-cache-quant-stability-audit-playbook-2025
- eval-harness/latency-sensitivity-eval-routing-fallback-protocol-2026

For questions or suggested changes, add a comment on this page or ping #eval-ops on Slack.

title: Anchor-based workload synthesis and probe seeding playbook
content:
Summary:

This playbook describes a repeatable process for synthesizing representative workload probes using an anchor-based strategy and for seeding those probes into our eval harness (eval-orchestrator and probe-farm). The goal is to improve coverage of rare but impactful workload slices (e.g., long-context, tokenization edgecases, multimodal anchors) and to make shadow/quantized evaluations more likely to catch regressions before promotion. This document covers architecture, synthesis heuristics, seeding cadence, metrics to monitor, and a triage procedure for failures that surface during these probes.

Motivation:

- Empirical coverage of real traffic is incomplete: production traffic contains long-tail combinations of user intent, formatting, and quantization sensitivity.
- Generic random probes miss structured anchors that reliably trigger failure modes (e.g., specific punctuation patterns, nested JSON payloads, language-mixing).
- Early detection of quantization-induced degradation requires probes that are both workload-anchored and quant-awareness-tagged.

When to use this playbook:

- Before promoting model artifacts from staging -> shadow -> canary.
- Prior to enabling a new quantization profile on Dedicated or Private.
- When telemetry identifies recurring unexplained quality drops on a slice with low sample counts.

Definitions and concepts:

- Anchor: a compact, high-leverage token sequence or feature (e.g., long code block, multilingual snippet, repeated enumerations, math-laden text) known to stress a model or inference path.
- Anchor seed: a synthesized example centered on one or more anchors.
- Probe: a single eval example run through the eval harness with deterministic seeds and telemetry capture.
- Probe farm: the service that schedules, executes, and stores probe runs (internal service name: probe-farm).
- Eval orchestrator: coordinates probe batches and routes runs to shadow/dedicated endpoints (internal service name: eval-orchestrator).

Architecture overview:

- Probe generation pipeline (anchor-extractor -> synth-engine -> probe-store).
- Eval scheduling (eval-orchestrator) that tags runs for quant-profile and routing policy.
- Telemetry collection (kinesis -> eval-store -> enrichment -> metrics).
- Alerting/triage integration (Prometheus alerts, Sentry events, regressions dashboard).

Synthesis heuristics (anchor extraction):

1. Anchor sources:
   - Telemetry-derived fingerprints: extract high-MI tokens from request text when a quality alert was observed.
   - Static catalog: known anchors curated by applied ML (e.g., "triple-backtick code blocks", "nested JSON with arrays", "RTL scripts + emojis").
   - Seeded generative transforms: take high-traffic utterances and apply controlled transforms (lengthening, shuffling lists, injecting noise).

2. Anchor ranking: score anchors by a composite score: frequency_in_failures * rarity_in-prod * severity_impact. Keep top-K anchors per week (K default 250).

3. Compositional probes: combine 1–3 anchors per probe to stress cross-slice interactions. Limit composite probes to combinations that appear in production fingerprints or are logically plausible.

Seeding strategy and cadence:

- Daily: add 50 new single-anchor probes and replay prior failing probes.
- Weekly: add 100 composite-anchor probes prioritized by cross-slice coverage delta.
- Pre-promotion: run a full anchor sweep (all anchors ranked above threshold) through the promotion pipeline (staging -> shadow -> canary).

Probe metadata and tagging (required fields):

- probe_id: UUID string
- anchors: comma-separated anchor tags (e.g., codeblock,long_context,rtl)
- origin: telemetry|catalog|generated
- intended_models: comma-separated model ids (e.g., rwd-7b-v2, rwd-13b-quant8)
- quant_profile: name or "none"
- deterministic_seed: integer (for eval reproducibility)

Sample probe JSON (stored in probe-store):

{
  "probe_id": "uuid-1234-abcd",
  "anchors": "codeblock,long_context",
  "origin": "generated",
  "intended_models": "rwd-7b-v2,rwd-7b-quant8",
  "quant_profile": "q8_telemetry_tuned",
  "deterministic_seed": "42",
  "input": "```python\ndef factorial(n):\n    if n <= 1:\n        return 1\n    return n * factorial(n-1)\n```\nDescribe the complexity and edgecases..."
}

Integration with quantization profiles:

- For each probe, synth-engine must schedule runs across: float baseline, quant-profile variants in the promotion matrix, and fallback policy variants (e.g., hybrid FP16 codepath).
- Track a per-probe quality delta between baseline and quantized variants. We consider a probe failure if: (absolute_quality_drop >= 3 percentage points) OR (semantic-fidelity-score decrease >= 2%). Thresholds are tuned per workload bucket.

Quality signals and telemetry fields to capture:

- generation_latency_ms (median and p95)
- token_count_input and token_count_output
- semantic_similarity_baseline_vs_variant (0-1 float)
- exact_match_for_anchor_tokens (boolean / percent covered)
- logit_gap_or_confidence_delta (float)
- failure_mode_tag (string): hallucination|truncation|formatting_error|execution_mismatch

Alerting and SLOs:

- Probe guard SLO: 99.9% of scheduled probes must complete end-to-end in 24 hours.
- Quality guard: for anchor-ranked probes in the top-100, any model/quant pair with semantic_similarity_baseline_vs_variant < 0.90 triggers a P1 evaluation ticket and blocks promotion.
- Latency guard: p95 generation_latency_ms increase > 2x relative to baseline for top-100 probes triggers investigation (SLO owner: Runtime Performance Team).

Runbook: triage for failing probes (order of operations):

1. Confirm: check probe-run logs in eval-store and the attached artifacts (response diffs, token-level alignments).
2. Re-run: schedule a deterministic re-run with the same seed to rule out transient infra flakiness.
3. Cross-quant check: compare baseline float -> all quant variants. If only quant variants fail, mark as "quant-sensitive" and escalate to Quant Team.
4. Regression bisect: use automated-regression-bisect tool to identify the first failing model commit or kernel change. Attach bisect report to the ticket.
5. Create remediation plan: options include quant-profile tweak, local FP fallback for anchor class, model retune, or probe exclusion if proven noise.
6. Canary rollback policy: if canary fails on >5% of top-100 anchors, rollback canary deployment and create incident.

Owners and responsibilities:

- Probe generation and synth-engine: Applied ML (owner: Priya Desai).
- Probe execution and scheduling: Eval infra (owner: Marco Nguyen).
- Quant-profile tuning & fallback policies: Serving runtime / Quant Team (owner: Lin Zhao).
- Triage and incident coordination: Eng SRE + Applied ML on-call rotation.

Examples and CLI snippets:

- Add a new anchor to the static catalog:

$ rw-probectl add-anchor --name "nested-json-arrays" --pattern '{"items": ["<var>", ...]}' --owner "applied-ml" --tags "json,structure"

- Seed a generated probe batch:

$ rw-probectl seed-batch --source generated --anchors "nested-json-arrays,emoji-mix" --count 50 --quant-profiles "q8_telemetry_tuned" --seed 20260302

- Query recent failing probes:

$ rw-probectl list-failures --since 7d --min-severity 1 --anchor-tag long_context

Configuration examples (YAML snippet for eval-orchestrator routing rules):

routing_rules:
  - name: "quant-sensitive-shadow"
    match_anchors: ["codeblock","long_context","nested_json"]
    prioritize_models: ["rwd-7b-v2"]
    route_to: ["shadow-cluster-01"]
    quant_profiles: ["q8_telemetry_tuned","fp16_fallback"]

Operational notes and best practices:

- Keep anchor catalog explicit and auditable. Each anchor entry must include an author, justification, and production fingerprints if available.
- Limit compositional probes during high-cost evaluation windows to control budget. Flag these to finance when totals exceed monthly threshold.
- If a probe repeatedly flakes, mark with "transient" and add additional diagnostics (GPU traces, kernel selection logs).

Appendix: telemetry schema (CSV header example)

probe_id,run_id,timestamp,model,quant_profile,anchors,latency_ms,semantic_similarity,token_in,token_out,failure_mode

References and related pages:

- Eval mesh and workload fingerprinting (internal reference): /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026
- Quant profile synthesis playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024

Change log:

- 2026-01-15: created initial playbook (Priya Desai).
- 2026-02-20: tightened quant failure thresholds and added routing YAML example (Lin Zhao).
- 2026-03-02: added CLI examples and clarified ownership matrix (Sofia Alvarez).

title: Evaluation Horizon and Holdout Strategy 2026
content:
Summary:

This doc defines the evaluation horizon and holdout strategy used by Redwood's eval harness to ensure robust, reproducible model quality signals across short- and long-term windows. It prescribes how to synthesize probes, anchor holdout sets, schedule evaluation horizons, and measure stability across traffic slices and quantization variants. The goal is to provide a single, auditable approach teams can adopt when promoting models to hosted, dedicated, or private deployments.

Scope:

- Applies to all model onboarding and promotion workflows that use eval-mesh and probe-orch orchestration.
- Covers generation and curation of holdout probe sets, horizon windowing, stratified sampling, and telemetry signals used for gating.
- Does not replace safety-specific sandboxing; follow the safety-sandbox-fingerprint-certification procedure for high-risk deployments.

Definitions:

- Evaluation horizon: a fixed calendar window (e.g., 7/30/90 days) used to aggregate probe results and compute stability metrics.
- Anchor holdout: an immutable subset of probes reserved for continuous regression detection (not used for model tuning).
- Rolling probe set: probes refreshed every N days to surface distributional shift.

Design principles:

1. Immutable anchors for regression detection: keep at least one anchor holdout per workload family that is not mutated during model tuning.
2. Multi-horizon monitoring: compute metrics over 7d (fast feedback), 30d (stability), and 90d (regression drift).
3. Stratified holdouts: guarantee representation across high-value slices (e.g., top customers, long-context queries, non-English).
4. Reproducible probe synthesis with seeds: all synthetic probes must be generated with explicit RNG seeds and stored in probe metadata.

Holdout composition and sizing:

- Anchor holdout (immutable): 1,200 probes per workload family.
- Short-term rolling set: 5,000 probes refreshed weekly with TTL = 60 days.
- Production mirroring samples: 0.1% of live traffic (sampled reservoir) kept for 7-day horizon checks.

Sizing rationale:

- 1,200 anchors provide statistical power to detect medium-effect-size regressions (Cohen's d ≈ 0.3) with alpha=0.05 across common metrics (accuracy/F1/semantic-similarity).
- Rolling sets prioritize breadth and recentness to detect distributional shift while keeping annotation costs bounded.

Probe synthesis and anchoring procedure (step-by-step):

1. Define workload family and slices. Label owner and add tags: e.g., workload:email-drafting, slices:[long-context,enterprise-customer].
2. Use probe-orch synth generator with a fixed seed to create candidate probes. Command: 

   $ probe-orch synth --workload email-drafting --seed 20260210 --size 6000 --template-file templates/email-primers.yaml --output probes/candidates_20260210.jsonl

3. Run automatic coverage and adversarial checks: run coverage-checker and adversarial-noise-scanner. Exclude probes failing policy thresholds.

4. Reserve anchors: deterministically select 1,200 probes from candidates_20260210.jsonl using the same seed + offset. Persist anchor set to storage path: s3://redwood-eval/anchors/email-drafting/anchor-v1.jsonl and lock metadata: {anchor_id, created_at, seed}. (See metadata convention below.)

5. Create rolling set by sampling remaining candidates stratified by slice weight. Attach TTL and refresh schedule.

Evaluation horizons and metric computation:

- Fast feedback (7d): used by model engineers for micro-canary decisions. Alerts for metric delta > 5% relative change.
- Stability window (30d): used for promotion gating. Acceptance requires: RSI (Response Stability Index) >= 0.985 and no critical safety sentinel failures.
- Drift window (90d): used by platform to detect slow regressions and need for retrain or prompt repair. Trigger: monotonic decline in RSI over 3 successive 30d windows totaling > 3% decrease.

Metric definitions used in gating:

- Response Stability Index (RSI): an aggregate [0..1] combining semantic-similarity (Embedding cosine mean), repetition rate, and calibration bias. Thresholds: RSI >= 0.985 for green, 0.96-0.985 yellow, <0.96 red.
- Latency SLA pass rate: p95 <= 250ms for hosted small models; p95 <= 400ms for larger context models. Thresholds are configurable per route.

Integration with eval-harness services:

- eval-mesh: schedules cross-region evaluation jobs. Use queue: eval-high-priority for anchor validation runs.
- probe-orch: generates and manages probe lifecycle.
- quant-eval: runs quantized artifact gating; must be invoked for any model variant with a quant-profile.

Sample YAML holdout config (store with model promotion artifact):

---
holdout_config:
  anchor_id: "email-drafting-anchor-v1"
  anchor_size: 1200
  rolling_size: 5000
  rolling_refresh_days: 7
  mirror_sample_pct: 0.001  # 0.1% of prod traffic
  stratify_by: ["customer_tier","language","context_length_bucket"]
  rng_seed: 20260210
  locked: true
---

Promotion gating checklist (for model owners):

1. Anchor run: run eval-mesh against anchor set for 7d and 30d horizons. Export RSI, per-slice deltas, and failures.
2. Quant-eval: run quantization profile suite with mixed-precision and int8 variants. Verify quant-fallback-quality SLA.
3. Canary: deploy canary traffic split 1% for 24 hours; monitor RSI and latency. Roll back if RSI drop > 1.5% in 24h or p95 latency breach.
4. Approval: collect sign-offs from reviewer list and add to promotion ticket.

Operational thresholds and alerting:

- Alert: RSI drop > 1.5% within a 24-hour window for anchor set — Pager (SRE oncall).
- Warning: any per-slice RSI delta > 3% on 30d window — alert to owning team Slack #ml-quality.
- Quant alert: any quantized model where top-3 semantic similarity buckets drop more than 2% vs float baseline — post to #model-onboarding and create triage ticket.

Oncall and triage playbook (high-level):

1. Detection: Alert hits with anchor_id and metric snapshot URL.
2. Triage runbook: run quick-delta script to isolate top 10 failing probes: 

   $ eval-mesh quick-delta --anchor s3://redwood-eval/anchors/email-drafting/anchor-v1.jsonl --candidate s3://redwood-eval/candidates/email-drafting/20260216/candidate.jsonl --top 10 --out /tmp/delta_10.jsonl

3. If failing probes show prompt-sensitivity or tokenization-regression, engage applied-ml team and open a regression-bisect job (see automated-regression-bisect-and-blame-assistant).

Ownership and links:

- Owner: Leila Chen (Applied ML, model-onboarding)
- SRE contact: Ravi Iyer (eng-sre)
- Related pages: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-orchestration-2026, /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails/response-stability-index-calibration-and-deployment-2026

Appendix: probe metadata convention (flat JSON per probe)

| field | type | description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| probe_id | string | stable UUID |
| workload | string | workload family |
| slice_tags | list[string] | slice tags |
| gen_seed | int | RNG seed used |
| template | string | template reference id |
| created_at | date | ISO date |
| anchor_flag | boolean | true if part of anchor |

Example probe JSON line (single-line JSON for storage):

{"probe_id":"8f4b1f4a-3b2d-4c9a-9f2d-1a2c3b4d5e6f","workload":"email-drafting","slice_tags":["long-context","enterprise"],"gen_seed":20260210,"template":"templates/email-primers.yaml:salary-negotiation","created_at":"2026-02-10","anchor_flag":true}

Governance and change control:

- Any mutation to an anchor set requires a documented change request with statistical justification and a reviewer from applied-ml and product quality.
- Anchor versioning: anchor-vN naming convention; never delete old anchors.

Appendix B: quick reference thresholds (copyable)

- RSI green: >=0.985
- RSI yellow: 0.96 - 0.985
- RSI red: <0.96
- Anchor size baseline: 1200 probes
- Rolling refresh cadence: 7 days
- Mirror sample: 0.1% production traffic

If you are onboarding a new workload and need help synthesizing anchors, open an onboarding ticket and tag @applied-ml. For urgent regressions, follow the eval-oncall-runbook-for-model-regression-debugging guide.

Document history:

- 2026-02-10: Draft created by Leila Chen.
- 2026-02-17: Added quant-eval integration notes and thresholds (Ravi Iyer review).

title: SLO-driven eval gating and quantization handoff playbook
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines an SLO-driven gating strategy for automated evaluation pipelines and prescribes the operational handoff for quantized model artifacts into shadow and production-serving lanes. The goal is to prevent quantization or performance regressions from reaching customers while enabling fast, reproducible promotion for models that meet both quality and latency/cost objectives.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all model promotions that include a quantized artifact (int8, 4-bit, hybrid-mixed precision) or runtime kernel/packing changes.
- Covers: automated eval gates (pre-promotion), manual triage escalation, shadow deployment gating, and final rollout controls.
- Excludes security-only certification (handled by security-and-compliance).

Definitions:
- Eval Gate: A checkpoint in the CI/eval pipeline that requires pass/fail criteria before artifacts move downstream.
- Promotion Candidate: A model version + quant artifact produced by the quantization pipeline.
- Shadow Lane: Isolated serving environment with production-like traffic for fidelity and performance validation.
- Delta SLO: The allowed deviation from baseline for a given metric (e.g., -1.5% mean accuracy).

SLO matrix (examples):
| Metric                        | Baseline (prod model) | Allowed Delta (gate) | Action on breach       | Monitoring source           |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------|----------------------|-------------------------|-----------------------------|
| Mean ROUGE / BLEU / F1        | 0.78                  | -0.015               | Block promotion        | eval-summaries, slices API  |
| Latency P95 (ms)              | 180                   | +40ms                | Block promotion        | perf-traces, runtime-metrics|
| Token cost / 1k tokens (USD)  | 0.032                 | +10%                 | Warn + require signoff    | cost-ledger                 |
| Response Stability Index (RSI)| 0.94                  | -0.02                | Block promotion        | stability-service           |
| Functioncall success rate     | 99.6%                 | -0.5%                | Manual triage            | functioncall-metrics       |

Gating rules (high-level):
1. Unit-level evals (fast): run on PR; must pass regression sentinel tests and tokenization sanity checks. Failure: block PR merge.
2. Slice-level evals (medium): run in CI-eval cluster against prioritized slice set (latency-sensitive, high-value intents). Failure: create regression ticket; require owner triage and signoff to proceed to shadow.
3. Shadow smoke (slow): promote candidate to shadow lane with 1% production traffic multiplexed for 24–72 hours. Monitor SLOs; any block-level metric breach for > 30 minutes triggers automatic demotion.
4. Final rollout: if shadow passes, schedule staggered rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with canary hold windows and automatic rollback on live regressions.

Quantization handoff checklist (artifact producer responsibilities):
- Produce deterministic artifact bundle: model.card, quant.metadata.json, kernel-config.yml, and checksums.
- Attach eval manifests: commit hash for eval harness, slice-set id, random seeds used, and perf seed trace.
- Run local safety checks: tokenization parity, functioncall smoke, and small-sample coherence tests.
- Upload artifact to artifact repo with tag: quant/<model>-<version>-<quant-profile>-<date>. Example: quant/gpt-style-1.4-q4_1-20260112

Handoff YAML (example):
---
artifact_tag: "quant/gpt-style-1.4-q4_1-20260112"
producer: "quant-team/autoquant-v2"
eval_manifest: "evals/manifest/2026-01-10-quick.json"
required_gates:
  - unit_sentinels
  - slice_regressions
  - shadow_smoke
promotion_policy:
  shadow_duration_hours: 48
  canary_steps: [5, 25, 100]
  rollback_on: [response_stability_index, p95_latency, mean_fidelity]
---

Operational runbook: step-by-step
1) Submit artifact: producer uploads artifact and triggers "eval-harness run" with tag.
   CLI: eval-harness run --artifact quant/gpt-style-1.4-q4_1-20260112 --slices priority-slice-set --parallel 12
2) Fast gate: unit tests and sentinel checks run (target: < 30 minutes). If any sentinel fails, pipeline creates an automated regression incident and marks the artifact failed.
3) Slice gate: run full slice suite (target: 2–6 hours). Summary report posted to /evals/reports/<artifact_tag>.
4) If slice gate passes, orchestrator triggers shadow promotion job. Shadow config: 1% traffic, 48h, telemetry piped to shadow namespace. 
5) Monitoring and alerting: paging thresholds are configured in monitoring-playbooks:
   - RSI drop >= 0.02 sustained for 30m -> P1 on-call page
   - Latency P95 exceed baseline + 40ms for 4 consecutive 5m windows -> P1
   - Token cost > baseline + 15% for 1h -> SRE on-call.
6) Failures during shadow: run quick rollback script and open triage.
   CLI: eval-harness rollback --shadow quant/gpt-style-1.4-q4_1-20260112 --reason "p95_latency"
7) After successful shadow, schedule canary rollout with annotated ticket linking eval report, perf traces, and signoffs.

Triage decision tree (condensed):
- Block-level metric breach? -> Immediate demotion and assign regression-owner -> create incident -> run bisect (if multiple quant profiles) -> if root cause is quant param, attempt localized re-quant or adjust kernel config.
- Cost regression only? -> Flag for product + finance review; require explicit product signoff to proceed.
- Small quality delta within allowed but customer-sensitive slice affected? -> Run targeted human review on slice, consider per-tenant hold.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Quantization team: produce artifacts, include metadata, respond to quant-specific failures.
- Applied ML / Eval team: owns eval manifests, slice prioritization, and gate automation.
- SRE: owns rollout orchestration, shadow routing, and emergency rollback tooling.
- Product owner: approves cost deviations and tenant-risk signoffs.

Metrics to publish with every promotion candidate (minimum):
- eval_summary_url (string)
- delta_metrics: {"rsi": "-0.006", "p95_latency_ms": "+12"} (as JSON blob in report)
- perf_trace_id
- artifact_checksums

Common failure modes and remediations:
- Non-deterministic eval results across seeds: increase sample seeds to 10 and run multi-seed aggregator; check for tokenization nondeterminism.
- Latency regression only on long contexts: add context-limited micro-bench and consider KV cache tuning or kernel selection override.
- Functioncall mismatch after quantization: run functioncall-priming harness and verify call-signature fidelity; if failing, mark quant profile as unsuited.

Fast rollback checklist (emergency):
1. Set routing to previous stable artifact: routingctl set-default <service> --artifact <stable-tag>
2. Pause ongoing shadow/canary promotions.
3. Open incident with tags: quant, regression, auto-rollback.
4. Triage owner runs bisect on quant parameter set and uploads findings to incident.

Promotion signoff template (required in ticket):
- Artifact tag:
- Eval run id and link:
- Shadow duration and traffic: (hours, %)
- Key delta metrics (table): RSI, P95 latency, top-5 slice regressions
- Risk notes and mitigation plan:
- Approvals: quant lead, applied-ml lead, SRE lead, product manager

Appendix: example eval-harness commands and useful endpoints
- Start controlled eval: eval-harness run --artifact <tag> --slices <slice-set> --output /evals/reports/<tag>.json
- Promote to shadow: eval-orchestrator promote --artifact <tag> --lane shadow --traffic 1% --duration 48h
- Query stability: curl -s "https://monitoring.internal/api/v1/slices/<slice-id>/stability?artifact=<tag>"

References and related policies:
- Eval orchestration: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-workflow-optimizer-for-mixed-slo-scenarios-2026
- Quant safety baseline: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024
- Shadow deployment pattern: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/shadow-deployments

Revision history:
- 2025-09-12: Created initial draft (Marisol Chen)
- 2025-10-23: Added shadow demotion windows and RSI thresholds (review feedback)
- 2026-01-18: Aligned monitoring thresholds with SRE playbooks and added rollback CLI example (Rina Sato)

Contact: marisol@redwood-inference.internal for questions or proposed updates.

title: Crossroad Eval Orchestration and Quant Compatibility Blueprint
content:
Overview

Purpose: This blueprint defines a pragmatic, auditable contract between the evaluation harness, prompt/catalog stewardship, model onboarding, quantization handover, and regression triage systems. It codifies the runtime and offline checks required to promote a model variant across environments (shadow -> staged -> canary -> prod) when quantized artifacts or prompt transformations are involved. The goal is to reduce surprise regressions while preserving inference cost improvements.

Scope and audience
