2. Run local repro with `eval-harness run --bundle <bundle_id> --slice <slice_id> --seed 0..4` and capture diffs.
3. If repro successful, run `bisect-model-variants --start <previous_promoted> --end <candidate>` to identify the first model introducing delta.
4. If bisect points to a recent model promotion, trigger automatic rollback per Deploy Rollback playbook and notify stakeholders.
5. If bisect inconclusive, escalate to Model Regression oncall and attach probe bundle and anchor outputs.

Quick CLI examples

- Validate manifest locally:
  eval-harness validate-manifest ./slice_manifest.json

- Run a targeted probe slice locally:
  eval-harness run --bundle ./rb-probe-2026-031 --slice payment-instructions-vague --samples 200 --output ./tmp/results.jsonl

- Produce anchor report for onboarding:
  eval-harness anchor-report --bundle ./rb-probe-2026-031 --out ./tmp/anchor_report.json

Telemetry and observability contract

Every shadow run must emit a standard set of telemetry fields (JSON lines) tagged with bundle_id and slice_id:

- bundle_id (string)
- slice_id (string)
- request_id (uuid)
- model_variant (string)
- latency_ms (number)
- token_count (int)
- perplexity_window (number)
- rsi (number)
- safety_flag (bool)

These fields should be mapped into the central eval metrics pipeline. Dashboards must include: slice-level RSI trends, anchor KL trends, median latency by slice, and failure rate by anchor tag.

Promotion checklist (before scheduling canary)

1. Manifest schema validated (CI job).
2. Anchor fidelity within thresholds on eval harness.
3. Conciliation status: accepted or merged.
4. Shadow-run smoke pass (>= 95% success on non-safety anchors).
5. Resource perf check on representative instance type passed.
6. Runbook and rollback owner assigned.

Ownership and contacts

- Eval owner (creates bundle): role/eval-engineer@redwood.ai
- Onboarding owner: role/model-onboard@redwood.ai
- Shadow operator (if automated): eng-platform-shadow@redwood.ai
- Regression oncall: pager oncall-model-regress@redwood.ai

Appendix A — Example reconciler output (diff summary)

```
reconciler_summary: {
  "incoming_slice": "payment-instructions-vague",
  "matched_existing": "payment-instructions",
  "overlap_pct": 42,
  "resolution": "merged_as_alias",
  "merged_fields": ["expected_failure_mode","anchors"]
}
```

Appendix B — Minimal local smoke test script

```
#!/bin/bash
BUNDLE=$1
SLICE=$2
set -e
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -U redwood-eval-harness
eval-harness validate-manifest $BUNDLE/slice_manifest.json
eval-harness run --bundle $BUNDLE --slice $SLICE --samples 50 --output ./smoke.jsonl
python tools/anchor_check.py --input ./smoke.jsonl --anchors $BUNDLE/anchors --threshold 0.88
```

Notes and open questions

- Should we add a canonical schema registry for slice definitions to avoid subtle tokenization mismatches? Proposal: small JSON Schema + example canonical tokenizer config embedded in manifest.
- When slices are merged, how should historical metrics be backfilled? Current plan: annotate historical dashboards with alias resolution, do not rewrite historic IDs.

References

- Eval harness: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026
- Onboarding readiness matrix: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026
- Regression triage: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026

Change log

- 2026-02-10 (Riley Chen) — Initial draft and example manifests.
- 2026-03-01 (Riley Chen) — Added conciliation decision matrix, telemetry contract, and CLI examples.

title: Federated Probe Prioritization and Orchestration Playbook
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines a federated probe orchestration pattern and a deterministic prioritization schema for the Redwood eval harness. It is intended to align evaluation traffic across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments (including VPC/on-prem shadowing) so that scarce eval capacity is used to maximize signal for regression detection, quantization stability, and rollout safety while respecting cost and privacy constraints.

Scope and motivation:
- Scope: evaluation probes executed by the central eval mesh and by regional probe farms. Includes both synthetic probes (generated test cases) and production-derived probes (anonymized slices).
- Motivation: rising eval volume, heterogeneous capacity (quantized vs FP16 runtime), and mixed confidentiality requirements have caused uneven coverage. We need a single prioritization policy plus lightweight orchestration controls that teams can tune per-model and per-customer.

Goals and constraints:
1) Maximize early detection of high-severity regressions (safety, hallucination, critical-slice failure).
2) Provide deterministic probe scheduling so rollouts are comparable across variants.
3) Respect data residency and privacy: probes tagged restricted must not run on non-compliant infra.
4) Keep per-probe compute budget and global daily budget enforceable.

Definitions (for this playbook):
- Probe: a single eval input + expected behavior metadata (annotation, slice id, weight).
- Probe farm: a regional execution pool (can be private customer infra).
- Federated orchestration: central scheduler issues probe assignments and collects results; execution can be delegated to local farms when required.
- Critical slice: probes that exercise high-risk behaviors (e.g., PII handling, code generation safety).

High-level architecture:
1) Central scheduler (EvalOrch service) maintains a prioritized queue and global budgets.
2) Regional executors (probe-farms) subscribe to assignment topics and pull tasks compatible with local policies (capacity, confidentiality, runtime).
3) Telemetry collectors emit per-probe trace: latency, token-usage, success indicators, and model-version tag.
4) Aggregator computes per-slice stability metrics and alerts guardrails.

Prioritization strategy (score formula):
We compute a numeric priority score for each probe. Score is normalized 0-100.
- Base factors:
  - SeverityMultiplier (S): 1 (low) | 2 (medium) | 4 (high)
  - RecencyBoost (R): 1 + min(0.5, days_since_last_run / 30)  (encourages recent slices)
  - FailureDelta (F): min(3, historical_failure_rate_ratio)
  - ComputeCostPenalty (C): 1 / (1 + estimated_token_cost)
  - ConfidentialityPenalty (P): 0 if allowed; 0.1 if restricted and farm supports it; -Infinity if forbidden

Score = 100 * normalize( S * R * F * C * (1 - P) )
Note: normalize rescales scores across the candidate set for a scheduling window.

Priority buckets (examples):
- P0 (score >= 90): immediate, run on all available compatible farms; require human review if failure detected.
- P1 (70-89): scheduled within 1 hour, prefer Dedicated farms.
- P2 (40-69): batchable within 24 hours.
- P3 (<40): opportunistic, low-cost synthetic probes.

Table: example probe metadata (presented as text table)
- Columns: probe_id | slice_tag | severity | estimated_tokens | residency_tag | last_run_days | hist_fail_rate
- Example row: probe_2026_42 | code-injection | high | 120 | eu-only | 3 | 0.18

Orchestration patterns and routing policies:
1) Local-first: if regional farm has compatible runtime and confidentiality, schedule locally to reduce egress and latency.
2) Central-augment: when local capacity is saturated, push only P0/P1 probes to central Dedicated capacity.
3) Shadow-tiering: during model rollout, use a two-phase routing rule: replicate a fraction of live traffic-derived probes to a dedicated shadow pool (canary) and route synthetic high-severity probes to a separate high-fidelity farm.

Privacy and compliance rules:
- Probes tagged with residency: "eu-only", "us-only", "customer-A-vpc" must only run on farms with matching attestations.
- PII probes must be flagged and will only run in private farms or on redwood-hosted private lanes with KMS-enabled logging.
- Audit trail: every probe execution must emit a signed execution event with model_version, farm_id, and a confidentiality_label.

Operational runbook: scheduling and triage (numbered steps):
1) Submission: Authoring team submits probe bundle with metadata (JSON schema example below).
2) Preflight validation: EvalOrch validates residency, estimated token cost, and required annotator labels.
3) Scoring: compute priority score and assign to bucket.
4) Dispatch: assign to farm(s) per routing policy and quotas.
5) Execution: farm runs probe, collects telemetry, and returns result.
6) Aggregation: aggregator updates slice stability dashboards and triage queues.
7) Alerting: if a P0 probe fails beyond threshold, open regression ticket and trigger oncall paging.

Probe bundle JSON (example snippet):
{
  "probe_id": "probe_2026_42",
  "slice_tag": "code-injection",
  "severity": "high",
  "residency": "eu-only",
  "estimated_tokens": 120,
  "annotations": ["expected_footnote", "safe_answer"]
}

Triage escalation criteria:
- Immediate high-severity regression: any P0 probe with delta >= 2x historical failure rate -> Pager (SRE + MLE) and block model rollout.
- Persistent mid-severity regressions (>= 3 P1 failures in 24h) -> create regression ticket, assign primary owner from model-onboarding team.
- Quantization instability: if quantized artifact shows token-deviation > 5% vs FP16 baseline across an ensemble of 50 probes in a slice -> mark artifact as 'requires-retrain/retune'.

Instrumentation and dashboards (minimum):
- Per-probe result stream (success, error class, latency, token_usage).
- Slice stability heatmap: 7/30/90 day windows.
- Priority queue occupancy and average wait per bucket.
- Budget burn-rate panel (compute units/day) and per-farm utilization.

Onboarding checklist for new probe producers (short):
1) Register schema and ownership in the probe registry.
2) Supply residency and severity tags.
3) Provide baseline FP16 and candidate artifacts for a 2k-sample shadow run.
4) Validate annotations with at least 3 human reviewers for safety-critical slices.

Rollout and tuning knobs (config snippets described):
- daily_global_budget: 1e6 compute_units
- per_model_max_pct_of_budget: 10
- p0_replication_factor: 3 (number of farms to run concurrently)
- quant_fidelity_threshold: 0.05 (relative token-output deviation)

Ownership and SLAs:
- EvalOrch service: Eng - Eval Platform (oncall team: eng-platform@redwood.ai).
- Probe farms: regional infra teams (eu-farm, us-west-farm, private-farm-ops).
- SLO: 95% of P0 probes scheduled within 10 minutes; 99% of P1 scheduled within 1 hour.

Example incidents and mitigations (short):
- Incident: large synthetic probe flood saturated eu-farm, delaying P0 runs.
  Mitigation: enacted central-augment policy and raised per-farm P0 reserve to 15% of capacity.
- Incident: mis-tagged residency allowed PII probes on non-compliant farm.
  Mitigation: added stronger preflight residency checks and signed attestations.

Change control and rollout plan for this playbook:
1) Draft -> internal review (2 weeks).
2) Pilot on eu-farm with a set of 500 probes (4 weeks).
3) Measure KPIs (detection lead-time, false-positive triage rate, budget delta) and iterate.
4) Full rollout with config default in EvalOrch (6 weeks).

Related pages and references:
- Eval mesh design doc: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026
- Probe farm onboarding guide: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/probe-farm-orchestration-for-rare-regressions-2026

Appendix: quick CLI examples (pseudo):
- Submit probes: redwood-eval submit --bundle probes.json --priority auto
- Inspect queue: redwood-eval queue --list --bucket P0
- Force-run probe: redwood-eval run --probe probe_2026_42 --farm eu-farm

Contact and owners: Maya Chen (mchen@redwood.ai) for orchestration policy questions; Diego Alvarez for telemetry contracts.

Revision history:
- 2026-01-15: created by Maya Chen
- 2026-02-10: updated scoring normalization and added P0 replication guidance by Priya Natarajan

title: Eval mesh topology and slotting cookbook
content:
Overview:
This cookbook defines the recommended topology, slotting strategies, and operational patterns for the eval mesh used across Redwood’s evaluation fleet. The document covers: mesh topology patterns, slot types and sizing; the slot allocation algorithm; cost and fidelity accounting; backfill and rebalancing strategies; safety and privacy gates for shadow workloads; and an operational runbook for deploying topology changes.

Goals:
- Provide a predictable, cost-aware mapping from eval workloads (probes, shadow traffic, backfills) to scarce evaluation capacity.
- Minimize eval latency for high-priority probes while maximizing overall probe coverage within budget.
- Ensure safe rollouts and auditable chargebacks for tenant-aware evals.

Audience:
- Evaluation platform engineers (owners of eval-orch and shadow-mesh).
- Onboarding engineers preparing probe manifests and budgets.
- SREs responsible for eval fleet capacity and cost allocation.

Key services and components:
- eval-orch: central orchestrator that assigns probes to slots and emits allocation events.
- probe-fabricator: generates synthetic probes and seeds shadow traffic.
- shadow-mesh: per-cluster runtime that executes shadow workloads; supports isolation modes (tenant, mixed, anonymized).
- telemetry-ingest: collects token-level latency/cost/time-series for evals.
- eval-ledger: accounting service that records slot consumption and cost attributions.

Definitions:
1) Slot: a reserved execution slot on the eval mesh. Slots have attributes: tier, cpu/gpu profile, qps limit, and cost weight.
2) Probe class: a logically grouped set of probes (e.g., functioncall-stability, longcontext-coherence, embedding-drift).
3) Fidelity budget: the allocation of high-fidelity slots for a probe class over a time window.

Topology patterns (recommended):
A) Hierarchical mesh (default) — used for most workloads:
   - Global control plane (eval-orch) + regional shadow-mesh clusters.
   - Each regional mesh exposes three slot pools: fast (low-latency), steady (balanced), bulk (throughput-optimized).
   - Routing policy: prefer local fast -> local steady -> cross-region steady -> bulk.

B) Isolated shadow mesh (sensitive tenants) — for regulated customers:
   - Dedicated shadow cluster with tenant-only slots and KMS-protected probes.
   - No cross-tenant colocation; telemetry scrubbed at source.

Slot types and sizing (reference table):
| slot_type | cpu/gpu | qps_limit | median_latency_target | cost_weight | recommended_use_cases |
| fast      | 1xA100 | 50       | < 40ms                | 5x         | interactive probes, micro-canaries |
| steady    | 1xA100 | 200      | < 120ms               | 2x         | baseline continuous probes        |
| bulk      | 2xA100 | 1000     | best-effort            | 1x         | backfills, large-scale simulations|

Slot allocation algorithm (summary):
1. Ingest probe manifest with metadata: priority (P0..P3), fidelity_required (high/medium/low), probe_weight, tenant_id, SLA_window.
2. Compute effective score = priority_weight * fidelity_multiplier / expected_tokens_per_probe.
3. Run candidate selection: try to place in same-region fast pool if score >= fast_threshold; otherwise steady; if no fit and probe is low-fidelity, schedule into bulk with sampling.
4. Perform cost check against probe class fidelity budget in eval-ledger; if budget overrun, enqueue for token-sampled run or reject with recommendation.

Allocation heuristics and thresholds (tunable knobs):
- priority_weight: P0=1.0 (critical), P1=0.6, P2=0.3, P3=0.1
- fidelity_multiplier: high=1.0, medium=0.6, low=0.2
- fast_threshold: 0.7
- steady_threshold: 0.3
- backfill_sampling_rate (for bulk): default 0.05 (5%)

Cost and fidelity accounting:
- Eval-ledger records: slot_id, probe_manifest_id, start_ts, end_ts, tokens_processed, cost_estimate.
- Monthly billing export includes: tenant_id, probe_class, total_tokens, slot-weighted-cost.
- Fidelity budget alerts: generate when projected spend > 80% of allocated monthly fidelity budget for probe class.

Backfill and rebalancing policy:
- Trigger conditions: underutilization > 20% for 15m OR overload (queue depth > 2000).
- Backfill steps:
  1) Identify candidate low-priority low-fidelity probes for bulk migration.
  2) Apply progressive sampling ramp (0% -> 5% -> 25% over 30m) with telemetry gates.
  3) Monitor fidelity signal (response-stability-index, latency-tail) — abort if degradation > configured delta.
- Rebalancing (auto): every 10 minutes, eval-orch computes target distribution and migrates slots with live cutover window of 2 minutes.

Safety, privacy, and gating:
- All shadow traffic must be redacted by probe-fabricator before entering telemetry-ingest.
- Sensitive-probe flag triggers isolated shadow-mesh placement.
- Rollout gating: new topology rules must pass canary on 3 regional meshes for at least 24h with no fidelity or latency regression > 2x baseline.

Operational runbook: topology change flow
1) Draft topology change PR (config: pools, thresholds, weightings) and post to #eval-ops.
2) Create an experiment manifest in eval-orch with scope=canary (regions: us-west-2, eu-central-1).
3) Dry-run allocation for 24h (simulation mode) and gather: slot fill curves, projected ledger spend, telemetry delta.
4) If dry-run passes, enable canary with 1% of global probe volume for 24h.
5) Escalation criteria (immediately rollback if any fires):
   - fidelity_delta > 3% for P0 probes
   - latency tail (p99) increase > 150ms for fast slots
   - spending rate > 2x projection
6) Gradually increase canary (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) with 12h observation windows between steps.

Example slotting config (YAML example):
---
slot_pools:
  - name: fast
    gpu: a100-40gb
    concurrency: 50
    weight: 5
    allocation_threshold: 0.7
    owner: eval-platform@redwood.ai
  - name: steady
    gpu: a100-40gb
    concurrency: 200
    weight: 2
    allocation_threshold: 0.3
    owner: eval-platform@redwood.ai
  - name: bulk
    gpu: 2xa100
    concurrency: 1000
    weight: 1
    sampling_rate: 0.05
    owner: eval-platform@redwood.ai
---

Probe manifest fields (example):
- probe_id: pc-2026-485
- probe_class: longcontext-coherence-v2
- priority: P1
- fidelity_required: high
- expected_tokens: 1200
- sensitive: false
- owner: search-team@redwood.ai

Telemetry and alerting knobs to configure for topology rollouts:
- response-stability-index (RSI) delta alert: > 2x baseline -> sev-2
- p99 latency increase (fast slots): > 150ms -> sev-2
- fidelity-budget burn rate: projected > 80% -> paging to cost-ops
- slot-fill anomaly (< 10% utilization across 30m) -> investigate potential overprovisioning

Debugging checklist (when probes are not scheduled or fail):
1) Check eval-orch allocation logs for allocation_reject reasons.
2) Query eval-ledger for probe_manifest_id and cost budget status.
3) Inspect shadow-mesh metrics for slot health (oom_count, preemptions, avg_qps).
4) If privacy gating blocked allocation, confirm probe redaction passed (probe-fabricator logs).

Rollout example (real case study):
- Goal: reduce cost for continuous functioncall-stability probes by 18% while preserving p99 latency for P0 canaries.
- Action: introduced a new steady pool with 1.5x concurrency and weight=1.8, enabled progressive bulk sampling for low-fidelity sub-slices.
- Result: after staged rollout (1% -> 20% -> 100%), observed 17.9% cost reduction and p99 for P0 canaries remained within 8ms of baseline.

Ownership and contacts:
- Owners: eval-platform team (primary), evaluation-costing (secondary).
- Oncall: eval-sre rotation (pager: #eval-oncall).
- Escalation path: eval-oncall -> eval-platform -> platform-sre -> eng-lead.

Appendix A — tuning knobs and recommended defaults:
- fast_threshold: 0.7
- steady_threshold: 0.3
- backfill_sampling_rate: 0.05
- fidelity_alert_pct: 80
- rebalancing_interval_minutes: 10
- canary_step_windows: [24h, 12h, 12h]

Appendix B — links to related docs:
- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-shadow-fidelity-simulator-2026
- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/telemetry-driven-prompt-surgeon-and-repair-playbook-2025
- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-ledger-and-billing-export-spec-2026 (internal)

Change log:
- 2025-11-12: initial draft (Aisha Patel)
- 2025-12-10: added backfill sampling recipe and cost accounting section (Miguel Santos)
- 2026-01-15: tightened rollout escalation thresholds and added example YAML (Lena Zhou)

title: KV cache behavioral eval and control playbook
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines a repeatable, automated evaluation and control strategy for diagnosing and preventing regressions caused by the KV (key-value) cache in Redwood's serving runtime. It combines synthetic probe design, production shadow comparisons, and a small battery of controlled ablation experiments to: 1) detect behavioral regressions introduced by cache changes, quantization, or kernel swaps; 2) attribute regressions to cache interactions; and 3) provide safe remediation and rollback criteria.

Scope
-----
- Applies to models and service routes that use prefix / KV caching (all autoregressive and chat-style routes).
- Intended for use during: model onboarding, quantized rollout, runtime kernel upgrades, and any change to cache policy.
- Not intended for model algorithmic changes unrelated to token caching (those have separate evals).

When to run
-----------
- Pre-promotion: mandatory for any model variant that will be deployed with cache enabled (required gate).
- On quantized or perf-optimized rollout (canary): run full playbook on canary traffic and shadow runs.
- Continuous: run lightweight probes daily on a stratified sample of production keys.

Key definitions and assumptions
-------------------------------
- "Prefix" refers to any cached prior tokens including system prompts and shared conversation context.
- "Cache hit" means the runtime reused KV state for an attention window slice.
- Tests compare three configurations: cache=on (baseline), cache=off (cold), cache=partial (first-n tokens disabled).

Metrics and signals to monitor
------------------------------
1) Behavioral / quality signals (primary)
- Semantic drift score (dev-set BLEU/ROUGE proxy + embedding cosine delta): absolute drop > 4% triggers investigation.
- Response divergence rate: fraction of responses with token-level edit-distance > 10% between cache=on and cache=off. Alert if > 3%.
- Functioncall fidelity: mismatched function call name or argument schema between modes. Any mismatch is P1.

2) Operational signals (secondary)
- Latency delta (p50/p95) comparing cache on vs off. Expect p50 improvement; if p95 increases > 15% investigate.
- Token churn / repeated-subword inflation: sudden increases can indicate inconsistent tokenization or cache corruption.

3) Privacy / leakage checks
- Cross-user prefix contamination checks: 0 tolerated leaks. Automatic fail if any non-empty overlap of private tokens across user IDs is detected.

Probe design and synthetic workloads
-----------------------------------
- Probe families:
  * Priming-probes: long system messages that exercise KV compression and eviction.
  * Prefix-perturbation probes: replay same user prompt with small prefix alterations to detect brittle reuse.
  * Stateful-dialog probes: multi-turn interactions that depend on KV for referent resolution.
  * Functioncall anchors: prompts designed to trigger deterministic functioncall outputs so mismatches are unambiguous.

- Probe dataset composition: 2k probes stratified by context length (0-256, 256-1024, 1024-8192) and intent type (instruction, QA, multi-turn, functioncall).

Experiment matrix (minimum cells)
--------------------------------
- Configurations: [cache=on, cache=off, cache=partial(n=64)] x [model variant: float32, int8/quantized] x [traffic: synthetic, 1% shadow production].
- Measurements: run each cell with seeds=3, sample size per cell >= 1k probes, capture logits, tokens, KV-access traces, and timing.

Acceptance criteria (example gate)
----------------------------------
- No P1 behavioral mismatches (functioncall fidelity, toxic output regression).
- Semantic drift score delta <= 4% vs baseline (cache=off).
- Response divergence rate <= 3%.
- Latency p95 must not increase by more than 10% on canary traffic.
- Zero cross-user contamination events.

Runbook: triage steps when a cache-related regression is detected
----------------------------------------------------------------
1) Confirm signal: reproduce locally with the failing probe set across the three cache modes.
2) Collect artifacts: full request/response pairs, KV traces, kernel logs, quantization artifacts, and deterministic seed.
3) Narrow the change set: is the regression associated with (a) cache policy change, (b) kernel swap, (c) quantization variant, (d) eviction/compaction regression? Use binary bisect on deployments.
4) Quick rollback path: revert to last known-good cache policy or kernel; if regression persists, disable cache for the route and escalate.
5) Root-cause experiments:
   - Re-run targeted probes with increased context length to stress eviction logic.
   - Replay the exact token sequence with and without compressed KV encodings.
   - If quantization suspected, test float32 vs quantized weights with cache on/off.
6) Remediation options:
   - Patch: fix KV encoding/decoding mismatch or eviction bug.
   - Configuration: reduce cache window size or switch to partial caching strategy.
   - Long term: add sentinel checks in runtime to detect corrupted KV entries.

Automation recommendations
--------------------------
- CI integration: add a KV-cache-aware test stage to model promotion pipeline that runs full matrix on PRs touching runtime or quantization code.
- Canary automation: when enabling cache on a canary, automatically run the playbook with synthetic probes + 1% shadow traffic and block rollout on failures.
- Alerting: create dedicated SLOs and alerts for the primary behavioral signals with playbook links in the alert body.

Canary / rollout policy (example)
---------------------------------
1) Stage 0: internal synthetic only, pass acceptance criteria.
2) Stage 1: 0.5% shadow production traffic + synthetic; hold for 24h, require no P1 and metric stability.
3) Stage 2: 1-5% live routing with revert-on-failure; monitor for 72h.
4) Stage 3: graduated ramp with automated health checks every 1h.

Ownership and artifacts to attach to a run
-----------------------------------------
- Owner: ML Infra / Serving Runtime team (primary), Model Onboarding (secondary).
- Mandatory artifacts for promotion: probe dataset ID, probe results snapshot (CSV), KV trace archive, canary logs, diff against last-good.
- Ticket template: include incident id, failing-probe-ids, command to reproduce, and candidate fix patch link.

Appendix A — sample test YAML
----------------------------
```yaml
playbook_version: 1.2
probe_set_id: kv-probes-v3
matrix:
  - cache_policy: on
    model_variant: float32
  - cache_policy: off
    model_variant: float32
  - cache_policy: partial_n64
    model_variant: int8
seeds: [1001,1002,1003]
min_samples_per_cell: 1000
artifacts_to_collect: [responses.jsonl, kv_traces.tar.gz, logs.tgz, timings.csv]
```

Appendix B — quick CLI examples
--------------------------------
- Run local probe runner (docker):
  docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/probes:/data redwood/eval-runner:latest \"--probes /data/kv-probes.jsonl --config /data/kv-test.yaml\"

- Query results summary (example):
  python tools/kv_eval_summary.py --results s3://redwood-evals/kv/2026-01-12/summary.json

Related pages
-------------
- Link to model onboarding checklist: /applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026
- Link to quantization audit: /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/kv-cache-quant-stability-audit-playbook-2025

Contact / escalation
--------------------
- Primary oncall: infra-ml-sre rotation (see team wiki).
- If P1 behavioral regression: page infra-ml-sre and model-quality leads and open an immediate incident with priority tag KV-CACHE-REGRESS.

Change log
----------
- 2026-01-12: created by Maya Chen (initial draft).
- 2026-02-10: expanded probe set and hardened acceptance thresholds after two internal canaries.

title: Stochastic Eval Replay and Determinism Protocol
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines the protocol and runbook for capturing, replaying, and triaging nondeterministic behavior observed in evaluation harness runs. It codifies artifact capture, deterministic-mode execution, tolerance thresholds, and escalation steps so engineering and applied ML teams can reliably diagnose and reduce stochastic divergence between runs.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all automated and manual eval harness runs used for production model certification, A/B tests, and regression detection.
- Covers sources of nondeterminism including sampling configs (temperature, top_k/top_p), tokenizer differences, runtime kernel scheduling, batch coalescing, KV cache state, and hardware/driver variance.
- Does NOT cover data-collection-level label noise or human annotation variance (see separate QA guidelines).

Goals
-----
- Make a failing or flaky eval reproducible within the harness >= 90% of the time using captured artifacts.
- Provide a consistent artifact set that allows replays across environments (dev -> staging -> dedicated).
- Reduce actionable nondeterminism by 30% year-over-year via instrumentation and targeted fixes.

Terminology
-----------
- Replay bundle: a single tarball containing request payloads, RNG seeds, tokenizer checksums, runtime snapshot, model binary id, and KV cache dump where applicable.
- Deterministic mode: runtime mode where sampling is disabled (greedy / beam) or sampling is run with explicit seed control and kernel pinning.
- Divergence: measurable difference between responses (token-level edit distance, log-prob delta, or evaluation score delta).

Artifact capture (what to collect)
--------------------------------
Collect the following for every eval run flagged as flaky or when running a determinism sweep: 
- run_metadata.json (schema below)
- request_payloads.ndjson (one request per line, include full prompt, headers, and model_version)
- tokenizer_snapshot.txt (tokenizer version + serialized vocab checksum)
- rng_state.bin (binary RNG state for CPU/GPU PRNGs if accessible) or seed log entry when binary not available
- kv_cache_<shard>.bin (kv cache snapshot for the session; optional and gated by storage policy)
- runtime_snapshot.txt (container image id, kernel id, CUDA/cuDNN driver versions, pinned kernel flags, environment variables relevant to runtime)
- batching_log.jsonl (log of batch composition and timing for the run)
- model_artifact_id.txt (release tag + checksum)
- system_hardware_checksum.txt (GPU model + BIOS + minor revision string)

Example run_metadata.json (single-line example)
------------------------------------------------
{"run_id": "eval-2025-03-12-2048", "env": "staging", "model": "redwood-7b-v1", "deterministic_mode": false, "seed": null, "sampling_policy": "top_p=0.95", "max_tokens": 256}

Config reference table (keys accepted by harness)
------------------------------------------------
| key | type | description | default |
|-----|------|-------------|---------|
| deterministic_mode | boolean | Force non-sampling generation or enable seeded sampling pathway | false |
| seed | integer | PRNG seed for sampling pathways; applied to CPU/GPU PRNGs when available | null |
| sampling_policy | string | JSON-encoded sampling config (temperature, top_k, top_p) | \"{\"temperature\":1.0}\" |
| runtime_snapshot | string | path to runtime_snapshot.txt to force replay env | current |
| capture_kv_cache | boolean | whether to snapshot KV cache for the session | false |
| batch_strategy | string | \"auto\" | \"auto\" |
| tolerance_threshold | string | metric-specific threshold for acceptable divergence | \"metric:0.03\" |

Protocol: capture -> replay -> classify
-------------------------------------
1) Capture: When a run is flagged (automated check or manual), immediately tag run as \"capture_required\". The harness should persist all artifacts above to S3 under /eval-replays/<run_id>. A capture job must finish within 30s of detection to maximize fidelity.

2) Replay (local/staging):
   a) Run the replay harness with the same request_payloads and runtime_snapshot. By default, start in deterministic_mode=true and seed=42.
   b) If deterministic-mode reproduces the issue, classify as \"sampling-agnostic\". Proceed to kernel/runtime triage.
   c) If deterministic-mode does NOT reproduce, run seeded sampling with the original sampling_policy and try seed enumeration (see Seed Enumeration below) up to 1,000 seeds or 1 hour wall time.
   d) If seeded sampling finds a match, classify as \"seed-sensitive\". Record the matching seed in the replay bundle metadata.

Seed Enumeration (when to use)
-----------------------------
- Use when nondeterminism is suspected to be due to sampling and the failure signature is easily comparable (exact token sequence or evaluation score threshold).
- Enumeration approach: deterministic-mode -> seeded sampling sweep with offset strategy (seed = base_seed + offset) in parallel shards. Stop early when match found. Log seeds tested in seeds_tested.log.

Classification of failures
--------------------------
- Deterministic mismatch: reproduced under deterministic_mode -> root causes: tokenizer drift, model binary mismatch, floating-point math/precision.
- Seed-sensitive: reproducible only under specific seeds -> root causes: sampling edge cases, prompt-sensitive sampling boundaries.
- Environment-dependent: reproduces only when runtime_snapshot differs -> root causes: driver/kernel/runtime flags, pinned kernels.
- Batch-induced: only reproducible when batch composition matches original batching_log -> root causes: KV cache reads/writes, request interleaving, race conditions.

Runbook: Reproduce a failing eval
--------------------------------
1) Fetch the replay bundle: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-eval-replays/<run_id>/bundle.tar.gz ./ && tar xzf bundle.tar.gz
2) Inspect run_metadata.json and batching_log.jsonl for obvious mismatches.
3) Start a replay node with runtime snapshot: eval-harness --runtime-snapshot=runtime_snapshot.txt --replay-dir=./<run_id>
4) First attempt: eval-harness --deterministic-mode=true --requests=request_payloads.ndjson --model-id=$(cat model_artifact_id.txt)
5) If step 4 fails to reproduce, run seeded sweep: eval-harness --seed-sweep --base-seed=1000 --parallel-shards=8 --requests=request_payloads.ndjson
6) If reproduction occurs, create an issue with classification, attach matching seed (if any), and link to relevant telemetry (traces, GPU logs).

Mitigation and rollback guidance
--------------------------------
- If classification shows tokenizer drift: pin tokenizer version in model onboarding and trigger a republish of tokenization artifacts. Notify model-onboarding team.
- If environmental: pin runtime image + driver and roll forward to stable image across environments. Consider gating on canary traffic for 24h.
- If batch-induced: enable strict batch boundaries for the failing route or force KV cache isolation for the short term.
- If seed-sensitive but low impact: add seed-stability tests to the eval suite for the prompt in question. If high impact, consider adjusting sampling_policy (reduce temperature or clamp top_k).

Acceptance criteria and SLOs
---------------------------
- Reproducible replay success rate: target >= 90% for high-confidence failures within 1 hour of analysis.
- False-positive divergence alarms: < 2% of daily alerts.
- Automated capture completion: 99.5% of flagged runs must have a complete replay bundle within 30s.

Instrumentation and telemetry requirements
-----------------------------------------
- All eval harness runs must log batch composition (request ids + sample offsets) and streaming chunk boundaries.
- RNG seeds (or seed generation method) must be logged to run_metadata.json for every run.
- Tokenizer version and checksum must be recorded and surfaced in the Console for each model version.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Primary owner: Eval Harness Team (eng-applied-ml). On-call: eval-harness-oncall rotation.
- Escalation path: Eval Harness -> Serving Runtime -> Model Onboarding -> Security (if artifacts contain customer PII).
- Contact: evan.brooks@redwood.ai for process questions; use #eval-replay Slack channel for coordination.

Appendix: Practical examples
---------------------------
- CLI: force deterministic replay
  eval-harness --replay-dir=./eval-2025-03-12-2048 --deterministic-mode=true --model-id=$(cat model_artifact_id.txt)

- YAML eval job snippet:
  job_id: replay-2025-03-12
  deterministic_mode: true
  seed: 42
  requests: request_payloads.ndjson
  runtime_snapshot: runtime_snapshot.txt
  capture_kv_cache: true

References and related pages
----------------------------
- Serving simulation harness (simulation guidelines) -- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/serving-simulation-eval-harness-2026
- KV cache quant stability audit -- /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/kv-cache-quant-stability-audit-playbook-2025

Revision history
----------------
- 2025-03-12: Initial draft filed (Evan Brooks).
- 2025-04-08: Added seed enumeration strategy and example CLI (Sarah Liu review).
- 2025-06-01: Formalized capture schema and SLO targets; moved to published status (Mateo Alvarez review).

title: Shadow-to-Production: Eval Continuity & Safety Guidelines
content:
Summary:
This document prescribes the end-to-end process for using shadow (mirrored) traffic and continuous eval outputs to safely promote models into production for text generation and embedding workloads. It connects eval-harness artifacts (workload fingerprints, prompt coverage, quantization evaluation), runtime observability, and automated rollback triggers so teams can preserve quality SLOs while iterating quickly.

Goals:
- Ensure production promotions are gated by real-traffic shadow evaluation + synthetic continuity checks.
- Define concrete metrics, thresholds, and automated actions for safe rollback and triage.
- Provide runbook steps and ownership for degradation investigations spanning eval-harness -> runtime -> model-promotion-service.

Applicability:
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes that support request mirroring (shadow routing).
- Target workloads: text-generation/chat, embeddings, and reranking.

Key Concepts and Signals:
1) Shadow run: mirror a sample of production requests to candidate model instances without affecting user-visible responses. Shadow traffic should preserve original request headers and sampling ratios.
2) Continuity test suite: a short, prioritized set of prompts derived from prompt-sets-and-benchmarks that exercise long-tail failure modes for the target workload.
3) Response Stability Index (RSI): a composite signal combining token-level edit distance, semantic-similarity delta (embedding cosine), and policy-safety flags. Range 0-100, lower is better.
4) Token Amplification Ratio (TAR): ratio of mean tokens generated by candidate model to baseline. Flags unbounded or degenerate generation.
5) Quantization Delta: measured difference in essential eval metrics (RSI, semantic-score, latency) between full-precision and quantized variants during shadow runs.

Gating Metrics and Thresholds (default baselines):
- RSI: <= 4.0 relative increase over baseline (if >4.0, fail gate).
- p95 latency: no more than 20% regression vs baseline and absolute p95 <= 1.2s for small-chat profiles.
- TAR: between 0.8 and 1.5 (outside => investigate hallucination/verbosity).
- Semantic Recall (embedding cosine on ground-truth checks): >= 0.92 average for retrieval prompts.
- Safety flags (policy classifier): no more than 0.2% absolute increase in high-severity flags.
- Quantization Delta: RSI increase <= 1.5 and latency improvement >= 10% (otherwise treat quantized variant as incompatible for that workload).

Traffic Sampling and Shadow Configuration:
- Shadow sampling rate: start at 0.1% of requests for initial verification, ramp to 2-5% as confidence increases.
- Sampling strategy: stratified by route and prompt-type fingerprint (use eval-orch fingerprint tagging) so slices are covered proportionally.
- Forge requests exactly as sent by clients (including conversation history) but set header X-Shadow-Run: candidate-model-id.
- Storage: persist shadow responses in the eval-orch datastore for at least 30 days for retrospective triage.

Continuity Test Suite (runtime-synth):
- Run 1: latency-sensitive prompts (short queries, token cap 64) x 200 samples. Check p95 and token tail behavior.
- Run 2: long-context prompts (>= 2048 tokens) x 100 samples. Verify KV-cache correctness and output truncation.
- Run 3: adversarial prompt set (from prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/adversarial-noise) x 300 samples. Measure safety flags and RSI.
- Run 4: embedding recall microbench (100 paired queries). Measure semantic score and embedding variance.

Promotion Workflow (high-level):
1) Preflight: run inference-readiness-eval-matrix locally with model candidate (unit-sized synthetic suite).
2) Shadow rollout stage A: mirror 0.1% traffic for 48 hours. Collect metrics and continuity tests.
3) Review: automated report generated by eval-orch summarizing gating metrics; reviewers assigned (owner + applied-ml) must sign off or open a triage issue.
4) Shadow stage B: increase to 2% mirror for 72 hours if stage A passed. Run full continuity suite nightly.
5) Canary (optional): route 1% of live responses to candidate for actual responses with rollback guardrails and customer-scope opt-outs.
6) Promote to production routing if all gates pass for 7 days; otherwise, rollback to previous stable model and open a regression investigation.

Automated Rollback Triggers (examples):
- Any RSI increase >8.0 vs baseline within a 1-hour window.
- Safety flag spike: >=0.5% absolute increase in critical flags in 15 minutes.
- Latency SLO breach: sustained p95 > 1.2x baseline for 30 minutes or p99 > 2.0x baseline.
- Token amplification: TAR > 2.0 sustained for 10 minutes.
- Quantization catastrophic: semantic recall drop > 0.08 absolute.

Immediate Rollback Procedure:
1) Alerting: Pager duty escalation to oncall-model-owner and applied-ml triage@redwood. Notify customer-success if any customer-visible regressions are observed.
2) Execution: call model-promotion-service API to revert traffic to previous model_id. Example: 
   curl -X POST https://internal.api.redwood/v1/model-promote 
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RD_TOKEN' 
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
     -d '{"action":"rollback","target_model_id":"model-1234","reason":"RSI spike"}'
3) Preserve artifacts: snapshot shadow response storage slice, collect profiler traces from runtime-collector, and start automated bisect job if enabled.
4) Postmortem: within 72 hours produce a regression triage that includes top failing prompt slices, quantization parameters, and kernel-level profiling.

Investigation Playbook (triage owner responsibilities):
- Step 0: Confirm alert validity (check noise, infra events).
- Step 1: Compare shadow vs baseline slices in eval-dashboard; prioritize high-severity slices with >0.5 RSI delta.
- Step 2: Run hypothesis checks: quantization delta? prompt-tokenization mismatch? KV-cache context corruption? model artifacts mismatch?
- Step 3: If quantization suspected, re-run quant-eval job with --deterministic-seed and capture full logits for 100 seeds.
- Step 4: If infra suspected, attach runtime profiler traces and coord with eng-serving-runtime for kernel scheduling logs.
- Step 5: If model bug, label and route to model-onboarding team for rollback/retrain.

Quantization Specific Guidance:
- Always include a quantization shadow pass in Stage A for any new quant profile. Record Quantization Delta (RSI, latency, memory) in the promotion report.
- Reject quantized promotion when RSI increases >1.5 and semantic recall drops >0.02 for retrieval/rewrite workloads.
- Recommended quant profiles by workload:
  * chat-medium: int8-gptq-8 + group-size=64 (fast path; verify with long-context tests).
  * retrieval-heavy: fp16 fallback preferred; quantized variants must pass embedding-stability audit.

Observability and Dashboards (what to monitor):
- eval-orch/shadow-metrics: RSI-by-slice, TAR, safety-flag-rate, embedding-delta.
- runtime/latency: p50/p95/p99 per-model and per-route.
- stability/rolling: 1h, 6h, 24h windows for RSI and safety flags.
- promotion-service: model-version lineage and active traffic splits.

Example CLI / YAML snippets:
- Run a targeted continuity eval (eval-orch):
  redwood-eval run --suite continuity-short --model candidate:2026-04-01 --out results/continuity-short.json --samples 200

- Shadow routing rule (kubernetes Ingress annotation):
  annotations:
    redwood.io/shadow-target: "model:candidate-2026-04-01"
    redwood.io/shadow-sample: "0.001"

Ownership and Roles:
- Model Owner (primary): responsible for promotion and initial triage.
- Applied ML (secondary): owns eval-harness suites, continuity tests, and quantization pass criteria.
- Serv‑runtime: responsible for tracing, profiler data, and kernel-level reconciliation when latency/throughput regressions appear.
- Customer Success: notified for production-visible regressions and coordinates customer communication.

Risk Register (common failure modes):
- Silent semantic drift due to tokenization mismatch between training and serving. Mitigation: tokenization fingerprint checks in preflight.
- Quantized hallucinations: mitigation: additional adversarial-run sweep and reject quant-profile if TAR or RSI flags exceed thresholds.
- Data leakage in shadow logs: mitigate by PII scrubbing and strict retention policies (30-day default, 7-day for sensitive customers).

Appendix A — Quick Checklist Before Promotion:
- [ ] Preflight eval matrix passed (unit and synthetic).
- [ ] Shadow stage A (0.1%) passed gating metrics for 48h.
- [ ] Continuity test nightly runs succeeded at 0 regressions for top-5 critical slices.
- [ ] Quantization Delta measured and within thresholds.
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards provisioned and reviewers assigned.
- [ ] Rollback playbook tested within the last 30 days (game-day).

Appendix B — Example Promotion Acceptance Table (fill in in review):
| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Delta | Pass? | Notes |
| RSI (avg) | 2.4 | 3.1 | +0.7 | Yes | within 4.0 threshold |
| p95 latency | 820ms | 900ms | +9.7% | Yes | under 20% cap |
| TAR | 1.0 | 1.12 | +12% | Yes | acceptable verbosity |
| Safety flags | 0.12% | 0.15% | +0.03% | Yes | low absolute delta |

Document Maintenance:
- Owner: applied-ml team (Marisol Chen).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any production regression.
- Next scheduled review: 2026-04-01.

Related resources and links:
- eval-harness: orchestration runbooks and runner CLI (link internal)
- prompt-sets-and-benchmarks: canonical continuity and adversarial suites (link internal)
- model-onboarding: inference-readiness and promotion matrix page (link internal)

Contact and escalation:
- applied-ml-oncall@redwood (primary)
- eng-serving-runtime-oncall@redwood (secondary)

This guideline balances safe promotion speed with robust automated protection. Follow the thresholds as defaults and tune per-product with signoff from applied-ml and product owners.

title: Quantized Artifact Evaluation Gate and Canary Rollout
content:
Overview
--------
This document defines the evaluation gate for quantized model artifacts and the associated canary rollout orchestration used by Redwood Inference. It codifies the entry criteria for promoting a quantized artifact from shadow/onboarding environments into production routes (hosted, dedicated, or private), the telemetry and tests required, and the rollback/troubleshooting guidance to tie into existing regression triage playbooks.

Scope
-----
- Applies to artifacts produced by the model onboarding and quantization pipelines (both automatic and manual quant profiles).
- Covers hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments where binary/quant artifacts are deployed.
- Integrates with: eval harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, quality guardrails, and regression triage procedures.

Goals and Principles
--------------------
- Safety-first: do not promote artifacts that show statistically significant regressions on prioritized slices.
- Reproducible gating: every promoted artifact must carry provenance (checksums, quant profile, kernel pins).
- Cost- and latency-aware: accept modest throughput/latency regressions only when quality is preserved.
- Fast rollback: automated fallback to pre-quantized or previous-quant artifacts on breach of SLOs.

Acceptance Criteria (high level)
-------------------------------
All of the following must pass for a quantized artifact to be eligible for canary:

- Core prompt-set stability: weighted-regression-delta (WRD) <= 0.03 on the core prompt suite (see Prompt Suite table below).
- Embedding anchor fidelity: mean cosine similarity >= 0.995 on the embedding anchor set.
- Response Stability Index (RSI) >= 0.92 across representative interaction traces.
- Token-level divergence: KL divergence of token distributions <= 0.10 vs float baseline for the same contexts.
- Latency impact: P95 latency <= 1.25x of float baseline for equivalent batch mix.
- Resource footprint: GPU memory footprint and KV-cache size within the profile targets documented in artifact metadata.

Note: Any metric exceeding these thresholds triggers an automated failure and requires an explicit triage (see "Failure Modes").

Detailed Metrics and Thresholds
-------------------------------
- WRD (weighted-regression-delta): aggregated per-slice; slices are weighted by production traffic share. Threshold: 0.03.
- Embedding Cosine: measured on N=2k anchor pairs covering English/Spanish/FR. Threshold: 0.995.
- RSI (Response Stability Index): similarity of canonical answers measured by BLEU+semantic-similarity heuristics; threshold 0.92.
- Token KL: base-10 log KL aggregated over tokens emitted for core prompts; threshold 0.10.
- Latency P95: measured on synthetic & shadow traffic; threshold 1.25x.
- Throughput (tokens/sec/GPU): should not degrade more than 20% for same batch configuration.

Evaluation Pipeline (steps executed by rwi-eval harness)
------------------------------------------------------
1) Artifact registration
   - Upload artifact bundle to artifact storage and record metadata: model_id, model_version, quant_profile_id, checksum (sha256), source-float-checksum, kernel_pins, expected_sequence_length, supported-clients.
   - Example metadata table (see Appendix).

2) Smoke tests (automated, ~15 minutes)
   - Run unit-level generation tests (sanity responses, tokenization roundtrips).
   - Run embedding consistency sanity check on a 200-item anchor subset.
   - Command: rwi-eval smoke --artifact s3://rwi-artifacts/<id> --profile quant 

3) Full harness run (automated, parallelized, 2–6 hours depending on artifact size)
   - Execute core prompt-set, edge-case probes, multilingual anchors, and latency-quality slices.
   - Produce JSON report, per-slice diffs, and a signed acceptance artifact.
   - Command: rwi-eval run --artifact s3://rwi-artifacts/<id> --slices core,edge,multi --profile quant --output report.json

4) Telemetry snapshot
   - Snapshot baseline telemetry from the float baseline run that produced the artifact. Required fields: baseline_tokens_per_sec, baseline_P95_latency_ms, baseline_RSI, baseline_embeddings_stats.json.

5) Signoff gating
   - Automated pass/fail decision based on thresholds above.
   - If pass: artifact moves to "canary-ready" state and a canary deployment is scheduled.
   - If fail: record fail reason, notify model-owner and QE, and open a triage ticket with labels: quant-fail, artifact:<id>.

Canary Rollout Orchestration
----------------------------
Principles: incremental traffic, real-world telemetry, and short feedback loops. Canary uses the same route-level instrumentation as production (token-level, cost, latency, error breakdowns).

Canary configuration (example YAML):

---
canary_name: quant-canary-<model_id>-v<version>
initial_traffic_percent: 2
stages:
  - { percent: 2, duration_hours: 6 }
  - { percent: 10, duration_hours: 24 }
  - { percent: 30, duration_hours: 24 }
monitoring: [rsi, wrd, p95_latency, error_rate, embedding_drift]
rollback_policy:
  breach_thresholds:
    rsi_drop_absolute: 0.04
    wrd_increase_absolute: 0.02
    p95_ratio: 1.5
    error_rate_absolute: 0.01
  immediate_on_breach: true
---

Traffic routing is controlled by the canary controller (service: canary-orch) which will bump percentages according to the YAML schedule if and only if monitoring windows show no threshold breach. Canary controller posts events to #canary-observability and creates an automated incident if immediate_on_breach triggers.

Promotion checklist (pre-rollout)
--------------------------------
- [ ] Artifact metadata published and signed.
- [ ] Eval harness report uploaded and signed.
- [ ] QE and model owner sign off on per-slice notes (explicitly mark tolerated regressions).
- [ ] Canary YAML created and reviewed by infra and SRE on-call.
- [ ] Backup fallback (previous float artifact or previous quant artifact) staged and smoke-tested.

Failure Modes and Triage Guidance
--------------------------------
Common failure categories and immediate checks: 
- Tokenization / vocabulary drift
  - Symptom: high token KL and degraded RSI on short prompts.
  - First-check: verify tokenizer version and tokenization parity with float baseline.
- Kernel mismatch / pinned-kernel divergence
  - Symptom: large latency variance, small but systematic generation differences on long context.
  - First-check: confirm kernel_pins listed in artifact metadata are available and identical on target fleet.
- Quant rounding and clipping
  - Symptom: semantic shift in numeric outputs, embedding drift on numeric-heavy prompts.
  - First-check: run the per-token delta diagnostic in rwi-eval with --debug-quant to produce token-level rounding stats.
- Cache/KV interaction issues
  - Symptom: failures or degraded quality after repeated multi-turns.
  - First-check: run a kv-cache stress scenario from the harness (rwi-eval kv-stress).

Linking to Regression Triage
---------------------------
When a canary breach occurs, the canary controller automatically creates a triage ticket (component: applied-ml/regression) and attaches: the full rwi-eval report, canary telemetry snapshots, and the artifact metadata. Use the regression-triage playbooks to run bisect, blame-assistant, and probe-farm if needed. Prioritize triage steps that can rule out infra/kernel mismatches before assuming a model-quality regression.

Ownership and Contacts
----------------------
- Model owner: defined on artifact metadata (required).
- QE contact: applied-ml-qe@redwood.example.com.
- Canary controller / infra owner: infra-orch@redwood.example.com.
- On-call SRE (short link): /eng-sre/oncall-rotations/current

Appendix A — Artifact metadata table (required fields)
------------------------------------------------------
| field                    | description                                                  | example                       | required |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|----------|
| model_id                | internal canonical model id                                  | rwi-llama-65b                 | yes      |
| model_version           | semantic version or build id                                 | v2026-02-10-quant             | yes      |
| quant_profile_id        | id of quantization profile used                               | qprof-int8-kv-opt-v2          | yes      |
| sha256_checksum         | artifact bundle checksum                                      | 9f3b...a12c                   | yes      |
| float_source_checksum   | checksum of float baseline artifact                           | 1a2b...9f8c                   | yes      |
| kernel_pins             | list of GPU kernel ABI tags expected                           | [cu12-kern-v3, cu11-kern-v9]  | yes      |
| expected_seq_len        | expected typical sequence length                              | 1024                          | recommended |
| memory_footprint_mb     | expected GPU memory usage for profile                          | 34567                         | recommended |
| provenance_uri          | S3 or internal URI for build logs and reproducibility manifest | s3://rwi-builds/1234/manifest | yes      |

Appendix B — Example triage commands
------------------------------------
- Run full eval harness locally: rwi-eval run --artifact s3://rwi-artifacts/<id> --slices core,edge,multi --output /tmp/report.json
- Run per-token quant debug: rwi-eval debug-quant --artifact <id> --prompt-file core-prompts.txt --out quant-debug.csv
- Trigger a controlled canary rollback: rwi-canary rollback --canary quant-canary-<id> --reason "p95 breach" --initiator <username>

Notes and Caveats
------------------
- This gate is tuned for production safety. Teams may create experimental quant profiles that bypass parts of the gate for research, but such artifacts must be explicitly labeled "experimental" and are not eligible for any production routing.
- Some customers (private on-prem) will have custom kernel availability; ensure kernel_pins and artifact packaging are validated in the customer's staging cluster before promotion.

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-02-15: created by Priya Nair (initial draft).
- 2026-02-22: added RSI / token-KL thresholds after QE review (Carlos Mendes).
- 2026-03-01: finalized canary YAML and rollback-policy (Ellen Park).

Related reference docs
----------------------
- Model promotion playbook: /applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026
- Quant output degradation protocol: /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-output-degradation-detect-and-repair-protocol-2026
- Regression triage playbooks: /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026

title: latency-tail-capture-and-synthetic-backfill-procedure-2024
content:
abstract:
Playbook for capturing high-latency tail events in production traffic, synthesizing deterministic probes that reproduce tail behavior in the eval harness, and backfilling historical shadow traces for offline quant/quality analysis. Focuses on observability signals, probe generation, synthetic backfill policy, and a triage runbook for applied ML teams.

background_and_motivation:
We observe intermittent 95th+ percentile latency spikes (tail events) that are costly and can correlate with quality regressions after quant or routing changes. Typical failure modes include KV-cache thrash, quantized kernel stalls, and rarely seeded memory pressure on GPU nodes. Root cause analysis is slow when spikes are ephemeral and requests are not reproducible. This playbook defines a reproducible capture -> probe synthesis -> synthetic backfill workflow so model-onboarding, quantization, and runtime teams can reproduce, validate, and fix tail regressions without impacting live traffic.

scope_and_invariants:
Applies to text generation and chat endpoints served by eval-mesh and production-serving. Not in scope: unrelated network-level outages, control-plane-only incidents. Invariants: all captures must be sampled and redacted to PII policy; probes must be deterministic given seed and tokenizer version; backfill workloads must not exceed 20% of eval-fleet capacity and must be scheduled during maintenance windows unless explicitly approved.

signal_definitions:
1) Latency-tail trigger: p99 > 1.2x baseline_p99 for 5 consecutive 1-min windows OR single-request latency > 3s for short-context endpoints. 2) Quality signal: embedding cosine drift > 0.07 on monitored slices OR token-entropy change > 0.25. 3) KV-cache miss storm: cache_miss_rate increase > 10ppt for request shard. 4) Quantization suspect: runtime quant-decoded-error > 0.5% on probe samples.

capture_pipeline_overview:
Steps: 1) Detection: alert from eval-mesh-alerting (rule: latency-tail trigger). 2) Live-snapshot: invoke probe-fabricator capture job (captures request headers, tokenized input, model_version, runtime_profile, kv-cache-hash, node_id, seed). 3) Redaction: automated PII redaction using redaction-service v2.0. 4) Provenance: store snapshot in snapshot-archive with tags (incident_id, slice, model, runtime). 5) Notification: create triage ticket in Regression-Triage board and attach snapshot link.

probe_generation_steps:
1) Confirm capture integrity: run `probe-validate` against snapshot-archive/<snapshot-id>. 2) Synthesize deterministic probe: `probe-fabricator synth --snapshot <id> --tokenizer v3 --seed <snapshot-seed> --output probes/<id>.json` 3) Add contextual priming: append the production prompt-prefix and system-role observed in original request. 4) Create probe metadata with: model_variant, quant_profile (if any), runtime_kernels, kv-cache-state-hash. 5) Register probe in eval-mesh as a debug-probe with low priority: `eval-mesh register --file probes/<id>.json --priority debug`.

synthetic_backfill_playbook:
Purpose: reproduce tail behavior across historical windows to determine onset and frequency. Steps: 1) Select historical window: choose up to 72 hours of traffic centered on first observed tail spike. 2) Extract compatible snapshots: use snapshot-query tool `snapshot-query --tags incident:<id> --window 72h` 3) Create backfill batch: `backfill-orchestrator create --probes probes/<id>.json --window <start>:<end> --fleet-tag eval-backfill --max-concurrency 50` 4) Throttle policy: default QPS cap at 0.2x production and backfill concurrency <= 15 per model. 5) Data retention: backfill traces stored for 90 days in backfill-archive. 6) Output artifacts: per-probe response timelines, per-token latencies, kernel-time breakdown CSVs, and per-slice quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/Embedding drift).

triage_runbook:
When a tail capture is generated: 1) Triage lead (owner: runtime-team) verifies capture within 30 minutes; 2) If capture reproduces in eval-mesh: mark priority=canary and start focused diff (compare kernel timings and kv-cache hit profiles). 3) If not reproducible: run synthetic backfill with three seeds (original-seed, +1, -1). 4) Escalation: if p99 remains > baseline for 2 hours and probes show quant-decoding errors > 0.5%, open a cross-team incident with runtime, quant, and model-onboarding in #inc-quant-tail. 5) Rollforward/rollback guidance: prefer model variant rollback to last known-good if quality delta > 2% and latency improvement > 20%. 6) Postmortem: attach all probes, backfill outputs, and RCA draft to the incident within 7 days.

config_table:
| Parameter | Default | Acceptable range | Purpose |
|---------------------------|----------------|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| p99_trigger_multiplier    | 1.2            | 1.05 - 2.0            | Sensitivity for tail detection
| single_request_threshold  | 3000ms         | 1000ms - 10000ms      | Hard threshold for immediate capture
| backfill_max_concurrency  | 50             | 1 - 200               | Max concurrent probes across eval-fleet
| backfill_qps_cap          | 0.2x           | 0.05x - 1.0x          | Fraction of production QPS allowed for backfill
| probe_retention_days      | 90             | 14 - 365              | How long to keep probe artifacts
| redaction_profile         | pii-v2         | pii-v1,pii-v2,pii-off | Redaction profile used during capture


cli_examples:
1) Validate a snapshot: `probe-validate snapshot-12345 --expect-fields tokenized_input,seed,model_variant`
2) Synthesize a probe: `probe-fabricator synth --snapshot snapshot-12345 --tokenizer v3 --seed 98765 --out probes/snap-12345.json`
3) Register for eval: `eval-mesh register --file probes/snap-12345.json --priority debug --tags incident:2024-058`
4) Create a backfill batch: `backfill-orchestrator create --probes probes/snap-12345.json --window 2024-11-10T08:00:00Z:2024-11-10T20:00:00Z --max-concurrency 20 --fleet-tag eval-backfill`
5) Quick inspect latency breakdown: `latency-inspector analyze --trace backfill-archives/snap-12345 --metrics per-token,kernel-ms`

ownership_and_slos:
Owners: runtime-team (primary), model-onboarding (secondary), applied-ml (observer). Contact: #runtime-ops, runtime-oncall@redwood.com. SLOs: p95 generation latency <= 420ms for short context routes; p99 <= 900ms (production baseline). Alerting thresholds: p99 > 1.2x baseline triggers capture; p99 > 1.5x baseline opens incident. Backfill SLA: initial backfill artifacts available within 4 hours of orchestration request (90% of time).

remediation_guidance:
Example remediations mapped to findings: - KV-cache thrash: increase prefix cache TTL, enable sticky routing for affected tenancy, and re-run warmup probe set. - Quant kernel stalls: revert to float kernel for variant, flag quant_profile for re-tuning, schedule quant stress test on the hybrid-quant harness. - Node-level memory pressure: cordon node_id found in snapshot, redeploy model replicas to nodes with free memory > 80%. Always validate fix by re-running the synthesized probe set and a 1h backfill sample.

postincident_analysis_and_metrics:
Track the following per incident: number of captures, reproduction rate in eval-mesh, mean time to first reproducible probe (MTFR) goal < 3 hours, percent incidents resolved by rollback vs code fix, and percent reduction in tail incidence after remediation. Use dashboard 'Latency Tail Index' (dash-id: LT-23) to monitor long-term trends and meta-analyses.

references_and_links:
- Eval mesh register docs: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-register-spec-2025
- Probe fabricator README: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/probe-fabricator-readme-2026
- Redaction service runbook: /security-and-compliance/data-management/redaction-service-runbook-2024
- Incident board: /oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/incident-board


notes_and_future_work:
Planned improvements: automated root-cause classification using probe feature vectors, tighter integration with quant-simulator to pre-run possible regressions before backfill, and a lightweight browser for probe diffs inside the console. Roadmap ticket: APPL-EVAL-522.

conclusion:
This playbook provides a repeatable, low-risk path from production tail observation to offline reproducibility and remediation. Following the capture -> probe -> backfill -> triage lifecycle reduces MTTR and increases confidence for quant and model rollouts.

title: Hybrid eval cost-fidelity splitter and routing framework
content:
Summary:

This document defines the "Hybrid Eval Cost-Fidelity Splitter" (HECFS) — a deterministic policy and runtime component that routes evaluation probes across multiple fidelity tiers (smoke, standard, deep) to maximize coverage and failure signal while enforcing a configurable cost budget. HECFS provides (1) an allocation algorithm, (2) runtime routing knobs, (3) operational SLOs/metrics, and (4) a small runbook for triage when the splitter misbehaves.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers operating the eval harness and shadow fleets
- Platform engineers integrating probe routing into shadow and federated evaluators
- Product owners responsible for evaluation cost/perf tradeoffs

Why this exists:
- Continuous evaluation at scale has variable marginal value: not every probe needs full-fidelity instrumentation.
- Without systematic allocation, teams either overspend on deep evaluation or under-detect regressions.
- HECFS provides a principled way to amortize eval spend while preserving sensitivity to regressions.

Scope and definitions:
- Probe: a single evaluation input (prompt + metadata) executed by the harness.
- Fidelity tiers:
  - smoke: single seed, lightweight metrics, fast, lowest cost.
  - standard: deterministic seed set, additional metrics (coherence, hallucination proxies).
  - deep: multi-seed, function-call simulation, quant-shadow comparison, human review gating.
- Cost unit: normalized token-cost equivalent (used by the budget allocator).
- Sensitivity score: dynamic estimate of how likely a probe is to reveal a regression (0.0–1.0).

High-level design:
1) Offline profiling produces per-slice base-cost and baseline-variance. Profiling includes quant-shadow runs and prefix-cache sensitivity.
2) A lightweight estimator assigns each incoming probe a sensitivity score s and an expected token_cost c for each fidelity tier.
3) The Splitter uses a knapsack-inspired allocator to distribute probes into fidelity buckets given the global budget B and soft quality target Q (target detection probability).
4) A small rebalancer runs every minute to migrate probes (where possible) from standard -> deep or deep -> standard based on live telemetry (e.g., rising variance, new latency anomalies).
5) Routing decisions are recorded in the probe registry and emitted as telemetry (route_reason, expected_cost, chosen_tier, estimator_version).

Allocation policy (concise):
- Prioritize high-sensitivity probes for deep evaluation until marginal detection gain < marginal cost fraction.
- Maintain a minimum coverage floor: at least X% of probes in each important slice must be run at standard fidelity to preserve baseline comparability.
- Reserve a small opportunistic budget P for on-demand deep escalations triggered by anomaly detectors.

Configuration table (example):
| parameter | meaning | recommended default | notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| global_budget_B | total token-cost budget per-hour for eval fleet | 15_000_000 | set at account/team level |
| quality_target_Q | target detection probability (0-1) | 0.92 | soft target used by allocator |
| floor_coverage_slice | min percent of probes per slice at standard | 0.10 | important slices set by ownership |
| opportunistic_reserve_P | percent of B reserved for escalations | 0.06 | used for anomaly-driven deep runs |
| estimator_version | model id used to compute sensitivity | v2025-11-17 | pinned per-deployment |

Estimator notes:
- The estimator uses a small ensemble: a lightweight classifier over probe metadata + recent telemetry (token length, tenant, historical failure rate) and an uncertainty proxy (variance estimate from prior seeds).
- Estimator must be validated offline against prior incidents (see validation checklist below).

Pseudocode: allocation loop

# Inputs: probes[], B, Q, floor_coverage, P
# Outputs: routing decisions {probe_id -> tier}

1. sort probes by sensitivity_score descending
2. allocate_reserved = B * P
3. remaining_budget = B - allocate_reserved
4. ensure per-slice floor: for each slice s, mark floor_count(s) = max(floor_coverage * count(s), 1) and allocate those at standard tier, deducting expected cost
5. for probe in probes (high -> low sensitivity):
     expected_deep_cost = cost(probe, deep)
     marginal_gain = marginal_detection_gain(probe, deep vs standard)
     if remaining_budget >= expected_deep_cost and marginal_gain / expected_deep_cost >= threshold(Q):
         assign probe -> deep; remaining_budget -= expected_deep_cost
     else if remaining_budget >= cost(probe, standard):
         assign probe -> standard; remaining_budget -= cost(probe, standard)
     else:
         assign probe -> smoke
6. opportunistic pool: route up to allocate_reserved probes to deep when anomaly detectors flag them

Operational metrics (emitted every minute and available in Console dashboards):
- route_distribution: pct {smoke, standard, deep} (goal: stable within 5% of configured target)
- budget_utilization: used_B / B (alert at > 0.95)
- detection_gain_curve: marginal_detection_vs_cost (visualization to tune threshold)
- false_negative_rate_estimate (post-hoc labeling pipeline)
- escalations: count of opportunistic_reserve usages (alert if > configured P limit)
- estimator_drift_index: KL divergence of estimator feature distribution vs training baseline

SLOs and thresholds:
- Evaluator sensitivity SLO: maintain estimated detection probability >= Q - 0.03 (soft).
- Budget SLO: no more than 1% of hours with budget_utilization > 1.0 (hard).
- Escalation SLO: opportunistic_reserve usage limited to configured P within a 24h window.

Rollout plan (canary -> graduated):
1. Canary (5% of eval fleet across low-risk tenants): run HECFS in audit mode (make routing decisions but do not enforce; log "shadow_route" field) for 48-72 hours. Compare budget/utilization predictions and detection_gain_curve vs baseline.
2. Soft-enforce (25%): enforce routing, but keep a doubled opportunistic_reserve to allow manual escalations. Run human-in-loop reviews for any missed high-sensitivity probes.
3. Enforce (all): full policy, enable automated rebalancer.

Promotion checklist (must pass before increasing traffic fraction):
- estimator false positive/negative rates on canary labels < 10%
- budget_utilization predictions within 8% of observed
- detection_gain_curve monotonic (no counter-intuitive inversions)
- monitoring dashboards verified and alerting wired to oncall

Failure modes and runbook (top 5):
1) Overbudget (budget_utilization > 1.0)
   - Immediate action: toggle global_budget_B to emergency-reduced value (CLI: hecfs-cli set-budget --id <env> --value <reduced_B>) and scale opportunistic_reserve_P to 0
   - Triage: check estimator version, recent traffic spike, and any new slices with unexpectedly high deep_cost
   - Postmortem: corrective action may include increasing economy of standard tier or adjusting floor_coverage_slice

2) Estimator drift (estimator_drift_index > drift_threshold):
   - Action: revert to fallback_estimator (rule-based) and open ticket for retraining.

3) Detection regression (false_negative_rate_estimate increases > baseline + 0.05):
   - Action: pause deep -> standard demotions, temporarily promote top N high-sensitivity probes to deep for human review.

4) Router lag (routing decisions delayed > 2s):
   - Action: switch to stateless fallback routing (round-robin based on slice priority) and scale routing workers.

5) Telemetry loss: missing route_reason or chosen_tier fields
   - Action: pause enforcement, enable audit-only mode until telemetry pipeline repaired.

Validation and bench tests (recommended suites):
- Synthetic spike test: create a burst of high-sensitivity probes in a low-budget simulation and assert opportunistic_reserve limits are respected.
- Regression injection: replay a historic incident (known regression) and verify detection probability under HECFS >= baseline detection.
- Cost simulation sweep: run iterated allocators across B values to produce detection_vs_cost frontier for stakeholders.

Interfaces and example CLI commands:
- hecfs-cli evaluate-batch --input probes.json --budget 15000000 --estimator v2025-11-17 --output routing.csv
- hecfs-cli set-budget --env staging --value 10000000
- hecfs-cli promote-estimator --env prod --version v2026-01-12 --rollback-to v2025-11-17

Telemetry schema (fields emitted per probe):
- probe_id (string)
- tenant_id (string)
- slice_id (string)
- sensitivity_score (float)
- chosen_tier (string)
- expected_cost_per_tier (string; comma-separated cost map)
- route_reason (string)

Ownership and escalation contacts:
- Primary owner: Maya Chen (Applied ML Platform) — pager: #applied-ml-oncall

Documentation and developer guidance:

- Unit tests required: allocator unit tests, estimator regression test, cost-sensitivity integration suite (CI gate)

Appendix A: Estimator validation checklist
- Holdout dataset: at least 10K labeled probes spanning longtail slices
- Minimum AUC: 0.78 for high vs low sensitivity classification
- Calibration curve: max ECE < 0.07
- Adversarial checks: vary tokenization and quantized model runs to ensure false negatives don't spike

Appendix B: Example allocation simulation table
| scenario | B | allocated_deep_pct | expected_detection | notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| baseline | 15_000_000 | 18% | 0.92 | uses default params |
| constrained-budget | 6_000_000 | 7% | 0.74 | triggers more smoke |
| high-reserve | 15_000_000 (P=0.2) | 25% | 0.95 | opportunistic finds rare regs |

Related artifacts and references:

title: Eval Mesh and Workload Fingerprinting: Orchestration & Decisioning
content:
summary:
Design and runbook for the Eval Mesh: mapping production workload fingerprints to targeted eval workloads, prioritizing scheduling, and decision rules for routing traffic to shadow/dedicated eval variants.

body:
Overview
========
This document defines the Eval Mesh: an orchestration layer and fingerprinting specification used to (1) capture lightweight production workload characteristics, (2) map them to canonical eval workloads, and (3) drive priority routing and scheduling decisions in the eval harness. The goal is to make evaluations reflect production signal distribution while keeping privacy, cost, and reproducibility constraints.

Motivation
----------
- Production traffic is heterogeneous: latency, context length, few-shot pattern, and function-calling density vary by customer and route.
- Traditional static eval suites drift from production and miss failure modes tied to rare workload slices.
- Eval Mesh allows continuous, targeted, and cost-aware evaluation: create small representative eval jobs that mirror production slices and route them for regression detection and model promotion gating.

High-level architecture (components)
-----------------------------------
- traffic-tap: lightweight tap running in the serving runtime that emits anonymized fingerprints to fingerprint-db and a streaming topic (kafka/eval-ingest).
- fingerprint-db: time-series store for fingerprints (TTL 90d) used to compute slice prevalence and trends.
- eval-orchestrator: central decision engine that maps fingerprints -> eval-workload-id, computes priority, and schedules runs on the eval cluster.
- scheduler: eval harness scheduler (k8s jobs + priority-queue) that executes eval workloads, respecting cost and SLAs.
- result-aggregator: collects eval outputs and writes signals to metrics-store and regression-triage queue.

Key definitions
---------------
- Fingerprint: compact anonymized descriptor of a request (schema below).
- Workload ID: a canonical eval workload recipe (prompt set, input distribution, model config).
- Slice: a named subset of traffic identified by fingerprint matching rules.

Fingerprint schema (textual):
- id_version: v1
- timestamp_utc: iso8601
- route: service route identifier (e.g., text-gen/v1)
- token_histogram_bucket: one of ["<=64","65-256","257-1024","1025+"]
- call_pattern: one of ["pure-gen","function-heavy","rerank","embed"]
- avg_shots: numeric (0,1, few, many) encoded as string buckets ["0","1","2-5","6+"]
- kv_cache_hit_rate: bucket ["0-10","11-40","41-70","71+"]
- anonymized_user_locale: normalized locale code or "unknown"
- PII_flag: boolean (always false when exported)

Example fingerprint JSON (emitted by traffic-tap):

{
  \"id_version\": \"v1\",
  \"timestamp_utc\": \"2026-02-28T13:22:07Z\",
  \"route\": \"chat/commerce-v2\",
  \"token_histogram_bucket\": \"65-256\",
  \"call_pattern\": \"function-heavy\",
  \"avg_shots\": \"1\",
  \"kv_cache_hit_rate\": \"41-70\",
  \"anonymized_user_locale\": \"en-US\",
