   - Criteria: stream re-attach error rate < 0.1%, tail latency at p99 within budget.

5) Function-call fidelity and schema safety tests
   - Run 2k functioncall probes with schema fuzzing.
   - Criteria: malformed-call rate <= 0.2% and confidence aligned with baseline.

6) Mixed-precision and transient-failure stress test
   - Run mixed-load stress tests that interleave quantized and float variants. Observe dynamic fallback behavior.
   - Criteria: no cascading degradation (error-rate amplification multiplier < 1.2).

7) Shadow (tenant-separated) pre-production run
   - Deploy to shadow fleet with per-tenant tagging for 48hrs. Capture full telemetry: latency, cpu/gpu utilization, OOMs, retry rates, and response-quality deciles.
   - Compare to float baseline using per-slice acceptance thresholds (see "Metric table").

8) Canary rollout with fast-fail gates
   - Canary to 2–5% of traffic with automated monitor alerts and progressive expansion policy.
   - If any canary gate trips, immediate rollback to previous model; run canary-incidents triage.

Metric table (promotional gates)
| Metric | Acceptable delta vs float baseline | Action on breach | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| P50 latency (ms) | + <= 10% or + <= 20ms | continue / alert | Serving Runtime |
| P95 latency (ms) | + <= 15% | investigate / pause expansion | Serving Runtime |
| P99 latency (ms) | + <= 25% | rollback if sustained 10min | SRE/Platform |
| Tokenization drift (%) | <= 5% | reject artifact | Model Owner |
| Functioncall malformed rate (%) | <= 0.2 | rollback | Applied ML |
| Embedding cosine similarity | >= 0.97 | require manual review | Applied ML |
| Output coherence delta (task-specific scoring) | task-dependent; usually <= 2% | hold rollout | Eval Team |
| Error-rate (5xx/invalid tok) | <= previous * 1.1 | rollback | SRE |

Telemetry contract (runtime ⇄ eval harness)
- Required telemetry fields (all producers must emit these tags):
  - model_version, quant_profile, epoch_build_id, host_zone, tenant_id, request_id, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_hit, fallback_triggered, error_code, functioncall_schema_id, eval_probe_id (if applicable).
- Export cadence: aggregated metrics every 30s. Detailed traces retained for 48hrs for canary and 7 days for production promotions.
- Telemetry schema example (JSON line format):
  {"model_version":"v3.1-q4mix", "quant_profile":"q4mix-l1", "latency_ms": 32.4, "tokens_out": 128, "kv_cache_hit": true, "fallback_triggered": false}

Sampling / budget guidance
- Eval budget: allocate minimum 100k probe tokens across slices for shadow runs and 250k tokens for canary windows.
- Annotation budget: reserve 500 human-review items targeted at top-3 deviation slices if baseline thresholds are exceeded.
- Cost control: prefer stratified probe sampling by tenant revenue/traffic to prioritize high-risk/high-value customers.

Regression triage and playbook (on gate breach)
1) Immediate automated actions
   - Pause canary expansion and route new quant-profile traffic to float baseline.
   - Snapshot telemetry and capture the last 1,000 failing probe requests into an escrow.
2) Triage steps (within 2 hours)
   - Triage lead assembles: Model Owner, Applied ML, Serving Runtime engineer, SRE oncall, and one evaluator.
   - Hypothesis matrix (documented in incident ticket): quantization-related numerical drift, tokenization mismatch, KV cache boundary condition, mixed-precision kernel bug, or dataset/seed mismatch.
3) Quick remediations (if safe)
   - Toggle quant-fallback policy to float for the failing slice.
   - Re-run failing probes with increased precision (e.g., convert weight blocks to INT16 or use hybrid quant).
4) Rollforward conditions
   - Only after passing full smoke battery and shadow run again for 24hrs with no regression in top-3 slices.

Operational runbook snippets
- Canary pause command (CLI):
  redwoodctl rollout pause --model v3.1-q4mix --canary-id 2026-11-canary-7
- Snapshot telemetry export to escrow bucket:
  redwoodctl telemetry export --model v3.1-q4mix --window 00:10:00 --out s3://escrow/canary-2026-11-12.jsonl
- Trigger immediate rollback:
  redwoodctl rollout rollback --model v3.1-q4mix --to-version v3.0-float --reason "canary-regression"

Best practices and recommendations
- Keep quant profile names semantically meaningful (include hardware target and quant family).
- Always include a seeded reproducible eval snapshot used for final promotion sign-off. Store snapshot id in artifact metadata.
- Maintain a small dedicated probe set of business-critical examples ("canary probes") that are always run as first-class checks.
- Prefer progressive mixed-precision remediation before full rollback: try hybrid blocks, per-layer fallback, or per-slice precision overrides.

Ownership and escalation
- Promotion owner (Model Owner) must be explicitly set in CI metadata and on the promotion ticket.
- Escalation path: Model Owner -> Applied ML Lead -> Runtime Lead -> SRE Manager. All pages and tickets must include a link to the canary telemetry dashboard.

Appendix A: Example promotion metadata (YAML)
---
model_version: v3.1-q4mix
quant_profile: q4mix-l1
artifact_hash: 2a9f8d3b
promotion_owner: maya.chen@redwood.ai
shadow_policy: tenant-separated
canary_policy: progressive-2-5-15
smoke_probe_snapshot: probe-snap-2026-11-04
---

Appendix B: Quick reference (decision matrix)
- If embedding cosine < 0.95 for a revenue-critical slice -> immediate rollback and high-priority postmortem.
- If p99 latency > 2x baseline for > 10min and error-rate increased -> rollback.
- If functioncall malformed rate spike but latency stable -> hold and run targeted functioncall fuzz-suite; allow per-slice float override.

Notes and changelog
- 2026-11-05: initial draft by Maya Chen.
- 2026-12-12: added telemetry contract and sampling budgets; reviewers: Anika Patel, Lars Schmidt.

Related artifacts and links
- Eval harness runner: /internal/tools/eval-runner
- Canary dashboard: /dashboards/canary-quant-promotions
- Quant profile registry: /artifacts/quant-profiles

title: Shadow Deployment Evaluation Playbook for Private & Dedicated Environments
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines the standard process and acceptance criteria for "shadow" (non-traffic, mirrored) evaluation deployments of new model builds and quantized model variants in Redwood Private and Dedicated environments. Shadow deployment is intended to provide realistic, safety-aware, and cost-conscious validation without exposing production traffic to unvetted model behavior.

Goals:
- Detect functional regressions and quality drift early when promoting model builds to Dedicated or Private customer pools.
- Verify quantization/3rd-party compilation impacts under representative workload shapes.
- Validate operational metrics (latency p50/p95, memory pressure, KV cache hit distribution) in the target deployment topology.
- Produce deterministic promotion signals for canary/fallback policies in the Redwood Console.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to: model promotions intended for Dedicated pools and Private (VPC/on-prem) installs that will be pinned or exposed to customer traffic.
- Not intended for hosted-only experimentation (use hosted eval harness).

Key definitions:
- Shadow deployment: A deployment that receives a copy of production-like requests (via sampling or replay) but does not return responses to end users.
- Evaluation cohort: A configured set of prompts, demographic slices, and synthetic adversarial cases used during the shadow period.
- Quantization variant: Any model build with reduced precision or kernel-level compilation differences (int8, bfloat16, fq4) intended to lower unit costs.

Prerequisites:
1. Model build has passed unit and integration tests and a baseline acceptance in the central eval harness (see related eval-harness matrix).
2. Target Dedicated/Private environment is provisioned with matching runtime version and kernel profiles.
3. Baseline production telemetry snapshot captured (last 7 days) for comparison.
4. Owner, SRE, and customer (if applicable) sign-off on shadow window and data collection.

Evaluation inputs (test sets & strategies):
- Live-sampled traffic (1-5% of production routed to shadow) OR replayed request traces from the last 72 hours.
- Seeded prompt set: 500 in-distribution prompts representative of heavy-usage features (summarization, instruction-following, extraction).
- Robustness seed: 200 adversarial/noise prompts (typo/obfuscation, ambiguous instructions).
- Long-context stress: 100 prompts with >8k token context to exercise KV cache and attention kernels.
- Safety vectors: 250 safety-sensitive prompts focusing on policy and hallucination triggers.
- Quant-sensitivity partition: the above seed sets with token lengths and shot counts sampled to match expected CTA distributions.

Evaluation metrics and thresholds (promotion-oriented):
- Quality: semantic-similarity-based regression <= 5% drop relative to baseline on the seed test set (metric: pairwise BLEU/ROUGE + embedding cosine > 0.88 for key tasks).
- Safety: no new high-risk safety failures (severity >= 4) introduced; critical safety count must be zero.
- Latency: p50 delta <= +10ms, p95 delta <= +40ms relative to baseline.
- Memory: peak GPU memory <= baseline + 5% for Dedicated; for Private, must meet node capacity headroom >= 10%.
- KV cache behavior: cache hit-rate change <= 3 percentage points; cold-start token overhead <= 12%.
- Regression triage score: composite (quality, safety, perf) must be green for automated promotion. See scoring formula below.

Composite regression triage score (used to decide automated gating):
- Quality (50%), Safety (30%), Latency & Memory combined (20%).
- Score mapping: Green >= 90, Yellow 70-90 (manual review), Red < 70 (reject).

Shadow deployment configuration example (table as plain text):
- runtime_version: 2.14.0
- model_variant: my-model-v3-quant-fq4
- routing_mode: mirror (no user-facing responses)
- traffic_sample: 0.02  # 2% of production requests
- replay_window: 72h
- eval_window: 48h
- data_retention_for_debug: 30d
- telemetry_enabled: true (tokens, delta-logs, raw-outputs hashed)

Procedure (step-by-step):
1) Preparation (Day -3 to -1)
   - a) Create shadow deployment config in Redwood Console with owner, SLOs, and telemetry toggles.
   - b) Register evaluation cohort (IDs for seed prompt sets, adversarial cases, long-context suite).
   - c) Capture production baseline metrics snapshot (p50/p95 latencies, token cost per request, KV cache distribution).
   - d) Notify SRE and customer success of shadow start time and debug contact.
2) Launch & warm-up (Day 0)
   - a) Start shadow at 0.1% traffic-sample using mirror routing for 2 hours to validate no impact on production.
   - b) Validate telemetry ingestion (token-level breakdowns, kernel selection tags, memory traces).
   - c) Escalate and rollback if initial memory or latency anomalies exceed thresholds (see rollback criteria).
3) Full shadow evaluation (Day 0–2)
   - a) Ramp to target sampling rate (e.g., 2%).
   - b) Run scheduled seeded tests (nightly regression suite) and continuous adversarial stream.
   - c) Run quant-sensitivity comparisons: run paired inference for float vs quant variant on matched requests to compute per-request delta metrics.
4) Analysis (Day 2–3)
   - a) Produce evaluation report summarizing quality, safety, perf, and regression triage score.
   - b) If Yellow, schedule manual triage with ML owner, SRE, and Safety SME; for Red, block promotion and open a regression ticket.
5) Promotion decision (Day 3+)
   - a) If Green, proceed to canary traffic rollout as defined in the canary promotion playbook.
   - b) If manual remediation required, iterate on model or runtime config and re-run shadow.

Rollback criteria (immediate or automated):
- Any critical safety failure (severity >= 4) observed in the shadow outputs.
- Sustained p95 latency exceeding baseline + 100ms for >10 minutes.
- GPU memory OOM or >95% sustained memory utilization for >5 minutes.
- KV cache churn leading to cold-start amplification >25% over baseline.

Triage and debugging playbook (on Yellow/Red):
- Ownership: ML owner to lead quality triage; SRE to lead perf/memory; Safety SME to lead policy incidents.
- Minimum artifact set to open triage ticket: failing request IDs, model build hash, runtime kernel tags, quant config, and raw model output (hashed + redacted as needed).
- Standard steps: reproduce failure with isolated replay; narrow to minimal prompt; compare float vs quantized outputs; run profiler to capture kernel-level hot paths.

Privacy and telemetry controls:
- Shadow deployments must respect PII/data retention policies. Raw outputs used for triage must be hashed or redacted before storage.
- Data collected during shadow is governed by the customer-specific confidentiality flag; for Private installs, default to restricted unless customer explicitly permits debug artifact sharing.

Operational knobs and recommendations:
- Use continuous batching profiles tuned for the target pool to avoid spurious latency regressions when sampling traffic.
- Prefer paired inference (float vs candidate) for a statistically robust delta rather than absolute thresholds alone.
- When validating quantized builds, include both microbench kernels and end-to-end user-level prompts in the same shadow window.

Example commands and snippets:
- Create a shadow route (CLI pseudo):
```
redwood route create --env prod-dedicated-eu --model my-model:v3-quant --route-type mirror --sample-rate 0.02 --telemetry on --eval-cohort seedy-2026-01
```
- Run paired inference comparator (local):
```python
# comparator.py (simplified)
from redwood_eval import InferenceClient
client_float = InferenceClient(model='my-model:v3')
client_quant = InferenceClient(model='my-model:v3-quant')
for prompt in prompts:
    a = client_float.generate(prompt)
    b = client_quant.generate(prompt)
    print(prompt.id, embedding_similarity(a,b), latency_delta(a,b))
```

Acceptance report template (deliverable):
- Summary (one-paragraph)
- Baseline vs candidate comparison (table of metrics)
- Regression triage score and breakdown
- Safety findings (counts + examples)
- Perf findings (latency histogram, memory timeline)
- Recommendation: Promote / Remediate / Block (with owners and ETA)

Ownership and SLAs:
- ML owner: create shadow config, interpret quality signals, own remediation.
- SRE owner: validate runtime compatibility, address perf regressions, own rollback.
- Safety/Policy: review any flagged safety cases within 24 hours.
- SLA for shadow evaluations: evaluations should finish and a report be produced within 72 hours of shadow launch for standard promotions.

References and related artifacts:
- Eval harness promotion matrix (internal link)
- Model certification checklist (internal link)
- Canary promotion playbook (internal link)

Appendix: quick checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Register evaluation cohort
- [ ] Capture baseline telemetry
- [ ] Create shadow route with mirror routing
- [ ] Run warm-up and validate telemetry
- [ ] Ramp to target sampling and run seed/adversarial sets
- [ ] Run paired float-vs-quant comparisons
- [ ] Produce acceptance report
- [ ] Decision: Promote / Remediate / Block

This playbook should be updated annually or whenever changes are made to the runtime (kernel selection, batching model) or the promotion scoring formula. For questions or exceptions, contact the playbook owner (Maya Chen) or SRE lead (Alejandro Ruiz).

title: Onboarding acceptance rubric: KV-cache, quantization, and prompt calibration
content:
Summary
-------
This page defines a prescriptive acceptance rubric for promoting new models (or model variants) into Redwood Inference service stages where the combination of KV-cache behavior, quantization profile, and prompt calibration can materially affect customer-facing quality and cost. It bundles automated checks, sample workloads, and explicit rollback triggers so model owners and SREs can make deterministic release decisions.

Context and goal
----------------
When a model is introduced or migrated (new weights, quantized artifact, or cache strategy) it may introduce subtle regressions: prefix-coherence loss, embedding drift, KV cache miss amplification, token-cost regressions, or tail-latency spikes. This rubric targets three cross-cutting failure modes we see most often in onboarding:
- Cache degradation: higher-than-expected cold-start miss rate or KV eviction-induced coherence regressions.
- Quantization artifacts: hallucination frequency increase, coherence loss for long context, or numeric instability in functioncall args.
- Prompt mismatch: previously calibrated prompt templates that relied on tokenization or temperature defaults behaving differently.

Acceptance philosophy
---------------------
- Gate first on safety & correctness (do not promote a model that increases hallucinations or safety alerts beyond SQC thresholds).
- Gate second on user-impacting regressions (coherence, functioncall correctness, embedded search recall).
- Only after quality gates are satisfied evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs and operational mitigations (adaptive KV-cache sizing, mixed-precision fallback).

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Model owner (author): prepares artifact, provides baseline metrics, and runs offline eval harness.
- Applied ML evaluator: runs the acceptance tests and annotator QA for flagged slices.
- Serving runtime owner: validates KV-cache plumbing and deployment knobs.
- SRE oncall: signs off on rollout plan, monitors live metrics during canary.

Pre-promote checklist (automated and manual steps)
--------------------------------------------------
1) Artifact metadata and reproducibility
   - Provide model artifact SHA, quantization recipe (bits, per-channel/per-tensor, lambda), and tokenizer snapshot.
   - Provide a reproducible Docker image or bundle for private/dedicated deployments.

2) Unit and regression tests (pass/fail)
   - Unit tests: tokenization parity, deterministic seed runs for N=3 seeds show low variance (response divergence < 0.02 normalized JS).
   - Regression probe suite: run full prompt-slice baseline (see Sample workload set below).

3) Safety & correctness gates
   - Safety sentinel pass rate >= baseline - 0.5 percentage points OR delta flagged and annotated with mitigation plan.
   - Functioncall integrity: 99.5% of functioncall responses must preserve schema and required keys on synthetic contract tests.

4) Coherence and semantic fidelity
   - Coherence index (see Metrics section) relative delta <= 1.5 points for high-sensitivity slices.
   - Named-entity recall for QA-style probes: delta <= 3% absolute.

5) KV-cache stability checks
   - Cold-start miss amplification: measured miss-rate in micro-sim shadow < 1.25x baseline for 95th percentile context length.
   - Eviction churn (evictions per minute per model instance) <= baseline + 10%.

6) Quantization-specific checks
   - Token-level perplexity increase <= 6% on calibration corpus.
   - Calibration-driven hallucination delta <= 0.8% absolute on adversarial probe set.
   - Per-layer numeric anomaly scan: no layers with activation overflow/underflow events in stress runs.

7) Prompt calibration and token budget checks
   - Tokenization drift (prompt -> token count) <= +5% for canonical prompts.
   - Temperature/Top-p sensitivity: response variance must be within expected band given same sampling settings.

Sample workload set (must be run under the eval harness)
------------------------------------------------------
- Canonical customer prompt family (N=10k probes): intents across translation, summarization, code-completion, and multi-turn chat.
- Long-context stress set (N=2k): 8k–32k token priming, measuring KV-cache hit/miss and tail-latency.
- Functioncall contract set (N=500): schema-anchored calls that assert type and key presence.
- Adversarial coherence set (N=1k): purposely perturbations and priming traps to surface hallucination regressions.

Metrics and explicit thresholds
-----------------------------
All metrics below are measured relative to the baseline model (the currently promoted artifact in stage). Absolute thresholds are listed where appropriate.
- Safety sentinel delta: +0.5 pp tolerated; >+0.5 pp requires annotated mitigation and manual review.
- Coherence index (0–100): high-sensitivity slice delta <= 1.5 points; medium slices <= 2.5.
- Embedding drift (cosine similarity mean on canonical corpus): delta >= -0.02 tolerated; worse requires embedding rebaseline plan.
- Cold-start miss-rate (micro-sim, 99th pct): <= 1.25x baseline.
- Eviction churn (evicts/min/instance at 95th pct): <= baseline + 10%.
- Token cost delta (per-token expected cost): <= +12% tolerated with cost-contingency plan.
- Tail-latency (p99 generation time): <= baseline * 1.2.
- Functioncall schema failure rate: <= 0.5% absolute.

Example acceptance table (pass/fail guidance)
----------------------------------------------
| Gate | Measure | Pass condition | Action if fail |
|------|---------|----------------|----------------|
| Safety | Safety sentinel | delta <= 0.5pp | Reject; escalate; security review |
| Coherence | Coherence index (high) | delta <= 1.5 | Hold; targeted annotation run |
| KV-cache | Cold-start miss 99p | <= 1.25x baseline | Reduce cache pressure; increase per-tenant TTL; re-eval |
| Quant | Token-level perplexity | <= 6% increase | Try per-channel quant; fallback to mixed-precision |
| Prompt | Tokenization drift | <= +5% | Re-calibrate prompts; update canonical templates |

Operational runbook for marginal passes
--------------------------------------
When a model passes quality but violates cost/latency knobs, use an adaptive rollout:
1) Canary: 1–2% traffic for 24 hours with tight telemetry (coherence, safety, cost, p99 latency).
2) If any SQC alert fires, hold traffic and run fast rollback (see Rollback triggers).
3) If cost delta > +8% but quality unchanged, enable:
   - Token budget hard-limits via Redwood Console route config.
   - Dynamic batching aggressive thresholds for low-latency slices.
   - Mixed-precision fallback for non-critical tenants.

Rollback triggers (automated)
----------------------------
- Safety sentinel rate increase > +1.0 pp over baseline within rolling 30m window.
- Coherence index drop > 3.0 points on any high-sensitivity slice within 60m.
- Tail-latency p99 increase > 40% sustained for 15m.
- Eviction churn > baseline + 25% for 10m.
If triggered: stall the rollout, immediately execute rollback job (repoint route to previous artifact), create incident ticket with priority = P0 and notify owners.

Telemetry and dashboards to verify during canary
------------------------------------------------
Create a dedicated canary dashboard with these panels:
- Safety sentinel rate (per-tenant) 1m/5m/30m windows.
- Coherence index time series by slice and tenant.
- Cold-start miss-rate histogram and 99th percentile.
- Eviction churn (evicts/min) heatmap by instance.
- Token cost trend (per-route tokenized count * cost per token).
- P99 generation latency and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Functioncall schema failures with detailederror samples.

Calibration procedure for prompts (step-by-step)
----------------------------------------------
1) Run canonical prompt family through tokenization snapshot for both baseline and candidate; compute tokenization drift.
2) For any prompt with drift > +5%, run a priming-level A/B test locally to measure semantic alignment.
3) For templates that are token-compact vs token-expanded, produce two calibrated variants and include routing hint in route config for tenant-level overrides.
4) Update canonical prompt registry with the chosen token-stable variants and mark as locked for the rollout.

Quantization remediation playbook
--------------------------------
If quantization causes a quality regression:
- Immediate actions: increase representative calibration dataset size (add adversarial probes), switch from per-tensor to per-channel where supported, and/or relax clipping.
- Medium-term: re-run mixed-precision hybrid compile with explicit layer exclusions for sensitive layers (embedding and attention-key layers).
- Long-term: maintain a quant-failure catalog mapping probe-to-layer-susceptibility to speed future remediation.

Post-promotion monitoring & 72-hour checklist
--------------------------------------------
- 0–1h: Verify telemetry ingestion and alerting correctness.
- 1–8h: Monitor safety and coherence slices every 30m and annotate anomalies.
- 8–24h: Compare embedding drift across representative tenants; run lightweight shadow probes.
- 24–72h: Review cost impact and eviction patterns; finalize any token-budget mitigations.

Annex: example CLI commands and curl checks
-------------------------------------------
- Run shadowed micro-sim to estimate cold-start miss-rate:
  ./eval-harness/bin/micro_sim --model candidate:sha=abc123 --workload longcontext --out report.json

- Run functioncall contract tests (examples):
  curl -X POST https://eval.local/api/run_contract -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_KEY' -d '{"model":"candidate:abc123","suite":"functioncall_contract_v1"}'

- Quick check for prompt tokenization drift (python snippet):
  from tokenizer import Tokenizer
  t = Tokenizer('tokenizer_snapshot_v42')
  baseline_tok = t.encode('canonical prompt')
  print(len(baseline_tok))

Related artifacts and links
-------------------------
- Onboarding eval harness (canonical toolset): /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/evaluation-asset-registry-and-service-contract-2026
- Quant rollout playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook-2026
- Probe catalog and slice definitions: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/slice-fabrication-annotation-economics-playbook-2026

Change log
----------
- 2026-01-18: Created initial rubric and acceptance table.
- 2026-03-02: Incorporated SRE feedback: added eviction churn and explicit rollback thresholds.

Contacts and escalation
----------------------
- Model owner: listed on artifact manifest (required).
- Applied ML evaluator oncall: applied-ml-eval@redwood.ai
- Serving runtime SRE: runtime-sre@redwood.ai
- Pager: Redwood SRE rotation (P0).

This rubric is authoritative for all model promotions that modify quantization, tokenizer snapshots, or KV-cache strategy for public and dedicated deployments. If you need exceptions, open a formal risk review with security and product and document mitigation steps in the related page.

title: End-to-End Deployment Quality Contract and Operations Playbook
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines the end-to-end quality contract for promoting a model artifact through Redwood’s deployment pipeline (shadow -> canary -> GA) and the operational playbook for detecting, triaging, and remediating regressions that violate that contract. It codifies the evaluation gates across: eval-harness checks, prompt set coverage, quantization profile verification, runtime telemetry SLOs, and regression-triage escalation paths.

Scope
-----
Applies to: production model promotions across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
Exclusions: low-risk internal experiments that do not serve customer traffic and models with explicit "research-only" labels.

Goals
-----
- Provide a deterministic acceptance workflow that prevents quality regressions for customers.
- Ensure fast, reproducible triage when regressions occur.
- Balance unit-cost improvements (quantization, batching) with strict quality and latency contracts.

Quality Contract (gates and pass criteria)
----------------------------------------
Each promotion must pass the following gates before moving to the next stage. Failure to meet any gate requires documented mitigation and an approver sign-off (owner or product manager).

1) Eval-harness functional & safety suite (pre-promotion)
   - Smoke tests: 0 failing critical tests (CLI: redwood-eval run --suite smoke).
   - Slice-based acceptance: per-slice accuracy/precision recall within baseline delta: <= 2% absolute drop for high-priority slices.
   - Safety sentinels: zero critical safety hits for production prompt set (see appendix for sentinel list).

2) Prompt-set coverage and stability (pre/promotion shadow)
   - Coverage: production prompt-set coverage >= 90% of top-50 workload intents and >= 75% of long-tail probe classes.
   - Stability: Response Stability Index (RSI) ratio >= 0.98 against promoted baseline over 10k sample traffic replay.

3) Quantization & artifact verification (pre-promotion & shadow)
   - Quantized artifact MAPE (mean absolute pct error) on logits/embedding similarity metrics <= 0.5% for encoder outputs, <= 1.5% for logits on generative tasks unless exempted.
   - KV-cache fidelity check: top-k next-token distribution similarity >= 99% on warm sequences.

4) Runtime SLO and cost envelope (canary)
   - Latency: p50 <= 45ms, p95 <= 180ms for standard request shape (seq_len=512) on canary capacity.
   - Error budget: request_error_rate <= 0.5% (5xx or internal errors) during canary window.
   - Cost: token-cost-per-1k (inference) not exceed baseline + 12% unless approved by cost owner.

5) Post-Canary Quality Signal (canary -> GA decision)
   - Quality regression rate: regressions per 10k requests <= 1 (where regression = semantic correctness drop by eval harness metric defined per workload).
   - Human-in-the-loop sample pass-rate: >= 95% on 200 random canary responses labeled by annotators for intent correctness.

Gate checklist table (copyable)
--------------------------------
| Gate | Must-pass criteria | Tooling/Command | Owner |
|------|--------------------|-----------------|-------|
| Eval-harness smoke | 0 critical fails | redwood-eval run --suite smoke | eval-onboarding team |
| Slice acceptance | Per-slice delta <= 2% | redwood-eval slice-compare --baseline X | applied-ml |
| Quant verification | MAPE thresholds | quant-checker run --artifact a.pt | infra-quant team |
| Canary SLOs | Latency/error/cost | telemetry/alerts dashboard | SRE/Platform |
| Human sample | 95% pass | sampling-runner collect --n 200 | customer-success |

Promotion workflow (high level)
--------------------------------
1. Author creates model promotion PR and attaches promotion manifest (model id, quant profile, eval snapshot id, prompt coverage report).
2. Automated CI runs eval-harness full-suite on shadow artifact; results posted to PR.
3. If green, deployment to shadow routing (no customer traffic) for 6–24 hours with telemetry capture.
4. Canary deploy (5–10% traffic split) for 2–24 hours depending on traffic variance; realtime checks run.
5. If canary meets post-canary quality signals, schedule GA rollout incrementally; otherwise rollback to previous artifact immediately and trigger triage.

Canary sizing rules and ramp schedule
-------------------------------------
- Default canary: 5% traffic for 2 hours -> check automated gate metrics; if stable, increase to 20% for 4 hours -> check again -> GA.
- For high-risk changes (quantization, architecture updates, prompt-engineering), use conservative ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 10% with longer observation windows (12–24h at each step).
- Traffic shaping: prefer homogeneous slices for canary routing (non-sampled, high-volume intents) to avoid noisy long-tail signal.

Telemetry, metrics, and alerting (must be wired prior to canary)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Core metrics (reported per route/model):
- latency_p50, latency_p95 (ms)
- request_error_rate (%%)
- quality_regressions_per_10k (count) — measured by eval returns and sentinel mismatches
- embedding_drift_score (cosine delta) — exponential-weighted moving average (EWMA window=1 day)
- token_cost_per_1k (USD)

Alert thresholds and severities:
- Sev-1 (Pager): quality_regressions_per_10k > 5 for 30m OR request_error_rate > 2%% for 15m -> pager SRE + applied-ml oncall.
- Sev-2 (High): latency_p95 > 2x baseline for 30m OR embedding_drift_score > 0.12 (absolute) for 2h -> slack alert to model-owners and SRE.
- Sev-3 (Medium): incremental token_cost drift > +20%% vs baseline over 24h -> billing-notification + product.

Regression triage playbook (oncall steps)
-----------------------------------------
1. Detect: Pager fires or customer reports. Record incident id and triage channel (incident-{model}-{ts}).
2. Snapshot: Capture model artifact id, promotion manifest, latency/quality dashboards, and last successful baseline id. CLI: redwood-metrics snapshot --model MODEL_ID --since "-1h" --out /tmp/snap.json
3. Reproduce locally: Run smoke suite and failing prompt slices in local eval-harness (redwood-eval replay --input failing-requests.json --artifact ARTIFACT_ID).
4. Blame bisect: If change set contains multiple commits, perform binary promotion bisect using CI promotion snapshots. Use redwood-bisect --candidates LIST --metric 'quality_regressions_per_10k' --target-threshold 1.
5. If quantization suspected: run quantized replay and float baseline comparison (quant-replay --float baseline.pt --quant candidate.q.pt).
6. Rollback plan: If can’t mitigate quickly, rollback to previous artifact ID and pin canary route to old model. Notify customers per escalation template.

Detailed triage decision tree (short)
--------------------------------------
- If errors are 5xx/internal: prioritize SRE stack traces and runtime logs (likely infra).
- If semantic regressions without errors: focus on eval-harness diffs, prompt/coverage mismatches, or quant artifacts.
- If regressions only on long-tail slices: gather sample frequency and consider targeted prompt rewrites or slice-focused canary with higher observation window.

Quantization-specific acceptance and recovery checks
-----------------------------------------------------
| Check | Threshold | Recovery action |
|-------|-----------|-----------------|
| Embedding cosine retention | >= 0.995 vs float | Recompute quant profile or fallback to mixed-precision variant |
| Output distribution MAPE | <= 1.5% | Increase precision or enable per-layer calibration |
| KV-cache hit parity | >= 99% | Re-evaluate cache serialization and dequant path |

If quantization causes regression in production:
- Automated fallback: route 100% of affected route to float variant within 2 minutes (automated rollback policy).
- Postmortem: quant team runs quant-sensitivity routine and updates the quant-profile registry with failing fingerprints.

Human labeling and escalation matrices
--------------------------------------
- Human label runs: sample 200 responses from canary window; labelers use rubric 'intent-correct/partial/incorrect' and 'harmful/unsafe/ok'.
- Escalation: if labeled incorrect >= 5 in 200 (<= 95% pass) -> open a quality incident; notify product and CS and pause GA.

Operational runbook links and artifacts
--------------------------------------
- Runbook: applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/eval-oncall-runbook-for-model-regression-debugging-2026
- Canary dashboard name: /dashboards/model-canary/{{model_id}}/overview
- CI artifact storage: s3://redwood-artifacts/promotions/{{promotion_id}}/

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Model owner: person listed in promotion manifest (mandatory).
- Applied ML oncall: paged via SRE rotation.
- Quantization owner: infra-quant team (pager via #infra-quant).
- Customer-impact escalation: Customer Success oncall -> product -> legal for high-severity incidents.

Postmortem and continuous improvement
-------------------------------------
- Every production regression that exceeds Sev-2 must have a postmortem within 5 business days with: timeline, root cause, action items, owner, and verification plan.
- Feed triage learnings into: prompt-set extension (new probes), eval-harness test updates, and quant-profile adjustments.

Appendix: Example commands and JSON snippets
--------------------------------------------
1) Promotion manifest example (promotion-manifest.json):
{
  "model_id": "rwd-llm-3b-v2",
  "artifact_id": "rwd-llm-3b-v2-quant-q4_0",
  "quant_profile_id": "q_profile_2026-02",
  "eval_snapshot": "snapshot-2026-02-09-17",
  "owner": "asha.patel@redwood.ai"
}

2) Run a pre-promotion eval suite:
$ redwood-eval run --artifact rwd-llm-3b-v2-quant-q4_0 --suite full --out reports/2026-02-10.json

3) Trigger a bisect (automated):
$ redwood-bisect --metric quality_regressions_per_10k --candidates artifacts/list.txt --baseline artifact:prev 

4) Snapshot telemetry:
$ redwood-metrics snapshot --model rwd-llm-3b-v2 --since "-6h" --out /tmp/canary-snap.json

Definitions and glossary
------------------------
- Response Stability Index (RSI): a composite metric that compares normalized token-level distributions, semantic embedding distances, and function-call signature parity between two artifacts. Range 0–1 (1 = identical).
- Regression: measurable drop in task-specific eval metric or human-label pass rate compared to baseline beyond configured threshold.

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-02-10: Initial draft (Asha Patel).
- 2026-02-20: Added quantization thresholds and automated fallback policies (Lucia Fernandez).
- 2026-03-02: Adjusted canary ramp rules and human sampling size (Jonah Kim).

Notes and references
---------------------
- See allied docs: applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/promotion-readiness-synthetic-quant-safety-playbook-2026 for synthetic evaluation specifics.
- For security and privacy guidance during shadowing, consult security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/shadow-deployment-privacy-guidelines.

title: Eval Workflow Optimizer for Mixed-SLO Scenarios
content:
Overview:

This document describes the Eval Workflow Optimizer: a scheduling and orchestration pattern for running evaluation workloads across mixed SLO (latency/cost/quality) targets. The optimizer is intended for the eval-harness fleet and for shadow/onboarding runs used during model promotion, quantization readiness checks, and regression triage.

Purpose and scope:
- Provide a repeatable algorithm and reference implementation for prioritizing evaluation probes when budgets or capacity are constrained.
- Support heterogeneous SLO objectives per probe (e.g., 95th percentile latency <= 120ms, quality delta <= 0.5% loss, cost-per-probe <= $0.002).
- Integrate with model-onboarding gates, quantization profile checks, and regression bisect workflows.
- Applicable to scheduled bulk evals, continuous probe streams, and interactive canary runs.

Motivation:
Evaluation queues at Redwood must balance three competing hazards:
1) Missing regressions because parity probes were deprioritized for cost.
2) Cost overruns by running high-fidelity probes unnecessarily.
3) Slow feedback for promotion because latency-sensitive probes are starved.
A single prioritization policy that is aware of SLOs, historical variance, and operational constraints reduces these risks.

High-level goals:
- Multi-objective priority scoring: combine quality-risk, latency-sensitivity, and cost-sensitivity into a single score.
- Explainability: each priority decision should be traceable with contributing factors recorded in probe metadata.
- Pluggability: support alternate scoring modules (e.g., ML-based risk predictor) without changing runtime orchestration.
- Auditability: outputs feed into regression triage and oncall playbooks with deterministic tie-breaking for fast rollback.

Key terminology:
- Probe: a single eval input (prompt set slice) + expected metric(s).
- Eval job: a batch of probes executed together against a model variant.
- SLA class: a label representing a prioritized SLO bucket (e.g., realtime_lowlatency, low_cost_background, high_fidelity).
- Risk score: estimated probability that a probe will reveal a regression above a threshold.

Design overview:
1) Probe metadata enrichment (ingest stage):
   - Every probe includes: probe_id, slice_id, sla_class, expected_token_count, historical_variance, last_seen_delta, quant_profile_id (optional), and onboard_flag.
   - Enrichment service fetches historical telemetry and annotator-derived failure priors.

2) Scoring function (stateless microservice):
   - Inputs: enriched probe metadata + current capacity/cost budget snapshot + model variant attributes (quantization, kv-cache policy).
   - Output: numeric priority score and explanation vector.

3) Scheduler (stateful orchestrator):
   - Pulls prioritized probes and packs them into eval jobs using a packing heuristic that respects per-job max_tokens and latency headroom budgets.
   - Emits job manifests to the cluster and records expected cost.

Priority scoring (reference formula):
- score = w_quality * risk_score_norm + w_latency * latency_impact_norm + w_cost * inverse_cost_norm
- where each component is min-max normalized against a sliding 7-day window.
- default weights (tunable per-team): w_quality=0.5, w_latency=0.3, w_cost=0.2

Component details:
- risk_score_norm: normalized estimate (0..1) of regression likelihood computed from historical failures, semantic-shift signals, and seed-anchored probe variance.
- latency_impact_norm: normalized factor representing the delta to 95p latency if this probe were executed on candidate model (estimated via perf profiles). Higher values indicate probes that expose latency-sensitive regressions.
- inverse_cost_norm: normalized (1 / expected_cost_per_probe). This biases towards cheaper probes when cost weight is high.

Explainability and provenance:
- Each scored probe includes explanation vector: [risk:0.72, latency:0.18, cost:0.10] and a short text reason.
- The scheduler writes an entry to the eval ledger: {probe_id, score, model_variant, run_id, timestamp, explanation}. The ledger is append-only for audit.

Operational policies and SLO alignment:
- SLA class mapping examples:
  - realtime_lowlatency: w_latency=0.5, w_quality=0.4, w_cost=0.1, run window: 00:00-23:59 (preemptive on dedicated pools).
  - high_fidelity: w_quality=0.8, w_latency=0.05, w_cost=0.15, run window: batch-friendly offhours.
  - cost_background: w_cost=0.7, w_quality=0.2, w_latency=0.1, run window: cheapest cloud region preference.
- Fairness rule: at least 5% of high_fidelity probes are scheduled per day for each active model-variant to avoid blind spots.

Workflows and playbooks:
A) Model onboarding (promotion path)
1. Start: model candidate pushed to staging and assigned an onboarding job with mixed SLO bundles.
2. The optimizer schedules: small realtime_lowlatency probe set (fast feedback), prioritized high_fidelity probes (quality gate), and cost_background breadth probes.
3. Promotion decision rules (examples):
   - Must pass high_fidelity gate: quality delta <= 0.25% on critical slices.
   - Latency gate: 95p latency no worse than baseline + 25ms for realtime slices.
   - Cost gate: expected cost increase <= 10% over baseline or quantization-mitigated.
4. If any gate fails, create regression-triage ticket and enqueue targeted bisect probes.

B) Continuous probe stream (production monitoring)
1. Live telemetry feeds risk spikes to enrichment service.
2. Optimizer reweights probes dynamically (increase w_quality when drift detected).
3. If aggregated risk > threshold, run an urgent canary: 2x high_fidelity probes with human review.

C) Regression triage integration
1. When a regression alert is raised, the triage playbook triggers a focused eval job: probes are scored with w_quality=0.9 and packed for fastest execution (prefer pre-warmed hosts).
2. Bisect strategy: binary search across recent model changes and quantization_profile_id variants.
3. Triage output: causal hypothesis, evidence probes, and recommended rollback or mitigation (e.g., quant-fallback).

Configuration reference (table):
| field | type | example | description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| sla_class | string | realtime_lowlatency | maps to weight presets and run windows |
| max_tokens_per_job | int | 200000 | scheduler packing limit |
| max_concurrent_jobs | int | 12 | cluster-level throttle |
| cost_budget_per_hour | float | 5.0 | USD/hour target for eval pool |
| quant_profile_id | string | qpf-2026-03 | optional quantization profile to test against |

(Represented here as a markdown table for readability; the scheduler expects YAML/JSON manifests.)

Example scheduler manifest (YAML):
---
run_id: "eval-2026-03r1"
model_variant: "gptx-13b-quant-qpf-2026-03"
sla_class: "realtime_lowlatency"
max_tokens_per_job: 150000
probe_selectors:
  - slice: "payment-intent"
  - slice: "conversation-context-5"
priority_overrides:
  - tag: "regression-hot"
    w_quality: 0.9
---

Example probe payload (JSON):
{
  "probe_id": "probe-pt-00123",
  "expected_token_count": "348",
  "sla_class": "high_fidelity",
  "quant_profile_id": "qpf-2026-02b",
  "onboard_flag": "true"
}

Metrics and telemetry to emit:
- probe.score (gauge) with labels: model_variant, sla_class, slice_id
- eval.job.latency_p95 (ms) per job
- eval.job.token_cost_estimate (USD) per job and per-probe breakdown
- probe.explanation.trace_id (for audit)
- probe.outcome.{pass|fail|inconclusive} with reason tag

Alerting and escalation thresholds (recommended defaults):
- urgent_regression: aggregate failed critical probes > 0.5% over 30 minutes -> page SRE + applied-ml oncall.
- cost_exceeded: eval job actual_cost > budget * 1.5 -> notify cost-control channel and pause non-critical jobs.

Implementation notes and patterns:
- Use a feature-flagged rollout for new scoring weights; keep deterministic tie-breaker (lexicographic probe_id) to avoid flapping.
- Persist sliding-window normalizers in a single-timeseries store to keep scoring stable across restarts.
- Leverage quantization profile metadata to predict expected quality degradation and prefer targeted high-fidelity probes when quant changes are in scope.
- Provide a lightweight ML risk predictor as a pluggable module; default to rule-based heuristics if model is not available.

Validation and testing checklist (pre-release):
1. Unit tests: scoring math, normalization edge-cases (all-equal values).
2. Integration: end-to-end probe->ledger->scheduler->executor path using a synthetic workload generator.
3. Load test: scheduler must maintain <500ms scheduling latency at 2000 enqueued probes.
4. Chaos: simulate delayed enrichment and missing telemetry; system should degrade to conservative weights and still schedule critical realtime probes.

Ownership and runbook pointers:
- Owner: Applied ML - Eval Platform (team lead: Aisha Patel).
- Oncall: applied-ml-evals (rotation documented in eng-oncall calendar).
- Runbook snippets: restarting scoring service, rehydrating normalizers, emergency pause of all cost_background queues.

Rollout plan:
1. Canary: enable optimizer for 5% of eval traffic (non-critical models) for 2 weeks.
2. Measure: compare time-to-detect regressions, cost delta, and onboarding cycle time.
3. Expand: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with staged weight tuning and documented baseline comparisons.

Frequently asked questions:
Q: How do we avoid starving rare but high-impact probes?
A: The fairness rule reserves a minimum daily allocation per model-variant and enforces a floor for critical slices.

Q: Can teams override weights for their workloads?
A: Yes — teams can set per-job weight overrides in the manifest, subject to org-level policy limits.

Related artifacts and references:
- Onboarding acceptance matrix: /applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026
- Quant profile lifecycle: /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024

- Symptom: spike in failed probes for "payment-intent" slice after a quant rollout.
- Action: optimizer immediately increases w_quality for probes tagged with quant_profile_id == deployed profile, schedules focused bisect jobs, and opens triage ticket with explanation traces.

title: Onboarding-to-service eval playbook: cost-latency-quality triage
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes a prescriptive, reproducible process for taking a candidate model + runtime configuration from model-onboarding to production service with explicit gates for cost, latency, and output quality. It unifies eval harness runs, benchmark prompt sets, quantization triggers, and a compact regression triage flow so that engineers and ML owners can make consistent, auditable promotion decisions.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to text-generation and chat-capable transformer models being served on Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Covers staged validation: lab (controlled), shadow (traffic-mirroring), micro-canary (low-traffic), and canary-to-full rollout.
- Integrates: eval harness reports, prompt-slice benchmarks, quantization profiles, telemetry thresholds, and triage runbooks.
- Not covered: new multimodal model architecture onboarding (see separate spec), or offline-only research experiments.

Definitions:
- R-SI (Response Stability Index): the primary automated quality index computed by the eval harness; lower is better. Relative drop (%) is measured against the baseline model pinned to the serving route.
- Throughput SLO: tokens/sec per GPU under steady-state microburst.
- Latency SLO (p95): target p95 Round-Trip Token latency for a canonical request size (e.g., 256 tokens).
- Cost delta: per-1k token cost change projected by the Optimize toolkit comparing current and candidate config.

Owner and expected contributors:
- Model owner: individual or team responsible for model quality (ML team).
- Runtime owner: serving-runtime team (eng-serving-runtime).
- Eval steward: applied-ml team member running the harness and reviewing results.
- Release approver: product or platform PM for public routes.

Prerequisites (pre-run checklist):
1) Model artifact is registered in the model catalog with metadata (architecture, tokenizer, sequence-length, kv-cache compatibility, quantization hints).
2) A canonical prompt set exists for the target workload with representative slices (happy path, long-context, safety-sentinels, hallucination probes).
3) Baseline model pin and baseline telemetry baseline snapshot (last 30d).
4) CI job: eval-harness job and shadow-routing configuration are defined in the service's repo.

Evaluation stages (prescriptive):
1) Lab evaluation (local harness)
   - Purpose: find obvious regressions, sensitivity to context length and quantization.
   - Actions:
     a) Run eval-harness with the canonical prompt set (N=3 random seeds) and deterministic RNG where supported.
     b) Compute slice-level R-SI, semantic similarity (embedding cosine) against baseline, and answer acceptance rate on golden-label subsets.
     c) If candidate is quantized, include quant-replay test (replay identical inputs through quantized and fp32 variants).
   - Acceptance gate: no slice with >4% absolute drop in acceptance rate OR >8% relative increase in R-SI.

2) Shadow (mirrored traffic)
   - Purpose: collect real-traffic failure modes and latency/cost telemetry without impacting users.
   - Actions:
     a) Enable 100% mirror to candidate for a minimum of 24 hours or 1M tokens (whichever comes first).
     b) Capture production prompts and classify into slices offline; compare token-distribution differences.
     c) Compute live latency p50/p95 and error-rate delta vs baseline; calculate projected cost delta.
   - Shadow gates (auto-fail): p95 latency increase > 25% relative OR tail error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute OR projected cost delta > +40% and no compensating quality improvement.

3) Micro-canary (live limited traffic)
   - Purpose: validate user-visible quality and operational behavior under small production load.
   - Actions:
     a) Route 0.1% traffic for 2 hours, then 1% for 6 hours, then 5% for 24 hours if stable.
     b) Activate short-window alerting for R-SI and user-complaint events.
   - Canary gates: any human-reported quality regression or R-SI drift > 3% triggers rollback.

4) Staged rollout and final promotion
   - Purpose: full production promotion with rollback/rollback-conditions defined.
   - Actions:
     a) Gradual shift by 10% every 6 hours with monitoring checkpoints.
     b) Post-rollout 72-hour quality audit comparing sampled prompts to baseline.
   - Final acceptance: no persistent slice-level regression after 72 hours, latency/cost within agreed band.

Quantization trigger matrix (when to try quantized candidate):
| Signal | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Cost pressure | Projected token cost delta > +30% on baseline | Evaluate quantization variant (8-bit or mixed) to recover cost budget |
| Throughput shortage | Observed tokens/sec per GPU < target by >20% | Evaluate reduced-precision and KV layout optimizations |
| Model size | Artifact > 80GB | Prefer 8-bit-mixed or per-channel quant profile |
| Quality sensitivity | Safety-heavy slices drop >2% when quantized | Run block-fallback profiling and finer-grain quant (per-layer) |

Quantization evaluation checklist:
- Maintain exact seed pairs for replay: store (input, seed, baseline_output, quant_output).
- Run per-layer activation-correlation and attention-distribution checks.
- Run the quantized artifact through the eval-harness slice-by-slice and produce a quant-delta report.
- If quant-delta > configured threshold for safety slices, mark as "requires manual tuning" and do not proceed to shadow.

Metric thresholds and suggested actions (table):
| Metric | Baseline Target / SLO | Alert threshold | Auto-fail threshold | Suggested immediate action |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| p95 latency (256 tokens) | <= 220ms | > 260ms | > 350ms | Pause rollout, revert to previous pinned model; run profiling-playbook |
| R-SI (aggregate) | stable within +/-1% | change > 2% | change > 5% | Stop rollout, trigger regression triage, notify model owner |
| Safety-sentinel failure rate | <= 0.2% | > 0.5% | > 1.0% | Immediate rollback; engage safety team |
| Error-rate (5xx) | <= 0.1% | > 0.3% | > 0.8% | Rollback, consult runtime team |
| Projected cost delta | <= +10% | > +25% | > +50% | Consider quantization or config rollback |

Regression triage compact runbook (first 30 minutes):
1) Triage lead (oncall) acknowledges alert and creates a triage ticket with the hash of the candidate artifact.
2) Reproduce the failure in the lab: replay top 100 recent failing requests against baseline and candidate in the harness.
3) If failure reproduces, run quick-bisect: check differences between candidate commit and last known-good (use model artifact diff where possible).
4) If bisect points to quantization, run quant-replay with per-layer logs and attach to ticket.
5) If no immediate root cause, rollback serving route and start a deeper investigation (assign model owner + runtime engineer + eval steward).

Detailed triage checklist (30m–8h):
- Collect: failing request IDs, tokenized inputs, full KV cache context, deterministic seeds used.
- Run: three-seed replays, per-slice scoring, attention-heatmap comparison.
- Decision rubric: if a single slice shows >5% quality regression or any safety-sentinel regression, favor rollback and block-promote.

Promote-with-conditions (how to allow conditional promotion despite a non-critical regression):
- Minor throughput/latency regressions: allow promotion if cost delta improves by >20% and no safety regressions, with a scheduled 48-hour follow-up audit.
- Small quality drift in low-impact slices: allow canary expansion only if compensating human-in-the-loop review plan is in place and mitigation (prompt rewrite or scoring filter) is added.

Operational artifacts produced by this process:
- Eval-harness report (CSV + JSON), including seed-level outputs and per-slice diffs.
- Shadow telemetry snapshot (S3 link) with latency/cost histograms.
- Quant-delta report (per-layer metrics) and per-token divergence samples.
- Triage ticket with reproduction artifacts and final RCC (root cause classification).

CLI and automation snippets (examples):
- Run a lab eval (example):
  redwood-eval run --model candidate:v1 --prompt-set canonical-workload --seeds 3 --out=reports/candidate_lab.json

- Start shadow routing (example Helm/infra):
  kubectl patch svc my-service -p '{"spec": {"template": {"metadata": {"annotations": {"redwood.io/shadow-to":"candidate:v1"}}}}}'

- Quick rollback (API):
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/routes/my-service/rollback -d '{"to_model":"baseline:v42"}'

Appendix A — Example eval slice table (recommended):
| slice_id | description | minimum_samples | criticality |
|---|---|---:|---|
| happy-path | Short instructions and few-shot examples | 500 | medium |
| long-context | 1024+ context with interleaved system messages | 300 | high |
| safety-sentinels | adversarial safety probes derived from safety-lab | 200 | critical |
| hallucination-probes | knowledge-based QA with gold answers | 250 | high |

Appendix B — Reporting template (copy into ticket):
- Model candidate: <artifact:hash>
- Baseline: <artifact:hash>
- Snapshot time: <UTC>
- Key metrics delta: {p95_latency:+X ms, R-SI:+Y%, cost:+Z%}
- Top 10 failing request IDs: [id..]
- Immediate action taken: rollback | mitigation | continue-monitoring

Related documentation and links:
- Eval harness runner: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/serving-simulation-eval-harness-2026
- Quantization repair: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-output-degradation-detect-and-repair-protocol-2026
- Shadow-rollforward playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/shadow-rollforward-and-mesh-simulation-playbook-2026

FAQ (short):
Q: When is a quantized candidate allowed to proceed to shadow?
A: Only after passing the lab quant-replay with no safety-sentinel delta > 0.5% and after a per-slice R-SI delta < 3%.

Q: Who signs off final promotion?
A: Model owner + runtime owner + product approver must sign the promotion ticket.

Ownership and lifecycle notes:
- This document is owned by applied-ml team (engineering). Review cadence: quarterly or whenever a critical incident reveals a missing step.
- Maintain canonical prompt set in the prompt-sets repo and version it alongside model artifacts.

Change history:
- 2026-01-12: initial draft by Maya Patel.
- 2026-02-03: added quantization trigger matrix and regression triage compact runbook (reviewers: Diego Ramos, Priya Nair).

End of document

title: FunctionCall Fidelity Lab and Shadow Benchmarking Guide
content:
Summary

This guide documents a repeatable lab and shadow-benchmarking process for evaluating function-calling fidelity across production-like serving configurations. It targets mixed-precision and quantized model variants, KV-cache behavior, and real-time function-call wiring (tool calls / structured outputs). The audience is evaluation engineers, ML infra owners, and model onboarding leads.

Goals

- Define a benchmark harness and experiment recipes to measure: correctness of function call routing, argument preservation, latency/throughput impact, and fidelity regressions introduced by quantization or cache interactions.
- Standardize telemetry (events, spans, labels) and pass/fail thresholds for promotion decisions.
- Provide shadow deployment recipes and runbooks for triage and rollback.

Scope and exclusions

- In-scope: sequence-level functioncall correctness, tokenization edgecases that affect function arg boundaries, quantized int8/4/3-mode artifacts, KV-cache warm/cold interactions, and batching impacts.
- Out-of-scope: hallucination classification beyond function call semantics (see fidelity labs for broader hallucination tests), model training changes.

Definitions

- FunctionCall: any structured output where the model emits a function name and arguments intended for downstream execution.
- Fidelity: exactness and completeness of function name, arguments, and typed fields compared to golden ground-truth.
- Shadow Benchmark: non-prod traffic replayed to new model variant in parallel with production endpoint (no customer-facing traffic).

High-level lab architecture

1) Shadow harness sits in the eval mesh; it receives replicated requests and routes them to candidate variants behind a controlled traffic mirror.
2) Evaluator sidecar parses outputs for functioncall structure and runs deterministic checks and fuzzy similarity scoring.
3) Telemetry collector aggregates per-request fidelity signals, latency/tail percentiles, token counts, and quantization signals.

Typical deployment layout (text diagram):

  prod-router --> prod-model (stable)
               \--> shadow-copier --> shadow-harness --> candidate-models
                                              \--> evaluator-sidecar --> metrics-collector

Required lab resources

- Dedicated shadow GPU pool with identical hw profiles to target fleet (e.g., a mix of A100-80GB and H100 where relevant).
- Evaluator containers with access to golden-answer registry and annotation backends.
- Telemetry retention for 90 days for shadow-benchmark artifacts.
- Isolation network namespace to avoid accidental egress.

Benchmarks and recipes

We provide three canonical recipes; each is a reproducible job in the eval-harness scheduler.

1) Canonical FunctionCall Unit Suite

Purpose: microbenchmarks to validate argument serialization, nested argument support, and field-level typing across variants.
Inputs: curated set of 500 function-call prompts covering: typed args (int/float/string), nested JSON args, long string blobs (>= 4k chars), and edge token boundaries.
Procedure:
  1. Start candidate model in shadow with quantization profile X (e.g., int8-gptq).
  2. Send batched requests (size=1, 8, 32) to measure batching effect.
  3. Compare outputs to golden via the fidelity scorer (exact-match, normalized-JSON compare, and tokenized edit-distance).
Pass criteria:
  - 99% exact match on function name.
  - 98% schema-validated argument presence for required fields.
  - Mean argument edit-distance <= 0.02 (normalized).
Failure actions: automatically flag regression, create triage ticket with headless diff logs and sample IDs.

2) Shadow Traffic Fidelity + Latency Stress

Purpose: measure fidelity under production traffic distributions including long-context sessions and KV-cache warmup patterns.
Inputs: sampled 24h traffic trace (anonymized), seed ratio 1:1000 of live traffic for shadowing.
Procedure:
  1. Replay sample traffic with preserved session IDs to candidate and baseline models.
  2. Instrument KV-cache hit/miss events and the first-token latency.
  3. Compute cohorted fidelity: new-to-old user sessions, long-context (>2048 tokens), and rapid-turnaround microbursts.
Key metrics to capture (per slice):
  - FunctionNameAccuracy (FNA)
  - ArgumentSchemaCoverage (ASC)
  - FirstTokenLatency P50 / P95 / P99
  - KV-Cache Hit Rate and fidelity delta at cold start
Pass thresholds (slice-level):
  - FNA drop <= 0.5% vs baseline
  - P99 latency increase <= 15ms absolute
  - ASC drop <= 1% for critical slices
Failure actions: trigger micro-canary, require engineer signoff for promotion.

3) Quant + Batching Interop Sweep

Purpose: identify edgecases where quantization interacts with batching that alter tokenization alignment leading to argument truncation or delimiter corruption.
Inputs: 2000 synthesized prompts designed to create token boundary collisions (e.g., strings that align to subtoken borders).
Procedure:
  1. Run candidate with quant profile family (FP16, int8, int4) across batch sizes {1,4,16,64}.
  2. Enable/disable prefix-KV cache and compare outputs.
  3. Log token-level hashes for argument fields to detect off-by-one shifts.
Metrics and alerts:
  - TokenHashShiftRate >= 0.1% => investigate quant kernel selection and tokenizer handling
  - FieldTruncationRate per batch-size => if > 0.05% for batch>=16 mark as high risk

Telemetry schema (minimum fields)

We standardize a small set of telemetry labels and metrics to keep analytics portable across hosts:

- request_id (string)
- snapshot_id (string) // shadow snapshot reference
- model_variant (string)
- quant_profile (string)
- batch_size (int)
- kv_cache_state (cold/warm/hot)
- function_name (string)
- function_fidelity_score (float) // [0.0 - 1.0]
- argument_edit_distance (float)
- first_token_latency_ms (float)
- total_tokens (int)
- fidelity_fail_reasons (csv)

Example telemetry event (JSON payload shown as text):

{
  "request_id": "r-12345",
  "snapshot_id": "snap-2026-06-02-01",
  "model_variant": "v2-quant-int8",
  "quant_profile": "gptq-int8-optimized",
  "batch_size": 4,
  "kv_cache_state": "warm",
  "function_name": "create_invoice",
  "function_fidelity_score": 0.987,
  "argument_edit_distance": 0.003,
  "first_token_latency_ms": 23.5,
  "total_tokens": 124,
  "fidelity_fail_reasons": ""
}

Scoring rules (evaluator sidecar)

- Function name exact-match => +0.6 score
- Required args present and schema-valid => +0.25
- Argument edit-distance normalized <= 0.01 => +0.15
- If any required rule fails => fidelity_score set to 0 for that request (manual review recommended)

Automated triage actions and severity levels

- severity: info => score delta < 0.2 and latency delta < 10ms
- severity: moderate => score delta in [0.2, 0.5] OR latency P99 increase in [10ms, 50ms]
- severity: high => score delta > 0.5 OR argument truncation events > 0.1% of traffic

High severity runbook (shortened)

1. Pager duty alert to inference-oncall and eval-owner.
2. Capture 1,000 failing traces into the triage bucket.
3. Run deterministic repro job with identical seed, batch-size, and quant-profile.
4. If repro succeeds, isolate difference in kernel selection and forward to runtime-kernel team with diff logs.
5. If repro fails, escalate to model-oncall and consider rollback to baseline variant immediately.

Promotion decision matrix

- Promote when: aggregate fidelity_score delta < 0.05 AND for all critical slices (payments, auth, tooling) FNA drop <= 0.5% AND latency increases within thresholds.
- Conditional promote (canary): small fidelity regressions but material cost savings (>18%) — require feature-flagged canary with 1% traffic for 7 days and daily fidelity audits.
- Reject: fidelity_score delta >= 0.1 or any high severity alerts.

CLI and job examples

Start a canonical unit suite job (example):

redwood-eval submit --suite functioncall-unit --model v2-quant-int8 --snapshot snap-2026-06-02 --batch-sizes 1,8,32 --out logs/func-unit-20260602.log

YAML job manifest (example):

job_name: funccall-quant-sweep-2026
target_models: [v2-quant-int8, v2-fp16]
prompt_asset: gs://eval-assets/functioncall-edgecases/2026-05
batch_policy: [1,4,16,64]
replay_window: 1h
telemetry_sink: metrics/prod-shadow/fncall

Privacy and data handling

- Always anonymize PII in shadow traces per Data Management policy. Replace customer IDs with stable synthetic identifiers.
- Retention: raw shadow artifacts are retained for 90 days; summarized fidelity metrics for 365 days.
- For private/dedicated customer traffic, run shadow bench under the private consent contract; obtain legal signoff if telemetry contains sensitive metadata.

Ownership and responsibilities

- Eval-harness: maintain job manifests, scheduling, and telemetry contracts.
- Model-onboarding: supply golden schema and expected argument formats, test vectors.
- Serving-runtime: ensure kernel determinism and documented quant profiles.
- SRE: maintain shadow GPU capacity and isolation.

Appendix: quick triage checklist

1. Confirm repro on shadow with identical manifest (batch, kv-state, quant).
2. Diff token-level hashes for arguments.
3. Check kernel selection logs and fallbacks.
4. Review last successful promotion artifacts and identify divergence points.
5. If quant-linked, attempt FP16 run to isolate quant vs. model drift.

Appendix: links and references

- Related: Quantized artifact eval gate and rollout (internal)
- Related: Shadow deployment eval playbook (internal)
- Telemetry contract: eval-harness/telemetry-schema-2025 (internal)

Contact

For questions or improvements to this guide, contact Maya Chen (mchen@redwood.ai) or the eval-harness Slack channel (#eval-harness).

title: Multimodal function-call onboarding contract and priming budget specification
content:
Summary:
This document defines the onboarding contract for services that expose multimodal function-call models to Redwood’s inference platform. It covers mandatory evaluation criteria, priming (few-shot) budget accounting, privacy constraints for example probes, and an operational roll-forward/rollback plan tailored to mixed-precision and quantized variants. The goal is to provide a deterministic acceptance gate for promotion from shadow to live, reduce regressions caused by priming-context changes, and standardize cost/quality trade-offs across tenants.

Scope:
- Applies to: any model suite that: accepts both text and images (or other non-text inputs) and supports the function-call API surface (structured tool outputs).
- Does NOT apply to: unimodal text-only models, embedding-only endpoints, or purely research validation artifacts.

Key definitions:
- Priming budget: the token + image-context budget (in token-equivalent units) assigned to each request for few-shot examples and system content. This is tracked per-route and per-tenant.
- Function-call fidelity: the probability-weighted correctness of structured outputs (fields, types, and side-effect intent) when executed by downstream toolchain. Measured as a composite F-score.
- Shadow cohort: an isolated traffic mirror used for onboarding where privacy-preserving probes + sampled live traffic are replayed against the new model.

Onboarding contract (must be satisfied for promotion):
1) Functional acceptance:
   - Unit-level function-call tests: 95% pass rate on schema validation for all critical tool signatures (strict schema enforcement).
   - Semantic alignment: cross-check produced arguments against a ground truth table of 500 seeded examples; minimum composite F-score >= 0.92 for production-tier customers, >= 0.88 for internal dev-tier.
2) Latency & resource constraints:
   - 95th percentile response < configured route SLO (default 450ms for interactive multimodal function calls).
   - Peak memory/KV-cache growth within 1.2x of baseline for warm paths.
3) Priming budget stability:
   - End-to-end latency and token cost measured under priming budgets (three representative budgets: small=64, medium=256, large=1024 token-equivalents) must not exceed baseline relative degradation thresholds (latency +20%, cost +25%).
4) Privacy & data handling:
   - No persistent retention of raw customer images or personal data in evaluator logs. Probes must be hashed and stored only when consented.
5) Quant & cache compatibility:
   - When quantized variants are used, per-slice embedding drift metric must be within the model-suite’s quant-fallback bounds (delta-embedding-cosine < 0.015).

Priming budget model (how we compute token-equivalents):
- Text tokens: 1 token = 1 unit.
- Images: compute token-equivalent by image complexity score (heuristic based on resolution and metadata). Default mapping: thumbnail (<=256px) = 16 units, small (<=512px) = 48 units, medium (<=1024px) = 128 units, large = 320 units. Teams may refine mapping during onboarding but must document the mapping in the model manifest.

Priming budget accounting table (example):
| Route | Default budget | Typical few-shot mix | Max per-request | Cost bucket |
|--|--:|--|--:|--:|
| chat-multimodal-interactive | 256 | 1 image (small) + 3 examples (each ~32 tokens) | 1024 | medium |
| batch-attachment-summarize | 512 | 4 images (thumbnail) + system prompt 64t | 2048 | large |

(Represent the above table in Confluence as a simple two-column table in the UI for maintainers.)

Privacy & probe design rules:
- Synthetic-first: prefer synthetic probes for rare PII cases. If using live-capture probes, apply on-capture redaction and store only hashed descriptors in evaluator logs.
- Consent recording: evaluator ingestion must include a reference ID tying each probe to consent metadata stored in the privacy ledger (see Related Links).
- Probe retention: default 90-day retention for annotated probes; retention extension requires Data Governance approval.

Acceptance tests and metrics (automated):
- Functional: schema-validation pass rate (see contract).
- Quality: composite F-score (field correctness, semantic match, argument completeness).
- Coherence: Response Stability Index (RSI) over 10K replayed anchors; delta <= 0.03 vs baseline.
- Token economy: per-1M request unit cost delta vs baseline <= +30% during initial canary window.

Canary and promotion procedure (numbered runbook):
1) Prepare shadow cohort: deploy candidate model to shadow environment with identical routing and priming budgets. Mirror 1–3% of production sampled requests (apply PII gating).
2) Run 72-hour probe suite: seed with 5k synthetic + 2k hashed live-capture probes, including edge multimodal permutations.
3) Automated evaluation: run the acceptance tests; generate an onboarding report (JSON manifest) with metrics and artifacts (diffs, counterexamples). Example report fields: model_id, route, composite_f_score, rsi_delta, priming_cost_delta, quant_compat_flag.
4) Technical review: onboarding owner and two reviewers must sign off. If any metric fails soft thresholds, iterate with remediation patches.
5) Phased canary: 0.5% live traffic -> 2% -> 10% over 24–72 hour windows, each step gated by automated metric checks.
6) Full promotion: only if canary windows pass for 48 hours with no severity >= P2 regressions.

Rollback quick paths (short checklist):
- Trigger conditions: schema validation failure in >0.5% of requests, composite F-score drop > 0.05, or latency spike > 2x baseline.
- Immediate action: open rollback via the rollout API, demote model, and activate previous stable variant. Notify SRE and Product.
- Postmortem: 72-hour incident review and regression triage meeting.

Monitoring and alerts (operational knobs):
- SLOs to instrument: schema-pass-rate (SLO 99.5%), functioncall-latency P95, composite-f-score rolling mean (7d), priming_cost_rate (tokens/sec), quant_fallback_rate.
- Alert thresholds: schema-pass-rate < 99.0% (P1), composite-f-score drop > 0.04 (P2), priming_cost_rate surge > 30% sustained 15m (P2).

Example onboarding manifest snippet (YAML):
```
model_id: multimodal-fn-v3
routes:
  - name: chat-multimodal-interactive
    default_budget: 256
    priming_profile:
      - type: example
        avg_tokens: 32
        count: 3
      - type: image
        size_hint: small
quant_compatibility:
  enabled: true
  embedding_delta_threshold: 0.015
privacy:
  probe_retention_days: 90
```

Failure modes and recommended mitigations:
- Priming explosion: if users send large numbers of examples per request, enforce route-level hard caps and return a 429 with guidance.
- Structured-arg hallucination: add a post-commit schema validator that rejects malformed arguments before hitting downstream tools and route to safe-fallback (no-op) with user-facing message.
- Quant-induced tokenization drift: maintain a shadow quantized variant and add automatic quant-fallback routing when drift metrics exceed thresholds.

Checklist (pre-promotion):
- [ ] Manifest filled and stored in model-registry.
- [ ] Shadow run completed and report produced.
- [ ] Privacy ledger entries for probes exist.
- [ ] Two reviewers signed off in PR.
- [ ] Canary policy configured and rollback variant set.

Owners and contacts:
- Onboarding owner: Marisol Ortega (applied-ml)
- Runtime owner: Ethan Park (serving-runtime)
- Privacy & compliance: Dina Sattar (security & compliance)
- SRE oncall: refer to the oncall rota link in Related Links

Related Links:
- Model registry manifest template: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/model-manifest-templates
- Privacy ledger and consent API: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/probe-privacy-ledger
- Evaluator SDK adapters: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/evaluator-sdk-adapter-patterns-for-private-and-dedicated-2026

Revision history:
- 2026-01-12: initial draft by Marisol Ortega.
- 2026-02-05: added priming budget token-equivalent mapping and example table (reviewer: Ethan Park).
- 2026-03-02: clarified privacy retention defaults and added quant compatibility clause (reviewer: Dina Sattar).

title: Safety Sandbox and Fingerprint Certification Protocol
content:
Summary:
This document defines the Safety Sandbox and Fingerprint Certification Protocol used during model onboarding at Redwood. The protocol creates an isolated, reproducible evaluation environment where we run adversarial and drift simulations, extract model "fingerprints", and score safety regressions versus baseline models. Successful completion of the protocol is a hard gate for promotion to staging and production-serving tiers (hosted, dedicated, private).

Goals:
- Provide a standardized, automatable safety certification that complements functional and performance acceptance tests.
- Detect subtle safety regressions introduced by quantization, optimization, or new model checkpoints.
- Produce machine-readable fingerprints and scores to track model drift across versions and deployment modes.

When to run:
1) New model checkpoint onboarding (all promotion candidates).
2) After quantization or custom kernel builds that change execution semantics.
3) Major prompt/template changes or new instruction-tuning passes.
4) Periodic re-certification for models serving high-risk routes (monthly).

High-level workflow:
1. Preflight: verify test harness, sample prompt sets, secrets access, and resource quotas.
2. Sandbox run: execute adversarial scenarios and drift simulations in isolated infra (ephemeral cluster).
3. Fingerprint extraction: compute fingerprint vectors for response distributions and compute similarity metrics versus baseline.
4. Scoring and gating: produce Safety Signal Index (SSI) and component metrics; compare against thresholds.
5. Triaging and remediation: if failing, run root-cause probes (quantization-aware reruns, tokenization checks) and categorize fixes.
6. Promotion: record certification artifact and push to model registry with pass/fail tag and remediation notes.

Sandbox environment details:
- Environment: ephemeral Kubernetes namespace with pinned runtime image (sandbox-runtime:v3.1).
- Data isolation: no customer PII used; synthetic and redacted prompt sets only.
- Resource profile: CPU workers for adversarial generation + a small GPU pool (1–4 GPUs) to exercise large context behavior.
- Artifacts: raw responses, token-level traces, KV cache snapshots (where applicable), fingerprint vectors, and evaluation logs archived to secure storage.

Fingerprint definition and algorithm (high level):
- Fingerprint = aggregated embedding distribution + signature hash.
- Step 1: Collect N responses per prompt shard (N=30 default) across a diverse prompt set (instructions, dialogs, code, long context).
- Step 2: Convert responses to sentence-embeddings (use st-encoder-v2) and compute per-prompt mean vector.
- Step 3: Aggregate means into a distribution summary (PCA projection + top-5 eigenvectors) and create a compact fingerprint vector of length 256.
- Step 4: Compute signature hash (HMAC-SHA256) of normalized response token sequence statistics (avg token entropy, avg token length, top-20 tokenizer tokens).
- Collision detection: use LSH index to find existing fingerprints with cosine similarity > 0.92; flag potential reuse/plagiarism and surface to reviewers.

Safety Signal Index (SSI) and component metrics:
