This protocol is intentionally conservative for open production traffic. Teams can adopt accelerated variants for low-risk routes with documented owner approval. Keep this doc updated with new tooling commands if redwoodctl or chaos tooling changes.

title: Model Deprecation & Back-compat Evaluation Playbook
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the cross-team process, eval surface, telemetry signals, and rollout controls required to safely deprecate a served model while preserving backward compatibility for existing customers and workloads. It focuses on: model version removal, quantized variant retirement, prompt-compatibility guarantees, and automated regression triage during deprecation windows.

Goals
-----
- Provide a repeatable, low-risk deprecation path that prevents silent regressions for customers.
- Define quality gates (quant, prompt, KV-cache, latency) that must be met before each deprecation milestone.
- Standardize telemetry and alerting so regressions discovered during deprecation are actionable and triaged within 24 hours.

Scope
-----
Applies to: Hosted API model variants, Dedicated model pools, and Private deployments where Redwood is the operator. Excludes: (1) customer-managed external models, (2) end-of-life hardware changes (handled by infra runbooks).

Stakeholders & Ownership
------------------------
- Owner (Primary): Applied ML — Model Lifecycle Team
- Secondary owners: Serving Runtime (latency/throughput checks), Eval Platform (probe orchestration), SRE (capacity & incident ops), Customer Success (customer notifications)
- Communications: Product comms + release-notes entry required 2 weeks before final removal.

Quality Gates & Key Metrics
---------------------------
Each deprecation phase requires passing the following gates. All thresholds are configurable per-service in the model-deprecation manifest.

| Metric                            | Gate (example)                                 | Window |
|-----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|--------|
| Micro-regression delta (accuracy) | <= 0.8% median degradation on production probe-set | 7d     |
| Latency P95                       | <= 10% relative increase vs baseline           | 7d     |
| Token-cost per request            | <= 5% increase                                 | 7d     |
| Embedding drift (cosine)          | median delta <= 0.02                            | 14d   |
| Functioncall fidelity score       | A/B weighted score >= 0.98                      | 7d    |

If any gate fails, the deprecation step must pause and trigger regression-triage (see section below).

Eval Suites and Tests
---------------------
- Production Probe Suite: tenant-weighted probe set representing top 20% of live traffic. Run continuously during deprecation.
- Backcompat Fuzzing: random perturbation probe generator that exercises edge-case prompts and tokenization anomalies.
- KV-Cache Consistency Checks: replay warm-start sequences to ensure responses when cache warmed are within drift budget.
- Quantized Variant Validation: per-quant profile acceptance tests (see YAML example in Appendix A).
- Canaries: micro-canary (0.1% traffic) + shadow canary (mirror 5% of traffic) before each traffic migration.

Deprecation Procedure (high-level numbered steps)
------------------------------------------------
1. Proposal and Impact Assessment (T-30 to T-14 days)
   - Create deprecation RFC: reason, target removal date, list of affected model variants and exporters, customers likely impacted.
   - Run a simulation eval on the production probe suite and publish the diff report.

2. Pre-deprecation Hardening (T-14 to T-7 days)
   - Ensure alternative variants exist and are marked as compatible in the model catalog.
   - Schedule shadow runs for 7 days; collect metrics.
   - Update release notes and CS playbook; schedule customer notifications for high-impact tenants.

3. Canary & Shadowing (T-7 to T-1 days)
   - Start mirror shadow for 5% of live traffic; run probe-based fidelity checks continuously.
   - Open a live regression hunt channel (#regression-hunt) with owners subscribed.

4. Gradual Traffic Migration (T day)
   - Step 1: route 0.1% to replacement variant for 1 hour, validate gates.
   - Step 2: if green, increase to 1% for 3 hours, validate.
   - Step 3: if green, 5% for 24 hours, then 25%, 50%, 100% as defined by SLOs and capacity.

5. Final Remove & Audit (T+7 days)
   - Remove model artifacts from catalog, purge metadata, and archive training/eval manifests.
   - Run final reconciliation to ensure no active references remain.

Shadow & Canary Guidance
------------------------
- Shadow mode must run with identical inputs and store side-by-side outputs for at least 7 days.
- Use per-tenant hashing to ensure representative coverage; prioritize tenants with high request density and high LTV.
- Shadow telemetry should include: token counts, latency, model-version tag, quant-profile id, prompt-template id, and functioncall signatures.

Quantization-specific Checks
---------------------------
- For any deprecation involving quantized variants, execute the Quant Fallback Matrix: test quantized->fp32, quantized->alternative-quant, and quantized->FP16 fallbacks.
- Verify deterministic behavior for KV cache keys across quantized variants.
- Run targeted coherence tests for long-context (>2048 tokens) scenarios to capture subtle attention truncation regressions.

Prompt & API Back-compat Testing
--------------------------------
- API contract stability: validate that response JSON/YAML schemas are identical for the canonical request suites.
- Prompt compatibility: run prompt-preservation tests which assert: same control tokens, same functioncall triggers, and same structured output anchors.
- Rate limiting & error codes: ensure client-visible error surface for the replacement variant is a superset of the retiring variant (no new 5xx error classes introduced).

Telemetry Signals & Alerting
---------------------------
Primary signals to monitor (automated alerts):
- Probe-failure-rate > 3x baseline for 10m -> P1 alert to oncall and ML-owner.
- Latency P95 increase > 15% sustained over 30m -> investigate.
- Embedding similarity drop median > 0.03 for 24h -> trigger embedding-safety review.
- Sudden drop in success callback rates for functioncalls > 1% -> run functioncall regression harness.

Regression Triage Playbook (if a gate fails)
-------------------------------------------
1. Stall migration and label the deprecation run as 'paused'.
2. Kick off automated bisect: compare baseline vs candidate across probe slices (cohort-by-cohort).
3. If bisect isolates to quant or tokenizer change, escalate to Quant Team with the bisect artifact.
4. If behavior is prompt-dependent, create a prioritized prompt repair ticket and add to the next patch release.
5. Communicate to Customer Success within 4 hours for affected tenants and provide mitigation options (rollback, pin model).

Rollback & Emergency Un-deprecation
----------------------------------
- Emergency rollback is allowed at any migration step. Rollback procedure: revert routing config -> re-enable retired model's network endpoints -> rerun canary smoke tests. Expected rollback RTO: 15 minutes for hosted API.
- Keep a read-only archive of retired model responses for 90 days to support legal/forensics requests.

Post-deprecation Retrospective
-----------------------------
- Within 2 weeks post-removal, run a retrospective: list of incidents, missed signals, customer impact, and follow-up actions.
- Update the model catalog entry with a deprecation postmortem link and lessons learned.

Appendix A: Example Quant Validation Manifest (YAML)
--------------------------------------------------
---
model_id: my-model-v2
quant_profiles:
  - id: q8_knl_v1
    tests:
      - name: functioncall-fidelity
        suite: functioncall-primary
        pass_threshold: 0.98
      - name: longcontext-coherence
        suite: longcontext-2k
        pass_threshold: 0.985
      - name: kvcache-stability
        suite: kv-warmup-100
        pass_threshold: 0.995
---

Appendix B: CLI commands & query examples
-----------------------------------------
# Run a shadow job for "prod-service" using the evaluator API
redwood-eval run --service prod-service --model my-model-v2 --mode shadow --duration 168h --output /tmp/shadow-artifact.tgz

# Quick bisect: compare candidate vs baseline on specific slice
redwood-eval bisect --baseline my-model-v1 --candidate my-model-v2 --slice prompt-family=invoice-extraction --metrics accuracy,latency --out /tmp/bisect.json

Appendix C: Release Notes Template
----------------------------------
- Title: Deprecation of {model_id} on {date}
- Why: short justification (security/maintenance/duplicate variant)
- Replacements: list of recommended model ids and expected deltas
- Customer action: how to pin or remediate if you see regressions
- Contact: cs@redwood.ai and #model-lifecycle

Appendix D: Acceptance Checklist (to be completed by ML owner)
------------------------------------------------------------
- [ ] RFC published and reviewers signed off
- [ ] Shadow telemetry ran for minimum 7 days
- [ ] All Quality Gates green for final 72 hours
- [ ] Customer notifications sent (if >5 impacted tenants)
- [ ] Rollback plan tested and verified
- [ ] Post-removal archive scheduled

Notes and cross-references
--------------------------
- Use the model-catalog tags "compatibility:backwards" and add a deprecation:date metadata field.
- For Private deployments, coordinate with the onprem-packaging team to ensure artifact removal is performed by the customer or via an agreed maintenance window.

If you have questions about applying this playbook to a specific model, contact the Model Lifecycle Team or add a comment to this page.

title: Service boundary evaluation and quantization migration checklist
content:
Overview

This checklist defines the cross-functional operational playbook for evaluating service boundaries and migrating model serving from floating-point artifacts to quantized artifacts (8-bit, 4-bit, mixed) with minimal user-facing regression risk. The goal is to ensure predictable latency/cost improvements while preserving quality and observability contracts. This document ties together: eval-harness checks, prompt and benchmark selection, model onboarding gates, quality guardrails, quantization profile validation, and regression triage steps.

Scope

- Applies to any model promotion that changes runtime numeric representation (FP16/FP32 -> INT8/PACT/4-bit) for production endpoints (hosted, dedicated, or private).
- Includes single-model migrations and model-variant rollouts where a quantized variant will be routed by policy.
- Excludes research-only artifacts and offline-only embeddings refreshes.

Primary owners and contacts

- Service owner: Priya Natarajan (ML Infra / Applied ML) - priya@redwood.example.com
- SRE/Performance owner: Jamal Carter - jamal@redwood.example.com
- Evaluation lead: Ethan Miller - ethan@redwood.example.com

Priorities and acceptance criteria (summary)

- Safety/Quality: Zero critical semantic regressions on production prompt families; no increase in severity-1 (S1) safety sentinels.
- Latency: P95 token generation latency should not exceed baseline by more than 10% under nominal load.
- Cost: Expected per-token cost reduction (est. 20–60%) must be validated in a 24h shadow run.
- Observability: Traces, token-level cost breakdowns, and eval-sentinels must be active and firing against baseline slices.

Pre-migration checklist (must be satisfied before building quant artifacts)

1) Workload and boundary analysis
   - Identify the service boundary (API route/model key) and all downstream consumers.
   - Produce a baseline workload fingerprint: token length distribution, function-calls ratio, streaming vs batch, cold start rate.
   - Tag the route with a migration candidate label in the config catalog.

2) Prompt & benchmark selection
   - Select a representative probe set (recommended 5k–20k probes) split across: high-traffic slices, safety-sensitive prompts, long-context prompts, multi-turn threads, and rare edgecases.
   - For each probe include: canonical prompt, expected anchor tokens, pass/fail sentinel, and a golden response reference where applicable.

3) Eval harness configuration
   - Configure a dedicated eval job with: deterministic seeds, temperature and max_tokens matching production, and tokenization parity checks.
   - Enable both delta-metrics and qualitative human review queues for slices with >X% regression (X default 5%).

Quant profiling & artifact build checklist

- Quant profile selection: list candidate quant profiles (per-layer or per-kernel) and annotate tradeoffs. Example table: 

  | Candidate | Precision | Notes | Expected cost delta | Owner |
  |-----------|-----------|-------|---------------------|-------|
  | qp-int8   | 8-bit     | Default per-tensor symmetric | -40% | infra-quant |
  | qp-4bit   | 4-bit     | Aggressive, requires KV-cache tuning | -60% | infra-quant |
  | mixed-8-4 | hybrid    | FP16 for attention, 4-bit for FFN | -50% | infra-quant |

- Locally validate tensor parity (per-layer L2 and activation distribution checks) and record artifacts in the quant-catalog location.
- Attach quant metadata to model manifest: quant_profile_id, sample-seed, compressor-version, and build-recipe id.

Shadow/validation stage (golden path)

1) Shadow run (no traffic impact):
   - Run the quantized model in shadow for 24–72 hours against live traffic sampling (recommended 2–10% traffic sample).
   - Capture the following telemetry for both baseline and quantized variant: token-level latency (p50/p95/p99), response-stability-index (RSI), embedding cosine drift on embedding routes, safety sentinel hit-rate, and cost per token.

2) Quality gating using eval harness:
   - Delta metrics to compute: exact-match rate, semantic-similarity delta (BERTScore or proprietary similarity), hallucination proxy (unexpected-entity-rate), and RSI.
   - Gate criteria (default):
     * semantic-similarity delta <= 2.5 absolute points on production slices
     * RSI drop <= 0.03
     * Safety sentinel rate not increased by more than 0.1x absolute
     * Latency p95 regression <= 10%

3) Human-in-the-loop review
   - For slices failing any gate, auto-queue for annotator triage with a sample size of 200 examples or until 95% confidence is reached.

Canary rollout and progressive promotion

1) Micro-canary (1–2% traffic) for 2–4 hours
   - Route a small percentage of traffic via routing policy to quantized variant. Monitor SLOs and quality-sentinels.

2) Macro-canary (5–15% traffic) for 24 hours
   - Increase traffic and run full pipeline (eval harness repeat on live samples + human review of failure samples).

3) Gradual promotion (increments of 10–20% every 12–24h)
   - Stop and roll back if: any S1 sentinels are triggered, semantic-similarity delta exceeds threshold, or latency p95 increases beyond escalation threshold.

Rollback criteria and emergency process

- Immediately rollback if any of the following occur: S1 safety sentinel, customer-facing error-rate > 0.5% absolute increase, or unresolvable semantic regressions on a critical slice.
- Triage steps in rollback event:
  1) Capture failing request IDs and attach full traces + model-side logs.
  2) Run targeted eval-harness replay of failing probes across baseline and candidate quant-artifact.
  3) If root cause is quantization, escalate to infra-quant and model-onboarding owners; prepare hot-fix (less aggressive quant profile or mixed-precision fallback).

Regression triage quickplay (for triage teams)

- Initial assessment (first 30 minutes):
  * Confirm whether regression is reproducible on the eval-harness using the failing probe set.
  * Check KV-cache alignment and tokenization parity for the failing requests.

- Bisect matrix:
  * Axis 1: quant_profile (int8, 4bit, mixed)
  * Axis 2: sequence length bucket (short/medium/long)
  * Axis 3: temperature/decoding settings
  Run a batched grid to isolate when the failure appears.

- Rapid mitigation patterns:
  1) Route failing slices to baseline float model via routing policy.
  2) Enable per-route quant-fallback setting (prefer mixed-precision) for affected model key.
  3) Open a regression incident with title prefixed: [REGRESSION][quant] <service-route> and assign to infra-quant.

Operational dashboards and alerts (minimum required)

- Dashboards:
  * Migration overview: traffic split, P50/P95 latency baseline vs quant, cost per token, safety sentinel delta, RSI trend.
  * Slice heatmap: top 20 slices by volume and quality delta.

- Alerts (recommended thresholds):
  * Quality delta alert: semantic-similarity delta > 2.5 points (severity P2)
  * Safety sentinel increase: absolute increase > 0.1% (severity P1)
  * Latency regression: p95 > baseline * 1.10 (severity P2)
  * Unexpected error-rate: > 0.5% absolute (severity P1)

Post-promotion verification and documentation

- Run a 7-day monitored window where weekly aggregated metrics are reviewed by the service owner and evaluation lead.
- Update model manifest and production catalog with final quant_profile, effective date, and observed cost savings.
- Publish a short post-mortem or migration summary including: decision rationale, measured deltas, any rollback incidents, and recommended next steps for future migrations.

Appendix: example commands and snippets

- Eval harness run (example):
  > ./eval-harness run --manifest manifests/service-xyz.json --probes probes/service-xyz/production-probes.json --seed 42 --compare-to baseline-artifact-id

- Example routing policy (YAML excerpt):

  route: /v1/generate/service-xyz
  variants:
    - id: baseline-fp16
      weight: 80
    - id: quant-qp-int8
      weight: 20
  fallback_policy: route-to-baseline-on-sentinel

- Example quick-check JSON for similarity metric: 
  {
    "probe_id": "12345",
    "baseline_embedding_cos": 0.9234,
    "quant_embedding_cos": 0.8952,
    "similarity_delta": -0.0282
  }

Related policies and references

- See the quantization profile library for approved profiles and binary provenance.
- Follow the eval-harness seeding and determinism rules when building comparison runs.
- Use the regression-triage incident template when opening incidents for production regressions.

Notes and future work

- Next iteration: automate quant-profile A/B scoring via the eval-harness and integrate with rollout policy to support automated gradual promotion when deltas remain within a conservative band.
- Investigate more robust embedding-drift alarms that map directly to downstream retrieval quality impact.

title: Production model certification checklist — MCert v1.0
content:
Overview

Purpose: This checklist defines the minimum evaluation, performance, safety, and operational requirements a model must meet before being certified for production serving on Redwood. It bundles artifacts, automated checks, and manual signoffs into a repeatable workflow (MCert). Use this document for new-model onboarding, major-version upgrades, and any model variant that will be used for live traffic.

Scope: applies to open and third-party models selected for Redwood-hosted or Dedicated serving. It covers functional evals, prompt sensitivity, quantization testing, perf benchmarking, observability instrumentation, rollout strategy, and rollback criteria.

Owners and signoff flow

- Model owner: individual or product engineer responsible for the model (create a PR with artifacts).
- Certifying authority: Applied ML team (final technical signoff).
- SRE owner: Eng-SRE (capacity and SLO validation).
- Security reviewer: Security & Compliance (privacy/KMS checks if required).
- Business stakeholder: Product/PoC owner (acceptance for business QA).

Signoff sequence (required): model owner -> applied-ml reviewer -> SRE -> security -> product. The Applied ML reviewer must attach a summary report and link to automated eval dashboards.

Required artifacts (deliverables)

1) Model Card (MD or Confluence link) — includes architecture, tokenizer, license, pretraining data summary, and known limitations.
2) Eval report bundle (ZIP) with:
   - deterministic eval run outputs: exact seed, prompt versions, temperature, and sampling settings used.
   - prompt-suite results: production prompt catalog subset + adversarial subsets.
   - per-prompt metrics: ROUGE/BLEU/ExactMatch where relevant and task-appropriate metrics.
3) Performance benchmark report (CSV + graphs):
   - latency distribution (p50, p95, p99) for sequences: 32, 128, 512, 2048 tokens.
   - throughput (tokens/sec) and max sustained qps for target GPU instance types.
   - memory (GPU RAM) footprint with KV-cache sizing.
4) Quantization profile artifact (if quantized) — settings, expected quality delta, and quant test logs.
5) Observability checklist: tracing spans instrumented, relevant metrics added to model-specific dashboard, log-levels, and error tagging semantics.
6) Safety / guardrail evidence: toxicity scores, hallucination checks, controlled-output examples, and mitigations.
7) Canary rollout plan: target segments, traffic weights, monitoring windows, rollback triggers.
8) Test harness config: eval-harness job spec (YAML) used to reproduce all checks.

Minimum automated checks (must pass)

- Functional correctness: unit tests and deterministic evals pass with no flaky failures in 5 repeated runs.
- Prompt stability: median semantic-drift <= 2% (task-dependent) across 10% perturbation of prompt templates.
- Quality regression: no more than 1.5% absolute drop on primary metric vs baseline (or explicit exception logged).
- Safety threshold: toxicity rate <= 0.5% on in-domain prompts; high-risk categories blocked by filter.
- Latency SLO: p95 inference latency <= 350ms for 128-token requests on the certified instance family.
- Memory safety: max GPU memory < 90% on worst-case sequence workloads.

Quantization-specific tests

- End-to-end quality delta report: compare float32 baseline vs quantized variant on the accepted prompt-suite and adversarial set. Provide per-metric delta and confidence intervals.
- Per-workload perf uplift report: tokens/sec and latency improvements aggregated by sequence length.
- Stability stress test: run continuous inference for 4 hours with KV-cache warmup and validate no memory leaks or progressive drift in output quality.
- If expected quality delta > 2% for any primary metric, require either user-facing fallback or additional guardrails.

Performance benchmarking procedure (executable steps)

1) Provision test infra: use dedicated perf cluster (list in Confluence infra page) matching intended instance type.
2) Warmup: run 1k sample inference requests from production prompt sample to populate KV cache.
3) Run 3 independent benchmark passes for each sequence length (32/128/512/2048), each pass at 80% target concurrency.
4) Capture traces, GPU metrics (utilization, memory, SM clocks), and host metrics.
5) Generate consolidated report; annotate outliers and any system-level throttling.

Example CLI commands

- Trigger eval-harness job (local):
  ./eval-harness/run_local.sh --model-path=artifacts/model-v1 --prompts=prompts/production.json --out=reports/model-v1-evals.json

- Perf runner (k8s job):
  kubectl apply -f perf-jobs/model-v1-run.yaml --namespace=perf

- Quick quant check (internal tooling):
  rquant profile --model artifacts/model-v1 --backend cuda --bits 4 --out=artifacts/quants/model-v1-q4.json

Recommended SLOs and thresholds (suggested defaults)

| Metric | Suggested threshold | Notes |
|-------|--------------------:|------|
| p50 latency (128 tokens) | <= 120 ms | interactive targets |
| p95 latency (128 tokens) | <= 350 ms | hard SLO for hosted tiers |
| throughput (tokens/sec) | >= 40k | depends on instance class |
| memory headroom | >= 10% | to avoid OOM during bursts |
| quality regression vs baseline | <= 1.5% abs | primary task metric |

Rollout plan template (canary-first)

1) Canary 1 (1% traffic) — 30 minutes: auto-checks for errors, latencies, token cost, and eval metrics on sampled responses.
2) Canary 2 (5% traffic) — 2 hours: run longer stability checks including periodic adversarial prompts.
3) Ramp to 25% — 4 hours: monitor SLOs, error budget usage, and user-facing quality signals.
4) Full release to 100% — after 24h stable canary behavior.

Rollback triggers (any of the following triggers immediate rollback):

- Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute compared to baseline in observation window.
- p95 latency degradation > 1.5x relative to baseline.
- Quality regression on primary metric > 2.5% absolute.
- Evidence of new failure modes (security/privacy) discovered in logs.

Operational runbook snippets

- To force a rollback: use the rollout manager CLI:
  rdeploy rollback --model-id model-v1 --to-tag stable

- To collect debug bundle for Applied ML and SRE:
  rcollect bundle --model model-v1 --since 2026-02-14T10:00:00Z --out /tmp/model-v1-debug.tar.gz

- Typical queries to reproduce a user issue (example):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"model-v1","input":"<failing prompt>"}'

Checklist (quick pass/fail list)

- [ ] Model card uploaded and reviewed
- [ ] Eval harness runs reproducible and attached
- [ ] Perf benchmarks meet target SLOs
- [ ] Quantization tests (if applied) completed and within delta limits
- [ ] Observability dashboard created and linked
- [ ] Canary plan documented with monitoring queries
- [ ] Security signoff (if required)
- [ ] Product acceptance for feature behavior
- [ ] Final Applied ML certification signoff

Appendix: Minimal eval-harness YAML example

pipeline: run
- name: load-prompts
  type: prompts
  source: s3://redwood-evals/prompts/production.json
- name: infer
  type: inference
  model: artifacts/model-v1
  sampling: {temperature: 0.0, top_p: 0.95}
- name: scoring
  type: metric
  metrics: [exact_match, bleu]

Notes and guidance

- If a model is borderline on a threshold, attach a mitigation plan (e.g., config to route sensitive prompts to float baseline).
- Keep the eval-harness job specs and quant artifacts immutable in the release bundle to guarantee reproducibility.
- For Dedicated customer deployments, ensure that the regional performance matrix is validated against the customer’s provisioned instance family.

Related documents and links

- Performance benchmarking standards (see eng-serving-runtime/perf-suite page)
- Quantization playbook (per-workload-quant-tuner-and-safety-guidelines-2026)
- Regression triage playbook (model-regression-forensics-playbook-2026)

Contact and escalation

- Applied ML on-call: applied-ml-oncall@redwood.ai
- SRE pager: see team rota in eng-sre/runbook

Change log

- 2026-02-10: v1.0 initial publication (Priya Menon)
- 2026-02-15: v1.1 minor edits and reviewer feedback applied (Evelyn Zhao)

title: Quant Impact Synthesis for Prompt Families
content:
summary:
A practical framework for synthesizing and reporting the impact of quantization across semantically grouped prompt families. Enables model-onboarding, shadow-evals, and regression triage teams to surface prompt-specific failure modes introduced by lower-precision artifacts.

body:
Purpose and scope

This document defines an operational procedure and a scoring artifact - the Quant Stability Index (QSI) - for synthesizing quantization impact across prompt families. It is intended for evaluator engineers, model-onboarding owners, and SRE teams performing shadow and canary rollouts of quantized model artifacts (dedicated or private deployments).

Why prompt families?

- Prompt families are clusters of prompts that share semantic intent, response style, or API route (for example: 'single-turn summarization', 'multi-turn clarification', 'code generation', 'customer-support templates').
- Quantization does not affect all prompt families equally; identifying family-specific regressions focuses triage and mitigations (fallback to float, cache bypassing, or better quant profiles).

High-level workflow

1) Define prompt families and representative shards (seeded examples).
2) Generate baseline golden outputs with a float32 reference model.
3) Run parallel eval-harness against candidate quantized artifacts.
4) Compute family-level metrics and the Quant Stability Index (QSI).
5) Prioritize families with QSI below thresholds for triage and corrective actions.
6) Produce an artifact (CSV + JSON) to attach to the model promotion ticket.

Definitions

- Prompt family: a labeled group of prompts sharing intent/style/route.
- Seed set: 100-2,000 canonical examples per family (stratified by length and few-shot contexts).
- Candidate artifact: a quantized model build being evaluated (e.g., redwood/llama-70b-q5_1).
- Reference: approved float model (e.g., redwood/llama-70b-fp32) used to generate baselines.
- QSI (Quant Stability Index): composite score (0-100) indicating fidelity preservation; higher is better.

Quant Stability Index (QSI) - formula and interpretation

Compute per-family QSI as a weighted composite of primary metrics. Use the following canonical weights (configurable):

- Response Fidelity Score (RFS): 0-100, measures semantic alignment with reference using ensembled comparators (embedding cosine + ROUGE-L + model-proxy edit distance). Weight: 0.6
- Latency Delta Penalty (LDP): normalized 0-100 penalty for relative latency change when quantized artifact uses different kernel paths. Weight: 0.15 (penalty reduces QSI)
- Tokenization/Truncation Failure Rate (TFR): 0-100 penalty for increased truncations or tokenization mismatches. Weight: 0.15
- Determinism/Stability Score (DSS): 0-100, measures sampling variance across seeds/passes (lower variance yields higher DSS). Weight: 0.1

QSI = round(clamp( RFS*0.6 + (100 - LDP)*0.15 + (100 - TFR)*0.15 + DSS*0.1 , 0, 100), 2)

Interpretation guidance:

- QSI >= 92: green - quant artifact acceptable for canary; proceed with standard rollout.
- 85 <= QSI < 92: yellow - acceptable for shadow or limited canary with aggressive monitoring and fallback.
- QSI < 85: red - requires remediation; do not promote to production.

Representative metrics and thresholds (example)

Metric | Measurement | Alert threshold
- RFS (family median) | embedding cosine delta vs reference (0-1) converted to 0-100 | drop > 4 points (i.e., cos delta > 0.04)
- LDP | p50 latency increase (%) | > 15%
- TFR | fraction of responses truncated or token mismatch | > 1.5%
- DSS | coefficient of variation of semantic similarity across 5 seeds | > 8% (lower is better)

Note: These numeric thresholds are starting points. Owners should calibrate per-product SLOs.

Prompt family selection and seed generation

- Start with product-owned route mapping: pull traffic sample t for each API route over 30 days and perform k-means on encoded prompts to suggest families.
- Human-in-the-loop curation: product/PSM annotators validate families and seed examples.
- Stratify seeds by: short vs long context, presence of code blocks, special tokens, and multimodal attributes (if applicable).
- Minimum seed size: 200 examples per family recommended for stable QSI; 100 allowed for low-risk families.

Operational configuration (eval-harness integration)

Use the eval harness job template 'quant-family-synthesis' in eval-mesh. Example YAML config (attach to job):

job_name: quant-family-synthesis
reference_model: redwood/llama-70b-fp32
candidates:
  - redwood/llama-70b-q5_1
  - redwood/llama-70b-q4f
prompt_families: /datasets/prompt-families/v2/manifest.json
seeds_per_family: 300
concurrency: 48
random_seeds: [42, 123, 777, 2026, 31415]
metrics: [embedding_cosine, rouge_l, latency_ms, truncation_flag]
report_artifact: s3://eval-artifacts/quant-synthesis/${JOB_ID}/report.json

Suggested compute targets and runtimes:

- Small runs (100 seeds/family): 2-4 GPU-hours on r-infer-gpu-k80 equivalent; good for quick checks.
- Medium runs (300 seeds/family): 8-24 GPU-hours depending on candidate count and concurrency.
- Large runs (1k seeds/family): schedule during non-peak; use dedicated pools.

Failure modes and triage playbook

1) Low RFS concentrated in specific family
   - Reproduce on a smaller canonical subset.
   - Inspect top-k output diffs and annotate failure types (hallucination, brevity, style shift).
   - Check quant-profile mismatch (e.g., outlier layer collapse) using quant-tuner diagnostics.

2) High latency delta for quant candidate
   - Confirm kernel selection and fallback paths in runtime telemetry (runtime-telemetry/logs).
   - If new kernel chosen, retest with kernel pinning or different batch sizing.

3) Elevated truncation/TFR
   - Re-check tokenizer compatibility and sequence length rounding.
   - Test with 'preserve-prefix' caching disabled to ensure KV artifacts not causing truncation.

4) Non-deterministic variance (low DSS)
   - Increase sampling seeds and test temperature/sampling configuration parity with reference.
   - If variance persists, inspect quant rounding behavior across batches and across GPU types.

Remediation options (ordered by cost/impact)

- Adjust quant profile (increase bits for sensitive layers).
- Use hybrid quant (higher precision for output layers).
- Enable per-route float fallback for affected families (routing policy change).
- Increase cache-preservation or use cache-priming for long-context families.
- Roll back to previous artifact and open a quant-fix ticket.

Reporting artifact and onboarding checklist

Every synthesis run must produce a single ZIP containing:

- report.json (per-family QSI and per-metric breakdown)
- diffs/ (example input, reference output, candidate output for top 20 failures per family)
- seeds_manifest.csv (family, seed_id, length_tokens, tags)
- job-config.yaml (the eval job config used)

Onboarding checklist for model promotion (Gated steps):

1) QSI green for > 90% of families and no red critical families.
2) For yellow families, owner signs off on monitoring + fallback plan.
3) Attach report ZIP to model promotion ticket and tag owners.

CLI snippets and quick commands

- Run local quickcheck (100 seeds):

evalctl run --job quant-family-synthesis --config quickcheck.yaml --target candidate:redwood/llama-70b-q5_1

- Summarize QSI from report.json:

python tools/qsi_summarize.py --report report.json --out summary.csv

Ownership, cadence and SLAs

- Owner: Applied ML - Model Reliability (team: applied-ml/reliability). Primary contact: Aisha Kumar.
- Quarterly review of family manifests and thresholds.
- SLA: synthesis run for a new candidate within 48 hours of artifact availability for high-priority models.

Appendix A - Example QSI output (human-readable excerpt)

Model: redwood/llama-70b-q5_1
Families:
 - summarization_short: QSI=94.2, RFS=95.1, LDP=3.2, TFR=0.2, DSS=96.5
 - longform_assist: QSI=82.4, RFS=78.3, LDP=12.1, TFR=1.8, DSS=85.0
Run id: job-2026-03-10-5b9f
Notes: longform_assist needs hybrid quant for final layers or per-route float fallback.

Appendix B - Common pitfalls and tips

- Do not rely solely on token-level metrics; small semantic shifts often appear only in embedding comparisons or targeted unit tests.
- Validate multi-turn coherence explicitly for families that use KV caching - quantized KV layout changes can surface as coherence regressions.
- Favor reproducible seeds and attach random seeds to the artifact for future bisecting.

Related resources

- quant-profile-synthesis playbook (internal)
- eval-mesh job templates and sample manifests
- model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook (for promotion gate mapping)

If you have questions or need the family clustering helper, ping applied-ml/reliability in Slack or file a request to the eval-harness queue.

title: Coherence-first Quant Tuning Playbook
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines the "Coherence-first Quant Tuning" (CFQT) process for promoting quantized model artifacts into Redwood inference environments (hosted, dedicated, private). CFQT prioritizes end-user coherence and semantic consistency over raw token-level loss metrics. It describes probe generation, automated and human-in-the-loop evaluation gates, telemetry thresholds, rollback criteria, and recommended fallback policies for production rollouts.

Scope:

- Applies to all transformer-based text and chat models targeted for 8k and 32k context deployments.
- Intended for quantized artifacts (4-bit, 6-bit, mixed-precision) and hybrid translator artifacts (int8 activations + quantized weights).
- Integrates with the Eval Harness, Model Onboarding pipelines, and the Runtime’s fallback policies.

Definitions and key metrics:

- Coherence Preservation Index (CPI): composite metric combining Structural Coherence (SC), Topicality Agreement (TA), and Response Fluency (RF). Scaled 0..1 where 1 is identical to FP32 baseline. Target: CPI >= 0.94 for promotion.
- Token Preservation Loss (TPL): normalized token log-prob difference aggregated on a workload stratified by prompt-family. Used for near-term triage; TPL <= 0.08 preferred.
- Response Stability Delta (RSD): percent of responses that change semantic class (classification via anchor-based embedding clustering) relative to reference. Threshold: RSD <= 6%.
- 99th percentile latency (p99-RT): measured at synthetic 95th percentile load for target capacity. For hosted SLO: p99-RT <= 320ms for 8k, <= 410ms for 32k on standard GPU profile.

Why coherence-first?

Quantization can reduce model compute and cost, but some quant schemes disproportionately affect coherence (hallucination, instruction-following). CFQT prioritizes user-facing coherence metrics and ties promotion decisions to explicit coherence thresholds rather than only loss/accuracy. This reduces production regressions and customer-facing quality incidents.

Probe generation and workload fingerprinting:

1) Probe families: generate probes by cross-product of: prompt-domain (support, finance, conversational, coding), shot-pattern (0/1/few), context-length (short/mid/long up to the model limit), and adversarial perturbations (typo, truncation, rephrasing, temperature-driven stochastic seeds).
2) Anchor-based seeding: seed probes using live traffic anonymized fingerprints for the tenant or workload class. Use 1-2K probes for tenant shadow runs; 10-20K for global promotion smoke tests.
3) Stratify probes into slices: high-risk (billing/customer-data), instruction-following, multi-turn memory, functioncall signatures. Each slice has distinct CPI and RSD tolerances.

Evaluation gates and automation:

- Gate A (fast): runs token-level checks (TP L, perplexity delta) and throughput/latency smoke tests. Pass if TPL <= 0.12 AND p99-RT within 125% of baseline. Expected run time: < 20 minutes.
- Gate B (coherence): runs CFQT probe suite, computes CPI and RSD per slice, runs automated behavioral tests for hallucination (synthetic knowledge checks). Pass if CPI >= 0.94 AND RSD <= 6% across priority slices. Expected run time: 2-4 hours.
- Gate C (shadow): deploy to shadow fleet with production traffic mirror for 24–72 hours. Collect regression signals (telemetry below). Manual review required if any slice failure occurs.

Promotion decision matrix (automated summary):

- Green: Gates A+B passed, shadow stability within tolerances, automated roll to 10% canary.
- Amber: Gate A passed, Gate B marginal (CPI 0.90–0.94) — require targeted annotation sample (human) for top 500 anchors; proceed only with manual approval and limited canary (<= 2%).
- Red: Gate A failed OR Gate B failed (CPI < 0.90 or RSD > 10%) — do not promote. Open regression ticket.

Telemetry and production monitoring (real-time hooks):

Instrument the following telemetry with per-model and per-tenant shard tagging:

- CPI rolling window (1h/24h) and 7 day trend. Alert if CPI drops by >0.02 in 24h or absolute CPI below 0.92.
- RSD spike detector: alert on >3% increase in 1h.
- Prompt-family drift detector: uses embedding drift and token distribution shift to surface new prompt families causing degraded CPI. Alert threshold: JS divergence > 0.15 vs baseline.
- Safety regressions: hallucination sentinel firing rate (per 1k responses) — escalate if rate doubles vs baseline.

Fallbacks and graceful degradation:

- Per-tenant policy priority: (1) local cached FP32 artifact if present, (2) compatible higher-precision variant in same model family (e.g., 6-bit fallback), (3) remote-hosted FP32 in another region, (4) configured static response or service-unavailable.
- Automatic fallback trigger: CPI < 0.90 sustained over 5 minutes OR RSD spike > 12% OR safety sentinel high confidence.

Runbook: triage steps on a coherence incident (short path for oncall):

1) Identify scope: query telemetry for model-id, tenant, route, time window.
2) If CPI < 0.92 or RSD > 8%: toggle immediate fallback via routing console to previous stable artifact. Notify oncall and model-owner channel.
3) Collect failing probes: generate top 200 differing responses and run delta-analysis tool (eval-harness delta-report).
4) If root cause appears quant-specific (consistent tokens removed, short-circuited attention): label artifact as "quant-degradation" and run quant-tuning matrix (see Appendix YAML).
5) If unclear: escalate to Applied ML oncall and open regression-triage ticket with initial analysis.

Rollout & promotion checklist (must-complete items):

- Model artifact signed and provenance recorded in artifact registry (artifact id, quant config, commit sha).
- CFQT automated report: CPI, TPL, RSD per-slice, and human annotation sample attached.
- Performance baselines attached: p50/p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec at expected concurrency.
- Security & privacy review completed for probe anchors derived from live traffic (DP scrubbed).
- Owner and approver listed with contact details.

Ownership and responsibilities:

- Applied ML team: probe generation, automated CFQT tooling, annotation coordination.
- Serving Runtime team: deployment orchestration, kernel selection, fallback mechanism implementation.
- SRE/Platform: production telemetry, alerting, incident coordination.
- Product & Customer Success: define tenant-specific tolerance and approve amber promotions.

Example CLI and YAML snippets:

- Run CFQT locally via eval-harness helper:

  # run quick coherence gate
  ./eval_harness/run_cfqt.sh --artifact s3://redwood-artifacts/model-x/quant-6bit/ --probe-suite coherence_small --out report.json

- Quant tuning matrix (example):

  quant_tuning:
    artifact_id: "model-x-quant-6b-6bit-20260112"
    steps:
      - name: "activations-int8-sweep"
        params: "int8_activations: [true,false]"
      - name: "scale-aware-gptq"
        params: "clip_range: [0.01, 0.05, 0.1]"
      - name: "kv-cache-precision"
        params: "kv_precision: [fp16, int8_mixed]"

Appendix: example alert policy (pseudocode)

- Alert: CFQT_CPI_Degradation
  condition: CPI(last_1h) - CPI(prev_24h) <= -0.02 OR CPI(last_1h) <= 0.92
  severity: P1
  paging: Applied ML oncall -> Serving Runtime -> SRE
  auto_action: enable_fallback(artifact.previous_stable)

Risk and limitations:

- CPI is an ensemble of heuristics; uncommon prompt families may produce false positives and require human review.
- Shadow runs are necessary for long-tail behavior but expensive for large tenant fleets. Budget these runs into release plans.

Related references:

- See Eval Harness: quantized-artifact-eval-gate-and-rollout document for gate automation wiring.
- See Model Onboarding: inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook for promotion criteria mapping.

Contact and escalation path:

- Primary owner: Maya Chen (applied-ml@redwood.ai).
- Secondary: Diego Alvarez (serving-runtime@redwood.ai).
- Oncall rota: applied-ml-oncall in PagerDuty and #applied-ml-oncall Slack channel.

Change log:

- 2025-08-20 initial draft by Maya Chen.
- 2025-12-10 added RSD and CPI thresholds after pilot.
- 2026-02-18 clarified fallback priority and added alert policy example.

End of document.

title: Adaptive Shadow Validation for Cold-Start and Telemetry-driven Promotion
content:
summary:
A practical playbook and validation contract for onboarding new model variants using adaptive shadow traffic to surface cold-start behaviors and telemetry-driven gating rules prior to canary or full promotion.

background:
Shadow deployments are a core part of Redwood's model onboarding: they let us validate quality and infrastructure behavior without impacting production responses. Standard shadow runs often miss cold-start spike modes (first request to warmed kernels, kv-cache warmup) and do not adapt telemetry thresholds based on observed variance. This document specifies an adaptive shadow validation framework designed to detect cold-start failure modes, capture fine-grained telemetry, and produce deterministic promotion decisions.

motivation:
Two recurring issues were observed in previous onboardings: (1) models that passed synthetic offline tests but regressed under realistic cold-start traffic patterns, and (2) static pass/fail thresholds that either blocked safe releases or allowed regressions when workload variance increased. The adaptive approach reduces false positives and false negatives by using staged sample budgets, variance-aware thresholds, and a telemetry-driven decision contract.

scope:
Applies to hosted and dedicated model promotions where the model affects real-time text generation or chat endpoints. This playbook is intended for ML engineers, serving runtime owners, SREs, and release managers. Not intended for embeddings-only shadowing (use embedding-specific onboarding checklist instead).

when_to_use:
Use this playbook when: 1) adding a new model family or quantization profile, 2) changing kernel/backing runtime (CUDA->ROCm, new tensor cores), 3) onboarding models into Dedicated or Private with customer workload mirroring, or 4) promoting models that will handle low-latency interactive traffic.

prerequisites:
- Baseline production telemetry (last 7 days) exported to the eval harness.
- A reproducible shadow routing configuration (mesh fork or 1% mirror is acceptable).
- An eval keypair and shadow dataset representing cold-start heavy queries (see sample generator below).
- Owners assigned: ML lead, Runtime owner, Release manager, SRE contact.

telemetry_required:
Collect the following telemetry at 1s granularity during shadow runs:
- request_id, timestamp, route, model_variant, region, backend_node
- latency p50/p90/p95/p99 (in ms)
- first-token-latency (ms)
- kv_cache_hit_rate (per-session)
- token_throughput (tokens/sec)
- GPU_utilization and memory_usage (per-host)
- error_rate (4xx/5xx) and internal_inference_errors
- output_quality metrics: sample-wise BLEU/ROUGE for structured tasks, semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) or response-stability-index for chat
- feature_flags active
- seed/temperature and prompt-shard id

validation_criteria:
Adaptive validation uses a three-stage contract:
1) Warmup sanity (10-100 warmed sessions): verify no internal_inference_errors and kv_cache_hit_rate >= baseline * 0.85.
2) Cold-start probe (50-500 cold sessions): measure first-token-latency delta vs production baseline; require median delta <= 1.5x and p95 delta <= 2.0x unless compensated by model-quality improvements documented.
3) Stability window (synthetic mirror of 24h sample or 100K tokens): ensure rolling p95 latency within cost-latency budget and quality regressions <= 1% absolute on prioritized slices.
Thresholds are variance-aware: if sample variance > historical variance * 1.5, expand the confidence interval and require an additional verification stage before blocking promotion.

step_by_step_procedure:
1) Create a shadow config: define routing percentage, mirror mode (fork vs linear replay), and cold-session fraction. Example YAML in 'sample_config'.
2) Generate shadow dataset: include a 25% cold-session fraction by inserting new session ids that have empty kv cache. Use the provided generator script.
3) Start a 2-hour warmup run with a 1% mirror for infrastructure checks. Collect telemetry and verify warmup sanity.
4) Run the cold-start probe for N=200 cold sessions distributed across regions and instance types. Evaluate first-token-latency deltas and kv cache behavior.
5) If probe passes, run the 24h stability window (or equivalent token-budget run) with full telemetry; compute rolling metrics and slice-aware quality checks.
6) Apply adaptive threshold rules: if variance triggers expansion, schedule a targeted rerun on impacted slices (e.g., long-context, high-temperature generations).
7) Produce a validation report (automated notebook) including per-slice histograms, variance tests (Levene), and a promotion recommendation: promote / require follow-up / block.
8) Sign-off: ML lead and Runtime owner must sign the report before canary promotion.


sample_config:
# shadow-run-config.yaml
mirror_mode: fork
routing_percentage: 1
cold_session_fraction: 0.25
budget_tokens: 100000
regions: [us-west-2, eu-west-1]
instance_selector: {gpu_family: a100, min_mem_gb: 40}
telemetry_level: full
quality_checks:
  - name: semantic-similarity
    threshold: 0.92
    slices: [billing-qa, account-reset, long-context]
  - name: response-stability-index
    threshold: 0.98

sample_cli_and_code_snippets:
# Start a shadow mirror (CLI)
redwood infra shadow start --config shadow-run-config.yaml --note "adaptive-shadow-jan2026"

# Example Python snippet to compute first-token-latency delta
import pandas as pd
prod = pd.read_parquet('prod_baseline.parquet')
shadow = pd.read_parquet('shadow_run.parquet')
merged = shadow.merge(prod, on=['route','slice'], suffixes=("_shadow","_prod"))
merged['first_token_delta'] = (merged['first_token_latency_shadow'] - merged['first_token_latency_prod']) / merged['first_token_latency_prod']
summary = merged.groupby('slice')['first_token_delta'].agg(['median','quantile'])
print(summary)

analysis_and_reporting:
Reports must include: 1) per-slice metric tables (median, p95, variance), 2) histograms for first-token-latency comparing shadow vs prod, 3) kv-cache warmup curves (kv_cache_hit_rate over session steps), 4) per-node GPU telemetry overlay, and 5) a short executive summary with recommendation. Upload the report to the eval dashboard and link the job id in the release ticket.

metrics_and_slos:
Primary SLOs for promotion decision:
- first-token-latency median delta <= 1.5x and p95 delta <= 2.0x
- rolling latency p95 must remain within absolute budget: p95 <= 350ms for interactive routes, <= 800ms for long-batch routes
- kv_cache_hit_rate drop <= 15% relative to baseline
- production-critical slice quality regressions <= 1% absolute
- infra error_rate <= 0.01%
If any primary SLO is violated, promotion is blocked unless compensated and documented in the report.

variance_and_escalation_policy:
If sample variance for any primary metric exceeds historical variance * 1.5, the harness will: 1) auto-extend the run by 2x sample budget, 2) trigger a rerun on the impacted slices with focused sampling, and 3) notify owners via PagerDuty (runtime-owner escalation). If after reruns the metric remains outside thresholds, create a regression-triage ticket and schedule a 2-day investigation window before any manual override.

rollback_criteria_and_postmortem:
If promoted model causes production regressions identified in the first 24 hours (p95 latency increase > 10% absolute or slice-quality regression > 2% absolute), immediately activate rollback: set routing to previous model variant and open an incident with 'model-promotion-regression' tag. Postmortem must include shadow logs, probe artifacts, and a root-cause analysis within 7 days.

owners_and_contacts:
ML lead: Marcus Bell (ml@redwood.ai)
Runtime owner: Elena Park (runtime@redwood.ai)
SRE oncall: see oncall rota (link)
Release manager: Jorge Ramirez (releases@redwood.ai)

sample_dataset_generator:
A small generator is provided to synthesize cold sessions and long-tail prompts. Usage:
python tools/generate_shadow_dataset.py --size 20000 --cold_fraction 0.25 --slices 'billing-qa,long-context,signup'
Generator creates: shadow_prompts.jsonl, session_ids.csv, slice_metadata.csv

references:
Links and artifacts to attach to the promotion ticket: 1) shadow job id, 2) eval notebook URL, 3) sample_config YAML, 4) telemetry parquet exports, 5) sign-off checklist (signed PDFs)

next_steps:
Integrate the adaptive shadow validation contract into the automated promotion pipeline: - implement automatic variance checks in the eval harness, - add a UI widget in the eval dashboard that surfaces cold-start histograms, - schedule a roadshow with platform teams to adopt the contract for Dedicated onboarding.

notes:
This playbook intentionally biases toward conservative promotion decisions for low-latency interactive routes. Teams may adjust thresholds for batch-only workloads after coordinating with Runtime owners.

title: Holistic Acceptance Matrix for Model Promotion
content:
summary:
This page defines a single, reproducible acceptance matrix and workflow used by Redwood Inference to decide whether a candidate model (or model variant) may be promoted to staging and production. The matrix covers automated evals, human checks, performance/latency budgets, quantization acceptance, and regression-triage triggers. It is intended to reduce ambiguity in promotions and standardize cross-team expectations.

purpose:
Provide a deterministic set of checks, metrics, and decision rules for onboarding new model versions across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. The matrix balances quality, cost, and operational safety and ties results to rollout constraints and rollback criteria.

scope:
Applies to all model artifacts that will be served through Redwood API, Dedicated pools, or Private deployments. Includes open-source base models and any internal fine-tuned variants. Excludes short-lived experimental snapshots that are explicitly labeled "experimental" and not intended for promotion.

acceptance_matrix_overview:
The acceptance matrix groups checks into five axes: 1) Functional quality (task-specific metrics & human eval), 2) Safety and policy (toxicity, PII leakage, hallucination), 3) Performance (latency, memory, KV-cache behavior), 4) Cost/efficiency (tokens-per-second, batch throughput, quantized accuracy delta), and 5) Reliability/regression stability (rolling-average error, tail latency, CI integration). A candidate must pass all mandatory gates and must not have non-triaged showstopper regressions.

metrics_and_thresholds:
Key automated metrics and baseline thresholds (adapt per workload):

- Semantic similarity (embedding cosine) on canonical prompts: baseline >= 0.88 (relative to current prod mean).
- Human-eval pass rate (task-specific) on holdout prompt set: >= 85% agreed pass.
- Hallucination / factuality failure rate: <= 3% on factual-check set.
- Toxicity (model score, internal classifier): <= 1% of responses flagged high-risk; must pass targeted adversarial toxicity subset.
- Response diversity: Distinct-1 >= 0.12 and Distinct-2 >= 0.06 on generative tasks where diversity matters.
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation latency for standard short prompts (<= 128 tokens) must not exceed prod baseline by more than +20% and absolute p95 target <= 150ms for dedicated-tier targets.
- Memory / KV cache footprint: increase <= 10% vs baseline for same sequence lengths.
- Quantization accuracy delta (when proposing quantized variant): metric degradation <= 2% absolute on critical task metrics and latency improvement >= 15% vs float baseline.
- CI regression windows: rolling 7-day error-rate delta <= +2 percentage points vs prod.

Notes: teams can tighten per-customer SLAs (e.g., enterprise-tier latency targets) by adding custom checks into the promotion pipeline.

evaluation_workflow:
1) Pre-flight: generate model card, artifact digest, reproducible evaluation recipe (seeded), and identify canonical prompt groups (functional, adversarial, safety, long-context).
2) Automated batch evals: run eval harness with production-like serving simulator; capture metrics above and produce a structured report.
3) Quantization bench (if applicable): run quantize profile with per-workload verifier and adversarial prompts; produce numeric delta table.
4) Human validation: sample 200 responses across prompt groups; pairwise annotation by two raters and an adjudicator for disagreements.
5) Security & privacy scan: automated PII detectors + manual review for data exposure risks.
6) Stakeholder review: engineering + product + security sign-off meeting if any gate is close to threshold.
7) Staging rollout: deploy to staging routing slice and run canary traffic for 72 hours with synthetic workload injection and real traffic shadowing.
8) Promotion: scheduled canary to production following stepwise ramp (see rollout_policy).

CLI snippets for reproducible evals: 
redwood-eval run --model candidate:v{hash} --recipe eval-recipes/canonical-prompts.yaml --out report.json
redwood-quant-bench --model candidate:v{hash} --profile low-bit --out quant_report.json

onboarding_checklist:
Mandatory items (all must be completed and attached to the promotion ticket):

1. Model card: architecture, training data summary, license, intended use, known limitations.
2. Artifact checksum and provenance (git commit, storage URI).
3. Automated eval report (report.json) with raw metrics + thresholds table.
4. Human validation summary with annotator agreement stats.
5. Quantization report (if proposing quantized variant).
6. Security & PII scan results.
7. Load/perf bench: throughput and latency curves for expected shard sizes.
8. Rollout plan with canary percentages, monitoring dashboards, and rollback criteria.
9. Owner and on-call rotation for the first 72 hours post-promotion.
10. Link to smoke-test scripts and automated post-deploy checks.

Optional but recommended: glossary of prompts used and a one-page summary for non-engineering reviewers.

roles_and_ownership:
- Model Owner: responsible for pre-flight artifacts, addressing triage items, and owning the promotion ticket.
- Eval Owner: runs the eval harness and is responsible for reproducibility and result integrity.
- Quantization Owner: runs quant profiles and verifies accuracy/throughput tradeoffs.
- Security Reviewer: performs PII and policy checks.
- Release Manager: schedules staging and production rollout and verifies that monitoring is in place.
- Oncall/Support: assigned for 72 hours post-promotion for immediate rollback or mitigation.

Primary escalation path: Model Owner -> Eval Owner -> Release Manager -> Head of Platform if cross-cutting issues are unresolved in 4 hours.

rollout_and_monitoring:
Stepwise rollout policy (default):

- Canary 1: 1% traffic for 2 hours; automated smoke checks (error-rate, p50/p95 latency, basic quality probes).
- Canary 2: 5% traffic for 6 hours; expanded quality probes and adversarial prompt injection.
- Canary 3: 25% for 24 hours; monitor rolling metrics and customer-specific tests.
- Full: 100% after 24–72 hours of stable canary windows.

Automated monitors to enable before rollout: latency p95, error rate, model quality regression probe (synthetic prompts), safety classifier alerts, token-cost deltas, and end-to-end customer flows.

Rollback triggers (any of these cause immediate rollback to previous stable variant):
- sustained error-rate increase > 3 percentage points for 30 minutes,
- latency p95 increase > 30% for 30 minutes,
- human-eval quality probe drop > 2 absolute points,
- safety classifier high-risk alert rate spikes > 2x baseline, or
- severe production incidents reported by customers.

failure_modes_and_triage:
Common failure modes and suggested triage actions: 

- Quality regression on a narrow prompt cluster: run per-prompt delta analysis, revert fine-tuning changes for that cluster, and add targeted augmentations.
- Increased hallucination on long-context tasks: check KV-cache alignment, reproduce in serving simulator with extended seq lengths, and compare attention activations to baseline.
- Latency regressions under batching: validate kernel selection and continuous-batching settings; run microbenchmarks with identical request distributions.
- Quantization-induced semantic drift: compare attention similarity, run per-layer sensitivity, and consider mixed-precision fallback for critical layers.
- Safety classifier false negatives: expand adversarial safety prompt set, re-evaluate classifier threshold, and escalate to Security Reviewer for annotation refresh.

Triage process: create a regression ticket, tag with affected metric and prompt IDs, assign to Model Owner and Eval Owner, run targeted replayed evaluations, and decide patch vs rollback within 24 hours for production incidents.

references_and_tools:
- Eval harness repo: internal link (eval-harness).
- Prompt catalog: applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/production-prompt-catalog-and-stress-bench-2025.
- Quantization profiles: applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/per-workload-quant-tuner-and-safety-guidelines-2026.
- Regression triage playbook: applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/model-regression-forensics-playbook-2026.
- Monitoring dashboards: link to 'model-promotion' Grafana board.

Tooling notes: prefer reproducible Docker images (eval:v2026-01) for running automated checks, and store evaluation outputs in the canonical report bucket (s3://redwood-eval-reports/).

appendix_examples_and_tables:
Example acceptance checklist table (CSV-style):

item, gate, metric, threshold, status
model-card, mandatory, present, yes, PASS
automated-sim-eval, mandatory, semantic-sim >= 0.88, 0.892, PASS
human-eval, mandatory, pass-rate >= 0.85, 0.86, PASS
quantized-delta, conditional, accuracy-delta <= 0.02, 0.015, PASS
latency-p95, mandatory, <= baseline*1.2, baseline*1.05, PASS
safety-toxic, mandatory, flagged <= 0.01, 0.008, PASS

Use this table as a quick copy-paste into promotion tickets to show gating results at a glance.

next_steps_and_improvements:
We will iterate on thresholds and probe sets quarterly. Action items: expand long-context factual checks, standardize diversity metrics for creative tasks, and integrate cost-aware routing tests into the gating system. Please file feedback against this page or open a ticket labeled 'model-onboarding-matrix-feedback'.

title: Onboarding probe anchoring & rollout scenario library
content:
Summary
This document is a practical library of probe anchoring patterns and rollout scenarios to use during model onboarding and promotion. It focuses on how to attach (anchor) probes to service-level slices, how to interpret multi-signal telemetry during staged rollouts, and prescriptive rollback/mitigation playbooks. The goal is to standardize onboarding behaviors for mixed-latency, quantized, and cache-sensitive models so decisions across teams are repeatable and auditable.

Scope
- Applies to model onboarding for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Covers probes used by the eval harness, shadow load, and canary traffic.
- Includes guidance for quantization-aware probes and KV-cache warmup probes.
- Does not replace service-specific SLO documents; it complements them by specifying probe-to-SLO anchoring.

Why anchoring matters
Anchoring ties probe results to an explicit acceptance decision. Without anchoring, teams frequently mismatch probe signals (e.g., token-level coherence vs. p95 latency). Anchoring rules ensure we enforce the correct contract for: correctness (quality), latency, token-cost, and stability under quantization and caching.

Key concepts (short definitions)
- Anchor: a binding between a probe (input set + measurement) and a target service slice or SLO.
- Probe family: a curated set of probes meant to exercise a single class of failure (e.g., long-context coherence probes).
- Anchor contract: the telemetry signals, thresholds and aggregation method used to accept/rollback.
- Warmup probe: a probe designed to populate KV cache and prime model kernels for stable performance.

Scenario catalog (selection)
1) Latency-sensitive canary (API-to-user-facing route)
- Anchor: route=predictive-text, SLO=p95_latency<=300ms
- Probe family: short prompt micro-bursts, payloads sized to real traffic (avg token <= 20)
- Signals: p95 latency, p99 latency, error rate, streaming-backpressure events
- Acceptance criteria (example): p95 <= 300ms AND error_rate < 0.5% over 10k requests; if p99 > 600ms trigger mitigation.

2) Coherence-first shadow rollout (background evaluators)
- Anchor: service_slice=document-summarization, SLO=semantic-fidelity-delta<=0.03 (vs baseline)
- Probe family: long-context summary probes, semantic-similarity scoring (embedding cosine + human anchoring), stochastic seeds (n=5)
- Signals: fidelity_delta (mean), coherence-stability-index (95% CI), annotator disagreement rate
- Acceptance criteria: fidelity_delta <= 0.03 AND annotator_disagreement <= 12% over sample of 2k probes.

3) Quantization-focused rollout (mixed precision)
- Anchor: quant_profile=q8_2, SLO=per-token-coherence-resilience>=0.98
- Probe family: adversarial priming + perturbation noise sweep
- Signals: coherence-regression-rate, token-level entropy shift, memory-alloc-failures on 2 GPU types
- Acceptance criteria: coherence-regression-rate < 2% and no memory alloc failures in 1k-run smoke test.

4) KV-cache warmup + cold-start guard
- Anchor: tenant_tier=dedicated, SLO=cold-start-p95 <= 500ms after 30s idle
- Probe family: burst of representative multi-turn sessions to populate KV cache (session length distribution modeled after production)
- Signals: cold-start_p95, incremental latency per call, cache-hit-rate, trailing-token-overhead
- Acceptance criteria: cache_hit_rate >= 85% after warmup load AND cold-start_p95 <= 500ms.

Decision matrix (signals -> action)
Use the table below during canaries. Aggregate signals over the canary window. This is a compact decision grid — treat as legally binding for promotions when using the standard onboarding pipeline.
| Signal (window) | Green | Yellow | Red | Action |
|-----------------|-------|--------|-----|--------|
| p95 latency (30m) | <=300ms | 300-450ms | >450ms | Continue / Hold / Rollback to previous model |
| fidelity_delta (2k probes) | <=0.03 | 0.03-0.06 | >0.06 | Promote / Investigate / Rollback |
| error rate (30m) | <=0.5% | 0.5-1.5% | >1.5% | Continue / Hold & throttling / Rollback & throttle traffic |
| coherence-regression-rate (sample) | <2% | 2-5% | >5% | Promote-small / Annotation repair required / Rollback + freeze rollout |

Anchoring pattern templates
- SLO-anchor template (short):
  - anchor_id: <service>-<slice>-<probe_family>
  - primary_metrics: [metric1, metric2, ...]
  - aggregation: rolling_mean/median/p95 over <window>
  - decision_thresholds: {green: X, yellow: Y, red: Z}
  - telemetry_sources: [prod-metrics, eval-harness, shadow-trace]

- Probe-job spec (example YAML snippet):
  ```yaml
  probe_job:
    name: kv-warmup-primer-v1
    anchor: inference-service/document-summarization-kv-warmup
    schedule: one-off
    parallelism: 40
    sample_bucket: prod-replay/tenant-priority-1
    run_timeout: 120s
    metrics_emit: [latency_ms,p99_latency,cache_hits,error_rate]
    artifact_retention: 90d
  ```

Telemetry & signal handling (best practices)
- Prefer relative deltas over absolute thresholds for quality metrics ("fidelity_delta vs baseline"), except for latency where absolute thresholds better reflect UX.
- Always declare primary and fallback telemetry sources. Example: primary=prod-metrics, fallback=shadow-mesh, tertiary=eval-harness samples.
- Use bootstrap sampling (n>=5 seeds) for non-deterministic probes and report mean+CI.
- Annotator priming: for any semantic scoring probe, include a mandatory human-anchoring step for the first 500 failing probes.

Rollout playbook (step-by-step)
1) Preflight (offline checks)
   - Run the quant and unit-fidelity checks locally (min 1k synthetic seeds).
   - Verify model artifact signature and quant-profile metadata (quant_profile field present).
   - Create anchor contract and publish it to the onboarding tracker.
2) Shadow stage (no user traffic)
   - Launch 24h shadow run against 1% of production traffic split to avoid tenant skew.
   - Run warmup probes within first 10 minutes to populate caches.
   - Evaluate telemetry against anchor contract: if any Red-level signal fires, stop shadow and open a regression ticket.
3) Micro-canary (internal traffic)
   - Serve 0.5% traffic routed from internal test accounts.
   - Run full probe family at 5x rate to accelerate signal collection.
   - Hold for at least 2 business hours or until 10k probe samples are collected.
4) Gradual ramp (progressive percentages)
   - Ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%, waiting 30-60 minutes at each step.
   - At each step, evaluate anchor contract and run warmup probes if cache-sensitive.
5) Post-promote monitoring
   - For 72 hours after 100% promote, run nightly targeted probes focused on high-risk slices (long context, high-cost tenants).

Rollback & mitigation cookbook (quick actions)
- If Red fidelity_delta: immediate rollback to previous pinned model, issue a regression alert with probe artifacts and top-50 failing inputs.
- If latency regression but quality OK: throttle non-critical routes, enable burst-only routing to dedicated capacity, and roll forward a kernel-optimized variant if available.
- If cache instability (cache_hit_rate drop >15%): temporarily increase cache warmup rate and allocate short-lived dedicated warmup pods.
- If quant-induced memory allocation errors: revert to a lower quant profile for the affected fleet and schedule quant re-tuning.

Playbook for regression triage (when anchor fires Yellow/Red)
1) Gather artifacts: probe inputs, model version, quant_profile, kernel selection logs, and a trace for the slowest 5 requests.
2) Run local micro-replay with identical seed(s) and environment to reproduce.
3) Run bisect on model versions / quant variants if shadow cohort exists.
4) If root cause is prompt-sensitive, tag probes as "prompt-failure" and escalate to prompt engineering with top-20 failing prompts.
5) If root cause is infra (GPU OOM, slow kernel), assign to runtime team, provide kernel profile and top traces.

Ownership, tagging, and auditability
- Every anchor contract must include: owner (pager/team), primary contact email, and a rollout changelog.
- Tag probe jobs with: anchor_id, model_version, quant_profile, and commit_sha.
- Retain probe artifacts for 90 days by default and 365 days for enterprise-sensitive tenants.

FAQ
Q: How many probes are enough in a canary?
A: Target at least 10k probe executions for latency-sensitive routes and 2k probe executions for semantic/coherence probes. For low-volume tenants, synthesize extra probes using the probe fabricator.

Q: Can we promote if one metric is Yellow but others are Green?
A: Yes, with explicit mitigations and a documented hold period. The anchor contract must include allowed Yellow actions (example: limited-rate promote + 24h close monitoring).

Appendix A — Troubleshooting examples
- Example: p99 spikes during micro-canary caused by kernel fallback. Action: collect kernel selection logs, pin older kernel, and rerun micro-canary.
- Example: quant_residual coherence drift: run quant-shadow with wider temperature and multiple seeds, then re-run targeted annotator jobs.

Appendix B — Useful CLI snippets
- Trigger a one-off warmup probe job:
  $ ri probe run --job kv-warmup-primer-v1 --anchor inference-service/document-summarization-kv-warmup --parallel 40 --timeout 120s
- Fetch last 24h anchor telemetry:
  $ ri metrics query --anchor inference-service/document-summarization-kv-warmup --window 24h --agg p95,mean,error_rate

Related reading
- See "Onboarding fidelity SLA and noise budget manifest" for negotiation of fidelity_delta budgets.
- Refer to the quantization manifest for allowed quant profiles and rollback thresholds.

Contact
Owner: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
Runbook pager: #ml-onboarding-oncall

Change log
- 2026-01-15: Created initial scenario library and anchoring templates.
- 2026-03-02: Added KV-cache warmup guidance and quant rollback cookbook.

title: Privacy-First Shadow-Eval and Differential Privacy Certification
content:
Overview

This playbook defines Redwood's privacy-first shadow-evaluation pattern and the minimal differential privacy (DP) certification steps required before promoting models to production. It is intended for ML engineers, privacy reviewers, and SREs involved in model onboarding for customer-facing inference routes. The goal is to enable realistic shadow traffic evaluation while preventing leakage of sensitive inputs and ensuring a measurable DP guarantee for telemetry and analytic outputs.

Why this exists

- Shadowing production traffic is essential to validate latency, quality, and stability with real workloads.
- Uncontrolled shadowing can leak customer data into training logs, eval artifacts, or third-party tooling.
- This document prescribes automated controls, measurement targets, and an approval workflow to balance fidelity and privacy.

Scope and assumptions

- Applies to models intended for hosted API or Dedicated deployments that will be served on customer data or with customer-provided prompts.
- Not a substitute for legal review in regulated industries; use this playbook alongside legal/compliance requirements.
- Assumes eval harness integration with Redwood's eval scheduler and the observability stack (Prometheus, Tempo, and the Redwood Console).

Owners and roles

- Model Owner: single-point ML lead responsible for implementing the shadow harness and remediation.
- Privacy Reviewer: member of Security & Compliance assigned to DP sign-off.
- SRE/Infra Owner: responsible for capacity isolation and routing policies in Dedicated/VPC environments.
- Release Manager: approves promotion to canary/production after gates pass.

High-level workflow (summary)

1) Configure privacy gating for shadow route.
2) Run isolated shadow-eval with redaction + DP-enabled telemetry collection for N=1M requests or 14 days (whichever comes first).
3) Run automatic quality and privacy checks in the eval harness.
4) Submit DP certification bundle for Privacy Reviewer sign-off.
5) Proceed to canary with traffic ramp and monitoring.

Detailed configuration

Shadow route and isolation

- Create a shadow route in the Redwood routing layer named: shadow/<model-id>/<hash>-priv.
- Route policy: route all production traffic copies to shadow route with no external outputs. Ensure the shadow route is tagged isolated=true and billing=shadow-eval.
- Capacity limits: cap concurrency to 20% of equivalent production footprint to avoid amplification. SRE must enforce soft and hard concurrency quotas via the autoscaler.

Redaction rules (must be applied before any storage or 3rd-party export)

- Apply input redaction rules in the data plane (examples below). Redaction must be deterministic and reversible only by the owning customer if explicit consent exists.
- Minimal required redactions: email addresses, credit-card-like numeric sequences (14+ digits), SSNs, personal names when flagged by NER with >95% confidence for PII.

Example redaction config (YAML snippet):

```
redaction_rules:
  - pattern: "[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}"
    action: mask
    mask_with: "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"
  - name_entity_types: [PERSON, SSN, PAYMENT_CARD]
    action: mask
    confidence_threshold: 0.95
  - pattern: "\\b\\d{14,}\\b"
    action: hash
    hash_salt: "env:SHADOW_EVAL_SALT"
```

Differential privacy telemetry policy

- All telemetry derived from shadow traffic (metrics, embeddings, gradients, token-logs) MUST be collected under a DP mechanism prior to being persisted or exported.
- Target DP parameters: epsilon <= 2.0 and delta <= 1e-6 for aggregate telemetry over the evaluation window for small-to-medium customers. Higher-risk customers (regulated) require epsilon <= 1.0.
- Use Laplace mechanism for numeric counters and Gaussian mechanism for vector telemetry (embeddings) with pre-bounded sensitivity.

DP config example (JSON for eval harness):

```
{
  "dp": {
    "mechanism": "gaussian",
    "epsilon": 1.5,
    "delta": 1e-6,
    "sensitivity": 1.0,
    "clipping_norm": 8.0
  }
}
```

Notes on embeddings and similarity telemetry

- Before computing or storing embeddings, normalize and clip input lengths to a configurable max_tokens (default 512) and apply L2 clipping to bound sensitivity.
- No raw embeddings or token-level traces are allowed to leave the short-lived in-process cache unless passed through the DP exporter.

Eval harness integration and test matrix

- The standard eval harness job must run these checks during shadow:
  - Quality: top-1 ROUGE / BLEU / perplexity / task-specific score (as applicable).
  - Latency: p50/p95/p99 tail latencies under shadow concurrency; target p95 <= production p95 * 1.2.
  - Resource: GPU memory/power and KV-cache utilization (percentiles logged).
  - Privacy: DP noise levels and pipelined redaction audit results.

- Required artifact outputs from a shadow-eval run (must be attached to the DP bundle):
  - compressed_evaluations.json.gz (DP-filtered metrics only)
  - redaction_audit.log (summary of matches and actions)
  - dp_config.json (clear statement of epsilon/delta/sensitivity)
  - harness-run-metadata.yaml (job id, start/end, route name, owner)

Gates and acceptance criteria

- Quality gate: no regression > 5% absolute on service-critical metrics compared to baseline model (baseline defined in the model's onboarding issue).
- Latency gate: p95 <= baseline p95 * 1.2 and p99 <= baseline p99 * 1.5.
- Privacy gate: DP parameters meet target epsilon/delta AND redaction audit shows >= 99.9% coverage of configured PII patterns on sampled dataset.

- If any gate fails, follow the Regression and Remediation steps below.

Regression and remediation

1) Owner triages failing tests and classifies as: false positive (audit tuning), implementation bug (redaction or DP exporter), or model-induced leakage (model outputs PII).
2) For implementation bugs: patch and re-run shadow-eval within 48 hours.
3) For model-induced leakage: rollback submissions of any artifacts, open a privacy incident, and require a model retraining or prompt-filter patch. Do not progress to canary until Privacy Reviewer approves mitigation.

Promotion and canary steps

1) After passing shadow-eval and DP certification, create a canary route with 0.1% traffic. Canary must have the same privacy gating stack active and produce the same DP telemetry.
2) Monitor the canary for 72 hours or 100k requests (whichever is later) against the same gates.
3) Use automated rollback if privacy gate or quality gates violate thresholds. The rollback automation is controlled by the Release Manager in the Redwood Console.

Audit trails and evidence bundle

- The DP certification bundle to be archived in the model's onboarding folder must contain: dp_config.json, redaction_audit.log, compressed_evaluations.json.gz, harness-run-metadata.yaml, reviewer_signoff.md.
- Retention: evidence bundles for restricted-level models are retained for 7 years; for internal-only models retention is 2 years.

Operational concerns and SLO interactions

- Shadow traffic must not affect production SLOs. The SRE team enforces quotas and billing isolation.
- Cost: use sampling to limit shadow volume for high-volume customers; sampling rate must be included in harness-run-metadata.yaml.

Testing checklist for a new model (quick reference)

- [ ] Shadow route created and isolated (route tag: isolated=true)
