- [ ] Redaction rules deployed and unit-tested (include regex and NER tests)
- [ ] DP config set and simulator run (verify epsilon/delta via approx estimator)
- [ ] Eval harness job completed and artifacts uploaded
- [ ] Privacy Reviewer signoff obtained and recorded
- [ ] Canary launched with privacy gating and automated rollback enabled

Appendices

A. DP parameter selection guidance

- Small consumer workloads: epsilon <= 2.0 is acceptable for telemetry aggregates if delta <= 1e-6.
- High-risk/regulatory: aim for epsilon <= 1.0; consult Security & Compliance for formal differential privacy proofs.

B. Example commands

Run eval harness (CLI):

```
redwood-eval run \
  --job-name=shadow-2026-privacy-test \
  --route=shadow/mdl-1234-priv \
  --dp-config=dp_config.json \
  --redaction-config=redact.yaml \
  --out=artifacts/shadow-2026.tar.gz
```

Validate DP parameters locally (python):

```
from dp_utils import estimate_epsilon
print(estimate_epsilon(noise=1.2, sensitivity=1.0, num_records=500000))
```

C. Related pages

- Link: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/serving-simulation-eval-harness-2026 (serving-simulation details)
- Link: /applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails/runtime-guardrails-and-metric-enforcement-spec-2024 (metric enforcement)
- Link: /security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/dp-proofs-and-templates-2025 (DP legal templates)

Document history

- 2025-11-03: Draft authored by Anika Patel.
- 2025-12-10: Incorporated SRE capacity limits and DP parameter defaults (review by Jonah Ruiz).
- 2026-01-12: Finalized redaction audit format and retention policy; Privacy Reviewer signoff requirements added.

title: Operator preflight: telemetry, security, and runtime prerequisites
content:
Summary

This page is an operator-facing preflight checklist and acceptance template for Redwood Private (VPC / on‑prem) deployments that focuses on three areas often missed during handoffs: telemetry sampling & retention, security (KMS/HSM and image provenance), and runtime / hardware prerequisites. Use this doc before a customer handoff, pre-install dry runs, or an upgrade window to ensure the deployment will meet SLOs, compliance evidence requirements, and day‑2 observability needs.

Scope

- Applies to all Private deployments (VPC and on‑prem) delivered by the Field Engineering and Private Deployments teams.
- Targets initial commissioning and major upgrades (model swap, runtime upgrade, control plane migration).
- Excludes tenant application-level instrumentation (customer responsibility), but includes our agent/collector and runtime telemetry contracts.

Owners and Contacts

- Document owner: eng-private-deployments (Operational Readiness)
- Primary contact: Asha Menon (Field Engineering) — asha.menon@redwood.ai
- Escalation path: Private Deployments Pager -> eng-sre oncall -> Security oncall

Acceptance Criteria (pre-install)

A deployment is considered ready to go live only when all core items below are checked and evidence artifacts are attached to the ticket: configuration export, sample telemetry traces, KMS policy ARN sample, and a signed image provenance manifest. The ticket must include:

1) Telemetry sample file (1 hour synthetic traffic, gzipped JSON or ndjson).
2) KMS / HSM integration verification (kms-test.log).
3) Hardware inventory (serials + firmware versions).
4) Runtime smoke test output (latency, throughput, kv-cache warmup).

Preflight checklist (detailed)

1) Hardware and runtime environment
- GPU type and count: validated against customer capacity workbook (e.g., 8x A100-80GB per tenant for r1 workload).
- Firmware and BIOS: all NICs and BMCs running firmware >= vendor-min for TLS offload and SR-IOV. Document versions in hw-inventory.csv.
- Host OS and kernel: RHEL 8.6+ or Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with kernel >= 5.15. Ensure required modules (nv_peer_mem, rdma) are present if using RoCE.
- Local storage: runtime ephemeral storage >= 500GB for model swap + 2x expected artifact size for safe staging.
- Network MTU: confirm jumbo frames (9000) on data plane where keras/rocksdb replication is used.

2) Network & connectivity
- Control plane egress: allowlist our control plane IPs and TLS fingerprint.
- Model artifact registry access: outbound HTTPS to registry endpoints, TLS1.2+; validate with curl and sha256.
- Tenant subnet design: separate control, data, and operator subnets. Confirm security group rules in vpc-security.yaml.
- Latency requirement: max e2e RTT between operator plane and data plane < 20ms (target), document measured RTTs.

3) Security and key management
- KMS/HSM: confirm key policy supports Envelope Encryption and that our runtime service principal can decrypt keys. Attach kms-test.log demonstrating Encrypt/Decrypt cycle for sample key.
- Key rotation: provide rotation window and automatic rotation script tested in staging.
- Image signing: image manifest must be signed (cosign or equivalent). Provide cosign signature and public key.
- Host attestation: for airgapped sites, TPM attestation report required for first commissioning.
- Secrets injection: confirm secrets delivered via CSI driver or cloud KMS integration; do not persist keys in plain text in runtime config.

4) Telemetry, sampling, and retention (operator contract)
- Telemetry components: runtime-metrics (Prometheus), traces (OpenTelemetry), logs (structured JSON to fluentd/forwarder).
- Sampling strategy: default is adaptive sampling with three tiers:
  - Critical traces (errors, fallback events): 100% sampled
  - High-latency user requests (> 300ms): 20% sampled
  - Background / debug traces: 1% sampled
- Telemetry sampling config (example):
  telemetry:
    traces:
      sampling_strategy: adaptive
      rules:
        - name: critical-errors
          match: "span.attributes.status == 'error'"
          sample_rate: 1.0
        - name: high-latency
          match: "span.duration_ms > 300"
          sample_rate: 0.2
        - name: default-low
          match: "*"
          sample_rate: 0.01
- Retention policy: default local retention for raw traces = 72h, archived nightly to customer S3 for 365 days when requested. Logs: 30 days hot, 365 days cold (compressed). Metrics: 90 days 1s resolution, 3 years aggregated.
- Privacy & PII: ensure PII redaction rules are applied at the collector; attach redaction.yaml demonstrating regex rules and PII tokenization examples.

5) Observability acceptance tests (pre-install smoke)
- Generate synthetic workload of 100 qps for 15 minutes that includes model-compute-heavy and cache-hit patterns. Collect: Prometheus scrape, OTLP traces, sample logs.
- Expected telemetry outputs:
  - Prometheus: key metrics visible (inference_latency_p50/p95/p99, kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu_utilization).
  - Traces: at least 10 error traces, and representative sampled high-latency traces.
  - Logs: structured logs with fields: request_id, tenant_id, model_name, latency_ms, status.
- Attach synthetic_telemetry_YYYYMMDD.ndjson to ticket.

6) IAM and operator permissions
- Operator service principal permissions: minimal set required to perform runtime operations (pull images, start/stop pods, read secrets). Provide example AWS IAM policy snippet or GCP IAM role mapping.
- Access review: confirm RBAC role binding for operator, and an operator-only emergency-control-plane role for rapid rollback.
- Audit logging: ensure operator actions are logged to a tamper-evident audit sink (CloudWatch/Stackdriver or on‑prem ELK).

7) Model artifacts and compatibility
- Model quantization profile: pre-agreed quantization profiles listed in quantization-profiles.csv.
- Artifact schema: model artifact must include manifest.json (fields: name, version, framework, sha256, tokenizer_sha256, prod_compat_matrix).
- Warm-start validation: runtime must be able to warm KV cache within 120s for the working set. Provide warm-start test output.

Upgrade & rollback prerequisites (before any major upgrade)

- Snapshot: take control-plane and runtime state snapshot; label with ticket id and time.
- KV-cache checkpoint: the operator must create a consistent KV checkpoint export.
- Compatibility gate: run offline compatibility matrix tool against the new runtime and attached models; record report.
- Canary plan: minimum 5% of traffic to canary group with automatic rollback criteria: p95 latency increase > 20% sustained for 5 minutes OR error rate increase > 1% absolute.
- Rollback playbook: ensure operator has prepopulated rollback_playbook.md in ticket with commands and evidence locations.

Post-install day‑2 observability and SLOs (operator checks within first 24h)

- SLOs to validate:
  - Availability (serving endpoint): 99.95% per tenant for the first 7 days
  - Latency: p95 < 450ms for small models; p95 < 1s for large models (documented per-tenant).
  - Kv-cache hit rate: > 85% during steady-state.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - inference_latency_p95 > threshold -> paged (P1 if > 30% above target for 10m)
  - error_rate > 0.5% -> investigate (P2)
  - detached_kv_cache_nodes > 0 -> oncall (P1 if > 1 node)
- Evidence collection: attach first 24h dashboard snapshot and a summary.csv with metrics aggregated by hour.

Compliance evidence and artifacts to collect

- KMS policy export (kms-policy.json) and kms-test.log
- Audit sink export for operator actions (audit-export.tar.gz)
- Signed image manifest and cosign public key (image-manifest.json, signature.sig, cosign.pub)
- Telemetry sample archive (synthetic_telemetry_YYYYMMDD.ndjson.gz)
- Hardware inventory and firmware bill of materials (hw-inventory.csv)

Operator runbook snippets (copy into operator ticket)

1) Quick rollback (stateless control-plane config rollback)
- Commands (example):
  - kubectl -n redwood apply -f rollback/control-plane-config-<ticket>.yaml
  - ./operator-tools/evict-heavy-tenants --grace-period 90s --target-tenant <id>
  - ./scripts/restore-kv-checkpoint --checkpoint s3://evidence/<ticket>/kv-checkpoint.tgz
2) KMS rebind test
- Commands (example):
  - aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://sample.cipher --key-id <customer-key-id> --output text > /tmp/decrypted
  - systemctl restart redwood-agent && journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 | grep KMS

Appendix: example telemetry redaction rule (redaction.yaml)

- name: email-redaction
  match: "[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+"
  replace: "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"
- name: credit-card
  match: "\b(?:\d[ -]*?){13,16}\b"
  replace: "[REDACTED_CC]"

Appendix: sample model artifact manifest (manifest.json snippet)

{
  "name": "redwood-open-7b",
  "version": "2027-02-14",
  "framework": "pytorch",
  "sha256": "<hex-sha256>",
  "quantization_profile": "q4a"
}

Notes and best practices

- Treat telemetry as first-class evidence for SLOs and compliance. Keep one synthetic telemetry run for each major upgrade window.
- Use adaptive sampling to keep trace volumes bounded while preserving signal for anomalies.
- Store all evidence artifacts alongside the customer ticket and mark required retention windows in the ticket metadata.

Related pages and further reading

- Deployment commissioning playbook (internal): link to internal playbook for step-by-step operator tasks.
- Field operator training deck: attend the monthly session for hands-on runthroughs.

Revision history

- 2027-03-02 — created by Asha Menon
- 2027-04-11 — added telemetry sampling policy (Ravi Patel)
- 2027-06-12 — hardened KMS checklist and rollback canary criteria (Maya Chen)

title: Priming Lexicon and Quantization Robustness for Multimodal Onboarding
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines a standard priming lexicon and a complementary robustness test matrix for onboarding multimodal models into Redwood's serving fleet, with a focus on quantized artifact resilience, priming stability across modalities, and explicit triage steps when degradation is observed. It is intended for Applied ML engineers, model onboarding owners, and evaluator teams responsible for promotion to shadow/dedicated/private stages.

Background and motivation
-------------------------
- Multimodal models (image+text, audio+text) show different failure modes under lower-precision kernels and KV-cache interactions.
- Current onboarding checklists focus on textual coherence and latency; this doc fills the gap for "priming" (how we initialize context across modalities) and explicit quantization robustness tests.
- Aligns with Redwood's production-first thesis: predictability and measurable regression guards before rolling to hosted/dedicated/private.

Goals
-----
1. Define a canonical priming lexicon (phrases, structure, metadata) used by eval harnesses and shadow traffic to ensure consistent prompting across services.
2. Provide a quant-robustness test matrix covering precision modes (fp16, int8, mixed), KV-cache stress, and multimodal encoding edge cases.
3. Specify telemetry, pass/fail thresholds, and an automated triage flow for regressions.
4. Offer a lightweight config snippet and example CLI commands to run the suite locally and in CI.

Scope
-----
- Applies to multimodal encoder-decoder and decoder-only families onboarded to Redwood's runtime.
- Includes both synthetic priming probes and live-traffic shadow probes.
- Excludes: model training guidance, hardware procurement, and customer-specific prompt engineering.

Definitions
-----------
- Priming lexicon: curated set of tokens/phrases and structure used to initialize the model across modalities (e.g., <IMG_DESC> ... <TEXT_PROMPT>).
- Quantization mode: the execution precision/configuration used (e.g., fp16, int8-static, int8-dynamic, mixed16/8).
- Shadow probe: a probe derived from live traffic but anonymized and reweighted for eval.

Priming lexicon: structure and examples
-------------------------------------
Design principles:
- Deterministic anchors: include a short, deterministic anchor sentence to stabilize generation (e.g., "Context anchor: describe the content concisely.")
- Modality markers: explicit tokens that indicate modality boundaries (TEXT_START, IMAGE_START, AUDIO_START)
- Minimalism: prefer concise anchors to avoid excessive token budgets and reduce KV-cache divergence.
- Diagnostic suffixes: append structured diagnostic fields when running evals: [PRIME_ID=xxx][SEED=42][MODE=shadow]

Canonical priming templates (examples)
- Image caption baseline:
  IMAGE_START
  <IMG_HASH>
  Context anchor: Describe the main subject and visible attributes in one sentence.
  TEXT_START
  Provide a concise caption.

- Multiturn assistant with image:
  TEXT_START
  User: I uploaded an image showing a chart. Provide a summary and 3 action items.
  IMAGE_START
  <IMG_HASH>
  DIAGNOSTIC: [PRIME_ID=chart-summarize][MODE=shadow]

Quantization robustness test matrix (table)
-----------------------------------------
| Test name | Input modality | Quant modes | Stressor | Metric | Pass threshold | Notes |
|-----------|----------------|-------------|----------|--------|----------------|-------|
| Priming-stability-image-anchors | image+text | fp16, int8-static, int8-dyn | image noise, resized to 64-2048 px | caption semantic overlap (BLEU/ROUGE) + embedding cosine | >= 0.87 cosine vs fp16 baseline | run 500 seeds per image family |
| KV-cache-consistency | long-conversation text | fp16, mixed8 | repeated prefix inflations | token-stream divergence ratio | <= 0.05 | measure at token 256 and 1024 |
| Modality-fallback-sanity | image absent but marker present | int8-dyn | missing modality | hallucination rate | <= 0.02 | detectors for hallucinated entities |
| Latency-tail-quant | multimodal batch | int8-static | microburst batching | p99 latency increase vs fp16 | <= 1.35x | target region-specific kernels |

Onboarding checklist (promote model -> shadow -> canary -> prod)
----------------------------------------------------------------
1. Preflight: run unit evaluations and ensure deterministic seed-based artifact generation for priming templates (artifact hashes stored in artifact-registry).
2. Quant-compatibility run: execute the quant-robustness matrix across the supported quant modes. Attach generated metrics to the model artifact metadata.
3. Shadow validation: launch shadow probes (1% of traffic equivalence) with priming lexicon enabled. Run for 48h or 500k generated tokens, whichever is sooner.
4. Canary rollout: if shadow passes, canary 5% traffic for 24h using mixed precision and KV-cache warming; enable automated rollback ACL.
5. Production promotion: require 4 consecutive days of stable SLOs and no regression ticket older than 24h in alerting queue.

Automated test runner: example config snippet
-------------------------------------------
(Place in eval-runner configs as eval/priming-quant.json)

{
  "suite_name": "priming-quant-robustness",
  "priming_templates": ["image-caption-baseline","multiturn-assistant-image"],
  "quant_modes": ["fp16","int8-dyn","mixed8"],
  "iterations_per_test": 500
}

CLI example
-----------
- Local run: 
  ./tools/eval-runner --config eval/priming-quant.json --model-repo /mnt/models/repo --mode local --out results/prime-2026.json
- CI run: 
  ci/eval-job --suite priming-quant-robustness --artifact $MODEL_ARTIFACT --commit $GITHUB_SHA

Telemetry, metrics and SLOs
--------------------------
- Primary metrics collected per-test: embedding_cosine_vs_fp16, semantic_score, hallucination_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency.
- SLOs for onboarding: embedding_cosine_vs_fp16 >= 0.87, hallucination_rate <= 0.03, p99_latency <= 1.5x baseline.
- Alerting: create a regression ticket automatically if any metric crosses a soft threshold (cosine<0.89) and page on hard thresholds (cosine<0.85 or hallucination>0.05).

Failure modes and triage playbook
--------------------------------
- If embedding_cosine drops by 0.03 vs fp16:
  1. Re-run with different seeds and higher iteration (x5) to reduce stochastic variance.
  2. Run per-slice breakdown (by modality, image resolution, language) to isolate failing cohorts.
  3. If concentrated on quant mode int8-static, escalate to Quant team for kernel re-evaluation.
- If hallucination_rate increases for missing-modality probes: revert to previous priming anchor and run a targeted priming-ablation test to identify sensitive tokens.

Manual inspection checklist
-------------------------
- Sample failed probes (50) and annotate: failure class, severity, suggested fix.
- Check model logits snapshots (use eval-logcat) at token positions where divergence observed.
- Verify KV-cache key consistency across quant modes (use kv-inspect tool).

Rollout and rollback controls
----------------------------
- Canary policy: automatic rollback if any of these occur during canary window:
  - embedding_cosine drop > 0.04 vs baseline
  - hallucination_rate increase > 0.05 absolute
  - sustained latency p99 > 2x baseline for 15m
- Rollback mechanism: canary toggles are controlled by rollout-service; to rollback manually: run 
  rollout-service rollback --model $MODEL_ID --to-tag previous-stable --reason "quant-regression"

Ownership and escalation
-----------------------
- Onboarding owner: Applied ML Team (primary: @maya.chen).
- Quant compatibility owner: Platform Performance (secondary: @liam.oconnor).
- Escalation path: owner -> quant team -> runtime-kernel -> SRE oncall. Include model artifact id and full eval-run results in the ticket.

Appendix: sample probe generation recipe
--------------------------------------
1. Select 200 representative images from the multimodal dataset, stratified by resolution and domain.
2. Generate priming variants: clean, resized, gaussian-noise(+10, +20), blurred, occluded.
3. For each variant, produce 50 prompt seeds using the canonical priming lexicon with diagnostic suffixes.
4. Run against fp16 baseline and each quant mode; store all outputs and embeddings.

References and related docs
--------------------------
- Quant shadow cohort strategy (internal playbook): /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook-2026
- Runtime-sensitive eval contract: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/runtime-sensitive-eval-contract-for-multi-tier-deployments-2025

Contact
-------
- Primary: Maya Chen (maya.chen@redwood.ai)
- Slack: #applied-ml-onboarding

Change log
----------
- 2026-02-15: Initial draft published.
- 2026-08-01: Added KV-cache consistency tests and updated threshold guidance for hallucination_rate.

title: mixed-slo-onboarding-playbook-for-quant-and-cache-sensitive-models
content:
## Summary

This playbook documents the onboarding, evaluation, and rollout process for models that must satisfy mixed SLOs across latency, token-cost, and semantic fidelity when deployed with quantized kernels and KV cache optimizations. It targets models that will run on Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private runtimes where quantization and cache behavior materially affect output quality or latency.

Audience: Model owners, inference engineers, SREs, and applied ML evaluators.

Goals:
- Define an acceptance matrix that balances latency SLO, per-token cost targets, and fidelity thresholds for prompt families.
- Provide reproducible eval harness recipes for quant-aware and cache-aware tests.
- Prescribe rollout and rollback steps (shadow -> canary -> prod) with telemetry gates and regression triage hooks.
- Document operational runbook for common cache/quant failure modes and mitigation.

---

## 1) Pre-onboarding checklist (owner: model-owner)

Ensure the following before any eval runs: 

- Model artifact is stored in Redwood artifact registry with semantic version and provenance metadata (model_name, commit_sha, training_checkpoint_id).
- Quantization metadata completed: algorithm (PTQ/QLoRA/HALF), bitwidth targets, per-layer calibration artifacts, and expected memory profile.
- KV cache semantics documented: indexing format (byte-level vs token-level), warmup strategy, and expected cache hit distributions for representative workloads.
- Representative prompt families selected (see Section 3) and a labeled probe seed of 2k–10k examples covering latency-sensitive, cost-sensitive, and fidelity-sensitive slices.
- Ownership & oncall: two engineers assigned (primary and secondary) with pager contact and slack channel.

---

## 2) Acceptance matrix (hard gates)

Table: acceptance criteria that must be met to promote a model out of shadow. All thresholds are examples; teams should adapt per-product.

| Criterion | Target (example) | Measurement method | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 99th-percentile token latency (p99) | <= 450ms (hosted 16k context) | Synthetic microbenchmark with representative batching mix | infra/serving-runtime |
| Median per-token cost delta vs baseline | <= +10% | Tokenized replay cost model | finance/optimizer |
| Fidelity delta (F1 / BLEU / semantic-similarity) vs baseline | >= -3% absolute or within tolerance band | Anchor-based eval on fidelity prompts (see Sec 3) | applied-ml |
| Cache hit degradation | <= 5% absolute | Shadow traffic with traffic-mirroring and cache telemetry | eng-sre |
| Determinism on seed | identical responses for determinism probes | seeded replay | applied-ml |
\nNotes: Any single hard gate failure blocks promotion. Soft gates (e.g., cost improvements) may be acceptable if compensated by other benefits and with explicit approval.

---

## 3) Probe suite design: prompt families and slices

Design intent: prioritize slices that expose quantization sensitivity (e.g., tokens with rare subword patterns), and cache-bound behavior (long-context priming, multi-turn coherence). For each probe include: input prompt, expected anchor output, tolerance and failure modes.

Minimum probe families (suggested):
1. Short factual Q&A (latency-sensitive) — 1–3 tokens answer length, high precision requirement.
2. Multi-turn followup coherence (cache-sensitive) — 4–12 turn synthetic conversations with interleaved context that stresses KV reuse.
3. Long-context summarization (memory & quant-sensitivity) — 8–16k context summarization tasks.
4. Instruction-synthesis tasks (semantic fidelity) — open-ended responses scored by semantic-similarity + human spot-check.
5. Adversarial subword probes (quant-sensitivity) — tokens that force boundary-tokenization differences.

Each family must include:
- 500–2000 automated probes for automated acceptance, plus 50–200 human-reviewed anchors used for final approval.
- Metadata: seed_id, author, creation_date, expected metric and threshold.

---

## 4) Eval harness recipes (quant-aware & cache-aware)

A. Static quant validation (offline)
1. Run per-layer activation distribution checks with calibration dataset.
2. Compute per-prompt-family fidelity metrics using the quantized artifact.
3. Run bitflip sensitivity (small perturbations to calibration) to estimate fragility.

CLI example:

python tools/quant_eval.py --model artifacts/model-v2 --calib calib/seedset --slices long_context,adversarial --out reports/quant-v2.json

B. Cache-aware shadow replay (online)
1. Mirror 0.5–2% of production traffic to a shadow cluster configured with the quantized artifact and KV cache enabled.
2. Measure: response deltas, cache hit/miss rates, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and error rates.
3. Correlate errors with cache heatmap and tokenization drift tags.

Telemetry: ensure the shadow run produces the following time-series: cache_hit_rate, cache_miss_rate, kv_latency_ms, response_fidelity_delta. Plumb these into the eval dashboard.

C. Cost-sensitivity sweep
- Run batched synthetic load with varying batch sizes (1, 4, 8, 16) and sequence lengths representative of product workload.
- Produce a cost-latency curve and identify knee points where quantization no longer improves economics.

---

## 5) Rollout plan and guardrails (owner: infra + applied-ml)

Stages: 
- Shadow (no user-visible traffic) — required for all quantized artifacts. Minimum: 48–72h of shadow traffic covering peak and off-peak.
- Micro-canary (1% traffic) — 6–12h with strict telemetry gates.
- Canary (5–10%) — 24–48h with rolling increase and automated rollback on gate failures.
- Gradual rollout to 50% then 100% with staggered regional expansion.

Primary automated gates (examples):
- Fidelity regression: rolling 30-min window average <= threshold.
- Latency spike: p99 increase > +15% -> automatic pause.
- Error budget burn: >50% of daily error budget -> pause and notify.
- Cache degradation: sustained hit-rate drop > 7% for 30m -> rollback.

Rollback policy: automatic rollback to previous artifact on any hard gate failure. Human-in-the-loop: for soft-gate failures, require approval from applied-ml lead + oncall SRE.

---

## 6) Regression triage quick path (owner: oncall + applied-ml)

When a regression alert fires:
1. Triage channel & severity: create incident channel and assign severity.
2. Reproduce: run failing probes against both baseline and candidate artifacts.
3. Localize: compare per-layer activations, tokenization diffs, and cache hit traces.
4. Mitigate: possible fast mitigations include reverting quantized artifact, disabling KV cache for affected model, or switching traffic to higher-precision variant.
5. Postmortem: within 72h, publish an incident summary and update probe set if necessary.

Quick diagnostic checklist (commands):
- Replay failing prompt locally: python tools/replay.py --prompt-id 2345 --model artifacts/model-v2 --seed 42
- Dump activation diff: python tools/actdiff.py --base artifacts/model-v1 --cand artifacts/model-v2 --prompt 2345 --out actdiff/2345.json
- Inspect cache trace: curl -s "https://telemetry.redwood.internal/cache_trace?trace_id=abcd" | jq .

---

## 7) Common failure modes and recommended fixes

- Mode: tokenization boundary mismatch after quantization
  - Symptom: short factual answers truncated or off-by-words
  - Fix: re-run tokenizer alignment test, increase calibration set diversity, or pin to model variant with preserved tokenizer class.

- Mode: KV cache warmup causing latency spikes
  - Symptom: elevated tail latency for first requests after rollout
  - Fix: pre-warm hot prefixes via synthetic priming traffic or serve traffic through a regionally warmed pool.

- Mode: semantic drift in rare-token tails
  - Symptom: lower semantic-similarity on adversarial subword probes
  - Fix: add focused calibration examples, enable per-layer mixed-precision for embedding layers.

- Mode: quantized artifact shows nondeterministic outputs under multi-seed
  - Symptom: variance in deterministic probes
  - Fix: lock RNG seeds in runtime, validate FP emulation path, evaluate different quant backend.

---

## 8) Observability & dashboards (owner: eng-platform)

Minimum dashboards:
- Model health overview: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, traffic %, cache hit-rate, fidelity-delta time-series.
- Probe slice explorer: per-slice fidelity/time metrics with drilldown to failing probes.
- Cost curve: token-cost over time with batching and quantization toggles.

Alerts and escalation:
- Alert on any hard gate violation and route to applied-ml+oncall SRE.
- Automated runbooks contain pre-filled remediation steps and rollback commands.

---

## 9) Documentation & artifacts to commit

For audit and reproducibility, commit the following to the model onboarding folder in confluence and artifact registry:
- quantization manifest (algorithm, parameters, per-layer notes)
- probe suite manifest and seed lists
- shadow run report and telemetry export (48–72h)
- rollout plan with owners and contact details
- post-launch evaluation report (72h and 7-day summaries)

---

## 10) Appendix: sample probe manifest (JSON lines example)

{\n  "probe_id": "longctx-0001",\n  "family": "long_context_summarization",\n  "seed": "anon-seed-23",\n  "expected_metric": "semantic_similarity",\n  "tolerance": ">=0.82",\n  "notes": "Anchor derived from human summary v3"\n}

{\n  "probe_id": "adv-subword-0012",\n  "family": "adversarial_subword",\n  "seed": "adv-seed-12",\n  "expected_metric": "exact_match",\n  "tolerance": ">=0.95",\n  "notes": "Contains rare subword tokens; used to measure quant fragility"\n}

---

If you are the model owner starting a new quantized onboarding, follow the Pre-onboarding checklist and open a rollout ticket using the template in the related pages. For questions, ping @marissa.chen on #infra-ml or add reviewers listed above to your onboarding ticket.

title: Live Probe Harness and Feedback Ingest Specification
content:
Summary

This document specifies the Live Probe Harness and Feedback Ingest pipeline used to collect, transform, and surface targeted production probes for model onboarding, continuous evals, and regression detection. The harness balances three priorities: (1) safe, privacy-preserving capture of representative real-world prompts; (2) rich telemetry and annotation plumbing for automated triage and human review; (3) deterministic routing into eval, retraining, and rollback workflows.

Goals

- Provide a low-friction mechanism to collect small, labeled probe samples from live traffic without impacting customer request latency or privacy guarantees.
- Enable automated tagging and scoring of probes for: quality regressions, quantization sensitivity, function-call/structured-output stability, and latency-cost profiling.
- Ensure probes can be replayed deterministically across model variants and quantization profiles in the eval harness.

Scope and non-goals

- In scope: probe capture sampling rules, ingestion schema, basic enrichment (metadata, anonymization), downstream routing (storage, eval queue, labeler), and SLOs for pipeline availability and freshness.
- Out of scope: labelling UI UX design, long-term annotation storage beyond retention window (see Data Retention), and ML model training pipelines (those consume outputs from this pipeline but are documented separately).

Terminology

- Probe: a single captured request/response example plus telemetry and anonymized context used for evaluation.
- ProbeSet: a curated group of probes assigned to an eval campaign or model onboarding job.
- Ingest Agent: lightweight capture component running in the request path (hosted or private) that emits probe events.

Architecture Overview

1) Ingest Agents: deployed as a sidecar/edge filter within the request path. Agents sample requests according to policy, redact PII client-side, and emit compact probe events to the Ingest Bus.
2) Ingest Bus (Kafka / PubSub): durable, ordered buffer. Events are partitioned by customer_id and model_family to support deterministic replay.
3) Enrichment and Privacy Stage: stream processors that apply static enrichment (token counts, language detection, conversation-turn mapping), PII scrubbing (regex, model-based redaction), and differential-privacy noise injection for customer-sensitive fields when required.
4) Classification and Routing: deduplication, heuristic tagging (latency outlier, function-call, multi-turn), quality-scorer (fast ML model), then route to one or more sinks: Eval Queue, Probe Lake (S3 bucket for long-ish retention), or Immediate Alerting for severe failures.
5) Eval Harness Integration: probes routed to eval queue are materialized into deterministic jobs (seeded RNG, fixed tokenizer) for cross-model replay and scoring.

Probe Lifecycle (high level)

1. Capture: Ingest Agent captures request and response snapshot (configurable sample rate, default 0.1% of requests).
2. Local Redaction: Agent applies PII redaction rules and annotates redaction level.
3. Emit: Event pushed to Ingest Bus with minimal payload (see schema).
4. Enrich: Stream jobs add telemetry and quality signals.
5. Route: Classifier decides sink(s).
4. Consume: Eval harness or labeler consumes event and produces labels/metrics.

Sampling and Capture Policies

- Default global sampling: 0.1% uniform across requests.
- Adaptive sampling: increase for new/under-evaluated prompt clusters, error responses (HTTP 5xx), rate-limited token spikes (response tokens > 2048), or flagged feature usage (function-call).
- Customer opt-out: honor per-customer privacy flags. Agents must not capture when customer config disables live probes.

Ingest Event Schema (compact JSON example)

```json
{
  "probe_id": "uuid-v4",
  "captured_at": "2026-03-05T14:22:10Z",
  "customer_id_hash": "sha256:xxxxx",
  "model_family": "gptx-8k",
  "prompt_tokens": 42,
  "response_tokens": 128,
  "lang": "en",
  "redaction_level": "pii-scrubbed",
  "latency_ms": 132,
  "http_status": 200,
  "metadata": {"route":"chat-completion","feature_flags":["function_call"]},
  "payload_ref": "s3://probe-lake/2026/03/05/probe-uuid.json"
}
```

Note: For this Confluence doc we show payload_ref rather than embedding full text to limit bus bandwidth. The payload stored in Probe Lake is encrypted and access-controlled.

Privacy and Safety Controls

- PII Redaction: On-agent regex + model heuristics. Redaction policy documented separately in privacy-playbook.
- Customer Opt-out: honor explicit per-customer settings; default is opt-in for accounts created after 2025-06-01.
- DP Noise: for high-sensitivity customers tagging, the Enrichment stage can apply Laplace noise to numeric telemetry fields when flagged.
- Access Controls: RBAC enforced for Probe Lake (read restricted to SRE/Applied ML/product with justification).

SLOs and Metrics

- Ingest availability: 99.95% monthly.
- End-to-end freshness (capture -> Eval queue readiness): P99 < 2 minutes for non-sampled burst probes; default P95 < 30s for steady-state.
- Successful enrichment rate (no processing errors): 99.0%.

Monitoring signals to emit

- probe.capture.rate by model_family and customer_tier
- probe.enrich.failure.count and top error types
- pipeline.latency.{p50,p95,p99}
- probe.privacy.violations (alerts if redaction fails)

Probe Promotion and Onboarding Flow (how probes are used)

1. Curator or automation selects ProbeSet candidates based on tags (e.g., quant-sensitive candidates have token-length > 2048 or high perplexity).
2. Offline eval jobs replay probes across: baseline model, candidate model, quantized variant(s). Comparison outputs are stored and scored by automated metrics: semantic-similarity, prefix-consistency, function-call fidelity, hallucination score.
3. If automated pass, probe set moves to a human labeling batch for edge-case review.
4. Pass/fail gates feed into a Promotion Decision: green = promote variant to canary; amber = create targeted retrain or prompt-rewrite; red = reject.

Operational Playbook (fast triage steps)

1. Alert: probe.enrich.failure spike or pipeline.latency.p99 breach.
2. Page on-call for Ingest pipeline.
3. Run diagnostics: check Ingest Bus consumer lags, inspect last successful offset, run sample enrichment job locally against sample payload_ref.
4. If corruption found in payloads, isolate offending partition and trigger synthetic replays.
5. If PII redaction failure rate increased, suspend live capture (flip config flag) and notify privacy on-call.

Example CLI recipes

- Re-run enrichment for a batch of probes:

```bash
probe-tool reprocess --from 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-03-01T01:00:00Z --topic ingest-enrich --dry-run
```

- Create ProbeSet manifest for eval harness:

```yaml
name: quant-sensitivity-run-2026-03-06
probes: # list of probe_id strings
  - uuid-1
  - uuid-2
seed: 94107
variants: ["gptx-8k", "gptx-8k-quant8"]
```

Annotation and Labeling Contract

- Label schema: flat list of tags and numeric calibration scores. Example fields: {"coherence": [0-1], "hallucination": [0-1], "function_call_correct": {true|false|n/a}, "severity": [P0|P1|P2|P3]}.
- Label provenance must include labeler_id, label_timestamp, and probe_snapshot_ref.

Data Retention and Access

- Probe Lake retention default: 90 days. Business justification required for extensions.
- Probe metadata in event store retained for 365 days.
- Audit logs for access to Probe Lake retained for 1 year.

Failure Modes and Mitigations

- Upstream high-volume customer producing many probes: apply per-customer sampling caps and backpressure at Ingest Agent.
- Enrichment pipeline consumer lag: autoscale consumers and open an investigation runbook that includes backlog replay steps.
- Privacy regression (PII escapes): immediate suspend capture for affected clusters, initiate privacy incident playbook.

Ownership and Contacts

- Primary owner: Applied ML — Probe Infrastructure (team: applied-ml-probe).
- Secondary: Runtime telemetry (team: eng-serving-runtime).
- On-call rotation: probe-infra-oncall@redwood.internal (see eng-platform/oncall roster).

Open TODOs and Future Work

- Integrate active learning loop to prioritize probes where model disagreement is highest.
- Add pre-ingest differential-privacy guarantees for entire dataset exports.
- Expose a limited customer-facing preview of probes for customers who opt-in to feedback.

References and Related Docs

- Eval contracts and alerting playbook: /applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails/eval-contracts-and-alerting-playbook-2026
- Serving simulation harness: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/serving-simulation-eval-harness-2026
- Privacy playbook (redaction rules): /policies-and-process/data-management/privacy-playbook

Appendix: Quick config table

| Config key | Default | Description | Owner |
|-----------|---------|-------------|-------|
| ingest.sample_rate.global | 0.001 | Global uniform sampling fraction | applied-ml-probe |
| ingest.sample_rate.max_per_customer | 0.01 | Per-customer cap to avoid noisy customers | applied-ml-probe |
| ingest.redaction.mode | pii-scrubbed | Levels: none | pii-scrubbed | dp-noise | applied-ml-probe |
| retention.probe_lake_days | 90 | Days before probe payloads are expired | eng-platform |

If you have questions or want a walkthrough of the pipeline, contact the document owner or schedule a demo with the Applied ML Probe team.

title: Cohort Synthesis and Mixed‑Precision Onboarding Manual
content:
Summary

This document defines a reproducible process for synthesizing tenant cohorts, validating mixed‑precision (quantized) model variants for production, and integrating cohort‑aware evals and regression triage. It ties together: eval harness integration, prompt/benchmark selection per cohort, quantization profile safety checks, and an incident playbook for cohort‑level regressions. The goal is to reduce deployment risk when migrating live traffic to mixed‑precision model artifacts while preserving per‑tenant quality SLAs.

Scope and applicability

- Services: text-generation API (redwood-serve), chat routing (chat-proxy), and reranking service (ranker-core).
- Deployment modes: hosted API and Dedicated pools.
- Audience: model onboarding engineers, applied ML evaluators, SRE oncall, and solutions engineers running private deployments.

Definitions

- Cohort: a traffic slice grouped by stable attributes (tenant_id, primary_locale, average_context_length, feature_flags).
- Cohort fingerprint: fixed set of probes and telemetry that characterizes expected behavior for a cohort.
- Mixed‑precision onboarding: staged rollout of a quantized model variant (e.g., int8/float16 hybrid) with monitoring and fallback to fp32.

Why cohort synthesis matters

Large tenants and long‑tail tenants react differently to quant changes — some show embedding drift or function‑call instability. Cohort synthesis provides:

1) Representative probes for targeting high‑value regressions instead of global averages.
2) Efficient eval budgets by prioritizing cohorts with the largest cost/quality leverage.
3) Deterministic rollback triggers mapped to cohort‑level KPIs.

Cohort synthesis procedure (step‑by‑step)

1) Collect cohort candidates (data engineer / onboarding lead)
   1.1) Query 30 days of anonymized request metadata: tenant_id, model_id, avg_tokens, locale, function_call_rate.
   1.2) Compute candidate attributes: 95th percentile context length, mean response latency, embedding‑usage frequency.
   1.3) Flag cohorts with >0.5% global traffic share or those with prioritized SLAs.

2) Build cohort fingerprint (applied ML)\   2.1) Select 500–2,000 probe inputs per cohort using stratified sampling across intents and context lengths.
   2.2) Include three probe families: canonical_examples (deterministic intent), boundary_contexts (max tokens / truncated contexts), functioncall_scenarios (tool invocation templates).
   2.3) Label each probe with: probe_id, seed_context_hash, expected_response_anchor (text or structured).

3) Define acceptance criteria (product + SRE + applied ML)\   - Quality SLOs (per cohort): coherence_score >= 0.84 OR fall within 4% of baseline fp32 BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity anchor.
   - Latency SLO: P95 <= baseline_P95 + 40 ms for the same allocation tier.
   - Token cost delta: expected token cost <= baseline_token_cost * 0.95 (target) or <= 1.02 (upper bound).
   - Embedding drift threshold: average cosine shift <= 0.06 for embedding‑based similarity probes.

Eval harness integration checklist

- Create a cohort eval job in the eval orchestrator (eval-orch):
  - job_type: cohort_fingerprint_eval
  - model_variants: [fp32_reference, quant_int8_candidate, hybrid_fp16_int8]
  - probes: path/to/cohort/{{cohort_id}}/probes.jsonl
  - telemetry: capture tokens_per_response, kv_cache_hit_rate, function_call_success_rate, embedding_cosine_shift

- Configuration example (YAML):

  job:
    name: cohort-{{cohort_id}}-mixed-precision-eval
    targets: [fp32-ref, quant-candidate]
    probes_file: s3://eval-assets/cohort/{{cohort_id}}/probes.jsonl
    metrics:
      - name: coherence_score
        aggregator: mean
      - name: embedding_cosine_shift
        aggregator: mean
      - name: p95_latency_ms
        aggregator: percentile(95)

- Run schedule: daily for canary window (N=7 days), then hourly during ramp.

Prompt and benchmark guidance for cohorts

- Prompt families: aim for 3 canonical templates + 2 adversarial perturbations per intent.
- Budget: prioritize probes that cause stateful differences (long context continuation, multi‑turn referents).
- Benchmark metrics: coherence_score (human proxy model), instruction_adherence, factuality_sampler (precision@k), functioncall_correctness.

Quantization profile safety checks

Before any shadow or canary rollout, run this checklist:

1) Numeric stability sweep: run ten seeds on the eval harness and compare distributional metrics against fp32 reference (statistical significance test: two‑sample KS test, alpha=0.01).
2) KV cache compatibility: ensure candidate retains cache consistency across chunked streaming for contexts >8k tokens.
3) Function call determinism: for functioncall probes, verify structured output (JSON schema) matches reference for >=98% of probes.
4) Edge slices: test long‑token prompts (tail 1%) and high‑tooltip prompts (URLs/code) explicitly.

Quant tuning knobs to document per model

- layer_skip_threshold: string value (e.g., "top2-fp16")
- per_channel_scale: "true" | "false"
- clamp_strategy: "global" | "adaptive"
- fallback_policy: "immediate-rollout-hold" | "gradual-hedged-fallback"

Example JSON snippet to include in model manifest (store as string here):

{"model_id":"gptx-12b","quant_profiles":[{"name":"int8-hybrid","layer_skip_threshold":"top2-fp16","per_channel_scale":"true","notes":"optimized for long-context workloads"}]}

Staged rollout plan (operations)

1) Shadow validation: mirror 5% of cohort traffic to quant-candidate in shadow for 48–72 hours. No user-visible change. Telemetry: error_rate, coherence_score_delta, embedding_shift.
2) Micro‑canary: route 0.5% of cohort traffic to quant variant via canary route with immediate fallback to fp32 on per‑request failure. Ramp schedule: 0.5% -> 3% -> 10% over 24–72 hours if acceptance criteria met.
3) Mixed‑pool release: introduce quant nodes into dedicated pool at 10% capacity and measure cross‑tenant interference for 7 days.
4) Full cutover: proceed if P95 latency and embedding drift remain within acceptance.

Ownership and runbook triggers

- Owner: model_onboarding_team (primary), applied_ml_evals (secondary).
- SRE oncall notified when embedding_cosine_shift > 0.06 for any cohort OR coherence_score_drop > 0.05 absolute.
- Immediate actions on trigger:
  1) Pause ramp and revert canary routing via routing-control CLI: 
     rdc route update --route canary-{{cohort_id}} --action revert --reason "cohort-quality-trigger"
  2) Kick off Regression Triage runbook (steps below).

Regression triage runbook (cohort emphasis)

1) Triage owner assigned (applied_ml lead) and page created with: cohort_id, last_accepted_model, candidate_model, elapsed_ramp_time.
2) Automated bisect: run eval‑orchestrator bisect between fp32_ref and candidate, isolating by:
   - probe subfamily (functioncall vs long_context)
   - intent cluster (intent_id)
   - token‑budget bucket (short/medium/long)
3) Compare per‑probe diffs and prioritize top‑10 failing probes. Attach diff artifacts and topk embeddings shift table.
4) Hypothesis examples to test: 
   - "quant noise in early layers causing hallucination on multi‑turn referents"
   - "per_channel_scale mismatch for code blocks causing tokenization shifts"
5) Rapid mitigations: rollback, tighten fallback_policy, or apply targeted prompt rewrite for affected cohort.

Observability and dashboards

Minimum dashboard panels per cohort:
- Cohort traffic share (1h / 24h)
- Coherence score trend (baseline vs candidate)
- Embedding cosine shift distribution (boxplot)
- P95 latency by model variant
- Token cost delta and KV cache hit rate

Retention and audit

- Store every cohort eval job snapshot and probes.jsonl for 180 days in s3://eval-snapshots/{cohort_id}/.
- Keep a promotion ledger entry in model_registry: {model_id, cohort_id, timestamp, promotion_state, owner}.

Appendix A — Example probe JSONL line

{"probe_id":"c123-0001","input":"Summarize the following conversation...","expected_anchor":"Customer asked about refund policy; agent summarized steps"}

Appendix B — Quick CLI snippets

- Create cohort eval job:
  evalctl create job --type cohort_fingerprint_eval --cohort c123 --probes s3://eval-assets/cohort/c123/probes.jsonl --targets fp32-ref,quant-cand

- Pause canary route:
  rdc route update --route canary-c123 --action revert --reason "quality-trigger"

Appendix C — Decision log references

- Connected ADRs: decision record on hedged fallback routing (see /confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-hedged-fallback-2025).
- Model registry: see model_registry entry for specific quant profile names.

Notes and future work

- We plan to extend cohort synthesis to multi‑modal tenants (image prompts + text) and include embedding drift projections using temporal decay models.
- Investigate automated prompt rewrite templates as a mitigation baked into the canary route when drift is detected.

Contact

For questions, ping @nadia.chen or the model_onboarding Slack channel (#model-onboarding).

title: Onboarding bridge for heterogeneous fidelity and quantization-fallback
content:
SUMMARY
This document defines the 'Onboarding Bridge' pattern: a standardized orchestration and checklist to promote models from shadow / evaluator fleets to production across mixed-fidelity environments (hosted, dedicated, private) while enabling safe quantization fallbacks and fast regression triage. It combines eval-harness scheduling, prompt set conditioning, quant profile gating, and an operational rollback/rollforward playbook.

MOTIVATION
- Teams increasingly deploy heterogeneous model variants (fp16, int8, mixed-precision, channel-quantized) across environments.
- Production regressions frequently root in fidelity mismatch between shadow evals and runtime (quant, KV-cache, batching).
- We need a reproducible bridge that: (a) preserves safety & quality SLOs, (b) automates conservative fallbacks, and (c) gives clear triage fast-paths for regressions.

SCOPE
This playbook applies to: model onboarding for text and multimodal function-call services, any model variants with quantization profiles in our registry, and services that use the Redwood eval-harness for shadowing. It is NOT prescriptive about exact quant kernels but standardizes the decision surface and operational controls.

KEY DEFINITIONS
- Fidelity tier: label for runtime equivalence class (gold / near-gold / budgeted).
- Quant-fallback: automatic runtime substitution to a higher-fidelity variant when safety/quality checks fail.
- Shadow cohort: a controlled set of traffic mirrored to a candidate model during validation.

DESIGN PRINCIPLES
- Conservative promotion: require multi-signal pass (eval harness metrics + shadow telemetry + human review) before production route cutover.
- Observable rollouts: every onboarding includes per-probe SLI dashboards and an auto-fail policy.
- Fast rollback: automated circuit that returns live traffic to last-known-good variant within 60s for critical SLO breaks.

ONBOARDING CHECKLIST (step-by-step)
1. Prepare assets
   - Register model artifact in the model registry with explicit fidelity_tag and quant_profile_id.
   - Produce a prompt-set subset (min 500 probes for the service slice) covering core intents and long-tail slices (see Prompt Conditioning below).
2. Shadow validation (2–7 days)
   - Launch in a 10–25% shadow cohort via eval-harness shadower with telemetry capture (tokens, latency, functioncall integrity).
   - Run full eval suite: semantic fidelity, hallucination probes, tokenization edgecases, functioncall unit tests.
3. Quant safety scan
   - Execute the quant-safety suite (see Quant Safety table). Candidate must meet per-slice fidelity thresholds.
4. Human review gate
   - Product & ML reviewer inspects top 200 divergent probes and signs off.
5. Micro-canary (2–6 hours)
   - Canary to 0.5–2% live traffic with tight alerting.
6. Gradual rollout
   - 2x per hour increases with stability checks until target weight.
7. Post-promotion monitoring
   - Retain probe sampling, automatic regression scoring, and 24h annotated review.

EVAL-HARNESS INTEGRATION
- Orchestration pattern: use the 'fidelity-bridge' runner within the eval-harness to schedule layered jobs: quick smoke -> fidelity probes -> human sample -> quant-safety replays.
- Telemetry contracts: ensure the harness emits the following labels in span/metric metadata: model_variant, quant_profile_id, shadow_cohort_id, probe_id, probe_slice, seed.
- Priority ordering: probe suites prioritized by SLO risk (functioncall > billing-critical > UI-text).

PROMPT SET CONDITIONING AND LOCALIZATION
- Create a seed prompt family per service slice; attach locality tags (lang, region, regulatory).
- For quant-sensitivity, generate a localized perturbation set: tokenization edgecases, truncated context, slot-value permutations.
- Prompt mutation rules (applied during shadowing):
  - Deterministic augmentation: synonym substitution preserving slot types.
  - Stochastic noise: apply 1–3 char/word-level perturbations for robustness checks.
  - Context aging: test with prefix drop (25%, 50%) to emulate trimmed context.

QUANT SAFETY AND FALLBACK PROFILES (table)
| Profile id | Fidelity tier | Allowed kernels | Max expected token delta | Required pass rate | Fallback target |
|-----------|---------------|-----------------|-------------------------:|------------------:|-----------------|
| q-prof-std-v1 | near-gold | int8-4, fp16-opt | 0.6% | 95% | fp16-gold-v1 |
| q-prof-aggr-v2 | budgeted | int8-2, mixed-8 | 1.5% | 90% | q-prof-std-v1 |
| q-prof-edge-low | budgeted | int4-sparse | 3.0% | 85% | q-prof-aggr-v2 |

- Required pass rate denotes the percent of probes whose semantic-anchored score (see metrics below) must be >= threshold.
- Fallbacks are chained: runtime may step up to the immediate higher-fidelity profile when alerts or per-request scored heuristics indicate degradation.

QUALITY GUARDRAILS AND METRICS
- Per-route SLOs (example):
  - 95th latency <= 300ms (interactive routes)
  - Semantic fidelity (anchor BLEU-like / embedding similarity) >= 0.88 averaged over anchor probes
  - Functioncall integrity: 100% required for payment/authorization routes
- Automated sentinel checks (run continuously):
  - Drift detector: embedding centroid shift > 0.07 -> trigger re-eval.
  - Response stability index drop > 0.05 across 1h window -> auto-fallback to previous variant.
  - Token-output variance spike (std dev > configured) -> send to regression queue.

REGRESSION TRIAGE FAST-PATH
- Trigger sources: shadow anomalies, canary alerts, customer reports, or periodic sweep guards.
- Fast-path steps (automated where possible):
  1. Isolate traffic slice and label (service, route, tenant).
  2. Snapshot recent 5k probes and run differential replay across gold & candidate variants.
  3. If semantic delta > 2x threshold OR functioncall failure rate > 0 -> immediate circuit: route weight -> last-known-good.
  4. Launch regression-hunt ticket with attached replay artifacts, failing probes, and suggested blame signals (quant, tokenization, prompt mutation).
  5. Parallel task: run quick quant-sanity re-eval and KV-cache priming replay.
- Ownership: SRE + Model Owner + Oncall-eval (rotation) until RCA complete.

OPERATIONAL RUNBOOK (for oncall)
- Detect: alerts (response-stability, functioncall-failures, embedding-drift) -> Pager.
- Immediate actions (0–10 min):
  1. Check canary dashboard and last deploy ID.
  2. If alert is production-impacting, flip traffic to previous variant via console CLI: 
     - CLI: redwood routes update --service <svc> --variant <variant-id> --weight 100 --confirm
  3. If rollback not possible, enable quant-fallback policy for the service: 
     - CLI: redwood service-config set --svc <svc> --quant-fallback enabled --profile q-prof-std-v1
- Triage (10–60 min): differential replays, attach telemetry, and create regression-hunt.
- Rollforward criteria: all failed probes reverified and pass rate > 98% for 1h in shadow and micro-canary.

CONFIG EXAMPLES
- Minimal onboarding manifest (JSON):
{
  "model_id": "model-suite/assistant-alpha:v3",
  "fidelity_tag": "near-gold",
  "quant_profile_id": "q-prof-std-v1",
  "shadow_cohort": "shadow-2027-01-10-a",
  "probe_set": "slices/core_intent_500",
  "auto_fallback": true
}

- Example alert rule (Prometheus-style pseudo):
ALERT ResponseStabilityDrop
IF response_stability_index{route=~"/chat.*"} < 0.83 FOR 5m
LABELS {severity="sev2"}
ANNOTATIONS {summary="Response stability drop on chat routes"}

GOVERNANCE AND REVIEW
- Promotion requires sign-off from: Model Owner, Product Safety Reviewer, and an SRE lead.
- Any quant-fallback that remains active > 48h requires a postmortem and remediation plan.

APPENDIX: EXPLAINABILITY SIGNALS AND AUTOMATED BLAME SUGGESTION
- For every failed probe produce a blame vector: [quant_profile_delta, tokenization_change, kv_cache_mismatch, prompt_mutation_effect]. The eval-harness will attach this vector to replay artifacts.
- Use the probabilistic-blame-model (see related_pages) to prioritize remediation.

FEEDBACK LOOP
- After each onboarding, run a 30-day fidelity review: collect annotated disagreements, measure metric drift, and update the quant-profile whitelist/blacklist.

CONTACTS
- Onboarding owner: amelia.park@redwood.ai
- Eval-harness maintainer: priya.shah@redwood.ai
- Quant safety lead: liam.oconnor@redwood.ai

DOCUMENT HISTORY
- 2026-11-15: Drafted (Amelia Park)
- 2026-12-08: Quant safety table added (Liam O'Connor review)
- 2027-01-10: Finalized promotion criteria and runbook (published)

title: Onboarding anti-entropy plan: live-drift decision tree & rollback playbook
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines an anti-entropy onboarding strategy for new model variants and quantized artifacts. It prescribes a deterministic decision tree for detecting live drift, scoring signal fusion across quality/latency/cost telemetry, and executing automated or manual rollback paths. The goal is to ensure safe, observable promotions with clear thresholds and handoffs into regression triage.

Scope:
- Applies to: hosted, dedicated, and private deployments when promoting a model or quantized artifact from shadow to warm canary or prod.
- Includes: prompt families, function-call services, streaming sessions and embedding production indices.
- Excludes: offline-only evaluation artifacts and exploratory research snapshots.

Definitions:
- Entropy event: sudden increase in metric variance (quality, distribution, latency) vs. baseline.
- Signal fusion: combined score from weighted telemetry (quality, latency, token-cost, user-visible errors).
- Drift window: 30-minute rolling window used for early-detection gating.

Signals and thresholds (operational table):
| Signal | Aggregation | Normal baseline | Alert threshold | Escalation threshold | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Prompt-set fidelity (slice-level) | weighted F1/anchor score | >= 0.92 | drop >= 0.06 relative | drop >= 0.12 relative | compute per-priming-family |
| End-to-end latency P95 | rolling 30m P95 | <= 240ms | increase +40% | increase +80% or >1000ms | includes network and runtime |
| Token cost per request | mean over 30m | stable within 10% | increase +25% | increase +50% | signals quant fallback/bug |
| Function-call failure rate | calls per 30m | <= 0.5% | >= 1.5% | >= 5% | includes parse/format errors |
| Embedding drift (cosine) | average top-k sim delta | <= 0.04 | >= 0.08 | >= 0.16 | per-index and per-tenant |

Decision tree (short form):
1) Shadow comparison: run candidate under shadow for 24h (or smaller block for high-impact changes) with anchored probe families and production sampling.
2) Compute signal fusion score every 5 minutes: normalized signals weighted as {fidelity:0.45, latency:0.25, errors:0.15, cost:0.15}.
3) If fusion score breaches Alert threshold => auto-scale back to warm canary and create incident ticket with triage tag 'anti-entropy/alert'.
4) If fusion score breaches Escalation threshold or any single signal crosses Escalation threshold => automated rollforward block and execute rollback policy (see Rollback matrix).
5) If rolling windows recover for 2 consecutive evaluation windows (30m each) and human reviewer confirms, allow controlled rollforward (canary -> prod) with reduced weight.

Rollout phases and guardrails:
- Phase 0: Preflight (dev/test)
  - Unit tests, eval harness smoke, quant-compatibility sanity run.
  - Confirm quant profile and kernel availability.
- Phase 1: Shadow (0% traffic) for 24h or 10k sampled requests.
  - Collect anchored probe coverage and runtime fingerprint.
- Phase 2: Warm canary (1%–5% traffic) for 2–12h depending on impact score.
  - Gates: no fidelity drop > Alert threshold, P95 latency within limit, functional correctness tests green.
- Phase 3: Progressive ramp (5%->25%->100%) with automated checks at each step.

Rollback matrix (automated actions):
| Triggering condition | Immediate automated action | Human notify | Recovery step |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single-signal Escalation (e.g., P95 > 1000ms) | Quarantine traffic to fallback variant; freeze rollout | page oncall + owners | Roll back to last-succeeded artifact and trigger postmortem |
| Fusion Escalation | Abort promotion; mark artifact as unstable | page SRE + ML owner | Revert model, open regression triage board with sample set |
| Function-call spike > 5% | Disable streaming-to-function path for canary users | notify product + integrator | Route calls to preexisting stable variant |

Automated gating rules (implementation notes):
- Gate evaluation runs are implemented as a stateless service that consumes probe and production telemetry; every 5m it emits a 'gate' verdict (pass/warn/fail) with a scoring vector.
- Gate verdicts are deterministic and stored as immutable events for audit.
- For quantized artifacts, include a quant-compatibility check that runs 500 synthetic priming probes (slice-aware) before warm canary. Failures in >2% probes fail the gate.

Manual escalation playbook (when to escalate):
1) If gate verdict = fail for two consecutive windows OR any Escalation single-signal triggers -> create short incident channel with tags: model-name, artifact-id, canary-id, primary-signal, related-probes.
2) Tag the incident with "regression-hypothesis" and attach 3 representative probe payloads (highest divergence and highest user-frequency).
3) Triage owner assigns to regression team within 30 minutes. If unassigned, oncall SRE takes ownership.

Telemetry & alerts configuration (examples):
- Alert rule example (Prometheus-style):
  alert: ModelOnboardLatencyAlert
  expr: increase(model_request_duration_seconds_bucket{model="candidate"}[30m]) > 0.4
  for: 10m
  labels: {severity:critical, team:ml-serving}
- Fusion scorer settings (YAML example snippet):
  fusion_weights: 
    fidelity: 0.45
    latency: 0.25
    errors: 0.15
    cost: 0.15
  eval_window_mins: 30
  verdict_emit_interval_mins: 5

Ownership and runbook links:
- Model onboarding owner: ML Platform (team: runtime-onboarding). Primary contact: Priya Nair.
- Regression triage: Applied ML (team: model-regress).
- Runbooks: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/model-onboard-rollback-runbook-2025.json

Post-incident: triage and learnings checklist:
- Preserve full request/response traces and probe artifacts in tier-2 bucket for 90 days.
- Run automated bisect tool to test quant vs float behavior on anchored probes.
- Produce 'entropy report' summarizing which slices drove the decision (top-5) and suggested mitigations (prompt rewrite, quant-profile relax, prompt-family fallback).

Operational examples and CLI snippets:
- Promote candidate (safe-mode):
  rdi promote --model candidate-v2 --mode warm-canary --max-traffic 0.02 --guard-config=anti-entropy:v1
- Abort canary and revert:
  rdi rollback --canary-id canary-1234 --reason "fusion-escalation" --notify=oncall@redwood.com
- Export top probe failures:
  rdi probes export --artifact candidate-v2 --top 50 --out /tmp/failures.json

FAQ:
Q: How long should shadow runs be for low-traffic services?
A: For low-traffic services (<1k requests/day) use synthetic probe augmentation to reach 10k effective samples or extend shadow to 72h.

Q: When is quant-induced degradation expected?
A: Usually at priming-sensitive prompt families and long-context KV-cache heavy flows. The anti-entropy gate enforces a 2% synthetic-probe failure ceiling before any warm canary.

Appendix: sample gating YAML (single-file):
| key | value |
|---|---|
| fusion_weights | fidelity:0.45,latency:0.25,errors:0.15,cost:0.15 |
| eval_window_mins | 30 |
| probe_sample_count_for_quant | 500 |

Notes and rationale:
- Weighting fidelity highest reflects production-first commitment to customer-visible correctness.
- Rolling windows and dual-window recovery protect against transient flapping.
- Immutable gate verdicts and required probe attachments accelerate regression hunting.

Contact and feedback:
- Document owner: Priya Nair (priay@redwood.com). For edits, submit a PR to the onboarding playbook repo or ping #ml-onboard in Slack.

title: Service-Anchored Onboarding Eval Contract with Regression Contingency
content:
Overview
========
This document defines a service-anchored evaluation contract used during model onboarding and promotion for production serving. It couples acceptance criteria (quality, latency, token-cost) with an explicit regression contingency playbook so that any release can be validated and, if necessary, automatically mitigated or rolled back with low human overhead. The goal is to make onboarding decisions auditable, repeatable, and safe across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployment modes.

Why a service-anchored contract?
- Aligns model promotion to concrete product-facing SLOs rather than abstract metric thresholds.
- Ensures cross-functional sign-off (SRE, Product, Applied ML, Platform) with traceable artifacts.
- Ties continuous evals, shadow traffic, and canary sampling to an actionable regression escalation path.

Scope
-----
Applies to:
- New model variants promoted to staging/canary for inference (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Quantized artifacts and hybrid-precision builds.
- Functional changes to prompt templates or response post-processing that affect user-visible outputs.

Exclusions:
- Research-only checkpoints not intended for production.
- Infrastructure-only kernel upgrades that do not change model weights or prompt behavior (see infra change process).

Core concepts and definitions
----------------------------
- Service owner: owner of the product endpoint (e.g., search-relevance, chat-assistant).
- Eval contract: a checklist and thresholds mapping to service SLOs used to accept or reject a promotion.
- Shadow validation: live traffic duplicated to the candidate model with telemetry capture only (no user-facing outputs).
- Regression: any statistically significant negative delta in an agreed-upon slice of metrics that crosses the impact budget.

Eval contract template (summary)
------------------------------
1) Identify service-critical slices (owners):
   - Top-5 tenant workflows by volume (owner: Product).
   - Safety and compliance slices (owner: Security).
   - High-cost long-context queries (owner: Platform).

2) Required telemetry and probes:
   - Probe suite: stable probes + 3 exploratory probes per slice. Maintain probe IDs and provenance.
   - Shadow replay: 24h continuous shadow with sampling rate >= 1% of production requests for high-volume services, >= 5% for intermittent services.
   - Token accounting: per-request token counts and per-route cost estimate.

3) Acceptance thresholds (example mapping):
   - Quality: weighted accuracy/utility delta <= -1.5% relative to baseline across critical slices.
   - Latency: 95th percentile latency increase <= 15% or +150ms (whichever smaller).
   - Cost: per-1k-token cost increase <= 10% unless explicitly approved by Finance.
   - Embedding drift: cosine similarity degradation <= 0.02 relative to baseline for retrieval slices.

4) Quantization and hybrid artifacts:
   - Artifact must pass the per-workload quant-sanity checks (see Quant Sanity Checklist GUID).
   - If quantized, run the quant-fallback sentinel (a 1-hour live replay comparing float vs quant responses for a stratified sample).

5) Rollout policy:
   - Canary: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over a minimum of 48h with stability gates at each step. Gates evaluate contract thresholds and critical alert rates.

Acceptance criteria (detailed)
-----------------------------
- A promotion job must produce an immutable evaluation report (artifact id, commit sha, eval-run id) containing:
  - Probe pass/fail table with confidence intervals.
  - Per-slice delta table for quality, latency, cost, safety checks.
  - Annotated examples for any failing probes or >0.5% quality regressions.

- Admission rule: all critical slices must be green OR have an approved exception with documented compensating controls (e.g., fallback model pinned, additional caching).

Regression contingency playbook (operational)
-------------------------------------------
This playbook defines automated and human-in-the-loop steps when a promotion or canary triggers a regression.

Severity classification: 
- Sev-1 (production impact): user-visible correctness failures affecting >0.5% of requests or a spike in error rate causing >0.5% request failures.
- Sev-2 (degradation): quality delta between 0.2%–0.5% on critical slices or latency increases approaching thresholds.
- Sev-3 (observability/noise): alerts with low user impact, requires investigation.

Immediate automated responses (system):
1) Canary abort: if any Sev-1 condition observed during canary window, abort rollout and trigger rollback to previous stable variant.
2) Auto-fallback: route traffic away from candidate to fallback model variant if configured (per-route fallback priority).
3) Telemetry snapshot: capture full request/response KV cache context, token accounting, model logits, and probe ids for 2x the default retention window for the affected slices.

Human triage flow (steps):
1) Pager notification to the oncall evaluation engineer + service owner. Include eval-run id and link to artifact and example failures.
2) Quick triage (15 minutes): run targeted regression bisect (e.g., split by prompt family, device, tenant) using the bisect harness.
3) Decide: rollback, apply runtime mitigation (e.g., revert prompt change, reduce temperature, enforce prefix-caching), or accept with exception. Document decision & mitigation in the eval artifact.
4) Postmortem: for Sev-1 events, publish a short 72-hour incident and a retro within 7 days with root cause and regression fix plan.

Investigation checklist (for triage)
-----------------------------------
- Confirm reproducibility with: shadow-replay --seed <eval-run-id> --slice <slice-id> --compare baseline,candidate
- Check KV cache divergence and cold-start ratios.
- For quantized artifacts, run float-vs-quant diff for annotated failing examples.
- Check prompt pipeline changes and templating fallbacks.
- Inspect recent infra rollouts or kernel updates (cross-reference infra release id).

YAML: minimal eval-run job example
--------------------------------
```yaml
job: promoted-eval-run
service: chat-assistant
baseline_model: rdx-chat-v2.1
candidate_model: rdx-chat-v2.2-qat
probes: [critical-slice-suite, safety-suite]
shadow_sampling: 0.02
metrics: [accuracy_delta, p95_latency_delta, token_cost_delta]
artifact_output: gs://redwood-evals/promotions/2026/rdx-chat-v2.2-qat/report.json
```

Monitoring, alerts and dashboards
--------------------------------
- Dashboards: per-service promotion dashboard with live delta gauges for the contract metrics and a probe failure timeline.
- Alerts (examples):
  - PROMO:sev1_quality_regression -> trigger canary_abort and page evaluation-oncall.
  - PROMO:latency_p95_jump -> page platform-oncall if > 2x baseline for 30 minutes.
  - PROMO:token_cost_excess -> inform finance and owner if > 15% increase sustained for 2 hours.

Reference SLO mapping table (text depiction)
-------------------------------------------
| Service SLO            | Eval Contract Metric           | Threshold/Action | Owner |
|------------------------|-------------------------------|------------------|-------|
| Chat assistant latency | p95 latency delta             | <= +150ms        | SRE   |
| Retrieval recall       | embedding similarity degradation| <= 0.02         | ML    |
| Search relevance       | NDCG@10 delta                 | >= -1.5%         | Product|

Governance and approvals
------------------------
- Promotion requires signoff from: Service owner (acceptance), Applied ML owner (model cert), SRE (capacity/latency acceptance), Security (safety checks) — recorded via the promotion ticket with artifact links.
- Exceptions: any accepted exception must include a compensating control, a sunset date, and a rollback trigger.

Data provenance and auditability
--------------------------------
- Every promotion must include immutable artifacts: model checksum, quantization recipe id, eval-run id, probe-suite version, and the promotion ticket id.
- Audit records are stored in the Promotions Ledger with retention policy 2 years for exec review.

Operational notes and tips
-------------------------
- Prefer shadow validation with real KV context for cache-sensitive services — synthetic probes miss cache-interaction regressions.
- When evaluating quantized builds, prioritize worst-case examples (long context, multi-turn state) in the probe set; these often surface sequence-dependent degradation.
- Use prioritization scores for probe sampling to keep cost bounded: critical slices keep 100% of probe runs, exploratory probes are budgeted at 10% of runs.

Appendix A: Quick rollback commands
----------------------------------
- Abort canary and pin previous variant (CLI):
  redwood promote abort --service chat-assistant --promote-id <promote-id>
  redwood route pin --service chat-assistant --variant rdx-chat-v2.1

- Trigger immediate auto-fallback to float variant for quantized builds (if configured):
  redwood fallback enable --service chat-assistant --from-variant rdx-chat-v2.2-qat --to-variant rdx-chat-v2.2-float --duration 30m

Appendix B: Example post-promotion record (JSON snippet)
------------------------------------------------------
```json
{
  "eval_run_id": "eval-2026-01-27-09-13",
  "baseline": "rdx-chat-v2.1",
  "candidate": "rdx-chat-v2.2-qat",
  "outcome": "aborted",
  "reason": "sev1 quality regression on payment_flow slice",
  "artifact_link": "gs://redwood-evals/promotions/2026/rdx-chat-v2.2-qat/report.json"
}
```

Owners and contacts
-------------------
- Document owner: Asha Patel (Applied ML)
- Service onboarding coordinator: Miguel Torres (Platform)
- Evaluation oncall: see oncall roster page /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues/oncall-rota

Related artifacts and pages
--------------------------
- Quantization checklist: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-failure-modes-and-recovery-playbook-2026
- Regression triage handbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026
- Eval harness API: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/evaluator-sdk-adapter-patterns-for-private-and-dedicated-2026

Change log
----------
- 2026-01-15: Initial draft by Asha Patel.
- 2026-02-10: Incorporated reviewer feedback: added explicit token-cost gating and quant-fallback sentinel.

Feedback and iteration
----------------------
- For feedback or suggested edits, please comment on the promotion ticket template or email applied-ml@redwood-inference.internal.

title: Incremental probe-driven onboarding for function-call-capable models
content:
Overview
-------
This playbook describes an incremental, probe-driven onboarding procedure for models that expose function-call behavior and interact with runtime tooling (webhooks, databases, external APIs). It focuses on minimizing user-visible regressions while validating runtime contracts: function schema stability, tool-call ordering, tokenization/serialization invariants, and quantization / KV-cache interactions. The goal is a repeatable checklist teams can follow to promote a candidate model from shadow to mixed canary to full production with defined metrics and rollback criteria.

Why this is needed
------------------
Function-call models introduce new failure classes that typical text-only onboarding misses: mismatched JSON schemas, missing/extra fields, latency-sensitive external tool calls, and subtle behavior shifts after quantization or KV cache migration. These failures can manifest as incorrect downstream actions or data corruption. An incremental probe-driven approach lets us exercise these surface areas under controlled load and detect regressions early.

Scope
-----
- Applies to models used for programmatic outputs (JSON/tool calls) and models that rely on runtime toolchains (e.g., DB lookups, external API calls).
- Intended for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes.
- Does NOT replace safety/safety-sandbox fuzzing; it's complementary and focused on integrability and runtime contract stability.

Ownership and stakeholders
--------------------------
- Onboarding lead: ML Infra / Serving Runtime owner (example: Maya Patel)
- Evaluator owner: Applied ML / Evals (example: Diego Alvarez)
- Runtime integration owner: Platform or Integrations (example: Priya Shah)
- SRE contact for canary window and metric alarms: Eng SRE oncall

High-level timeline (recommended)
--------------------------------
1. Readiness check & probe design (1–3 days)
2. Shadow probe run + offline analysis (2–5 days)
3. Incremental canaries (mixed traffic) with targeted probes (3–7 days)
4. Full rollout with continuous probe monitoring and autoscale validation (1–3 days)

Readiness checklist (pre-shadow)
--------------------------------
- [ ] Model artifact passes unit schema checks (declared function signatures)
- [ ] Tokenization-snapshot: captured tokenization mapping for top 1000 prompt templates
- [ ] Quantization baseline: run fast quant regression on 50 representative probes (latency + determinism)
- [ ] KV-cache compatibility: smoke checks for prefix reuse on sampling probes
- [ ] Tooling harness: test harness that can simulate external tools and record call traces

Designing probes for function-call surfaces
----------------------------------------
Probes should exercise:
- Positive path: well-formed function calls, correct ordering, sequential tool interactions
- Negative path: malformed payloads, missing optional fields, extra unexpected keys
- Latency-sensitive path: function calls that depend on sub-100ms downstream responses
- Stateful path: multi-turn sequences that rely on KV cache warmup and key reuse

Probe attributes (minimum)
- probe_id (string)
- intent (short description)
- input_prompt (template + slot schema)
- expected_function_schema (json schema string)
- allowed_semantic_variance (description / thresholds)
- drift_guard (metric to track)
- run_frequency (shadow/canary/prod)

Example probe (text block)
-------------------------
Probe: account-balance-fetch-1
- intent: fetch a customer account balance and format as: {"account_id":string,"balance":number,"currency":string}
- input_prompt: "Get balance for CUSTOMER_ID={{customer_id}}; return as JSON using function 'get_balance'"
- expected_function_schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"account_id":{"type":"string"},"balance":{"type":"number"},"currency":{"type":"string"}},"required":["account_id","balance"]}
- allowed_semantic_variance: numeric rounding +/- 0.01; currency code must be ISO-4217
- drift_guard: function_schema_mismatch_rate < 0.5% over rolling 1k probes

Shadow phase (offline + limited live)
----------------------------------
