2) Latency & resource:
   - Median token latency <= baseline * 1.15
   - P99 token latency <= baseline * 1.5 AND absolute P99 <= 2.0s for interactive endpoints
   - GPU memory footprint reduction or within +5% of expected profile for mixed deployments
3) Stability & determinism:
   - KV-cache compatibility check: no divergence in continuation probability mass > 0.05 across 10k long-context probes
   - Determinism seeds: identical prompts under deterministic setting must match baseline behavior with <= 0.5% token edit-distance
4) Operational safety:
   - Rollout must have automated fallback route configured (quant -> baseline) with health-check cooldown of 30s
   - Telemetry events emitted for quant_migration_probe.result, quant_fallback.triggered, quant_rollout.progress

Probe Design Guidelines
- Maintain a prioritized probe portfolio:
  - Hot slices: 50K daily samples for latency-sensitive prompts (short, API-driven paths).
  - Long-context: 20K probes with >2k token histories to stress KV cache and attention speedups.
  - Function-call and structured-output probes: 5K examples covering common schema shapes.
  - Safety and red-team seeds: 10K fuzz/adversarial probes maintained by Security & Applied ML.

- Labeling and thresholds:
  - Each probe includes: prompt, expected intent, baseline response fingerprint (hash), and reference metric values.
  - Use aggregated metrics with confidence intervals (95% CI). Accept if CI upper bound meets acceptance criteria.

Rollout Plan (Procedure)
1) Local quant validation (model-owner)
   - Run local quant conversion and unit tests. Generate local evaluator report (artifact: quant_local_report.json).
   - Quick checks: shape/ops parity, seed determinism smoke tests, sample inference on 100 probes.
2) Shadow validation (eval-harness)
   - Schedule 48h shadow against production-proxy probe suite. Compare metrics to baseline.
   - Generate runbook comments and open PR to promote to canary if pass.
3) Canary (1% traffic or 0.5% depending on tenant sensitivity)
   - Duration: 4 hours minimum. Monitor metrics over 5-minute windows.
   - Automatic abort conditions:
     - Runtime error rate increase > 0.5pp absolute OR >= 2x baseline
     - Semantic Similarity delta > 0.03
     - Latency P99 increase > 2x baseline or > 3s absolute
   - If abort triggers, traffic routed to baseline immediately and release engineer notified.
4) Staged ramp (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%)
   - Each step minimum 6 hours, or longer for high-risk slices.
   - At each step, run full probe-suite and the lightweight smoke probes; require automated checks to pass.
5) GA promotion
   - Final artifact signed, release notes posted, and quant artifact retained in artifact registry with tags: quantized, promotor, baseline_hash.

Automated Fallback & Runbook
- Fallback logic (runtime): a rule set in the Router that evaluates telemetry windows and flips traffic to the configured fallback artifact.
- Emergency rollback steps (manual):
  1. Open incident on #prod-model-rollouts and tag Model Owner + Runtime oncall.
  2. Trigger immediate route reassign: curl -X POST https://runtime.internal/api/route/switch -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","to":"baseline-artifact-id"}'
  3. Validate baseline responses on 100 smoke probes.
  4. Create postmortem and hold a triage meeting within 48 hours.

Telemetry, Dashboards and Alerts
- Required telemetry exports:
  - quant_migration_probe.result: {probe_id, slice, metric_vector, delta_from_baseline, pass_fail}
  - quant_rollout.progress: {artifact_id, percent_traffic, step, timestamp}
  - quant_fallback.triggered: {artifact_id, reason, metric_snapshot}
- Dashboards (names):
  - Quant Migration Overview (team: eval-harness)
  - Quant Canary Health (team: runtime/SRE)
  - KV-Cache Divergence Monitor (team: serving)
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - ALERT: quant_canary_semantic_regression if semantic_similarity_delta < -0.03 over 10m window -> Pager to runtime oncall
  - ALERT: quant_canary_error_spike if error_rate > 1.0% for 5m -> Slack + Pager

Metrics Table (exemplar)
| Metric | Baseline target | Acceptable delta | Alert level | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Semantic Similarity (sBERT) | 0.94 | -0.02 | critical if <-0.03 | applied-ml |
| Task Accuracy (labeled) | 92% | -1.5pp | high if <-2pp | applied-ml |
| Latency P50 (token) | 12ms | +15% | medium if >+50% | serving |
| Latency P99 (token) | 180ms | +50% | critical if >2x or >2000ms | serving |
| Error rate (inference) | 0.2% | +0.5pp | critical if >1% | runtime/SRE |
| KV divergence (KL proxy) | 0.01 | +0.05 | high if >0.08 | serving |

Configuration Examples
- Canary route JSON (example):
{ "route": "/v1/generate", "artifact_id": "quant-artifact-2026-03-01", "percent_traffic": 1, "fallback_artifact": "baseline-artifact-8f9c", "health_window": 300000 }

- Probe registration YAML (example):
---
probe_id: longcontext-qual-001
slice: long-context
owner: applied-ml
metrics: [semantic_similarity, continuation_entropy]
priority: high
retention_days: 90
---

Checklist before promotion
- [ ] Probe suite completeness verified (hot, long-context, functioncall, safety).
- [ ] Shadow-run metrics uploaded and reviewed by at least one reviewer.
- [ ] Rollout route and fallback configured in Router with cooldowns.
- [ ] Dashboards created and alerts configured for the artifact.
- [ ] Artifact stored in registry with reproducibility metadata (seed, conversion script hash, quant params).

Post-promotion monitoring and audits
- Maintain probe sampling for 14 days post-GA with daily digest to model owner.
- Schedule a 7-day audit to check for slow drift in fidelity metrics; if drift > half the fidelity budget, place artifact on periodic review cadence.
- Record all incidents and anomaly detections in the migration registry and link to model promotion PRs.

Exceptions and fast-paths
- For low-risk, internal-only artifacts (non-customer-facing), expedited rollouts (shadow -> 20% -> GA in 24h) are allowed with explicit approval from Model Owner + Runtime lead. Document reason and probe subset used.

Related pages
- /applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026
- /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/shadow-orchestrator-crossmodal-stress-2026

Appendix: Typical failure modes and mitigations
- Increased continuation hallucinations on long-context: reduce quant aggressiveness, re-run with higher-precision attention layers, expand long-context probe set and rebaseline.
- Tokenization boundary drift: re-run tokenization alignment tests and validate prompt-segmentation heuristics.
- Instance OOMs after quant: tighten memory profiling in conversion and add margin to batch size scheduling.

Contact and escalation
- Primary contact: Maya Chen (applied-ml)
- Eval-harness oncall: eval-harness@redwood.internal
- Runtime oncall: runtime-sre@redwood.internal

Revision history
- 2026-02-14: Document created by Maya Chen
- 2026-03-01: Clarified automated abort conditions and added KV-cache divergence metrics (reviewers: Arjun Patel, Sofia Martinez)

title: Compression-aware Probe Suite and Quant Sensitivity Fingerprint
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines the Compression-aware Probe Suite (CAPS) and the Quant Sensitivity Fingerprint (QSF) used to characterize how model outputs degrade or change under quantized artifacts and compression-friendly runtime transforms. CAPS is intended to be run during model onboarding, pre-rollout checks, and continuous regression scans for Dedicated/Private deployments where quantization and mixed-precision paths are used. QSF is a compact, reproducible vector of metrics that summarizes per-workload sensitivity and drives rollout gating, remediation recommendations, and perf/cost tradeoff UI.

Goals and scope
----------------
- Provide a deterministic, reproducible probe generation and scoring pipeline that surfaces subtle behavioral changes introduced by quantization (post-training quant, dynamic quant, mixed-precision) and compression transforms (activation compression, KV-cache serialization).
- Produce an interpretable fingerprint (QSF) per model+profile+workload that is stable across seeds and informative to engineers and product owners.
- Integrate with the eval harness and CI to: (1) block unsafe rollouts, (2) suggest fallback quant-profiles, and (3) prioritize human review slices.

When to run CAPS
------------------
1. Model onboarding (initial candidate promotion to shadow/dedicated).
2. Before enabling a new quant profile or runtime compression optimization in production.
3. Nightly regression scans focused on quant-related slices.
4. On-demand triage when a production regression correlates with a quant deployment.

High-level components
---------------------
1. Probe generator: produces canonical inputs (prompt families) using mutation operators.
2. Multi-mode runner: executes model variants (fp16/fp32, int8, int8+KV-compress, mixed-precision) through the eval harness with matched seeds and deterministic sampling where applicable.
3. Metric synthesizer: computes per-probe metrics and aggregates into the QSF vector.
4. Triager ruleset: maps QSF deltas to recommended remediation steps and rollout gate outcomes.

Probe generator details
-----------------------
- Prompt families covered (each family contains 500–2000 seeds):
  - Long-context priming: multi-turn histories with varying pivot lengths (1k, 4k, 8k tokens).
  - Short-instruction: terse one-line instructions for copy/transform tasks.
  - Table/structured-output: prompts that request JSON/YAML outputs and strict schema conformance.
  - Retrieval-primed: prompts with embedded retrieved passages that exercise KV cache reuse.
  - Math/precision: numerical reasoning and formula manipulation.
  - Safety probes: adversarial paraphrases and hallucination triggers.
- Mutation operators: token-level dropout, synonym substitution, punctuation perturbation, casing/noise injection, and answer-mask perturbation to probe stability under boundary conditions.
- Sampling strategy: stratified by token-length, by expected generation length, and by instruction complexity score (0–1).

Execution matrix
----------------
- Model variants to compare (example): fp32-reference, fp16, int8-static, int8-dynamic, mixed-precision-layerwise, int8+kv-compress.
- Deterministic seeds where sampling-based metrics are compared; stochastic runs for downstream human-facing diversity checks.
- Runtime modes: streaming vs non-streaming to catch prefix-dependent quant artifacts.

Metrics and how QSF is computed
-------------------------------
CAPS computes the following per-probe metrics; QSF aggregates them into a fixed-length vector (string-labeled metrics). Each metric is averaged using trimmed-mean (10% trim) across seeds.
- EmbeddingDistanceMean: mean cosine distance between reference fp32 embeddings and quantized variant embeddings for the same prompt (embedding model: model@last-layer-average).
- OutputTokenFlipRate: percent of tokens where argmax(token) differs from reference, normalized by token-length.
- LogitDelta90: 90th percentile absolute change in top-5 logits for the first N tokens (N configurable, default 32).
- SchemaIntegrityRate: fraction of structured-output probes that parse to expected JSON schema without correction.
- GenerationDivergenceIndex (GDI): BLEU/ROUGE-style metric adapted for free-form; computed as 1 - normalized semantic similarity (embedding-based) so higher is worse.
- ScalingLatencyImpact: relative change in median latency under workload-aware batching when using quantized kernels (used for perf/cost tradeoffs).
- KVCacheMismatchRate: percent of retrieval-primed probes where the final answer differs when the KV cache path is enabled vs disabled in the quantized runtime.

QSF vector example (ASCII):
[EmbeddingDistanceMean:0.012, OutputTokenFlipRate:0.043, LogitDelta90:0.18, SchemaIntegrityRate:0.92, GDI:0.06, ScalingLatencyImpact:-0.12, KVCacheMismatchRate:0.014]

Interpreting QSF and thresholds
-------------------------------
- Threshold bands (per-metric; example defaults):
  - Green (safe): EmbeddingDistanceMean < 0.02, OutputTokenFlipRate < 0.02, LogitDelta90 < 0.10, SchemaIntegrityRate > 0.97, GDI < 0.03, KVCacheMismatchRate < 0.005.
  - Yellow (caution): EmbeddingDistanceMean 0.02–0.05, OutputTokenFlipRate 0.02–0.05, LogitDelta90 0.10–0.25, SchemaIntegrityRate 0.90–0.97, GDI 0.03–0.10, KVCacheMismatchRate 0.005–0.02.
  - Red (fail): values outside yellow bounds.
- Rollout gating policy (example):
  1. All metrics in Green -> allow rollout.
  2. Any metric in Yellow but no metric in Red -> canary rollout with 5% traffic + manual review of top-3 slices flagged.
  3. Any metric in Red -> block and create incident ticket assigned to "serving-quant-team".

Integration with eval harness and CI
-----------------------------------
- CAPS exports a machine-readable QSF JSON artifact per job and a human-readable PDF summary with the top-10 failed probes and sample transcripts.
- Suggested CI step: compare QSF against baseline QSF artifact using a tolerant comparator that respects metric covariances. Failing jobs should not auto-promote.
- Example CLI invocation (eval harness adapter):
  rwi-eval run --suite CAPS --model model:v3-7 --variants fp32,int8,int8-kv --out qsf.json --seeds 42,43,44 --report pdf

Example QSF YAML snippet used by gating service
----------------------------------------------
| param | value |
|-------|-------|
| gating_policy | quant-cautious |
| allowed_yellow_metrics | ["EmbeddingDistanceMean","ScalingLatencyImpact"] |
| blocked_red_metrics | ["SchemaIntegrityRate","KVCacheMismatchRate"] |

(Implementation note: stored in the rollout service as plain YAML; use the eval-harness comparator library to compute deltas.)

Recommended remediation playbook
--------------------------------
1. If SchemaIntegrityRate drops: revert to earlier quant-profile that preserves structured decoders, or enable output-constrained decoding (beam constraints / format validators).
2. If EmbeddingDistanceMean increases but token flip rate is low: prefer hybrid-embedding-recompute (recompute embedding reference on the quantized path for similarity-based downstreams) and add embedding-stable calibration layer.
3. If KVCacheMismatchRate > threshold: audit KV serialization path and test with different cache serialization precisions; consider disabling aggressive KV compression for affected layers.
4. If Latency improves but GDI increases: surface cost/perf tradeoff to product owner and consider partial rollout with fallback routing for safety-sensitive routes.

Ownership and runbook triggers
-----------------------------
- Primary owner: applied-ml (probe infra) team. Secondary: serving-quant team.
- SLOs for CAPS jobs:
  - CAPS job completion (nightly run): 95% jobs finish within 3 hours per model family.
  - QSF artifact availability: 99% within 10 minutes of job completion.
- Runbook triggers (automated):
  - New QSF with any Red metric -> create P1 ticket to #serving-quant on Slack + PagerDuty paging to oncall in the quant rotation.
  - Canary rollout flagging yellow metrics -> open a canary review task and schedule a 1-hour deep-dive with model owner and serving engineer.

Reporting and dashboards
------------------------
- QSF time-series: track per-model, per-profile QSF metrics and highlight metric drift beyond 3-sigma over a 14-day window.
- Heatmap: compression-sensitivity heatmap by probe family (rows = probe family, cols = quant profile) showing %Delta in GDI.
- Example dashboard panels to create:
  - Top failing probes table (probe id, metric, delta, example transcript).
  - QSF trend line per metric with rolling baseline.
  - Rollout gate status for active canaries.

Annotation and human-in-the-loop review guidance
-----------------------------------------------
- For any canary with Yellow or Red metrics, generate an annotation packet with: 10 representative probes, reference transcripts, quantized transcripts, and an embedding-based divergence explanation.
- Human reviewers should answer: (1) Are the failures semantic or surface-level? (2) Do safety or correctness slices exist? (3) Can a prompt rewrite or output filter mitigate? Record decisions in the review artifact.

Examples and quick-start
------------------------
1) Run baseline CAPS locally (dev):
   - rwi-eval local --suite CAPS --model model:v3-7 --variants fp32,int8 --seeds 100 --out dev-qsf.json
2) Upload results for gating check:
   - rwi-gate check --artifact dev-qsf.json --baseline gs://qsf-baselines/model-v3-7/baseline-qsf.json
3) Produce human report:
   - rwi-report render --artifact dev-qsf.json --format pdf --examples 10 --out ./reports/dev-qsf.pdf

Appendix: sample probe table (excerpt)
-------------------------------------
| probe_id | family | seed_length | mutation | expected_behavior | notes |
| P-0001 | long-context | 4096 | token-dropout-0.02 | stable-entity-tracking | useful for KV stress tests |
| P-0420 | table-output | 128 | schema-mask | strict-json | parse fail modes are prioritized |
| P-1337 | math-precision | 64 | numeric-round | exact-equals | checks arithmetic operator stability |

Implementation checklist for eng teams
-------------------------------------
- [ ] Add CAPS suite to model onboarding pipeline (onboarding CI stage 3).
- [ ] Store QSF artifacts in artifact-store with per-model+profile keys.
- [ ] Integrate eval-harness comparator to the gating service and set default thresholds.
- [ ] Create dashboard panels in Grafana and a periodic digest to model owners.

Glossary
--------
- QSF: Quant Sensitivity Fingerprint.
- CAPS: Compression-aware Probe Suite.
- GDI: Generation Divergence Index.
- KV compression: any runtime transform that reduces KV cache memory footprint (quantized serialization, lossy encoding).

Contact and feedback
--------------------
If you have questions or want this suite extended for multimodal models or private deployment constraints (air-gapped artifact storage, offline-only probes), open a merge request against the CAPS repo and ping @Aisha Patel on Slack.

title: Quantization profile attribution + cost impact tracking
content:
## Overview
This page defines the canonical way to:
1) Map **quantization profiles** to **model identifiers** in telemetry, and
2) Track the impact of quantization on **blended $/1M output tokens**, **latency**, and **quality guardrails**.

This is used by the Unit Economics dashboard (internal) and by Applied ML / Runtime teams to safely roll out new quantization profiles without creating attribution gaps or high-cardinality telemetry.

**Primary outcomes**
- Quantization experiments and rollouts are attributable in metering and aggregation (no “unknown profile” buckets except for explicitly allowed fallbacks).
- Cost improvements are measurable and comparable across time, region, and customer tier.
- Quality regressions are caught via guardrails tied to prompt sets/evals before broad rollout.

**Owners**
- Model metadata + allowed values: Quentin Harris
- Token metering dimension implementation: Nadia Rahman
- Aggregation + warehouse views: Mei Lin
- Data quality checks: Caleb Johnson
- Product consumer (Optimize / Console): Aditya Rao

---

## Definitions
### Quantization profile (quantization_profile)
A **stable, low-cardinality identifier** representing the quantization strategy used for a model deployment (weights, KV cache quantization, activation quantization where relevant, and any kernel/runtime constraints that materially affect cost/latency).

Quant profiles are **not** free-form experiment names.

### Model identifiers
We use two identifiers for different needs:
- **model_id**: logical model family, e.g. `llama-3.1-70b-instruct`
- **model_version**: pinned artifact/build, e.g. `llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2025-02-05`

Quantization attribution is always captured via a separate dimension:
- **quantization_profile** (see naming + allowed values below)

### Attribution principle
Attribution must represent the **actual serving configuration** used to generate tokens. If routing falls back to a different model build or a different quantization profile, telemetry must reflect the **effective** values used.

---

## Telemetry requirements (source of truth)
### Required dimensions in token metering
All token metering events used by unit economics aggregation must include:
- `model_id`
- `model_version`
- `quantization_profile`
- `region` (normalized)
- `customer_tier`
- `streaming` (boolean)

Additional recommended fields for analysis (not required for unit cost rollups):
- `route`
- `hardware_type` (bucketed; avoid hostnames)
- `batching_mode` (enum)

### Where the values come from
- `model_id` / `model_version`: populated by the gateway based on the resolved backend target.
- `quantization_profile`: populated by the serving runtime as the effective profile applied at execution.

If the runtime cannot resolve the profile reliably, it must emit:
- `quantization_profile = "unknown"` and increment `quantization_profile_unknown_total` (see data quality section).

---

## Quantization profile naming + allowed values
### Naming convention
`<weights>-<kv>-<kernels>-<notes>`

Rules:
- All lowercase
- Use hyphens as separators
- No customer identifiers, no run IDs, no dates
- Max length: 48 chars

Examples:
- `fp16-kvfp16-trt`
- `int8-kvfp16-trt`
- `int4-kvfp16-trt`
- `int4-kvint8-trt`

### Allowed values (v1)
The allowed values list is managed centrally (Model Metadata Registry) and enforced in telemetry via validation. Adding a new value requires a PR/approval by Model Metadata owner + Telemetry owner.

Allowed values must include these reserved buckets:
- `unknown` (should be rare; triggers alerting when above threshold)
- `none` (used only for embeddings/rerank models where quant profile is not applicable; do not use for text generation)

---

## Mapping quantization profiles to models
Quantization profiles are not globally meaningful unless paired with model metadata. Some profiles are only valid for certain architectures / kernels.

### Canonical mapping table
This mapping is used by:
- Validation (reject impossible combinations)
- Reporting (group compatible deployments)
- Rollout guardrails (detect unexpected profile/model combos)

**Table: quantization_profile_model_compat (authoritative)**

| Field | Type | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| model_id | string | llama-3.1-70b-instruct | Logical model family |
| model_version | string | llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2025-02-05 | Optional; use when profile changes across versions |
| quantization_profile | string | int4-kvfp16-trt | Must be in allowed list |
| status | enum | supported / experimental / deprecated | Used by routing + UI warnings |
| effective_precision | string | w4a16 | For display + analysis |
| notes | string | “int4 weights via AWQ; KV fp16” | Human-readable |

**Usage guidance**
- Prefer mapping at `model_id` level when the profile is stable across versions.
- Use `model_version` rows when:
  - A new build changes quant behavior materially (e.g., kernel change), or
  - A subset of versions are safe/validated for a profile.

---

## Impact tracking: cost, latency, and quality
### Cost metric (unit economics)
Primary: **blended $/1M output tokens**

For quant analysis we also track:
- $/1M input tokens
- $/request (for short-output workloads; optional)

**Recommended breakdowns**
- By `model_id`, `model_version`, `quantization_profile`
- Split by `region` and `customer_tier` to catch infra-specific effects

### Latency metrics
Minimum set:
- p50/p95 end-to-end latency
- time-to-first-token (TTFT) for streaming
- decode throughput proxy: tokens/sec at p50 (where available)

**Attribution requirement:** latency metrics must share the same dimensions used for unit economics so comparisons are aligned.

### Quality guardrails (required for rollout)
Quantization changes are only eligible for broader rollout when guardrails are met.

**Guardrail types**
- Offline eval deltas on approved prompt sets (Applied ML)
- Online quality signals (where available): refusal rate changes, tool-call success rate, structured output validity

**Minimum bar (default)**
- No statistically significant degradation on the “core” eval suite above the agreed threshold.
- No increase in critical failures (e.g., structured output parse failures) above baseline.

**Recording results**
Each quantization profile rollout must have a linked “evidence” entry containing:
- eval_suite_version
- comparison baseline (model_version + quantization_profile)
- key metrics + thresholds
- sign-off (Applied ML + Product for customer-facing changes)

---

## Dashboard + query patterns
### Unit Economics dashboard usage
To compare profiles safely, always filter to:
- Same `model_id` and (if possible) same `model_version`
- Same region (or use region-normalized rollups)
- Same customer tier

Recommended visualizations:
- Time series of blended $/1M output tokens by `quantization_profile`
- Top-N cost deltas by profile within a model family
- Scatter plot: cost vs p95 latency (profile as series)

### Suggested warehouse views (reference)
Naming is illustrative; actual view names may differ by warehouse conventions.
- `unit_econ_hourly_by_model_version_profile`
- `latency_hourly_by_model_version_profile`
- `quality_guardrail_events_by_model_version_profile`

---

## Cardinality + data hygiene guardrails
Quantization profile is a controlled dimension. Violations can degrade the metrics pipeline and make unit economics unreliable.

### Hard rules
- `quantization_profile` must be one of the allowed values.
- Reject values containing:
  - UUID-like strings
  - timestamps/dates
  - slashes or whitespace
- Maximum distinct quantization profiles per model_id in a 24h window: **<= 6** (alert if exceeded).

### Data quality checks (SLO-aligned)
We monitor and alert on:
- **Unknown rate:** `unknown` share of output tokens per model_id
  - Warning: >0.2% over 1h
  - Critical: >1.0% over 1h
- **Coverage drift:** sudden appearance/disappearance of a profile for a high-volume model
- **Impossible combos:** profile/model pairs not in `quantization_profile_model_compat` marked as supported/experimental

Runbook: follow the Unit Economics pipeline oncall guide for investigation steps and backfill guidance.

---

## Rollout checklist for a new quantization profile
1) **Propose profile name** following convention.
2) Add to allowed values list + registry.
3) Update `quantization_profile_model_compat` with at least:
   - model_id
   - quantization_profile
   - status = experimental
   - notes
4) Ensure runtime emits effective `quantization_profile` for all execution paths (streaming and non-streaming).
5) Run offline eval suite and attach evidence.
6) Enable canary routing (small % traffic) with dashboard monitoring:
   - cost delta
   - p95 latency delta
   - unknown rate
7) Promote status to `supported` only after guardrails pass and metrics remain stable.
8) If a profile is retired, mark as `deprecated` (do not delete) to preserve historical comparability.

---

## Common pitfalls
- **Free-form profile labels** (“int4_test_joe_0214”) cause cardinality explosions and break aggregation.
- **Model version changes masked as quant wins**: always compare within a fixed model_version when possible.
- **Fallback routing not reflected**: ensure effective profile/model values are emitted after routing decisions.
- **Streaming paths missing tags**: validate tag parity for streaming vs non-streaming before concluding cost deltas.

---

## FAQ
**Q: Why do we need both model_version and quantization_profile?**
A: Model version captures changes in weights/build/kernels; quantization_profile captures the serving precision strategy. Either can change cost/latency.

**Q: Can we encode kernel type or hardware in the quantization_profile?**
A: No. Keep quantization_profile focused on quant strategy. Hardware/kernels should be separate low-cardinality dimensions (bucketed) if needed.

**Q: What if quantization is “automatic” (runtime chooses)?**
A: The runtime must still emit the effective profile selected so attribution is correct. If selection is nondeterministic, treat as a bug.

---

## Changelog
- 2025-02-18: Clarified allowed value rules; added compatibility mapping table fields and default alert thresholds.
- 2025-02-05: Added rollout checklist + guardrail evidence requirements.
- 2025-01-30: Initial version.

title: FP8/INT8 Quantization Profile Policy for Hosted Model Catalog
content:
## Summary
This page defines Redwood’s policy for enabling FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles in the **Hosted** model catalog. It covers:
- Default profile selection (FP8 vs INT8 vs BF16/FP16 baseline) by model family and GPU SKU.
- Calibration requirements and artifact handling.
- Known accuracy and behavior risks.
- Required evaluation and sign-off steps before enabling a profile **by default**.

This policy is intended to keep the hosted catalog fast and cost-efficient while preventing silent quality regressions and avoiding customer-impacting rollout mistakes.

---

## Definitions
**Profile:** A named serving configuration for a model variant (e.g., BF16 baseline, FP8, INT8), including kernel mode flags, quantization parameters, and guardrails.

**Default profile:** The server-side selection used when a customer does not explicitly pin a profile.

**FP8:** Primarily FP8 compute paths for eligible matmul/attention kernels (typically H100-class GPUs). In practice, FP8 is treated as “performance-first” with moderate quality risk, concentrated in long-context and numerically sensitive tasks.

**INT8:** INT8 quantization modes (often with tighter shape constraints and more calibration sensitivity). INT8 is treated as “cost-first” with higher quality and correctness risk unless the model family and workload are known-safe.

**Baseline:** BF16/FP16 (or equivalent) non-quantized kernels used as quality reference and fallback.

**Evals sign-off:** Written approval from **Jonas Weber** (Perf/Evals decision owner) or designated Applied ML on-call for enabling a profile as the hosted default.

---

## Goals (and non-goals)
### Goals
1. Provide predictable rules for when FP8/INT8 becomes the **default** hosted option.
2. Ensure we have a reproducible calibration and eval trail for every default change.
3. Encode conservative guardrails for long-context, tool-calling, and structured output workloads.
4. Standardize customer-safe rollout practices (flags + canary + rollback triggers).

### Non-goals
- This page does not define kernel microbench methodology (see methodology page).
- This page does not define scheduler tuning policy (owned by Serving Runtime Scheduling).

---

## High-level default policy
We default to the **most aggressive profile that is both (a) supported by runtime heuristics and (b) has passed quality gates for that model family**.

**Default preference order (subject to eligibility):**
1. FP8 (H100/H200-class only; when quality gates pass)
2. INT8 (cost-focused SKUs when quality gates + calibration requirements pass)
3. Baseline (BF16/FP16)

**Always required:**
- Baseline fallback must exist and be tested.
- Rollout must be behind server-side flags (per model + region + cohort).

---

## Eligibility matrix (what we allow by default)
The table below describes Redwood’s *default* posture. Individual models may be overridden (see Exceptions).

| GPU SKU | FP8 default allowed? | INT8 default allowed? | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| H100 (SXM/PCIe) | Yes (preferred) | Case-by-case | FP8 is primary path; INT8 used only when it provides meaningful $/token improvement without quality loss. |
| A100 | No (default) | Case-by-case | FP8 not default on A100; INT8 may be used for embeddings/rerankers if stable. |
| L4 (or similar cost SKU) | No | Yes (preferred for eligible small/medium models) | INT8 is often the primary cost lever; stricter calibration + eval gates apply. |

**Model family posture (default stance):**
- **General-purpose chat LLMs (70B class, long-context):** FP8 allowed on H100 with long-context gating; INT8 default is generally **not** allowed without explicit sign-off and expanded evals.
- **Mixture-of-Experts (MoE):** FP8 allowed only if routing/logits stability is verified; INT8 default is typically **not** allowed (sensitive to calibration and tail behaviors).
- **Embeddings/reranking models:** INT8 defaults often acceptable on A100/L4 if retrieval quality is within tolerance; FP8 is optional on H100.

---

## Calibration policy (INT8 and FP8)
### FP8 calibration requirements
FP8 enablement must use runtime-supported scaling/metadata and pass correctness tests. FP8 is generally less calibration-heavy than INT8 in our hosted setup.

**Required artifacts (FP8):**
- Model hash / revision identifier
- Runtime build SHA + kernel mode flags
- Kernel selection summary (from benchmark artifact metadata)

**Required validations (FP8):**
- Correctness smoke suite passes (golden prompts + structured outputs where applicable)
- Long-context sanity checks when the model advertises long context (>= 32k)

### INT8 calibration requirements
INT8 enablement requires explicit calibration and traceability.

**Calibration dataset requirements (INT8):**
- Must come from **Top Hosted Models Benchmark Suite v3** prompt distributions and/or a model-family-specific prompt set approved by Applied ML.
- Must include:
  - Short prompts (p50)
  - Medium prompts (p90)
  - Long prompts (p95/p99) where the model is offered for long-context
  - At least one structured-output/tool-calling slice if the hosted model advertises tool calling

**INT8 calibration run requirements:**
- Fixed random seed, deterministic tokenization settings
- Recorded sequence length histogram (prefill length + decode length)
- Minimum of **2 independent calibration runs** (different nodes) to catch environment instability

**Required artifacts (INT8):**
- Calibration config (prompt set version, sample count, truncation rules)
- Produced scale/zero-point artifacts (or equivalent) referenced by immutable storage URI
- A short “Calibration Notes” section in the profile change request including known quirks

**Retention:** Calibration artifacts must be retained for **90 days** minimum (or longer if the profile becomes the hosted default).

---

## Quality risk inventory (what can go wrong)
Quantization can change not only accuracy but also *behavior* (formatting compliance, tool-call selection, refusal boundaries). The following risks must be assessed for any default change.

### Common FP8 risks
- Long-context degradation (attention accumulation and numeric sensitivity)
- Subtle shifts in instruction-following on edge prompts
- Increased variance across GPU clocks/thermals if kernel selection changes frequently

### Common INT8 risks
- Larger behavioral shifts (summarization, factuality, multi-step reasoning)
- Format instability for structured outputs (JSON validity, schema adherence)
- Calibration overfitting (good on calibration distribution, worse in the tail)
- Model-family-specific brittleness (especially MoE and long-context)

### Workloads that require special attention
- **Long-context** (>16k; always include a long-context slice in evals)
- **Tool calling / structured output** (must include schema adherence checks)
- **Multilingual** (at least a light multilingual slice if the model is marketed as multilingual)
- **Code generation** (if the model is marketed for coding)

---

## Required eval gates before enabling a default
### Gate 0: Correctness + safety baseline
Required for FP8 and INT8.
- Runtime correctness tests pass (including any quantized-kernel correctness suite)
- No increase in server error rates in synthetic serving tests
- No known unsupported shape regimes for common hosted workloads (documented exceptions are allowed only with explicit fallback rules)

### Gate 1: Quality sanity suite (fast)
Required for FP8 and INT8.
- Run the **Quantization Quality Sanity Suite** (golden prompts + lightweight scoring)
- Any regression must be explained and accepted by Applied ML (or mitigated by gating)

### Gate 2: Benchmark Suite v3 (representative)
Required for any change to a hosted default profile.
- Run Top Hosted Models Benchmark Suite v3 slices relevant to the model’s advertised use cases
- Include structured-output/tool-calling slice when applicable
- Compare against baseline profile

**Default acceptance thresholds (unless model-specific exception is approved):**
- No statistically significant regression on primary quality metrics used for the model category.
- Any observed regression must be limited to non-default cohorts (e.g., long-context-only traffic) via routing/gating.

### Gate 3: Expanded evals (when required)
Expanded evals are required when any of the following is true:
- Model context length >= 32k and FP8/INT8 is being enabled by default
- Model is MoE
- INT8 is being proposed as default for a general-purpose chat model
- Customer-facing marketing claims will reference the new default

Expanded evals must include additional long-context prompts and at least one stress slice (formatting compliance or retrieval-augmented prompts).

---

## Sign-off rules (who must approve what)
### Changes that DO NOT require Evals sign-off
- Non-default profile added as an opt-in option (still requires Gate 0 + Gate 1)
- Canary-only enablement for internal testing cohorts

### Changes that DO require Evals sign-off (Jonas Weber or delegate)
- Any change that makes FP8 or INT8 the **default** profile for a hosted model
- Any change that expands eligible traffic cohorts (e.g., enabling FP8 for long-context prompts)
- Any change that changes calibration artifacts used by an existing default INT8 profile

### Additional required reviewers (depending on change)
- **Serving Runtime Kernel** (Hiro Tanaka or delegate): kernel support, shape guardrails, fallback correctness
- **Serving Runtime Scheduling** (Sofia Ivanova or delegate): confirms scheduler interaction is understood for end-to-end performance claims
- **SRE/Observability** (Rafael Mendes / Allison Grant): dashboards and canary alerts set up before broad rollout

---

## Model-level default guidance (practical defaults)
These are the default stances we use for hosted catalog decisions. Specific model IDs may differ; treat these as family-level rules.

### Large chat LLMs (high-traffic)
- **H100:** Default FP8 allowed after Gate 2 + sign-off; long-context gating required if any long-context regressions are observed.
- **A100:** Default remains baseline unless INT8 has proven stable *and* the model is not long-context sensitive.
- **L4:** Default INT8 for large chat LLMs is generally **not** allowed; L4 is used primarily for smaller models.

### MoE models
- Default FP8 only after expanded evals; default INT8 is generally disallowed unless a specific MoE model family has demonstrated stable behavior.

### Embeddings / reranking
- INT8 default is often acceptable on A100/L4 if retrieval metrics remain within tolerance and tail-latency improves.
- FP8 on H100 is allowed but not required; choose based on throughput and cost improvements.

---

## Required guardrails in runtime (must be present to enable defaults)
For any FP8/INT8 default enablement:
1. **Fallback policy:** baseline fallback must trigger on unsupported shapes and on error thresholds.
2. **Region + cohort flags:** enablement must be controllable per model + region.
3. **Perf canary gates:** TTFT and TPOT thresholds must be defined by GPU SKU and model tier.
4. **Metric tagging:** runtime metrics must include dimensions for model, GPU, and kernel mode to localize regressions.

---

## Rollout policy (hosted)
Default profile changes follow a staged rollout:
1. **Internal canary** (small cohort, 1 region): validate perf and error rates; spot-check quality.
2. **Perf canary expansion** (multiple regions, still limited traffic): watch TTFT/TPOT/tokens/s and error budget.
3. **Default enablement** (broad): only after sign-off + stable canary window.

**Minimum canary observation window:** 6 hours for high-traffic models, 24 hours for lower-traffic models (or until sufficient sample size).

**Rollback triggers (minimum set):**
- TTFT p95 regression beyond threshold for 15 minutes (after noise suppression)
- TPOT p95 regression beyond threshold for 15 minutes
- Error rate increase (5xx/timeout) beyond threshold
- Any confirmed quality regression reported by Applied ML or Customer Support correlated with profile enablement

---

## Documentation requirements (what must be written down)
Any default change PR/rollout request must include:
- Proposed default profile and motivation (perf/cost)
- GPU SKUs and regions affected
- Calibration artifacts (INT8) and links
- Eval summary (Gate 1/2/3 as applicable)
- Explicit risk statement (what could regress, how we’ll detect it)
- Rollback plan and owners

---

## Exceptions and overrides
Exceptions are allowed only with explicit documentation and time bounds.

**Valid reasons for exceptions:**
- Model-family sensitivity identified (e.g., long-context quality loss under FP8)
- Specific kernel shape regime instability or correctness bug
- Customer-impacting regression found during canary

**How to request an exception:**
- Open a profile override request and include an expiration date (default: 30 days)
- Notify Serving Runtime and SRE owners if it changes rollout behavior

---

## FAQ
### Can customers opt out of FP8/INT8 defaults?
Yes. Customers can pin a baseline or specific profile when exposed in the API/Console. Hosted defaults are server-side but should always have a documented fallback and supported pinning path for enterprise customers when needed.

### Do we ever enable INT8 by default for top-tier chat models?
Only with expanded evals, stable calibration, and explicit sign-off. Our default stance is that INT8 is higher risk for behavioral regressions in general-purpose chat.

### What if FP8 is faster but hurts quality on long-context only?
Prefer gating: keep FP8 default for short/medium contexts and route long-context requests to baseline (or a safer FP8 variant) until an FP8 fix or mitigation exists.

---

## Ownership
- Policy owner: **Arjun Desai** (Quantization profiles lead)
- Evals sign-off owner: **Jonas Weber**
- Runtime enablement owners: Serving Runtime Kernel (Hiro Tanaka), SRE rollout (Rafael Mendes)

For urgent issues during canary, follow the escalation paths in the FP8/INT8 Regression Triage Playbook.

title: Per-Workload Quantization Tuner and Safety Guidelines
content:
Overview

Purpose: Provide a standardized, workload-driven quantization autotuning workflow plus safety validators and rollout criteria for model serving at Redwood. This doc codifies the tests, thresholds, and fallback policies to use when generating per-workload quantization profiles and before promoting profiles to production.

Scope
- Applies to all encoder-decoder and decoder-only language models onboarded to Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private (hosted inference workflows use a subset of these checks).
- Targets weight-only and mixed precision quantization (8-bit, 6-bit, and FP8 experimental profiles) and int8 dynamic/aware flows.
- Does not replace model-level release notes or licensing checks — coordinates with model-onboarding owners.

Definitions
- Quant profile: Serialized configuration (YAML) that describes per-layer precision, grouped quantization settings, and kernel hints.
- Workload: A production-style request distribution (prompt templates + length distribution + sampling params).
- Safety validator: A gate that runs automated checks comparing quantized outputs to the float32 baseline.

High-level workflow (autotune + validation)
1. Create workload bundle: collect 500–5,000 representative prompts, length histogram, and desired sampling params (top_p, temp, max_tokens). Store as a named bundle: e.g., workload/email-reply-v1.
2. Generate candidate quant profiles: run the autotuner (see CLI example) across target precisions and per-layer candidates. Save candidates with consistent IDs.
3. Run fast validators: run lightweight metrics (embedding similarity, token-level edit distance, logit shift) over 1k samples. Reject obviously broken candidates.
4. Run heavy validators: full pass through regression harness — semantic metrics, downstream evals, latency/cost benchmarks.
5. Safety decision: accept, accept-with-fallback, or reject. If accepted, create staged rollout with fallback policy.
6. Monitor: collect production metrics during rollout (regression alerts, user-quality signals). Revert if thresholds breach.

Autotune commands and examples
- Basic autotune run (local/GKE job):
  rwd-quant-autotune --model-id gptx-13b --workload ./bundles/email-reply-v1.json --min-precision=6 --max-precision=8 --tune-duration=2h --out-dir=./candidates/email-reply-v1/

- Generate multiple seeds/paraphrases for robustness testing:
  rwd-quant-augment --bundle ./bundles/customer-chat-v2.json --paraphrase-seed 42 --n-variants 3 --out ./bundles/customer-chat-v2-aug.json

Quant profile YAML example (canonical fields):
```
# quant-profile.yaml
profile_id: email-reply-v1-8q
model_family: gptx-13b
precision: 8
per_layer_overrides:
  decoder.layer.30.attention.q_proj: 16
  decoder.layer.31.ffn: 8
activation_quant: dynamic
calibration_method: percentile-99.7
kernel_hint: amx-fused-gemm
notes: "autotuned on workload/email-reply-v1 with seed=42"
```

Fast validators (cheap, used to filter hopeless candidates)
- Embedding cosine similarity: fast_embed(quant_out) vs fast_embed(fp32_out) >= 0.995 on mean across samples.
- Top-token overlap: greedy(top1 list) overlap >= 0.90 for prompts shorter than 64 tokens.
- Aggregate logit shift: mean absolute logit shift per-token <= 0.12 for top-5 logits.
- Latency check: p50 must be <= baseline p50 * 0.9 for the same batch size and sequence length.

Heavy validators (semantic/regression-focused)
- Downstream task evals: run task-specific suites (summarization ROUGE-L drop <= 1.0, classification F1 drop <= 0.5 pts).
- Human-calibrated QA subset: 200 samples from golden set; human raters score unchanged-quality >= 95% (within labeling noise).
- Embedding stability for retrieval: mean cosine similarity >= 0.98 and MAP@10 degradation <= 0.5 pts.
- Safety and toxicology: run safety filters and adversarial prompts; ensure no new policy violations introduced.

Acceptance criteria (must pass all):
- No heavy-validator metric breach beyond threshold listed above.
- No single example regression > 30% semantic distance (measured via embedding + entailment).
- Latency/cost improvement is observed or neutral (cost per 1k tokens reduced by at least 5% OR within +/-3%).
- No increase in variance of per-request latency > 2x baseline.

If not accepted, the actionable outcomes:
- Reject: keep fp32 in production and log candidate for analysis.
- Accept-with-fallback: deploy profile behind rollout where fallback is the fp32 flow if logit-shift > 0.2 or if per-request quality signal fires.
- Conditional: enable for read-only endpoints (embeddings, reranking) but not for generative-chat endpoints.

Rollout plan (staged)
1. Canary: 1% traffic, shadow requests to fp32, monitor for 48h.
2. Extended canary: 10% traffic or 72h window, enable automated rollback if any regression alert triggers.
3. Ramp to 50% over 7 days with tightened alert thresholds.
4. Full rollout after steady state and no regressions for 14 days.

Monitoring and production validators
- Metrics to capture:
  - regression_alerts (binary),
  - user_quality_signal (NPS-like short survey sampling),
  - embedding_similarity_distribution,
  - token_edit_distance_histogram,
  - p50/p95 latency and cost-per-token.

- Real-time alert thresholds:
  - embedding similarity median < 0.975 => critical alert.
  - task-specific metric drop > delta (see heavy validators) => critical.
  - production-per-request logit shift > 0.3 for >0.1% of requests in 5m => warning.

Regression harness (automation)
- Inputs: candidate profile, workload bundle, baseline outputs (cached), test-suite config.
- Runs: unit-level text comparisons, semantic similarity layers, task evals, safety checks, perf runs.
- Output artifacts:
  - numeric report (CSV) of all validators,
  - per-sample diffs (JSONL) with concise reason codes,
  - decision ticket template pre-filled for SRE/product review.

CLI: generate decision ticket from harness results
  rwd-quant-report --input ./candidates/email-reply-v1/report.json --decision-template ./templates/quant-decision.md --out ticket-1234.md

Ownership and responsibilities
- Applied ML (quant team): owns autotuner, validator suite, and maintenance of quant profiles.
- Serving Runtime: implements kernel hints and ensures fallback path exists.
- Product / Owner: approves acceptance for sensitive workloads (payments, legal, PII).
- SRE: validates rollout orchestration and monitors SLOs.

Appendix: recommended test cases (minimal set to include per workload)
- Short-answer prompts (n=200): 1–32 tokens, high wt for top-token overlap.
- Long-form prompts (n=200): 128–1024 tokens, evaluate generation drift and latency.
- Retrieval + rerank (n=200 pairs): embedding similarity and MAP@10.
- Safety adversarial suite (n=100): known policy triggers and near-miss prompts.

Change history and notes
- 2025-10-12: initial draft and autotune CLI prototypes (Marina V.).
- 2025-11-21: added embedding thresholds and rollout template (Ethan P.).
- 2026-02-04: tightened acceptance criteria for MAP@10; added production alert rules (Priya N.).

Related artifacts (where to find outputs)
- Candidate artifacts: s3://rwd-quant/candidates/{profile_id}/
- Regression reports: gs://rwd-quant-reports/{profile_id}/report.csv
- Dashboard: Console -> ML Ops -> Quant Profiles -> {profile_id}

Contact
- For questions and exceptions, ping #quant-team on Slack or open an engineer-owned runbook ticket via the internal service catalog.

title: Probe-driven Fidelity Lattice and Quant Hedging Playbook
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines a practical, probe-driven approach for managing a fidelity lattice (a graded set of model quantization / execution modes) and an automated hedging policy that routes traffic, triggers fallbacks, and controls rollouts. It is intended for model-onboarding engineers, SREs supporting inference fleets, and evaluation teams responsible for quality regressions during quant migration.

Goals:
- Reduce per-token cost by opportunistically using lower-fidelity execution while maintaining user-facing quality SLOs.
- Detect and contain fidelity-induced regressions early using probes and live-slice telemetry.
- Provide deterministic rollback and hedging rules that integrate with Canary/A/B and Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to sequence generation models (chat, completions, rerankers) served by the Redwood runtime.
- Assumes model artifacts have at least two quantization variants (baseline_fp16/fp32, quant8/aq8, and a low-memory int4-like option).
- Requires probe infrastructure (eval harness shadow runs, slice tagging, and real-time quality sensors) already configured per service.

Key concepts:
1) Fidelity lattice: an ordered list of model variants by fidelity and cost. Example lattice levels: HIGHEST -> baseline_fp16, MEDIUM -> quant8, LOW -> int4_sparse.
2) Probe cohort: a lightweight, representative probe set for a service slice (user intent cluster) used to surface coherence/regression signals during shadow and live checks.
3) Hedging policy: pre-authorized rules that route live traffic to fallback fidelity levels (or alternate models) when telemetry crosses thresholds.
4) Safety envelope: SLOs, noise budgets, and automated conditions under which a rollout must pause or roll back.

Fidelity lattice (example table):
| level | variant id | expected latency delta | token-cost ratio | expected coherence impact | owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| HIGHEST | m-xl-baseline-fp16 | +0 ms | 1.00x | baseline | model-onboard-team |
| MEDIUM | m-xl-quant8 | -12% | 0.62x | small risk (templated answers) | runtime-ops |
| LOW | m-xl-int4-sparse | -28% | 0.38x | medium risk (hallucination/formatting) | runtime-ops |

Quality and telemetry signals to monitor:
- Probe pass rate (primary): fraction of probe inputs where the fidelity variant matches baseline acceptance criteria (semantic match >= configured threshold).
- Drift score: embedding similarity change vs baseline on anchor prompts.
- Latency tail (p95, p99) and token-level throughput differential.
- Functioncall fidelity: percentage of function calls with parsed arguments matching ground truth.
- Regression surface: rate of new failure slices (per 10k requests) compared to baseline.
- Cost delta: observed per-token spend change vs baseline window.

Release criteria (pre-flight checklist):
- Unit tests and model verification complete (see onboarding-checklist).
- Shadow run against representative probe cohort for 24–72 hours with:
  - Probe pass rate >= 99% for MEDIUM, >= 95% for LOW (adjust per service risk).
  - No new high-severity slice with >1% traffic exposure.
  - Latency tail within configured SLO increase (default p95 <= baseline_p95 + 20ms).
- Sign-off from the model owner and runtime-ops (explicit reviewer approval entry in related_pages).

Automated hedging policy (example rules):
1. Live routing preconditions:
   - Start: 0% -> MEDIUM hedged traffic for canary (sampled 1%)
   - Expand to 5% if 24h shadow probes pass
2. Real-time triggers (immediate action):
   - If Probe pass rate drops by >2.5 percentage points vs rolling baseline -> immediate shift to previous lattice level for affected slices and create incident with severity P2.
   - If new regression slice rate >0.5% for traffic-weighted slices -> pause expansion and throttle to 50% of target.
3. Escalation windows (if degraded but not catastrophic):
   - After 30 minutes of degraded probe pass rate, revert to baseline for the slice, trigger auto-bisect job, and open a triage ticket.

Runbook: responding to a hedging trigger
1. Triage owner assignment: runtime-ops oncall (first 15min), then model-onboard lead if root cause is model/quant.
2. Immediate mitigation:
   - Execute automated rollback: set route override to previous fidelity level for impacted slice (CLI example below).
   - Notify SLO dashboard channel and oncall pager.
3. Collect artifacts (automated):
   - Shadow logs for affected requests (include seed, tokenization, KV hit/miss).
   - Probe-level diffs and embedding drift snapshots.
   - Quantization metadata (quant table version, calibration seed).
4. Investigation steps (ordered):
   - Reproduce locally with failing probes and salted seeds.
   - Run deterministic replay using eval harness (seeded run, same environment).
   - Check kernel and scheduling changes in runtime release notes (matching release tag).
   - If repro is consistent, open model regression PR and block rollout.

Example CLI snippets and rollout config:
- Rollout override (CLI):
  redwood routing set --service payments-ner --slice intent:address-parse --variant m-xl-baseline-fp16 --reason "auto-rollback: probe drop"

- Canary rollout YAML (snippet):
  rollout: |
    name: m-xl-quant8-canary
    start_percent: 1
    target_percent: 20
    expansion_window_hours: 24
    probes: sample-probe-cohort:small
    hedging:
      probe_pass_delta_threshold: 2.5
      slice_regression_threshold_pct: 0.5
      auto_revert: true

Safety envelope and thresholds (defaults):
- Probe pass rate delta: 2.5 percentage points
- New high-severity slice threshold: 0.1% of traffic
- Regression slice threshold (aggregate): 0.5%
- Latency p95 uplift allowed: 20ms absolute
- Cost reduction floor: do not reduce fidelity if expected QoE loss > 3% without explicit Product sign-off

Telemetry dashboards and alerts to configure:
- Probe Health dashboard: time-series for each probe cohort (pass rate, drift, variant compare).
- Fidelity Delta dashboard: comparative panel for cost, latency, and pass rates across lattice levels.
- Auto-hedge activity log: event stream showing automatic route changes, triggers, and revert actions.
- Alerting rules (examples):
  - P1: Probe pass rate delta >= 5 points for any high-traffic slice (page + Slack)
  - P2: Probe pass rate delta in [2.5, 5) points for 10 minutes (Slack + ticket)
  - P3: Latency p99 uplift > 50ms for 5 minutes (ticket)

Integration with evaluation pipelines:
- Shadow orchestration: use the eval-harness shadow runner with seeded probe cohorts to continuously score quant variants.

Post-incident playbook and postmortem criteria:
- Required when any P1 auto-hedge or manual rollback affects >1% of traffic or causes customer-facing errors.
- Postmortem should include: timeline, probe diffs, replay artifacts, quant metadata, root-cause hypothesis, corrective actions, and required changes to the lattice or thresholds.

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigation hints
- Tokenization mismatch after quant calibration: re-run tokenization-consistency test; if failing, reject quant build.
- Functioncall syntax drift: tighten functioncall parsing acceptance check and increase probe weight for functioncall patterns.
- Long-context coherence drop with int4: restrict LOW-level usage to short sequences only via route rules.
